I hated them, with their placid smiles and patience. I hated the sameness of their clothes, their open doors, their utter lack of want. " Will you be comfortable here? " they asked, when they brought me to a glass dome atop a tower. It looked over the shining city, and was furnished in sleek, fine style. An oligarch would live here, holding court in this urban throne. " Yes, " I said, " If this is part of my estate, then my trust executors invested well. " " Oh, " they laughed, " Estate! Invest! How quaint you sound. " I felt that I was going mad. " Ownership is no longer practiced, brother! All things are freely shared. Brother Zane has been staying here, of late. He has been painting the city from this vantage, and thought that the view might bring you joy. " " What does he do, this Brother Zane? " " Why, he does what we all do. " they replied, " Create. Discover. Explore. The hierarchy of needs that plagued the ancients is obsolete. This is the age of transcendence. We are free. " What did they know of creation? What fools, these doe-eyed people, resting on their even plane of amity and order. No great creation was ever birthed on equal ground; it is the child of chaos, of pitting man against man in willful strife and competition. How could they explore, without greed? What was there to discover, without ambition? Once, I commanded wealth and power, as I flogged the backs of lesser men. I would restore my world again. " Are you sad, brother? " they asked. " You join no assemblies and keep to yourself. Do you like music, or writing, or art? Come, try to share our pleasures! " " You are right, " I said, " Art moves me. Perhaps - an installation? I find myself inspired by historic structures. " " Ah, " they cried, " How wonderful that you have found direction! Let us show you how to work the bots, and the material manipulators, so that you can sculpt what you need. " " I envisioned a performance element, " I said, " Where we would all participate, together. A celebration of brotherhood, and of mankind's great designs. " They were overjoyed at the thought of this universal collaboration. Now, I sit atop my tower, surveying what they do not know I own. A thousand, thousand people labor down below. They have built me the Pyramids. They have built me Versailles. They have built me, sans resistance, the Palm Resort of Dubai. Shall I direct the construction of The Empire State Building, next? Here are my blue-collar subjects, ignorant and equal in their happy union. I pay them no wages, and profit alone. What a piece of work is man! How noble in reason, how infinite in faculty - how unbounded in capitalist Godhood he stands!

Moment of Clarity End of the line. I always knew it would happen. Eventually all the misdeeds catch up to you. The path I set out on was long and treacherous. I believed what I was doing was right, that what I was doing would make a difference. I was a fool. But now..... at the end..... I can finally make things right..... atone for my past. I know what I'm getting into. The odds are heavily stacked against me. I don't think I'll see tomorrow, but yet I will go forth and face my fate like a man. I hope that with my sacrifice I will have redeemed my soul. All the lives I took, all the people I hurt..... I'm sure I'm too far gone already. But right now, those people in the hospital are counting on me to buy them some time to evacuate. I will do my duty to the utmost of my abilities. They have a saying for this: "You either die a villain, or you live long enough to see yourself become the hero." My actions always spoke louder than words, and they shall speak once more. For duty. For honor. For my fallen brothers and sisters. I will fight to my last bullet, until my blade dulls, and my hands are battered and bruised. They will remember me for this, for what I did, and in that I shall have gained immortality. To whomever reads this hastily scrawled note, find my body and give it a proper burial. I know my enemy won't.

Most scavengers didn't dare to scale the skyscrapers on the ruined mound of earth that was once Manhattan. That was what made Cloud and Rain so valuable. The pair of 11 year olds were light on their feet, quick-witted and had a knack for spotting the most valuable chunks of Old World technology. When the ringing started, neither of them panicked or rushed for the sound. They hid. They hid and waited for the cycling marimba chorus to stop, but it wouldn't. Cloud, who had stashed herself in the entry closet of the apartment, stuck her head out first. "I don't think it's dangerous." Rain had been further in the room when the ringing started and had hidden herself behind the tattered remains of a couch. While crouching behind it, she had studied the fabric to see if any of the leather was salvagable, but it was tattered and stunk. Cats, most likely. Cats were the ruin of most things this high up. Rain slipped out from behind the couch and made her approach. The ringing was coming from a piece of machinery positioned at the end of a long table. It was all white with a silver rectangle thrust into the center of it. The rectangle was the source of the noise, and was flashing light across one side of it. "It's a screen." The two girls walked closer to it, step by step, each of them wary that it might be a trap: they'd once encountered a home security system that ran on an old microfusion battery that had chased them around for an hour. By the time Cloud was in reaching distance, though, the girls had lowered their guard. "What's it say?" Cloud squinted. "Reminder: 11 AM, Spin Class. Tap to dismiss." She tapped the screen and the ringing stopped. Cloud frowned some more and reached out for the rectangle and plucked it from the rest. "Cloud! It could be dangerous!" "No, I don't think so. I think it's a phone." "Really?" Rain leaned over Cloud's shoulder. "The thing like a radio?" "Yeah but they used to do a lot of other things too, grandfather told me about it. I've seen some of these in the workshop, but none of them work. I wonder how come this one still works..." She handed the device to Rain, who started to touch the surface. She made a face at it. "C..... con..." "Contacts." Cloud examined the rest of the machine. The old phones used to have batteries, but it was far too small to hold a microfusion battery, which meant that it was still getting a charge from something. "G..... gamus?" "Games. Here, let me show you." Cloud took the phone back, pretending she knew what she was doing. she touched a few icons and marveled at how they swiped and flickered on the screen. Satisfied, she handed it back to Rain. "What is it?" "It's a game. Something about a bird, just touch it, you'll figure it out." She did, then immediately spat a curse. Then she reset the game and started again. Cloud went back to the machinery examining the base. There were several more rectangles of dark metal glistening in a patch of sunlight pouring in through the hole in the wall. "Solar cells! That's how this thing keeps charging, it has solar cells!" Cloud went to work immediately dumping away the other chunks of metal and bits of electrical wiring from her pack. "With this, grandfather might be able to get a lot of the Old World tech working! Come on, we have to get it home right away." Rain had settled onto a chair, absorbed. "Rain!" "Yeah, yeah, fine..... just as soon as I get this stupid bird..... come on bird..... avoid the pipes!" Cloud snapped the phone away and tucked it into her pocket.

"Not until you just asked," he chuckles back. The laugh is a little too boisterous for the man, the answer a little too swift for the stoicness he so exemplifies. "Come on," I chide. "I'm serious," I lean forward at him, fiddling with the beer can. In my experience, inebriated on a moonlit night is the best time to be serious. It coaxes the truth out of people. Must be something to do with reducing inhibitions. "Look, Diane," the worry lines form across his face, creases appearing in familiar places. A face he'd made far too many times. "I do not want to talk about it." "Well, you've clearly been thinking about it," I shrug. "First thing that came to your mind." On another night I would've dropped it, the same dance we'd made a million times before. I prodded the campfire with a stick and watched as the flames flickering across his face changed positions. He looked grim one second, pensive the next, and I wasn't certain whether it was a trick of the light. "I did what I had to do. I do not need to be poked and prodded about it. Especially not by you," he said, pointedly. He tossed aside his can of beer and reached for another. "You can't keep it all bottled up like that," I inch my chair closer to him, the plastic legs scratching into the gravel. "One day it's all going to come out, and it won't be pretty." "Yeah, well, cross that bridge when we come to it," he swigs another beer. "Fine," I sigh. "I think the marshmallows are done anyways."

"That's not good enough, you're havin' a laugh if you think that's a good swap." I held his stare. I was always bad at haggling. Once I went to Morocco with my girlfriend. We got pressured in to buying some tacky necklace for about fifteen times the asking price. I was so ashamed that I lost face in front of her like that. It was emasculating. "Mate, are you for real? Those carrots have two days left, tops. This is a good radio." Actually, it was a pretty crappy radio. A charity started giving them out just after the war started so we could hear news about the front line, so most people had one at some point. However the build quality was terrible and most of them stopped working in the damp. "I've got two already - can't sell them. You got anything else?" I hated this part. I'd lost, and he knew it. Food was getting valuable, especially fresh food like that. I looked again at the carrots. Last year I would have tossed these mangy things back in to the organic, fair trade, simply delicious basket and not thought anything of it. Did you know that baby carrots were just those mangy ones cut down? I didn't. "No, that's it." I tried to look as pathetic as possible. It was a long shot, even if he doesn't sell them he could eat them himself. We both knew there wasn't any reason for charity. "Sorry, mate. Can't help you," he looked past me, "Alright, mate? Any carrots for you? What you got?" Fuck sake. I turned away and started back since it was late in the afternoon. Bad haul today. I left with some screwdrivers and a lump hammer, and now I'm coming back with a radio and a pair of gloves. That girl really laid it on with the radio. Good price, good price! Fuck off. Can't eat a fucking radio. What was I thinking? Still, it's something. Mainly I've just been bored. A little music on the windy-up radio could be a pleasant change of pace. The streets in this part of town, which used to be an inner city slum, haven't really changed. A little more dirty, a little more rubble, but aside from that not too different. Most people here weren't smart enough to leave, or just straight didn't have the money. It's probably the most inhabited part of town. I turned down the alley that took me towards home, and the streets started to fill with more debris. A wall missing here, a half destroyed car there, and a badly shot up checkpoint. Most of the damage to it was done after the soldiers left by the rebels. I never understood what was so satisfying about shooting it up. They did it sporadically for days. There's something about the war that turned everything grey and brown. The sky was the colour of old tea stains on the pot, the walls a uniform state of drab. I wandered in to the courtyard of my newest home, a small, two storey, derelict workshop building. It was a little safer here as the fighting wasn't in the immediate area, and there wasn't much left to bomb. Some other people had taken a cursory look at the place, but the ground floor is full of water. The first floor wasn't too bad but from the outside it looked pretty beat up, even if the windows were still mostly there and the roof was intact. I walked up the metal fire escape and blew in to my hands. Oh yeah, I have gloves. Maybe not such a waste after all. And there was a little rice left. What didn't happen you say? Well, I'll tell you. Everything happened I supposed, from the beginning. The world was warm and bright, while a little cold at some times. It was a rich, a dirt pile with enough soil for the worms to eat, enough worms for the birds to eat, enough birds for the cats to eat, enough cats for the wolves to eat, then enough bears for man, the greatest of the worms, to eat. But then nothing happened. It didn't stop. It simply didn't happen. Nothing was there. No lights, no sounds. Not even the person you are sitting next to happened. There wasn't even an empty void. For how can you have a void of nothing when nothing happened? Time never happened. The universe never happened. You never happened. All thanks to a vengeful god, the last of his species, who survived the battle of the heavens and was it's greatest killer. Whose mind dove into the wild and fire of insanity until he was nothing more than a beast. And he too was nothing.

It was always a pain to laugh. "Number 43,493, Number 43,493" echoed through the linoleum tiled, white washed waiting room. "I'll see you after work," the man said. "Wont you come in? " , the woman. They stared at each other for a fleeting moment, and then the man turned without another glance. He stepped back out the door and after a few swipes was back in an Auticar. The city around him transfigured into a blur of gray. The dreariness of this particular day was not lost on him, however, he always felt sad after leaving the treatment facility. What drove her to do it? They said after your first visit you could never stop, and that much remained true for her. They would wait for hours in the rain, for that brief moment. His Auticar came to stop in front of his office. She always seemed to full of life after her session, and then so empty after the sensation faded away. He entered a lift and found himself staring through the small window in the doors glimpsing fragments the skyline on each floor. Of course, nothing came cheap, and after she left her job there was no choice but for him to keep working. The treatments would have left him and her on the street as it did many others. Through his little window, he could see the illuminated sign, dazzling with sparkling lights and twirling smiles. The grinning faces dancing across the screen. The words "Knock, Knock" were marching on the lower boarder. His lift stopped and he walked down the bare hallway wondering what the words mean, and imitating the faces on the screen. He would ask her about it when he got home.

It was a particularly sunny Tuesday in early November, approximately seven minutes after lunchtime, during which Patrick finally decided he'd had enough. Precisely what brought this on wasn't entirely clear. It could have been his henchmen's fourteenth failed attempt at producing drinkable coffee to start off the day. It could have been the cough he'd had for over a week, which was not being helped by the frankly moldy cave Patrick reluctantly called his lair. It could have been the fact that when his archenemy, Muscleman, had defeated Patrick's plans of world domination, the local paper had printed a large front page image of the super-wedgie he'd received for his trouble. This particularly irritated Patrick, as the paper had arrived with the undrinkable coffee, and he'd had to read it standing up, as the super-wedgie had made it too painful to sit, even a day after Patrick had received it. Of course, all of these things happened just as Patrick arrived for work in the morning. Therefore, none of these things actually caused Patrick to finally decide he'd had enough, as this was a decision he came to approximately seven minutes after lunchtime, and Patrick, being a punctual man, always arrived for work promptly at eight o'clock, well before any reasonable person would want to eat lunch. So, by use of reasonable deduction, one might assume that the event that truly pushed Patrick over the edge was the television. Patrick was not the best super villain there had ever been. He never quite managed to realize his dreams of total world domination. In fact, he'd never managed so much as domination of a single city. But Patrick, being rather prideful, had never quite blamed himself for that particular failure. As mentioned, Patrick had an archenemy named, of all things, Muscleman. Because Muscleman had superpowers and was the designated ' good guy'according to the karmic balance of the universe, Muscleman had always managed to thwart Patrick's admittedly ingenious plans to take over the world. Naturally, this engendered a certain amount of antagonism between himself and Patrick, which was therefore why Patrick scowled as he looked up to see Muscleman's face on the television. "Well, I'm just happy to keep the fine citizens of this city safe," Muscleman said to the smiling reporter. Patrick never understood why people so admired Muscleman. Past the good looks, majestic cape, charismatic smile, heroic deeds, and unwavering belief in justice, he wasn't all that great. Actually, Patrick thought while rubbing his backside, the man was a bit of a jerk. Muscleman continued talking to the reporter about various dull things, such as a bus full of children he'd saved from falling into the river when the bridge collapsed, and the plane he'd managed to catch before it crashed right in the center of the city. Right when Patrick was getting bored, and was reaching for the remote to turn off the television, the interview led into a more interesting topic. Him. "Unfortunately, the police haven't yet managed to find Cape Guy," Muscleman proceeded to explain. Patrick frowned. He'd never really liked the villain name the media had given him. It's not as if he'd never given his name out. Patrick had always figured that when he finally did manage to take over the world, he'd quite like people to know his real name, thank you very much. That's beside the point that Cape Guy was not intimidating, and misleading. Not intimidating because referred to his dress sense rather than the countless death rays Patrick used mercilessly on his enemies. Or would, once he found something that could actually hurt Muscleman (the closest Patrick had yet come to this was a slight tickle). The name was misleading because Patrick never wore a cape. Not really. Patrick himself would describe it more as a cloak. He thought it added gravitas, and his henchmen had agreed. However, any who disagreed were often thrown into a pit of bloodthirsty muskrats, so perhaps they hadn't been entirely forthcoming in their assessment of Patrick's outfit. Still, if anyone deserved a cape related nickname, it would have to be Muscleman. Of course, Patrick thought to himself, it's unsurprising that the public would give their savior a more flattering title and aim to belittle himself. "Still, I doubt the people of this city have anything to worry about," Muscleman continued. "Cape Guy is, well, pretty much an idiot. He couldn't take over the world if we handed it right to him." The reporter laughed appreciatively at the joke, while Patrick glowered, mostly angry because it wasn't even funny. But really, how dare he! Did Muscleman have any idea how hard it was to take over the world? Patrick bet he didn't. The world is a very big place, and people never really responded well when someone tried to take it over, even if they were as smart and well meaning as Patrick. Really, all Patrick wanted to do was make the world a better place. And get monumental amounts of power and wealth in the process, but that was besides the point. Being a super villain was much harder than being a superhero. Why, Patrick thought, if I became a superhero, I would get rid of all the crime in this city inside a week. With this thought, Patrick paused and thought some more. After all, this whole super villain job wasn't working out quite how he'd expected it to. And Patrick was still young, it's not as if a career change at his age was entirely unheard of. Perhaps being the hero for once might work out better for him. Hell, if he ended up doing a better job than Muscleman, it could even be quite fun. That settles it! Patrick thought to himself. Today, I become... Hero Guy!

My love, my destiny, my dream. It's for you I yearn and for you I scream into the hissing steam of my kettle. I crave you like a serpent craving its next kill, my hunger grows ever more as I watch you move about your habitat, unaware of my presence. You're so graceful, a swan in a dreary lagoon. Oh, love, how beautiful our life will be together. When I think of you and me I purse my lips and wrinkle my nose, I dig my nails into the palms of my hands in anticipation. I need you. I want every piece of you; your skin - oh yes, I want your soft skin to me mine. Your hair..... so badly that whenever you run a comb through it, I pick the fallen strands out of the teeth and keep them in the locket around my neck. When you bite your nails, I want to lick the broken tips. Just as I have no chance against you, as you have defeated me wholly (heart, mind, soul, beyond) you will be mine. I'd rather us both burn in a fire of sulphur while consuming bleach. You and I are entangled together like the hair in my locket. My sweet darling, writing this now I want your hand in my hand, your skin in my mouth and your heart in my pocket.

I loved watching her twist and attempt to free herself, her beautiful green eyes filled with determination. She didn't realize I was watching her, watching as she rubbed her wrists together, attempting to loosen the bonds. Watching as she slowly began to give up, her head hanging so that her red hair fell like a curtain down her shoulders. Even from the slightly blurry screen I could see that her skin was starting to sheen with sweat, most likely from stress. With familiar movements I made sure I had all my tools: paint brushes, Wartenburg wheel, surgical gloves, needles of varying sizes, piercing needles and rings, matches, candles, clamps. Slowly I picked up the final item, my treasured scalpel. There were many wonderful, and some upsetting, memories that involved the blade. I twisted it slightly, watching the light gleam off the side of it and began to remember the first time I used it. I was a less educated lad then, I had not thought of gagging the toy and she was begging for me to let her go. I recalled the way I held my blade bare-handed, my own eyes tearing up as I really considered I was being a monster. I was able to convince myself that I was wrong, that she was just not able to understand what I was doing, and as she began to cry, the steel felt so very cold in my hand and so very heavy. I almost stopped, almost let her go, but went through it. It was so satisfying to watch the blood flow from her, to hear her scream. I smiled, the memory both sad and fond. Sad because of my own fears, but fond because I had gone through and was strong. I glanced one last time at the screen, the girl's shoulders were shaking as if she were crying. I glanced at a few of the other monitors around me, making sure we were still completely alone. The blade was still in my hand as I walked out the door, humming to myself as I went to introduce myself to my new toy. - Hi, guys, go ahead and critique this as desired, I love having feedback so I can grow as a writer. Thank you -

I was too busy failing my AP History Class to notice her at first. Obviously, I hate history- it's boring and feels as though all we ever do is learn about the achievements of someone who we can't relate to at all. That's no reason to fail it- I was failing because I wouldn't do my damn work. Rachel was the top student in the class, getting the questions right every time she was called on. She had been seated behind me from the beginning of the year, and yet I didn't notice her before that one fateful Wednesday in early November. The rain that was coming down outside the windows of the classroom was heavy and cold, the typical state of November rain in southern Michigan. Our teacher, Mr. Harvey, was droning on about something that was probably interesting to someone who had never heard a history lesson in their life- and had never heard anything about the Mongols. The sound of the rain hitting the ground outside, combined with the warmth of the room, created a deadly combination. My eyelids had begun to droop, and I could feel myself falling asleep. "I like your drawing." Rachel's voice pierced the fog in my head. "Mmm?" I mumbled, turning to face her. She had pulled her curly blond hair back behind her ears, and her sea green eyes seemed to pierce me. "The one that you're working on." She smile, revealing two rows of perfect teeth. Suddenly, I became fully awake. "You mean the one of the mountains?" I asked softly, careful not to attract attention. She nodded. I stared at her. "I my voice shook slightly, "haven't shown that to anyone. It's at my house. How do you-?" She chuckled, cutting me off. Slowly, she raised her hand and hit the desk, very softly. The rain stopped. The voice of my teacher vanished. The room was frozen in time. "I like your drawing." She repeated softly. "Let's leave it at that." "What's going on?" My mind raced. I raised my hand, slowly extending a finger to point at her. "You aren't human." I shouted. "Very bright." Again, she laughed. "You're right, I'm not human. I guess you could say I'm sort of superior. However, I'm on your side for now. Most of us aren't." "Us?!" I cried. "What do you mean, us?!" "There are many of my kind." She shrugged. "Most want to wipe your race from the earth, and create a new paradise." "This can't be happening." "Oh, but it is. We walk amongst you, unseen. The day is coming when many will make themselves visible." She paused, and a shadow flickered across her face. "Pray that you do not live to see that day." "Stop." I held up my hand. "If you really are a- oh, I don't know- a god, then why am I seeing this?" The smile that she gave then would haunt my memories over the coming weeks. "You have a beautiful soul, Felix, and I enjoy watching it."

I was going to be late for class. Again. I had no choice but to sprint. That little yellow sign seemed interesting. I slip. I try to catch myself on the lockers. Books go flying in the air. I feel my head hitting the wet floor and a blinding white light. The next time I open my eyes, a hall monitor is shaking my shoulder and looking at me like I'm an idiot. Why am I lying on the floor? Oh you know, just enjoying the spectacular view of fluorescent lights and green lockers. Ok, fine I will go to class. As I walk away with my head throbbing, I wonder why he's wearing a floating 4 over his head. Mr. Albright stops to give me a disappointed stare as I walk in late, he too is wearing a number over his head, a 2. He carries on the fascinating historical lesson as I turn to walk towards my desk near the wall. Either this is some weird teletubby practical joke with everyone wearing a number on their head, or I've finally lost it. They are all wearing numbers ranging from 1 to 8. Mr.Albright uses his ruler to point to the map above the board and it..... it just moves through the number 3 floating on his head. How..... What..... Joan raises her hand through her number 1. What is happening? I don't think this is a costume party that I wasn't told about anymore. Studying those numbers, I realize that the nicest person in class is a 1, while the class bullyasshole is an 8. Fuck you Jimmy, I want my hat back. The class is disrupted a second time by the arrival of a new student. Short, big round classes, a bowl cut. I bet his parents are Harry Potter fans from the way he looks. His number is a 10. I guess my theory that the number relates to danger level was utter bullshit. He has good timing, once Rickard is introduced to class; it's already time for lunch. Poor Rickard, Jimmy stands over him as he eats his sandwich screaming some inventive profanities. Bull dick fucker eater, a true poet that Jimmy. Rickard stands up and puts his hands up like he's under arrest. Jimmy laughs and as he does, his number changes to a 9. He throws a punch. My jaw hits the floor as Jimmy's unconscious body lands on the cafeteria floor, his number now a 0. Rickard, always the 10, just sits back down and continues eating. All around the room, complete silence is accompanied by numbers dropping. I get up with the remains of my lunch and walk towards the new kid. I bend down and retrieve my fucking hat. As I put it back on my head, I look this weird kid in the eyes and ask " You like Doritos? " He grins at me and as he does, I see my reflection grinning like an idiot in his metallic lunchbox and I see my number jump to two digits, to an 8.

Today was the day. Everyday before today I begged Captain Raw to let me intern with his squad of heroes. He always hesitated though because of his fear for my safety. He enjoyed my superpower, but the rest of the Hero Squad laughed at how mediocre it really was. I could not blow fire out my mouth like Inferno Boy or stop time like Rolex Man, but I knew I could contribute if I was given the chance. We met up at the official Hero Squad clubhouse and discussed the latest assignment: The Clone Master. Much like his villain name states, he could clone himself as much as he wanted. He had great speed and was trained in every martial art known to man of our time. He interrupted Super Cities' Channel 4 News to announce that he would be robbing every bank in a 50-mile radius at one time, and told the public and police force that there was nothing they could do to stop him! Little did he know that the Hero Squad had a new recruit. Me. "Sir Slippery." Okay I'm working on my Hero name bare with me please..... My power was that I could make people step wrong thus tripping them to their knees. That's right, I brought my enemies to their knees! Captain Raw finally saw potential in me today, and I was not going to let him down. Screw what the other heroes with obvious powers think about my mutation! We rolled out in the Hero Mobile and traveled to the nearest bank. It was time to play the waiting game..... Suddenly, an army of 30 - NO 40 clones dressed in chrome and black raced to the entrance! It was time to take care of business! "I'll stop time!" Shouted Rolex Man. "No you fool! Your power only lets you stop time at your current location, and the other clones will rob the rest of our town's banks while you freeze clocks!" Captain Raw spoke over him. Inferno Boy took a huge breath of air and exhaled a fiery blast towards the clones! But it was no use, their speed allowed them to avoid being fried. "Dammit! If only the rest of our squad wasn't sick today, we could stop these things!" Inferno Boy complained. Now was my time. I had never used my powers on a group of people this big before, only three or four enemies at a time! I closed my eyes and felt the energy of my mutation in my blood stream. It flowed fast, at the speed of a wild river. I was ready to attack! My eyes opened and I threw my hands in the direction of the clones! "BOOM BANG BAM CLUNK CRASH!" Half of the clone group stumbled together causing a 20-body pile-up in front of the bank! Captain Raw smiled at me and then slammed his fists into the ground, sending a wave of pressure through the earth resulting in a shower of clones above us. "Nice work kid!" He commended me. A single clone rose from the pile-up and gave us the most nasty and angered state I had ever seen. It was the Clone Master! He looked at me with a confused face next, and ran towards our group. "Again Sir Slippery!" Captain Raw directed me. "RAH!" I tripped him! This time he face planted in front of Inferno Boy. He was shortly after burnt to a crisp, and brought into a maximum prison cell on our Villain Island Lock up. I had stopped my first villain with the help of the Hero Squad, who learned to accept me despite my minor mutation; being able to trip people.

From the forest apes, carving trees and sowing cloth to place atop their thinning fur, to the great wolves, large as bears upon hind legs, carving claims of the herds they follow across the great open plains, to soaring, roaring dragons, making their valley kingdoms, jealously guarded. From the Avians, making nests over lakes and seas, ever watching the surface of the water for new prey, to the lizards, striking banners and armies, clad is sparkling, black metal armor as they march across land after land in their endless pursuit of greatness.

The word "Don't" was carved on the table, next to a pile of bones. I shouldn't be doing this, I thought. But I had come to far to stop now. "Where does this go to?" I said as I picked it up to get a better look, and at that point the table split open and collapsed into the wall, leaving only a hole in the ground. I was in awe to see that a gigantic console rose up from the black emptiness. As I stepped towards it, I realized that that was what the lever was for. I slammed it into, what looked like, a giant USB port. Suddenly, words came on the screen. "Don't" it repeated, over and over. I was scared and wanted to go home. But we've come to far. So I pulled the lever, and the countdown started. 00:01:00. Oh no, oh no, oh no. Yes, oh yes. Why would you do this? We said no more adventures. But I like adventuring. I like controlling you guys. I like hearing your death curdling screams over and over as you destroy the universe again and again for the sake of'adventure.' What do you mean? The last thing I saw before the flash was the words on the console reading'Don't.'

The Apple What is a God? I've always wondered, Is there one or many more? Is God just something we made up, To make up for our flaws? Does God follow me around, Everywhere I go? Can God provide the answers, To all I need to know? How is God supposed to sound? Does he even have a voice? When I have a hard decision, Can he help me make a choice? Is he always watching me? Does he know now where I am? Can God give me guidance, When I find myself in a jam? I searched for him, high and low, But he was nowhere to be found. And still it tugged away at my soul, There must be a God around! Then the answer dawned upon me, As I started to text a friend. And I slowly stared in horror..... At the iPhone in my hand.

I've seen some freaks in my day but this one? Well, he sure as hell takes the cake. Scars on his face. Pale skin. Eyes so yellow you'd swear he had jaundice. He kept laughing to himself like someone kept telling him jokes but, I was the only other person in the bar. And his breath. Oh god his breath. It was horrible. And you could smell it from 10 feet away. It was as though he had just eaten a truck load of chimichangas. All he would drink is Canadian beer. After a while he looked at me and started talking about killing some guy named Slade. Something about the guy stealing his style. Anyway, so this guy is here smelling like a homeless guy covered in rotten blood and in walks this clown. Literally. A fucking, clown. So this clown sits next to the first guy and starts in on him. "Dear god, what sewer did you climb out of?" "The same one you pulled that suit from." "HA! Good one. You got good humor kid but to be a humor pro, like me, you got ta smile more." The clown grabbed a knife, put it in the poor fucks mouth and sliced a giant smile through his face. The guy dropped to the ground. I was up against the back counter of the bar, a bit shocked by the severe display of violence, when the clown slaps the counter and orders a shot of whiskey. After he downs it he looks to his left and there sits the first guy. I was in shock. No cuts on his. No new scars. He just sat there sipping on his beer as if it had never happened. "Didn't I just slice your mouth open?" The clown was in disbelief "What? Oh yeah. It happens." This agitated the clown. So much so that he pulled a gun and shot the bastard in the head. "HAHAHAHAHAHA! We got him that time, didn't we, old chap?" And just like that the fucker gets up again. This went on for hours. The clown killing the guy and him getting back up. The clown was losing it. He was furious and erupting with laughter each time the guy died and came back. I was going to do something but after a while, I hate to admit it, I was entertained. After some time had passed a third weirdo walks in dressed like a bat, calls the clown "The Joker" and spouts off about the clown needing to go to some asylum. The clown practically begged to go stating that nothing could be worse than whatever it was that was happening in my bar. After the bat and the clown left the other guy got up off te floor, paid his tab, and left. Craziest thing I've ever seen.

I can see again, another day to myself. Nothing is different, same brick wall in my way. Now and then someone passes by, but they always seem to make an effort to ignore me, shielding their eyes as they pass by. Two hundred and seventy nine times I've lost my sight, Two hundred and eighty times I've seen. Seven of those times were different, seven of those times I wasn't alone. Always the same couple, they never spoke to me, but I enjoyed their company. They would always come in close, shoulder-to-shoulder, exchange gifts, take a step back, smile, say a few words and split paths. I never see the gifts, but I can tell by the smile on their faces that they're both happy. I want them to be happy, I'm worried that if they aren't, I wont see them as much. If not them, then who will keep me company. These friends of mine who's faces I try to remember. I only see a few of their features each time, leaving me excited for the next. It's all I look forward to. An eighth time, they are here again. " Hello my friends " I want to say, but I won't distract them. I wonder what gifts they've brought each other this time. Again shoulder to shoulder, a step back, no smile, a sudden movement, a shattering noise. I can not see. One splits, but the other stays. He is silent, but I can hear him. Has he decided to stay? I wonder what I'll see tomorrow.

"Hey! Hey!" I clang the corrugated steel siding of my cart. Wielding my tongs like lecturer's pointer, I gesture to the sign celotaped to the back of my toaster-oven. "No fightin' an' no powahs. Or no hot pastrami." Neither one wanting to lower their guard first, The Specialist and his nemesis Jack-O-All kept brows low and dukes high. "Now Richard, I can't let Jack-O..." I give the tongs a resolute snap and gesture to the sign again. "B-but justice never sleeps in..." "Yeah? Well if justice wan'stah eat, no fightin' an' no powahs." I flip the pastrami on the griddle so rough, you could swear they saw the technicolored'Pow!' "An' the name's Rick, get it right." The Specialist lowers his fists, prompting Jack to go in for the strike. Another thunderous snap of my tongs halts him in his track. "Listen up Mac!" "Uh, it's Jack..." "Whatevah! I got two rules! No fightin' an'..." "Yes, yes, and no powers. However I, Jack-O..." "It's late right?" I'Slam!' some onion on the griddle. "Well, yes..... But Villainy also never slee..." "An' it's real cold out heah on the streets right?" I'Wham!' some peppers down onto the cook-top. "I suppose there is a bit of an Autumn chill tonight." He murmurs. "An' all ya really want right now is a hot pastrami sammich an' tah go home after a long day right?" The toaster-oven timer dings and I'Biff!' two hot rolls out into separate paper boats. Jack-O-All's shoulders go slack and he let's out a sigh. "Yes that does sound nefarious right about now." The Specialist mutters in agreement. I layer in the pastrami, onions, peppers, cheese. As I slide the boats across the swing-up counter, The Specialist starts patting around for his wallet. "Oh darn-it-all! I must have left my cash in my other unitard." "Don't stress, I'll cover you this time. You did suggest it and all." Jack-O-All said pulling out a crisp twenty. I took the bill and held it up to the street light, no watermark. "Fake." I'Thwacked!' the dollar down. The Specialist snapped it up and shot Jack a cross look. "Haha, oops." Jack said, feigning innocence. "This one should be fine." After it checked out I slip it into my lockbox and start counting out change. "Just keep it, my treat." Said The Specialist as he takes the sandwiches. Jack-O-All indignantly swipes his sandwich away. They both mumble a'thanks' and walk off into the night. As I turn off my griddle for the night I hear them talking like old friends, through bites of food. Good? Evil? None of that matters on a cold night with a hot pastrami.

My power had never amounted to much. I was popular in college, but compared to people who could fly and teleport, or teansform into giant animals, you can see free refils isn't all that great. Apart from those parties in my twenties, I wasn't very well-liked by my super-peers. I was looked down upon because of the lameness of my power. I always lived comfortably, though. While publicly revealing powers tends to ruin your life if you can't threaten to just smite the haters, I found an easy way to make money: I opened a distillery. With one barrel of fine scotch, made in a state of the art home distillery, I was set. I eventually invested and improved the quality, and could replicate any age after some time. My brand, Draoidh (Druidwizard in Scottish Gaelic) became one of the most popular single malts in Great Britain. It all changed when my facility was inspected by the Committee for Traditional Scottish Exports. I was discovered, and though they didn't like it, what I was doing was perfectly legal. Also by this point I was pretty rich, which tends to help. The change came when I was approached by a scientific committee from the United States. They had learned of my power and wanted to employ me in a plan to provide free, energy-rich, clean-burning fuel to the world. The job was simple. I just had to refill the container of this new fuel they had invented. The original amount that they had made in a lab, after testing, was 50mL. I started there, filling and refilling larger and larger containers until I was doing massive tanks, a very physically straining task. Luckily these scientists were paid the perfect amount that they were satisfied, with their humanitarian drive intact, and didn't want to privatize the operation for profit. And that, kids, is how I saved the world.

They say curiosity killed the cat, but here I am, holding this tail, and there still isn't any blood. Just a sweet little kitten, purring away while my new laptop finishes installing its latest update. Thanks, Microsoft. After what seems like an eternity, I'm finally able to plug my cat's tail into my computer. It only takes just a moment of jiggling it in, what with all the fur getting in the way, but soon enough, I'm watching in awe as my computer informs me it's installing the relevant drivers for whatever I've just plugged in. I was sure it might not recognize the technology, but not only does it..... it's already installing an update! Talk about a buttery smooth transition. "Huh. Hey Fluffy, this works better than my iPhone on here. How about that?" The kitten at my side responded by pawing at the offending phone innocently, knocking it off the couch and onto our hardwood floor. I winced as a tinkle of glass followed. Thanks, Apple.

"That's bull-shi But before Mike could finish his sentence, God snapped his fingers and was gone. Mike was dismayed with emotion. "Mike started to bang his head against the floor and scream "Not my pizza rolls, you savage!" Mike's fish then jumped out of it's fishbowl and started to smack Mike on the face repeatedly with his fin "I'm gon na flush you like you did to my brothers!" The fish then began to force Mike down the toilet, flushing him. "GOODBYE CRUEL WORLD!" Mike screamed as he was flushed away. So anyways, be careful what you wish for or your fish might just flush you down your own toilet.

We all know you're the one who keeps taking all the fucking paper clips home you dumb skank. Are you trying to use them to hold your family together, I'm sure you're running out of ideas by now?" Before I could even look to Libby a ninja star was poking out of Ulyssas thigh and 3 shots came from somewhere in the room. The man was a fucking legend. All legends must end though, and a quick shock from my tazer baton was more than enough to ensure that I would be the one to end his. After removing my blade, I spun to meet a head on rush from Tiffany the scheming bitch had this coming and flung her over my shoulder through the glass window. A quick look around showed that Ulyssa had done well despite her injuries, a mess of clipboards and briefcases lay in her apparent path and Steve stuck beneath her as she struggled to point the gun toward his head. A few shots insured that Libby would give me no problems as I walked through the madness that engulfed what was currently Steves office. Steve, that post-it-note-leaving 5-foot 2-inch bastard. He didn't even see me before my hands were at his throat. I was sure I had had him before his hammer bashed into my knee, we tumbled in a heap with him ending on top of me, the exacto knife popping from the tip of his pen. The man truly did deserve his title as the director of the board I held him inches from my throat when the buzzer rang. The clamor around the room began to cease and Steve was wearing that shit eating grin again. I'm never going to get this damn promotion.

Age 1: He picks his teeth idly, it's strange to watch a skeleton pick its teeth. Cabbage, I think. I have a permanent smile, but I watch him, so tiny, crawl on the floor. Age 2: He killed the dog. I don't think he knew what he was doing. He laid his head on the dog for a day until the dog disappeared. I'm blaming Alaine for that. He didn't seem bothered. Age 5: Touching flowers wilts them. He doesn't understand, but he touches them nonetheless. Edit: his left hand kills, his right hand revives. He asks me about the dog. I shake my head, he's gone to a better place. But I've never seen this'better place' - I.... feel bad for telling him this. I feel.... I feel? Age 6: School. Where do we send him? Angel, demon, each have their own education but where do we send him? Arin and I decide to split out duties, we educate him at home. Age 7: "Why can't I go to school with the others?" A difficult conversation ensues, he locks himself in his room. Age 8: Halloween. Not easy to find a grim reaper costume with angel wings. We do what we can. No one understands, but he's happy with the candy nontheless. Age 13: It's not always easy explaining why your son's touch killed his crush. I'm more worried about him than the victim. He's locked himself up in his room. It's been three days. Age 16: No cloak, but a suit. Black, white undershirt, red tie. I am almost envious, he's so handsome. She laughs and kisses his forehead. Good luck, my boy. His first day of high school. Age 17: Career handouts. His is blank. Both of us sit with him and wait. We say nothing, simply wondering what our boy would like to do. His world is waiting, but he doesn't know. "You're of both worlds." she says. "You can do whatever you want." He looks up at his mother, it doesn't matter his eyes are black, you see emotion in them anyway. Age 18: REAPER TRAINING! I couldn't be happier. Donning his cloak, I look at my boy.... my sad boy. I shake my head. "This is not want you want, is it." He looks up at me with eyes filled with tears. I already know what he wants. Smiling, I lean down and rest my forehead against his. "Go tell your mother. Be the angel you are meant to be, boy." I grip her fingers tight as he ascends, his wings growing bright as he flies upward.

"Why did you do this?" God asked. "Well," the Oracle said, "I got tired of the greeks constantly writing about me." "So you changed the entire culture so that people would constantly write about me?" "Yup" the Oracle said. "Do you have any idea how much trouble you've caused me?" God asked. "Oh, come on, it's not that bad." "Every day! Every single day! Someone comes on to rWritingPrompts and puts up a prompt about god! Every. Me-Damned. Day." The oracle shrugged. "The least you can do," God said, "is tell me if it'll ever let up." "Outlook..... not so good."

I sat up and stretched to loosen my stiff muscles. I looked around and watched the hatches of twenty other pods pop open, cool air falling over the sides. Men and women, all naked, got out and grabbed the clothes in the container next to them. A middle aged man, graying at the temples, approached me with my clothes. " How are you Jason? " He asked politely as he handed over the clothes. I heard the slight whine of a servo motor and realized the " man " was actually an android, assigned to pilot the ship while we slept. As I began to take in my surroundings, I realized this was not my ship. None of the people on here were familiar. And most disturbingly, my parents were nowhere to be found. Panic crept into the back of my mind. " Where are my parents? " I asked the android uneasily. The android made a face which passed for perplexed and turned and looked at the human captain of the ship, a balding black man with a bit of a belly. " Hi son, " he said, " My name is Fred Zelon. I'm the human captain of this ship. Now this is going to be difficult to hear and I am sorry to have to be the one to tell you this. Your ship was destroyed during one of our periodic exits from FTL. You were the only pod we could salvage before we had to jump again. " He put his hand on my shoulder. I shook it off and turned angrily to him. " Why did we leave my parents behind? Why did we leave anyone behind? And what the hell even happened to the ship in the first place? " More questions flooded my brain but before I could say anymore, the android spoke. " It is not ' what happened'to the ship, but more ' who happened'to the ship, " he said cryptically. " What does that mean? " I demanded of him, but he just turned and looked at Fred again. " We're running son, " Fred said. I wanted to ask what we were running from but an elderly woman beat me to it. Probably for the better anyway. I was shaking with rage and fighting off a deep sadness that I could feel in the back of my mind. As she asked her question, the ship decelerated, indicating an exit from FTL. " From them, " the android said and pointed out the window. feed back appreciated:)

After living through epidemics, natural disasters and merciless wars, we've become a dull blade, I feel we've been walking through a jungle with no end. Restrictions and limitation set upon our previous bodies lifted, we've become something less, no we've become more than simple beings whose only goal was to survive. Despite our self proclaimed immortality we never achieve or reach out to our now estranged world. We've lost our purpose, no reason to struggle and fight. Material wealth has accumulated to a point where we do not need to lift a finger for ourselves and it has left us docile. We're no better than animals left to rest in it's cage. it was the struggle and fight that put a light in our eyes, we dull in convenience and frail in comfort. So I ask you to hand over the key and let me walk away. I wish to travel the world once more, I'd rather be burned than buried, my ashes to urns have them carried. They say finding your soulmate is one of the best things you can do in your life. The joy and happiness it brings into your life is incomparable to everything else - nothing even comes close. When I met her for the first time, I didn't know that my whole life would revolve around her. She was just another girl in one of my classes, and yet I found myself talking to her every day, dreaming of her, writing down her likes and dislikes. Before her, I'd never even bothered to learn or remember someone's favorite color, or flower, or anything for that matter. I lived my life for myself; I now live for her. Within a year, we had become an item - inseparable, my love for her was unparalleled - the stuff of legends. In five years, I found myself deeper in love than I'd ever even known possible. Our love blossomed and we had a long marriage and life together. I am old now, decades have passed. I miss her every day.

No one believed him, but he felt different. Really different. He could feel the sky, the wind. And he always felt the urge to shout at that confounded dog, but he couldn't risk the rage of his getting-on-for-seven foot owner. The traffic jam had been going on for hours. He was late. Goddamnit, it was his first job interview after the accident. He drummed his fingers against the steering wheel, glancing jitteringly to the left, to the right and in the rear-view mirror, looking for an opening in the endless wall of tin cars. Finally, the column started moving. He was going to be late. And, they stopped again, quite abruptly. Goddamnit. Thump! "That's it, That's fucking it," he thought to himself, getting out of the car. The other one didn't even have the decency to get out and apologize, the fucker. Out of sheer rage, without even thinking of what he was saying, he shouted, with a voice he didn't even know he had in him: "Yooooou're a FOOOOL." He stopped, shocked. That wasn't his voice. It sounded wrong, as if he had a big burly viking speaking out of his mouth with a heavy accent. The windscreen had broken. Had he just done that? With his voice? All of a sudden, something started going wrong. Really wrong. It was as if the world was falling towards the car. It made him think of that bloody Dali painting, the one with the melting clocks he had in his bathroom. Then he felt himself falling forwards, sucked into a blindingly white void. Where the hell was he? Some sort of cart? He could definitely hear the clopping of horses hooves. And Jesus! it was cold. Yes, he could see now. Maybe he was dreaming. He was in a cart with one blond guy, a redhead and a fancily dressed-guy with a gag on his mouth, somewhere like in Alaska, on a forest trail. Hmm, his hands were bound. All of their hands were bound. What were they, some sort of criminals? And the clothes..... Looked lke something out of one of those crazy cuzplayers or whatever, those conventions where they all got dressed up like their bloody game characters. Sure was an interesting dream, no doubt about it. "Hey, you! You're awake!." The blond guy looked at him. He had an accent, like a..... Glaswegian? Ah, he wasn't good at recognising them, all europeans sounded alike to him. "You were trying to cross the border, right? Walked right into that Imperial ambush, same as us, and that thief over there." What? Ok, this was getting strange. He supposed the thief was the redhead, he looked scruffy and kind of guilty. But it was the fancy guy that really interested him. He didn't care for that bollocks they where saying about Rorikstead and Hammerfell..... Goddamned nerd lingo. His daughter had given him enough before she left, in 2007. 21 and still playing games, ha! At her age, he was already working his ass off, on building sites.
