"All those years?" I was crying. "I missed you so much. I hated everybody. I took out my loss for you on them. Now you come back. Finally." "Yes," she said firmly. "I promised I would always love you. I have fought everything to save the people I found myself amongst and when we made it they wanted to make me queen or something but I refused. I didn't want to govern anybody or anything. I wanted them to be free and that's self rule to me and I just wanted to come home to you." "But it has been so long and it hurt so much," I stared into her eyes. "You might not like what I have become." "We can fix anything," she insisted. "I set the space ship to trace you and bring me straight to you. You are everything to me and now I have you again." "But I'm changed," I was holding my head in my hands. "You deserve better. Much better." "You aren't married," she looked suddenly worried. "Or in a relationship or something are you?" "No, No," I said, "There could never be anybody but you. I could never love anybody else." "So what have you done with your life?" she brightened up. "You seem to have a pretty nice place here." I drew a deep breath. She had to know. "I am James the Imperator," I said. "I am Absolute ruler of the whole Earth. Well. All that is left after my wars of conquest."

You must go on. "What are you going to do if I don't open it?" Tiny vents in the walls and ceiling silently open up and pump in an odorless gas. The man starts feeling lightheaded. It's time for him to lay down for a bit. This short day has been taxing on him. This'll just be a quick nap, he says to himself. The man in the lab coat rolled his eyes as he read the message in the envelope. "Cause of Death: Not reading this message" He gave the body on the ground in front of him a swift kick. "You stupid, stubborn asshole! I can't do anything with this!" The development of the machine had been plagued with delays and now it was going to take forever to properly test and calibrate it. With the recent crackdown on cloning it was becoming very difficult to find reliable test subjects. Judging by the salty temperaments of the last few subjects, it was clear that suppliers were beginning to scrape the bottom of the barrel. "This machine is going to be the death of me!"

I got the call again. This one was a doosey that even he bomb squad elite couldn't crack. They always call me to get the job done, the only problem with that however, is I have idea what I'm doing. I'm rushed over to the scene by an officer. "There's only five minutes left!" Screams out the officer in charge. I can see the panic written all over his face. He wasn't prepared for this, none of them were. Not even te bomb squad, hell even I wasn't. The closer I got the louder the ticking was. I wasn't even in bomb gear but I've also never failed to defuse one of these confusing contraptions. I see the timer, just four and a half minutes left. What did I do with the last bomb? Pull some wires out or something. I'll try that again. The remaining time on the timer is now half of what it was. This is bad, why is it always me that gets stuck doing the job I have no clue of how to do? I'm gon na try something new, I'm going to kick the bomb. I stand up, pull my leg back and swing my leg forward. The bomb flew towards the closest building and hit the wall breaking into pieces. Well that was lucky, it didn't explode and the ticking has stopped. I motion with my hands that it was safe. The bomb squad comes in and retrieves the bomb while I head back to the scene commander. "How did you know that would work?" He asked puzzled. "Lucky guess." I smirked. All in a days work for not knowing what the hell you are doing. I see a pub across the street and head towards it. I could use a drink.

"Ok everybody freeze! " , yells Officer Darrell Park. The handful of people around Officer Darrell in the subway stopped moving and looked at one another. "Quick do it! One of them has a bomb! " , the voice repeated again. Darrell looked at the five people around him. It was a homeless man, a man in a suit, a women holding a baby wrapped in sheets, and a young couple. "Let the games begin," the voice said. "What did you say to me? " , the man in the suit turned and said to the homeless man. The man in the suit threw a punch and hit the homeless man in the jaw causing him to fall. Officer Darrell stepped between them, but at the same time the couple started arguing and the women slapped her boyfriend across the face. Another officer who happened to be in the subway stepped in between them, but while holding both of them back Darrell's fellow officer turned to him and said "You did what to my wife?" He started walking toward Darrell and put his hand on his holster. Darrell stepped away from the homeless man and rich man and backed away. He caught a glance at the women in the middle of the arguing group. She looked at him and smiled while revealing the contents of the wrappings. What should have been a baby was actually C4. Darrell tried to scream, but the bomb went off first. First story on this sub so yeah. Feedback is helpful!

I'd danced between them, curdling their souls like a toxic poison within myself. I'd wooed and whispered toothy notes of passion, cooing springing melodies of love. I'd wrapped my web around both of them until no one but myself could unravel them from their delusions of what they viewed as perfect. I had underestimated them. Death tore through my lies like acid through flesh, ripping and tearing them apart until nothing but my fearful mind was displayed. Frostbite numbed me and turned my skin blue and black. Death demanded my fingers, and then my toes. Since I was of deceit and hate, I deserved no fingers to write my spite with, nor any toes to lift my soul up. Time screamed at me till nothing but my vision remained. Deafness was granted to those who would twist others to their will, using their poisonous tongue to hiss lies and spread the contorted words of others. They refused to touch me. Not afraid so much. Of revulsion, more so. Timeless and without Death, I walked upon Earth. Death did not greet me when I stepped upon a trip mine in the early age of World War 2. Death did not greet me when the concrete of the twin buildings crushed me into the pavement in 2001. Death did not greet me when I was electrocuted as a convict. Death never met me. Time wore on, but not to me. Time did not touch me. Like a snake to a flame, Time merely curled around me. A bubble, invisible to all else but there all the same. It wrapped around me, suffocating but not too much so. Beautiful golden wraps hovered just on the edge of meeting my skin, but never, did they ever touch. Isolation. Something that grew to be something of a comfort in my five centuries of living. At first, it'd been harsh. Like a slap to the face or a chill up my spine, it'd hurt. So long I'd been weaving my lies and hurtful deceit upon my two lovers. For that all to be gone in a second, mortal and lost in a world ravaged by hungry beasts in pursuit of power and money. Much to say... I'd grown lost in a mind trapped behind the bars of insanity.

Dr. Jackal stared at his report on the podium as the press found their seats. He continued to question the sanity of what they found. It seems impossible, science fiction, yet the evidence was on the podium in front of him. As his watch struck 2:30, he cleared his throat. "Good afternoon ladies and gentlemen. NASA has called this conference to disclose new information on the planet Mars." The press stared at him, jotting every word on various devices. "With the successful launch of the deep red explorer, we have received new information on the history of the red planet as of 8:20 this morning. After boring down into Mars, we have discovered..." He trailed his words off as he stared up. After a few seconds he lowered his head and uttered the ending to his sentence. "human-like inscriptions." The press room exploded into a wave of noise.

He walked, holding the bundle as he approached the grave. The man looked down into the grave he had dug. It was a sad day for a funeral, and here he was, alone. Rain fell quicker now, turning the pile of dirt nearby into mud. He did not move from the spot, shoveling heap upon heap of the now muddy mixture into the hole. He remembered when he first met her. She was a stray, a young mutt that he had encountered on the road. It was long ago, when he first started to travel that he met her. She wagged her tail as he stood there, and he smiled. He knelt down, and she walked shyly forward, her tail wagging. They had been friends since that very moment, and she walked away from him, just once. She walked into the ditch, and he saw it. He saw her old master, flies buzzing around him as he lay in the ditch. She whined, looking up at him with those brown eyes that he had grown to know so well. The disease had taken many. But it had not taken her. That was an oddity, but then again, so was their meeting. He kept walking, and he heard the familiar patter of her paws on the ground behind him. He smiled, for the first time in a long time. They had many adventures together, wandering through the decrepit cities.... Meeting people. Hell, he even remembered when she had puppies, and he paused his long session of wandering just to stay there with her. He had played with her puppies, and watched them be parted out in that community. He thought he had finally found love, in that small community, with his little companion. He felt his anger boil over inside, shaking as he patted the grave with his hands. He stood, knowing that he would take his revenge. Those idiots had gone too far, and it wasn't just his dog anymore. They had taken his friends, his new family. He was just sitting there when they rolled up in their gasoline guzzling vehicles, and they started in on his little community, as they always did. He was walking now, lost in his thoughts as he did. It had all happened when they stopped in front of his worn home, and he looked out the window, watching them carefully. Their old motorcycles guzzled more gas than he could imagine. His daughter sat in the garden in front of the home, nearly 14. She was tending to the garden, and they looked to his dog. She wagged her tail, barking at them, and they began to talk to her. He knew what they wanted. They wanted the dog. The argument grew heated outside, and he walked quickly to the drawer. Gunshots rang out, and he ran outside. He awoke, bruised and beaten, but otherwise unharmed. All of them lied, his daughter choking in a pool of her own blood. He clamped a hand onto the wound, the bullet had gone through her neck. She was trying to speak, but as she choked her last breath away on a clot of blood, the only sound that came out was a scream. He lifted it out of the drawer, feeling it. He tested the stock, wondering if it was the right choice. He loaded it. When was his birthday again? 1983? He was old, nearly sixty now. But, he finally thought he found happiness in a world stricken with violence, disease, and greed. He walked, his feet nearly bleeding in their thick wool socks. He had walked for miles, and finally reached the old factory. The weapon weighed steadily in his hand, and he stormed towards the door. He did not care if he was shot. Gunshots rang out. Ten minutes later, enough to end a life, he came out. He smiled, thinking of the graves he had dug at home. He would never live to see his daughter marry a young man. But as he held his side, the wound bleeding. The disease had taken all that he had at one point. He was walking, his side wrapped up. He had not ate or drank for several days, and his scraggly beard covered his entire face. He passed a puddle, kneeling to drink from it, and he saw a reflection of himself. He reminded himself of one of the diseased dogs that he used to see, the ones that starved as the disease ate them from the inside. He understood their pain now. It wasn't the disease itself that consumed him. He was completely immune to it, or so he had thought.He heard a growling noise, looking up to spot a dog, not unlike his old mutt. "She used to be my best friend, you know." He said deliriously. The mutt barked, and raced towards him. Gunfire rang out. He kept walking.

Four days. Four miserable, exhausting days I spent climbing this mountain. I ran out of food early on the third day and my stomach wouldn't shut up about it. I left my wife and children behind 4000 miles away so I could fly to a nearby village, hike to this miserable mountain, and nearly die climbing it, all to ask the great sage for the answers I seek. It'll all be worth it soon, though. I can see the top. There they are! The great sages! Wait a second..... There was only supposed to be one. They don't look very sagely. They all sit cross legged and straight backed staring into the distance just like sage does. At least, I think that's what a sage does. Sure, some have beards and some of those beards are grey, but they aren't long enough. I suppose that's not really a rule, but- my thoughts are interrupted. "How do we get down?" They ask in unison. What a stupid question. Surely they are just testing me. I turn around to gesture at the winding path I had just come from only to find that it was no longer there. Suddenly, I didn't know how to get down either. There's something about there up here that makes me okay with that..... I find a free space between two great sages, cross my legs, and have a seat.

I try to be happy, really I do. After all, I have the best job in the world. I take a great deal of satisfaction in giving these wingless, featherless creatures the ability to experience life from 15,000 feet in the air. But today is different. Thomas packed me with the utmost care and concern for my well being. That's why I like him. Always looking out for the little guy. Not even five minutes later, his business partner Rupert approached me with a knife. I tried to scream out for help, but no one could hear me. He cut two big slits through my beautiful red canopy before packing me back into my nylon cocoon. When Thomas came back to get me, he put me onto his shoulders, clipped the buckles, and tightened down the straps. I tried again to scream, to give him some kind of warning but alas, the great gods of the sky never thought to give me a mouth. There was nothing I could have done. After Thomas leapt from the plane, his giddiness turned to horror when he pulled the rip cord, expecting to slow to a nice glide over the landing zone. Instead, he and I hit the ground still traveling at 120 miles an hour.

His leaving of the Bureau came as a surprise for many. He was in the most enchanted position with no where to go but up and he seemingly just walked out. His coworkers didn't really care that much though, as Seamus had never really been liked by many. He had worked hard at what he did..... and yet it felt as if he hadn't put any effort into it at all, which was a concept not understood by many. In his position he could cast some more of the obscure spells without a second thought and could finally feel safe to dabble in the realm of the truly arcane without the fear of a deficiency reaction, a luxury to most. To Seamus though he didn't care about traditional magic. He had always kept what little life outside work he had separate, and no one, even if they had known, would have understood anyway. His wife had recently developed a sickness that nothing could cure, and he felt that spending the the last months of her life with her would be more magical than anything he could obtain at work.

I was eight when I got lost here. We were playing hide-and-seek, a game I was horrible at and a game I was determined to win at. As Sarah counted down and we all scurried away as fast as our feet could carry us. I ran to my dad's office. No one was allowed there, no one dared, no one would look for me there. Before I knew it I was standing in front of the wooden door. The door I was never allowed past. The door my dad had forgotten to lock today. And it was at this point that I hesitated. I forced my hand to reach for the door knob and it was probably the slowest action I had ever taken. The cold metal against my skin surprised me so much I nearly pulled my hand away but at that moment something came over me. It was now or never. I tore open the door in I went. The room was simple and yet, somehow, beautiful. A large wooden desk stretched along the far wall under a bay window with the curtains drawn. A lavish chair sat in front of it and the walls were lined with books from floor to ceiling in old dark shelving. I wanted to explore it all, I wanted to see what had always been hidden from me. It was the'here I come' cry jerked me back into reality. I was here to hide, here to play a game, here to win. I looked over the room and wondered where a good spot would be and was immediately annoyed at how everything was in plain view. This wouldn't be easy. It was then that I noticed one of the curtains hide something other than the just the windows. I rushed over, planning on squeezing behind them. I tore them aside and there stood a mirror. Disappointment spread through me as I realized I wouldn't fit. And my reflection echoed the anger that crossed my face. I noticed how silly I looked and laughed. Mimicing me it laughed, I raised my right hand to scratch my head and it raised it's right hand to do the same. Then it smiled. And against my will I smiled too. At that moment I noticed I couldn't move. The boy in the mirror bowed at me and I bowed in turn. He said something, and my lips echoed,'Thank you.' The curtain dropped back in front of the mirror and everything went dark and I was all alone.

Tom began to slowly open his eyes, then jolted upright with a sudden gasp of breath. He was in the middle of the woods, and the autumn leaves were stuck to his naked body by a mixture of dried blood and mud. Horrified, Tom clambered to his feet and tried his hardest to brush off the nauseating muck. His stomach churned grossly in failure - unable to completely rid himself of the filth - and he heaved, throwing up an unrecognizable, bloody meal. Tom fell to his knees, shivering in the cold. He saw the droplets of blood dribbled across the forest floor half a dozen feet away. The knot in his gut tightened, but he rose - feeling an innate responsibility to see the carnage with his own eyes, to be absolutely positive - and followed the trail. At first, it was difficult, then it became sickeningly easy as the dribble became less sparse. He fell against a tree, overwhelmed with relief at the sight of the dead deer. At the sight of its scattered intestines and torn jugular, he thought, suddenly mortified. Oh god, next time, you won't be so lucky. It's gon na be a kid next time. Next time, you're gon na cut a kid to ribbons.

Chaos. It was as simple as challenging the premise, though proven long ago, that chaos existed. Edward Lorenz'work in the field was upended with a complex, yet elegant computer algorithm devised by a student in Bangladesh. The basic principal that a bouncing ball's exact placement in a spce could not be accurately calculated after its third bounce was disproven by simply tweaking the known parameters with what Rahhman had named the Rah, or sun effect. In laymen terms, a single set of all known parameters could not predict chaos, however, a second set of known parameters from an adjacent, though unrelated, event, when equated together, led to the answer for both. So the question that surfaced was why? The evidence the algorithm worked transferred to all facets of science. For the first time, when the algorithm was applied at a macro level, and then projected further, even weather could be predicted. To answer the why, one had only to work the equation backwards. Not only could weather be predicted, the inverse was also true, and that led all the way down to Einstein's greatest " blunder, " the God particle - a very simple root formula for all things matter. The exact same formula, when worked backwards, was discovered for everything. What was of particular interest was that it was complex. Clearly there was thought behind it, and so two theories emerged, one that sited God as the origin, and the other that someone or something was the creator, but the convergent thought that a creator existed was not disputed. Professor Darko from MIT didn't subscribe, or particularly care, with either school of thought, only that the God particle held a key to finding out Root. After all, no matter the origin of the creator, its formula was very likely used beyond the sphere of our own existence, and there began the Origin project. At first, Origin was a distributed computing experiment that would find correlations along " generational " progressions, and while there were some ups and downs, Darko turned his attention back to weather. With macro level progression, recorded points, and connections, he discovered artificially changing a variable to throw the simulation off, only affected the projected weather temporarily, and it would eventually return to total accuracy. Intrigued further by the phenomenon, he created a program to work all known current weather trends in reverse, but at a much accelerated event. That program survived longer than he did - 77 more years in fact. On September 19th, 2083, the computer program reached a point with so few variables left, that it was expected to simply terminate, but instead it continued. The data produced was unlike anything one would expect from a glorified weather program. A single string emerged: 6EQUJ5. Fisher, an MIT post graduate student, took the Rha algorithm, and used 6EQUJ5 as Root, and ran the program again, except moving forward, and on modern day hardware. The results were remarkable. An entire universe was simulated. Mountains rose. Oceans rose and dried up. Civilizations appeared and were extinguished. One Civilization, in honor of Rahhman and Darko, was dubbed the Darkrah, a people that lived for millennia, without an end in sight. Fisher, and the scientific community at large, witnessed, via computer terminals and interpretive texts, they had found a way to capture long lost worlds within tiny computer capsules that would reset their lives in simulated universes. It was here that The Bridge was found - a common backplane that connected the creators to those they created. It was simply a matter of sending a message back along The Bridge. On December 25th, 2091, " 6EQUJ5 " was sent back across the bridge. There was an deafening silence for approximately 30 seconds, and then a reply: HELLO WORLD

"And the process is now complete." I heard that before I could open my eyes. They felt as if they'd been cemented shut for so long. Light blinded me from all angles. I felt a sickly ringing in my ears that was slowly subsiding. "Patient vitals seem normal...." I listened to the voice as I tried to avert my eyes from the light. I then realized something crucial, I couldn't breathe properly..... I tried grasping for air but to no avail. Oh shit, I'm going to die like this. I began struggling in place, only to realize I'd been in some kind of weightless suspension since the beginning. I suddenly rolled over, the shift adding more pressure on my lungs. The feeling's worse now; almost crushing. This must be it. "Completing reanimation in 3..... 2....... 1...." The blow to my back made me open up and vomit violently. I could only watch the synthetic fluid hit the floor in a large puddle. I could breathe again..... I could breathe again?? The last thing I remember was that truck coming right at us. Where am I? What is this? Why am I vomiting fluid? I could only ask these to myself as I lost consciousness. I came back again, only to realize I'd been strapped to a bed. A man sat nearby in anticipation, his lab coat bristling quietly as he sat. "Hello there, don't be alarmed. I'm here to let you know that you're back from the dead. Don't panic." I panicked alright. Who wouldn't? I asked him where my family was. He just shook his head, and explained, they had no way of tracing them until arrival. "Why'd you bring me back man?" I asked eventually. "It's what we do." He sighed, "Bio-organic resuscitation. We bring you back from death to live your life here." "Okay, that doesn't make much sense, but okay." I nodded, "I got one question though?" "Go ahead." The doctor nodded. "Why the fuck am I strapped to the bed?" I asked haphazardly from my position. The doctor could only chuckle to himself and he watched me wriggle my feet in an attempt to escape. "You've always had a sense of humor, you know." He stood up, "The memories we scanned from your brain are impeccably comical. 2016 was such a bizarre time compared to my own. I gave the missus a good laugh with that one..... I digress. The simple fact of the matter is, you may be violent. You could be suicidal. Or maybe you came back wrong. That's why we're scanning you to find out." "Came back wrong?" I interrupted, "You brought me back from the dead, and you're tellin' me you're only worried about me coming back wrong now??" "You say that like it's a bad thing." He said while shaking his head randomly. "It's not like I planned on getting resurrected. I ain't Jesus." I countered. "No you're not." The doctor paused, "Besides, we brought him back two years ago. Good guy, always turns water to wine for a joke..... Ah, but where are my manners, I never introduced myself." I could only muster more confusion as he took off the hat he'd worn the entire time I seen him. "Doctor Henry Heimlich. And you must be?"

Who rings the doorbell at 7am on a Saturday? I grumbled to myself as I stuffed my feet into the slippers and pulled my robe tight around my waist. I glanced out the window overlooking the front door a nondescript black car was parked out front, and I could see a slightly balding head waiting on the stoop. I shuffled down the stairs, detoured through the kitchen to start a pot of coffee, and was almost to the door when the bell rang again. Impatient. My grouchiness was increasing. What could he want? I opened the door slightly, evaluation the stooped man standing in front of me. He was slight, his curved body hunched within a trench coat, dark pants and shoes emerging from the hem, and apparently impervious to the 95 degree heat. "Can I help you?" His eyes almost meet mine, before sliding away again. I notice now that he's mumbling slightly and keeps his hands tucked deep in his pockets. His eyes trace back and forth, as if he's looking for something on the edge of his field of vision. "You are Miss Katya Balisov, no?" His accent is odd, I can't quite place it; he talks like he has marbles in his mouth, jumbled and with care. I nod slowly. "Why do you ask?" "On September 17, 1999, you purchased the star Alcyno 29184. I need to buy this star from you. I will pay any price." I stand there, stunned. Of all the questions I would have expected, this would never have been one of them. I rack my brain, trying to recall purchasing a star. Nearly twenty years ago I was in college. Perhaps it was one of my notorious blackout purchases? I'd gone on several spending sprees while drunk before wising up and hiding my credit cards. But I didn't recall specifically buying a star. "I'm sorry, I think you may have the wrong person. I don't believe I own a star...." He pulled his hands from his pockets, his left hand gripping a crumpled piece of paper that he thrust at me. I took the paper gingerly, and smoothed its wrinkled corners until I could see what looked like a receipt. There it was - my name, address, email address, and billing confirmation for purchase of one star. How odd. He gestured towards the paper. "I just need you to sign, there, to transfer the ownership." There was some fine print and two signature lines at the bottom of the page, and he was now holding a pen out for me. "Why is this so important? And how much are you offering?" I was still confused by the whole situation, but if I could offload something of value that I didn't even know I owned, that could certainly help with my upcoming car payment. "I promised someone I would acquire this star for them, many years ago. I have been searching for you for some time now. I can not fully explain, but there is great...... sentimental...... value to me." He paused, furtively glancing around him in either direction, then pulled a pile of cash from another pocket. "I will give you ten thousand." I gaped at him, taking in again the strangeness of his appearance, his flighty nature, the outstretched hand (which I now saw was covered in a thin glove) with the proffered pen. Ten thousand dollars! For a star? a piece of paper? "Will this get me in trouble with anyone? You seem a bit nervous." He shook his head emphatically. "No, no, no, of course not, I am only in a small rush. Will you please sign?" I could certainly use the money - and what harm could it do? I took the pen in one hand, the money in the other, and signed quickly. I'd barely finished my signature when he'd crumpled the paper back and pushed it into the depths of his pockets. He gave me a short grin, his eyes excited, before turning and trotting down the steps to the black car. With a screech of the tires, he was gone. I stood at my front door, still a bit dazed by the strange encounter, then turned to go pour my morning coffee. As I sat at the kitchen table, gleefully counting the bills, I didn't even notice the morning news alert scrolling across the TV, announcing the failed space colonization negotiations and the beginning of the first interstellar war.

A small plastic pack of jellybeans raised up from the snack slot in Jone's desk. The top of read "Smart Snacks! Sponsored by Kydny's." "Nice job, Jone," said his teacher, but the voice came through the speakers; the teacher stood in the center of the room, three large screens surrounding her head with students on all sides, her body teeny in comparison at the center. Sometimes the head flicked over to two-dimensional scrolls of text. "Reddit: A Rendition of the World in the Early 2000's" read the banner-scroll at the bottom of her screen (and in small scrolled print underneath- "Sponsored by Tykut!. A video intro splashed across the teacher's face with the words "Real Life Accounts From the Long Dead Past" thrown in sharp relief across the screens while hyped up music played. One student rode in late and the screen to Jone's left flashed back to the teacher's stern gaze on him as he parked at his seat. As the lecture began multiple screens went into play. "Last lecture we left off with the growth in banana usage as a measuring device." To the forefront, a photo. "Here, a banana." Another photo replaced the first. "Here, another banana." Another photo came up. "Here, another banana." Droll began to spill lightly over Jone's lips. Just as he began to fall asleep the QA lights and music went off and Jone's desk lit up. "Which boy was a Reddit banana inspiration?" Three names, with photos. One person answered the question correctly. "Nice job, Hanly," said the teacher. Jone began to salivate and licked his lips. He pressed on one at random. The desk turned rouge with the message "Wrong: The Answer is'Carter. Carter's picture flashed in the answer choices. His teacher spoke again. "Nice job, Wynta." The desk glowed a gentle white again. The question came back. Jone chose another boy. The desk glowed green with a bright "Correct!" Jone's snack tray lit up again and he reached for the plastic container under the "Smart Snacks! Sponsored by Kydny" sticker. He pulled out a plastic pack of cheese crackers.

Mountainous heaps of colored metal that rested on round rubber circles scattered the landscape. The day was hot, the wind was..... windy. I can do this, Tim thought. Tim had been carried away from his web by a random gust of wind. He knew where his home was. It was beyond colored metal. He knew if he tried, and if he gave it his best, him and all eight of his legs could move quickly enough across the hot black asphalt, but he had to make sure to not meet the bottom of the giant flesh beings shoes. They were everywhere. Tim had to be most careful. He moved quickly. His legs moved in unison, one after another, he moved his small body across the parking lot. Another gush of wind! Tim lowered his body, feeling the wind try and pick him off the ground! Two of his legs dangled in the air! Then, the wind died.Tim collected himself and continued forward. Tim passed several more of the giant metal bodies, looking up at them as he passed. He had seen them before, but never so many, so orderly, lined up next to each other. Each one a few feet apart as they lined the Then suddenly one of the giant vehicles pulled in front of him! Tim tumbled in the wind that was generated by the rotating piece of rubber that moved in front of him! The giant metal object paused, Tim look up at it. "Ha!" Tim bellowed. "How dare this mighty vehicle think it can defeat me! I may be small! I may be tiny! But you can never keep me from getting home! If I have the will! I will find the wa Silence. A small flesh being looked at his shoe from the open door from the moving giant piece of metal, exclaiming. "MOM! I STEPPED ON A SPIDER!"

Sorry, I forgot it was after retirement.... I hope you still like it. - " God damnit! He sent me another one. " Detective Alan Coolidge threw his Styrofoam coffee cup onto the floor. It hit the tile with a quiet clunk. Every month, Coolidge received a gift from the infamous Holiday Killer. The festive nickname was coined by a local journalist for the serial murders taking place on a holiday. It didn't matter what the holiday, so long as it can be found on a calendar someone will die. Coolidge's partner glanced at his watch, 10:30PM. " Go home, Alan. You need a break. That sexy wife of yours is probably waiting for you spread eagle on your dining room table. " " What the fuck, Jason? " " Now you're not thinking about that fucking killer. " Coolidge, angry -though aroused- by Jason's comment, was thankful for the distraction. He nodded in agreement, grabbed his coat, and ran out. This was the longest shift, nearly 20 hours of nonstop searching. Today, he received a package; a bloody branch. An Arbor Day murder. Tomorrow morning, Detective Coolidge will answer his phone to be informed that they found another body. He pulled into his driveway. The lights were still on inside, his wife waiting for him. Alan knew that dinner was warm in the oven, and Natasha- the love of his life- would be sitting on the sofa in her pajamas reading Agatha Christie. Pulling himself together, Alan entered his home, and as predicted Natasha put down her novel to greet her husband. " Hi, Honey. You look awful, " she joked. Alan kissed her on the forehead. In the kitchen, he poured himself his nightly whiskey. He took it in one swig, slammed his glass down, cracking the base. " Damnit! " Alan grabbed walked over to the trash to toss it, when he noticed clipped branches shoved to the bottom of the can. He pulled it out slowly; it looked the same as the one... No, he thought, there's no way. Detective Coolidge continued to rifle through the trash. Below the potato peels, napkins, and week-old Chinese leftovers, he found a bloody paper towel. " Alan, what are you doing? " Natasha stood in the doorway. The detective began seeing her in a different light. Could she be the one? She knew his movements, how he thinks, how he works. The Holiday Killer lives in his own home. " Is this about the Holiday Killer? " Natasha continued, " What was in the package? " " How do you know I got a package? " " You're acting weird. Usually, that means something happened. " " What did you do while I was at work? " " I don't know. Cooked? Cleaned? Other things? Why are you asking me these questions? " Coolidge pulled the bloody paper and the branches from the trash. He tossed them onto the counter, " what the fuck is this? " " You're scaring me, Alan. " " Did you do this?! " " Trimmed the tree? Yeah. " " Who did you kill this time? " " You need to go to bed. You've been working for a whole day, you're tired. " " You're the Holiday Killer! My own wife. I LOVED YOU! " Natasha took a step back. She couldn't hide the fear from her face. " You're insane. I'm calling Jason, you need help. " She moved towards her cell phone charging on the coffee table. Her husband grabbed a knife from the drawer and lunged at her. He pushed it deep into her back. Natasha fell forward, screaming and begging. Alan's body held her down as he continued to stab her in the back, finishing her off by plunging the knife into her throat. Underneath him, his wife's lifeless body stared out into nothing, blood pouring from her mouth. - Detective Jason Frankel visited his old friend in prison for the first time. Prisoner 79016 sat chained to the table, clad in a bright orange jumpsuit. Alan's eye lit up, smile spreading across his face. " You did it! You found the evidence that Natasha was the Holiday Killer! " Detective Frankel chose to stand; he knew his visit would be short. " We received another package. A Mother's Day murder. " He handed the prisoner a photo. A sonogram with the name " Natasha Coolidge " printed on top. " We found a pregnant woman murdered in the park this morning, but this was addressed to you. " Alan reached out with shaking hands. A small peanut of a fetus stared back at him. He flipped the photo over. Written in what former detective Coolidge believed to be blood, it read " Oops. "

My story started where a lot have ended these past 10 years: with a single bullet. Living in post-war Britain, death was not an uncommon sight. Everyone had at least one firearm to defend themselves, everyone had encountered gunfire in the streets, and everyone knew what it meant to live every day like it could be their last. The revolution that was supposed to end the tyranny of a dictatorship had ripped the country apart; counties had split into factions, all threatening total destruction of the others. In ten years the population was decimated, the country reduced to a crumbling mass of fallen buildings and civilians with guns. All around me was depression, death, dirt, famine. Thinking about it, it's quite hilarious, in such a depressing way. The sacks of bones, flesh and organs we saw everyday were once living, breathing, talking human beings. They had a mother, a father, a pet, a first love, they were educated, they succeeded and they failed. And they died. A single bullet can end so much. That morning, as I wandered to the local shop for some bread, clutching my rifle, my world completely ended. I had no time to react; as soon as I entered Grange Avenue a bullet burrowed into my head, smashing part of my brain, and knocking me straight out cold. I woke in a beautiful wooden chalet, bright natural light streaming through vast windows above the soft, clean bed that I rested in. My itchy, dirty clothes were replaced with beautiful white robes, soft as silk and cleaner than anything I had ever seen. I sat up, and looked around the room - it was furnished luxuriously, with beautiful gold-leaf chairs and fantastic bright works of art hanging around the room. I got up and left the room, and immediately my breath was forced from me. The crumbled grey streets of London had gone. In their place were beautiful old chalets, bright white skyscrapers, and marble streets. I could also see a very unfamiliar sight - a beautiful emerald park, littered with tall, radiant trees, ferns, and glowing coloured flowers. Clear water ran through them. All around the streets were people dressed similar to me, smiling and talking and laughing. The smog-ridden sky had been replaced with a beautiful, deep purple, but the world was light around me and the I could see the vast orange sun dipping behind the structures around the city. For the first time in ten years I smiled. That bullet took me to a better place.

Her name now is the Witch. She hates it: Vuen knows she does, because when she hears the title - the name - her face shifts in the way she holds her mouth and eyes, and there is a strange line to her posture, but she accepts it. "Vuen," she says, at night, when they are pressed against each other, eyes weak and vulnerable in the way she never is otherwise, "say my name." Vuen does. - Vuen has loved the Witch ever since they were young, with knobby legs and long hair. She remembers their earliest kisses, then, exchanged between them without question. After some time, when their legs grew longer, and they wore their hair up, they stopped. The times then were still full of fondness, though restrained. The hold of a hand became a brush of the fingers; a hand on a cheek became a touch of the hair; the way they had rested on each other before dissipated, but they smiled at each other, and in there was the unspoken leaning. When she had to go back home, they wrote letters, and often, the Witch would send her poetry, written in that incredibly elegant handwriting, ink and loops: soft phrases, curved, and so quietly tender that Vuen never really bothered to write poetry in reply, though she too had learned how to write the sian and the rekil. She had tried to send her a poem, once, and felt her message dilute within the confines. I miss you dearly, Vuen wrote, instead; the Witch replied a month later with a letter charming as the rest, ended with a cutting and beautiful poem about the sun and the moon, and to wait, and to never end. The only thing they had in similar, their words, was the unmistakable whisper beneath. Vuen remembers very distinctly when it began: the Witch's first kill, won in a duel over herself. It had been an obvious thing that she should win, and not so surprising that she had gotten so heated over an insult to Vuen, but the kill was unprecedented against such a noble man, and the Witch's family exiled her. " Where do I go? " the Witch asked, not even crying; she was beyond that. Her face was empty, hollow. " Where can I go? " " It doesn't matter, " said Vuen, gently, " I'll come with you. " She took the Witch's hands, a gesture they rarely gave, now, and swept her thumbs over her knuckles before the Witch's hands clenched, and they both gave a shudder before the Witch pushed her away, and then she was burning. " God, " she said, in the ancient tongue, not as a blessing or prayer, but as a curse, " God! God! Why have you forsaken me? " There she trembled, swathed in golden flames as if they were silks, and when Vuen reached out to grasp her, undeterred, she shook her away. " Stop, " she sobbed, golden and shining and terrible, then, desperately: " I'll hurt you. " That was the kind of person the Witch was, before she was the Witch. They said no goodbyes, and went to an inn. " I'm sick of this, " the Witch said, softly. " I'm sick of the people. I'm sick of everything. " I'm sick of myself. Vuen heard that, underlining her meaning, and when the Witch's hands fisted, Vuen came and held her. Vuen did not say, you did not realize, no matter how much she regretted it now. There were many high tales and praises of the daughter of one of the greatest magic families, and they existed for a reason. The kill was not a mistake. " I'll get my vengeance, " said the Witch, into Vuen's shoulder, numbly. " I have sacrificed everything for their stupid honor, to be the perfect daughter, and this is what they have done. They have cast me away, like I am an animal. " " I'll help you, " Vuen said, and the Witch drew back, but this time, the only thing aflame was her gaze, molten and angry and full of something that made Vuen ache to see. " But, I don't - " " I don't care, " Vuen said, knowing what she was going to say. " I don't care. " She didn't: who cared if she had killed him? Who cared if she had been wrong? Who cared? Vuen saw her, wounded yet strong, furious yet sorrowful, and saw her the most for herself, in all of her cruelty and kindness, in the fire that burned and the fire that kept away. She loved her. " I don't care, " Vuen repeated, more fiercely. When they kissed, there was no starter: it was a mutual agreement. - Vuen stops counting their kisses, and stops counting the corpses. Both numbers grow too high to keep track of. " I wonder, " says the Witch, then, who is just beginning to grow into her title, " I wonder, when will it be enough? " She steps over more charred flesh. Her eyes are wondering and strange and lost. Never, Vuen knows, but does not say it. - " I miss home, " the Witch tells her, one day, when they are staying at a stable, pretending to be merchants. She has a pure, soft light at her fingertips, which she holds up so they illuminate the darkness, just a little. " Me, too, " Vuen admits, and the Witch inhales at that, sharply, and the lights dim. Vuen catches an ankle with her hand. " I would have missed you more, " she says, a reminder, and the Witch trembles. " I don't deserve this, " the Witch says. Vuen says nothing: she will not lie to her. There are some things love does not permit. The Witch knows this, and turns her head. " Goodnight. " " Goodnight. " The lights extinguish, but neither are afraid. " Have you heard of the Witch? " they hear, another time, when they are eating at a stall. It is piping hot, roasted apples, covered in melting cheese. The Witch freezes at that. " Of course, dolt, " someone replies. " The newsman came last week. Said she's burning everything in sight. " " We ought to head out, " the original speaker replies. " She's dangerous, and some tell me she might be heading this way. I'd watch out. " " She's crazy, " someone says, and a chorus of agreeing hums rise. " Let's go, " Vuen says, and they leave. In the future, people will puzzle at the absence of a burning of a town in her path. She is, Vuen thinks, beautiful when killing. There's something clear about the way she does it, without thought, acting solely on the heart and mind, and awash in radiance of flames that go crimson to white to gold, setting her hair to gleam and her face to shine, distant from the crisping humans, from the trembling screams. It is, Vuen realizes, like the purity of a child. It is, Vuen realizes, later, watching the tears roll down her cheeks as she sleeps, caught in a nightmare, the purity of her heart, simple in its honesty, in its horrible nature. Later, when the Witch wakes, Vuen asks her what she was dreaming of. " I can't quite remember, " the Witch replies, and both know it is a lie, but the topic is not breached. One day, they are walking, and picking roses from stray bushes. It is only then when Vuen realizes, as she plucks yet another blossom from its home, that in history, she will be remembered as the Witch, as the burning one who set the land to flames over bitterness. They will never see her, holding a spray of sweet flowers in her arms, rosy as her cheeks, her laughter simple and bright as daylight; they will never know her poems, more wonderful than even her laugh; they will never know that she fought over an insult to her beloved. They will never know her name. " Ilaese, " Vuen says, and Ilaese turns, smiling. " Yes? " Oh, her! Clasping such broken life, killing such innocent life, her, passionate and awful, unredeemable and undeserving, cruel and unbelievable, and beautiful in it, in her purity and her humanity, in her stains and monstrosity, in herself, incredible, a heretic, a bitch, the Witch, Ilaese: loved, beloved, the only and the one, forever and always. How beautiful, truly, and how ugly, and how beautiful in both of those things. " Nothing, " Vuen says, and smiles back, feeling her heart rend with love.

For the last six months my wife and I had been worried sick. If we didn't find enough food soon there was no way that she, myself and more importantly our child would survive the winter. After the third phase we guessed that there was less than 1,000 survivors, considering that we hadn't come across anyone for years and years. The first ten years after it ended had gone by slowly, a haze, we as a race had returned to our hunter gather phase. My wife and I collected as much paper as we could and wrote down as much as we could. WE collected as many books as we could find. We crammed as much information as we could into our bunker. The next five years we spent cramming up on food. We got as much as we could, but then she got pregnant and we knew it wasn't enough. At first we kicked ourselves for our mistake. How could we be so careless. Then we realized that what we had done was actually a beautiful thing. We could resurrect our species, humanity could survive. My wife and I agreed eventually we could find someone else in the world, hopefully they would have made the same beautiful mistake we had. All that information we had though, and there was one more thing I wanted to write. The wind beat my face and caked on layer upon layer of sand. I flipped over the aluminum trash can lid that I had been staring at for twenty minutes. This was likely my last hope and it was a small one. There, however, in all its irony was the piece of trash I had been searching for. Paper. I took the half melted pen in my hand and began. This may be the last scrap of paper on the planet. I was so glad that I found it I cried for hours, but that probably isn't the reason I'm crying. Son when you finally read this I want you to know that your mother and I did everything with you in mind. You need to know our story, but not from a scrap of paper. Your mother will tell you all you need to know. I love you. Have a good life son. I started my walk back home and began thinking of all the wonderful things my son would accomplish. He may be president one day, considering there won't be to many other candidates. I left my note with my wife and kissed her hard on the lips then kissed my son on the forehead. I climbed up the later and out the hatch. I reached in my pocket and pulled out my salvation, and more importantly my son's. The cold steel felt good on my forehead. I smiled and saved my son.

My friend, Evan, and I were doing typical kid's play and shooting at each other with our fingers. Cops and robbers. I was the robber and he was the cop. It was great fun. "Put your hands up!" Evan would yell. I'd try and retaliate with something like, "Bite me!" The times were great, and I wanted them to last forever. That was when we saw Tony coming our way. Tony was one of our friends, but lately he began to act strange. One night while we were going from door to door, ding ding ditching, Tony wrecked his bike and had to go the hospital. The damn police wouldn't even tell us were he was at. When he came back he was a lot different. He kept going on about stuff that wasn't there. It was frightening us all. He even tried to steal my bike, the bastard. After that he quit hanging around us. He was addicted to Sweet Tarts, he couldn't get enough of the sugar rush. We all did them, but he was going overboard. He had began to hang out with The Bozos, a group of some messed up kids, just to get his fill of Sweet Tarts. Tony came into the yard, and before we could even ask him what he was doing around he pointed his finger at Evan and yelled out, "BANG!" Blood instantly jolted out of the bag of Evan's head. He was thrust backwards onto the ground. I yelled out to him and held him in my arms. He was..... dead. My friend Evan was killed. "Tony! You bastard!" I called out. "Kevin!" Tony said while sneering down at me, "Are you going to stand in my way?" "You killed him!" "And I'll kill you if you try and stop me!" I wasn't even sure what he meant at the time. Stop him from what? I wasn't about to let him know that I was unaware to what his endgame was. I decided I wasn't going to back down from Tony. He was always just another member in our gang. I shook my fist at him as I said, "You can kiss my ass!" "That's too bad, Kevin. I thought I'd let you join me," he said while raising his finger towards me, "Before I kill you, will you tell me where you hid that damn bike of yours?" My bike! I had forgotten. It was right around the corner of the house. I just needed a plan to get it. I saw a rock down by my foot and knew what I had to do. I dropped down on my knees and began to act as if I was sobbing. "Are you crying?" Tony said while beginning to laugh, "I never thought I'd make you cry like a bitch, Kevin." He started to laugh hysterically and lowered his finger. This is when I took my chance. "Eat this, you bastard!" I said while throwing the rock at him. He had no idea what was coming as the rock hit him square in the face. He yelled out in pain while he fell backwards. I quickly jumped onto my bike and began to peddle out of there like a bat out of Hell. "Where do you think you're going, prick?" Tony said while firing everything he had at me. Bullets were whizzing past my head. I didn't dare turn back. I shifted the gears and flew out of there. He wouldn't be able to catch me on foot. I needed somewhere to go that would be safe. The old treehouse was certainly a place Tony would know where to look for me. I decided to find Aaron. Hopefully he was still alive. I knew he had piano lessons today so I went towards downtown to find him. I had to find out what the Hell was going on.

"It's who we are, I suppose. Whether it be worth it in the end or not," the first said. Eyeing his alien cohort. Before the two, a column of smoke slowly dissipated as the sun began to rise, the human of the two striking a light. Shaking his lizard like head, the second found a seat in the dirt. "We will make them pay. We will rebuild. Do you think Cortorol thinks that two of us exist?" The human turned away from the early dawn, striding toward the distant tree line, "Doesn't matter now does it. For all he knows his nemesis is dead. We can let him think that anyone is alive. And when the time comes we will retrieve our partner." As the dawn slowly encroached, the two onlookers disappeared into the receding shadow. The sound of water dropping into small puddles ticked through the silence. Who would've thought the rebels plotting a coup would hide in a cavern? Arthur did, and a short investigation confirmed his assumptions. A woman dressed in typical high-nobility attire laughed quietly, suppressing her laughter with the back of her hand. She was accompanied by a dozen brutes wielding various kinds of weaponry. A smirk slipped onto her face, " Although I applaud you for coming this far, you'll go no further. " She looked the intruder up and down. The man that had so boorishly lumbered into her hideout looked like your typical down-on-his-luck mercenary. A ragged tunic, faded pants, old leather boots and a sword not tied to a proper sword belt but to a rope. She eyed him with mixed feeling of disgust and annoyance, " Take care of him. " she waved dismissively. The brutes that had been awaiting her command sprung into action. The first man to reach Arthur swung down his mace in frightening overhead swing. In the blink of an eye Arthur unsheathed his sword and parried the mace. Rather than blocking it outright he held his weapon at an angle and the mace slid down the length of the blade. The man stumbled and Arthur opened the man's neck, his body drooped to the floor. Four other attackers came charging, faces red with anger. They raised their weapons: spear, sword, axe and cudgel. Each of them proficient in a different kind of weapon. Having a wealth of experience to draw from, Arthur instantly decided on the best course of action. One man yelped in surprise as their enemy stepped in between them. He plunged his spear at Arthur, it made its way towards him like a snake closing in on its prey. Arthur stepped aside at the last second and kicked the shaft of the spear, deflecting it. The spearhead disappeared in the gut of the man that had been closing in from behind. The spear-wielding man went pale, " Fredrick! " Fredrick could only gurgle in reply, blood bubbled at his lips. Arthur gripped the wooden shaft and pulled it. The man on the other end of it was tugged forward, stumbling in an attempt to recover his balance. Arthur stabbed him in the stomach once he had stumbled close enough. A large iron axe closed in on Arthur's side. He jumped backwards and landed in the fold of the brute's arm. Arthur freed his sword from the bowels of the first man and hammered the hilt down on the axe man's wrist. The man dropped his axe and cried out as arrows started zipping by. Arthur swung the man around towards their origin, using him as a human shield. Moments later, a dozen arrows had collected on the surface of his body. He pushed his man-made shield towards the archers, whom fired additional arrows at it - hoping to hit the target behind it. The human shield made it several steps before slumping towards the ground but it was enough, Arthur had already closed the distance. Some of the archers had the presence of mind to reach for a dagger or attempt to stab him with an arrow, they were far too slow. Others simply stopped moving, their faces showing the same fear before and after it had been separated from their shoulders. Witnessing the spectacle, gazing upon a man who smiled amidst blood and gore, two of the remaining brutes turned to flee. Arthur picked up the bow of a fallen archer and neatly placed an arrow between their shoulder blades. The woman failed to comprehend to scene in front of her, staring with her mouth agape. Plans and proper ethics had all made room in her mind to accommodate the overwhelming sense of dread. She lifted the skirt of her dress and hastily turned in the direction of a nearby escape route. An arrow found a way into her side and she crashed into the rocky cavern floor. Finally able to catch his breath, Arthur breathed hard. Surrounded by whimpering moans of the dead and dying. Out of the corner of his eye Arthur spotted his final enemy. The man sat on the ground, holding the head of his dying friend, thoughts of combat long forgotten. Arthur kicked away his sword, stepped up behind him and slit his throat. The woman cried out, " He had already surrendered! " Arthur shrugged, " Seems like an unnecessary risk. " "You mongrel," she cried, "you filth!" She buckled at her knees, " It's too late, " she replied with a smirk, " The plans are already in motion. " Blood from her arrow wound started seeping into the fabric of her dress. " You can not stop all of us. " she added with a cough, " The fellowship will prevail. " He spoke without turning, " Secret fellowship. " Arthur replied with a chuckle. Arthur plunged down his sword into the gut of the limp form in front of him, " You mean your sleazy gathering of exiled nobles? " Groans echoed throughout the cavern, the fallen archers were desperately clawing their way towards the escape route. Arthur took on a mild jog and met with the men with arrows protruding from their backs. He flipped them over, stabbed them in the chest and twisted the blade. Arthur sighed in satisfaction. He walked over to the last idle body and kicked it in the stomach, the body screamed and started wheezing. Arthur smiled to himself, glad that he had made a habit of checking. He lowered his sword and slit the man's throat before returning his attention to the woman. Arthur pointed at her using the tip of his bloodied sword, " You're the last one, " he said, " the last noble, that is. " Her eyes went wide, " Impossible, " she cried, " word would've reached me by now. I would've known! " Arthur closed the distance and stood over her, " Words won't get out if there's nobody left to speak them. " He drove his sword deep into her chest. After some choking breaths, the life faded from her eyes. Arthur stabbed her an additional five times before sheathing his sword. - Feedback is always appreciated. I sat down at the table. Honestly this wasn't the sort of place where I expected Lucifer to have his meetings, but then, what did I know? The shop was a little hole-in-the-wall deli, specializing in Greek gyros. Other than the shopkeep, no one else was around. I made my order, and settled in for the wait. Figures that he'd be late. Two weeks ago when I received the postcard in the mail, I thought it was a joke. Some teenage prankster with a sick sense of humor probably. The card had been scrawled with a beautiful script, but the ink was of blood. You are cordially invited to a luncheon with the Prince of Darkness, Lucifer, Satan, the Devil, et al, on the First day of November (Gregorian), this year of Two Thousand and Fourteen. Please wear appropriate attire. Refusal is not permitted. Certainly sounded absurd. But I had the feeling it was legitimate when I tried to get rid of it and it kept coming back. Garbage can, disposal, shredder, the local dump..... each time it ended back in my mailbox. Even on Sunday, when there's no post. So here I am, taking the day off for a meeting with Evil incarnate. My boss wouldn't have believed me, so today I'm "sick." I seated myself facing the door, so that I would have a chance to see him first, but apparently there was no fooling the Devil, because from behind me a gorgeous woman walked past, turned on her heel, and smoothly set in the chair across from me, all with the grace of a panther. Noting my startled look, she smirked. "Why does everyone always expect a man?" "I'm..... I'm sorry. That's just what I thought." I stammered, trying to be polite. So much for the Prince of Darkness. The woman before me was an absolute 10. Five feet, ten inches tall, not an ounce of fat on her, and a perfect hourglass figure. Her hair was a sultry crimson, though I wasn't surprised. Gingers didn't have souls, after all. Each nail on her hands was perfectly manicured, and she wore no apparent makeup, though didn't appear to need any either. "No matter. How are you doing today Charles?" "Er..... good I guess. What's this about?" "What? No questions trying to ascertain my authenticity?" The Devil looked surprised. "Well, I mean.... are you? Real, I mean?" Rolling her eyes, she snapped a finger and set the shopkeep's eyebrows ablaze. "Huh. Well ok then." "Yea. Now that that's over with, I'll formally introduce myself." Satan whipped her hair out of her eyes with a shake of her head and extended her hand. "You can call me Patrick." " ..... Patrick?" "Is there a problem with that?" A fiery light glowed from her pupils and I quickly shook my head. "No, no, no problem at all." "Good. Now, why do you think you're here?" "You..... want my soul?" I ventured the obvious reason. "Heavens no! I stopped that program 20 years ago! Turns out, people don't own their souls anyway. Couldn't sell them if they wanted to." Patrick laughed and I glimpsed her perfect teeth, dazzled by their brightness. "Well, then what?" "Simple. I'm selling timeshares and I think you'd love what I have to offer. Lunch is on me, of course, as long as you stay for the whole hour." I snorted derisively. "Really? Timeshare spiels don't work with normal salespeople. What makes you think I'm interested?" "Because you're going to Hell anyway Charles. I figured you'd want a chance at better accommodations." "What? Why am I going to Hell??" I sputtered. "Look," Patrick yawned dismissively, "I don't make the rules. Well I sort of do. But I didn't make you touch that dog. My point is, for a price, you can get a great fire-side condo." "What price?" "Your reddit account name and password, of course." I stood up resolutely, and shoved my chair in. "Ma'am, you can go to Hell."

"Hi, Dave. I need you to distract Rob for a few hours next Saturday," Sarah spoke in a hushed voice. "Oh." I called their house as Rob asked me to. He wanted me to be that guy. I'd call up Rob, but the line would ring until Sarah picked up and I'd make up some excuse which would drag her husband out of the house so he could do final preparations for her surprise dinner party. "Yes, sure, that sounds like it would be fine." "Perfect. Between 12 and 6," said Sarah. "Perfect timing too, I was just about to call you. What did you call for?" "I don't remember. It's slipped my mind," I lied. "Are you planning something? It's both of your birthdays on Saturday, right? Is that why you need me to distract Rob?" "Yes, but don't tell him, okay? I've arranged for strippers to perform at our house, and they need to set up for the night." "What, really?" I was worried, I knew that Rob had already booked out a section of their favourite restaurant, one with a dance floor. "Strippers? You hired strippers for your husband?" "Yes, it's a little unconventional, but he'll enjoy it I think. It will be good for him. We've been married for a few years and he's a pretty timid guy. It will be nice to see some new boobs once in a while. And I'm sure the rest of the guys will enjoy it." "Are you sure? Maybe he'd prefer a different kind of venue?" I was getting desperate. They've both entrusted me with their party plans and I wasn't going to let them crash one into the other. "Oh hush, Dave. I've booked a man as well, for the women, and you. Anyway, everything's paid for; no refunds. Oh, it's Rob," she cut herself off. "Rob, Dave's calling for you." She handed off the phone to Rob. "Hey Dave," he said. "How's it going?" "Well," I started, "I told her I'm moving next Saturday and I'll need your help. So, you'll be out of the house and it won't be suspicious." "Thanks, great, buddy. I knew I could count on you." The confidence he had in me fed my feelings of dread. "Listen, do you really think that Sarah would want to eat out for your birthdays? I mean, wouldn't it be better to cook her a meal yourself?" "What? Don't be silly." Rob waved away my suggestion. "It's our party. I don't want to cook. Especially not for six tables' worth of people. Anyway, I can't do that now; I'm supposed to be out of the house the whole day." He was right. They're screwed. How am I supposed to fix this? Am I supposed to fix this? Shit. The guests. They'll know, and they'll blab. One pair of loose lips will shoot this thing down. Oh, I thought Sarah was having strippers over. Will they be at the restaurant? Are we eating at a strip club now. "I'll help with the guest list," I blurted out. "I'm ready to send out the invites. It's fine," Rob said. I guess I'll be that guy. "Come on Rob, I thought you trusted me. Isn't that why you asked me to help. Let me help. I'm your friend." I sounded like a douchebag of a man, playing the "friend" card. Silence, then "Okay, I'll send you the guest list." Rob is pretty timid..... - I called Sarah's mobile immediately after Rob hung up. With a little coaxing, I got her guest list as well. It's your birthday, you've planned enough. Relax..... Now what? I have their guest lists, a non-refundable strip show, and the entire back-end of a restaurant booked out..... - The week went by, and the day was Saturday. I accompanied Rob on his errands, distracting him as promised. He thought it was unnecessary, but I convinced him that it would be safer considering the lie we told Sarah. He picked up his new suit, and a matching dress for Sarah. It wasn't overly formal but would make them look quite handsome. Afterwards, he drove by the florist for a bouquet he ordered earlier in the week. All the while, I was sneaking off to make phone calls. The party bus was ready and picking up the guests. By the time we arrived at the restaurant, everyone was there, except Sarah. Rob went around making sure everything was perfect, before he went back to his car to bring Sarah to her surprise. As soon as Rob was out of sight, I set my plan into action. The restaurant staff guided all the guests to the fire exit in the back, each one carrying a hot foodstuff in foil party trays, and onto the party bus with "Homecoming" decaled on the side. I tipped the manager 100 for the trouble of it all. Heading out the front, I saw Rob standing by the car, kicking his tires. They were flat. "Don't worry, I have an air pump." I opened my trunk and started it up. It gave the bus a good head-start. I tailed Rob without him knowing, or at least hoping he didn't notice. He didn't make it obvious that he noticed, unlike with the party bus parked across his house. I lost sight of him as he rounded a corner and entered his house. "SURPRISE!" I heard from the driveway. I made my way to the door. "Surprise, Rob." I patted him on the back, and sighed.

Log one: The End. Is this thing on? Oh it is. Well, log one, the end. It happened so fast, no one could have known. The virus had spread so fast that even the government, with all its money and power, could not stop it. This virus, I don't know how to describe it, but it, makes people rot while they're still alive. They can feel it to. John, one of my squad mates, got infected. We had to lock him outside of the compound. When his flesh started to rot he began screaming and screaming for hours on end. I still remember how his eye was dangling out of his eye socket. Sorry, I just needed to get that off my chest. We're in a military compound in the Mojave desert. We have around thirty survivors. The general is dead, shot himself in the head after learning that his family died. The people look to us soldiers look up to me for help, considering I'm second in command. The civilians look up to soldiers. Moral isn't doing so good at the moment. I don't feel like talking anymore for the day, I'll talk more tomorrow. Log 2: No word We haven't heard anything from the government for awhile. They usually call in for us to give them a status report or some bullshit like that, but today they haven't. There's talk among everyone in the compound about how the government have collapsed or had moved or abandoned us or something. We have around a years worth of supplies here so we should be fine for awhile. Log 3: New World No one has called us in three days. I'm assuming that the government is dead at this point. Some people attacked us yesterday. I sent some men out to check the surrounding area to check for any other survivors. I sent five of my soldiers out, and only two came back. I saw them coming in on a jeep and I saw one of them was bleeding out. They had apparently been attacked by some bandits. They were able to get the jump on them. The government has collapsed. We now live in a new world. Log 4: Desperation I don't have a lot of batteries. so I'll have to make this quick. Its been six months since I found any batteries or anything. We're running out of food, and there is twenty people here. We didn't have enough supplies as we thought. We were desperate. When they found food this morning, they ate it all up. They didn't care that Henry, one of the older survivors, was gone. That they knew how low they had sunken too. They just wanted food. Log 5: I'm sorry I'm sorry momma. I'm sorry for what we have to do. I'm sorry! I'M SORRY I ATE THE CHILDREN!!! I DID N'T WANT TOO!!! I WAS JUST SO HUNGREY!!! Log 6: Last log There's only nine of us left. We invite people into our compound, promising them that they will be safe. When they sleep, we kill them, cook them, and eat them the next morning. The general would be ashamed to see what we have become, but he's dead and we're alive. I don't want to talk anymore.

And all this is thanks to one person. Alfonso. You see, Alfonso is a inventor too. But not as brilliant of one as I am. However, he's rolling in dough. For some reasons unknown, everything I invent, he somehow manages to invent the exact same thing right before I complete mine. And what disturbs me is that I cant sue the bugger because I dont have evidence that he is outright stealing my ideas. Then it hit me. I can invent a time machine, go back in time, and figure out Alfonso's game, stop him and become successful myself! That was the plan.
