I miss the trip to the mall, when you went slack in my arms and we breathed in every ounce of that kiss we could give. I miss your eyes, how they looked into me with a sense of understanding. I miss your dark sense of humor, I miss the smell and the feel of your hair. I miss when your parents would mock us and we'd smile for it. I miss that night under the stars, where our breath shown and your eyes lit up my world as if every star had fallen directly into you, and the crashing force knocked the wind out of me, I miss how in love we seemed to be. But I'm sorry, I'm sorry for the way you treated me. I'm sorry that you would leave me alone for days, then tell me I wasn't reaching out enough. Tell me that I needed to hold on tighter, not to lose you, but that you were afraid of suffocation. I'm sorry you stopped all communication, without telling me. I have a lot of wishes, I wish that I had never told Richard to come to our school. I wish I hadn't let you go, that I had fought for you, I had kept on you, I had been the man you wanted me to be. I with I could have saved you from your anxiety, that you couldn't trust me enough to open up, and do what I was doing. I'm sorry I held back from being myself, because I didn't want to scare you away. I'm sorry that every time I let some of myself show and you reciprocated it and understood how I was feeling, unlike anyone else, I fell back in love with you. I know I did a lot of stuff wrong, but I also know I deserve better than the way you treated me. I hope you're happy with him, that you've found peace with what you did to me and what you did to Katie. But fuck you. -Surfinburd

The dust blew in gusts and waves over the deadlands of the Trilok'ag'nghzar. Cloaked against the beating winds, the lone bone-raker climbed the ridge unsteadily, a stabiliser clutched tightly in his lower left receptacle. It was cold, perhaps 63 Pelak, but his objective was clear - he had set the coordinates into his mnemonic web before setting out. As he crested the ridge, he perceived before him the outline of what would in ancient times have been a vast bay. A hazy light permeated the thick clouds of dust overhead, and lent a dull glow to the scene. And in the distance, the object of his curiosity - an image that he had burned into his mind. The bone-raker climbed down the ridge and made his way quickly across the plain. It was a flat, dry, unmarked expanse, with not a single feature apparent save for that which he kept always in his sight. A thin metallic peak, covered in metal spines, and towering over 50 units over the shifting sands. Too thin to provide a barrier to the sand, and unique amongst the other structures of the Forespirits. He scowled at the thought of the word - he was sure that they had been beings of biology, much like himself, but his people spoke of them as though they were of the supernatural or divine. His rebellion against the Engrams and their ideas had made him an outcast. He had suffered..... watched as his own mate was taken as tribute, along with the millions of others sent to the far havens of the Lightbeings..... did such a place even exist? He had narrowly escaped the "Giving" himself. He decided to put the thought out of his mind..... he would find his evidence here, if nowhere else. Now, he was almost upon the thing. Many rotations ago, it would have been a very tall structure, and this needle might even have appeared to pierce the sky. But thoughts of beauty and wonder were quite alien to the bone-raker and his people. He considered the scene, wondering if there were a way inside. Circumnavigating the structure, he finally found what he was looking for - a small portal in the side of a stone-like wall. This was a material that he had seen often in their structures..... but no one had ever investigated its properties, since all such questioning had been banned by the Engrams. He tried to push the portal-lid inward, but it had been fused to the wall by the sand. He took a few steps back, and smashed into it with his head-ridge. The portal opened, into blackness. The bone-raker walked in slowly. There could be nothing alive here, and the structure must be stable if it had survived so many rotations. He removed his photon-grub from its receptacle and shook it, casting a faint glow over the room. It was a small room, with strange metal objects on the walls. Sand lay in mounds on the floor, and in every corner. But he had little time to look. He moved on, forcing portals open where required, and climbing stairs when he found them. He didn't know where to go, but his wanderings led him higher and higher. In another time, he might have stopped to examine the strange script that he saw all around him - rare at other sites, but present almost everywhere in this structure. He had partially deciphered it based on the intermediate scripts of the Late Masters, more than anyone else had in any case. Prominently displayed on a wall, he observed characters that he believed were arranged to form the words "Heaven" and "Tall-House." It mattered little. He hurried on. After about 12 droghs of a suncycle, he came upon a portal larger than those through which he had previously passed - with its lid lying on the ground before it. He was about to step in when he made an observation..... the door was not covered in dust, unlike like everything else on the floor. The bone-raker moved cautiously over the door, and entered the room beyond. It was a vast room, and his light barely permeated the darkness. He moved forward slowly, looking around furtively. Suddenly, he heard a noise behind him - a groan of metal. He moved back to the portal, and found it closed tightly behind him. He smashed against it with his head-ridge until dazed and bruised, but to no avail. He clicked his signal into the darkness - "Wherewhat do they want," but was not met with any clicks in return. Droghs seemed to pass in silence. Suddenly, there was light everywhere. Light of an intensity of which the old bone-raker had not thought possible. He shielded his orbitals in pain, and cowered on the ground in terror. And then he heard the sounds. It had a strange rhythm to it. There was perhaps even something animal-like about it. Different sounds, calling and answering. But he had heard these sounds before..... many rotations ago in the larval stage, when he had been afforded a meeting with an Engram. Had they found him?! The lights dimmed, and he raised one of his orbitals. Two immensely tall figures, extremely thin, towering over him. One by one, their hoods were pushed back to reveal strange pitted globs of flesh and hair, supported on a thin appendage. On a wood composite sheet, in a building on the Plains of Sarg'glath long ago, he had seen images of such creatures. The Forespirits themselves. And then it came to him, in a swift wave of understanding and horror. The Forespirits had never disappeared. They had merely changed their form. The Engrams whom had ruled his people since the first gestation, in their metal shells..... with no lifefluid or flesh. They spoke this strange tongue, they called themselves Gods..... and they had always prevented the matter of the Forespirits from being investigated. But now..... he unflasked his heat blade and raised it over his head. He needed to escape, to show the others. But these creatures hardly seemed to take notice of him. He moved towards the portal slowly. One of the creatures raised a metal object, glinting in the light. There was a flash, and his world turned to black. 'Good', said Kwalid, re-adjusting his sand-cloak. We can use this one.'Nope', muttered Cheing, as he wandered towards the body. He bent down to take a closer look at the remains of the creature. He held the creature's blade to the light, examining it with amusement.'Looks like they've got their heat alloys sorted. The work of our friends, the Engrams, no doubt'. He looked up, and observing the annoyance on Kwalid's face, said'Well, this one's infected - look at the lower-left appendage. We can't take it back to the city..... we can't risk spoiling our stock'.'But the collectors have been so far behind on their shipment this month..... we don't even have enough fuel in our ration to get back', complained Kwalid.'Look, it won't hurt to extract this one, and leave the ship outside the city limits..... its a twelve day walk otherwise!' Cheing considered this for a moment, and acquiesced, removing an extractor from his belt and inserting it into one of the creature's raised fluid pouches.'Look, this should serve as a warning against moving so far outside the exclusion zone..... what if there had been ten of them Kwalid? The Skytower might have been an interesting find, but it just isn't worth the risk'. With that, he completed the extraction, and keyed the closing sequence into his pad.'Ok, let's get going then'. And the two Forespirits left, the body of the old bone-raker lying emptied behind them.

"Yes, Dr. Fish," he said, confidently leaning back in the chair on the other side of the desk from me. "I am Jesus." I wrote another few lines in my psychiatric notebook. I was new to this case, recently transferred to this hospital, and this was the first patient I'd had an opportunity to interview. If they were all like him, well. Megalomania, delusions of grandeur, the case file suggested that it wasn't schizophrenia, as this was the only identity that he had but I should ask to be certain. "No, doctor, this is the only persona that I have. I am me. Yes, I am that I am." He idly reached over, picked up a pen then started whirling it around his fingers. He was quite good, and perhaps I should be making more notes, so that I didn't talk outloud while I was writing them. Had I said anything? But, really, did he expect me to believe that Jesus was skilled at pen whirling? He was quite good at it, but that sort of skill just didn't fit the persona. "Doctor," he said, leaning forward and passing the pen back and forth from hand to hand as it whirled around each individual finger, "I'm the son of God. The son, the only begotten in the flesh. I oversaw the creation of this world. Do you really think whirling a pen is going to be difficult for me?" He gave it one last flip and it landed neatly back in my cup. He was very good, and I could see why other staff members had listed the reservations that they had in his file. However, I had arrived late and it was almost time for lunch. I was about to say something when he spoke up again. "It is almost time for lunch, won't you accompany me, Doctor?" He stood up and began walking towards the door, which wasn't locked. It never was when I was with a patient, so that if the patient became disturbed or began acting irrationally an orderly wouldn't have trouble getting in. I hurriedly got up from my desk and followed him I didn't want to unduly antagonize him or cause him to become riled and the next stop was lunch in any case. There was no need to try to detain him or to call an orderly, I would simply accompany him. He kindly greeted every person in the hall as we passed and I decided to take the opportunity to ask him a few more questions. It was slightly irregular to have a conversation in the halls, but my curiosity had been peaked. "If you are Jesus," I said, "It seems as though earlier you anticipated what I was about to say. Why, why haven't you spoken up this time?" "I wanted to let you marshal your thoughts," he said. You weren't certain what you wanted to say and I didn't want to abrogate your free will." "Well, I'm not really sure why you're here. Your file doesn't indicate that you have ever been a danger to yourself or others, you didn't self check in, even if you really are Jesus, or think that you're him, I don't see why you would still be here." "Because this is where I was needed, Doctor. I was waiting," he said, opening the door to the cafeteria for me. I stepped inside and paused. Everyone was sitting there, neatly lined up, looking at us, with only two seats left vacant. One seat in the very center of the farthest table, and one seat on its right-hand side. "I've been waiting for you." There are three parts to every story. The beginning, the middle, and the twist. [ More by me ] (https: ) I'll write more if people want it.

"TOM! Wake your lazy fucking ass up and go to school! I will NOT tell you again." The voice booms through the house so loudly that the bedframe rattled. I hate school, I wish I could just sleep all day. If I go to school, he'll just call me fatass and throw rocks at me when coach isn't looking, or he'll take my backpack and make me beg for it back, or he'll pull down my pants in front of Julie again. I don't want to go. Rolling over onto my stomach and clutching my pillow to my head does nothing to muffle the noise. "TOM! You little shit. Get up this instant or I will beat the shit out of you!" I pull the pillow tighter over my ears and push my face into the mattress. That's when the smell hit me. Mom washed these sheets yesterday, why do they smell so awful, like BO and wet dog all at once. I reel away at the stench, and the streak of sunlight falling across the bed reveals yellow and brown stains. Ugh. What is going on. Then I felt the scratch of my blanket, like an airplane blanket, covered in holes. This isn't my bed. I sit up and glance around the room. Everything is gone. No computer. No Lego sets on the shelves. Nothing. All my posters are gone too. The walls are blank, except for a fist-sized hole in the drywall. This isn't my room. "TOM! What the hell is going on?" Heavy footsteps come up the stairs, but only a few, like someone who is skipping steps, bounding closer and closer to my room. The voice is outside the door now. "I said WHAT THE FUCK IS GOING ON?" As I come out of my morning stupor I realize that I'm not Tom. I'm Frank. Tom is an asshole I have class with who torments me every day. The door slams open, and a man I've never seen before barges in and punches me in the stomach, knocking the wind out of me. He stands over the bed while I gasp for air. "That'll teach you to be lazy you little shit! That's why your mom left, she couldn't deal with how fucking useless you were. Now go to fucking school. NOW!" He punches me again before he stomps out, in the exact same spot. I can't breathe. When I do take a breath the stench of my sheets makes me gag. I roll out of bed onto the floor. The pain in my stomach, the smell, the yelling. What is going on? Sitting on the floor, I try to piece together reality. Without 30 seconds passing I hear the voice again. "What the FUCK did I tell you boy?" I hear footsteps on the stairs again, and I desperately scramble to put on the only clothes I can find. The dirty ones on the floor next to my bed. Too late. I have one leg into my jeans before he grabs me by the arm and drags me out of the room. In the hallway I spot myself in a dusty, cracked mirror. I'm Tom. Before I can even begin considering my situation, I'm falling down the stairs. I tumble to the bottom and hit my head on the floor. "You should be more careful around the house, or you'll get hurt. You hear me boy? Wouldn't want you to get hurt now, would we? Now get to fucking school, or I'll have to wake up your sister too." He throws a pair of sneakers at me. They miss my head and slam into the front door. Without a second thought I run outside, forgetting the shoes. More shouting comes from the house as I sprint down the street in my socks, the gravel tearing at my feet.

Nick rolled out of bed and on to the floor with a groan. He had hoped the uncomfortableness of the floor would help wake him up, but he was so sleepy the floor felt about as good as the bed. He felt himself drifting off, but forced himself to stand up. I just need some coffee, he thought to himself. He worked his way downstairs, where the TV was on. " Breaking News! " screamed the headline. The TV was turned down, and he couldn't hear what they were saying, and honestly he didn't care. He worked his way over to the coffee pot and turned it on. Working his back across the kitchen to the bathroom, he caught another glimpse of the TV. " War rages in..." he didn't bother to read the rest. The middle east was always in an uproar, he figured, wouldn't be surprised if more drama started there. Didn't really matter to him. Yeah it was unfortunate, all the death and such, but was he really affected by it? No, and no one he knew would. He reached the bathroom and plastered on some shaving cream. Carefully, he slid the razor down his face, taking all of the shaving cream and stubble, and leaving a fresh smooth finish. He got a small sense of pride from shaving well. As he was finishing around his chin, a police car threw on its sirens near the window as it raced by. He slipped, and cut himself. Shit, he thought, today is gunna be a rough day. He put a shred of toilet paper on it and went to put on his suit. Another thing he prided himself on was his ties. He had dozens of ties for dozens of occasions, and he always made sure his knot was perfect. A small or messy knot always tells a lot about a person, he figured. His knots were always double windsors; broad and perfectly shaped. As he was tying the knot, the tornado sirens went off. Probably just a test, he thought. He poured himself a cup of coffee and then it struck him, it was a friday, the last of the month, weren't the sirens tested at the beginning of the month? He glanced outside. The sun was rising, the sky was clear, and it looked like it was going to be a gorgeous, warm, sunny day. It couldn't be the weather. He grabbed the remote and turned up the volume on the TV. " ..... battle rages across Europe and the far east. In addition, Russian and Chinese forces are reported to be entering into some parts of Alaska, but are meeting fierce resistance from US and Canadian forces in the - hang on a second, We are just getting reports of..... of missile launches across the US and Russia..." The reporter sat back in her chair with a blank, shocked look. After a second she took a deep breath and continued. "Now, America, is the time to Nick shut off the TV, he didn't want to hear it. If he'd caught it earlier, maybe he would have had time to do something useful, maybe get close enough to his stocked cabin up north that he would escape the blast- but it was too late now. His story was ending. He poured himself a glass of scotch, and sat by the window and watched the chaos outside as the bright, burning light descended toward the city in the distance.

INT. FOYER - DAY Rain pours down outside. WILLIAM stands at the credenza, pouring himself a high ball of scotch. VERONICA sits on the divan, perfect posture, reading. WILLIAM Turquoise. (smirks) Very specific. Veronica lowers her book slightly. VERONICA Sorry darling? WILLIAM I never mentioned the color. Veronica runs a gamut of emotion with her eyes: guilt, denial, contempt, coyness..... WILLIAM Have you anything to say? VERONICA A lucky guess. WILLIAM Will Remy have the same to say? VERONICA How should I know? William smirks again and shakes his head. He sips his drink. Veronica raises her book back up and turns the page. A BUSINESS CARD falls out onto the divan. CLOSE UP on card. It says'Harson Bros. Inc.' FULL, INDICATIVE VIOLIN NOTE. Veronica panics and stuffs the card away. The double doors by the spiral staircase open and the MAID steps in. MAID Lunch is prepared. (to William) It's your favorite, goose. VERONICA How does she know your favorite wild game? William looks from her to the maid. He reddens and smashes his glass on the ground. WILLIAM I'm not hungry! Tension fills the air. A beat. The doorbell rings. The maid gasps. Veronica gasps. William throws his head toward it and seethes. MAID I'll get it. The maid moves slowly toward the door. Veronica stands, nervous. William grabs a cane from the coat rack and wields it readily. The maid opens the door. It's TERRENCE, soaking wet. He has one eye patched and a casted arm. MAID Terrence! VERONICA My god. WILLIAM You bastard. TERRENCE I'm going to turn myself in. I don't have much time. There's just one last piece of business I had to tend to. (He steps in) Now..... (gauges all three of them) Where is my daughter? SMASH CUT TO BLACK

The sound of the wailing klaxons thrust me out of my sleep. But then again it wasn't really a sleep. More of an uneasy nap similar to those of every other person in this country. We all knew it would be any day now. There wasn't a soul around who wasn't ready with a bug-out bag and a government-issued rifle. The population had been "prepared" for this moment for months, through militia training and and town planning. We had heard the Head Voice speak a countless number of times on why it was so important to "resist the enemy" and to stop them from committing the same atrocities they had in New York and Boston. No one could forget those images on TV of those mounted, belt-fed MG's tearing through the crowds of people on Park Ave. No one could forget those images online of armored vehicles running over all those university students in Cambridge. Now that it has begun, we know this is our last chance to stop them. The monsters were supposed to protect us. Instead they "protected" us from our freedoms. I stepped out the door and saw the night sky lit up in the distance with AA fire and incendiary shells. I closed my door and said our people's prayer before heading off to the rally point: "Fuck the Police."

I remember it like it was yesterday. The woman I'd met at the book store agreed to go out and get a burrito at the Freebird's and I was dressed to my best: No metal T-Shirts, my best pants, my best overshirt, and a nice shirt with no apparent logo. Driving to get her, I was hit with anxiety. What if I screwed this up? Oh my god, she was beautiful and I was this fat manbeast, why would she agree to this? What if she was standing me up? What if this was a mistake? Picking her up from her house, we made our way to the restaurant and I paid for our meal. I couldn't help but feel a twist in my stomach, and my head was getting sweaty and my breathing was faster. I asked to excuse myself and made my way to the bathroom. Pacing back and forth in there, a man stepped out of a stall and glanced over at me. He was the same height as me, thin, and had a nice suit on. "Hey. Listen. I've not got long. You're me from the past, and I'm you from the future. You've got to try your hardest here, man, this woman is the mother of our children. Without her, we won't find success in writing." I asked him so many questions, but he stepped past me and out of sight. Collecting myself, I cleaned myself up using the mirror and a napkin and made my way back to the table. "So, what do you do?" "I'm a moderator on a writing subreddit." "What's a subreddit?" "Oh. It's a site on reddit." "What's Reddit?" When I explained it to her, she left, despite my persistence she stay. Weeping into my bean and cheese burrito, I saw my future self enter with a somber expression on his wide face. He was no longer rich-looking, instead wearing a mustard-stained tank top and sweatpants with sandals. He was a fat slob, like I am today. He clutched his chest and dropped dead, to the shock of the other inhabitants of the restaurant. I merely bit into my burrito, tears in my eyes.

A dull rumble vibrated the floor beneath my feet, and I could feel something happening. Finally. The lights had been out for almost an hour, and I had been in one of the most remote segments of the facility dropping off a package for Dr. Horz, one of the biotech R D gurus. I had been stumbling around for what felt like ages, but my watch did confirm that it was only 56 minutes. 56 minutes of noiseless terror. This particular R D facility of Tegra was filled with wonders, but it was very nearly empty. I was in my second week of interning, a lowly, aspiring electrical engineer. Thus far, I had done little more than grunt work with the odd bit of logic design. Mostly just documentation though. Endless documentation. The ground stopped trembling, and the lights slowly inked a light incandescence. The walls in front of me slowly illuminated, and I was peering at a tremendous vault. A vault door - to be specific. A vault door...which was slightly cracked open. The metallic alloy comprising its structure wasn't flush with the surrounding wall. And then the door started cracking open more. The noise was probably the most frightening thing. The grinding of gears and servos, attempting to hold the door shut, was echoing riotously throughout the small room. I started backing away slowly. I don't know where I am. I don't know what is behind that door, and I don't want to be here anymore. I take a large, decisive step towards the door, and I hear a different kind of rumble - a throaty rumble, from some thing. And then the door quite literally gave up its effort to hold whatever was within and sprang backwards, slamming into the wall. The darkness was wholly shrouding the space beyond. A deep, primal terror was creeping into every nook of my being. What the fuck is happening? And then I see it. Six or seven feet in the air, slowly apparating into existence as the gentle illumination of the emergency lighting found it. A long, tube, slowly tapering to a point. No, not one. Many. The presence became more pronounced in the room. I watched as the objects source grew more visible. Dense, matted hair. The tubes were sprouting from it. And then the eyes. Yellow - slitted - orbs. It sprang. The last thing I perceived in those final moments, as my body was wrapped handily in a clawed grip, was a pronounced and deliberate, " Meow. "

"We don't have much time," he says. "My battery is almost at 10 and I can't sustain an erection in low power mode." I grin, fumbling with his belt and slipping a hand inside. He is smooth, hard, and warm. I lean close to his ear and whisper, "I need you." His hands - all four of them - tear at my blouse and pants. The servos in his fingers are too strong, too rough, and buttons from my blouse fall onto the concrete floor of the supply closet. "Jerk! I left my spare uniform at home - oh!" I gasp as two of his hands pull open my bra. I arch my back and press myself against him, against the unyielding metal of his perfect, molded chest. "Hurry," he pants. "I've turned off a few non-essential processes but I don't know how long I can last." I bat his hands away and bend down, shimmying his pants down to his wheels. Still on my knees, I look up and make eye contact with his visual sensors as I slowly trace a fingertip up his inner thigh. I stand and we kiss. He wraps his arms around me, cupping my head, my waist, my back and one arm. For a moment, I close my eyes and swoon in the warmth of his embrace. His battery beeps, loud and insistent. I open my eyes and smile as I snake a hand downwards. Suddenly, his steel feels cold in my hands. I look down between us, below his perfect chest, his perfect abs. I sigh. "Sorry," he mutters. "I told you to hurry." I step back and try to fix my ruined blouse. "Yeah, well, I told you to use Energizer." If you liked this story, you might like my other stories at rhpcisco7965 or rTMODAL.

"I sentence you to death!" intoned the Judge. You balk at hearing this, a coldness settles in the pit of your stomach. Several members of the jury gasp. A shocked silence envelopes the Court Room. The clerk clears his throat, which sounds louder than it should in the void of sound. He approaches the bench, each step echoing, leans over, and whispers something in the Judge's ear. You don't catch what he says. You just know that it can't be good. Anyway, didn't they remove the death sentence? You are quite sure they can't sentence you to death. "It appears I can't sentence you to death," the judge says. Almost as if reading your mind. His voice level and toneless. You are quite sure it would sound the same if he was telling you he'd won the lottery. A brief respite then, you feel relieved for a moment. It doesn't last long. "No, the death sentence has been replaced by something else," that same voice says. A Pause for effect, for drama. you always hated when they did this on quiz shows. What is the answer? Don't keep me in the dark. "The replacement sentence is a one way trip to mars," says the Judge. He looks at you briefly, then back down at his desk, as if searching for the reason for the sentence. He won't find it there. You run this through your head. So you don't die, you just can't come back. It's as good as dying but somehow you grasp the chance of life even knowing this. Maybe you will find a way back to earth one day? Suddenly the court grows louder again, almost as if you had lost your hearing temporarily and just now it faded back in. You are guided out of the Court Room, back into your holding cell. You run the idea through your head. Over, and over. This seems like a better fate than death you tell yourself. What's the catch? You are being marched down a hall way, towards another cell. When do you get to go to Mars? No one has told you anything, you've just been kept in one cell after another. How long has it been since your sentence? Weeks certainly, maybe even a month or two. The guards push you in roughly, they are deaf to your questions. They lock the door behind them. You hear their footsteps getting quieter as they walk back down the hall. You pace around the room, your only company a mirror on the wall, the harsh light above you, and a door that lets no light in. You stare at the mirror for a minute or two, you are not looking well. The stress, the uncertainty. These have taken a toll on you. You need a shave, you need a hair cut. You need a lawyer. "The time for lawyers has passed," they say whenever you requested one. You had your case in court, so maybe it has. More time has passed, still no change in your circumstances. Same room, same mirror, same light. They feed you once through a flap in the door. You have been in this room for a few hours now, at a guess. Suddenly, you notice a change. A change is welcome at this point. The floor is moving. Then it dawns on you, the floor will keep on moving until there is no floor, then no you. You bang on the door. The floor keeps moving. Not quickly, not slowly. The floor moves in the way of an escalator, no hurry. Inexorable, uncaring. More banging on the door. You realise the futility of this. But what else do you have? What else can you do? Next door in the Film Studio, Tracy has failed to solve the puzzle. The game is lost. The audience looks on as the last of the floor vanishes, then the poor soul in the room falls to his doom, screaming. "How does it feel Tracy? You were doing so well!" the gameshow host says excitedly. "I really thought you would solve the puzzle in time!" "Well Bradley, I tried my best. I had a lot of fun being here today," says Tracy. The audience clap and cheer. You scream. The hole in the floor swallows you completely. How deep does this go? You seem to be gaining speed with no end in sight. "Well, I hope he enjoyed his one way trip to Mars." said the Director. The other people in the darkened room on the other side of the mirror nodded, some general grunts of agreement. "Budget cuts, one way trips to Mars aren't cheap," the Director adds. No one in the room really expected them to spend that kind of money. No one wanted to be the one to pull the trigger either to kill the man. This was the perfect compromise.

If LSD or another Psychedelic has left you dangled, confused, afraid and tormented; ... Breathe... In time the trauma will unravel... You have found a difficult path, but you are OK. Living will still have beauty. You are not alone. I have seen total eclipse without hope of day. It took years but I am happy with a loving partner and a healthy sane life. I am a better, more aware, more caring and happier person than I would have been without these experiences. I would not change the choices I've made: It started with 2 hits of Blue Microdot. The 16 hours or more of tripping was only the beginning. It took years for me to stitch myself back together. I ate 1 and a Half hits of LSD, and I insufillated another half. Then I smoked about.2 grams of Hash. All ready I felt uneasy, that something wasn't right. It didn't take long before nothing was right. It is unexplainable... Beyond a thought, or feeling, or sense. A door opened... I was flooded with a new " seeing ." I was unprepared and resisted. This is when I met with insanity. I won't go into the details of my complex and confused mind. It still give me shivers. I'll just say that without a doubt that I was now insane, and going to stay that way for the rest of my life. Metaphors grew out of nothing. A string of strange coincidences and some strong acid made me believe that I was suddenly in on some syndicate that operated on a psychic level., through metaphors and " feelings ." I was being welcomed into the circle. Insanity was a network. I didn't want to be a part of but it was too late. Then I " realized " I wasn't insane but " dead " I had Overdosed on LSD (I now know this is impossible) and I was riding in limbo needing to choose heaven or hell. My cousin who I was close to all my life was cool with smoking cigarettes, weed and was high on the same LSD (having a great time with it I might add) became to me, a manifestation of Satan. My older brother who was as clean as they come and totally naive to drugs became to me a manifestation of Jesus. Of course I followed him around all night bugging the shit out of him to take me to heaven. This scared the ever living shit out of him. At one point I pissed my pants on purpose to try and convince myself I was still alive... But the trip had roots... and that was not enough to snap me out of it. I was willing to do anything he suggested... However with his inexperience he would tell me to do things like go to sleep... Go lay down in my room with the lights off. There my body would feel as though it was disappearing.... That I was slipping into hell. (I wish now that I would have let go and experienced my inner workings). I lept out of bed and did anything I could think of to get to heaven. I even tried calling my parents who were away on vacation. I went through my peak doing these random and frantic things as I was certain I was going to fall into hell at any moment. That night was long. As my cousin and I came down from our trips he ultimately talked me into finally going to bed and getting some sleep... I don't recall if I actually ever slept. He left the next afternoon. What is most formative and important is the week, and then, years afterward. A journey few people will ever make in this life. The first week I spent afraid, confused, unable to eat or sleep. Alone in a true dementia. I'd watch Television and it would be spewing messages directly to me. EVERYTHING was a metaphor for heaven or hell, or a message from this syndicate. I began to believe this blanket of metaphor was a secret code that the world spoke and I was getting hip to it. Going down to Strawberry fields. Still, nothing really made sense... all a jumble. One night that week I went to a friends house and believed every sentence they said to one another was linked to my dementia. Another close friend, who definitely knew I was in trouble said that he believed life was a test... and that everything had a reasonable and rational answer. Dunno if that's absolutely true, but it snapped me into my first taste of reality in over a week. I decide it was time to drive home to my parents house to reconcile my mind. I entered the house not really knowing what to say or do... I began telling them about this experience I had... Telling them that I had achieved a higher state of consciousness... etc. They looked frightened and confused. I realized that so was I. Suddenly I broke down... Began telling them about my use of LSD, Marijuana and other Drugs, how I was out of my mind, paranoid and afraid. Just the facts. My mother cried and my Father listened stone silent. That night was the most relieving and uplifting of my life. Likely the most difficult for my parents... all they could do was listen and hug me... This ladies and gents was way out of there league. I knew it... I knew I was teaching them. What mattered was that I was in a place where I was loved and accepted. I was 16 years old and I slept on the floor at the foot of their bed. I released all my secrets. If there is a sacred confession. This was it... I was cleansed by fire. I felt as though I rose from ashes... and I did. That night I was utterly humbled and humiliated by existence. I was a child again but also evolved. The next week I didn't leave my parents house I helped them with various jobs and house projects... If I found spare time, I'd find something to fill it. It was like every day I died.... and re-awoke. Every day I teetered between heaven and hell. Small decisions like " Which juice shall I buy and drink? " were wrapped in meaning and metaphor that extended beyond daily life, seemingly deciding my eternal fate. Just under everything was a mechanism, a test or a plot... Unraveling. I saw powers that we are all capable of... The power to live or to die any moment... I began seeing through the facades of judgment and morality. My learned belief systems eroded and were replaced with experience. I'd raise my concerns with a close friend who had had similar experiences. He would console me, encourage me to believe in what was in front of me, work with what I knew and be wise not to open up these thoughts to the wrong people, as most would just label me insane and become afraid of me. He was of course totally right and a good friend for his patience and protection. For a time I lived my life shadowing my true thoughts and feelings about daily situations. I made some stunning life decisions. I traveled overseas alone to search my soul and mind. I shed all my addictions, tobacco, TV, caffeine, sex, all drugs, and even meatprocessed foods. This was all between the ages of 16 and 23. It took me over a year till I could even talk to my cousin again. Many more till I could truly trust him. I wish that databases such as Erowid, The Shroomery etc. existed when I went through this journey. Their help could have turned this vicious, horrific and difficult experience into something meaning full and useful from the beginning. Much of my " delusions " weren't so at all. This life, this existence is a blanket of meaning and metaphor. Everything we see, touch, hear is a creation of our own perceptions. This can drive you mad, or make you powerful, exalted and blissful. I am 27 as I write this. The lessons and impressions left by the LSD trip, the full week of dementia and the years of re-evaluating evolved me to a state of consciousness few ever reach. I am at peace with myself and my existence. I don't want to die, but I am virtually unafraid of it. I see through the bullshit of war, violence and destruction. I seek and participate in peace. I believe we all wish to. LSD helped push these to the front of my consciousness. I had to go through hell. But these moments I now live are truly awake and free. To this day I wonder if I'm actually " alive " or if I'm alone - A drifting consciousness lingering in an endless construct of my own imagination - It doesn't matter really. I found peace.

"You're proposing we end it?" "Let's face it. They've over-run the planet. It's just not self-sustaining anymore." "They're so majestic, though..." "Doctor, it seems to me that you've become somewhat..... attached" "Maybe. We've been watching a long time after all." "We took an oath to remain objective. That's how science works. " "Yes, but wiping out whole species..." "They've done that several times all on their own. We would just be taking the decision out of their hands." "Don't sugarcoat it. That's genocide and you know that as well as me." "It's our right. We made them." "Still..." Silence. Then..... "We ought to step back. This obviously isn't working." "Just let someone else handle it?" "Precisely." "Have they decided what to run next then?" "Since Project D is quite clearly a failure, they decided to go with something a bit more economical: Project H." "Those things will never survive. Who's running it?" "New guy. Can't remember his name. Yawley? Yellwen?" "Never heard of him." "It's on the tip of my tongue. Huh, damn it. Guy just had a kid. Showed the pictures around the office. Kid's name was Jesse I think." "You mean Lou's brother?" "Yeah, him." "Damn. They get younger every year. I was going grey when I got my first lead." "I was there too. I remember." "Yeah. Maybe it's time to retire. I've got a nice beach house picked out and everything."

Quicksilver was slated to be a box office hit. The anticipatory buzz, however, came to a screeching halt as headlines everywhere screamed "Quicksilver director DENIES Stan Lee traditional cameo!" Fans were outraged, boycotts were called. Stan Lee himself remained quiet on the matter, allowing his legions of followers to helm the front lines. Neckbeards and casual fans alike voiced their opposition with varying degrees of fervor. This, in a political climate wrought with division and on the brink of collapse, had united the people. This had given them a truly common enemy, an insidious tormentor, a man fueled by the suffering of the innocent. He had betrayed the creator, and he had to be punished. The punishment: utter hatred from the entire world. Sure, there were some who agreed with the director in his choice to not include Stan Lee in the summer blockbuster. But they were quickly dismissed as invalid, and ultimately vultures to controversy. Pundits criticized the public for focusing on so trivial of a matter, entreating that the situation bore no significance to our reality as a civilization. They too were quickly hushed as everything political, economic, judicial, societal, and meaningful had been honed down to this singular issue. Stan Lee was the Creator. This betrayal grew to be compared to Lucifer's, the mythical betrayal of God himself. On the day of the premiere, only a handful of thirsty and oblivious celebrities showed up, only to quickly retreat upon seeing the hordes of protestors violently opposing any who dared enter. The situation rapidly deteriorated into a riot, with several people seriously injured in the frantic clouds of tear gas and smoke. That very next day, Stan Lee was found dead in his home, he had passed away comfortably in his sleep, never to enact his final cameo. He had helped to build an entire universe, rich with history and memorable characters. He had but one wish, to be a part of the universe to which he had given such bursting life. As news of his tragic death reached all corners of the globe, all hell broke loose, and the director of Quicksilver had to flee for his life. Christopher Nolan sat in the back of a Mom and Pop barbecue joint. He'd taken up smoking, and Ms. Simmons didn't mind, as long as he kept that back door open and didn't light up while other customers were inside. He had found comfort in the secluded and grungy restaurant, and the Orange Crush barbecue sauce was actually insanely delicious on pulled pork. Frank Underwood is on to something..... , he pondered with a chuckle. It was the little things, they were all he had. Years ago, he had made an agreement. He had promised his life away. He had agreed to become a pariah, forever shunned by the people of the world. This was the final stage: unity. Thousands of political experts, statisticians, economists, psychologists, behavioral analysts, and secret volunteer operatives had pulled together in the shadows to reach a singular goal: the unification of the American people. There was to be one scapegoat, one who would achieve greatness, become powerful, and finally commit a crime so heinous, so beyond the scope of current perceptions of evil, that the people would set aside their differences to strangle their truest traitor. Christopher was not only a traitor to tradition, but he was a traitor to freedom, happiness, well-being, truth, light. He was the epitome of evil in every sense, in every American mind. He sat smoking as a familiar shadow graced the threshold of the joint's back door. Christopher smiled. Stan Lee entered the room and stood there for a minute, lamentation on his face. He glanced at Nolan's burning cigarette, then to the stub on Chris's left side, where his arm used to be. Stan Lee stifled a heavy sob, years of emotional bottling had culminated to this point, but his training allowed him to remain composed no matter what. "Chris..... We did it." "We did, didn't we." Christopher absentmindedly caressed his phantom arm. "It's finished, the timeline has been corrected! We've done it..." Stan gazed at the broken man in front of him. " ..... you've done well, I'm sorry about your "All part of the game, sir. I'm grateful for the opportunity to be of use to mankind." "It's almost time, Chris." "I know sir..... I'll miss you. You've always been a great mentor to me, ever since that day in Constantinople, when it all began." Christopher smiled. "It was your father who rescued me. Without you both, I'd be dead with a spear between my eyes." Stan laughed. "If they'd studied you, they'd have worshipped you as a god. Even knowing the truth, I sometimes marvel at how well you played the part," Christopher said with a chuckle and a slight cough. Stan Lee approached the young man before him and held his hand with comforting fatherly warmth. "It'll be centuries, but we'll meet again. It will be a day of celebration. October 13th 2742. Until then, this world needs you, my boy. The Angel of Earth, the Planetary Protector, the Invincible Inhabitant..... My friend." As Stan released Chris's remaining hand, the young man began to change shape. His features melted into a metallic mercurial fluid. Within seconds, he had been reformed into an entirely different person. He no longer resembled Hollywood Director Christopher Nolan, most hated man on earth. He no longer resembled anyone. He was now a nameless human, about 5' 8" 160lbs. with a slightly asymmetric-but-average face. "Thank you," Christopher said, getting used to having two arms again, flexing his new fingers, feeling his new face, his newest form. "See you later, Bub. You're gon na have a great life, I've seen it. Say hi to Carla for me, that'll blow her mind later on." Stan said with a smirk, laughter bubbling. "Who is Carla?" Before he could get an answer, Stan popped out of existence, as if he were a bubble. Christopher, or whatever he'd eventually come to call himself, smiled. Before he left he put a hefty tip on the table for Mrs. Simmons, and tossed the half-full pack of cigarettes into the trash, the sweet smell of Crush Sauce lingering on him as he walked out into the sunshine again.

Uhh I groan, It's bright, too bright. Everything hurts. It's like there's a cloud in my head, nothing's quite straight..... Who am I? I lift my hand, feeling strange cracks in my arm as ice turns to liquid. Blood? The cryogenic research strange words pop in my head. I hazily turn my head to a man standing in triumph. For some reason I remember being stabbed. The research was getting too far? Ohh it hurts too much, I start to lay back down, ready to go back to sleep. "Aha no you don't old buddy, tell the people about yourself" The man makes strange noises. No..... He's speaking. "J-John.." The crowd bursts into applause. He turns and smiles at me. "Don't worry, I'm only doing this because your wife just wouldn't stop going on about the injustice of your death, it was really quite hard to sleep sometimes." He whispers in my ear, but none of it registering. "You can go back to sleep soon enough."

It is common knowledge amongst the people of Earth that gold comes from the ground. It is also common knowledge that unicorns only exist in one's imagination. However, it is common knowledge amongst other species that human knowledge is wrong. The story if gold, the scientific explanation of most precious elements was nothing but an elaborate ruse the Unicorns liked to play on humans. Long ago, they shifted into human form, and blended into the crowd of humans fuelled by their greed. They preached these theories, how all the shiny metals were worth something. Gold was seldom found back then, and when it was, it just so happened to be by a unicorn. Of course, as the unicorns were disguised, they were perceived as humans. They told stories of how they came across it near that lake or that river, and the humans trusted and worshiped their every word for the sole reason that they seemed trustworthy. The majestic aura that all unicorns posessed seem to translate into a godlike quality in the eyes of the humans. From then on, they made a living off selling gold and other riches that they had fooled mankind into thinking came from the Earth. However, as it was already established, mankind's knowledge is often wrong, and in this case plain unicornshit. And so the unicorns lived on, surrounded in their majestic aura and riches.

Consciousness filtered in slowly as I flopped over in bed, hoping to drift back off. My alarm hadn't gone off yet - and I was going to get whatever moments more sleep I could! Unfortunately, the bed was smaller than it should have been. Instead of flopping onto my favourite (extra floofy) pillow, I flopped halfway off the bed. The sudden drop and subsequent throwing out of my arms to stop myself from tumbling out ruined any possibility of going back to sleep. Confused and groggy, I hauled myself back up onto the single, 101 dalmatians print bed. I couldn't have fallen out of bed. My bed is surrounded on all sides by walls, shelving and a desk. There's only a less than a metre gap at the bottom to get out of. Finally, what I was seeing filtered in. Those little people toys - what were they called? - Oh yes, playmobile littered the floor. White shelves and toys. A window with light filtering - very different to my own bolted shutters. What the absolute fuck. My brain stuttered and started, trying to process what was happening. My hands flew to my face - small, slightly pudgy with puppy fat. Then my hands pulled back - tiny, childish things. Panic filled me. I slapped myself. It was a dream, clearly. My dreams have always been realistic - but usually not my own history. I carefully eased out of bed. What wouldn't have even been considered a drop twenty years from now suddenly seemed like quite a height to lower myself. I opened my bedroom door, peaking out. My childhood home. My bedroom was still cream. So I was..... before seven, at least. A noise startled me and I turned - only to see my beloved childhood dog Susan wagging both her tail and bottom furiously. I didn't even have to kneel over to pet her, she seemed so big! Even so, I ended up sitting there with her, hugging her, telling her how much I loved her. What a good dog she was. As I sat there, partially clinging to Susan, I took stock. The more I woke up, the less this seemed like a dream. It was still early, maybe about 7am. No one would be awake for hours..... I think. I don't remember much from this period of my life. Maybe waking up at 1pm wasn't normal for mum at this point. Locating what appeared to be my school bag, I found the date. 1997. Fuck, 1997. Was this real? Did it matter? My brain whirled. I didn't know if it was real or not, but ultimately..... on the chance it was? I walked up to the kitchen - God I was so short! Stairs seemed so much bigger. I had to use a chair to reach the counters. My memory of this time was so hazy. I don't know if it had happened yet, but I didn't care. I could at least stop what would happen to mum. They'd hate me, but it would be better in the long run. Everything would be better for them. I took a knife, the biggest, sharpest one I could find. I found the packing tape and secured it to my hand and arm as well as I could - little hands mean weak hands. I refused to be stopped midway. Briefly, sadly, I realised my little brothers would never exist. I loved those two. They're hilarious little fuckers. I'm so proud of them. But it's better this way. Down the stairs from the kitchen, and up the opposite stairs to the bedroom. I hid the knife behind me - creeping as quietly as I could. Mum and dad were asleep. God, mum looked so young. So many lines and etches simply non-existent on her face. She looked so happy. I wondered what she looked like awake - that night had changed her. I don't know this woman. I would have liked to, I think. I was hesitating. I'd get caught before I did what had to be done if I kept at it. Going around the right side of the bed, I looked down at my sleeping father. The man who destroyed everything. Who hurt mum. Who fucked me up for years. Who traumatised me so badly that twenty years later I'm still recovering repressed memories. The reason I don't remember anything about most of my childhood. Again, I hesitate. My poor older brother. My poor mum. They won't understand. They won't know. They still don't entirely know, even in the future. I mourn my little brothers that I love so much. I thrust the knife down with all my strength into his eye socket - the easiest, most lethal place for me to penetrate with my tiny arms. Dad wakes up, screaming, trying to push me off. Mum wakes up with a start, clearly confused and startled. I use my other arm to shove the knife-taped one deeper. I feel something give way. A squishing noise. Dad's face still looks like he's screaming, but sound stopped coming out. The arms scratching and pushing and clawing at my tiny body fall limp. My mother's screams echo in my ears. With all the strength in my little self, I pull the knife from the socket and sprint. Back down the stairs, back up the opposite stairs, through the kitchen - blood dripping from my equipped arm the whole way. I slam my way out the backdoor, running as fast as my legs will carry me. Out into the garden, up the hill, around the bed, into the shrubbery surrounding out home. I still remember where my tree is - the tallest one where I found a crows nest at the top. The one that years from now - and years ago - gave me a fear of heights after I fell from it, the only thing saving my life was being lucky enough to hit branches on the way down that slowed my fall yet didn't hit anywhere that would injure me permanently. I don't even bother removing the knife, I just scramble my way up the tree. I can hear my mum screaming my name now. And just screaming in general. I find it difficult to grab the branches with my taped, bloodsoaked hand - but I reach the top quicker than I thought possible. I take a moment, remembering how I used to feel on top of the world up here. Looking down at my home town at the bottom of the hill, feeling the wind cut through me, the bark biting my bare feet, seeing the beautiful pink and orange morning sky light up the sea in the distance below me. And I jump.
