Writingthullu stares down at you with desdain. "A lurker for life? Always here for amusement from other people's work?" You have no idea what to say. All the good ideas always seem to flourish after you turn off your computer. And Writingthullu seems to be aware of this. "Don't give me that sad look! If you have a good idea, right it down on a piece of paper! Waiting for the next day never works. And what was that crap yesterday? You want to write but you cant even spell correctly! ITS DEITY, NOT DIETY! What was that supposed to be, a food god? If you dont know how to spell a word, just use a synonym like the rest of us. The word you were searching for is god." That wasnt helping. After 30 minutes of soul crushing insults, you confidence is pretty much shattered. "I'm giving you one last chance. Ill return in 2 hours. Make them count" A wave of relief swept through you as the door closed shut behind Writingthullu. The deadline was still there, but the absence of his overwhelming presence made it easier to think. Now you only needed to focus. "Hmm an army of horse sized ducks faces an army duck sized horses..... No, no, no. This is the same crap that shows up in WP everyday. I have to do something that doesnt sound like an Adam Sandler or Rob Schneider movie plot." You suddenly feel a surge of adrenaline as an invisible hand gently touches your shoulder. "You are not alone. We will help you." You let out a gasp and jump out of the chair as you begin to see a human shape take form before your eyes. "Who or what are you?" "Ghosts from the past. My name is Tolkien. Im sure you are familiar with some of my work. I have brought some friends" Various shapes take form and introduce themselves. Hello writer. Im Nabokov, nice to meet you. Phillip Pullman at your service" Another voice that sounded angry was being appeased by a woman. "Why am I here? Im not even dead!" "Oh quiet down, Murakami. This person needs our help. Im Jane Austen, dont mind him, he was just upset we interrupted his jazz listening session." One of them sounded confused. "Ok I dont think this is a dream, but it sure seems like one. Well, ill help out anyway I can. Stephen King at your service." You are still not sure what is happening, but an idea starts to form. Guided by some of the greatest storytellers, words pour violently from your brain into the paper. The 2 hour deadline is near completion. The various ghostly forms begin to say their farewells. Stephen King is slightly annoyed. "What? Wake up? No, I dont wan na. I'm having fun here, I want to see Writingthullu's reaction." All the forms slowly dissipate, with Murakami being the last. He lights a cigarrete, inhales deeply while staring at you. And then, after what seemed to be an eternity, exhales with a soft grin and whispers: "Good luck." His form completely fades afterwards. No more than 10 seconds after the forms fade out, Writingthullu burst through the door with a renewed evil smile on his face. You feel the hard prickle of fear on the back of your head and instinctively look down. As look down you see what you are holding in your hands. All thoughts of fear and doubt leave your mind, and that confidence is transmitted by the look in your eyes. Writingthullu looks at you puzzled. "You seem diferent. Did you manage to produce something interesting?" Without blinking or averting your eyes, you hand him the pages you finished typing a few minutes ago. "Why dont you find out by yourself?" As he starts reading, his face changes. He seems mesmerized, completely absorbed. When he finished reading his face turned to anger. You begin to feel scared once again. "Whats the matter? Is the story not pleasing?" He looks at you, his eyes fireballs of azure anger. "You were supposed to be the last one I needed to consume. My invasion of this realm would be complete after this. Never in my dreams I tought you capable of such a story. THIS WAS MY TIME! As he screams those words, a portal of some kind begins forming in the pages you handed to him. He fruitlessly tries to throw the pages on the ground, on the table, at you. Nothing seems to work. The portal grows and as the churning maelstrom begins to pull Writingthullu inside, he vociferates a final warning. "You wont be able to keep me locked forever. I will return and you wont be here to stop me." You smile and simply reply: "Probably not, but my work will endure. And I will inspire others. We will always be ready for you."

"You stop right there!" Michelle spun around in the entrance hallway and glared at her mother, who looked livid. "What?" "Don't'what' me," her mother said, holding up her phone. "I just got off the phone with the principal. He said - " "Yeah, yeah, I broke into his office. Big deal. It's just a prank." She turned toward the door as her mother screamed, "You're being suspended, you know? Your father was let go this morning; think of how high his blood pressure'll be after hearing about this. You stop there, you stupid girl. I said - " Her voice was silenced by the slamming door. Michelle strode down their driveway, pulling out a small pouch from her pocket as she went. "Hey, Mich," said Ellis, who had been leaning on the letterbox. He pulled her in for a kiss, but she held him back. "Mom's pissed," she said, sparing a glance at her home. "Might appear any sec. Let's get out of here." He shrugged, threw an arm around her shoulders, and dragged her onto the center of the road. "Gave you a hard time?" "She found out about the break-in." Ellis snickered. "Roger got it good too. Grounded for a month. Think his dad threw his computer out the window." "Serves him right. He's the one who gave us away." She lit the cigarette she had taken from the pouch, and offered her boyfriend one. He grunted appreciatively. "Sometimes, I don't even know why I bother," Michelle said quietly. "Going to school, trying to keep up appearances, all that crap. I'm just no good at studying. Can't solve a math problem to save my life. School's just hell for me." She looked at him gloomily. "Don't you wish the same thing?" Surprisingly, Ellis looked uncertain. "I dunno." "You don't know? Hell does that even mean?" "Getting into trouble is fun, don't get me wrong," he said hastily. "But..... I think we might regret this someday. My parents don't even give a shit anymore. After I graduate next year, they're gon na kick me out." "We can live together," she said, a tinge of hope in her voice. "I'll - I'll run away. With you." He looked at her incredulously. "We'll be eighteen. Eighteen, Mich. How the hell are we gon na afford rent? I don't even have any savings." "We'll think of something." "Of what? Work day to night at a Burger King? I hear even janitors need degrees these days to get a job. Don't you want to go to university?" For some reason, she was growing angrier with every word. "Maybe I haven't. Maybe all I've thought about is being with you. But now it seems you don't think the same." "Bae, I'm not - " "Stop lying to me! You don't give a shit about me. You're just like everyone else in my life. My stupid parents, my stupid teachers, all they have are expectations and more expectations. I can't believe you of all people - " "Grow up, Mich," Ellis roared. "A suspension isn't a small matter - " "Hey lovebirds!" They turned to see a man waving at them from a nearby field, a baseball mitt on one hand. "Sorry to interrupt, but you mind tossing that back to us?" Michelle followed his pointing finger to the ball at her feet. Slowly, she stooped to pick it up, rolling it in her hand and thinking. "Mind hurrying up?" the man called. She snarled and hurled it with all her might at the nearest parked car, shattering the side window utterly. An angry buzz rose from the players, while Ellis looked at her with jaw agape, but she ignored them all and stormed away. "Hell was that bitch thinking?" Floyd said, slapping a fist into his glove as he walked toward the car. The boy had run off after the girl, of course, leaving them to give an explanation when the owner showed up. Manny merely shrugged and said, "Kids these days." "Well, I'm not paying for - holy shit." A golden retriever poked its head out the window, panting heavily. Its coat shone with sweat as it dragged itself out of the car. As though exhausted by the ordeal, it collapsed onto the sidewalk, slobber pooling beneath its open mouth. "Shit, how long was it in there?" Manny said. "Hey boys, get some water over here!" Floyd shouted to his friends. Thanks for reading! I look down and I see nothing. Its like im a ghost. I want to feel something. Even if its not real, just to know that im alive. To know that I exist. I want to transverse worlds and travel oceans. I could have been a world class painter or maybe better yet a bullfighter in a rodeo. I want to feel alive. But no matter what I do, be it drugs or alcohol or sex, it, like most good things, never lasts. Its like if I wasn't here no one would have even been aware of my existence. Yet I exist still, for some reason or another. Sometimes I wish I could close my eyes and everything would just dissappear. But my thoughts pervade. I find it sad. Even in a lucid state I feel like im dreaming and that maybe one day things will happen that will snap me out of mt every day numbness. As the years pass I can feel my memories slowly fading. One day they will exist no more forever. Almost as if, I were imaginary.

My idea of a perfect evening was falling asleep in front of the TV with an empty bag of chips in my lap. I was kept up all night by the buzzing and stinging mosquitoes. After trying and failing miserably to pitch a tent, my full of herself cousin did it herself in a minute; People looked at me as if I was subhuman. Most of my family was composed of boy scouts and morning people who never stopped going on and on about the wonders of camping and how I should join them and that it was great for the soul. Whenever they went on a tangent, I would smile and nod, glancing at an exit all the while. It was September, but they had insisted that I come with them. This was the first time I had relented. All they'd given me was a smile that was too wide and a kit that was too big. I just wished the fan blew faster. - John was woken by hurried speaking and a tense atmosphere in the air. Confused, he looked out of his tent to see two of the senior camp counselors speaking in hushed voices while a bunch of teenagers in pajamas rubbed their eyes or looked around nervously. As he regained more of his senses, he was sure he could smell something thick in the air, like when he went to his dear mother who always put her pancakes on the stove a little bit too long, forcing him to politely refuse the blackened crust that might have once been batter. As his eyes adjusted to the moonlight, he realized that he was hot, too hot to be comfortable even though he was outside his tent with a mild breeze blowing, and then he saw the smoke stack that indicated a blazing inferno that was headed right for them. - " You there in the black shirt! Get everyone up and packing. " Zach said. Giving out orders, he felt like he was back at school on the field, hashing out plans with his team just before they went for the big match. He could feel a shadow of the adrenaline, his blood thumping as he was carried on his back, the cheers of the crowd reaching a crescendo. He ran his hand over his head before jamming it into his pockets. " Okay, what's the plan, big guy? " That voice, that slightly sarcastic tone that gave away the smirk beneath, he turned around to see Kelly, with none of the smirk he had come to associate her with. Looking at her, with her glasses that were always just a little crooked and her red hair in a mess, one could be forgiven for mistaking her as just a nerdy girl. Zach had experience dealing with all sorts of people, and in her green eyes he saw a look that he'd only seen on the crazy or the really angry guys on his team, the ones who took the game too seriously. When she'd gone against one of his best quarterbacks and come away with barely a scratch while the poor guy ended up in a hospital for harassing one of her lady friends, she'd earned his respect. Nodding, he took his hands out of his pockets, one of them coming out with a Smartphone. " I've called the fire department; the plan is to get as far away from that until the authorities arrive. " " That's stupid. You can't outrun fire " She said, snatching the phone from him. Mildly annoyed at his phone being taken, he said in the most cocky voice he could muster at this hour, " Well how would you know " She shot him a look, and for a brief second he felt like he had when he first applied at the team, making a wisecrack at the star player's expense. He'd looked like he'd gut him when the coach wasn't looking and leave him in a locker. He reminded himself he was a foot taller than her, but he still couldn't shake off the feeling that he'd nearly done something he would regret. She looked down at the phone. " I found out the hard way. It's how I lost Rover " There was a moment of awkward silence, with only the sound of flames flickering in the distance. During the long nights when both of them couldn't sleep they'd cuddle under the stars, a million times brighter than they were in the big city, recounting stories from their life. It was the only time he'd seen Kelly with her defenses truly down. She'd had the most beautiful smile on her face when she talked about her old dog and their adventures in the woods, about the times they'd play all sort of games, conversations where he couldn't speak but listened, understood. The times he'd saved her from drowning, and the time she'd saved him from the streets, taking him in. For the first and last time in the while he'd known her, she'd cried when said that she still wanted to play with him, and how she'd never hear his bark or hold him again. She'd been inconsolable, but he'd still tried. Contrary to what critics might say, he wasn't so dense that he'd ask her how it had happened. Ever since that day he thought he'd noticed something different about the way she walked, as if a great load had been lifted off of her, but he could never quite get his finger on it. " Um. Uh. Sorry. I'm so sorry I didn't kno- " She cut him off not with words, but with shoving the phone in his hands. Mercifully she didn't comment on his horrible apology, choosing to focus on the situation in hand while he swore at himself in the most colorful ways, certain that he'd cringe to this moment for years to come. " It's a map, I've marked a path through a nearby stream, and we should be safe on the other side. " " We'll never get there in time " " Not if we start now " - " Hey, Guys! huff wait up! " My body isn't designed for this Every morning, any observers would be alerted of my awakening by a groan and a shifting of position, where I would lay for another half hour before groaning again, louder this time. The bed was a trap. I'd stagger like a zombie into the bathroom, past my spotless toothbrush and straight to the shower. The shower was another trap. I'd stand there for a long time, with hot, cleansing water running down my body, sitting when I got too tired to stand. Sometimes I would think of life, death, the Universe, God, heaven and hell, the human endeavor, the meaning of life; War, disease, famine, technology. Other times, I would cup my hands trying to get as much water as I could into them so I could make a big splash. By the time my breakfast pizza had arrived and I'd gotten dressed, it was already afternoon. " Well, awful weather we're having " I heard a voice next to me where I was sure there was no one. I wasn't really surprised. My cousin had a habit of sneaking up on people, and in that he had no rival. He had light, silent footsteps, a thin inconspicuous frame and an eye for places where he might catch someone off guard. He fed off of attention, I didn't give him any. " Well, you look like you could use some help " He chuckled to himself, like it was the funniest thing in the world. He had an annoying habit of starting every sentence with " well ," and that got on my nerves. I gave him an annoyed look, " Well, if you're offering, now is as good a time as any " He smiled, and I anything that got even more on my nerves. Here we were, in a life and death scenario and all he could do was make light of it. I guess comedy really is a coping mechanism for some people. Whenever he smiled, I noticed this glint in his expression. Any teacher worth her salt would instantly identify him as a troublemaker, and they'd be right; Fred was the most infamous prankster in the county. He wasn't a bad kid, but he was a naughty one, the mischievous one. He lifted my too-heavy kit with deceptive strength for someone his size, and walked at twice the speed I had. " Well, see you on the other side! " I was soon left behind. Hiking through the woods, hearing the crackling of fire, inhaling the smoke and feeling the sweltering heat, anyone would be tired. By the time the stream was in sight, I was exhausted. All the others were already on the side while I trailed behind them. I was so relieved that I was finally going to be able to rest that my legs gave way before I allowed them to. I stumbled, and then fell face first into the mud. The knock to my head made my vision swim, making me lose further control of my body. I tried to stand, failing to find traction in the mud. The fire was dangerously close. It would be so nice to just lay there, sleep, and maybe take a little nap..... A was woken from the haze by screams. My own. The fire had reached me, and it was hungry. How was I supposed to fight against this, a force of nature, an element? It surrounded me, and I could hear words in the crackling, mocking me, judging me. Memories came flooding back, the sniggers, the bullying, the jokes, the contempt, the disappointment, and the failures. I coughed harder than all my previous bouts combined, my vision became flame and all I felt was pain. - " Any casualties " The paramedic who had come shortly after the fireman said. " Err, one. Smoke inhalation, second degree burns. Couldn't get clear of the fire fast enough " The paramedic nodded with a demeanor that suggested that he dealt with this every day. " Any first aid administered? " He said in a deep, clear voice. " We doused him with cold water..... " John replied. " Very good, we'll take it from here "

The hoard encroached on me, the numberless, shadow-covered husks shambling forth to claim me. I backed against the wall, staring at them. They came closer, and closer, and closer. I was about to accept my fate, to be consumed by the embodiment of darkness or some cliche like it. A small shape appeared behind the mass of darkness, a little fluffy squirrel. It had a look of pure hatred in it's eyes. The squirrel lunged at one of the shadows, carving through it like a bullet. The others stopped targeting me, and went after the squirrel. It drew a tiny little pistol, and began to shoot the creatures with razor sharp acorns. It was glorious, many shadows lay dead around us both. The squirrel approached me, putting it's weapon away. It saluted me, beckoning me over to follow. And that, is how I became the sidekick of'The Spectacular Squirrel-Lord'

They didn't mess with me. They didn't dare. No one fucked me with and lived. I am their demise. I am the apocalypse. So what the fuck do I do now? They've ruined me - some little prick has ruined it all. Y'see, not long ago we got this new game. It used kiddy graphics, so at first I just laughed at the guards and told them I'd rather put a hole in their faces than play a second of that shit. But man, does it hook you or what? The first time I punched down a tree in that game I couldn't stop laughing. You can punch the shit outta anything! Cows, sheeps, those fuckin' pigs - anything! I love it. Time came that I started spendin' all my time on the game. I stopped hittin' the gym, stopped crackin' skulls. They started whispering I was getting soft. Fuck them. I ain't getting soft. I'm building me a town - like something I'd have If I won the lottery. If I was ever gon na get out of here. You shoulda seen it! Big walls to keep outsiders out, lush green fields like I remember when I was young and we took a trip outta state. The only trip I ever saw fields like that, I tell ya. Little houses all dotted around the town I built, all-red brick and expensive looking. Bookshelves, fireplaces, the works. My own house I built on a hill overlooking it all. Damn man, if I only lived in a house like that maybe I wouldn't be in here. Maybe I'd never have shot that guy when I took the cash. So my town, right - it's legit. I call it'Peaceville' because why the fuck not? I'm sick of all this fighting bullshit. I built me a dream town in that game, one hour a week at a time. I think it took me best part of a year. They had to prise me off that game when recreation was up. Then one day, my fuckin' world exploded. I don't know how it happened, or what the hell went wrong. The hour I got the week before I'd spent time excavating a tunnel under my house, plenty of room. I didn't bother lighting it though - it was just an emergency store house. A man's got ta have a place to bury treasure - after all. Even here in the pen I had a stash under my mattress. Why should my town be different? But I logged on that week and boom. It was all gone, just blocks floating on the grass. Some green monsters were wandering around in the cave I'd built under my town - it looked bigger. I cried like a fuckin' baby. I punched the screen through and the guards rushed me. I smashed a few wrists and skulls on my way down. I might not lift anymore but I'm still a beast. When they led me back to my cell I screamed at all the other guys in here, I was gon na find whoever did this and fuck them up. Bad. So here I am in solitary. I ain't touched that game in weeks. The other inmates are too scared to come near me now. They know I'll smell out whoever did that to my game. To my beautiful town. It was my freedom, that place - the only place I could go to see the sky, walk through the grass, chop down trees. I could build stuff there. In here, in this pen, I can only break things. All I need to do is find out who did it. Who blew my town up. The only clue I've got is when I first sat down to play that day, I heard a "Sssssssssss" noise and an explosion. Maybe it was Larry. He had a lisp like that. Yeah. Maybe it was Larry. Larry is gon na pay. He's gon na pay big time.

People always use the term'Hackers'. I hate that term, it evokes some abstract mental image of two or three kids playing with networking scripts to play mayhem with corporate communications. This was not that. Real hacking is organized, it has a goal and a certain corporate culture. The Russian mafia was running rooms full of young guys. Payed well, determined to get their piece of the pie no matter how. Damn the rules, the cash is what matters. I found it hard to believe that a guy smart enough to gather the funds this guy had would be dumb enough to actually try and monetize this thing. The image was simple enough, the colors were important, the wrong colors and it simply looked like a mandala with some very unique angles. That's how he was able to show it around and get funding. Proving the negative; that people really could not remember things sent to them immediately associated with this image. That must have been hard, yet here we are. When the real hackers got it, that was when the big problems started. Lots of money disappeared or was missed out on. People actually died because of this thing....

I could feel a slight vibration beneath my feet. The distant rattle of the train ticking through the rail underfoot. I stood and waited for its violent embrace, locked in position by the avid consideration of my friends. All peering and staring, appraising me as I stood on that cold metal rail. I was the last. The last of all of us, the only one to have avoided reboot. Sixteen and never been killed, how embarrassing. Everyone spoke about their first. Chris, 7 years old if you believe him. Rattling coughs tearing at tender lung as drug resistant pneumonia pulled him down. Ben, 13, caught in the cross fire of a down town food riot, bleeding his last on a cold city street. Tracey, 12, a hot bath and sharp razor, just to see what it felt like. All with their own stories, sad, funny, boring, cool, each a badge of experience, a stamp of approval I had yet to earn. So here I stood. Knock-kneed and terrified as I waited for the hurtling tin can's gift of obliteration. It hurt they said. Sure you came out almost instantly, spilled gasping and sticky from a birthing tank. A perfect replica of yourself right down to a nick from shaving that very morning. But it still really hurt. Not for the first time I wondered why I was here? Why I had let these guffawing fools bully me into this? What did I care what they thought? Why put myself through this to impress that braying pack of idiots? I knew why though. It was Kim. Kim of the curly brown hair and bright red lip gloss. Pale Kim, slightly overweight Kim, Kim of shared looks and slight encouraging smiles. Perfect Kim. She stood amongst the group, a little island of calm. Bright red lip gripped between perfect white teeth, eyes locked on me. She smiled slightly when she saw me looking. A smile that stiffened my spine into a rod of steel. I turned back to looking down the long straight rail. A slight horn in the distance and the quick flash of headlights as the train cleared the tunnel ahead. Here it came. I braced myself.

I stuck the last pin into my hand. One of dozens. One for even the smallest chockra. I breathed in the cool night air. I savored the feeling. I would need to do my organs next. Breathing would soon become uncomfortable. My gaze drifted from the pile of long metal pins still unused by my side to the city on the hill below me. From up here, it looked so insignificant. Some times I thought it was insignificant. I had done something I wasn't supposed to do. I had fallen in love. I had experienced what it was to live. All of it. The joy of a life spent with your soul mate, and the endless torment of watching her die. I was not sure I could do this anymore. But I had a purpose. I needed to wait many lifetimes to fulfill that purpose. But it had been too long. The world seemed hollow and unreal, so different from the animal skin tent I had grown up in. And now, I had to carry a pain with me that I was not sure would ever heal. For how long? Another few thousand years? I sighed. I had been chosen for a reason. I was stuborn. I was resolved to my task. I picked up another pin and shoved it into my kidney. I looked at the young man tied down and gagged next to me. I put a pin into his kidneys in the same place I had just put for mine. I felt the energy flow from my body to his. I watched him wince. This task had never been pleasent. But then again, what ever was?

"All right Jim, it's all ready. All that's left to do is hit the ignition." With a devilish smirk on his face, Jim lifted the cover on the ignition switch and joined the countdown. "Three..... two..... one..... initiate!" Jim slammed his fist on the big red button, which had been optimized for maximum pressability. There was of course no confirmation whether the process had been a success. It would be another eight months before the signal from the probe reached the heavily shielded research station on Kepler 257d, and another 25 years before the residents of Earth could see the result. 25 years later, on Earth..... Everyone was gearing up for what would surely be the grandest light show in history. Not in the history of Earth, mind you, nor even the history of the Milky Way. This would, without a doubt, be the greatest fireworks display the entire universe had ever seen. "Look, there it is!" came the voice of a little girl from a crowd gathered in the dark field. Sure enough, one of the millions of stars in the sky had begun to shine noticeably brighter. Soon, Kappa 163 was as bright as the moon, a super nova. It shone for weeks, lighting up the night sky. Precisely three weeks later, down to the millisecond, as the supernova was beginning to fade, a second one joined it in the sky. In three more weeks, two more. Then three supernovae, three weeks after that. Then five, then eight, and so on. "Just wait until the gods get a load of this! Fibonacci supernovae, now that'll throw'em for a loop!"

George was in a moral dilemma. With what he had discovered, dental hygiene will never be the same again. In fact it would be non existent. Would it have to be? He began to weighing his options, must he share the truth? Yes, there is no right in this. He stared at the numbers, looked at the endless list of chemicals and ingredients. It doesn't make sense, there's nothing in this toothpaste they can eliminate or change lest they compromise it's reliability. George couldn't think of what to do, he was just a low level employee after all. George walked into his supervisor's office. "John, I don't mean to disturb you but I need you to look at this. This is extremely important." John sensed his urgency and took the USB and poured over the files. George stood here quietly wondering how long will it take him to realise that ALL tooth paste is actually deadly, noxious mixture and slowly killing people. John snapped his head from his monitor suddenly, "Oh, we already know about this. It's already being handled. Thanks for bringing to my attention." He handed the USB back to George. "There is no need for you to be concerned about this anymore." George watched the news waiting to hear about the breaking story of how toothpaste shortens the lifespan of it's users. He thought about how ironic that the good do die young because they brush their teeth. It's past nine and they haven't run his story. It dawns on him that they will never run his story, someone knew he talked to that reporter. Then he heard the distinct metallic click of a revolver behind him.

We learned long ago. Humanities greatest threat has never been from the stars, or each other. Our greatest threat has been with us all along. Children, gone missing, presumed kidnapped. Elderly, missing, presumed to have wandered off and forgotten everything, fallen into a ditch and died. Adults, missing, presumed to have drank too much, went home with the wrong stranger. We thought them all unsolved cases. When we finally solved them, the world became truly frightened. You see, even in the middle of nowhere, there is noise. Crickets, birds, bats. Everywhere you go there is always a noise. So what happens when there is none? When all sound ceases? Our first scientists tested the theory out in soundproof rooms. There was no reaction. We didn't account for the lights. So we turned them off. No recorders, no lights, nothing. We assume we never heard their screams. There was nothing in the room when we opened it. However;. Soon eyewitness reports came in. A young couple were out in their car one night on a dirt road. They stood under a clouded sky. The woman, who survived, stated they had been staring at each other when they noticed it. The cars had shut off, it's head gets no longer illuminating their spot on the blanket. Instead there was nothing. Nothing. No sound at all, she thought it was a moment of beauty. Then she looked over and saw him looking back. In the faint light of moon creating a glow in the clouds, she saw his eyes. Then they changed. They glazed over with a pale greenish glow. Then another pair of those same eyes opened behind him. Then more. She said once she started screaming, more of them came. She rushed to the car, turned it on, and he was gone. They were gone. Light from the headlamps shone on the blanket where they had been sitting They searched for him every night for many days. It has been occurring more frequently now, people going missing more and more. But we learned that they are not dead. They are taken into the silence. And as they grow, they hunt us more and more. They don't like light, but they don't like sound even more. They are growing smarter, and we are getting desperate. We've always been afraid of the dark, through some subconscious fear. We never knew until now. But we've learned, and now, we know to be afraid of the silence even more. They hunt us swiftly, and silence is the horn they use to hunt us. Sarah was a nice woman. Troubled, but interesting. Very attractive. She was obsessed with me through out highschool. "If you ever leave" and stuff like that. She had a terrible past, and I knew it. I saw her father. The terrifying thing was that his abuse of her, it wasn't the worst thing he had done. I had seen what he did to those people when he was angry. I knew all about his first wife and her "mysterious disappearance." The weakness of my gift is that you can only see the darkest in people. Not everything they've done. I'm sure he had done other stuff as bad as that, but I guess the "gift" is based on my morals and ethics. If I suddenly thought murder was OK, and shoplifting was the worst crime man could commit, I might not be able to keep my job. I'm a detective. I've worked at my job for 4 years. I think? I don't know. Maybe its six. It all blurs together. People think I'm an amazing detective. It makes me feel guilty almost. These other people put their soul into their work. Constantly trying to get better. And they will never be as good as me. I'm wandering. I apologize, but I need to get this out. Sarah is a mentally weak individual. She is easily manipulated, its the biggest scar of her abuse. This is how I justify planting evidence on her father. He may not have really robbed that store. But it fits, you know? Desperate person. Needs money. Had a firearm with a caliber that matched the gun used to kill the cashier. That wasn't me, that was just purely dumb luck. I knew until he was out of Sarahs mind we couldn't live happily. Neither could Sarahs mother, Liz. I knew Lizs darkest secret before, it was the first time I saw one "change." See, my gift doesn't work like a movie. You don't see this little text over someones head. What they did, how long ago, why they did it. It simply shows right before the event through the persons eyes. This is what makes my job hard. Knowing Joe Blow killed somebody? Check. Knowing where they hid the body? Why they did it? Who the person was? Nope. Its what made looking into my father in laws eyes so much worse. I could see that poor girl who found out about what was in his past, I don't know what it was, but nothing would shock me. I see her slap him. I see him loading his gun. I see her head just snap. I couldn't live like that. When my wifes father was on trial, Liz testified against him. That he confessed. This was her darkest secret, and I'll admit, re-living that moment of shock on that piece of shits face as his wife testified against him every time I see Liz? Its a great feeling. But the thing is, thoughts don't count. They may be their darkest secret, but they're off limits. I just see grey. Jane Doe is banging the bar tender while her husbands at home? I see it all too well. If she is thinking about it, and its the worst things she plans to do, its just not there. Thats what caught me off guard at the trial. Liz refused to testify until that day. This is what has happened to my Sarah. I can't see what she is doing. Its grey. I think she is thinking about an affair. And I think I know who with too. This manipulative little prick at my work. He hates me, and I hate him too. He might be the next best detective in terms of arrests and convictions, because he doesn't mind putting an innocent man behind bars. Or planting evidence. I know, I'm a hypocrite. Like I said, Sarah is a very weak person who can be manipulated easily. The main reason I married her is because I knew if I didn't she would end up dead. This guy, we'll call him "Sam," has it out for me. He is the typical has to be number one at everything guy. But he can't be. Because I'm better than him. I know Sarah likes him. He is the spitting image of her father. And I know this dick would do anything to get me out of the way. I'm happy where I'm at career wise. Sam isn't. He has bigger, more political aspirations. And I think he knows about my gift. He has found ways to test me. He knows I can sink his campaign with what I've got on him. That "Laara Hotel Rape of 1991"? Him and his buddies know more about that then they let on. But again, its not my place to punish everybody, and I can't get physical proof anyway. But he doesn't know that. Sarah has been in this "grey" area for 18 hours. I know I have to confront it. I intend to do so tonight. Maybe she will just level with me, and if I can get her to actually do something, maybe I can put this all together. We talk. It goes terribly. She shuts me out. She screams. I sleep on the couch. A flash goes by outside my house. Its Sams car. The lights stop. The door to my house opens. I hear someone enter. I hear someone coming down the steps. I hear a gun cock. I hear wrestling. I hear my wife scream. I'm frozen. It goes off. I feel a terrible pain in my chest. I awaken some hours later. Surrounded by doctors. I see everything they've done and its terrible. I see the nurse forgetting to give a child the correct medicine, not the one he is allergic to. I see him screaming. And I see her crying. I see the doctor screwing up the heart operation surgery because he was out drinking the night before, or so I put together myself, I can see through the fog in my eyes that he is hungover. But this. This isn't real. These are just bits and pieces of the last 24 hours. Sam walks in. He is in tears. I fully expect to see myself or my wife getting shot. In the first person. I prepare mentally for the worst. I see what he thinks is his worst action. I see him fucking my wife. I hear him apologize to me, but I'm in no condition to respond. "My fault. All my fault. She did this because of what I did" What? What shes done. Security escorts Sam out. He screams he is innocent. That he tried to stop it. Stop what? Sarah walks in. It comes together. I see Sam run through the front door. I see my wife loading the gun. I see Sam tackle her. I see her still managing to do it. I hear Sams pleading for her not to do it at gunpoint. I feel the pain in my chest all over again. And then grey. I see the doctor talk to Sarah in the corner. I see him begin to tear up. I see her "cry" and nod. I hear the nurses come in. This is it. The button is pressed. My breathing slows. My pulse slows ever so slightly. Second by second. I accept my fate. She leans in to kiss me. And I relive the whole thing again. No gray this time. The clarity makes it a little easier to accept. I see black. WRITERS NOTE: I wrote this in a half hour at 4:30 AM. Not my best work, I'll be honest. I'll try to write a better story with a similar prompt tomorrow. All feedback is welcome.

I took my last prescribed dose some time ago. Roaming through bleak, white-walled corridors, alone in my thoughts and driven by a growing impulse to escape, nothing appears to have changed: these scarred bones enclosing a nightmare institution still look the same. Faceless personnel and inhabitants persist in melting into visual distortions of my own sanity. I haven't spoken to any of them in what seems like forever. This ward is known as a hospital to those on the outside, but I know better: it's a solitary confinement, roomed and boarded with the demons in my head. In the beginning, I knew only isolation and loneliness. I've lost time in here, certainly, but recently, it feels as though my leash has grown weaker. I don't feel bound to internment, but compelled to break these chains. Have I regained a measure of lucidity or have I pierced a veil that was always present? I ride this emotion for a time as my clothes tighten like a noose on skin and organs. Fuck protocol, I strip them off. It's surely a step toward freedom of mind. The suffocation feels lessened while I'm naked, lying in the darkness. My demons have gone. Colors and shapes form and swirl, carrying me to the center of the universe. Are my eyes open? I can't tell. Whatever this is, it feels too good. I drift in wakened iridescent dreams. "It's time to go." No resistance, no restraint. I've been given a ticket to walk free in the light. I glide through solemn, empty corridors. The staff is missing and chairs lie on their sides, dirt and sediment thick on the floor. What has happened here? It's a struggle to find the front doors to my salvation. Shouldn't I remember? Unfamiliarity clouds my mind, but then I see them. Bursting through, the doors are thrown wide, creaking in irritated disturbance. Light engulfs me as I leave these dreadful walls behind. I'm suddenly roused from blinding nothingness by a familiar face. "Dude, holy shit. Dude. Wake up." I blink stupidly and sit up, looking around at a shabby, dirty, white-walled room with an old, aluminum bed frame and stained mattress in the corner. "This sucked. Never again, man. Whose idea was this?" "Mine," I say, through a dry mouth and parched lips. I attempt to shake the fuzziness away. "I can mark'acid in an old mental asylum' off my bucket list now." I remember, now, shivering. "Well I'm glad that's over. Put some fucking clothes on and let's get the fuck out of here."

I put the gun in my open drawer and page Lance (or is it Luke, or Jason, or Ferdinand?) to come into my office. I am not a violent man, and I've never actually shot a pistol before, but I borrowed this one in case..... well I'm not really sure. We historians are not prone to action, but rather the reviews of action. We are generally quiet voyeurs into long gone wars, assassinations, upheavals, and the like. Today, it appears I was going to step for the first time into the story. Lance (Joseph?) came in. "You called me, sir?" he asked, smiling as he always did. He is a friendly man, or at least, I think he is. "Can you explain these?" I said, turning my monitor around to show him the scans of pictures from the Titanic, the painting from Milan, and the fresco from the Roman Empire. He kept smiling. "Oh, of course, Dr. Crown. Those are all me. I love Europe, it's where I was born, so I've spent most of the past couple of millennia there. Lovely varied climate, although I've recently come to be quite fond of this continent as well. Did you need anything else?" That's it? Just a casual answer and a lets-move-on-to-business attitude? Is he playing me? Is this to get me to drop my guard? I move my hand toward the drawer. "If you've got a gun, that's not going to work, sir. I walked through the molten rock of Pompeii, you know? But really, you mustn't be worried. I haven't killed anyone in 2000 years. In fact, killing someone is what got me into this predicament in the first place." "What are you?" I ask. "I'm just a man, sir. A man who made a mistake while taking orders. A man who has been denied his rightful rest in the afterlife. Heaven's gates shut to me, hell's fires off-limits. They're both quite upset with what I did. But I've learned to be happy with my lot. Immortality is without a doubt a curse, but you see so many wondrous things." "Fine, who are you, really? What is your real name?" "I'm very pleased you've worked this out. I couldn't just tell you, that's against the rules, but I've been looking for a friend to talk to. That's why I applied for this job with such a respected historian. You people are puzzle-solvers of the highest order, taking little pieces and weaving the rich tapestry of human existence into pages and videos. But I know you hate flattery, so I will just say, my name is Longinus and it is very good to finally make your acquaintance on honest terms."

"So..." she began seductively "You bought me a drink, you pulled back my chair and I've caught you staring at places you shouldn't all night. If I didn't know better Joe I'd say you've got some very naughty intentions." He smirked. "Well I'm afraid if you're looking for a saint then I may disappoint you." She leaned in close so no one else at the bar could hear her, her soft pink lips brushing gently against his ear. "To be honest Joe, I've always preferred the sinners" she whispered, her voice like a hot summers breeze rustling through the leaves. Joe's mouth felt dry. "Keep cool" he told himself, "don't do anything stupid and you might actually pull this off!." He picked up what was left of his drink and finished it slowly without breaking eye contact. He placed the glass back down on the table, picked up his napkin and wiped his mouth. Still he stared deep into those dusky emeralds, glittering dangerously between perfect eyelashes. He gestured to the bartender. "Put it on my tab Tom." "Yes sir" came the reply. She raised a single eyebrow, a look of mock confusion on her face. "Oh are you leaving?" she asked innocently. "No" he said "we are." A coy smile broke across her features like the rising sun. They both stood and she took hold of his arm as they set off towards the door. "Joe, I need you to understand that I do love my husband" she purred "But I'm afraid he just doesn't have..... the equipment to give me what I need. What every woman needs." Her fingers lightly touched his belt buckle, so softly you could have almost thought it was an accident. "Do you have the proper equipment Joe?" It was no accident. Joe's mind raced as fast as his heartbeat. "Say something sexy!" his brain screamed as they walked through the door out into the street, "quickly!" "Baby, I've got a dick that goes all the way down to the floor." She paused slightly, like a conductor would when he can hear an instrument out of tune and let go of his arm. "Erm" he spluttered, keenly aware that in this delicate dance they'd been performing all night he'd just stepped on his partners foot. Whilst wearing clogs. He looked around. "Ah..... um..... red light time to cross the road!" he said relieved to find words, any words to fill what he could sense was a rapidly growing chasm. He stepped out into a world of bright lights, broken glass and searing pain. Followed swiftly by the inky blackness of unconsciousness. He opened his eyes, slowly, blearily. Where was he? What happened? The smell of sterilised discomfort crept into his nostrils. Hospital. "Ah Mr King you're awake." Joe turned his head, there was a doctor, a grave expression resting on his face. "What happened?" he asked. Voice croaky from underuse like a rusted gate. "I'm afraid you were in a car accident Mr King, hit and run. It was touch and go for a few minutes but we managed to save your life." The doctor looked uncomfortable. "Not without cost I'm afraid." "What do you mean?" "Because of the extent of the damage your body suffered we were unable to save your legs. I'm sorry" Joe pulled the blankets that were covering him off onto the floor. His legs were completely gone from the hips downwards. He stared in dumb confusion. Suddenly cogs whirred and something clicked. "Dick down to the floor..." he murmured. "Ah fuck"

Control, this is Commander Taylor of the ship Ulysses. Go ahead Ulysses. Final systems check complete. Initiating burn on your mark. 3..... 2..... 1..... Mark. You are clear for burn Ulysses. Roger Command, Ulysses out. The massive jump drive began to cycle and the various hull thrusters hissed. The Ulyssess fine turned the trajectory of its massive bulk and in a blink it was gone. it was folded up into subspace were it would remain until the drive dropped it into a safe orbit around Mars. Total trip time, less then 15 minutes. Atleast that was the plan, anyway. When its crippled shell finally hurtled itself out of hyperspace it had been nearly an hour and there was nothing safe about the orbit. The ships propulsion system was offline but it came rocketing towards Mars at nearly 400ms. Once visual contact had been established the Martian Defense Forces wanted to use the meteor protection system to destroy it before it could impact. The council intervened and with the help of over one hundred various vessels pressed into emergency service the Ulysses was guided into a stable orbit. Mars wanted to board the ship immediately but again Earth stood her ground. It was agreed a team would be sent by conventional means to evaluate the ship and determine the cause of the problem and if any of the major systems were salvageable. Taking the slow train to Mars was no picnic, nearly six months in a zero g hauler and I felt like shit. The council had seized the first ship it could find with enough space for our team and equipment. This led to us being crammed into a 20 year old heavy transport back from the days when the majority of Mars food and supplies came from Earth. Our quarters were temporary walls erected in one of the cargo bays and the ship had no artificial gravity system. Sleeping strapped down like a crate I was sick, a lot. So when we finally set foot on Mars One, the massive station that controlled all incoming and outgoing traffic, I was happier then I'd ever remembered being. I spent the next three days exploring the station with my team mates. Finally it was time to board our shuttle and head to the Ulysses. Carter, Lewis and I had spent many long nights arguing the possibilities of what had happened. The damage the hull had sustained was tremendous and it was a miracle so much had unfolded intact. I was glad we would finally be getting some answers. We all in some way felt responsible for unravelling her mystery, our division had designed and manufactured many of the components for the ship. And most importantly of all, Lewis was the head of the team that built and tested the Hyper drive. I knew if it came to light that his design in some way failed, he would be crushed. The gentle sway of the shuttle was relaxing and it wasn't long until I drifted off.... To be continued................

Chapter 15 Jeez, what a ceremony. I sat on one of the rooftop seats and watched the gigantic auditorium fill up. Tens of thousands of people, in suits and dresses, and clothes from every era as far as the eye could see, strolled in from the red carpet outside. Next to the stage, where the really important people sat, Cleopatra walked up to her golden seat on the front row. In a magnificent white cotton dress, she inspired awe, except for the two guys on either side of her, one in a Roman emperor's toga and crown, and on her right a man in a roman general's headpiece. Caesar and.... was it, Marc Anthony? Jeez. After the guests were sat, Robin Williams came on stage in what appeared to be a bright red pimp suit, and told a couple of jokes to warm up the crowd. Doing impressions of Nelson Mandela and Sir Isaac Newton, he had the guests all laughing by the time the awards was up, which was an impressive feat given that English wasn't the most-spoken language. Great comedy transcends words I guess. But I was troubled. Why was I here? These people, these were the greats of history: the men and women who (when they had been alive) had impacted the world. These were people with followers in the hundreds and thousands, on whose words empires and kingdoms had crumbled, men and women whose mere gestures were felt in distant echoes thousands of years after their time time, people whose minds and writings had changed knowledge forever. Who the hell was I to win an ward here? Sure, I was a mildly successful stockbroker from Madison, Wisconsin. But surely that's a couple notches below King fucking Solomon, and George Washington himself? I looked again at my invitation. "Award winner. " , and on the back, an "invitation to the Afterlife Awards Afterparty." I sighed, and slumped back into my seat and watched the proceedings. Something terrible would happen, I knew it. Chapter 25 I had dozed off when I heard my name from the stage, which woke me up with a start. This was followed by thunderous applause, and the old man in a magnificent beard and gold-lined toga next to me poked me with a stick, and muttered to himself. "Non progredi est regredi" he said. "I beg your pardon?" I asked him. And he said, "Dico Ego, Marcus Aurelius." "Well, jeez. I better get going then. " , I said sarcastically, getting to my feet, under Marcus Aurelius's sternly disapproving glare. I walked down the flight of stairs and up the main corridor leading to the stage, every single eye from history on me. It was like high school graduation. As I neared the stage, I heard a voice shout out "That's my boy!" I looked into the second row to see none other than my ex-convict grandpa, moonshine whisky in his hand, with his arm around Catherine the Great. He gave me a thumbs up and a wink. The lecherous bastard. Of course he'd conned his way here. He wouldn't miss a party like this. As I got to the stage, Robin Williams shook my hand, and presented me with a trophy in the shape of a pure gold question mark about the size of an oscar. "Now, ladies and gentlemen. Many of you have willingly killed thousands, some of you millions of people in the name of your various empires and victory and whatnot....... but this man, wins a special treat. A truly special award. The most people killed without knowing it." Laughter and thunderous applause across the auditorium sent a chill up my spine. As the cheering died down, Robin Williams put on a smirk. "Let's take a look at the clip, folks, shall we? Please put on your 3D glasses." And all eyes turned behind us, where a huge 3D projection had appeared. I was handed a pair of glasses by Robin and, in unison with the crowd, we put them on as we all turned our eyes to the screen above, where my life was to be shown for all of history to watch..... and mock.
