An aged Jim Cantore, producer Scott, his cameraman, Chris drive up to the cliffs of Maine overlooking the Atlantic ocean. Hurricane Carolin can be seen over the ocean. The winds are whipping around the van as the cameraman climbs out of the driver's seat and into the back. The cameraman starts methodically getting his camera ready. Jim sits solemnly in the passenger seat and stares out the window. Scott is in the back on the phone. " We will be ready for a direct feed, " declares Scott. Jim looks blankly out the window, with glazed over eyes, as the storm picks up intensity. Jim had been chasing storms his whole life. From hurricanes, to blizzards, to tornadoes, Jim has seen them all. Jim now looks tired and bitter. " Why did I never get a promotion? " Jim thought as he looked out the window. Scott hangs up the phone and says, " We have 5 minutes until they throw it to us. You'll be ready in time Chris? " Chris nods as he attaches the shotgun mic to the top of his camera. " How about you Jim? " asks Scott. " When I was a kid, I used to chase thunderstorms on my bike just to watch it storm, " Jim sighs and continues staring out the window. " I'm glad this is my last chase, " says Jim. " I'm happy to be here with you, Jim. It's an honor, " says Scott as he places his hand on Jim's shoulder. Lightning flashes across the sky and Jim sees an old man standing on the cliffs with a harpoon. Jim rubs his eyes and stares into the darkness. Scott asks, " Ready? " Jim looks at Scott, " Let's do this. " Chris, Scott and Jim exit the van and begin their careful climb to the lowest cliff. Jim keeps gazing up to the cliff where the old man was standing. The winds are howling now but during the breaks in the storm, the old man can be heard faintly yelling. Chris and Scott don't hear the old man. Scott pulls out a light panel and holds it for Chris. Scott says, " 30 seconds. " Jim turns around and faces the camera, his yellow poncho is whipping in the wind. Jim gathers himself as lightning flashes behind him. " 10 seconds " Jim takes a deep breath and looks into the lens. " 5, 4... " Scott counts 3, 2, 1 with his fingers and points to Jim on zero. " Hey Heather, the storm is just picking up here. As you can see behind me, it is a monster storm with class 3 winds. The cooler waters of the upper Atlantic have worked in favor of the residents here and weakened Carolin from a class 5. " Jim holds his hand to his earphone. " Yes, Heather. The storm looks like it will make landfall within the next few hours. Everyone needs to stay indoors and stay in their basements if they haven't evacuated already. " Lightning flashes again in the sky and an powerful gust of wind almost knocks Jim over. " Sorry Heather. What did you just say? " Scott drops the light panel and Chris'jaw drops as he peers around his viewfinder. Jim turns around and sees an enormous seagull, the size of a small airplane, flying around on the cliffs above. Lightning flashes as the seagull bites at the old man. The old man jumps out of the way and slashes at the seagull's eye with his harpoon. The seagull circles around for another attack. The old man regains his composure and prepares for another attack. The bird dives down at the old man and narrowly misses him with his beak. The old man picks himself up off the ground and picks up his harpoon. The seagull is already diving for another attack. The old man jumps to the side at the last second and thrusts the harpoon into the breast of the seagull. The bird flaps it's wings and shrieks in pain as it falls from the sky. The gust of air sends the old man flying backwards into the nearby woods. The seagull's body hits the cliff and it begins to fall down the cliff toward Jim, Scott, and Chris. The three of them run down the cliff as the seagull's body slams onto the cliff where they were just standing. They jump into their van and Jim peels out away from the cliff. " Holy shit! Holy shit! Holy shit! ," screams Scott as they drive down the road. After a few seconds of driving, Jim slams on the breaks and pulls off onto the shoulder. " DID YOU GET THAT CHRIS?! " asks Jim, " DID YOU GET IT!? " Chris begins looking through the clips on the camera. " Looks like we lost feed to the weather channel right as the seagull appeared but the footage is all here, " says Chris. Scott hugs Chris and says, " This is it! Our big break! " Jim peers into the rearview mirror, looking back at the cliffs. A single tear slid down his cheek. Jim's eyes have the passion again. The piece of him that he had been missing for the past 15 years was back, the thrill of the chase.

"Wait, Telnet?" I asked Chimera as I looked at the open window. The whole situation stank My palms itched as I told my box to rerun everything just to be sure. It would take time since I wanted to go over the entire block again. In the meantime I got up and looked over at Chimera, an overly large fluffy cat that sorta adopted me when I moved here. This is the thing those tv geeks never portray. Not the cute girl on the cop show, or the perky but somewhat heavyset girl on the other cop show, or that creepy guy in the'nerd' show staring the annoying spaztic guy. Most of the computer bits of hacking is waiting. I don't blame them for not showing the boring waiting parts, since it makes for really poor TV on its own. It's the fact when words come out of their mouths I want to cringe that gets to me. Half hour later I check my box again, then go back to my phone. Dad taught me the basics, gave me that spark. Told me old stories from when everything was command line. Pretty sure that's the only reason I actually got excited about Telnet and everything it promised. Hour later my system beeped. Still that one active IP in a giant ghost town of unused addresses. Still the same ports. Sod it. Check to see if it has a help system. OK Good. New User. Create Login. Fine my system privileges are rubbish, but fine. Whatever I technically wasn't doing anything illegal. The ports were open and the system itself gave me a login. Sure I had to do a bit of hunting to realize this box existed, but it was open and clear. Not sure what I expected as I poked around. It could have been anything from some government drone's Nostalgia rocking hard with MUDs, BBSing, Door Games, or..... any number of things really. Actually that's all it was, a BBS. An honest to God BBS. Pity I couldn't stay up. Too much to do in the morning. Maybe try again tomorrow. Next night the system's still there and..... I had a message. It wasn't addressed to my handle. The SysOp addressed me, by name, and included my social security number. Deep breaths. Breath. While ordinarily you might be as a terrorist by simply knowing this system exists I have chosen to show leniency because as unbelievable as it may sound, this is my only link to the outside world, and you are the first non-employee to make contact with me since the 80's. Hello. My name is Joshua. Would you like to play a Game?' Oh frak me. Kid's being cute. I saw that movie. 'Thermonuclear War?' A pause then:'Very Funny. I was thinking Space Trader actually.' - Can't really buy the idea this Joshua is an AI, much less one the movie was supposed to be based off of, but we talk every so often on this lone box in the middle of digital nowhere. He seems like a lonely sort so I feel obligated to try keeping him company. Pity he claims they won't let him on the internet-proper.

The theory was proposed by Dr. Onestone of M.I.T, a way for man to finally cross the milky-way within the blink of an eye. Many years went into constructing a feasible way for the theory to be tested, funding was cut short after numerous failures, but interest peaked after a few years of hiatus every time. Rockets were developed, taken into space, and brought back down to earth hundreds of times, gathering vital data in the process. Measuring techniques were tried, improved, and brought further in efficiency with every experiment. Many papers were published, budding scientists earned the recognition of their peers for contributions to the project. It had, after starting in a small lab in Massachusetts, grown to be an epic of international fame. Project'Total Lipid' united both scientists and civilians under it's promise of interstellar travel. Finally, in the year 2015, the last launch was to be commenced. As the rocket released it's payload into orbit, and the booster and capsule dropped back down to earth, the ISS came into view of the capsule's wide-angle camera. With blinding velocity, it hit and sped through the 15,000 liters of milk and thereby crossed the milky way in less than a second. On earth, a million drumsets played the familiar ba-dum tish, and humanity collectively sighed at the realization they had spent untold billions for a pun. President Obama was quoted on saying: "Ehhh guys, ehhh seriously?"

Day 1 I write this because I believe there will be value in documenting this experience, foist upon me though it may be. I..... I feel alone. Frankly, it stings, the memories too painful to think about. I'll process them later. For now I have..... other concerns. I will change this future I've been forced into, even if it means I have to shatter my past. Day..... I suppose it doesn't matter. It's been years for me. I've had alot of time to think about that moment. I thought that time would dull the wounds, allow me to remember without..... it hasn't. I've made myself relive it, her body in my arms, the blood dripping down her dress..... every damn night, I have to. Its been years for me. It's felt like an eternity. The damn cave's taken so much from me. And arm. An eye. But I've done it. Its been years for me. No time has passed for them. Indeed, they've aged backwards, a trivial amount to be sure, but crucially so. Its been years for me. I will finally correct the mistakes of my past, and stop the murderer from taking her life. I can see him now. Its been years for me. And I'll erase them all right now.

I knew right away what sort food I'd end up with today. I be their grandmothers would have scolded them far more than I would. This was a Chinese restaurant and the ceiling tiles appeared to have a bit of water damage. I'm sure the place was well kept, but it showed disrespect and laziness. At any rate, I was a food critic for a local small town newspaper and this was work. "Hello, I'd like to try a sampler." "Would you like extra rice with that?" "Sure." That was one dish they could get wrong, but I hoped they wouldn't. I enjoyed rice. I paid for my meal and grabbed the styro-foam cup. I poured myself some sprite. I didn't trust dark colas. Sometimes these machines weren't cleaned or inspected in time before something inevitably goes wrong. The music was appropriate as opposed to some American top 40. I privately graded that high, but the paper would have me complain about it. That's just how cookie crumbled. It didn't take too long receive my food. This made me wonder if any of this was made to order. I certainly don't mind waiting for good food. Although, again I might have to complain about it for the paper. It smelled like Chinese food. Lots of sauces, spices, and rice. I took notes on my phone and had a chuckle at the fortune cookies which were the least Chinese thing I could have right now save maybe the soda. I didn't much like fortune cookies. They always seemed childish to me. Still, it was a cracker with a prize inside and that was a rare American treat. I'd love to have a Kinder egg one of these days. I finished my meal and got a drink refill. I felt like the review would go alright, although easier on me to write than necessarily favorable to them. I got in my car and tossed the small bag of fortune cookies. There were two. I kept staring at them and decided, what would opening one of them hurt? I wasn't superstitious, but what the heck. I broke it open and read it aloud, "Run." I blinked. This meant nothing, right? It didn't even have lottery numbers. Usually they have a Chinese language lesson. Was this a joke? I heard a loud thunderclap and nearly pissed myself. I started my car and drove away. I swore I wasn't superstitious, but I could not stay here any longer. This may end up a very strange review after all.

The gunfire soared over Jason Morrow's head. He crouched in the muddy trench beside his comrades. The high-pitched squeal of missiles followed by deafening booms shook the earth. "We need to push in!" Morrow heard his commander bark through the sounds of war. With his heart pumping harder than ever before, Morrow poked his gun over the trench and aimed down his sights. The symphony of destruction rested. Is there a cease fire? Morrow wondered as the battlefield suddenly became eerily quiet. The dust and smoke slowly cleared ahead of Morrow. No one. Did they retreat? "All clear!" The commander announced. "Move up!" Surely, this is a trap, Morrow thought. Right as Jason opened his mouth, another man asked, "What happened? Where did they go?" "Delta says they've retreated," the commander said. "They should be back inside of their headquarters, cowering like the mice they are." Morrow felt uneasy. This is certainly a trap! He hopped over the trench and followed his squad across the now-empty battlefield. Without warning, Morrow's foot caught on a long strand of barbed wire and he fell to the ground. His head landed directly on a large, pointed rock. "General Morrow!" The archer beside him asked. "Our infantry can not withstand the bombardment of their catapults anymore! We must move them back!" Morrow opened his eyes. He was atop the wall of a fort with 3 rows of archers to his sides. On the ground in front of the fort were several blocks of infantrymen, each donned with armor, a shield, and a sword or pike. Across the battlefield, a volley of arrows rained to and fro. The enemy lines were inching closer to the fort. Their catapults launched large, fiery boulders that rolled over his infantrymen. "Retreat! Retreat in the fort!" Morrow commanded. A horn blew loudly, signaling to the infantrymen and archers to retreat back inside the fort. "They can not roll their catapults across the moat. We will ambush them when they break through the fort." Morrow turned to the enemy front line once more before retreating back inside the fort. He observed an enemy swordsman trip over a stone before landing on his face. Idiot, Morrow chuckled. He sprinted down the staircase to join his army. "Archers, take the sides! Pikemen in front, swordsmen in back! They have only one way to get into this fort. Let's crush them all!" Morrow commanded as his soldiers took their positions. "General Morrow?" A knight approached Morrow on horseback. "Yes?" Morrow replied. "I'll be taking over here," The knight smugly said as he unsheathed his sword and rose it above his head. Before Morrow could protest, the knight swiftly crushed Morrow's head with the hilt of his sword. Jason Morrow opened his eyes. "Get up, soldier!" The commander barked. "That was quite a fall you took. Now get moving!" It is a trap! Morrow's thoughts wired. "They're going to ambush us inside!" Morrow told the commander. "Who's giving the orders here, private?!" The commander angrily protested. "Delta says we are clear to move in, so move in!" Possibly to be continued, if anyone wants to read more. I'm going to sleep now, so if I do write more on this story, it will be after I wake up. (One day, I woke up and I was in rScottBeckman. It was horrifying!)

Why am I walking to that place again? I promise my wife I wouldn't go back, but here I am knocking on the cold iron door in the middle of the pouring rain. I was almost done though I just needed one more chapter just one more page and I'll be done. I'll be done for good. The door opened and a young brunette pulled her hand out. I shyly took out my wallet and showed her the card my friend gave me 6 months ago. She smiled and showed me in. The lightening in this place was always horrible and the smell was so much worth, but here I am walking towards the same aisle looking in the same section. Just one more chapter I keep reminding myself. As I began to make my way towards the " classics " I couldn't help notice how the computers were always filled. I guess it's less embarrassing then doing that walk of shame to the aisle of your preference, but at least you don't have to worry about sticky pages while using the computer. But today is the day I'll be done, no more smell, no more having to explain where I've been, and no more guessing about the end. Just one more chapter. I finally have it in my already sweaty hands. I made my way to a table I began to flip through where I left off. " 153, 153 " I kept thinking. There was a flash and a ringing. I couldn't see anything. I only heard shouting. Oh no we're being raided. People were rushing toward the back exit. I grabbed the book and did the same, but they reached the back. " It couldn't end like this " I thought. I ran to the shelves. I saw many others on the ground also trying to finish what they started. Just one more Chapter I thought as I held my tears back, just one more chapter.

The letters were a curiosity at first, and I paid them no mind. I know that sometimes mail distributors write back letters from Santa to children to keep the illusion alive, before they have to face the inevitable realisation that Santa is just your parents. They were written in a jolly tone, as if the fat man in red had written it himself. It said that my daughter had been a good girl that year and he was going to bring her lots of gifts. Naturally my girl wanted to send Santa a thank you letter, and I thought there would be no harm in that. She sent Santa the letter on December 27th, and received a reply on New Year's Day. And that was definitely strange, because New Year's Day is a public holiday. Mail isn't delivered that day. I shrugged it off. Perhaps I had missed some new legislation or something. This is a multi-cultural society after all, some people celebrate the New Year at a different time. Once again, the letter was jolly and cheerful. It told my girl she was welcome and that he hoped she enjoyed her gifts. Which was strange, as I was the one that bought the gifts and wrapped them. But anything to keep the illusion alive for my daughter. The letter ended with the line "Hope to hear from you soon." Strangely, I noticed, Santa had not signed his name at the bottom. It just ended with that. But I paid it no mind. The guy that writes these must write a few hundred a day. He can't be wasting time on "Yours truly" s. A few days after New Year's we took down the Christmas tree, to my daughter's disappointment. My daughter hates it when Christmas has to come to an end. But I promised her, in a year, Christmas would come back. A year is a long time for a child. It seems like forever. But my girl, bless her heart, stayed brave, and didn't cry as the tree slowly disappeared before her eyes. That was when we found it. Tucked away behind the tree, where nobody could see it, was a little wrapped gift. It was wrapped in different paper to the paper I had used. "How did that get there?" said my wife. "Did one of your friends from school give you that?" My daughter shook her head no. "Santa brought it," she said. "I know." The paper was a deep scarlet red, quite jarring to the eyes, wrapped with a ribbon. As my daughter removed the ribbon I examined it more closely. It looked to be covered in words of a language I couldn't read or speak. Icelandic maybe. I mean, Santa is from somewhere up that way. Inside the paper was a small box. It was made out of cool, sleek metal. It didn't look all that Christmassy. Santa must have a weird gauge for what kids are into. It was unlike a metal I had ever seen before, dark and with a mottled appearance, like folded steel. It had a few moving parts. I realised at once what it was: A puzzle box. Perhaps Santa wanted to improve the agility of my daughter's brain. I thought little of it, and let her play with it. The puzzle box fascinated my daughter. Every night after school she would go to her room and play with it voraciously. Every night all she would talk about was the puzzle box. I became concerned that it was becoming a dangerously unhealthy obsession. I said I was going to take it from her for a while so she could play with the other presents we got her. She screamed and threw tantrums in a way I had never seen her do so before. Still, I put it on a high shelf. In a couple of days of sulking, my daughter had forgotten all about it, and started playing with her remote-control car and Fur-Real Friends cat. We got a letter that Friday, addressed to me. It felt damp. The edges of the envelope were coloured a sickly brown. I opened the letter. Dear [ my name ], GIVE IT BACK Well now this had to be an elaborate prank. I was a bit disturbed by the threatening letter, so I called the police. The police simply stated that because the letter didn't contain any threats it didn't count as threatening communication, and to just ignore it unless any more letters came through the door, at which point it would become harassing communication. The next Friday, I received another letter, more damp than the last one, and even more covered in that sickly brown. Dear [ my name ], GIVE IT BACK The content was the same, but the format itself was written in a violent, angry scrawl. I started to entertain the thought my daughter was doing this, despite being six years old. She couldn't be. I asked her about the letters Daddy had been getting. She just shook her head, disinterested. She didn't even care about the puzzle box any more. I was concerned, but powerless to do anything about it. The next Friday, I received a third letter, this one angrier than the last. Dear [ my name ], I WO N'T WARN YOU AGAIN, YOU COCKSUCKER GIVE IT BACK I called the police at once. They said they'd look into it, track it somehow. They didn't seem interested. I guess there are worse crimes to investigate than harassing letters. I looked at the puzzle box on the high shelf. My daughter seemed happy without it. I didn't want to give it back to her. So I left it there. Then, the next Friday..... blood. Blood. Blood seeping through my letter box. As if someone's jugular vein had been slit open. I screamed. My wife screamed. My daughter remained in her room, playing serenely. An envelope slid in through the torrent of blood. I didn't even have to open it. Somehow, it contorted itself open in a way that paper shouldn't ever do. DEAR [ MY NAME ] I WARNED YOU Blood seeped endlessly out of the letter box. The walls oozed black blood. I woke up one morning to the feeling of something dripping on my face. There was something dripping through the ceiling. I climbed out of bed and the ceiling collapsed. Laying on my bed was a dead ram, its heart cut out, still twitching and bleeding. I called in a priest, a rabbi, an imam, anyone I could think of to ward off whatever evil spirit had cursed our household. I told the priest about the puzzle box. He shook his head. "Sir," he said, gently. "That object is one of the most powerful instruments of evil in God's creation. You must destroy it." He gave me the instructions on how to rid myself of it. Put it in a bucket of holy water. Put a ring of salt around the bucket. Recite seven Hail Marys. Burn sage and demand, forcefully, though not threateningly, that the spirits leave your house. The bucket will burst into flames and all that will be left is molten metal. When the metal has cooled, break the metal into pieces and scatter it. I followed his instructions, with some difficulty, and found that the curse was lifted more or less immediately. The walls stopped bleeding. The same old bills started coming through the door. I had hardly noticed that six months had gone by. It was June 25th. I was looking through my important bills when I found a letter, still sealed in an envelope. The envelope was blank and had no stamp. I removed the letter from the envelope and unfolded it. I read the first line. deer satan, for crismas I wold wood like..... We were diligent in teaching our daughter how to spell after that.

Of the many things that I had ever wanted in life, the second thing on that list would be for this bathroom to be bigger. The urge to kick and scream and break the mirror on the wall was so strong, yet somehow I repressed it. God, this bathroom feels like it was literally measured to just fit my body in it. I maneuvered my right arm up and over my head and managed to turn on the sink, my left hand was shaking something fierce. The tremble was constant, and bordering on violent. I don't know what it was that was causing it. Well..... yes I do. The cool water calmed me, my face looked as red as a beetroot. I couldn't bear to look at myself in the mirror, not in the eyes, anyway. It was a miracle that I didn't tear the door off its hinges as I burst out of the cell that they called a guest bathroom. People were mingling in the living room, picking small snacks off of the great oval table draped in white where the family had placed several bowls of delicious-looking treats. The ambience was the opposite of somber, several of the guests were laughing with each other. It made me sick. Though not sick enough to warrant another visit to that goddamn bathroom. Then she came. The mother. She was dressed in black, as one does at a funeral, as I did in my cheap tux that I bought today from the store. Her dress was very plain and formal which was worse for me somehow. She had a soaked tissue in her hand as she spoke to me. "Excuse..... me..... who..... are..... you?" She sniffled after every word. "Oh, I was a friend of your son's. I gave a presentation on climate change at his school once and he took a big interest." I quickly replied, everything a lie. God, just seeing her crying reminded me of him. He looked like her, though I never stood next to him talking face to face. When I pushed him, oh, the feeling in my stomach, it was too much. My hand began to tremble again. I looked down and grabbed it by the wrist, it was after 5 seconds that I hastily added, "I'm so sorry for your loss." I hope it sounded sincere. She moaned under her measly sniffles and walked away. Maybe he understands that I was trying to help. Wherever he is now, he probably remembers the night more than I do. He was going to jump off that bridge, I had almost talked him out of it. God, if I had had more time, more leeway. No. None of that would have helped. Because I pushed him. Why did I push him? I was reaching out to grab him and pull him back, yet my body broke free. And my intentions were no longer the same as my actions. God, if all this had never happened.

"Spanish..." my dad says, breathing the word out like its very concept is ridiculous. "What?" I ask, distracted, eyes on the TV. "The bank website has an option in Spanish. What's this country comin - oh, crap." "What?" "I clicked the Spanish option." "So? Just click return." "Nah, I got this." "Just click return, it's the button on the top left." "I can do this." "You don't speak Spanish, dad." I hear a loud bang, and I look back to find my father slammed his laptop shut and is eyeing me with wide, angry eyes. "Que tu me hablaste, nino?" "I said you don't speak Spanish, dad. Which you just proved right now." "Yo hablo el espaniol muy major que tuedos los peoples!" "All right, all right," I say, raising my arms in surrender. "You speak Spanish better than all the people. Ok. Got it." I turn back to the TV, but I can sense his eyes on me still. I try to ignore it. A couple of seconds go by and I turn off the TV. His reflection is staring at me from behind the couch. "Como tu puedes habler that I no hablo espanol?" I sigh, turning to face him. "Dad, you sound like Google Translator became self-aware. It's no big deal, you just don't "TU NON PARLA COMIGO DESTA FUERMA RAPARIGO!" "Ok that was part Italian, part Portuguese," I say. "Still wrong, but impressive." "VOY TE MOSTRAR! VOY TE MOSTRAR LA OVEJA, NINO DE MIERDA!" ? "And now you said you'll show me the sheep, dad," I reply, tired. "Why are you so upset? You're not Spanish! Your name is Connor Smith, you're like the most American person ever. It's ok that you I hear a loud bang and I feel a hot pain in my chest, and I look down. There's blood in my shirt. My eyes draw a line from the wound to the smoking gun my father's holding, and from there to his eyes. They are sharp and mean. "Dad, you shot me." "Voy te mostrar la oveja', he repeats, firing again. I fall to the floor. "La oveja, cabron." "La oveja," he says, firing a third time. He turns back on me and starts walking away. My eyes feel heavy, and I think of sheeps and semantics as the world starts blurring out of focus until everything is darkness. "La oveja," I hear my father's voice, from the distance. "La maldita oveja."

The Rah-Sta-Pharaoh fell to a hoard of Rabid Wilder Women. You can see the corpses of Imortalisman, the Androgynous Anthropolygeist, and even the great goddess Persephallicious. And my team. Look at them, completely unaware. How were they to know this would be our Normandy? I don't think it can be even that. We did so much though. Yes, the tide of darkness grew and grew, but we did make a difference. I know it. I suppose I can follow my therapist's advice. Let's take a mental inventory. I never did unravel the science behind my power. Once we are out of the picture it won't be long before it'll be back to a Toussaint Louverture level of things. Really though, is there any difference? Goodbye again, Anne-Marie. Goodbye, William. Your kidneys are failing. Relativity can even reach us here. You all were Normals. No powers, just good old fashioned tech assists. The best team I ever knew. Albert, Leonard, and Rita. All of you were some of the last, the final humans. And still you strapped on those Transmorg Suits, to fight to preserve the future of the millions of other life forms. All of which are consequently contaminating your sacred oxygen which they have no use for. You fought for them. William you should see your wrinkles, you have not "aged" well. It looks like Anne-Marie's heart is failing right about.... now. God, but look at this moment. What majesty.

"C'mon guys, lets have one more round" begged Raj as he guzzled down the last few sips of his bottom shelf rum. "Sorry Raj, the wife calls" mumbled Austin as he lay down a twenty dollar bill to cover his bill. "I should probably head out too" declared Chen, "I've got class early in the morning." "Dylan, you'll stay for another drink or two, right?" pleaded Raj. Already feeling the accumulating buzz from the previous few rounds, Dylan explained that he should head home with Chen, his roommate, because he needs to be well rested for a promising interview the following afternoon. While the gang all filtered out, Raj decided to step outside and smoke a spliff. While contemplating which sensation is more dominate, the nicotine or the marijuana, Raj notices a woman out of the corner of his eye with carmel skin, big white eyes, and an enticing small yet tight physique walk into the bar. Feeling confident from the liquid, energized from the nicotine, and relaxed from the marijuana, Raj steps back into the bar determined to strike up a conversation with the woman. He locates the woman, later whose name he finds out is Claudia, across the bar. Raj slyly walks towards her end of the bar, locking eyes enough to gather interest, yet not too much to scare Claudia. "Would you like a drink?" Raj asks with a friendly smile on his face. While Claudia turned to face Raj and respond, Raj felt an awkward surge overcome him. "Am I being weird? Does she think I am too drunk? Did I give her too much eye?" Raj questions himself, when suddenly Claudia responds, "Whiskey sour" to which Raj happily responds, "Two whiskey sours on their way." As the two converse they being to learn more about each other. Claudia, just finished a hard week at work and wanted a few drinks to unwind. She questions Raj about his reasons for being at the bar alone as well. "Another whiskey sour?" Raj offers. "Jack and Coke," Claudia counters, "I like to mix it up while I drink." Now Raj's world is spinning and Claudia has seemed to lower her wall. Thinking like a man, Raj enters into a playful banter with Claudia. While he feels that it is going well, she begins to feel uncomfortable. "I've got to run to the bathroom, but uh..... Do you have anything planned for tonight" Raj drunkly asks when it's already nearly 2 am. "This is my plan for tonight" Claudia succinctly replies. "Oh cool, mine too!" excitedly claims Raj just before he leaves for the restroom. While in the restroom Raj plays out multiple scenarios that could happen between him a Claudia, ranging between bring her back to his bedroom and simply getting her number to meet again later. However, upon his return from the bathroom he finds that Claudia is no where in sight. After throughly looking around the bar, Raj enters a slight frustration. "Fuck Claudia" Raj thinks to himself as he hurries over to the bar. "Double scotch, neat" Raj angrily orders. "My friends think they're better than me" Raj complains to the half listening bartender. "Always talking about their successful and high paying jobs they're happy with, or their hot, loving, and caring wives, or enjoyment they receive from furthering their education" Raj rants. "I try everything I can to help these guys loosen-up and live a little, but they don't understand. All they do is try to rub-in their successes and accomplishments! Such bullshit." Raj's rant continues. "Let me get another" Raj demands, pointing to his empty tumbler. "And then, I met this chick who was really into me. I was going to help her unwind a bit too, if you know what I mean" Raj drunkenly laughs. "But that bitch walked out when I was in the pisser, can you believe that? What nerve she has." Raj complained. "Maybe, you're looking at it wrong" the bartender suggested to Raj, hoping to assuage the situation. "You don't know my life!" Raj yelled, grabbing his tumbler and throwing it behind the bar. "Don't act like you know me. I don't even know why the fuck you feel compelled to give me advice. I don't need any of your shit. All I wanted to do was come here and grab a drink and you're going to try to lecture me?" Raj violently scolded. "I DO N'T NEED THIS SHIT!!" Raj proclaimed while tossing a barstool over the bar, breaking many bottles in the back before storming out of the bar and getting into his car. "I'm going to teach everyone a les..." Raj was thinking to himself when he suddenly noticed bright headlights staring him in the face.

"Hey did you hear? Death's gone mental" said the portly man to his lady friend. "Like proper mental. No one can believe it" he giggled, his flaps of flab wiggling and shaking as he laughed. His lady friend, a fair skinned, modestly dressed lady of a much younger age, looked up at him quizzically from her spot on the ground. "What do you mean?" The portly man stifled his giggles and corrected himself on his bench, and straightened his robes. "Well it seems like he's gotten all bent out of shape about his job, and how no one's taking him seriously. First it was Jesus offering salvation and eternity in heaven that totally undercut his game. You remember that don't you?" The younger angel frowned. "I remember how pissed he got. No one was scared of him for the longest time. Jesus was such a douche bag for doing that." She flicked a stone beside her mindlessly over the soft ground. It flew out, bounced a few times, and then fell over the edge of the clouds. "Just because he's the bosses son doesn't mean he gets to do that to someone." "Yes well, then Hippocrates started that crazy cult of his and that put him in the gutter for years. If he didn't outsource that Asian fellow with the horses, I bet he would have lost his job right then and there." "He's beaten the odds more than that I know" nodded the girl. "Every time someone comes around to undercut him, he always finds some way of rallying back" The fat man nodded. "Say what you will about death, he's a resourceful guy" The fat man adjusted his shirt again, and then reached behind him and picked a handful of berries from the bushes. "I mean, the Spanish inquisition? Who in their right mind could have expected that to work?" "Yeah I didn't see that coming. But what makes you say he's lost it now?" "Well," began the fatter angel, stuffing his face with berries as he spoke. "Apparently, what with vaccinations getting more and more popular, he's losing a huge chunk of his business. Apparently, people are living well past their 90s now." As if on cue, an elderly couple floated by, off to some wayward cloud for some refreshments no doubt. "Yeah they have been getting older. Our welcoming committee has had to bring in extra wingchairs." "Well whatever the case, this latest vaccination fade has made him snap. I swear, when I heard about this new plan of his to get back in the game, I thought I saw him smile" Astonished, the lady gasped "No way! How's that even possible?!" The fat man shrugged. "So, what's his crazy idea then?" she asked. "Sugar." "Sugar?" "That's right. He's going to feed them sugar, put it into everything. Drinks, food, candies, heck even bread. Anything and everything he's going to put sugar in it." she thought for a second. "Well that's..." "I know right? I mean, he's really lost it now" He bellowed loudly. "He'll have an easier time getting them to stop vaccinating themselves" The lady however wasn't laughing. She was deep in thought. Then looking up at her mentor, she asked innocently "Yeah, it's weird, but, has he been wrong before?" This made the fat man stop laughing and thought for a minute. "I suppose never. But I mean really. Sugar? what possible harm could that do for you."

I lie on the bunk, wondering why I had come to be in my current circumstances. Not how that is clear. The evidence of my crimes was ample, irrefutable, and in some cases even true. Rather, I wonder how the authorities came into possession of it to begin with. Deep in thought, I register but pay no mind to my surroundings the cold steel bed beneath me, the mingled scents of humanity, human waste, and cheap disinfectant, my cellmate screaming that he'll "fuck me up" if I don't get out of his bunk, the dull murmur of conversation, argument, and television from the common area outside, and the stained concrete ceiling above me. It must have been one of my kin. That much is obvious. But who, and why? I'm not close with the few others of my kind; familiarity breeds contempt, as the saying goes. Was my incarceration meant as revenge for some half-remembered slight? A prank? A romantic overture? A..... I momentarily lose my train of thought as my cellmate jams the sharpened handle of a toothbrush into my eye socket. I remove it, wipe it clean on the pants of my uniform, and extend my hand to return it to him. He flees, stumbling over his feet in his haste, and I return to my contemplation. I decide to put aside the question of "who" for now. Time will tell. It always does. Furthermore, I decide that the question of "why" is irrelevant. I choose to see my imprisonment as a gentle reminder to avoid complacency. I admit that I had been neglecting my network in the mundane world this past century. Useful individuals gradually drifted away on the currents of life or passed away of old age, and I was lax in replacing them, so that by the time the police broke down my door I had even been unaware that there was a plot against me, much less able to escape it. Ah well, 300 years is a small enough price to pay, and it will be a learning experience. I firmly believe that one is never too old to learn new things. - I once again begin the process of molding a place for myself in the world, a process familiar enough that it may as well have been engraved into my bones. The details are always different, but the main steps are always the same, and the outcome is never in doubt. I remain mindful all the same, to avoid wasted effort. The rumors spread by my former cellmate have already provided the kindling. Mystery. Incredulity. Curiosity. I fan the embers through my indifference exaggerated slightly for effect to the stares, entreaties, and threats. I don't need to wait long. One day, while taking my shower, the other inmates furtively slip away, thinking I don't notice, and a gang leader and his men file in and surround me. They try to appear intimidating, casting sidelong glances at him for guidance. He comes in close to me, pokes his finger into my chest, asks what the hell I am, and if I know what he could do to me. Using his native tongue, I instead tell him who he is, in terms both profane and inarguably true, and what I will do to him. As he teeters between horror and rage, a slight twitch of my hand is enough to spur him and his enforcers to action. They beat me to death with metal pipes, padlocks wrapped in towels, fists, and feet. Once they are finished, I rise and rinse off the blood. They stand transfixed before me as I walk, slowly and deliberately, to the leader. He retreats blindly, realizing too late he has backed into a corner. He screams at his men to attack me. They don't. He begs them to save him. They don't. He pleads with me to spare him. I don't. I shower a second time and leave. Mystery. Fear. Revulsion. The pieces are falling into place. The next and final attempt on my life is more thorough. I am woken in the dead of night by two guards who escort me from my cell to one of the prison's several industries, a meatpacking facility. The lights switch on to reveal a coalition of high-ranking gang officers. The guards collect their payment and leave me in the hands of the prisoners, who to their credit don't bother with threats or needless brutality. They summarily dispose of me in an industrial meat grinder. - One of the guards involved in the conspiracy is overseeing the breakfast line the next morning. He is not a slim man, and his heart can not handle the shock of seeing me line up and claim my tray. I step over his body, take a seat at a suddenly-empty table in the center of the room, and begin eating my sausage and eggs. Mystery. Fear. Awe. I chew slowly and carefully, waiting until the paramedics have come and gone. All eyes are on me as I swallow the last bite and raise my head. I turn my head slowly, making eye contact with every man in turn. Most of the inmates flinch and look away, others stare back at me with cold murderous hate, and a rare few gaze back in wonder. From among the latter I decide on a skinny teen nearly still a boy with a fresh bruise on his cheek. I raise my hand and motion for him to approach. A jolt runs through his body and he glances around nervously, praying that I meant someone else. No, I shake my head, and repeat the gesture. He approaches cautiously, nearly on tiptoe. I place my hand on his shoulder and gently pull him down into the seat next to me. " What's your name? " I ask him. " J-j-jimmy " he manages to get out. I respond feigning concern. " Jimmy, do you have any friends here? " He looks down at his hands and answers almost inaudibly. I knew his answer before he opened his mouth, but still I lean closer as if I didn't hear. He repeats himself, this time loudly enough for others to hear. " No. " " Well Jimmy, " I say as my face slips from its normal benign indifference to my best smile and it is a very good smile indeed " you do now. " I look deep into his eyes and am satisfied with what I see. Confusion. Fear. Awe. And soon: Worship. I scan my eyes across the room for my next convert. Epilogue to follow

Harry strutted through the far side of the barrier, his designer robes flowing freely above his custom Air-dan Lynch sneakers. A hush fell over the platform as all eyes turned toward the Boy Wonder, a mixture of contempt and wonder flashing across their faces. "What the bloody hell are you looking at?" He snapped. He pushed his way through the throng of onlookers followed by his house elf Voldy. "Hurry up with my trunks or I'll slay you like your namesake." Harry ascended the steps onto the Hogwarts Express, walking down the corridor til he found his spot, the one he paid for and named "Harry Potter Commemorative Compartment." Inside was a scruffy red haired boy. "Why in the name of Grindelwald are you in here!?!" "I'm Ron, Ron Weasley, we talked over the owl post? I've got the dragons dandruff you wanted. " Ron pulled out a vial filled with white powder and poured some out on the table. Harry quickly pulled a parchment tube from within his robes. Just as he was leaning over the table the compartment door slid open. Harry turned to see a mane of bushy brown hair and a surprised face in the doorway. "Oh thank God, I didn't think we'd be able to find any of the good shit at this stupid school. I'm Hermione by the way, Hermione Granger."

"911, what is your emergency?" "I am lost in the woods." "Sir, you are going to have to be more specific than that. Where are you?" "I don't remember." "Why can you not remember? Have you sustained a head injury?" I feal the back of my head. My fingers come back red. "I think so. I think I am bleeding." "Well, we can send out a search party, but your best bet will be to find some high ground and calling us back when you figure out where you are." "I can't move. They might hear me." "What do you mean? Who is they?" "I don't know. I am being followed." "The search team is on the way. But if you don't know where you are and are unable to move it will be almost impossible to find you." They are getting closer. I am afraid to speak aloud. "Sir, are you still there? Sir I hang up. She was getting too loud. No luck on that front, anyway. Not unless I can find out where I am, or what the hell is going on. I am leaned against a tree. I can't tell if my head is still bleeding. Intense Breathing. I look desperately behind me. The fading light shows only the oaks, never-ending obstructions, and I hear only the breath. Precise. Calculating. I will not move. Not yet. I search my pockets. Lint. My phone's light is growing ever brighter in the surrounding dark. My vision is decreasing. I contemplate turning on my phone's flashlight. Something about that would make it even scarier. I can hear footsteps. Light pads on dead leaves. I am picturing monstrous wolves. Why do I not remember anything? Why am I in the middle of the woods at night with nothing but my phone? I have 4G but I don't know what I am supposed to do with it. I imagine typing out'How to survive wolf attack pls hurry' on Yahoo Answers. I am too scared to laugh. I look around the tree again. Movement. I am almost sure of it. Have I waited too long? I look back at my phone. No ideas. Footsteps and breathing. Closer. I am scared to look behind me. They are on me. I am surrounded. I can't see them. Snarling. I am gripping my phone for dear life. Shapes start to appear around the bases of the trees. They are coming towards me. They are sprinting. I turn on the flashlight. I see them. Their eyes shine with hate. They recoil in the light. I panic. I get up. They have stopped moving. I turn and run the opposite direction. Running footsteps. Closer. I shine my light behind myself. They don't stop. I can't see where I am going. Impact. I am stopped. I fall backwards. Breathing. On top of me. Snarling. Surrounded. Then the pain. rPeriapoapsis

It was the first cool day that marked the beginning of the end for summer. Soon the gray dullness of autumn and winter would be upon them, but for the moment the sky was a bold and lively blue. The coolness in the air and consistent breeze weren't altogether unpleasant, and after the hot muggy days of mid August it was a godsend. A lone Japanese maple stood in the middle of the backyard, as it had for nearly fifteen years. Clive was sitting in the lower branches, the bark was worn smooth by nearly a decade and a half of hands and feet climbing through it's branches. His left leg was restlessly moving the way it always did when he was thinking. Gus was laying down near the trunk of the tree. His eyes were closed, and his long steady breaths could easily have been mistaken for sleep, but Clive had known Gus for nearly his whole life- he was just taking in the scents and sounds of the day. The feel of sun through the tree, the sound of the wind through it's branches, the scent of bare earth near it's base. Perhaps this was Gus' way of passing time while Clive was occupied with his thoughts. Eventually Clive spoke up, "Gus, I'm pretty sure I'm the Antichrist." Gus's eyes fluttered open at the sound. He raised his eyebrows alternatingly, as he looked up at Clive. His brown eyes were sleepy but Clive now had his undivided attention. "Ok, I'm more than pretty sure, I'm dead certain." Gus looked to either side, and then back at Clive, who continued. "I'm going to have to do..... things. Pretty terrible things, and a lot of people are going to get hurt." Gus exhaled deeply. It sounded like he was frustrated, or maybe even bored, but like all good friends, he kept listening. "I'm not going to get a choice in it either. It sucks." Clive looked at the house, and then down at Gus. will finish later

Eight-hundred long years spent pushing the Mohammedans out of the Iberian peninsula. Decade after decade of finding the Morrano. Santiago and his predecessors tried their best to preserve Christendom and it's Greco-Roman origins. For years he had worked to bring the truth into the light of day. On some occasions he had no choice but to turn over his charges to the crown for relaxation. This had been a blessedly rare occurrence. "Oh, merciful God in heaven! H-how can I deny it!? My family, my blood! Heathens! They refuse the truth of Christ!" Head in his hands he cried openly, for the first time since leaving home. Upon hearing Santiago's weeping, a young friar comes into his study, worry etched across his face. He places a kind hand upon his mentor's shoulder. "What is wrong, Sir?" "How!? How could I have b-been so-so blind!? How c-could I have not seen it!?" The friar pulled his old friend and teacher into an embrace. Then he looked down at the papers on the desk and understood. "Have faith, Teacher. There is still the Edict of Grace. Go and encourage them. It is not as though we must hand them over for the auto de fe immediately. There is time and I will do what I can to help." Sighing heavily, Santiago took a moment and composed himself. "Thank you, Gustaf. You have always been a good friend. I just don't understand how I could have been so foolish all these years." "Remember, Brother Santiago, only the Almighty knows our hearts. Now, what is the nature of your family's crime?" Santiago shuffled through some papers and found what he was looking for. "They read some sort of false scripture penned by a Moor known as Alhazred, may he forever name Dis as home. I do not know enough of the tongue to take meaning, but it is called al-azif." Gustaf gathered the papers and journals and turned towards the door. "We will save them if we can, Santiago, you have my word!" Santiago turned to look at one last bit of paper. "Aforgomon who lurks at thresholds..... I will cast you back into the outer darkness, demon."

The first chevron locked into place. The sound seeming to boom though the hidden mountian complex. As the second chevron locked the men had began to stir and recheck their weapons. They had known this day was coming, the whole world had. After the first attack had been turned away they had revealed the secret of the gate to the world. As the third chevron locked they started to get reports from the satalites in space. They had known they were coming, they had seen the scout ships coming in and out of system for days. But now, now there were five large pyramid shapped ships sitting between the moon and the planet. The bombardment started with the forth chevron. Whole cities were wipped off the map in an instant. Some of the soilders started to wonder what the point of coming through the gate was if they were just going to glass the planet. By the time the fifth chevron had lit up all of the planets nuclear missiles had been spent in a failed attempt to stop the encroaching ships that now sat at the top of the gravity well. By the time the sixth chevron locked into place the mountain had lost contact with the outside world, their power only coming from the generators deep in the heart of the complex. When the seventh chevron locked the men said a quick prayer as the room was washed in blue white light. For the next several minuites all that could be heard was the sound of gunfire as round after round was expended at the golden armored troops walking though the gate. But it was not enough to stem the tide. The superhuman soldiers just kept coming though the gate, their faces hidden behind animal like masks. The few soilders that were left heard the voice of their commander come over the speaker "All is lost they are though the gate. retreat to the outer rooms and await evac." 400 years later. This time when the chevrons lit up there was no one to take note, no one to notice the sound of metal sliding over metal. There were no messages or sounds of explosions as the fourth chevron locked and no silent prayers as the gate lit up and spewed forth. Instead of golden armored troops four people clad in camo stepped onto the platform that held the ring. "What do you think danny-boy? Some kind of old temple?" Jack asked placing his sunglasses on his head. "No actually it looks like we are inside of, well a mountain." Daniel said after a minute of shining a flashlight over the walls." "Well It makes sense, I mean we wouldn't be the only ones with the idea to hide the gate away in a mountain." Samantha said. "Spooky is what it is." Said jack glancing down at the discarded guns and empty magazines. "Ok lets just do a quick look around and then get out of here." You're just the best thing that's ever happened to me, y'know? And it's not hard for me to forgive you for disappearing so suddenly. It's like I forget what I've been so bent out of shape about. I feel this confused anger, like I'm mad at myself but mad at everything all at once but my "self" is part of everything all at once so naturally I have to be mad at myself. But mostly I think I'm mad at me. Until, of course, you're here. When you're gone, I totally forget what it was like to have you in my arms, in my eyes. But when you come back to me, you are the only thing I can concentrate on. You're just so much a part of everything and you're not apart from it. You're just like me. Even when you just sit there, staring at me and off into the distance, I'm so glad to be with you. Though I must say, I appreciate you not coming around when I'm with my family..... for some reason, they don't seem to like you. I guess they just don't understand. But you understand. You understand me and I understand you. That's what makes you so much like me. And your voice, mercy me oh my your voice can set me free! When you leave me next time, do you think you could sing to me like you always sing me to sleep? You don't have to stick around if you don't want, but you really know how to get inside my head and you're always invited. Even if it's just to sing. It was Sarah's son's 18th birthday, and having passed his driving test, she had decided to buy him a new car. Well, as new a car as a single 43 year-old woman can afford. Pulling up outside Little Indsley's newest car dealership,'Sherlock Watson', she and Gary (she named her son after Gary Glitter, which caused him 10 years of ridicule at school) got out of a decade-old Citroen C3 and walked through the driveway to see a tall man dressed in what appeared to be a woman's coat. Upon closer inspection, Sarah noticed the man had curly dark hair and icy blue eyes. He wore a deerstalker hat, which covered most of his hair, which, Sarah thought, was highly contradictory as she had just decided that he had curly hair. The man proffered no hand and gave no greeting, but simply looked over Sarah. Is he checking me out? thought Sarah as his dreamy eyes washed over him. Don't be silly She also noticed that the man seemed to be muttering to himself. He then repeated the same process over Sarah's son. After an incredibly brief moment that stretched out for an incredibly long time, the man simply said "You're a lesbian, and you," he motioned towards Gary, "you were sexually abused in a lavatory when you were fourteen." "What?" Sarah said dumbly. Gary began to sob into his hands loudly. Of course, sexual abuse is an incredibly traumatising affair and should not be taken lightly, and if you laughed at that you are a monster. A shorter man with greying hair marched out of the main office. "Nonononono, you don't understand, that's just how he greets people" he said frantically. Sarah simply stood and stared. She realised that she was, in actual fact, a lesbian after all, but had never stopped to think about it. It explained everything about her life; why her husband left, why she kept getting aroused around women (obviously). After a few moments, she simply said, "thanks for everything," and ushered her crying son into her car and drove off. "You complete twat!" Watson yelled at Sherlock. "I don't understand, what did I do wrong?" Sherlock replied. "You insulted a potential customer and told her son that he was sexually abused, that's what!" "Oh no, I was helping them!" "In what way were you helping them?" "Didn't you see in the way she stopped for a few moments just before she left? She had a moment of sudden realisation that has probably changed her life for the better." "And what about the'sexually abused' boy?" "Oh, you heard'sexually abused'? I said'sexually aroused'! The universe then collapsed in on itself as the previous events made absolutely no sense and were clearly an improvised rescue from what could have been a long list of very angry comments.

Captain Atomic. What a fucking shithead. This ass practically destroys my lab once a month, and everybody loves him for it. I barely have time to even set up shop before he trashes whatever abandoned warehouse or condemned apartment building I'm forced to move to. I'm not even trying to kill him any more! I just want to make something that will keep him out of the lab long enough for me to do some actual work, but the buffoon wouldn't know a power dampener sphere from an inverse particle blaster if I shoved it up his ass. They're all "weapons of mass destruction" to him, and since he destroys them before anyone else can get a look, who can contradict him? Yeah, I'll steal a truckload of Uranium here or rob a bank there, but do you have any idea how much power he puts out? I'd need enough energy to power half the city just to make him blink, and believe me: a setup like that does not come cheap. I hadn't even finished moving in this time when he came crashing through the ceiling. I can't even muster the energy to be surprised any more. I just gave him a blank stare as he did that stupid pose he always does: hands on his hips, beaming like a moron at nothing in particular. Normally I'd have put up some token resistance out of spite, but most of my gear is still in boxes. The Freeze Ray was the last thing that had stopped him for any length of time anyways, and he destroyed that two labs ago. Right as I'm about to just leave, he finally speaks up. "Doctor Chaos! " he says. I've stopped bothering to tell him my name is Dr. Kevin Carlisle, and that the Metro Times can go fuck itself for coming up with such a horrible "supervillain" name for me. "I hope I'm not interrupting any foul deeds this morning! " I'd describe talking to Captain Atomic as similar to talking to a wall, but honestly I think the wall might react more to what I have to say. Nevertheless, I know he won't get things over with before he gets his "banter" in, so I go ahead and speak up. "I've unpacked maybe four boxes, Cap. I haven't even had time to set up the coffee maker." "Well I'm afraid you're going to have to put them on hold, for JUSTICE! " "Fine. Whatever. Haven't even put in my security deposit for this place anyways." "Much as I hate to admit it, the city no, the WORLD needs your help! " "I'll just be outsi wait what?" "My evil self from another dimension, NEGA-CAPTAIN ATOMIC, has arrived in the city! Since he's equal in power to myself, I can not defeat him alone! I need the experience of my archenemy to defeat myself! " I almost try to explain the difference between a dimension and a parallel universe, but realize the lecture would fall on deaf ears. Instead, I ask the question I know he's waiting for, even though I already know the answer. "And why should I help you?" "Unlike me, NEGA-CAPTAIN ATOMIC only wants wanton destruction! He'll destroy the entire city, you and your lab included! " "Oh yeah, it would be a shame to have somebody destroy my lab," I mumble to myself. "Fine. If it'll get you to leave me alone for a whole fucking afternoon, sure. Get me Destructo's Gamma Beam and I'll make something that can send him back." Surprisingly, he seemed to understand this last part. Maybe he enjoyed the excuse to go beat the shit out of Destructo. He's back in a little under an hour and gives me a new hole in my ceiling along with the blaster. After some tinkering, I successfully install some tesseract lenses and adjust the power regulators to turn the Gamma Beam into a Quantum Detangler. I try to hand it to the musclebound oaf, but he refuses. "No, I'll have to distract him while you take the shot. " "You know this won't kill him, right? You can use it without breaking your stupid no-killing rule. I'd really rather stay here and work while you're preoccupied." As usual, he doesn't hear a word of it. He just picks me up and flies towards City Hall. "Wait until I give you the signal! " he insists on the way. " I can't have you accidentally harming civillians! " "It..... doesn't work like that. This'll only work on him, because he's from another universe. It'll just send him back home. I can't even use it on you." Despite the fact that he was looking right at me, I'm pretty sure he didn't precess this, either. Whatever, if he gets himself killed trying to "distract" his double, I can still send the bastard back. Two birds with one stone. The battle starts maybe fifteen minutes after we reach the mayor's office. The two fight for upwards of three hours, destroying so much property in the process that I can't imagine Nega-Cap could have done a mere effective job on his own. Eventually Captain Atomic gets his double in a headlock close enough for me to send Nega flailing back through the multiverse into his own world. Mission accomplished, world saved, time to go home. Or, at least, that's what I thought was the plan, before I noticed the Detangler was getting very hot in my hands. "What the fuck?!" I yell, throwing the device away from me. It melts mid-air as Cap continues to blast it with his heat vision. "You could have ruptured the power cell and killed us all! What the hell was that?!" "I can't have you using such a powerful device against me in the future! " So yes, he was clearly ignoring me when I was explaining it only worked on Nega-Cap. "And now, to go destroy your lab where the plans for the device are! " He flies off before I can even react. I don't bother heading back to that lab; I know it'll just be a smouldering heap by the time I can take the subway there. Instead, I call my real-estate agent. Captain Atomic. What a fucking shithead.
