(Part I) "Hey Honey." I awoke in a cold sweat. Upright sitting in my bed, I can feel the sweat beading down my back as I try to make sense of what just happened. "Lights On." The lights flash on, my vision strains as I adjust. I look at the clock, 7:00am. "Great." Its been three years since I lost her, funny, you would think in this day and age where everyone is saying "this is the future we've been waiting on" we would have a better grip on curing cancer. I dont buy into this future thing. Ever since Psy-net has come online I've been suspicious. I understand its useful, given the fact that crime has never been lower now that they can stop it before it happens, but im not to crazy about the idea of thought-monitoring even if it ensures my safety. Im glad Donna isnt around for all of this, she wouldnt have it, fighting tooth and nail to stay absolutely individual. Lately, things have been getting worse though.I think about her all the time, I feel like shes even around or I hear her voice. Psy-net analysis tells me its grief, but what does IT know. At the workplace "Hey Dave." "Hey Bucky, how was your weekend?" "It was good, man Dave you look like shit, you been sleeping alright?" "Yeah man, its just those late nights, you know?" "I hear you Dave, you know Francis? He is doing Neuro-coding down the street from Starbucks. He can give you an enhancement so you sleep better. Shit, Monica and I went and got an'update' to make things a little hotter in bed....if you catch my drift." "Oh yeah? Well thanks Buck, ill look into it." I'm not one for enchantments, tried it once. Bucky is crazy about them. Endorphin boosts, Adrenaline surges, etc. I am still coping with the fact we are now all'connected' and we can now use the previously'inaccessible' section of our minds via a visit to you local neuro-code office. The cold sweats have been going on since she passed..... maybe I should consider it. The last time I went was right after Donna passed. I was having trouble coping, I was fine for a week, totally removed from the sititution but then..... then I swear I would hear her call my name..... it doesn't happen often but it does. Ah, what the hell, im not a drinker so might as well make life a bit easier. At the Neruo-code office I walk through the holo-door and feel the air conditioning kiss my face. Those doors amaze me, but then again I've never really looked into it. Just the day in and day out accountant that cant cope with loss. Nothing Special. "Ahhhh! Dave!" Ugh, Francis....or should I say DOCTOR Francis. He is such a prick sometimes, only reason I come here is because he is so close to the office and the tram is always full of "outliers," people that rejected Psy-net. Outliers are funny, they all seem like this is one big conspiracy to track your thoughts and market to you like sheep. Sometimes I think they might have a point, but unless your on the'net you cant get a job....I would rather a job. Anyway, Francis is about 5'10 and always smells like Fun-yuns and can not seem to grow a full beard, which I thought there may be an enhancement for that, I guess not. His business is super popular in the city only because of the cut-rate prices and the fact that the only other one doesnt have the "under the table" enchantments Francis has. There is one thing about Francis though that makes me annoyed the most. He always, and I mean always, is wearing those toe-shoes. I wish that style had died out a long time ago. "Hey Francis." "That's Doctor to you, bud!" "Yeah I keep forgetting, considering you never went to med school" I mumbled that last bit. "What can I do you for Dave?" "I've been having trouble staying asleep lately" "A whole lotta that going around lately. Your about the 15th customer this week!" "Im guessing business been good then?" "Booming like you wouldnt believe." I dont give a shit. Just give me the fucking code and let me go home. "Hey Dave, what about and update on the last enchantment I gave you? Free of charge." The last one didnt do shit, something to do with my Melatonin levels, whatever that hell that is. "What is it even supposed to do?" "It is supposed to make you sleep you idiot! Ive been toying with code and realized that I had the dosage wrong to be delivered" Great, turns out my first enchantment was a test. There has got to be some kind regulations on this stuff. "Sure, as long as it wont kill me" "Nah Dave, you're good. This is one everyone gets. After all, who doesn't want to sleep better!" I lean back into what looks like a retro-fitted dental chair. The monitor buzzing about with what looks like hieroglyphs on the screen. This is the worst part of Psy-net. The way it works, to my understanding, is that when you first get the implant they inject it through a wide bore needle. You can feel something go into your veins, but the unpleasant feeling subsides. Anyway, they say it floats around your blood stream until it reaches the blood-brain barrier. Here the chip, nano-bot, whatever the fuck it is, is able to permeate through the barrier and embed into the brain matter. You dont feel any different but now you can go about your life and get enchantments and what-have you. To'update' or get enhancements you just wear this helmet that communicates through it via....i think it was RFID. I try not to think about it since its all over my head intellectually anyway. The machine buzzes, I get rung up at the front desk and I head on home. I feel more'awake' but I think thats just because I can breather normal air now instead of the Fun-yun laced air of Francis' office.

As the cool liquid filled his mouth he knew something was just.... off..... It was his favorite drink for years, bloody marry, spiced, but this tasted somewhat metalic and rusty..... He put the drink down and decided that he had a pretty rough week and should probably just go home and head to bed. The office had been slammed with new proposal work and the business development team had to work a double shift three nights in a row. As he jingled the keys and started the car, he had no idea that he was being followed. The man who was following him had been alone for too long. He had been without a partner for far too long and he was depressed. To spend all of eternity alone? Was that a fate even a monster diserved? His clan had been killed off in the 1400's and for over 600 years he had tried to live in peace. He had taken a mate over the years, but he hated being what he was, he would only drink animal blood and never harm humans, despite what they had done to his clan many years ago. All it took was one drop, one little drop of his own blood it that man's drink and he would no longer be alone in this world. He had already spiked three drinks this week, the other three babies chained up at his house waiting for their first meal in their new body. He lurked in the shadows following the man home, waiting for the change to begin.

I was at my Uncle's house the day before I turned sixteen. His house was a potpourri of spices and curry. They smelled amazing one by one, but together, they hit you like a spice train, each carriage hitting you with a new blast of pepper. I watched him flip pancakes for breakfast from thin air. I sighed and ate the pancakes, as they appeared one after the other. They tasted like pancakes all right, nothing special. Usually Uncle would constantly hammer on about the success of his restaurant, but after twenty years, the novelty of his powers soon ran out and his business was running downhill. That was often the case with the members of my family. Our powers were novel, but just because you were special it didn't make you useful. Although we were proud that we were different than the rest, I often wished that I could grow up with normal powers like flying and super strength. I mean, people from around the world would all gather around their television to watch the flying people compete in blitzball. In my family, we gather around my older sister. She picks up television broadcast or radio signals, processes them and displays them on her belly. She is happy that people always want her around, but I don't think that's for the right reasons. My dad was consoling me through Skype. He told me I should be happy with whatever power I got. I should be happy of my lineage and my power, because that's who I am. I told my dad that I wished he were here to support me. He told me he would, if he didn't find himself trapped in the Internet after he turned sixteen. I asked him how he made me then. He told me that I wasn't ready for that yet, and to just remember that my mother can travel through fax machines. My mother was upstairs reading. She reads a lot these days, not being able to work as a travelling saleswoman now that fax machines are a thing of the past. I couldn't help but cry. I wanted to shoot lasers from my eyes and phase through walls. My friends were already reading each other's minds and turning things to ice. I found my bed. The police didn't even bother to put me in quarantine. I closed my eyes. I woke with an energy pulsing through me. I tried not to get excited so the disappointment wouldn't hit me as hard, but it just felt so good. I don't know what took over me, but I jumped and crashed through the bedroom window. Suddenly I was flying, and the broken shards of the window bounced off my impenetrable skin. I shrilled in delight and waved to my friend dashing below me. He gave me a thumbs up, but I could here him say in his mind that he didn't really care. I was surprised; I had invisibility, flying and mind reading. I wanted to see what more I could do. I picked up the car parked below me. It was easy, like a feather. I felt as if all the generations of my ancestor's mediocrity had built up to unleash a combination of great powers within me. Within a few hours time, I was folding the ground from beneath me, I was balancing the earth and the sun on opposite hands, and I was ripping holes in time and space, sending galaxies into oblivion. My power was overwhelming, and I felt awesome. Uncle Brandon looked down on Peter who was laughing hysterically in bed. John was on the Skype call, and Mary put down her book. Together they watched Peter have the dream of his life, for his life.

Dearest Sally, You have indeed been good all year long. I am delighted to give you a pony. You earned it, and don't let anyone tell you differently. I will make sure it's in the living room on Christmas Eve, right by the tree, but on only one condition. I care about my ponies very much. When people lose them or give them away, then they feel upset. If you accept this pony for your very own, then you mustn't let anyone ever take it from you. All you have to do is agree to love it forever. Sign your name on the enclosed piece of paper, and then the pony is yours. If you don't, then I can't leave it with you. I do hope that's not the case. You want a pony, don't you? Many little girls in apartments lie to me about it, and I'd hate to have to give your pony to another little girl. - Satan - Dearest Bobby, There's no need to lie to me about having been good. In fact, I found your behavior so delightful that I'll let you in on a secret. Did you know that children can also order whatever they want online? You don't even need mommy and daddy's permission. All you need is one of their credit cards. If you buy from a store they usually purchase items from, then they won't even know it was you and will blame each other for the charge. There are also other, much cooler toys online than the ones on your list. Of course, you could still have Legos. But would you like a flamethrower Bobby? All the candy you can eat? It's all there. I suggest waiting until night, when your parents are asleep. Make sure the computer's speakers are off first. My very best, Satan

Last one. Last one. I promise, last one. Of course it never is, and I always know. Yet there's something oddly comforting about thinking it. Last one. Until it actually is, and then reality hits and its time to come home. I'll have to explain to Jane where the money went..... and I can't keep saying its on fishing supplies. She isn't stupid, she knows, but as I keep deceiving myself into thinking its the last one, she holds on to..... hope, perhaps, that I am not throwing our future into a machine or a deck of cards. I stumble out of the casino drunk with self-made shame, can't afford the fancy behind the counter shame. Nor do I crave it, but seeing there on the ground, just laying there, is a bottle and the urge to pick it up. There's nothing special about it that I can see, it's unlabelled, just a plain bronze bottle..... but it just looks so..... delicious? I quickly glance around to see if anyone has claimed this prize, but its already in my hands as I rub it possessively. The bottle hums, although I can't tell if its audible or just in my head, but I know it offers me three wishes, to be decided in the next three minutes. Like any reasonable adult, I have spent many a night thinking about these wishes, and they come immediately. "I wish for Pokemon to be real." Reality warps around me, and suddenly I am in a house. New memories come to me, Jane has left, my obsession with gambling lost all our money, but it was my fishing obsession that drove us apart. These wishes come at a cost, each wish is a gamble. I quickly move on to the next, nothing could go wrong with this. "I wish to be rich" Nothing has changed. Jane is still gone, but suddenly I am hit with new memories and experiences. I have wasted all the money. On fishing supplies and a new bike..... I was never good at gambling. But there is one thing I could be good at. "I wish for a shiny Magikarp!" A pokeball hangs on my belt, it's there. It is mine, yet I do not feel pride or joy. Why? And then it hits me. No one cares about the colour, it's all about the size. Even with my wishes I can't be the best. I need the biggest Magikarp. And as I am thinking, regretting, a young boy walks in, approaches me silently. Why doesn't he speak? A new thought comes to me, I will gamble one last time. I tell him that I want the biggest Magikarp, and that he will be rewarded. But he doesn't seem to have a rod. I knew that of course, but he seems like the one, the very best. So I give him my most prized possession, and hope this gamble pays off. I give him my Super Rod.

I waited until Lucy had finished her story and the others had left the break room before striking up a casual conversation, which was, unbeknownst to her, a dull preamble to the question that had been nagging at me since she had started talking. "What is a Mother?." I slipped it in whilst filling my plastic cup with water from the cooler. She looked surprised, and guilty. Like a child with her hand in the sweet drawer. "Something you said just then, about a Mother who you knew when you were younger. Is it like a pet?" "Ummmm yes, yes that's exactly what it is!" Lucy replied, unconvincingly. "It's a type of dog. Big, furry, y'know?." She scurried away back to her workstation and started clicking frantically on her keyboard. An internet search pulled back nothing for the word, I was just redirected to various adverts for holiday resorts and insurance policies. I would usually just let it go, but an odd feeling came over me. It was like the fading image of a dream, a word on the tip of your tongue. My head throbbed as I sat there, pushing myself to recall the meaning of that word. Mother. 2 men in white suits approached Lucy's desk and after a short discussion, escorted her out of the office. With one last look back at me, she was gone. The rest of the afternoon passed and Lucy did not return. On my way out I stopped by her desk, pretending to look through her in-tray for a file. A white envelope poked out from beneath her keyboard, my name scribbled on it. I deftly slid it from the desk and into my pocket. Once I was clear of the office and hallway to my car, I tore the envelope open and read the note that Lucy had left me. IT'S ALL FOR YOU. DO N'T QUESTION THE PAST. My heart thudded out of my chest. I felt like I was being watched, so put my head down and made my way quickly to the parking lot. I was home within 20 minutes, had changed and made food within the hour. I tried to put the events of the day out of my mind and focus on other things; I watched tv for a while, read an article about global warming, and fed my fish. I started to get tired so made my way to the bedroom and settled into my pod. I plugged the wires into the node in my arm and fell straight to sleep. I woke up at 8am prompt and made my way to work. Lucy gave me an odd look as I sat down. She looked guilty, like a child caught with it's hand in the sweet drawer. A strange feeling crept over me like there was something I should remember.

"I ain't Billy Crystal, son. I don't exactly keep em on tap." "But it's coming." He nods. "So it is, and a lot of people are gon na get hurt. More'll die. Sufferin' like ya can't describe. Shame of it is that so many of'em chose it. Eyes open. They didn't have to. Far as upstairs is concerned, that's a fair play. They'll save ya, but not from yourself." "Neither will you." "Oh?" A level look. "And you're not exactly batting for their team." "Well. Ain't this a turn? Been a while since someone with a clue was desperate enough to come to me for help. You know I don't work for free? You familiar with my rates?" "Immortal soul? Firstborn child? Contract in blood? That sort of thing?" He spits, and then grins wryly. "Naw. Don't believe them damn, useless stories." "What then? For this I'd pay gladly." "I know you would, son. I know." A shake of the head. "No. Got no use for either souls or brats. Payment'll be this: sometime down the road, you got to make a choice. Could be simple. One day you see me, an' I might ask'chocolate or vanilla?' You answer yer fancy. Do that for me three times and we're square." "But it probably won't be that easy." "Might. Might not. Might be'pick who dies'. Won't matter what you pick, just that you pick at all. You understand, son: you take my help and there's no backing out. Down payment'll be the choice take the offer. And these choices, they'll be powerful. And bindin'. You'll choose. You'll have to." "Why?" "Son, there's a lot more to that question than ya think it is. Some free advice: stick to one miracle a day." He looks at me slyly. "So we have a deal?"

I don't know why people call me "the evilest person ever lives." I mean, there's Hitler and some other bad dictator and army general out there. All I did is kill some people for fun, it's not we are running out of Humans anyway. We have..... How many again? 7 billion? 7 million? I forgot. "Prisoner." A guard called. He opened my cell and then entered it with another two guard just to be safe. The first guard handcuffed my hand, and then guide me out of the cell. There is no chanting as I walked through the hallway, like in the movies. Sorry to disappoint you, for I am locked inside the solitary jail for quite a while now. All because I stab some people with fork in the eye and neck, it's not like anyone is going to miss them murderer and child molester anyway. I did choke a priest before, that one is my fault I admit. The guards took me to a room, with glass panels where I could see the audience. Look of disgust, anger, sadness, and relief. They seated me in a chair, strapped my hands in addition of the cuff. The doctor fiddled with something, and then I could see a needle. Whatever substance inside it is going to end me. The guards took some step back, as the doctor approached me. "Any last word?" He asked. "This is your chance to speak up." I smirked at the doctor, startling him, before turning at the audience. I could hear them shouting, mocking, and insulting me. Which is great, for that means they could hear what I say as well. It come to me suddenly this morning, before the guards come to take me. Maybe it come to me because I killed so many people and love doing so, or maybe because I am going to die, or maybe this is a gift from the Devil. Maybe he likes how I helped him reaping souls. I licked my dry lips and said the Sentence of Death. There's a total silence, before people started gasping for breath and twitched. I watch as the doctor dropped the syringe and fall to the ground, pale as a sheet and as dead as my victims. I smiled, before laughing like never before.

At midday, the King signed me off with his sword and the waive of his wrist. My death rite, the last honor, to hold the same steel that I had betrayed my brethren with. They frowned down at me with scorn. Years of service forgotten. For a memory, of a memory, of a newcomer's whisper held more weight than my sword itself. These calloused hands would never grip a friend's again. These feet, never to ache under the march of heavy mail. My hair never to feel the closure of a helmet. My tongue the taste of beer it would mourn. Nor my spirit the raging passion of a battle cry. I turned the blade toward me, suddenly steel I knew so well felt so cold in my hands. We enter from a warm womb into an icy world. Why had I expected going out to be any different? Piercing my intestines, I felt blood ooze out onto my innocent hands. A soft whimper escaped my lips, adding more distaste to the scorn of the onlookers. It's one thing to be a false criminal, and another to suffer your King's judging eyes. I would rather be gone, than live with either. I hacked fresh dots of red into the snow. Letting my memories flash by. But as the world slowly slipped away, the wails of a widow guided me, into deaths permanent embrace.

I'm not like other people. I know how everyone will die. All I need to do is look at their face and it comes to me like a vivid memory. The boy who sits next to me in class will live to be 102 and then die of natural causes. The bus driver will see a woman getting mugged and try to be a hero, only to get shot between the eyes. My neighbor's stupid dog will run into the street and be hit by an oncoming vehicle while chasing after a stick that he was playing with. I avoid pictures and videos of myself, and have never looked in a mirror since this condition started effecting me when I was small. Last weekend, I was brushing my teeth after sleeping over a friends house and saw it. I looked in the mirror. All I could see was me walking across the street with my head down and being run over. Now I have the choice every time I walk somewhere. I can look at reflections of myself in cars so I don't get hit, but watch myself die a hundred times. Or, I can keep my head down so I don't have to watch myself die, but actually die. Obviously, I've been keeping my head up and watching myself die, since I'm writing this. I'm actually writing this while walking down the sidewalk. You see, I was on my way to class when I remembered my professor had told us to write an autobi " It seems like he dropped his pen into the street, and when he put his head down to look for it, a speeding car turned the corner and ran him over, it sure is tragic. " said the policeman to the paramedic.

My first lucid dream was in my mid-teens. I was laying on a bed, in a room, with an apparatus above my head. I knew this was a dream machine, and wires ran to my head, connecting me to it..... and the person on the other end. I knew it was a girl, in a room fully mirrored, laying in a bed, with the same wires attached to her. When the machine clicked on, there was a slip. Film noir. Following a man in third person. He's wearing a trench coat and a brimmed hat walking down a foggy sidewalk in some 1930s city. He stops at a bar and orders a drink. As the bartendress is making the drink, I realize that I can make stairs out of her hands. As this starts to happen, confusion on her face, she looks at me instead of the character I'm following. Then I feel like I've been punched in the face. My head bounces off the pillow of my bed and I'm awake, full of adrenaline. That's how the dreams were for years after, just your regular weird dream until I assumed control over it and almost immediately crashed it..... until years later. I was a lone warrior in some medieval setting, wandering the country-side. I journeyed into a rather large city and when I entered the front gate I was dumbfounded..... I had been here before! It was something about the shape of the castle's walls, and I could feel the dream start to crash, I was regaining the sense of my body laying in my bed. I stopped my thoughts as quickly as I could by humming a little tune and sauntered into an inn. The feeling of my body had subsided as I had totally forgotten what it was that I was just thinking. As I stepped through the threshold of the building everything became unusually vibrant. The colors and smells didn't have the same dream-like quality as they had had the moment before. This was surreal. As I stepped down out of the entryway onto the dirt floor of the common area I saw her for the first time. I immediately fell in love with her. Something seemed familiar about her. She had a black ponytail, pearly skin, and her eyes looked like emeralds. She squinted at me in recognition and my heart skipped a beat. Before I could realize what had happened everything between her and I blew away in some magical frenzy. The table she was sitting at split a patron in half before blasting through the wall to my right. Silverware and broken pieces of wood slammed into a few other bystanders, and something blew right through the ceiling. I was still staring into her eyes, as lost as a child when I heard her say, "You..." That's when the pain of the dagger in my neck registered. I awoke as I bounced clear of my mattress, heart about ready to explode. I stayed up all night. I struggled to remember what that place was, who she was..... WHAT she was. I drew blanks on all three. That night, when I finally HAD to go to sleep, I decided I would just run. As soon as I started dreaming, everything was as clear as it had been in the pub. I felt a tap on my shoulder. I turned to look but only saw my own blood leaving my face in a mist in front of an armored fist. I slid down the dirt street of the town briefly before hitting a brick wall and slumped to the ground. I couldn't move, I was searching for my body wondering why I haven't woken up yet. She walked over to me and said, "You must be out cold!" I was still searching for my ticket out of the pain in my face when she said, "I didn't mean in the dream you dumb fuck, MOVE YOURSELF!" She grabbed me by the arm and twirled round with it so hard that it took me a moment to realize I was flying higher than the tree tops..... without my arm, leaving a scattered stream of blood behind me. Then she was there, flying with me, over the city walls, holding me by my breastplate. When we locked eyes all my pain disappeared until she said, "Good luck sleeping." She then flicked her sword, severing my head from my body. Grabbing my head by my hair, she flung it high and far. Everything spun so fast I only knew that she could've thrown me over the mountains with her strength. I awoke in a sweat, this time with sleep paralysis. After a few minutes of panic, I was able to finally flop my arm right into my face. As my eyes teared up from the smack to my nose, I realized how traumatically real my death had felt in that dream. It was worse than any I had experienced before. Two straight days without sleep, I dozed off on the couch when I was just going to "lay down for a minute and that's it." I was in a dream, tending horses at some farm in the country..... I thought to myself, "At least she threw me far enough that I can get some actual sleep before she tracks me down and kills me again." I spent a whole day working on some farm, trying to think about nothing but what I was doing so nothing would pop me out of some much needed sleep. I woke up to my alarm, wanting nothing but to go back to bed. I just worked all day, I'm exhausted. This'll take me another day or two. I should've gone to bed hours ago.

"You seem to be a very troubled man, why? " , said the Guru. "Can't you see why!? I'm overwhelmed by debt and I'm all alone. So alone...," I cried out. I felt a hand on my shoulder, not one that tried to hold me back, but one to push me forward. The Guru spoke again, "Do not worry sir, you seem to be one who has endured through a lot of pain. Let that pain be your motivation to feel well again. Loneliness is something that everybody experiences so don't fret, it shall pass with time. The debt though, is something that can only be solved with time. So be patient and you shall be well again. Let my hand be the first to push you towards your future. It may not be much of a push, but it is a push that will give you a step into the right direction." My throat chokes up and I can barely whisper to him, "I have given my problems nothing but time though! It's been 20 long years and nothing has changed! I'm still in debt and all alone. How can you say that giving me a push will send me in the right direction when I've been going in the wrong direction all my life!?" The Guru sighs and says to me, "Do you truly believe that there is nothing left? Do you truly believe that it will never get better?" "Yes...," I whisper. "There is nothing I can do then, my friend. I have tried to help you but you will have none of it. So go, let go your earthly tether, enter the void, empty and become wind."

'The Age of the Burning Sun' I don't know much about the time before the Great Change, only the stories they told us about people living on the surface But I don't have time to worry about the past; there is a much greater problem at hand... We live miles underground; the Under-Republic calls us the ' Colonies' We can't go onto the surface anymore, because of the Sun. The Sun has gotten so hot that its rays kill humans on contact Scientists have come up with some reason for the burning sun, but as I said... I don't have time to worry about it As you might have guessed, living underground has its consequences Resources are spread thin Food is grown and Ore is mined in the Primary Colonies, most of our hard earned gatherings are shipped to other colonies, leaving us with little to survive off of. Manufacturing and Industrial factories are in Secondary Colonies, I've heard rumors that they kill ' useless'people and use them as fuel to burn Tertiary Colonies are for the rich and politically oriented people. I'm not exactly sure what they do except get fat and make money off of other Colonies There are also special colonies like Research or Botanic Colonies that grow trees and plants for Oxygen We have to mine space to live in, but where do we put the excess rubble? We have to dump it on the surface, which is increasingly expensive and difficult to do Obviously there isn't enough space to put all the people Every month the Under-Republic representatives of each Colony pick a handful of people that they deem ' useless' or not contributing to the society as much as they should These people get dumped to the surface at night, and they have roughly three hours before the sun comes up I'm a coal miner in a Primary colony, ' the lowest scum of the world' according to the Under-Republic Life wasn't easy but I still managed to survive and feed my family That was until I got sick It's called ' Black Lungs', which is damaged lungs from breathing in Coal dust. My productivity has decreased and there definitely isn't a Medical Insurance for Primary Colonies And that's why I'm on the surface today, because I was deemed ' useless'by the Under-Republic My brothers and I are running west as fast as possible to avoid the rise of the sun It's pointless to outrun the sun, but it gives us a sense of... hope, something we haven't felt in a long time I know the sun is just behind me, I can hear the burning of my brothers who are not as quick as me I try to run as fast as I can, but then I just... stop, realizing how pointless my efforts are In my last moments, I face the sun rays catching up to me and close my eyes I feel a warm heat come over my body, not a burning heat just a... warm heat... a comforting heat... How is this possible? How am I still alive? Am I still alive? I open my eyes and realize that yes, I am alive and the sun has passed over me. What is this? My brothers burning corpses are near me, but I do not burn. This is something new, this is something we haven't felt in a long time, this is hope

I slid the dragon's key into the metal sheath, slowly twisting it's spiral tail until I heard the sound of metal sliding across its' brothers. Gears moved and spun as the pipes let out a hiss and filled the room with air left untouched for thousands of revolutions. Stirring new motion in the air, I reached for the wooden handle and pulled. The door budged slightly, but wasn't going anywhere. I planted myself firmly on the ground, digging my feet into the hard rock and dust. I reeled back as the door creaked into motion, slowly opening the room. When it was of sufficient distance for me to enter, I did. Inside was a sea of darkness, yet reflective enough to see myself, a younger me. I stared down the maw of this liquid beast and felt my legs kick into motion. Was I running? Yes, I was running. Awareness crept back into my mind as I reached up, grabbing at the trapdoor that led me here. I rushed back to the town hall, where the king sang and rejoiced with the people. I tried to reach him, but I failed. The ooze wrapped itself around my legs and the legs of those around me, slowly enveloping us to the neck. Darkness set in, as I held my last regrets. I knew what I was doing.

It was my 4th visit. My friend Dan had been living here for over a year now and kept bragging how mankind had finally created a true democratic society. He wanted me to move in but I remained skeptical. These new Web-Towns we're emerging all over the world but I still had a bitter taste in my mouth from that three months experience in Los Google. Having to share all my private life with city officials every time I needed to take a piss wasn't my definition of "enhanced services." "Stop looking so grim, New Reddit is nothing like that shit hole you tried last year." Dan said as we reached our destination. I looked at the large marble arch in front of us, rAskReddit was carved in it. "What's so special about this place?" I replied. "I'm telling you man, this neighborhood will blow your mind. Anything you could possibly wonder, someone here will be able to answer it." He said with such enthusiasm that I finally smiled. We started walking around but I felt like such a tourist. The place looked like a giant fair. Everywhere we went, someone was standing on a little stage with a sign in his hands. What movie has the worst ending? What is career suicide in your industry? What sentence do you know that can start an internet war? I couldn't understand why these questions mattered to anyone but the crowd seemed to love it. Hundreds of them gathered around each stage, shouting their answers. "Chewing gum!" "Oranges!" "Pancakes!" I must have been pretty hungry. Out of everything being yelled around us, food caught my attention. This Asian kid was sitting at a table, in the center of a stage. To his left, the biggest pot of rice I'd seen in my life. To his right, a bunch of random food people gave him. Was this some sort of social experiment? This kid was asking his fellow citizen for disgusting food ideas to eat over rice and rating it on a scale of 1 to 10. It was so silly but oddly entertaining. I found myself watching him for over thirty minutes while he tested Nutella, Jelly beans and Spaghetti on top of rice. "C'mon buddy, there's plenty more stuff I want to show you today" Dan said while dragging me away from this hypnotizing spectacle. We resumed our walk, while he continued to sing the praise of New Reddit. It was just a few blocks later that we both stopped again but... not because of a stage act this time. "Ross, we got another one." It was still dark outside, but the rain outside had prevented me from falling asleep. As unhappy as I was over this, I walked to the dresser to get my uniform ready. "Is that so? Let me guess, another arms runner?" Centerfield had been a hive of black market activity for years. Despite all of the attention drawn to this issue, the situation has largely remained the same as it had been several years before. "No, it doesn't look like it..... If anything, it might be a serial kidnapper. Some of our steely-eyed rocket men got a few calls that reported that said perpetrator has been at this at least four times as of now." "Excuse me? This criminal hoisted four people without anyone paying attention to this?" Grumbling, I finished getting my outfit on. It was far less apparent than a standard issue cop uniform- only a grey sweater with a blue, logo-bearing t-shirt. "I thought we were better than this, Cal!" The lady on the other side of the line muttered unhappiness. "I know. Wait, someone's paging me..." "Yeah? What are they saying?" "Damn it. We got an empowered criminal on our hands. Looks like the forensic laboratories has reported that at least a quarter of our database might be it's alter egos "Hold on. Alter egos? C'mon, Calpurnia, we aren't dealing with the Joker. And how on earth is such a large portion of our suspects assumed to be the same person?" "No-one can tell if the criminal is a he or a she. Looks like a shapeshifter." I paused. "Oh sweet mercy." I quickly grabbed a shotgun from the bedside table, and walked outside into the storm. "Any clues on where the criminal might be located?" "No, I don't. Stand by for details The phone clicked. The call had suddenly ended. Sorry, Ross, we had a power outage over here. Now, as I was saying The voice was different. Cal wasn't there, only someone else had taken her place. This case just became even more interesting, if such a thing is even possible.

A rogue, clad in a simple white tunic, and wielding a short, sharp dagger, begins his decent into the dark, dreary, (and a little bit damp) dungeon. This isn't just any old castle dungeon though. This one is filled with strange and powerful magical artifacts. Many adventurers have delved deep, and returned bearing priceless rings and mounds of gold. But just as many people have never returned, lost in the darkness below. Though many people have attempted to map the dungeon, it never seems to stay the same. And there is a legend, of an incredibly powerful amulet, that can grant any wish, hidden in the darkest, deepest part, guarded by monsters an beings of mysterious might. Many have sought after this amulet, but none have ever obtained it and returned. This amulet is the goal of the rogue's quest. (Along with any other magical items he might happen to gather along the way.) While this might be attributed to a certain kind of selfishness (for he is a little greedy), the main reason he wants the artifact is a burning sense of curiosity. What could have created such a medallion? Does it really grant wishes? Even things like what it might look like are incredibly intriguing to him. And while curiosity might have killed the cat, it said nothing about a clever human. Underqualified though he might seem, he has an extra trick tucked up his sleeve. Or rather, pulled around his shoulders. Covering him from the shoulders down, practically trailing along the floor, is a thin black cloak, dark as the shadows around him, and almost as wavering. The hood is down, but pulling it up will activate the magic woven into the threads, turning both it and the wearer completely invisible. He stole this, long ago, from the kings treasury, and no one ever even noticed. And so he begins his quest. The first levels are the sewers of the city above, only moderately dangerous, but filled with rats and crabs and strange, bipedal creatures with an unnerving laugh. Clever tricks and the point of his dagger easily pull him through, and he even finds a nice set of chain mail to wear, for better protection for the occasion times he does get hit. But as soon as he slides the chain mail on, the dungeon starts to get interesting. The tiny chains clench together, tightening around the rogue, and at first he is sure the armor is trying to suffocate him. But even though it makes it a bit harder to breathe, it stops after a moment, and simply hangs tight to him, refusing to be budged. The armor is obviously cursed. And he soon finds out the penalty for trying out a strange piece of equipment. It's heavy, and slows him just enough that he can't dodge away from slashes and scratches as well. Not only that, but after the third pounding he takes, a strange magic activates in the links of metal. A massive crab gets a powerful blow in, and the armor reacts by emitting a terrifying hissing noise. Clouds of thick, green smoke billowing from between the links, getting in his nose and eyes, clouding his vision and making it that much harder to breathe. He struggles away from the crab, who seems to be affected by the gas too, from the way it weaves drunkenly across the floor, and runs from the cloud. When he is finally clear, he takes a deep breath, and the musty air of the dungeon cleared away the gas in his lungs. The first question he has is, funnily enough, not how do I get rid of this, but rather Who would make cursed armor, and then just leave it lying around? But, he keeps moving forward. Now he has more questions, about the dungeon itself as well as about the amulet he seeks. Deeper, deeper, deeper. Past the grungiest, muckiest, dirtiest part of the sewer, fighting a massive blob of congealed slime and dark magic, through an abandoned prison, battling past the crazed inmates and disillusioned guards, nearly freeing some sort of ninja assassin prisoner, but managing to stop him before he escapes. Past that are tunnels and caves, filled with more of the bipedal hyena creatures, but smarter and stronger, avoiding vicious bats and enormous green spiders. He nearly gets crushed by a massive, malfunctioning mining machine, but finding a way to dismantle it as well. The remains of previous would-be heroes warns him of more danger to come. After that is an ancient, crumbling city, build by dwarves and now inhabited by their creations and twisted versions of their original glory. Reining over the remnants is an old, insane and power-hungry king, who rules with an iron fist and undead minions. But, with some tricks and turns, the rogue overturns the tyrants rule, and then, without a second glance, continued, deeper. All along this way, he has found countless objects and items. Potions, helpful and dangerous, scrolls, magical in their very nature, made to remove curses and summon monsters, rings that, when worn, made him faster or stronger or smarter or harder to see. He even found more armor, and abandoned his dagger for a dual pair of electric swords, after stealing it from a living statue. The scariest moment up until then had been equipping a set of heavy metal armor that he then couldn't take off. As soon as he was hit, a flash of light drew all the energy and motion away from his attacker, and at first he was overjoyed when he saw them frost over. But the energy taken quickly built up, growing hotter and hotter, until he burst into a raging fire. But even being literally on fire would be nothing compared to the levels that would come ahead. Demons roamed the deepest dungeons, fire and lava and mysterious magic. And then, after fighting furiously, he encounters the guardian of the amulet. The last few pieces of an ancient demon, he has to contend with two gigantic fists and an eyeball filled with grubs. Finally, he obtains the amulet. He can go no deeper. But still he questions. Why was the dungeon so full of items, both helpful and hurtful? Countless adventurers had already come and gone with their loot, so why was there anything left? Where did the monsters come from, seemingly infinite? And, holding the amulet, he knew he could find out. Flipping the hood up on his cloak, and watching himself disappear from view, he clutched the amulet close and made a wish. In an instant, he was elsewhere. Surrounded by noise and chaos, it took the rogue a moment to adjust to the sudden change of surroundings. Glancing around, still invisible, he gaped in amazement He was in a workshop, shelves and tables covered with clutter. But the amazing thing was that all this clutter were magical items, swords, rings, cloaks. There was a whole shelf dedicated to intricate wands. Yet everything was thrown around and scattered like scraps or trash. Things were moving and working automatically, testing and changing, balls of fire and arcs of electricity flying every which way. A strange, shuffling movement caught his eye, and he turned to see a middle-aged man rummaging through one of the shelves, looking for something in particular. Curious, the rogue took a small step forward, and the man froze. The whole room ground to a halt, mechanics stopping and objects dropping to the floor. Without turning around, the man straightened up. "Well now, look what we have here! A visitor, and he didn't even bother to introduce himself!" Turning around, the man stared at the rogue with bright blue eyes, his gaze piercing right through the cloaks invisibility. "I haven't had a visitor in a long, looong time." He chuckled. "I didn't even know it was possible!" The man shuffled closer, and grabbed at the hem of the shadowy cloak. It instantly became visible again under his hands, and he inspected it carefully. "This must be the reason why. I stopped making these Cloaks years ago, but a decent number did get taken from my dungeon before then. It bypassed my wards entirely!" At a loss for words, the rogue stared at the man. Finally finishing his voice, he stammered out a reply. "Y-y-your dungeon, sir?" For some reason, this man scared him more than the ancient demon guardian had. "Oh, where are my manners." The old man tutted, and dropped the edge of the cloak. "My name is Watabu." He held out a hand, and the rogue hesitantly shook it. "Yes, my dungeon. I created it specifically for adventures, much like you!" Shuffling away, the man resumed searching the shelf. "I find it so much fun to watch people grow and attack challenges. Plus, maintaining it is fun, and keeps me busy." A little bewildered, the rogue glanced around. "You mean, you made all these? You're the one responsible for the monsters and magics all through the dungeon?" The man pulled out a sack and dropped a couple items in it. "Well of course, I'd have thought that'd be obvious. I add the magics, I feed the monsters, I shuffle the floors and traps so it's never the same twice!" Finally giving up on searching the shelf, he swept the whole thing into the bag, then slung it over his shoulder. "But, but, people die in your dungeon all the time? They never return! You find that fun?" The rouge was a bit panicked now. "Well of course people die. It's a dangerous dungeon!" Watabu opened a cabinet, which was lined with amulets, identical to the one the rogue held now. "But that doesn't mean they can't try again." He opened a door, in the middle of thin air. "Now, if you'll excuse me, I must bring a demon god back to life for the next adventurer." " Why? " the rogue's voice got louder. "What do you mean, try again?" Watabu looked at him one last time, hand resting on a nonexistent doorknob. "Dying isn't the last adventure, not in this game." He chuckled. "For all you know, you might have tried a hundred times already!" And with that, he stepped into nothingness and disappeared If anyone here plays pixel dungeon, you should understand where this is from:) That was actually really fun to write, though it took a while!

The pilgrims flocked to the massive temple in the center of the city, their dirty rags and bare feet failing to mask the fire in their eyes and the excitement in their voices. The temple, shaped like a great arrow pointing to the heavens, had two doorways flanked by ancient idols, their orange eyes twinkling with benevolence as they smiled down upon the bustling crowds. Inside the temple, the resident priest (or Eyeama in their tongue) preached thunderously from the sacred tomes. Upon each booming recitation, the swaying choir behind him chanted "Read it! Read it!" to proclaim their intimacy with the text. In the rear of the temple, the faithful hastily removed their ceremonial fedoras to kneel at the altars of various saints-Daw Kens and Dee Graas Tiesin among them. In the quiet corners smaller groups of pilgrims could be seen with their eyes tightly shut, clutching their icons and muttering prayers from a time long forgotten- "OP shall deliver us from evil, may he look down upon us yet lift us up upon his index finger; may he bless us with karma and may he reply with proper formatting. TLDR." And in the far room a lone pilgrim could be spotted who, unable to comprehend the instructions for worship provided to him, had somehow ended up with his genitals caught in a strange windmill on the ceiling.

Where did you go that night, when you became invisible, soundless, and disappeared? Are you huddled, cold and shivering in the pile of socks that went missing one by one, with the keys to our old apartment, with our cat, Sprinkles, who may still be alive? (She probably isn't). It should have felt like a light going out Instant shock of blackness, but it didn't. It came on like the night, slowly. So slowly I scarcely noticed it was getting dark, And when you became the dusk, shoes dragging across the ground, I didn't question it, Didn't try to make you bright as day again. When you became the twilight, I didn't wonder. I didn't try to help at all, as the stars shone through the blackness, you hung your head so low, and not noticing not caring I let you become the night. Afterwards, I lived but not in a way anyone would want to live if they had the choice.

Once upon a time, in some out of the way corner of the Hundred Acre Wood which is dispersed into numberless clustering trees and pathways, there was a bear upon which little brains invented'bother.' That was the most arrogant and mendacious minute of "bothering," but nevertheless it was only a minute. After a fear of heffalumps had drawn a few gasps, the forest's fervor cooled and congealed, and the beastly apparitions had to die. - One silly little bear might invent such a fable, and yet one would still not have adequately illustrated how foolish, how honey-driven and temporary, the fear of an unknown looks within nature. There were hillside adventures and stick races during which it did not exist. And when it is all over with the end of playing in the Wood, nothing will have happened. For this unbridled fear of figures has no additional mission, which would lead it beyond the edge of the forest. Rather, it is a figment created by you and I, and its honey and bear takes it so solemnly - as though the trees and land's axis turned within it. For this "bother" contains within itself the most flattering estimation of the value of caring; a concern for friends is the most general effect of such "bother," but even in its most particular effects contain within themselves something of the same altruistic characters.

Thirteen point eight two billion years. Thirteen point eight two billion years and somehow, out of all the stars in the sky, all the worlds in existence sprinkled here and there, ours was the single solitary speck to develop life? It seemed improbable, impossible even. Mike Stahl turned away from the porthole. It was too much. It was just too much goddamn space. Back home in North Carolina, the population had hit eighty million, bodies packed in so tight you might as well be leftovers in a vacsac. It was an apt comparison, he thought, there was really no room to breathe down there, nowhere to go to escape the constant adwaves that permeated the outdoors, screaming their sales pitches straight into your skull. But out here it was entirely the opposite problem; untold millions of light years of nothing but vast emptiness. Space as far as the eye can see, and yet nobody's home. It was a puzzle that had stumped scientists for generations. The Fermi Paradox, they called it, after one of the scientists had posed a question to his colleagues at lunch: If space is so big, and so old, why don't we see anyone else there? There had been guesses, sure, anything from outright fiction to serious attempts at some sort of theory to explain just why the universe was so lifeless. But that's all they were, really: guesses. He ran a hand through his hair, still thick and dark, though age was finally starting to creep in as specks of grey flecked the stubble on his face. There was no hair dye in space, not where the chemicals could easily contaminate some of the delicate experiments kept aboard. Mike grinned to think what his wife would say. She couldn't bear it, he thought. Hell, she never wanted me to go to begin with. A chime brought Mike from his reverie and back to the small terminal attached to the desk. It really wasn't necessary, not with his neural jack, but Mike felt more comfortable with the screen. What could he say? He was a'30s kid at heart. The jacks had been around for nearly two decades, but growing up with the screen had been too powerful an influence to overcome, at least when he had the choice. He tapped twice and proceeded to navigate slowly down the data stream, the screen advancing in time with his eye movements. Hey, the jack wasn't all bad. The experiments aboard the station ranged from the mundane to the extravagant. Ant farms, greenhouses, a miniature particle accelerator, and the project Mike was assigned to: a dark matter sieve. A scant decade ago they had discovered how to interact with this strange matter that seemed to make up most of the mass in the known universe, and had found that, not unlike oil deposits back on Earth, it made a wonderful fuel source, without the drawback of smog like that which blanketed New Beijing. Unfortunately, though they'd discovered how to tap the energy potential of the dark matter, no one had yet been able to explain just what it was made of. This experiment hoped to change that. Mike read the results, slowly at first, and then faster, skipping lines and skimming as quickly as he was able. This was astonishing. No, it was insane. He had done it, alright, but it was not what he had hoped, and now a dark feeling crept up his spine. Somebody was home, the universe was not quite so empty as they had thought - or at least, it hadn't been. Somebody had been home, but now they were dust, broken into strange matter scattered throughout the stars. An interesting coincidence, Mike thought, that mankind should launch an Industrial Revolution fueled by the liquid corpses of the dinosaurs, and a short five hundred years later begin his journey through the cosmos on the sludge that was once a galactic civilization.

He surveyed the field, keeping his eyes fixed on the players. His players. He was so proud of them. Jenkins, number 7, was a very focused, driven player and always intent on following the plan even if he didn't agree with it. Li, number 12, was the fastest base runner he'd ever worked with and could keep a clear head when it came to remembering where all the bases were and which ones he had to double-back to. Coach Watterson snapped back to reality. Glancing behind him at the audience, he noticed a shouting sea of red. His team, the tigers, were winning. Hastily, he scanned the field for whatever they were cheering for. Then, he spotted it: Jason Rodriguez from the New Mexico ET's had forgotten to touch the secret base. Saul Vasquez, the Tigers' best pitcher, lobbed the ball at Rodriguez hard. Rodriguez collapsed and tumbled to the ground, where he stayed until the medics arrived with a stretcher. The crowd went wild again as the Ref shouted "You're out, Rodriguez!" Watterson noticed that he was clutching his cap so tightly in his hands that he was practically tying it in knots. He was sweating like a pig. As he sat down to take a drink from his water bottle, he realized how sick and twisted Calvinball really was. It made no sense. A secret base? And how many are there anyway? Thirty? Fifty? He hadn't even seen anyone win at Calvinball. He's just an elementary school PE coach with a lot of luck and a degree in sports medicine. He wasn't cut out to coach a real sports team, but then again..... was anybody? As he watched two players get into a fist fight over whose turn to bat it was, he put his nearly sunburned arm over the shoulders of Jimmy Vasquez, the assistant coach, and let out a deep, heavy sigh "I can't believe this moronic sport is our new international pastime."

"But I didn't believe in God," I said. "That part doesn't matter as much as most people think," the man across from me said. The floors, walls, and the desk between us all radiated the same white, serene light. The same light colored his chair, his suit, and most of the room to the point where everything looked as if it were part of a single, flat image in front of me. "What about all the things that I've done?" "Most were inconsequential. You saw how your heart and the feather balanced with each other." "Inconsequential?" I asked. I thought of all the things that I'd done. All those horrible things. "There's no way." "There are no mistakes here," the man said as he produced an empty folder with my name printed in the top left corner. "It can't be right. I've hurt people. I've killed other men." I began sobbing. "I raped a girl once." The man across the desk pulled a sheet of paper from his empty folder. "According to this, Amie actually started that sexual exploit. Then, she fell asleep during. Her friend Ashley walked in on the two of you. As Amie was dating Michael at the time, she told Ashley that you raped her. Pretty clear to us up here that it was in fact consensual." "But, she fell asleep," I said, "and I didn't stop." "And look how horrible it makes you feel. Look how much you suffered your whole life for it. That suffering is important to us." "What about all the fights? The drugs? The sex?" The man across the desk pulled countless pages from the empty folder. "June 27, 1978, you became friends with numerous people that were much older than you, most by at least four years. By July of that year, all of you had started smoking. "January 13, 1979, you first started smoking marijuana and drinking at the urging of your cousin David. That same night, you had sex with a girl six years older than you, but she thought you were only a year younger. "March 28, 1979, you had sex with your cousin, Felicia. "May 11, 1979, you knocked out Justin Prather with a beer bottle, giving him a concussion. You proceeded to break the bottle to use the glass to carve your initials into his back. "May 27, 1979, you had sex with Amie Balock the first of numerous times despite neither of you even being in high school yet. "August 17, 1979, you stabbed Jacob MacLellan in the stomach eight times. "January 22, 1980, you got into a fight with Jonathan Simms over Brittany South. You torqued his arm behind him until it dislocated. You described the sound to the police as'a wet shotgun'. No charges were pressed, but you cried for weeks, and begged a God you didn't believe in to forgive you for the things you did. "That was a real turning point," the man across the desk continued. "You stopped doing those things, cold turkey. No more drugs. No more drinking. No more fights. Went on to finish high school. You married that girl from school, Arlene. You joined the military. When you got out you became a cop." "I tried to kill myself," I said. "I thought about it almost every day. I shot people as a cop. Some were defense, but two were just an accident. I thought they had guns. They were just boys. Every night I thought about killing myself. Arlene left me, and that just made it worse." "But you didn't," said the man across the desk. "You came through that. You realized that your life was more precious than a quick solution to your suffering. Why, you dedicated your life to helping other people. Built houses. Fed the poor. Alexander, you tried to help people." "I wasn't motivated by your God," I said. "I grew up reading comic books. Superman motivated me. I'd done so many terrible things, but I knew I could be better. I could help make sure other people didn't choose to be as awful as me." "I told you, believing isn't that important," said the man across the desk. "The intention is important. The suffering you endured and strove on through is important. The change is important. You started life as a bad, bad boy, but you went on to be a good man. You wanted to help other people, not because it would get you into Heaven. You wanted to help them solely for the sake of helping them. That's what counts, Alexander." "I just don't think any of it makes up for all that I've done," I said. "Maybe you could just send me to Hell anyway. Damn your scales. It's where I really belong." The man across the desk flashed me a strange, glassy smile. "I got ta tell you, Alex," he said, "your continued desire to suffer and be punished for the wrongs you done is actually making it more likely that you'll stay up here with us."

Ever since the last keeper disappeared without a trace, I had set up camp here, guarding this rickety old bridge. I have no idea why, but here I am, countless years into the job, and I find myself staring intently at my first visitor. Very intently. I burned my eyesight through her very eyes. Those green, emerald eyes, shining like jewels in this desolate place. She stared back, and she was a talented starer. Not even a blink for three whole minutes. Yet her eyes were still glistening. I think mine are already starting to shrivel. It hurts, it hurts so bad. But I feel like if I move my gaze, we'll break status quo, and what comes afterwards will be irrevocable. Four minutes now. I had learned to count time during my stay here. I instinctively know the passing of every minute. But I think I see her eyelids shaking. Please don't shake. Please don't let us stop this moment we share. But it was not meant to last. She blinked. Our staring contest was over. She smiled at me. She complimented me. "You're good!" She said, laughing. "So, why are you here?" "I'm the keeper of the bridge." I answered. "I manage this bridge. I do things to keep people who shouldn't cross from crossing and I might let people who are supposed to cross, cross this bridge, should they desire to cross and have the credentials to cross, in which case they are free to go over this bridge at their own risk." I kept thinking of ways to repeat what I'm saying in more ways to stall for time. "So, in other words, if you are here to cross, I may or may not let you cross depending on if you are going to be able to prove that you can cross this bridge, and if you can not, I can not let you pass, but if you can, I can let you pass." I'm getting a bit tired now, need a breath, but this breath is all it took for her to continue to conversation. "How diligent! Even though I bet visitors like me are quite rare." I had to think of something. Anything to delay the official procedures for crossing the bridge. I settled on the most basic of ways, and in a rigid, cracking voice, I asked, "What is your name?" "I'm Emirel Pendragon, my parents named me for my eyes." She smiled, and I could see an aura of satisfaction, as if she had accomplished something. Was giving out names that much of a deal? I must have been away from society for far too long, because I told her my name very awkwardly, without the same radiance. She was about to open her mouth, but I don't want her to take initiative. She might cross the bridge and I'm not sure if I want that. "What is your purpose here?" I asked, and immediately I realized my word choice was a bit off. Did my training manual state I should ask something similar? I honestly can't remember. "To search for my destiny." She spoke with such confidence those cheesy words, but that same aura of satisfaction, it is as if she is elated with every answer, as if she delighted in clearing the clouds in my mind. Had she perhaps been an angel? Or more likely, my imagination manifesting from my loneliness on this bridge? She was beautiful, and she was every bit as perfect a woman as I have in my mind. "I wonder what I am supposed to do next to keep her from crossing..." Now, knowing she might be just a figment of my imagination, that I might really be all alone, talking to myself, I began speaking my thoughts out loud. It would certainly be embarrassing to say that in front of a real girl. "Aren't you the bridge keeper? You have a third question to ask me, don't you?" "I, uh, I actually don't know." I answered. And my head became clear, as I was tossed into the sky by an invisible force, into the pit below the bridge. I was supposed to be guarding the Bridge of Death from those who seek the holy grail.

The guns went silent, completely silent. The wind together with the sound of people screaming in pain while trying to collect their scattered guts or press the severed arm back onto the body was the only hearable thing. A voice could suddenly be heard from the other side of the trench "Testing, testing, one two, one two." Realising what was happening people in the trench fumbled with their equipment to produce their earplugs, many had lost theirs in the battle and simply pressed their hands against their ears. You could hear someone clearing his throat, now much louder than before. "So, my dad used to work as a road worker, he was often accused of stealing from the job. Naturally I didn't believe it, until I got home and saw that all the signs was there!" It was not a particularly good joke, but one man laughed. It was the last thing he ever did, as soon as he started laughing he also started to shake. Blood swarming out from his mouth and his eyes growing like marshmallows in a microwave. In a last scream filled with laughter his eyes popped and he fell to the ground, dead. "My wife used to fake orgasms, not a big deal I say, I faked the whole relationship!" This time several people across the trench laughed. Those still alive had taken to shoving mud into their ears while firmly holding it in place with their hands. The voice once again cleared its throat, it seemed as if it was preparing for some higher-tier jokes. "When I was a kid I asked God for a bike, the preacher told me God doesn't work like that, so naturally I stole a bike and asked God for forgiveness." The joke was the last straw for many, they simply couldn't hold back their laughter. All across the trench people fell down to the ground, their eyes popped and their mouths filled with warm blood. Suddenly the sounds of airplanes could be heard in the distance, the voice went silent and panicked voices could be heard from the other side of the trench. It was the German airborne, no amount of jokes could get them to crack, they simply could not understand the jokes. As the airborne parachuted towards the other trench you could hear the voice panicking, it started shouting off jokes as fast as it could. The jokes were unfocused and sloppy, not even the normal soldiers in the trench cracked. Shortly after the airborne landed in the other trench and the voice went silent. Victory had been achieved, however it was but one of many battles to come.

On a distant world of sand and dunes, there comes a ship of steel and chrome. Out of the ship comes a man in practical clothing, which is to say a pressurized suit. He heads off into the endless desert. His pilgrimage is not long. He comes to an obelisk of a radio tower, rising high against the ruddy horizon. Around it lie hundreds of dead figures. Poison has dried on their mouths. They once would have stood tall. Their colonies were once of many systems, and they would have flourished on this world. They also had attempted to colonize parts of the human solar system. They watched us, maybe for years, maybe for millenia. On the tower, next to a dead figure, there lies a set of words in an alien tongue scratched into the metal by clawed hands. The tower sent a signal with the same message. The man looks closely at the inscription, examining it for a while. His eyes widen with guilt as he learns their meaning. "The human race is coming. Die here, be enslaved, or be exterminated."

I was teaching when my phone made that annoying Whatsapp beepity-beep sound. Thought it was probably just an ad or some shit. Nope, the girlfriend saying "I have something I need to tell you." My knee-jerk jokey reaction was, "Are you pregnant?" Silence. I assumed she had probably just wandered off to take a shower or something. So I returned to my student. I can't be sure if my memory is accurate about this, but in my mind, my student and I were analysing My Papa's Waltz by Theodore Roethke. But now there was a baby growing in the back of my mind, wrapping its little fingers around my concentration and pulling it apart like playdough. Ack, why didn't I use a condom that time? I used to ask myself these kinds of questions almost every other month: no period yet, should I worry? Nah, it'll be fine. I always pull out. I didn't that particular month though. She said her period was almost on. Two weeks later, nothing. I'm not blaming anyone. We were both fairly irresponsible about taking the correct preventative measures. She never wanted to go on the pill and I can't say I blame her. Wouldn't want to take it if I were female, so. Still, condoms. Fucking condoms. Period. Fucking with condoms and then period, ideally. I got home and she was sitting on the bed. By this point I had already rationalised away all possibility of pregnancy. It takes me twenty minutes to walk home, plenty of time to explain her silence away into insignificance. She was just sitting on the bed. Not reading, or using her laptop, or on her phone playing with'beebook', or whatever the hell that site is called. Just sitting. Quite normal. Nothing unusual about that. Nope. That's fine. Everyone sits. There was something in her hand. She showed it to me, and before my brain allowed me to understand what it was, my hands were clenched around the lower half of my face. I'm pretty sure I swore. Although I wish I hadn't now, but shock is a powerful thing. She started to cry. I was pumping with adrenaline. Part of me began to really panic and she notices. She starts to really cry and suddenly, out of some primordial part of my little brain, something said to me, "You've just got to accept this. You've just got to deal with it." So I exhaled. I relaxed my shoulders. I looked my girlfriend right in the eye and I said "We'll be okay, we can handle this." Her crushing credit card debt and the fact I am working six days a week earning a graduate wage doesn't really agree with what I told her, but all that's just money. It's not and never will be as real as that moment was. I felt unbelievably alive. The possibility of fatherhood does some seriously weird rewiring of your brain. Change in perspective and all that jazz. Life had presented me with a surprise, one that I could perhaps have avoided with a little more responsibility and less of a sex-drive, but hey. It's happened. Go with the flow, do what you got to do, and other, surprisingly useful, cliches of that nature. What I went through over the next few days was essentially a kind of grieving process. Actually, if I'm perfectly honest, I'm going through it right now. I've been oscillating between denial: "it's not certain yet, we're only a month in, we can't get our hopes up," anger: "fuck my boss for not giving me two days off per week..." Actually, no fucking seriously fuck that man. I asked to reduce my hours by literally an afternoon and he says "Okay, sure, but I'm taking the equivalent of two days per week pay." Fuck you, man. Seriously. Throw me a damned bone, my girlfriend is pregnant, you almighty arse! So I'm currently angry. But what am I grieving about? It's not anything real, not really. It's a projection of myself. It's what I had hoped to do in the future. I was literally seven months away from having enough savings to live without working for 6 months. I was going to write for six, solid months. It was going to be glorious. But, a kid. I can't not work..... My dreams seem to be sinking into a baby shaped hole. I have to accept the loss of identity, the loss of a future projection. Life is what it is. Having a baby doesn't mean I can't write. I just can't only write. I'll need to juggle my responsibilities for the baby alongside work and writing. Writing won't be the forefront of my life until I can break through. I'm still young. There are advantages of being a young dad. It's going to be fine. I'll manage. We'll manage. Even though my apartment is 300 square feet and my girlfriend's mother is expecting to come and live with us. It'll be fine, it will. At some point, I will have accepted this as true and won't have to keep repeating it. Until then: it will be fine, it will. - All of the above is 100, well maybe 99, true. It's darn weird to see that prompt a few weeks after I found out. I'm 25 even. How weird is that??

I hope this is ok, but it's actually a true story. The game setting is different, but the emotions and mild PTSD from it are real. This is the story of Leon. Haven. A wild forest filled with good things to eat. Hearth. Our first home on the river bank, little more than a fire and some drying racks. We decided to name it Two Rivers, after the winding waters around us that made the island we settled in. With hard industrious work, we managed to erect our first palisade. Some homes, and work was started on the mine. We were fresh in the world, and somehow managed to survive the occasional boar wandering in the woods. We quickly met our neighbours, each of our little settlements dotting the nearby lake like a small constellation. Donkey Punch to the north, Viridian City to the south east. We quickly banded together to form a defensive pact. Viridian were a peaceful set, but had access to a very good quality iron vein. Donkey Punch were ruled by an eccentric man, but he claimed to know his way around a sword. Industriously we built, peace to be had for a time. Then the Teletubbies struck. It was a vicious and brutal campaign. Twenty men armed with cheap but effective bronze, they ravaged their neighbours. Answering a call, Zach and Leon boated to the defense of Viridian against griefers. Zach did not leave those beaches. It was a trap. They had been waiting in the forest, at least ten strong. When we hit sand, Leon saw movement. He screamed at Zach to get into the boats, but it was too late. Desperately trying to get him on board, he was slowly dragged and beaten to his death on those shores. In this world, death is permanent. Zach would never walk the forests again, and his owner never made another to rise in the world of Haven. Leon though, had issues from his attempted rescue. One of the Teletubbies had boarded his boat and for the next three quarters of an hour an intense boat chase took place on the lake. It started with five against him, slowly he whittled down their persistence to three. And in a breaking moment, a split second, Leon managed to escape to hearth teleport home. Then, the heartbreaking news hit. Zach had the palisade keys on him. There was no way to change the lock, and the invaders would find our home soon. Quickly evacuating, as much of value was hauled out of our camp into a secondary enclosure we'd set up nearby. Leon stood at the gates and fought two more invaders to a standstill giving enough time to evacuate. The loss of the Two Rivers was enough that we didn't want to risk living there anymore. We lost another to a sling stone over the walls, he hadn't been careful about standing idly outside where snipers could see him. Two dead, never to return, two left, and two newcomers joining from a smaller camp to the south. We couldn't go on living like this in the cramped secondary encampement. But we didn't want to spend the resources to repair the original and almost as cramped Two Rivers encampment, so we moved in with our northern ally. And so four entered the town of Donkey Punch. Little did we know, more pain and bloodshed awaited us.
