We had always joked that the maths teacher, Mrs. Gresnich, was a dragon. Boy did she roar, and after shouting you down there was nothing but ashes left. Not to mention her purse, which glittered like fake gold and which she clutched close at all times. But, James, he didn't care. She'd screech at him, and all he'd do was pick his nose. Of course, he spent half the classes sitting outside, or outside the headmaster's office. That was the thing with teachers: you never won, even when you were right. Nothing to be gained, but the glory. Because, really, everyone knew James. He was a legend that would get passed on until the day Mrs. Gresnich kicked the bucket. That we stood there at the memorial, and people would come over to see him, well, that spoke to the truth of it. He didn't look particularly happy about it, but he shared a smile and a handshake with them. In a way, his arrival surprised me. I was stuck in the neighbourhood, taking over my old man's shop. He was half the world away, more or less, working over in London. Surprised us all that, somehow he'd gotten into a half-decent uni and continued on from there. Never expected the old James to do that, when he could barely add two and two to make five - he normally got seven. So, I'd nearly missed him when he turned up in a suit and tie, hair neatly combed and expression sombre. Clapped him on the shoulder, and he lit up when he saw me. Hugged me hard, not like back in the day. Made me realise how much time had passed, and how much it could do. Basically took a lump of a boy and chiselled him into a man. Not like me, sitting on my arse all day selling cuts of meat for a meagre living. He'd brought along one looker of a wife, too. Legs for days and all that, but she seemed sweet. The two of us fell in like old buddies, as she drank up the stories of our misspent youth. He didn't intervene at all, but looked decidedly uncomfortable with the memories, no doubt something he wanted to distance himself from. But, well, where we all stood, that was a reminder that our past wasn't there to be forgotten. In their own way, many people had shaped us into who we'd become. The time I'd spent with James taught me what it meant to be a hero. No one cared about men in tights saving the world, but a mate that would tell old Mrs. Gresnich to bugger off when she set her sights on some poor, snivelling lad? Yeah, I'd spent a lot of my misspent youth wanting to be like James. A recurring dream of mine had been to turn up at our old school, walk into that dusty maths room, and tell her what I bloody well thought of her. Of course, I'd never actually do it. James was a hero because he was a puny git with a voice that cracked every other sentence. A hulk of a man like me shouting at an old lady, well, I'd be lucky if I got off without the coppers being called. James probably didn't think of himself as a hero either, not at the time and not after all that time. I dunno if he was ever scared, probably was. Always grinning, always scared, always standing up. A kind of trinity of hero-ness. I asked his missus what he was up to these days, and she rubbed her belly and spoke of moving out to a small town, far from the smoggy streets of the capital. Laughed, and threw in my thought that our old town had its charms, and she laughed too. James didn't, but he hadn't laughed at all, over the afternoon. The merriment died out during the service, and we wandered around the three of us, saying our kind words to the family. Of course, James couldn't catch a break there either. " James, as in James Williams? " He nodded, awkwardly avoiding meeting the daughter's eyes. " She spoke fondly of you, " she said, smiling what looked like a natural one, and not the fake, mourning one exchanged with the other guests. " She did? " he asked, surprised. Chuckling, she softly shrugged. " Well, she spoke of you. At least, she kept complaining about you and your legacy. " " I see, " he said, bowing his head. " I'm sorry, I was a troublesome child for her. " " No, no, " she said. " It got her fired up. Even in her last days, she'd perk right up when it came to telling us all what an ungrateful child you were. So, I'm thankful for your trouble, we all are. " Say what you will about Mrs. Gresnich, but her daughter was wonderful. I hadn't thought James felt guilty about those years, but she'd cut that all away. I could see the difference in him, and the smile he had was like when he spotted me. " I'm thankful for her trouble too, " he said softly. She laughed back, and replied, " She'd be glad to hear that. " And, we all left it at that. Me, him and his missus took off to a nearby pub. I dunno if I was spoiling plans or anything, but he needed a friend. Not to talk to or anything, just to keep her from badgering him. So, I did my best to keep her attention, telling her many tales about that old dragon of a maths teacher we'd had, while tears swelled in his eyes, and did my best to cough over any sniffles he did. It took a good half hour before he started regaining his composure, and a moment's reprieve was granted when she excused herself. James, he'd really grown up since those days. Or, maybe he hadn't, and I'd just been too busy admiring him.'Cause, he'd always been a kind person, good-hearted I should say. So, having such a nice and caring wife, well, that wasn't a surprise. And, getting emotional over how he treated Mrs. Gresnich, even if she'd deserved it, that wasn't a surprise once I'd thought about it. He reached over, and patted the top of my hand, before leaning back in his seat and staring at the ceiling. " Thanks, " he said. I smiled, taking a sip of something far less alcoholic than normal. But, my company was a pregnant lass and her designated driver, so I could put aside my usual for the day. " No problem. " His head tilted to the side, towards the bathrooms, and then back to how it was. " You know, Mrs. Gresnich was the bitchiest bitch who ever bitched. " I laughed. " Yeah, she was. " " But, " he said, and his voice grew strained from just that word. " Whenever I asked her for help, she didn't tell me to bugger off, or ask me what the point of helping an idiot was, or say it was too late for me to start now. " Ah, yeah, most of our teachers were like that. Oh sure, if you were a sweet, young girl, they'd help you out. Boys were a waste of time, couldn't be bothered to listen the first time, teachers had better things to do with their time. Really, it was a surprise any of us lads had even made it to uni, though I guess some of them actually did pay attention in class, and did their homework, and studied at home. " She never complained, just helped me. When no one thought I was worth a minute of their time, she helped me get into university. " I doubt anyone had ever been brave enough to ask her for help before. Not even heroes asked dragons for help. Heroes were there to slay dragons, to fight against them to the death and claim the treasure. Maybe get the girl, who had been trapped in a tower for some unknown reason. " Really, it's thanks to her I'm happy today, " he said, softly. " Thanks to her, I met my wife, found my dream job. " " Yeah, you really pulled your act together, " I said. " Hardly recognise you. " He laughed, nodding his head. " I always wanted to come back, and say thank you to her. But, I kept thinking she wasn't going anywhere. For some reason, I never thought she'd die. " " Same here. " Looking off the side, his missus emerged, walking over with the barest signs of a bulging tummy. Only a few months in, so another half a year or so to go. And, that led to me thinking about what Mrs. Gresnich had been like as a kid. For some reason, I thought she must have been like James. A wild child, full of vigour and more questions than answers. The tomboy who shouted down the boys that bullied girls, and gave them a good kicking if they answered back. I dunno why I thought that, but it was something about how he was the only one who could confront her. Kindred spirits, from different times. So, if she was a dragon, then surely he was too. Watching him dote on his missus, while he'd been so lost minutes prior, warmed my grimy heart. A real good guy, and I guess Mrs. Gresnich had known, even if she'd been a real nasty woman, who picked on kids until they cried. She was definitely a dragon, through and through. Him? He had the soul of a dragon, but the will of a hero.

"You have a choice now. You can either turn left at the fork of destiny or enter hyper speed and explore space. Roll for your choice." Kent picked up the dice and rolled them between his fingers before letting them out on the table. "Uhhhh....11. Scores of 9 and above indicate that you enter hyper-speed. Your ship enters hyper-speed. Around you stars are zooming by at a pace that you could only begin to imagine in your wildest dreams. You begin to hear colors and taste music. You and your shipmates are glued to your seats, the speed almost too much for your internal organs to handle despite your ship's preparedness for Ef-Tee-El travel mdash;" "Did you really just say Ef-Tee-El Trave mdash;" " mdash; THE SHIP is slowing down, and now you are in a galaxy you don't recognize. Ahead of you there is another ship that seems to be governed by an alien race. Do you a) approach the ship or b) send out a radio signal?" Kent stopped for a moment to consider before turning to Tyler. "Approach the ship." "You approach the ship. As your ship grows closer your radio blares and an electronic voice tells you not to come any closer. Your ship pauses. Catalina, your first in command, tells you to slow down. You grip the controls but before you can slow your ship to a pause the alien ship has sent out a missile. It damages your ship. Roll for damage." There was a pause as Kent rolled. "Four! Number under 7 means that your damage is quite high. The missile damages your ship's shields beyond repair, and warning signs are going off. Luke is radioing in from the engine room telling you that there's trouble abound, and the other ship looks like it's preparing to send a second missile. As it prepares you turn your ship. If you roll a 8 or above you land safely on a planet that you can see in the distance....ten, cool. Okay, your ship flies toward the planet. Another missile is sent and misses by a hair's breadth. Catalina is shouting at you to drive faster, but there's an alarm going off on the ship that indicates something is wrong. As you enter the atmosphere of this new planet you find that below you stretches only desert. Off in the distance you can begin to see some grass. Roll mdash; shit, three indicates that your ship has suffered too much damage and has to land in the desert. Stranded you, Luke and Catalina gather up supplies of water and food and exit the ship, beginning toward the horizon where you swear you saw the grass. In the distance there's a rumbling noise. You can a) examine it, b) keep walking, or c) turn back and go to the ship." "Examine it." "You walk toward the source of the noise, and notice a dot on the horizon. You give chase, running as your pack bounces against your back. It's heavy and the weeks of space travel have made your muscles weak and your lungs poor. You're breathless quickly, and as you reach the top of a hill you realize that you've lost your shipmates. You turn trying to find them but there is nothing but desert beneath you. Roll - seven, okay, below you the sand begins to give way. Do you a) struggle or b) stay calm?" "Stay calm." "You stay calm despite the quicksand burying you up to your waist, and then you see a figure on the horizon. You cry out to them, shrieking for help from one of your shipmates. As you grow closer, you realize that it's someone else. Something else, except these aliens look exactly like humans. As it comes closer, it speaks to you in English, which happens to be its native tongue mdash;" "Dude what the fuck?" Tyler stopped speaking, his hands coming down to the table. "What?" "You make up this entire cool story and you can't do better than making the first aliens humans?" "Well I didn't expect you to pick the choices you did. I was like, expecting you to fight, and then you'd have to find your way through space and hitch a ride with someone and I'd have like another day to think something up. I don't know, man. It's hard to come up with aliens that aren't little green people and that can communicate with you." "Come on. What about using something like a babelfish? Or like a translator? Or something?" "There weren't any cities. These beings are nomads. They just wander their world." "Are they seriously humans?" Tyler paused for a moment. "No..." "Tyler...." "Fine. Yeah, they were gon na be humans. I thought it would be kind of cool." Kent rolled his eyes. "You're the worst DM, you know?" "Whatever. Let's play WoW or something." - Thanks for reading! For other stories subscribe to rCelsius232

"Well he always was a bit dense." Said Kathy. "A bit dense! HA! A 70 year old man somehow still in the prime of his youth and just now he wonders about it? A bit dense..... that's a very kind way to put it. Somebody with a brain should have his fortune, there would be no limit to the good they could do. Why do the half-wits always win the lottery?" Sue replied, shaking her head. "You know I can hear you, right?" I called from the other room, annoyed at my decrepit and aging younger siblings. "Yes of course you can hear me. You don't have hearing aids you dim-witted meathead." Sue was always my favorite sister. Perhaps she can be forgiven, it must be difficult to feel the pains of age and watch your brother still bounce around with a spring in his step and not a care in the world. But she was wrong about one thing. I intend to do good in this world. Just now I'm packing my bags to get on a plane that will take me to Baltimore where I'll be paying a visit to John Hopkins Medical School. The fabled Fountain of Youth is coursing through my veins and the researchers there are..... well to say they are interested is to put it mildly. Maybe we can live forever.

This note will be found or not, and I don't know what's worse. Before it happened, I had a name. A quite good name that decorated official documents, that felt at home on office desks, that traveled about on business cards. It even made it onto a few plaques and awards, while maintaining its respectability. When it happened on that Wednesday night, I still remembered all the names. My wife. My son. My two daughters. How long did I shout for them inside the house and then out. When I failed, I tried so many things. Such stupid things that, looking back, I probably learned from countless forgotten movies. I tried the police and fire stations, the town hall, and the downtown shops. When I arrived finally at the local Walmart, no frail voice greeted me. The snacks still sat, the televisions still ran beneath the fluorescent lights. Each aisle remained a paradise that no storm had disturbed. And all remained silent. But search I did, up and down, left and right, until I saw it in the sporting goods. A shadow. I ran and called for it. But, the shape of darkness slipped away. I didn't see another human shade for a long long time. Until today, on the mountainside. I can see it now from the bush. It moves so carefree from one small room to the next, sometimes pausing for hours at a time. I watch carefully this shade and its smoke that curls up above the tallest tree and disappears. For now, I wait.

Sky sat at their desk, tapping their fingers on the hard wood. They stared out the window, lacking inspiration and happiness. "On days like today, there are only two things that will pick me up." They say to themselves, and sluggishly stand from their desk chair. They walked to the cabinets, and peeked inside of one. "Dammit! How the hell are we out of donuts?" They whispered to themselves. "Chandler, did you eat my damn donuts again!?" Sky yelled to their boyfriend, who had his setup down the hall. "Sorry baby! I can buy you more later! I'm in the middle of something right now though!" He called. "Ugh. Fine." Sky huffed, and walked over to the refrigerator. They cursed under their breath and glanced down the hall. "Goddammit Chandler! You drank my fucking chocolate milk too! What the hell am I going to do with you?" "Shut up Sky, you love me! I'm really in the middle of something here cupcake! Love you to bits!" He yelled. "Whatever asshole. I'll go get my own damn donuts." They grumbled, and grabbed the key off the counter. "I love you" Chandler yelled. "I love you too. You bastard." They laughed and walked out. Sky looked around the storage room. Not a single box of donuts to be found. And no chocolate milk in the refrigerator. "Damn, I thought place got restocked every night." They mumbled. They walked out of the storage room and glanced through the hallways. This institution isn't the biggest, or the most state-of-the-art, but it's home to its fifteen residents. Sky could hear someone splashing down at the pool room. Probably Lyra, she probably snatched the donuts too, Sky would have to talk with her about that. They could smell Ashley cooking in the kitchen, and hear Matthew and Rebecca flirting with each other. They walked to the library, hoping to find someone to talk to there. Of course, Dean was on his laptop, probably playing some video game, AJ and Keith were reading in the corner, and Samantha was writing her short stories at her quaint little desk in the center of the room. Joseph and Mary were probably on the second floor of the institution, trying on outfits or rehearsing songs or whatever ever they did when they weren't making out. Then finally the pounding coming from the gymnasium told them that Sam, Skylar, and Martin were playing basketball. Life wasn't exactly easy in the institution, no contact with the outside world, and no way to truly trust others. We were all random people, ages 20 through 25, who were stuck together in this place. We can only truly rely on ourselves to get out, and we all want to get out, but until then we bide our time and occupy ourselves. The only known way out is truly terrible though, so I hope no one plans to leave for a while. After all, none of us could ever really murder someone else here and get away with it.

He was small orc compared to his peers and had grown plump in his curation of the grand library. The dwarf bursted into the room gasping for breath but with an obvious excitement that couldn't slow him down. " Orc! " he exclaimed as he sprinted past the endless rows of books, tomes, and scrolls of the library. The orc looked up through his spectacles with an audible sigh and feigned excitement for his dward friend. As he approached the table he heavily dropped what appeared to be an ancient text and with the loud thud of the tome the orc's eyes bulged wide with excitement that rivaled the dwarf's. The orc opened the tome to discover a form of ancient elvish, being the grand curator he was well versed in all manners of the elvish language but he had never seen writing like this. An elvish writing void of any of the dwarf runes, harsh annunciations of orc influence, and the simplicity of the human tongue but it was still legible to him. The scroll described an ancient conflict between two side; the dark elves, orcs, and goblins fighting against humans, dwarves, and elves. It described the war as a constant struggle between light versus dark, good versus evil, and savagery versus compassion. It seemed all sides had their heros and their villains and the text went into excruciating details of great generals and battles won in lost. The orc marvelled in the detail of the work but knew something was amiss. Thousands of years before this day a great flood at unified the races of this world in the fight for survival and there was no record of any great wars even before the Great Flood, but the writing was too detailed and too enthralling to dawn on that for too long. In awe of the work that was placed before him the Orc pulled a special potion from his drawer to test the paper the tome was written on. The orc audibly scoffed and looked up at his dwarf companion through his spectacles again as the dab of potion on the corner turned yellow indicating that paper had been manufactured in the great mill in this city. " It appears we have discovered the rambling of a brilliant and imaginative writer nothing more, " he said as he cast the book aside to continue the work he was doing before being interrupted.

This tower is rumored to be occupied by some errant hedge wizard, and as soon as I entered the horrors of their work are present. Talking ponies of all colors swarm around me, giggling in satanic glee. Before their razor sharp hooves can do any harm, I dismiss them into oblivion with a small gesture and a shudder. Truly, this wizard is insane. I continue through the fluorescent halls, in awe of the debauchery and hellish creations within. Every surface is covered with tapestries depicting lewd and vividly drawn ladies, and somehow my own powers seem stifled by the aura of this place. I follow these tapestries for an hour or so until I find large wooden doors. This must be the lair of the wizard. With a push, I open the doors to find him waiting for me. I mastered the arts of imagination years ago, but in my time I have never seen such a disheartening scene. His beard looks disgustingly unkempt, and flows solely from his corpulent neck. Orange dust coat his fingers, obviously the by-product of some horrific eldritch magics. The waves of miasma roiling off him collide with me, and I lose focus. My mind is too muddled to work the arcane, and I look into his eyes. He smiles. "Its been too long since I've had visitors," he wheezes. All around me the women of the tapestries come to life. They clamber down the wall towards me, and whispers of "wizard-chan" echo through the chamber. I ready my fists, but the onslaught is too great. I can not defend myself from the hordes of flesh. They overwhelm me. My last sight before being torn apart is the sadistic glimmer of his eyes.

' He has a very sleepy conscience.'she said matter-of-factly. ' Sure.'I said noncommittally. ' I saw that he hesitated before giving that poor woman two rupees.'she said. ' He doesn't think too highly about begging. He feels beggars are a waste of space.' ' What?'I managed. ' Yes, I saw it.' ' What nonsense.'I said. A lot firmer than last time. She laughed. 'Oliur, I think you have a hard time believing that your friends have a sleepy conscience.'she declared. ' I... I don't know. I've never thought about that.' ' Yes, yes you do. In fact, your sense of morality applies only to strangers. You'll let a friend get away with wrongdoing because you'd much rather just stay friends with them instead of doing the right thing, which is to tell them off. That's all right. Telling your friends off is one thing. Being there for them despite who they are, is another. They're both admirable traits.' ' I... Yes. Yes, maybe you're right. It's not worth the effort as I have very few friends.'I said shamefacedly. She laughed again. ' Hm.'she added softly. I felt I had disappointed her by agreeing to her assessment of me. She made a motion to be helped up. I nodded and finished up my Earl Grey. I motioned ' One second'with my fingers, and then hastily mouthed a'Gim me a second, '. I ran across to the kitchen sink and opened a little cellar door below it. It hid a dustbin inside. I disposed off my plastic cup in it headed towards her. She raised her hand for me to take it. I took it and guided her up and helped her walk through the room and out of the kitchen door. ' Um- ' I started. ' Yes?'she said quickly. ' Er... since you can... since you can, you know, read stuff... I just wanted to say I'm not sympathetic of your condition. I'm just a little fidgety and careful. It's why I'm er- ' I made my arms flail around, ' -awkward.'I finished awkwardly. She laughed heartily. ' No, no. You're not a sympathiser. I know that. You know I know that.' ' I - I did, I suppose.' ' Then you said it because you wanted to hear me say you're not a sympathiser?'she asked. It was not an accusatory question. It was just a question she wished to know the answer to. Propelled by mere curiosity. ' Er-yes, that must have been it.'I said, mildly surprised with myself for admitting something so freely. We had reached the guest room. I punched the pillows and straightened the sheets a little. It was my way of keeping busy while she slowly walked into the room. It was apparent to there now that I couldn't keep still. I switched on the bedside lamp and then looked at her. A soft smile lit her face. She proceeded to sit on the bed. ' Goodnight, Oliur.'she said. ' Sure, yeah goodnight.'I said nodding my head vigourously. I walked to the door and hung around. ' Oliur'she said simply. ' I - Yes. Yes?'I fumbled. ' Oliur, it's OK.'she said with the same soft smile. ' It's OK what?' ' It's OK that Omar is who he is. You needn't apologise.' ' Lakshmi, I...' ' That's the thing. He thinks he's right about it. He feels this house is turning into a dharamsala for the poor, the handicapped and - 'a pause. ' - the blind.' ' No, Lakshmi, that's - ' I couldn't go on. She was saying all the stuff that was floating in my head. I wanted to make it go away so Lakshmi couldn't see through me anymore. ' It's OK. I'll live with it. I have to. It's the least I can do to pay you back for what you do for people like me.' Something about that sentence got me. She shouldn't be talking like this, I thought. She needn't be talking like this, I corrected myself. I walked up to her and kneeled on the floor in front of her. For the first time that whole night, I knew exactly what to say. ' Lakshmi'I said. ' People like you are people like me. There aren't kinds of people. There are just... people. I'm not ashamed or inconvenienced to have you here. I'm just glad. And I will continue to be. As for Omar, yes, you're one hundred percent right. I'm sorry he feels the way he does. And for whatever I'm worth, I'll put every ounce of energy I possess to make sure he stops seeing the world like that.' A beat. ' I'm sure.'she said. She leaned forward to kiss my forehead. Then she drew back. ' Just don't do so tonight. You're tired, he's going be tired. I think it won't go well for either of you.' ' What!'I exclaimed. ' How... How did you know I'd speak with him tonight?'I said. She laughed for a long time before managing to say something that would stay with me for life. ' The blind can see, stupid. Just not in the way you expect. '

This is the fifth goddamn time, why can't he pick up the trash himself? I existed in this world since the dawn of time. I fought in wars, I overthrew kingdoms, I ruled empires, but you know what this sack of flesh does? This despicable being uses me, a great entity, incomparable to others, to pick up the trash, and do the dishes. Do you know how many times I had to wash the dishes? Oh, you can not comprehend the amount of times I had to wash the dishes. Don't even get me started on the amount of times I had to clean the room. I'm always expected to do these menial chores every day. Every time I'm summoned I just hope - hope that I'm summoned for something actually useful. Why, he doesn't even know who I am. I'm invisible to this ape. The first time I was summoned, I was commanded to do the laundry. I thought, it can't be this bad until he screamed, "I have a power!" At that moment I smiled and was ready to serve the son of a great man, and then he finished his sentence. "The power to do CHORES!" At that second, my heart broke. Why can't he see me? All the previous generations saw me, I served under them, and led them to prosperity, but why, why couldn't he see me? I was bound to this foolish human, by his father. A foolish decision made by such a great man. I expected great things from this child, especially when he was the offspring of a man that even I admired. Sadly, this child will never make full use of this power. I just wished he stopped tapping that wretched stick of his, and why does he wear those stupid goggles indoors? Hopefully, I'll be passed on to a even worthy ruler after this failure.

"NEXT" I yell as another dreary soul steps through the gates. It's a simple job really, one long line, a whole lotta souls. You check each one as they enter, no contraband allowed on any soul entering hell. That means no happiness, no hope, no artifacts and especially no guardians. The god damn guardian angels. You think angels are bad enough, these guys are the real goody two shoes, the sort to really pine over a lost soul; not the type of soul who raped or murdered but the little sins, you know? Petty theft due to starvation, an accidental murder from an impassioned fight, lusting after the wrong thing, stuff the souls feel guilty about. Every now and then, one of these holier than though guardians thinks he can sneak on in. Piggy back a ride on a soul yeah? Thinks he or she or it, whatever, is just going to slip right damn by me and steal away the soul once its been accounted for. Bah! Not likely. You see, those white-winged, bright and shiny dogs have a stink to them. It's like honeysuckle and roses, and a little tinkly bell sound that seems to follow them around as well. You think they realise that? No damned way! Most are too arrogant doing "the Lords work," thinking they're so blessed that nothing can stop them, a lot of them don't even notice it at all! Anyway, an angel being caught down here is a big deal. You see, my master The Morning Star struck a deal with God a long, long time ago. No angel is to enter Hell, just as no demon is to enter Heaven. Keep the peace and all that business yeah? Doesn't happen often but it's always an embarrassment for Heaven to have an angel get caught down here, what with all their "honor" and general attitude of being those who take the "high road" and follow the rules. Demons getting caught in Heaven however is sort of a different matter. That one is a little more..... shall we say touchy? A demon is something of an expendable force to our great and wondrous master so being torn asunder by an Arch angel isn't much more than an affront to his power. Problem is though, they'd perceive any demons up there as a sort of act of war. A bit hysterical if you ask me..... Anyway, it seems I've gone off on a bit of a tangent there, not too sure why I decided to tell you any of that anyway you little wretch. Oh well, in you go, hell awaits. "NEXT!" " Hmmm..... I feel sort of dazed" " Wait..... is that..... honeysuckle and roses I smell..? " " SOMEBODY QUICK! FIND THAT SOUL! Oh fuck, Lucifer is going to have me for this one alright..."

I'm deviating from the prompt a bit. sorry, I just had an idea. Do you understand why I have become a guidance counselor? If you were a pious man, as I try to be, you would perhaps already see how it is the greatest opportunity to do God's work in His bountiful garden. I oversee everything which grows. I water the crops, and direct their leaves towards sunlight. Most of the work is His own, of course, I don't grow the plants. I am not capable of understanding such infinite complexity. No, plants grow on their own for the most part, but the growth is not the only part of His plan. Weeds, you understand, are also part of His creation. They are the sole feature of the garden of hell. When we abandoned Him, the decay of hell crept into our world, and gave us death, disease, poverty, and sin. Before the fall, there were no gardeners, only gardens. We have come a long way since then. The tree of knowledge has been a surprisingly effective substitute for his divine hand. But the tiniest slip in removing the scourge of Hell from our world would be catastrophic. We are the caretakers, Nathan, and I must not let you trample upon His flowers with your open..... toed..... shoes...

" Quick! " I gestured to the girl, pointing at the ever-growing pool amassing on the floor. She stood motionless, instead glancing at the dead man next to the shattered wine bottle. I hopped over to him and rolled his body out of the way. There was no time to deal with him. " Quickly, come on, it's alright, " I grabbed her by the hand and pulled her closer to the floor. " Mummy says I shouldn't drink that stuff, " she said innocently. " Mummy's not here, so you have to listen to me, okay? It wasn't okay to drink that stuff before, but it's good for you now, understand? " She stared back at me blankly. There was no way I could get through to her with words, and we were just wasting time at this stage. " Look, it's perfectly safe, I'll show you, " I bent down and started sipping at the red ambrosia. I didn't need to look up at her; I could hear her bending down and following suit. " Good girl, " I whispered, wiping the liquid off my lower face. She needed it more than I did. I calculated that I still had some left in my system, for the time being. She, on the other hand, well... she hadn't had anything at all. I wondered how she survived for so long. It was quite early on that I figured out it was the alcohol keeping me alive. On Day One I had woken up later than usual, not even hung over but still drunk. The night before was my first ' letting loose'event, and being a petite girl with absolutely no tolerance for alcohol, it managed to stay in my system for a while. In any other situation I would have been terribly ashamed of myself, but this time it was the key to my survival. When I left my dorm room, I noticed it was unusually quiet, but I thought everyone else was just hung over. It was only after a bit more wandering around that I realised a lot of people were just dead. I first came across the zombies stumbling their way slowly through the hallways, gurgling incoherently guttural sounds, and wearing clothes that looked a little worse for wear. To be frank, I just assumed they were all hung over from the night before. It was only when they started attacking the Non-Drunks that I realised something was terribly wrong. Day One was a big blur for me; it felt so long ago. All I can remember was the terrible looting that followed. When people started raiding the liquor stores before the grocery stores, I realised it had something to do with the alcohol. During the raids of Day One, I managed to grab a couple bottles of vodka. My small stature allowed me to go quite a bit undetected amongst the chaos. And the high alcohol percentage of the vodka meant that it would last me for quite some time. I knew I was going to run out soon, though, and I couldn't get my hands on anything else, so I went and grabbed a trolley-full of liquids, be it water, cordial, juice, milk... you name it. After all, you could die faster from dehydration than starvation. At night, I made my way to a friend's house nearby to the college. They were filthy rich, and I knew they had a wine cellar. When I reached their house, I found it abandoned save the young son dead in the cellar. The house was littered with empty wine bottles, but luckily there was still a few days'worth left in the cellar. My guess is that as they began to run low, they attempted to obtain more, but were attacked by the zombies. And since the zombies didn't go for the alcohol, that left a decent amount to me. The girl finished sipping the wine, and sat up. " What do we do now, miss? " " Well firstly, that was my last bottle so we will need more of that; it'll help us. If you're tired you can sleep first but I may need to wake you up to help me later. " " What are you going to do? " " I'm going to set up some bait. " I walked off, grabbing all the empty wine bottles that were sporadically placed in the house. I started filling them up with other liquids; the vodka bottles with water, the white wine with diluted apple juice, and the red wine with red cordial. I stared at the red wine bottles. They were the bottles I had the most of, and the red cordial was a poor imitator. I figured I may have to put some blood in them. I went back down to the cellar to grab the dead man. The girl was asleep already; I guess the alcohol helped in that. I figured she drank enough to keep her safe while she slept, so I had no issues with leaving her alone in the house. I struggled to drag the man up the stairs. It would have been easier to carry everything out in the cellar, but I didn't want the girl to wake up to a messy pool of blood. The stain of the red wine on the floor looked bad enough as is. By the time I managed to drag him up the stairs, I was exhausted. But every second counted, so I quickly got to work. I had strangled him, so he wasn't already bleeding. I'd have to make a cut somewhere. I went back down to the cellar to grab a piece of broken glass from the bottle he had smashed into my head shortly before he breathed out all the air in his lungs. There were plenty of empty bottles around, but he just had to choose my last full bottle. Once he died I couldn't even think about the gravity of my first murder; I had to get the girl to drink. I sat back down, cradling his head in my lap. I placed one of the red wines at an angle, close to his neck, and made a cut. The blood oozed out, and in the bottle it was already starting to look more like red wine. There was plenty of blood in this man to distribute amongst the red cordial, and by the time I was done I was quite happy with my efforts. The sealing of the bottles were much more difficult to pass off as the real thing, but I figured they would look okay from a distance. I filled the trolley up with the bottles, and strategically placed a small towel on top so as to have some of the bottles peeking through. More effort was exhausted as I dragged both the man I had just drained of blood, and the young boy who was already dead when I arrived. I lugged them to a nearby alley that I could see from the living room, and I knew that it could be easily accessed through the main bedroom's window. I then went and woke up the girl and explained to her my plan. Once she was stationed at the living room window, I quickly but quietly wheeled the trolley next to the men. I tried to make it look as natural as possible, as if they were trying to hide and sleep in a safe place, but I made the trolley stick out a bit so that it could be seen. I went back to the house, and checked in on the girl. " What do we do now? " She asked. I handed her the binoculars, and grabbed the shotgun from off the table. I started heading to the main bedroom next door. " Now, we wait. "

Brrkkzztrr Brinsonn, last of his kind, and indeed last of any kind swayed lazily above his favourite rock. Brinsonn, being a mutant mayfly, had achieved the capacity for thought that his fore bearers never could, and very much enjoyed pondering on the mysteries of life, but most of all he liked thinking about his rock. The rock had been there since he could remember. For all he knew, it was the oldest thing in existence. It wasn't, but a mayfly, even a mutant one, can't be expected to know such things. Brrkkzztrr had spent almost every waking moment of his life studying, probing and considering the deeper significance of the rock, but due to an unfortunate genetic blind spot, he was totally unable to come to grips with the concept of'underneath'. He had not once in his long freakish years considered the possibility that there might be something hidden under his rock. Had he done so, he would have reached some very insightful and interesting conclusions on life and the universe. As it happens, he did in fact eventually have that epiphany, albeit about three seconds before he was duly squashed by his coveted aggregate of minerals. The last thought that trailed through his insect mind was something like "hmm ," but it would have sounded slightly more of spittle and grinding of mandibles and jointed limbs. If anyone had been around to hear it, they would have been disappointed with the sound the last being in the universe gave when its life came to an end. "That's it? ," they would say, "That's all? One pathetic splat and a squeak? Not even a dying battle roar? No ode to the beauty and transience of all things?! Bloody typical! " No one alive was around to say that though. Certainly no one English. There would never be anyone or anything alive or English ever again. Just a grinning silhouette. This was the beginning of the End. A silent observer watched to make sure that Brrkkzztrr Brinsonn had properly deceased. This was an important job, and he wanted to be absolutely certain that everything was done just right. He didn't need to breathe, but he took a deep breath all the same, just for appearances, and then he lifted the rock. Satisfied with seeing the smear that once was Brinsonn, he put the rock down, pulled himself to his full, terrifying height and then he heard a loud crack. SHIT. SHITSHITSHIT. Death froze and didn't dare move. 'THIS CA N'T BE', he thought, knowing full well that it could, 'I DO N'T EVEN HAVE DISCS, HOW CAN THEY SLIP?' He tried moving, winced at the sudden and totally alien pain, and remained still again. I WAS TO RETIRE. AFTER THIS NEXT ONE, THE LAST ONE, MY DUTY IS OVER. THIS IS..... THIS IS.... He searched his ancient memory for the right words to describe what he was feeling. THIS IS SO TYPICAL. AN ETERNITY OF SERVITUDE, AND THEN THIS. BLOODY TYPICAL. He waited some more, and remained still for a long time. About 30 million earth years to be precise, but time is relative, and Death is absolute. He was used to waiting. Then, something happened. An almost imperceptible shift in the cosmic winds, a stirring of a stray Quaalude, magic in the air. Death felt a tug, and knew he was being summoned. His form twisted and spread, expanding over all creation, and then he was facing All. And All stared at him, weak and old and tired and cold, and spoke. End-itt Death saw himself hold out a bony arm, saw his scythe materialize, saw All close its many eyes and smile serenely. And Death replied, BUGGER THAT. I'M NOT SPENDING ETERNITY WITH A SLIPPED DISC, WITH NO ONE TO COMPLAIN TO. I'M NOT DOING IT. All recoiled in shock, and momentarily looked as angry and bright as in its youth. You-mustt You-promissd I DO N'T CARE. I'VE HAD ENOUGH OF DEATH AND LIFE. I WILL REST, AND THEN WHEN I AM FEELING IN BETTER SHAPE, WE WILL TALK. All shrieked and burn and contracted and swore, but Death had already left. You-will, said All, You-WILL It tugged and pulled everything it had and burned its form into one tiny, searing hot, focused point. Again, it said YOU-WILL..... Then All began again, from the beginning.

I had always felt..... different. My mom and dad had told me that I was perfectly normal, but I knew something was off with me. It was almost as if everyone else was on a completely different wavelength than me, one that enlightened them. It started in high school. That was when the differences became more noticeable. Now, of course, I found others that were similar to me, ones who were slightly off the "right" wavelength as well, however; they still seemed to know more than I did. They never even flinched when the cafeteria was flooded by the basketball team in song and dance. Some of them even partook. The first time it happened, I was under the impression that I had simply missed the announcement. But no. It began to happen all over the place, like a disease. Groups of individuals would spontaneously begin singing and dancing, people who I knew for a fact had never even met before, and they were always in perfect harmony. Nobody else seemed to find it odd or abnormal, when asked they seemed to not understand me. Sometimes they even began to look at me as if I were the one who was insane. I soon began to learn how to not stand out. I even drifted away from my "safe group" as they at least seemingly had a purpose. I started to avoid large groups of people, as many an occasion I had been caught off guard, stuck in a crowd who had begun the strange harmonious "performance." Being unable to join in, I stood there, until I could find a route to escape, under hateful, suspicious eyes. Nowadays I live in forests and abandoned places, changing locations everyday. I try not to go out in public. The life of a fugitive. Funnily enough, in my silence and inaction, I stood out the most, and soon was labeled a criminal. I haven't even heard for what yet, but I don't dare to show myself. I'm terrified what they might do to me. If they were able to force that many people to be so in tune with each other, and not even question it, who knows the extent of their power? I beg you, if you recognized yourself at all in what I said above, run, please, don't hesitate. They will soon be after you too, if they aren't already.

"Mars will be great" they said. "You'll be known throughout human history" they said. Didn't mention the giant Martian badgers though, did they? No, no they did not. When I told everyone I was going to Mars I imagined it would be all playing with beakers, riding slow Mars rovers, taking samples (whatever that entails), and growing a beard. You know, boring sciency stuff that would make me look smart in photos. "But Franky, why would NASA send a pest and animal control expert to Mars?" My friends would ask. I'd blow off their questions because fucking NASA wanted me - not my yacht owning, ex-fighter pilot now doctor arsehole of a best friend - me! Who cares about reasons! NASA, those clever bastards, even let me think it was all my idea for me to go first. I was at my arsehole of a best friend's house for a party when I somehow ended up in a conversation with some of the NASA folk that were mutual friends of the arsehole of a host. "Gosh, it would be good to get an everyman's view of the planet" Said a tall man who had the figure and hair cut you'd expect from a life in the military. "Yes, yes it would." Said his slightly shorter and equally muscled and crew-cut associate "Someone like a pest and animal control person." "Oh?" I said "It just so happens that I am a pest and animal control person!" "What a coincidence!" The two said in unison. I had not been interested in anything that the pair of muscular buzz-cuts had said up until this point - they were friend's of my arsehole best friend and so were arseholes by association - but now they had my interest. Me? On Mars? Fuck yeah! They asked me a bunch of questions about whether I'd be willing to go, what I'm like in confined spaces, what I'm like with animals - like badgers, what about big animals, what about big badgers - it was an endless sea of questions. In between each one, asked by the tall fellow, the shorter one would chime in with a: "Hypothetically, of course." "Look," I said in a drunken mumble "Just put me on Mars, and I'll do what needs doin!" "We might just do that." Said the tall one. Next thing I know I'm giving them my contact details and getting their business cards in return, and then I was left to go about my business at the party. And that business, as always, was to consume all the free food and alcohol I could - which I did. The next day I got picked up by a black SUV and was taken, hangover and all, to a local military base for some tests and to commence my training. "But what possible problems could you solve for them up there?" My correctly suspicious loved ones would ask, even after I'd dramatically let it be known that I didn't care. Turns out NASA had some huge problems for me to solve. Huge and badgery problems. Namely: huge badgers. Now you would think that NASA would be happy to have found alien life, right? Wrong. Are you not paying attention? I am a man who is trained to relocate animals or, when not possible to do so, it so happens that I am also trained to humanely dispatch said creatures. NASA discovers life on Mars. They send a man whose job it is is to moveend life. Does that sound like NASA is happy with life being on Mars? Hmm? Here's a hint: fuck you!

You know what, Chino? All you had to do was be honest with me instead of stringing me along. Four years of my life invested into something I thought would pay off in the long run, for what? So you could sing my praises in your office, promote me in private and then undermine the very authority you claimed to had given me in front of my peers? You like to see people humiliated? There was a time when I was grateful for the opportunity you gave me. For allowing me to be a member of the team and learn everything. I fell in love with all that came with this opportunity; from beginning to end. Back then, I felt renewed and happy to call this place home. I felt a sense of hope that my life could go on forever. But now, it's all backstabbing and lies; threats and disciplinary actions. The loyalty and respect I gave you, you no longer command or deserve. Back then, I might have had nothing without this job. Now, after four years, I feel I have most of it left. I was happy once, now disillusioned, defeated I close this letter with the only thing I couldn't say to your face: "I Quit" No longer your employee, therabbit86ed

"No, seriously, we do love our humans..... we just..... don't want to come off clingy." The kitten scratched itself a bit. "That's what mama taught me, anyway. Keep your distance but always make it clear you love them. S'kinda hard." "Okay..... then how do you explain the glasses?" I said, stretching a bit. "Glasses?" She tilted her head. I stumbled for an explanation that didn't go in circles, until she reacted. "The floating liquids! We just want a drink but they keep on leaping off the edge rather than be drank!" "Oh..... that explains a lot..." I tried to think of other things. "What else can you tell me about other animals?" "The less'cuddly' something is like a reptile, the more they LOVE affection. We all do, but you know how it is." She groomed herself between comments. "There are as many DOGS who look down on their humans as you think us cats do. Birds that can speak your language know WAY more than they let on. And those tiny scrawny purse-carried dogs really do think they're much bigger..... until you scratch some sense into them." Did I just catch her trying to smirk? "Oh, and you know how you can tell how good someone is by how we respond to them? We judge other animals by how good they are to humans. Especially kids. Your cubs are the ultimate test of character to us. Anyone who can't keep their cool around a curious human-cub is generally no one we want to associate with." I leaned back in my chair. "Wow..... the things I never thought about." "You should. We're not all that different, socially." She curled up. "Naptime..... plus the vet's coming." I panicked a bit and grabbed my textbook just in time for the door to open. "You sure you're going to be okay on night watch, Jake? It can get awful boring, and you'll be locked in, save for emergencies." The head veterinarian, here to check on me before she left. "Oh I'll be fine! I have my textbooks, some music, a game or two..... I can make it the night!" I said, looking down at my book to hide a smirk. "Besides..... I have a lot to learn tonight..."

No job. No family. No prospects that come to mind. I'm just sitting here at the stoop of a building, watching the traffic. I don't even have the will to panhandle at this point. The day has already passed me by, just as every day does. It seems like life has always moved just a little too fast for me. I watch a man in a suit, cell phone to ear, speed-walking. A to B, with a whole mess of work in between. How do they all keep up? A little girl heads toward me from across the street. She carries some change in her hand. Some people still have time to be sweet. Oh, she dropped some. She's bending down to pick it up- she doesn't notice the truck! I spring to my feet. It's faster than I've ever felt I've moved. It's instinct. I bolt. It seems like I'm fighting against my own nature. I can feel the air resisting me, the ground wanting to grab my feet and hold them, voices saying Stop. Slow down. You'll never make it..... I dive and grab the girl and hold her close and we roll out of the way as the truck swerves and skids and blares its horn. We both lay there in the street as a crowd forms around us. It may be the shock or the adrenaline or some trick of the mind but I swear, over there, past the crowd, is a shadowy figure, Death himself, walking away. Maybe he was expecting things to go differently. Too bad. I guess he'll have to wait.

The very earth we walked on seemed to breath life itself. The greenery, the animals, it was if our very presence reassured them that their life was of meaning. Each corner my brother, Harold, Gabriel, and I walked, they seemed to respond with a whirl of the leaf, or a cheerful chirp of the birds. I felt at place. I felt at peace. As we continued to walk upon the shrubbery, I saw other figures moving underneath the cliff we stood upon. They wore odd furs, as if they shaved the very beings that welcomed us here. As I tried to peer closer, my foot slipped, and the sudden movement caused the birds to fly in disapproval. "Who goes there?" A bellowing voice cried out. Suddenly, a felt a tingle in the back of my throat. I felt uneasy. These beings were not like anything I've seen. Their figure resembled humans, but their voices were so guttural, it created a visage that they were, perhaps, something more than that. Upon further noting, they had these claws that extended farther than a normal human's nails could ever reach. Gabriel grabbed onto my hand. "We need to go now." Sensing his matched uneasiness, we carefully trampled over the shrubbery, which were so welcoming, now seemed to snicker at our escape. "What were those things?" My brother exclaimed. He was rather shy to this new world. In fact, he often questioned things. He even questioned where we came from, and that I put my faith in a higher power. "I don't know, Harold. Just keep mo Suddenly, I bumped into one of the beings that bellowed their voices at us. He smiled a slow smile, revealing his jagged teeth one by one. "It seems we have game." Slowly, he twisted his head to the side, examining us one by one. "Humans." "We mean no harm. We will leave, as you please." I stuttered. These beings, They resembled us, but they didn't. It seemed as if the higher power failed and failed, until finally they perfected Humans. As if reading my mind, the being puffed out his chest, and uttered, "Rejects." Suddenly, I see the scarlet red of my brother's blood rippling through his scalp. The blood spattered on everything around us, including the plants that used to welcome us with their whimsical dances. Even at that moment, they danced, as if they now haunted me with the blood from my brother's body. He dropped to the ground, head dislocated from the rest. "Harold, are you alright?" I sputtered. Something was not right. No body should ever look like that. We should be whole, rightly beings. Not in two such as he. I dropped to the ground, trying to reclaim what was left of his head, and attach it to the rest, but to no avail. I knew something was wrong, the way his eyes glazed over, the way his body held no memory of movement or us. Why was this? Why did he no longer resemble human? Why would he not respond? I searched desperately for the answer, and when I looked upon the being's eyes, it looked as if it took satisfaction in uttering this word to me. "Death."

Gorillas, terribly strong creatures, capable of ripping a fully grown man to shreds at a whim. Tigers, yes, they are fast, bodies laced with lithe cords of muscle and sinew. Kitchen knives for teeth and talons for nails, they carry a sharpness to their eyes that seems to stop light. But the eyes do not stop light, nor do they project stillness. Some might interpret the eye as calm, but in reality the eyes tell the story of certainty. Certainty of death for most anyone who is unlucky enough to see such a sight. Lions and Gorillass, like most other animals, were born into the world near the limit of their physical capabilities. During the inception of war, animals like Lions and Gorillas dictated victor between armies. But all changed one day when a boy named Yag was gifted a duck by his senile grandma. Grandma Xu looked upon her grandsons ugly face and said, "Here is a duck, its for your birthday." No tears were shed. The duck walked up to Yag and nodded. Yag smiled at the duck and then named him Vladimir. Aside from the birth of one of the greatest friendships of all time, no other noteworthy events occurred on this day. Months later, Yag and Vladmir the duck were walking to school together. Yag was telling Vladmir about a new coconut juice and spicy pork that "poor mother fucking street cook" Shien was making. Shien was a good pal of Yag's, or at least Yag thought so. A lot of their relationship had to deal with the fact that Yag spent most of his money on Shien's spicy pork skewers. "I am telling you Vladmir, Shien's spicy pork skewers are going to be better than ever when accompanied by his new delicious coconut beverage," exclaimed the mildly round boy. Yag walked excitedly towards school with Vladmir the duck struggling to keep up with his compadre. Yag was a few strides ahead of Vladmir, when two young boys crossed the road and stared towards Yag viciously. These boys were class 7 assholes and have had it out for Yag all year long. Steven and Sarah were the boys names and they were flanked by two of their fathers warhorses and one giant cobra viper. The warhorses growled a low rumbling growl, eagerly awaiting the taste of blood. The snake slithered onto the horses backs and raised itself high into the air, preparing to strike. The snake was clad in combat armor. The two horses wore heavy mail jackets and shoes that were covered in razors. Yag looked up to see Sarah and Steven issue forth a decree of combat to the death. Yag looked to his right sheepishly as a shopkeeper barred his doors.A young mother grabbed her children, currying them inside, into safety. Death was in the air. Testing your animals strength in open combat was a common ritual in the Province of Tost. A common ritual that Yag had failed to regard with any interest his entire life. Yag looked up at the two terrifyingly large horses, atop which perched the viper. If death had a face, then surly this was the face it wore when smiling towards Yag. Vladmir the duck's heart was racing, he didn't know what to do. He wanted to quack but he couldn't, his heart was beating with the fury of an ocean storm. Yag turned around and smiled at his good chum Vladmir the duck and then time stopped. Sarah and Steven nodded towards their warriors. The horses smiled, foaming at the mouth with eagerness for blood, but before they could move, the viper lashed out towards Yag. Vladimr yearned to help, to move, to do anything, but all he could do was watch. With unbridled speed, the viper knifed through the air towards Yag, who was still smiling at Vladmir. Vladmir cherished this moment, time stood still, at this point their was no past or future, only the then. And during then, Valdmir was hanging out with his good pal Yag. Then ended abruptly as the cobra viper collided into Yag's back and exploded out through his chest, leaving a bowling bowl sized hole in the boys chest. Yag's smiling face faded as the life fell from his eyes and his body fell to the ground and became a corpse. Vladmir was left staring into the eyes of his dead comrade. Sarah and Steven laughed at the pathetic challenge that Yag presented. Vladmir continued to stare towards yag as his heart dissolved. He cringed in paralysis. As the taste of the world disappeared, vision became stationary, and sensation left his heart. Vladmir the duck was not even acknowledged as a potential opponent. The two warhorses of S2 kicked and neighed, irked that they had been cheated out of a fight. Sarah and Steven turned around and took their first steps home, eager to recant an exaggerated tale of combat to their fathers expectant ears. Vladmir's sorrowful gaze dirft towards his little duck feet. The warhorses turned to follow Sarah and Steven as the viper finished bathing in Yag's blood. Vladmir stood still, staring down at his feet as the cobra viper slivered away from Yag's corpse to rejoin his brothers of battle. The complex emotional structure that guided Vladmirs life was gone. It was as if a great storm had washed a large mountain chain away and replaced it with one long canal. And through this canal water did not flow. This was a canal that wanted to flow, but not with water, this was a canal that yearned to flow the souls of the dead. Vladmir razed his beak from the ground and belched a faint quack towards the viper. Vladmir's eyes were the blackness of ink submerged in the darkness of a black hole. The viper chuckled as it readied itself to strike. Sarah, Steven, and the two war horses casually turned to regard the slaying. Before the viper could strike, Vlad's eyes turned dark red, and two highways of light shot towards the viper, splaying him lengthwise with the heat of a thousand suns. The heat was so intense that after the viper was quartered, lengthwise, his innards burst into flame. Sarah and Steven froze, regarding the duck with faces of terror. They began to open their mouths to beg for mercy but it was too late. Vladmir opened his mouth and issued forth four quacks. No ordinary quacks were issued, these quacks were unrefusable commands decreed by an empower of death. The air shook as the sound approached Sarah, Steve, and their now meek looking warhorses. Warhorses, huh, more like birthday ponies. The sound slammed into the four warriors and their bowels erupted with the force of falling tree. The warriors excrement was jettisoned from their rectums with astonishing fury. After the fecal matter came the liver then their ribs then their heart and then followed the rest of their bodies, leaving the warriors to have shit themselves inside out. Like turning a garbage bag inside out, through its asshole. Brain and bone and heart all perfectly intact, beating on a ground full of shit and blood. Vladmir sighed to himself as a tear fell down his face in immense sorrow. And thus, the dynasty of the ducks was born into the world.

Coming back I inhaled sharply, the blackness in front of my eyes disappearing to show a white room. "Where am I?" I tried to say but heard only a strange rasping. My throat burned like fire. Looking around, I noticed a few cameras and a mirror in front of me. The sight was morbid. I was as skinny and sickly as before. Was this some kind of a joke? Last thing I remembered was falling asleep on my bed in the hospice. Struggling to breath and then darkness. Is this a purgatory? The view in front of me came into sudden sharp focus. The burning sensation from my throat spread to my face and head. My eyes darted around the room quickly but with perfect accuracy. The previous disease-induced blurriness disappeared. The fire retreated and made its way through the rest of my body which responded immediately both in feel and look. The mirror showed my body glowing with a flush redness, gaining mass quickly. I lifted my arm and unstrapped from the upright table I was bound to. I took a few steps and the mirror turned to a window. People were clapping and congratulating each other. Someone had a television screen playing in the background. I could read the title on it, though it was very far away. My vision had never been this good. "The first human revived from death: Marco Liebener," it read. I could hear them talk, "This will be revolutionary. No one will ever die again." one of the people said. "We will make a fortune off this." "The investors will be beyond ecstatic." "Probably will line up to have their loved ones revived right away!" Someone's eyes locked with mine and a sudden look of fear washed over their face. "I think he's looking at me!" he told one of the others around him. "Don't be stupid. It's a one way window." "I swear, he looked at me." "I know things get a tad spooky when reviving a human but drop it, alright? This is a monumental step in human history." I could hear new things, the whirring of the computers. The scattering of small bugs deep under the floor. The steps of people above me. My vision changed too. The room around me changed too. Bright white dots lined every square inch of the room. The light was coming from the cameras in the corners. I took a few steps and knocked on the mirror, startling them. I could see beyond their clothes, and could see perfect images from the reflections in their eyes and their glasses. Their IR camera showed my body burning up in heat. "That's a normal reaction," one of the scientists said to the assistant watching the screen. The heat kept increasing until they saw another type of reading. "His body is becoming highly radioactive!" One of the individuals there screamed, "We have to terminate him!" A higher up nodded in agreement. It was now or never. I punched the mirror, shattering it completely, melting away the pieces. I jumped through and weaved through the staff before they could react. Out the door, soon out of the clinic, I made it out. That's when it happened. Time stopped, leaves on trees stopped moving, wind ceased, and even lights went dark. My body grew in heat so much that I could see matter around me liquifying and becoming gas soon after. "The President called for an international state of emergency as what we call the'Radioactive man' detonated in the central Ohio area. A twenty mile crater was left after the detonation. "The bad news, unfortunately, do not stop there. After said detonation which will truthfully impact the future of our world, the satellites from orbit picked up the heat signature of the man. It is possible he is still alive and on the move."

"George? Are you in here?" No sign of him. Typical. Just like George Crowley to shirk out of his own house move. I knew George from work. Every time we had to work on a project together, George was always the one who somehow had to be somewhere else right up until the last moment when he'd breeze in and give the final presentation claiming all the glory from management. That was how he'd just secured his big raise and clearly new house. To top it all he'd asked me - in the middle of a meeting with my boss' boss no less - if I'd help him move into his fancy new place. So here I am on a precious Saturday afternoon trying to find George and get this over with as quickly as possible. I looked around, but the house appeared to be completely empty apart from a single box, about 2 foot on a side, sitting on the granite worktop in the kitchen. (How did that sneak manage to afford granite?). Stuck to the top was a hastily scrawled note. "Back in 30 minutes. George." The cheek of it! He expected me to sit, well stand, around and wait for him just to pack up one single box. Was he crazy? No chance! I turned to leave and as I put my hand to the front door handle, I heard a child's voice coming from the kitchen - "Help me!" My heart raced. In no way was there a child in the kitchen a moment ago. I turned and cautiously made my way back. "Hello? Who's there?" Silence. I reached out to open one of the fitted cupboard doors. The blood pounded in my ears. My mouth was dry. Palms sweaty. Empty. All of them empty. I called out again and this time I heard, a little muffled, "In here!" Surely there couldn't be a child in that box. It was far too small. Nonetheless, I stood over it, placed the note to one side and broke the taped seal holding it closed. I held my breath and peeled back the top flaps. There was nothing inside. Just completely black. Not a painted black, this was a darkness that sucked all the light out of the world and pulled it into itself, forever to extinguish all that is good. I could feel myself slipping towards it. Drawn to look deeper and deeper. A small distant voice in the far reaches of my mind called to me to look away but I couldn't. I wanted to fall into the eternal abyss and experience the bliss of nothingness. I leaned further forward. I couldn't feel my feet touching the floor only my hands on the sides of the box. I closed my eyes and prepared to let go. "Stop!" The voice was immensely loud and contained a force that seemed to physically push me back. A moment later I opened my eyes to find myself on the other side of the kitchen. George was standing over me. He looked more than a little worried. "Are you alright, Mike? Did it say anything to you? Did you speak to it? Quickly, man, answer me!" "Er, I heard it call out for help, I opened the box and looked in and felt really weird and now I'm on the floor of your kitchen. What the hell is going on, George?" As I was speaking George had moved over to the box and sealed it up again. He turned to face me. "OK. I think you're going to be fine. You didn't have a conversation and I managed to pull you back before you began to slide. I doubt it's gotten a hold on you." "You're not making any sense. What is in that box?" George sighed. "It's a portal to another world, Mike. A dark world that only wants to consume ours. It can't be closed and it needs to be watched. It's one of the lesser artifacts in my charge." "George, you work as software developer for a travel agency..... don't you?" I was starting to question everything now. Including my sanity. "No, Mike, that's my cover. Ever wondered why I'm never around, and yet the bosses can't see through my charade with the presentations? It's because they've been paid to look the other way." Suddenly everything was starting to make sense. I felt a little bolder. "So why not just keep it in a wooden create in a large warehouse in the middle of nowhere?" George smiled. "Funny you should mention that, Mike. That's exactly what we're doing." "Why did you ask me to help you today? And why set me up to almost die?!" I asked with more anger than I intended. George leaned back casually against the worktop. He looked me in the eye. "I've been watching you, Mike. You're clearly fed up with your current line of work and I think you'd welcome a change. Now that you've seen that it's real, how would you like to come work for me?" - Edit: Minor corrections.

I walked through the forest. The beautiful greens and browns of the trees enveloped me mas I moved deeper into the Northwest Crucible. Crucibles to contain the heat of youth, but what were we forging? I had said my goodbyes, but no one knew exactly where I was going. I see movement; I am prepared. Strung bow already in hand, the arrow looses, and it feels beautiful. I will come bearing gifts to the tribe. I hope food will lessen that first impact, the newness of me. An outsider with a rabbit is better than one with nothing. Swirling rapids below now as I cross a rope bridge, swaying dangerously. You're never tested like this in the city. Will they accept me? I needed people, I can't be alone all these years. Will they understand? Some must see their time approaching and feel the same. I had to come here, I couldn't see another option. River raging below, I felt alive. The wooden gate was more bar to me than any hardship of the forest; that was always the way of it with me. Why I came here, why I am afraid. Guards studying me. They know, they remember, and they let me in. I gather a crowd as I make my way to Leader. " How dare you? You break every rule of arrival and think a rabbit buys forgiveness? We have better hunters than you. " He didn't understand; Leader had been here 9 years now and he would soon enough. " Don't you get it? Don't you all see what is waiting for you? You go back, and they put you behind a desk. A desk, for nine hours every day and you can't feel what you should, what you do everyday here. The rest chuckle and say'barely made it out alive' but I see their sadness, I see the lie of it. These ten years were my life; the rest a wasting sickness. " I reached some in the crowd, but a pretty speech, no matter how true, never changes what you hope it will. " You have to remember, every year we get some like you, and you know how this goes. I've already sent the report, they'll be here to retrieve you soon. Why even try? It's honestly sad, trying to recapture it. " Let's see you say it in a year, Leader. Let's see you repeat it then. I barely heard him as I slumped down, resigned to my fate. " You are twenty-nine years old; I think it's time you grew up. "

I have loved many pretty little girls and beautiful young women in this family as they have cherished me, passing me down from one generation to the next. These women love me regardless of Oh, she's back! I do hope her evening was Who's that with her? No! No! Not her! Run, baby girl!! Run! No! My beautiful girl. This is the only time in my fifty years that I have wished to be anything other than what I am. I wish I had eyes; I would cry
