"Time for bath, mommy!" Laura smiled to herself. This was her favorite part of the day, getting Lani ready for bed. She picked up the adorable little girl and hugged her close. "You got it sweetie. Go get your clothes from your room." She walked into the bathroom and began running the bath. The hone in the living room began to ring insistently, and with a quiet sigh, Laura went into the living room and picked up the phone. The call lasted only a few minutes. That's when she noticed it..... the ominous quiet that stretched menacingly. "Lani?" She walked into Lani's room, only to find it deserted, clothes still placed neatly on the bed. She walked into the kitchen, as the little girl was always "stealing" snacks, only to find it empty as well. Panic began to settle in her chest. She called Lani's name a bit too loudly as she went back into the living room. That's when she heard it. The running faucet in the bathroom that seemed to echo loudly in her ears and drown out all other sounds. Her heart began to race, and she rushed into the bathroom, dark thoughts and recriminations clouding her mind. She fearfully pushed the bathroom door open as her breath caught in her throat and her hand began to tremble violently. Dreading what she just knew she was going to find, her gaze immediately sought the tub and she rushed over to the side of the tub. She could only stare at what she found: nothing but clear water. Relief poured through her momentarily but then she frowned. Where was Lani? "Boo!" Lani jumped out at her mother from behind the bathroom door where she had been hiding and giggled happily. "I'care you!" Laura smiled wearily and reached out to wrap Lani in a too tight hug. "Yes, baby, you scared me." She stretched out a hand and turned the water off.

"Corner-Cutting" I was worried about the efficiency of the engram compression, or the integrity of my telomeres. I didn't want my cells to age super-fast, or my mind to gradually decay into noise data. But those weren't the issue. What I should have paid attention to was resolution. It started on the fifth "respawn." Everything had been going fine up to then - incurable disease, radiation burns, blunt force trauma, blood loss. Horribly dead, safely alive, rinse, repeat. Then I noticed something odd. It wasn't immediately noticeable. It might have been happening in previous lives, in even less conspicuous ways, but I found it on my nose. A voxel. It was disconcerting, but not terribly so. A little extra skin and an odd right-angle wasn't something to make me question my latest biological vehicle, but I did wonder what would happen if it had happened in, say, my eye. A bullet through the head and I was back in the machine. After the standard checks, I tried to find a superficial voxel somewhere. This time it was a whole cube of extra skin on my upper arm, a few millimeters across. Now I started wondering if voxels could go missing instead of being added - and I started wondering if they could be missing internally. The tests continued. This time I was dropped unceremoniously into a small vat of fluoroantimonic acid - I barely had time to register pain before I chemically ceased to exist. When I woke up, voxels were the first thing I checked for. Nothing on my face, or my arms..... But on my side there was a large raised spot, with right-angled edges. But there was little time to worry about my volumetric resolution - the next test was explosive. Alive again, I looked for voxellation. To my growing concern, it was spreading. Like square tumors, the voxels showed up in patches on my arms, legs, and torso. I hoped they wouldn't reach my..... Higher-resolution areas. After the decompression test, the voxels were in all sorts of places. I started to feel like a combination of human and LEGO. They weren't impeding me in any way, but it was bizarre having irregular rectangular growths all over. They were pretty obvious from even a glance, but the tests continued. Death by rapid incineration. Voxels on my shins. Death by a laser through the heart. Voxels on my back. Death by electrocution. Voxels on my shoulders. I was still functioning perfectly - the voxels didn't seem to be happening to anything inside me. After a while I got used to them - I formed a habit of checking where my voxel patches had randomly generated with each "respawn." Eventually it had to happen. I awoke and found it mechanically difficult to extricate myself from the machine. A cursory examination revealed that my entire exterior surface was voxellated to a resolution of three millimeters. There was a fuss, and argument, and huddled discussion. Eventually someone noticed me standing around being extraordinarily Cartesian and told me to get back into the machine. It was just like dying - at least, like the particularly quick deaths. When I woke up, I had my contours back - you could say my resolution was molecular. It was refreshing not to have to worry about being compared to an old videogame. I did notice I weighed rather less than I seemed to remember - but I decided not to worry about it.

It caught me totally by surprise. I did not expect any resistance, the races of the inhabitants on this blue planet should not suppose any threat to the completion of my mission. But there he was, with a menacing gaze, and a overwhelming presence. I tried to reach for my disintegrating gun, but before I could finish the gesture, he yelled at me: do not even think about it, I do not want to harm you, but if you try to use that gun it will cost you your life. This does not make sense, I said. Who are you? How could you have found me? And How did you manage to interfere with the technology of my starship to stop my attack? why are you here? The answer to those questions is none of your business, but I will tell you that I have been here for a long time as an observer, since one of the races that inhabit this planet has had an unusual and extraordinary evolution, and some of the most important races of the galaxy are Interested on them. You may think on me and the ones as me as observers and guardians, and you can tell to the ones like you that we will not tolerate to you to do them any harm. Usually we are forbidden to use our authentic psychic abilities, but in cases of external invasion we have permission to do so. I will not asi it again, you and your race have been warned. now leave. The majestic creature remained quiet and robust, his eyes assured me that he was not lying, I felt that my life was in danger, if I tried something to attack I would die for sure, maybe also my own race would be in danger. I decided to leave, that creature, unknown to me so far, was obviously too powerful for me and my people. The small but powerful spacecraft disappeared on the horizon. The extremely powerful and intelligent creature stared up at the sky for a few seconds, then, when it felt there was no danger, he sniffed a nearby tree and proceeded to urinate on it. Then the dog returned to his home with his human; the race with which they had chosen to live in this world, while caring for and protecting to the most interesting race of beings that had never existed in the universe before: the dolphins.

A man by the name of Bill was in a self driving car that was driving on the highest road in North America (The Mount Evans Scenic Byway). As it was a very windy road, it was a challenge for his vehicle to maneuver. But that didn't stop Bill from taking the challenge. When he got to a sharp turn near the visitors center, a family was in the middle of the roadway, getting out of their car (albeit not one that was self driving). This presented a challenge, the self driving car had to make a nearly impossible reverse turn if it was able to save both Bill, and the family. However, that was out of the cars reach. Obeying its creator, to protect the most amount of people, the car drove reverse off the mountain. Bill didn't feel the impact, but the family that witnessed the incident did. That's why after the events of that fateful day, they became activists to change the "Cruel technology of robotics" as they put it. Tirelessly, the parents (Who went by the names Adeline and Rob) worked to ensure that the government banned these so called heinous machines. In the process, the public opinion on the issue rose, and was at a solid 60 percent. Fearing that all technology was evil, the majority of Americans took up to the idea of banning technology. The Amish states of America were born. The economy suffered, and the country became a shadow of its former self. As food became scarce, and more and more babies were named Jedidiah, some citizens started to rebel. The Robo States of America were born. The Electramish Conflict has begun.

The problem with personality is that so much of it depends on what happened during your life. There are certain things that change you for better or worse. I wish I could say that all the accumulated knowledge, wisdom and memories stay but each time we start again, it's like a reset on most things. Thomas was having another party according to his Facebook update. I remember the last time I was invited to one, he gave me a list of things to bring and I did, except no one else was there. He gave me the location of a lifeguard tower at the beach that they were at, except it didn't actually exist. I have a flask tucked into my jacket pocket on the chair with the potion that will set my plan into motion if I decide to try again. I'm still not sure if this is what I want to do, raising him again and starting over is an impossibility because he might not even be healthy enough to raise me so that I have a chance of repeating our plans again. The thing is, I'm still not sure about how I feel about not letting him know about his genetic predisposition for heart failure this time. I decided a few tries ago that this had too much of a negative impact whenever I told him, no matter how old he was when I did. Too many times I witnessed him going down the wrong path with drugs because of this. He's in college and happy now, not a care in the world. He has a slight idea of our plan this time even though he suspects it's just a story I used to tell to help him cope with being abandoned by his real parents. I've thought about this and if I really wanted to, I could just let him live normally. I could let him find out on his own. I know he's smart and might even figure something out. Medicine has advanced tremendously since we started. Personally, I feel like I've had enough of this life business but I'm not sure if I should make this choice for him. Maybe I was wrong and I can't reverse engineer what my friend used to be. He looks at me as a father figure and I guess that's understandable, I'm old enough to be his grandfather by now. So I decide to do what my heart tells me is right. I take the flask that I asked my lawyer to mail to me and pour it into my bedpan until the very last drop is gone.

" What do you mean you don't know what you want? " " Well, what've you got to offer? " " I-Well there's... " Lucifer sighed " This isn't how it works! " The man looked on, he could see his brow furrow, his eyes turned skyward as he tried to fathom up a reason for bringing the literal devil to his basement. Lucifer could feel his gnarled hands clenching into fists, the temperature of the room cranking up a few notches as steam began emanating from his pores. He wasn't even supposed to be here, not anymore. Once the human population had started growing rapidly he realised this whole " Babysitting the damned idiots " job was a bit more than a one mildly rebellious fallen angel job. So he'd made a call back upstairs, telling the big G to poof down some more helpers. Despite ' upper management'only sending down what he was pretty sure were the most inept of their already woefully unmotivated workforce, he had managed to rally the ever increasing group together into some semblance of a team, a team whose job was to see to the eternal suffering of every person who ended up down here. But then these deals started coming, at first he simply chose to ignore them, but as he had given most of the hands-on evil to the rest of his team, he admittedly started taking these deals to fill the void moving into management had left him in, it was almost cathartic, these people weren't already consigned to suffering, he could see the process in action. Despite there never being a positive outcome more and more people had started requesting him, to the point where he was pretty much constantly flitting from one deal to the other, he started losing track of who had promised what, and it was beginning to get a bit repetitive, a grind. He had his team take over that as well, although he did still tend to a few personal cases of long term clients. The people at the top had been impressed, and his customer service centre has been ranked as the 2nd most evil currently existing, He had given up on catching Comcast. So, while first confused by Zazuul, his PA, bursting into his office, hands full of blood covered contracts, and explaining they were at capacity, and that they would need everyone taking deals, he was quietly excited. This was a chance to get back into the action, just for a bit. But it wasn't right, the deals just didn't seem the same as before. Normally by the time people had got to ' contract with the devil'levels of desperation they had a pretty clear idea of what they wanted, but no, he was being given the most mundane requests. " My car's backfiring ," " Could you get me some shopping? " and " I think my cat's sick, it was probably the brand of cat food we bought because my wife said we normally get the green cans and I was like ' these are the green cans'but they aren't and I think I might be colour-blind ." How in the name of himself was he supposed to come up with an evil and maniacal solution to a misfed feline? And now this guy. This fucking guy, hadn't even thought of anything. He was still just stood there. The fact he was even respiring enough to make Lucifer begin to flame with rage, the heat from him seemed to bring the half-vegetable half-man back from his photosynthetic state, and cause a warm blast of air to fill the room, billowing the mans robes and sending papers from his basement desk flying off of it. One of these scraps came to rest in front of Lucifer's hooves, and something scrawled upon it caught his eye, the page burned up in his hand before he had even stood up, but it didn't matter, he'd seen what was on it. " How did you get that?! " Lucifer grabbed the man by the front of his robes; the smell of burning fabric filled the room. Despite this the man still seemed fairly unphased, tranquil in his stupidity. " Huh-I don't-aaah! " The smoldering robe caught fire, Lucifer tightened his grip on it. " This is my personal summons! " Real rage was emanating from him now, despite the confined space his voice filled the room like an organ in a church hall. " I personally give this to a very few trusted people, of which I'm certain you aren't one of, where is this from? " Fire was coming from his mouth now too, close enough to lick the now pale cheeks of the man. " I, I really just don't know! I'm sorry! Someone gave me it! " Lucifer could see it in his eyes, he really didn't, great, maybe the next imbecile with a ridiculous deal could shed some light on this. In his rage, and without really thinking, he threw the man across the room. As his victims limp body slid down the opposite wall, Lucifer looked down to his hand, the rest of the man's robe had been scorched away, but within the ash burned a metal symbol, white hot, an instinct and a revelation made him look up to a now enflamed calendar upon the man's wall. Despite the fire, a now gleaming pen-mark could still be seen, circling a day that Lucifer should never have forgotten. With a pounding of one fist into the other, he blinked out of the basement, knowing exactly where he had to go. As he blinked into existence, he saw exactly what he had expected to see. A man, stood solitary in black robes, in the middle of a forest clearing, watch in one hand, blood covered contract in the other. As the man turned to see Lucifer standing behind him, he dropped to his knees, pounding the ground with his fist. " No! " he screamed " So close! " the shout was so extreme it seemed to cast further lines into his already jagged face, being illuminated by Lucifer's own glowing firelight. " You were close, Brian, I'll give you that. " He extended his hand and snatched the contract away from the kneeled man. " But your ability of persuading others runs out today. " He could feel himself physically untense as he saw Brian's watch read fifteen minutes to midnight, plenty of time. " Who was it? Who told you? " " Oh, no one told me ," Lucifer replied, his trademark sneer returning to his face " One of your more idiotic followers left his robes on, and my summons scrawled on a piece of paper. I saw the emblem on it, your emblem, and brought it back here, where I knew you'd be waiting to burn our agreement. " Brian dropped his head, holding it in his wrinkled hands. Lucifer continued, " I know that's a lot to take in, but tell me, how did you do it? The people calling me personally obviously you gave my summons, but what about the rest of my staff? What happened to them? " All of a sudden, Brian lowered his hands and cracked a sly smile " Isn't it obvious? " He looked up at Lucifer, straightening his back. " I published the ritual on the internet. " " The what now? " He hoped this wasn't one of those modern inventions that humanity had a habit of concocting every so often, he had just gotten his head round people getting sent his way for sitting watching a small electric box for most of their lives, if it was up to him sloth would be taken off the list of seven sins, along with pride, that one never made sense. Realising he'd drifted off into his own thoughts, he looked up just in time to see Brian make a grab for the contract, he moved it away, still looking at him for an explanation. Brian slouched back down, seemingly accepting defeat for the final time. " You should probably look it up, it's going to be sending a lot more people your way. " Brian said with a derisive snort of laughter. " Well whatever it is, that plan is still pretty despicable, and it explains all the half-baked ideas from everyone I visited. " " I still can't believe one of my men left his robes on. " He was staring forwards, perplexed. You know, I try and man manage but with some people it just seems completely impossible " Lucifer let a small smile appear across his face " So right, you know when you just feel like ' I have too many staff Brian got to his feet " Completely, how am I supposed to keep everyone in check when I've got tens of people joining a day, not realistic, and I can't find anyone with enough aptitude to hire on as an assistant. " Lucifer was about to agree, when his brow furrowed " Yea... " an idea occurred to him, " Hey...I know I'm supposed to drag you to hell now and everything, but I think I could use more men, well, A man like you downstairs...what do you say? A truly despicable smirk rose across Brian's face, not to dissimilar to the devil's own, and he grabbed Lucifer's hand with an almost inhuman enthusiasm, saying... " You, my good friend, have a deal. " Edit: Grammar

"Two thousand years ago and more, in the time of our Great-Grandparents' ancient ancestors, Ragnar the Bold, first of the ShardBreathers, first discovered the World Heart." The mighty throng stood dead silent and reverential as I spoke. As the words pass by my tongues and fangs I fondly remember my own first time hearing an Elder Shardbreather address the gathered Cohorts in this mannger. The Gods Dome resounds with my voice for the first time, this moment which will be the pinnacle of my mortal life. I am proud, and I am ready. History follows my voice this day. "For centuries, our fate stood just outside our grasp. The many sons of Ragnar died in their times, lives lost to the mysteries of this great puzzle. Today, brothers and sisters, I announce to your that our sacrifices have not been in vain! Today, broodmates, I tell you, the ShardBreathers have conquered the world!" There is murmuring now. "Tell us, brother Osthar, what does this portend?" Chief Tallys stands before me, between the crowd and myself. "Our homes have seen the roofs quake above us and wondered. Entire tribes have been cut off from the Brood, and now you summon us before you to proclaim a victory. Do you claim that the ShardBreathers have caused the roilings that have claimed our kin?" "I do, great chieftain. I do, and I mourn their sacrifice." "And even now, our laborers and beloved slaves toil to free our Broodmates and bring them back to the fold, back to our festivals and our wars, and command us here on fear of the World Heart to listen to this empty talk. Speak, priest! What do you have to tell us?" "Be calm, great chief, and I will explain all." I wait for the murmuring to silence. "Three Floods ago, our brothers have finally shattered the mystery of the World Heart, and it is a great one." At the word "shattered" much of the crowd draws breath. "And while the Heart is well, we now know its' use, and know how to bend it to the will of the ShardBreathers." "To break our homes and slaughter our Kin?" "Silence, interloper! You have said too much in this hallowed space! You will listen or be struck down!" Tallys bares his lower teeth but is silent. "The roilings you have felt are but the birth pangs of the great eggs of conquest that are to be delivered when Eaotem finds her destiny. You all know of the discoveries of our day-seers, those who venture above and see the lights outside our safe caverns. They have told of the ripe lands we can not attain, with prey and fruit and new slaves for our pits and kitchens and playmates. You have heard how these other worlds stand far off, across the vast floods that rush in and refresh our stores. And you have all known how none who venture into the waters to visit have ever returned. Today, that destiny is changed! Today, I tell you, the World Heart has been conquered, and we, its chosen, may bring this small cramped world of ours wherever we please!" "Of all the neighbors that had to come knocking, of course it would be the ugly girl of the party." Lucas looked over at me. "Can you not be an asshole for like, 8 seconds? And give me back the spyglass." "Fine." I slammed the telescope closed and tossed it back to him. I could see the big wet wart skimming closer, inexorably closer by the hour. This one we called "Farthas' Wart" due to it's brutal ugliness, a stone pimple with an apparently omnipresent thundercloud following it every time the Coast Guard saw it floundering in the distance, slowly revolving in the waves. I stretched my claws thoughtfully as Lucas pondered the incoming vessel. "So, what's changed?" "Couldn't tell you. Nobody in the Guard has said anything though, we might be the first to notice. Maybe the priests know something, they've been even cagier than normal lately." "Seems to me that's more likely to mean they don't know anything." "Mayhap." I wandered over to the feed cage and pulled out a grammin. It squealed at me, obviously terrified. "Please, please, nooooooOOOO..." With a wet crunch, it stopped struggling. I spat the skull back out and began eating, closing the cage back with my underpaw to keep the others from trying to escape. I fondly recalled the stories my grandad told, of the time before the priests had blessed them with language, given them a name and the gift of the tongue. Probably a lot less stressful to have dinner that way. "So, we're sure it's actually coming closer?" "I'm sure. You sure?" "Yup." "Then let's get moving. Grab me one and then let the rest go, we need to move fast." I shrug and reach for the cage, holding up a quaking morsel. "Naw, the fat female please. It'll be a long run home." Tallys stands over me. "Give the order, ShardBreather." He holds a slave hostage. A gift from my predecessor, her name is Yessif, which means Fresh Washing, and she is my favorite. "Please, Tallys, might cheiftain. Not my slaves." "Do as I command, Osthar. You have seen me break the others and I will break you if I must. She has need of only one tongue." I gaze at her beautiful face and regret my life. I regret that I did not prepare my allies. I regret that I did not kill Osthar in the Gods Dome when he would not be silenced. I regret that I am bound and wretched and that my brothers are even weaker than I. "I will submit, for the life of the one pledged to me, Mighty Chief. Please, spare my slave. I offer my tongues and my wings to your service." He is appeased. Perhaps disappointed that I did not resist longer, draw out his victory and his sadism, he releases her gently. I close my eyes and weep. "Now, Tallys. Tell me the secrets of the Returned ones. My scouts have been many, and now I learn you have kept them from us. Tell me what they found." "Predators, Osthar. Eaters of live food and killers for sport. They keep no slaves for their appetites allow nothing weaker than themselves except food. Fearsome warriors, they carry weapons that cast darts farther than our spears and fly, and can reach us even on the wing. They are a terrible threat, with but one weakness." "Tell me, ShardBreather. What weakness must my warriors know?" I breathe my secret. "They do not see in the dark." "That was..... gentle." Everyone around us was lying flat on the ground. We had definitely felt it when the spinning black mountain made landfall, but it had slowed down and hit almost a full two days later than we expected. "I think maybe all that work was a bit wasted." For weeks the cities had been shoring up critical buildings, preparing for the shock of landfall. Apparently we needn't have bothered. The great black mountain, now ten leagues away, slowly ground itself to a shuddering halt over the course of the next three hours. "Hope it stops before nightall. Wouldn't want to miss anything." "I think it will, but only just. Probably have time for dinner." We began eating in shifts. The screaming and bawling and weeping were nerve-wracking. Damned priests, couldn't leave well enough alone. I mopped the blood off my paw with my tongue and kept watch. "Hey, look. Something's happening." Sure enough, about halfway down the cliff face, we saw movement, black on black. My eyes twigged to it pretty quickly, though it took my brain a few seconds to get a clear image. "Yup, it's the winged ones. Too bad, the snake-ones were tastier by accounts." We kept guard that night, with the invaders beginning to swarm around the Black Mountain like a flock of seagulls, or a swarm of flies on a dunghill. I went to sleep with a continent above me, blacker than the night around it, and crowned with a thunderhead. We came upon them on the second night. Swooping down from the darkness, low in the tallest mushrooms, we sprang and bit. Tallys struck first, it was well he was chief. I was second, no weakling or oldling. We heard their awful screeches and wails and I felt one of their enormous darts skim off my leg, but then my knives were on him. I bit deep and drank of my enemy. Tallys did not slay his, but skewered it's foot to the soft earth and noosed it, dragging it weeping and with the cracking of bone. "Tormmind, see to the new slave. It is badly hurt." "Yes, ShardBreather." "Beloved, come to me." "Yes, master." I followed Tallys' beckoning to the odd cage before me. Within, many small things like us, but unwinged and small-fanged, cowered. "These are the food-ones?" "Yes, master, they match all descriptions." "Free them, except two I will keep." "Leftior, break open this box." Brother Leftior wedged his spearhaft into the mossy bars and broke the cage handily. "Well done brother. Go and gather reports of the other parties." "Yes ShardBreather." With that, he was off into the clear darkness, lit by the sparkling points of light we had come to adore so quickly. "It is no mystery why those who went outside the floodholes always longed to return to the outside." "No, beloved, it is no mystery." Continued below.

I liked your story but I do have one point to make. The story seems not to be written by a truly immortal creature, because I feel that I understand too much of what he's saying. It's still written by someone who is mortal, because things are too clear. Even though you can attribute to the fact that the bath tub analogy is kind of like an ELI5, it doesn't feel like an all-knowing creature who tries to explain stuff, since it'll end up being way too complex too if such a creature would exist. Nevertheless, great job, your story got me thinking.

It had seemed so perfect. The one goddess who truly understood me, I had thought. The one goddess truly representing me, my teenage self had thought. The one goddess poised to piss my parents of, my teenage emo self had thought. Goddess of monsters, goddess of darkness, goddess of spiders (a surefire way to freak out my mom). And then..... and then it had turned out that Lolth was actually cheerful. Like, urgh. Spiders followed me everywhere, carrying little treats, scaring away my perceived "enemies" (that part was actually quite cool) or shooing me away from "danger." And then there was the knitting. Barely a day passed without me finding knew (and admittedly stylish) spidersilk clothes. It felt like..... it felt like constantly being accompanied by your mom. Have you ever tried dating a girl with a thousand spiders sitting on the table, simultaneously turning their bodies to stare at whoever was speaking right now? Like, urgh. I open my door to step inside. My high school bully is hanging in a net from the ceiling. He screams through his gag as he sees me. I grin. Maybe Lolth isn't so bad after all.

It'd taken years, but I did it. I had passed the New York Bar with flying colors. It took so much of myself, and everyone around me to get to this point, and it's a story I'm a little more willing to share now that all this hooplah is over and done with. My mother.... she worked two jobs trying to provide for my tuition you know? She worked tables in the afternoons, and worked at a call center during dusk work was murder, she would always say..... and true enough, it was. She was raped going home from her call center gig one night. I didn't let it bother me during the time, I was busy preparing for the Bar after all. She would have understood, right? My father, well, he was a different story altogether. He was empty baggage, a crazy drunk that just made everything difficult for everyone. It felt real good telling the old fuck that he was good for nothing. It felt even better when he took his own life. My sister..? Uh. Do I even have one? It must have been years since I've last even thought of her, actually. And now that I actually have the time and inclination to spare her a second thought well, I never bothered getting to know her. Her dying in 911 never bothered me in the slightest. It took a while getting here, you know? But, hey, it was worth it. They all knew it was.

I didn't know her name. We'd never actually even spoken. Still, I'd seen her every night. Ever since I was a child I've always dreamt of the same place. Another world..... fantastic, impossible. Anything I could ever imagine can become a reality there. I've always been the only human, though- up until recently, that is. I'd first caught a glimpse of her as I'd been flying over what I'd named "The Whispering Woods." Not a very creative name, considering the trees actually whispered. I'd been fascinated when I'd first discovered it (or created it? I'm still not sure how some things work there), although the novelty soon wore off as I began to realize that trees don't really have much to say. In the middle of the Whispering Woods was a large pool of unnaturally still water that created a perfect reflection of the sky above it. I'd named it (again, rather uncreatively) "The Mirror Pool." It had immediately caught my eye. Normally the surface would create a pristine mirror of the moon and the stars- however, this time the surface was marred by ripples. I could just make out the silhouette of something splashing around in the water. It didn't look like any of the animals I'd seen before. So far as I could tell, the animals here were the same as they were in the waking world, minus the fear of humans. One of my favourite things about my dream world was the ability to commune with the animals. They treated me as one of their own, and I'd become quite familiar with the denizens of my world. My world..... or so I'd thought. I flew down to take a closer look. Quietly, so as not to disturb whatever it was. I landed silently in the top of a tree and perched like a bird. As I began to realize what it was, I could feel myself blush and my ears burn. It was a woman. She was the most beautiful woman I'd ever seen. She was also completely naked. It caught me so off guard that I fell out of my tree and hit the ground with a thud. I'd never physically hurt myself here, but my ego was quite thoroughly wounded. I silently cursed myself as the woman turned to look at me, completely unabashedly. She made no attempt to cover up; she merely looked at me with the slightest hint of a smile and beckoned me to join her. My ears burned even hotter. Why was I so embarrassed? This was MY dream, after all. I was the only one who was actually here. I stood up and brushed myself off. I walked to the edge of the pool and moved to jump in, but she forestalled me with a look. She glanced at my clothes and raised an eyebrow as if to ask: "Seriously? You're coming in with those?." I blushed again. I wasn't sure if she could see me in the moonlight. I really hoped she couldn't. But really, why did I care anyway? She wasn't real. Instead, I decided to play it cocky. Hey, it's my dream, I can do what I want. I snapped my fingers and my clothes evaporated off of my body in a puff of smoke. She raised her eyebrow again, this time allowing her hint of a smile to blossom in to a wide grin. God, she was beautiful. The moonlight reflected off teeth as white as pearls and turned her eyes in to sparkling emerald pools. Her long, auburn hair cascaded down her back to her waist. Tiny dewdrops sparkled and ran rivulets down her body, winding their way along the gentle curves of her flesh. -cont.

They don't know you exist. You're hiding behind a screen. You are my Frankenstein and you, cursed to only move when looked at. And you are cursed down to your bones, "bones" because you don't have any, to twist your body in painful bends whenever their eyes shine into you. You are forced to contort your being into the twisted souls that stares into you. But you are patient. You listen. Behind your silent pain, you wait. You wait for their backs turned. You wait for that man. His back turned. Why is he stupid enough to turn away from you, and walk backwards into the mirror? I can't see a reason you have a chance. He has no reason to slide his back down the mirror. I watched the hunger grow and glow red in your amorphous black. He has no reason to take a further step back. But he does. Humans, I forgot, I assumed, I stiffened. Humans trust, and humans don't need reasons. His back collides against you, apart from the layer of glass, the slim silver. And down he slides. That instant, you striked. The laser red from your eyes now shone from his. And in that instant mirror, a confused, hungry grey brewed. I took a step back. I lost count. How many of you have I cursed?

The explorer delved further into the cave, torchlight flickering off the sandstone walls. He ran his fingers across this ancient stone, feeling every crack and crevice. As he went further in, he could feel a refreshing breeze blowing through. Shocked by the cool air on his face, he pressed deeper into the cave system, torch raised and gun at the ready. He followed the wind, leading him deeper into the earth. He could hear the clank of metal on metal, the burst of flame and the call of voices. He ran towards the sound, emerging into a vast cave, filled with buildings and people. Light filtered down from the surface as hundreds of people busying themselves with tasks. Workmen built structures out of shimmering metals, people flew through the air to get to destinations and the streets of this subterranean city bustled with a thousand tongues. The explorer fumbled for his bag, grabbing his sketch pad and scribbled down notes. Citizens then started to notice the explorer, his primitive light source and writing implements clashing with the futuristic tech of the cave people. Noticing that he had disturbed this underground metropolis, the explorer scrambled to his feet, trying to escape. He ran straight into a group of giant guards, dressed in glorious armour, who were blocking the exit. They looked down at the puny man, mumbling to each other in languages unheard of by surface dwellers. 'Stay back savages!' The explorer whimpered, pointing his measly gun at the guards. They looked to each other, eyes rolling. 'Great, we've got ourselves another Englishman.' The lead guard said, looking down at the quivering figure. He took a step towards the explorer. 'I said stay back!' He yelped, backing himself towards the outcropping's edge. The guard extended a hand in peace. 'Put the weapon away, we mean you no harm.' The explorer looked at the hand, then back to the guard. He clutched it hastily, getting to his feet.'You see, we don't want to hurt you, contrary to what you write about us?' 'How can you speak English? How can you read? You can let alone build a house on the surface?' The explorer answered, dusting himself down. 'You see, it is that kind of attitude which makes us hide our cities from you. We aren't all savage beasts, none of us are actually.' The guard said, gesturing to his city and fellow people.'If you would like to see our knowledge, you are more than welcome.' The explorer nodded, still flabbergasted by the scenes around him.'Very well then, come with us. Just one thing, you can not tell anyone about our cities or technology just yet. We would like to keep some of Africa ours, thank you.'

(I sort of took my own inspiration from this, but it's close.) " Come on..... move, you can do it. " A soft voice whispered. The mighty wizard Totaz was on his knees beside a well loved stuffed bunny. It was a dull pink color with two miss matching button eyes and some stitches where it once popped open then previously. A featureless paw twitched then started to move a little more, the other paw followed along with it's head, looking this way and that. " Aahh? haa? " Totaz let out a chuckle. " Ah, It wor- " " p..... paaa..pa? " He stopped breathing in that moment, smile gone and starring down at the bunny like it had turned into something else. " Pa..... pa..... " He shook his head and quickly smiled again. " N-no. Not quite..... I'm afraid I'm not a papa to anyone anymore. Hah..... " He used the overly large sleeve of his robe to wipe away a few tears and held out a hand to the bunny. " Come..... let's see if you can stand on those wobbly legs " Decades ago a mighty wizard gave life and sentience to a doll. Now, the wizard has finally died of old age and the doll is wondering: "Why can't I fix him? He appears unharmed so why can't I repair him?" Mr. Flopsy pushed against his masters head once more. " Wake up. Please wake up. I want to go to the garden again! You have a lot to do today! " There was no response and his skin was getting colder. " Master..... papa..... " He pulled himself away from the body and looked to the mirror where he has seen Totaz speak with others. He started running there, ears flopping around and nearly tripping him as he ran. Once he made it to the mirror he hit it with his near useless paws. " Hey, help! My master! He needs help! " The mirror shined white then a lady appeared. " What is your emergency? " She asked, then paused, looking around then down, seeing just the bunny. " My master, he's not waking. Please, if he doesn't wake he'll be late to seeing his friend. " The lady just stared for a moment then nodded. " Ah..... alright we're sending someone to your location right now. Can you check some things for me? " The Mr. Flopsy nodded then talked to the lady for a while, getting his masters heart rate, seeing if he was breathing, checking his temperature. There was a knock at the door before long and two men came in with a stretcher and black bag. " You're here! " Flopsy ran over to the men, hopping in place, seeming happy. " You'll help him right? He's been asleep too long. " The two men looked at each-other then one mumbled'I'll do it.' " I'm sorry but..... your..... uh..... maker. He's gone. " " What do you mean? He's right here. " Flopsy pointed at him, thinking that maybe one was blind. " Sorry, wrong words. He's..... dead. " ....." Dead? " The word was new to Flopsy and the man trying to talk to him could see that. " He's not waking up..... ever. " " What..... No. No he hast to wake up! " Flopsy ran over to his maker, pushing against the black bag now surrounding him. " Your not dead, you're just sleeping! Wake up, Wake up! " The one putting the body away tried to close the bag but Flopsy got in the way, putting both paws over his masters face. " No! He won't be able to breath. He's claustrophobic! " " Can you grab him? " One asked. " Yeah. " He moved and gently picked up the bunny. " No! Stop! " Flopsy struggled against the man's hands, trying to get away but with no luck. He closed the bag around Totaz and lifted up the stretcher with him on it. " Please..... stop. " The man holding Flopsy carried him to a table, setting the bunny down. " Listen..... uh. What's your name? " " Flopsy..... " " Listen, Flopsy..... I know this is hard to understand but this is what happens when people get too old. We die, and well, that's it for us. " " That's stupid. I don't like this. " " Yeah. I know. Hey, I got to help my partner outside, can you wait here for a moment. " Flopsy nodded. The man smiled and patted Flopsy's head, heading outside. When he returned the bunny was gone. " Flopsy? "

My part was picking up a pencil. Simple as that. Because I picked up the pencil, the person somewhere behind me in the hallway, who would achieve lasting world peace later in life, didn't slip and break their neck. Because I picked up that pencil, I was able to give it to a peer, who would share it with others until the person who would grow up to find the cure to cancer received and kept the pencil. It's pretty cool that the one small action amounted to a cure to cancer and world peace. Still, it would've been cooler if I was the person to find the cure to cancer.

Dan told them he didn't want a cake for my birthday. He didn't like his co-workers very much, and have no need for them to acknowledge that he was getting a year older. Of course they didn't listen, and he got stuck listening to 30 voices singing an awful rendition of "Happy Birthday" while they bought out a cake lit up with candles. "Make a wish, but don't tell anyone or it won't come true!!" His mouth acted before his brain could stop it. "I WISH I DID N'T HAVE TO INTERACT WITH IDIOTS LIKE YOU ON A DAILY BASIS. HOW CAN ALL OF YOU BE SO FUCKING STUPID? I WISH EVERY ONE OF YOU STUPID PEOPLE EVERYWHERE WOULD JUST GET FUCKING SMARTER SO I DO N'T HAVE TO INTERACT WITH YOU CRETINS EVERY DAMN DAY." What our surly friend Dan did not realize was that birthday wishes sometimes become reality, but only when spoken aloud and it was very rare. The opposite saying had been put into practice so that people wouldn't be able to utilize the special power they could possibly possess once a year. He had no clue anything had changed until he showed up to work the day after his tirade. His boss called him into his office, and Dan thought he was getting fired for sure. At this point he barely cared about losing the job; he just didn't want the axe to come down from this blithering idiot in middle management. "How are you feeling today, Dan? Were you able to get past the melancholy of yesterday so that we don't have any further diatribes from you?" "You're not angry about what I said?" Dan asked, pleased that he hadn't been fired but confused that his boss had just uttered two coherent sentences back to back. This was a first for him. "I thought a lot about what you said yesterday Dan, and you were right. We had an early staff meeting this morning, and we came to the conclusion we could very easily handle your job amongst ourselves and keep the extra money while increasing production at the same time." Dan wanted a witty comeback in the moment, but he was too confused to come up with anything. His boss was never anything resembling an intellectual but he sounded like a different person today. "I'm a specialist in the field. You can't just replace me that easy, and certainly not with some of the idiots here." Dan said with more than a hint of arrogance. "That would have been true yesterday, but today is a new day. You wished for all the stupid people to get smarter, it came true, and there were so many of us. You have made the world a much better place." "Hold on. What do you mean'my wish came true'?" Dan asked, trying to wrap his mind around all of this. "So all the stupid people everywhere are now smart?" His boss smiled a huge grin and nodded affirmatively. "You got it." "So I don't have to deal with my department being full of idiots anymore? This could make work a lot more pleasant." Dan smiled with him at the thought of no more dumbasses to get in his way. "Well, it isn't exactly your department anymore." His boss replied, still smiling but with a serious tone. "We had a staff meeting early this morning and we are putting Bill from the mail room in charge of your department now. We no longer have use for you there." "Bill? The guy who drools on himself all the time? How in the fuck are you gon na give him my job?" Dan asked, his short temper flaring again. "That guy taught himself 2 languages in the past 24 hours and could now do your job in his sleep. As he was exceptionally stupid before, your wish helped him even more than most. He is a brilliant man now, all thanks to you." "So, for helping everyone out I'm getting fired?" Dan asked, still in a bit of shock. His boss shrugged his shoulders, reached behind his desk, and picked up a broom. "We could use a janitor. That's about all you're qualified for here."

"I would find your tenacity inspiring, if it were not so pathetically futile. How far did you travel in your sad attempt for revenge? One? Two light years? Three at most. And for what?" I see the blinking light behind her eyes, the obvious sign of Valaxxian laughter. The synthesizer's monotone and robotic voice only adds to the words' sting. I grit my teeth and continue my ascent. The reactor is so close. "I have traveled seventy light years myself. A number that is nothing compared to the Valaxxian Empire. Your measly distance is the pinnacle of your species. An achievement gained on the backs of better creatures. My people out class yours in every way." Fifty more meters to go. I clutch the rungs of the ladder with my left hand and stare at plexiglass jar in my right. The small red droplets casually float around in zero gravity, slowly gathering together into larger droplets until reaching critical mass. A particularly large one shakes before violently separating into a billion tiny pieces. The other pieces delicately swirl out of the way of the new comers, repelled by the temporary like charge. The charge slowly fades and the pieces begin to swirl and clump due to their own gravity. The process begins again. The commander's voice snaps me back to reality. "Your people are gone dwarf. Consumed by their own arrogance. We gave them an ultimatum and they foolishly thought that they could resist our might. You were on the far post when it happened. Would you like me to describe it?" I can feel the anger grow inside of me. Ten more rungs and I will reach the reactor. My resolve has never been greater. "I saw the blast with my own eyes. Something that would have burned your vision. I felt the shockwaves upon my scales, something that would have torn you asunder." The fuel rods slide into view. This dose of radiation would be lethal at ten minutes in full gear. I only had a rebreather. I quickly push the jar down the open shaft, inertia would take it down to the core. Activating the valve, I watch the fuel rods descend. The rector was too loud for me to hear the crunch of the jar breaking but I know the red mercury has been released due to the contamination lights flashing. The alarm did not sound. Disabling that had been step one. "I have recordings of it. The supernova that took everything from you. Such a brilliant thing, the death of a star. It is a glorious send off. There is no better way to have such a wondrous thing as a star die. The life giver becomes the single most destructive force imaginable. All great stars supernova, the lesser ones consume and become black holes. You should be honored. Your star would have grown dull and sputtered out like a sad little candle, leaving no mark. Neither bright not dark, just sad remains. That's what your civilization was destined for. We gave it something better in death." My fingers deftly tap away as I input the override commands. This was the moment I had prepared for an entire year. Every waking second of the trip here had been in preparation for this moment. The mental fortitude to resist their invasive minds had been the hardest. "You humans are not so grand. What happens when you die? Nothing. You burn up along with your sad blue planet. Eclipsed entirely by giants. You never had a place in this universe. So tell me, dwarf, what do you have to say for yourself. What are your final words. The final words of the human race? What would you call your death? "Syria'th lika tal holt." The ship AI announces the message as it accepts my commands. The sounds are strange to my ears, true Valaxxian speech is airy, the result of three voice boxes. But I understand. I memorized those words so I would know when the deed was done. The blinking in her eyes is gone. A dull blue denotes rage. "Coordinates locked, accelerator engaged." I repeat the announcement in human tongue for emphasis. My eyes meet all four of hers. The mental image of herself that she has been projecting in my mind flickers. She's losing her concentration. I smile as I think of Salrius IV. The Valaxxian sun, a massive star near the center of the galaxy. I know she can see it in my mind. "Your right. Humans do not explode into a glorious supernova upon death. We don't have a fancy name for it. Its happened so much we didn't need a name for it. Death was everywhere, an unspoken constant. But like we warned you when you gave us the ultimatum, our death is unique. It has a quality that no other death has, not even a supernova. A long time ago a man said'Give me liberty or give me death.' You see that's the thing about human death. We didn't give it a name because it has something else. It has meaning. In death we become something more than we were. Human life is struggle, something you Valaxxites know little of, having been cradled in the care of those before you. In death that struggle becomes something real." I grip the sides of my head and concentrate, making sure she maintains the connection. "And one more thing, humans never die alone. We always take something along for the ride. I guess if you really want a name for the death of the human race, I'd call it the last thing the Valaxxian Empire ever did!" I could see the ship speeding toward the Valaxxian home world as her thoughts shifted from projecting herself in my mind to involuntarily picturing the death of her species. Solarius IV is big enough to set off a chain reaction. A scene of countess supernovae engulfing the galaxy plays out in her mind and so I see it too. "Do you have a name for the death of the Valaxxian Empire?"

For as long as I can remember, people have always told me I'm so sweet, such a caring person, and I am. My grandma especially thinks there's no one in the world as sweet and darling as me, you know how grandparents are. I'd do anything for them, for all of my family and friends and they know that. Then today happened. I'm still trying to process what I did, figure out how I could have handled it better, maybe. It just happened and it went wrong, too fast for me to think it over. The day started out just like any other, nothing unusual, I got up, did my morning stuff and then decided to go into town. I was running some errands and I went to the dollar store to pick up a few things, still nothing unusual. Just as I was done shopping and about to head to the register, I saw an old friend I hadn't seen in a few years and we stopped to talk. She began telling me this elaborate, sad, "down on my luck" story (I don't know how else to describe it), after listening long enough to be polite and a few ignored attempts to speak, I just began to try to remove myself from the conversation. This only proved to be as difficult as trying to talk to her. She seemed to be trying to trap me and did not want to let me get past her in the aisle. Her buggy had somehow ended up crooked in the aisle, with only a small space between it and the shelf, where she had planted herself and showed no signs of moving. Now, as I've said, I'm a nice person, but I feel that other people should be nice and considerate also and at the moment, she wasn't being those at all. So, I smiled my biggest smile and began backing up, the only way I could go, pulling my buggy back with me. This action caused a slight pause in her steady stream of words, the first pause and I took advantage of it. "It was great to see you! I hope you're doing better, I'm sure I'll see you soon. I'm around all the time," the smile never left my face as I said this and I turned my buggy around to retreat faster. "You're looking really good, too." I threw this one over my shoulder as I began to walk to the opposite end of the aisle. No fucking luck. She was behind me before I made it around the corner to the next aisle. And that's when it happened. You know the story, you've heard it before, it's always just a slightly different version of the same damn story, all that changes is the part wrong with their car and why they can't fix it right now. Then comes the fucking question, "Could you just give me a ride?" Then the other same story, I just really need to go here and if you can take me by such and such I can get some gas money for you. I really need to pick up my kid, my boyfriend, my mother..... anything to pull at the heart strings. I'm a nice person and I'm having trouble just saying no. What if her kid really is somewhere and needs to picked up? That's my reason for agreeing to give her a ride, there's a child involved and they aren't where they need to be. Next thing I know, we're in my car and have made two stops, no child at either stop and no gas money either. I got to see her lovely white trash boyfriend that she got into an argument with immediately. That was fun. Of course, his car is another version of that same story. At this point, I'm not exactly happy to be driving her and ready to be done with it all. "Ok, where's your daughter? Don't you need to pick her up from somewhere?" I ask as soon as we're back in the car and on the road. Her answer made my heart beat faster, my hands clenched the steering wheel so hard my knuckles turned white and I felt my face get hot. I knew it had turned beet red. She didn't need to pick up her daughter, I must have misunderstood her. The casual way she said this, the little laugh at the end, made my blood boil. Her ride was over. However, as I was just about to pull over on the side of the road and make her get out, I had a moment of clarity. We were still pretty close to her trashy boyfriends place and I wanted to make this bitch walk. The road we were on was perfect too, outside of town and deserted. It was going to be dark soon and there no street lights, I couldn't have found a better road if I had tried. I drove silently for another mile and a half, until I found a good spot to stop and pulled over. I slammed it in park, killed the car, taking my keys and jumped out, popping my trunk as I walked around to the back. In my trunk I dug around until I found my tire iron, I didn't know what this chick was going to do when she found out what was happening and I wanted to avoid an altercation if possible. If she decided to jump on me though, I wanted to be able to defend myself. I walked around and opened the passenger door, stepping back out of arms reach but holding the tire iron where it was plainly visible. "Alright, ride's over. You need to get out of my car. Right fucking now," I told her as she stared at me stupidly. Oh, she tried to argue with me, tried to act like she hadn't done anything, but I wasn't having any of that. I was done. And I told her that. It fucking sucked getting her to get out of that seat, she didn't want to budge but she finally did. Apparently I pissed her off enough that she decided to get out and try to take a swing at me. Dumb ass, I blocked her punch with my tire iron then just bopped her on the side of the head with it. She stumbled and fell in the gravel on the side of the road as I ran to my car, jumped in and took off. I'm sure she's fine. But maybe I'm not as nice as I like to think I am. I've got some thinking to do.

Snap The fire crackles before us. Who knows where we are anymore. I glace up to the face of my uncle, dimly illuminated by the fire. He's studying me. I don't particularly want to ponder greater truths at the moment. His gaze is unwavering. I sigh, and look up at the stars. Crack Other than the sound of the fire, silence. As I keep my gaze fixed on the night sky, my vision slowly adjusts to the dimness, and more and more stars come into view. "Stars are beautiful in their life as well. Men, not so much. As much as we try to make ourselves look beautiful, we never compare to the raw energy of the universe." Uncle nodded. He looked old. We'd been on the run for days. As far as we knew, we were the only humans left for miles. The fire was risky, but we were hungry. Snap That wasn't the fire. I looked over to the source of the sound, rising. I raised the hand sickle that we found in an abandoned farmhouse and had been using as a sword. "They found us." Uncle rose to his feet as well. He had our pistol, only a few rounds remaining. "I think you're right about the stars. They're so grand, so magnificent, so important. " "Uncle, we don't have time to ponder philosophy" He sighed. "No, we don't" Did I not have enough time, or was my shock just to much to move when the barrel leveled with my eyes?
