Tommy gasped, "I never thought these were real" he frantically typed back "I think your gorgeous." "Thank god I'd just about given up hope, my names Amanda, I live just around the corner, send me your address and I'll come over." Tommy panicked and shut his laptop quickly, this was surely dark forces at work, why would any woman want to talk to him? He finished his last beer and slowly fell into a stupor. The next morning Tommy opened his laptop, having forgotten the events of the night before he checked his email. Nothing, as usual, except a few marketing emails and one email from a Congolese general promising him 13 million dollars if he would provide his bank details. Today's the day he thought, I'm going to fucking do it, this world never loved me and I never loved it, who would miss me anyway. As he got up, he noticed a second email from the same Congolese scamster. He tentatively opened it "Tommy, please why won't you take my money? We desperately want you to have it." Fuck it, Tommy thought to himself, if I'm going to end it this pathetic cunt can have my bank details and the 38 dollars if he so wants. He sent the necessary details and went into his garage. Tommy lowered the garage door, entered his car, lowered the window and started his engine. As he began to grow dizzy from the fumes of the car he felt his phone buzz in his pocket. "You have a new notification from Natwest, a deposit has been made in your account." Dizzy and coughing he opened his account and stared down in disbelief as his bank balance read 13,000,038. He coughed and spluttered and with his final breaths cursed his lack of faith in internet spam. The world was not such a bad place, there may have actually been 38 MILFS within his town who wanted to sleep with him. That girl Amanda was likely telling the truth and all the African princes and generals he doubted, oh what a fool he'd been. As his vision went dark, he realised this was the final cruel twist of irony in his miserable existence. As Tommy awoke on the garage floor several hours later, with the garage door open and a fireman shaking him awake, he realised for the second time in his life a hybrid car had saved his life.

I came home, threw the keys on the couch, and began to strip off my shirt. I couldn't even notice the greasy McDonald's smell anymore, I just felt gross and needed to change. After I checked to make sure the glass I wanted didn't have any stray hairs from my dog, Nina, I twisted the knob to the sink and poured myself a glass with the sprayer. I don't know why, it's something I like to do, ever since I was a kid. I chugged, flipped on the light, and almost dropped the glass when I saw a huddled figure in the doorway. Her hair was long, brown, and covering her naked body. She made no moves, didn't look at me, just sat, staring ahead and taking quick breaths. "He..... hello?" I said. Nothing. "Can I help you?" She tilted her head finally, cocking it to one side and back. I spoke again. "Are you hurt? Can you walk?" The girl met my eyes, grinning, expecting something. I grabbed a blanket from the back of the couch, not turning my back to her, and draped it around her quickly. I asked again. "Can you walk?" There was no reaction from her until the last word. "Waaaaalk?" I said, watching her tilt her head the further I held the word out. Why, why did this feel so familiar? "Can you speak?" She coughed loudly. "Speeeaaak?" She coughed again. I held my breath. No, no it couldn't be. "Nina?" I asked. She looked up at her name. "Edward?"

The vessel was frozen in ice like an insect in blue amber. It hovered there, impossibly, the twists and cracks in the ice distorting the image, it could have been a hologram, or a mirage, or something. We knew we had to get to it. Days of drilling, chipping, we had it out. We open the top hatch and lowered ourselves down, braced to find frozen Nazis preserved since nineteen forty-something. There were no Nazis. There was hardly anything in that submarine. Clean walls, clear counters, no technology that we could see. I'm a biologist, not a computer scientist, but I know what the inside of a mid-century sub should look like - at least a little bit of an idea. Wait - there is a console at the front. Two square pads on an otherwise blank dash. I know, somehow, that they are meant for hands. I place my hands on the pads and the cabin glows red. The wall in front of me becomes a screen, and my eyes snap shut. I can feel inside myself, my will, my fear, my gaze is turned inward. I can't move my hands. The men behind me must see me frozen in place, I hear them come over to see what's wrong. I hear sharp breaths and I struggle to open my eyes and I see the screen. My heart stops beating. Adolf Hitler is staring out at me. I hear words in my head, German, but somehow they become English. " The Third Reich will rise again. You have found the backup plan, the way to restore the Aryan people to glory, should I fail. You have only to align your will, the will of the Superior Race, with the technology before you, and our Empire will extend to the edges of the world. " The screen is blank and no one speaks. I feel a surge of darkness through my body, my eyebrows furrow, all the worst in me rises to the surface. The men around me are yelling, I hardly hear them. The screen now shows the outside of the sub. We are descending: dive, dive. My mind is working furiously, something in the sub is aiding me. I have never felt power like this. I have never felt so alive. My mind is unlocked. I don't know where we're going, but I don't care, as long as I get to feel this way some more. As long as I get to stay this way. The ocean is dark outside and we are moving forward, towards something inevitable. The hair on the back of my neck stands up and I grin. Heil Hitler.

It is hard to be a supervisor in the death division. People think I have it easy because, mainly, my job is to oversee all the death agents in my unit, receive reports on their assignments, and according to those reports, create performance charts and submit their results. Excluding me, my unit consists of two agents. It is one of the smallest ones. We are known as the incomplete unit, but we have always been efficient at what we do, so my superiors overlook the fact that we are missing one more member. Throughout the eons of my existence, we have never had an issue. I must repeat never. Until now. The reason is this new agent beside me. A Shinigami. A clumsy apprentice from the Japanese Branch. And I, for the first time ever, am getting yelled at by my superiors. The Sovereigns. It might sound absurd, but the only thing I can think of is a stain on my pristine record! " You only had ONE job. " Their conjoint reprimand upsets my world. They compress me; I become a minuscule creature, barely living, hardly conscious. Their presence is everywhere and nowhere at once. My office reverberates with Their shared displeasure. An eternity passes in an instant and the blame deposited on me thickens, morphing into a weight that threatens to annihilate all that I am and ever was. I suppose I will not have to worry about a stain. In most cases, demotion is equal to imminent expiration. For this failure I might be demoted, I realize. But my real job, I believe, is to protect my subordinates, and that is what I'm doing. I look at the agent, the rookie Shinigami, behind me and he is certainly ready to expire on the spot. His bright brown eyes are wide, his face pale, his lips ajar - his impetuous disposition disintegrating beneath the judging eyes of true Gods - I have not seen him like this before, quailing as though he is experiencing an apocalypse. He is not a frail human anymore, and yet, he insists on acting like one. An Angel must always be composed. Though he is green still, he shows promise. He could grow to be a good supervisor. He has to be spared. How old is he again? Two hundred? He is but a child. A simple assignment: the retrieval of Gabriel's silver scroll at the Lands of Ebon. However, what can a supervisor do when an agent under their care departs with an assignment without authorization and the development of the aforesaid assignment degenerates into a catastrophe? Here I am. This is my duty. I am not an Archangel. Just another overworked Angel of Death. To protect. To protect - " Please!! " A young voice screams. No! You foolish child! " Blame's on me. Supervisor Isayel told me not to go! I disobeyed. " The child steps forwards to stand beside me with shaking legs. Waves of preternatural heat redden and blister his skin as boiling beads of perspiration drench his ensemble. " It should be me; the one punished for my insolence. " The child lets himself fall to the floor; he kowtows. His voice rings with resolve. The strength powering the words regress me to a certain happening in my infancy. Once, I heard The Supreme Guardian, Michael, speak. ' Protect. Defend and protect the wandering wounded.' Even Archangels would not display such audacity and mettle, at least not the ones born or groomed in this era. This strength feels ancient. What is this child? " Very well. " I gasp. I must be insane because I breathe out, " this child does not know what he is doing. " I implore, " Mercy. Please. " Stillness follows my interruption. I ignore the angry stare the rookie directs at me. Nature might have rebelled once more against mankind, succeeded in extinguishing any trace, and revived all living species during the lapse of time it took for this brutal heat to abate and turn into fond and forgiving warmth.

Vanya looked around the simple room and then at the dying fire in the grate. It was the last of their wood. He picked at nothing on the worn table in front of him, feeling ashamed. His wife cleared her throat. "What will we do for heat tomorrow? There's no more?" Vanya couldn't bear to look at her. His voice came out hoarse. "Muffin." "Yes?" Vanya frowned, "No, not you my sweet, there's muffin." "Oh." The fire spat a dying spit. "What about Herr Muffin?" his wife asked tentatively. "He was so kind to us last week." Vanya shook his head. "Muffin's got muffin. Or so he says." He felt a deep pain that his wife might leave him for Muffin. He knew jealousy well, knew that Muffin was sniffing around but it might only be muffin. His wife sighed. "Muffin." "Yes?" Vanya asked. "No, not you. Muffin." "Oh." The burnt wood gave up its last. Vanya whispered, "Is there muffin to eat?" "Muffin," his wife whispered back, "there's muffin except that nothing you're picking at." Vanya stared at the almost nothing-muffinness in his hand. He threw the crumbs into dark embers. With a shaking heart, Vanya looked at his wife of 32 years and cried loudly, "Muffin, I can give you only muffin it seems. Go to Muffin if you must and be well!" His wife cried back. "Muffin, Muffin's muffin!" The embers cooled to muffin.

When attempting to lose someone the best place to hide is within a crowd, blending in with the other people going about their day. So of course when Thomas saw the crowd of people forming down a side street he didn't think twice about joining them and being led away, far from the murderous glare of the man whose wife he had just slept with (In his defence she did say she was single....). Heading down into what appeared to be the basement of a pub he could hear the sound of shouting from further ahead. As he rounded the corner he saw a man, bloodied and bruised, get thrown back into a ring of people where another man, slightly less beaten, was ready with a straight jab that sent the man down for the count. "And we have our first winner of our elimination open ladies and gentlemen, give it up for Mr. Steven Lyons" A cheer went up from the ring of onlookers, the victor in the centre having his hand hoisted in the air by a short man who had apparently just been speaking. Thomas wasn't sure what he had stumbled in on but frankly he didn't want anything else to do with it. He barely had turned and put a foot forward before someone had grabbed his shoulder. Looking up he could see a man much bulkier than himself, clean shaven with scruffy black hair, and a wide grin that stood out more due to the fact that one of his front teeth was missing. "Hey Chris, it looks like we've got a quitter over here!" The large man exclaimed to the rest of the room. At this point the rest of the room's attention was now on Thomas, who squirmed ever so slightly at the amount of people staring. The small, and may it be said, slightly rotund man MCing for the evening gained a devilish smirk on his small pudgy face. "That's not a quitter you've got there, that's our next fighter." The small bellowed across the room. As if on queue the room took great delight in manhandling their next contestant until he was smack dab in the middle of them. He looked around fearfully, he didn't want to fight anyone here, not so much because he was against fighting but more the fact that most of them looked like they would squash him, literally. His fears were interrupted however when more noise erupted from near the doorway and another man was thrust into the centre of the ring. It seems he wasn't the only one who had decided they'd seen enough and wanted out early. "Ladies and Gentleman, it seems for our second match we have two men who don't fully understand how the rules work here, here you don't get too leave until either the event is over, or you've won a match. Want to leave early? Win your freedom here and now. Hell we've even gone easy on you both." By the end the small man was laughing to himself, though was quickly joined by the gathering crowd, interested to see what would happen when you put the equivalents of a rabbit against a mouse. Looking at his opponent Thomas could see why he had wanted to leave early, a small frame and a fearful look in his eyes it was clear that much like himself he'd wandered in here unaware of the purpose of this establishment. Now Thomas wasn't much better to be fair, slightly stockier due to the manual labour his part time job required he should stand a better chance. The only problem was, Thomas had never thrown a punch before. Hell he'd never even attempted to, violence wasn't something that he was accustomed to, any problems he'd had in the past was sorted out through words like civilised folk. "No time like the present. Fight!" The small man shouted as he backed into the crowd. Thomas looked up from where he'd disappeared ready to move at the slightest of movement, only to see his opponent do the same. They stared at each other waiting for the other to move. At the boos and jeers of the crowd they started to move, slowly circling round each other, neither of them holding up a guard or a fist ready to strike, just..... watching. The jeers from the crowd got louder as they soon realised that neither men would actually throw the first punch. Cries of'Sissies!','Do something!', and'Punch him!' rang from the circle, one man could be noted turning to the organiser Chris and remarking with some mirth in his voice'Who let these guys in the tournament? They're awful'. Eventually one particularly impatient gentleman decided to speed things along, and with an almighty shove Thomas was thrust forward at his opponent. Now what he lacked in size, the timid man apparently made up in speed, as he hastily dodged to the side of Thomas' impromptu charge. Regaining his bearings, Thomas decided to push his advantage and take a wild swing at his spooked opponent, however it was not quite wild enough and it was once again backed away from. Over extended and off balance as he was it was the perfect chance for Thomas' opponent to counter attack with a flurry of punches. Weak and sloppy punches mind, as Thomas realised when one connected with his jaw. Still from never being hit before the shock of getting punched in the face seemed to be a wake up call for Thomas. As the next punch came in Thomas stepped aside and grabbed the offending limb, pulling it forward and sending his opponent sprawling onto the floor. This elected a cheer from the crowd as some action was finally happening. Scrambling to his feet the mousey man turned ready to face Thomas once more, yet again without a guard. This came to be his final error as Thomas landed a clean shot to the man's nose, breaking it and causing blood to start trickling down, as he collapsed lifeless to the floor. As suddenly as he had disappeared the small man from earlier reappeared grabbing Thomas' hand and raising it in the air. "Well, he may have started off weak but came out with a strong finish, give it up for..." The small man dragged Thomas closer to whisper in his ear "What's your name kid?" "uhh, Thomas" was the shaky reply, still unsure of what he'd actually done to the smaller man lying prone on the floor. "Give it up for Thomas everyone!" The announcer shouted as the crowd began to holler and cheer. Thomas didn't really think as he walked away from the crowd of people, away from the man who still was unmoving on the floor of the ring of people, up the stairs and out into the fresh air. Once outside however, he looked back at the entranceway of the place he just left, he looked down at the blood that had splattered onto his crinkled white shirt, and he ran. He ran as far from there as he could, wishing never to see that place again.

Did that really happen? I knew it was coming, I was prepared for years, yet I still was panicking and stumbled over my words. That portal started closing immediately after it opened. Stocks, disasters and preventable wars. I had managed to fit that part of the message into a careful selection of words and ideas. I had unlimited power in my hands. I had a good 30 seconds left to fill it with any number of selfish and personal things I could have changed. My personal obligation to the world was done. About Vicky, how she tore our heart out. About Carlos, that backstabber. That summer with the red bike. I still have the scar. And yet, I stood there and said nothing. I thought I could change it. But I froze. At least, that's what I remember. That older me standing there. Just looking. Trying to form words. Spouting gibberish. That's what I remember. I thought I could change it. But then when the time came, I understood. If I changed things maybe this glimpse wouldn't happen. Maybe I would be different. Maybe it everything that happens is meant to happen and there's nothing I can do about it. Maybe the only function of this event was to cherish the moment. So there I stood, the same frozen statue that couldn't utter out a single comprehensive thing. I hope this young me didn't hate me like I hated the future me I saw the glimpse. But I knew the truth. He does resent me. And only when he gets to my point in time will he understand.

Everyone played the game, it was like the new.... the new.... whats that old popular first-person shooter called again? Oh yea, Call Of Duty, I loved playing that for hours on end, wasting weekends away behind the controller of a silly game. It felt empowering to be able to have 30 kill-streaks and rack up thousands of points.... Where was I again? Oh yea, Merlin. Everyone plays Merlin, its the new Call of Duty. Even though the gear is an expensive 800 and could fill up a small bedroom, everyone still played it for hours and hours on end, just like the old game. But this game was different. You were literally immerses you into this new world of bloody war and the same concept of murdering other people to rack up points, fake points and fake people of course, but slowly progressing to more and more to real war and real people. Every move you made within this large black frame was recorded, an invisible light projected from over 50 projectors built in the frame. All you had to do to see the new world around you was put on a pair of ski-goggle like glasses. Soon I was up the leader boards, 6th ranking player of all time, while playing Merlin at least 6 hours every day. I'd get up an hour or two early just to meet my daily score to keep myself on the leader boards. Weekends were wasted, chips and soda were consumed at alarming rates, and I even turned down a family dinner because some asshole beat my score and bumped me down to 9th on the worldwide leader boards. I knew this game was spiraling out of control but it wasn't until I had my first night terror did I realize the effect. After a 16-hour long Saturday Merlin-a-thon I decided to hit the sack. Turning off the controls felt like I was already losing my 6th place spot. After a shower and some food, I went to bed. I had a dream where my assault team was pinned down by sniper fire, and we were hiding out in a two story building. I had my M14 assault rifle, when all of the sudden some towelheads (the term for the terrorist team) stormed in and put a gun or two to each of our heads. We obviously slowly put down are weapons, but I wasn't really concerned as I've been in similar situations more then once. Then all of the sudden they bring in my 7 year old niece, and the usual feel of the goggles against my face is gone. It felt way too real, and I started panicking. Then they put a glock in my hand and tell me to shoot the crying little girl in the head..... I woke up screaming, thrashing, doing anything to get that horrible image out of my head. My bedsheets were soaked in sweat, my pillow soaked in tears. My red-glowing alarm clock read 3:24am. My heart raced impulsively and out of rhythm, my muscles twitched and my vision blurred. I was in full on fight or flight mode. After calming down with the help of tea, I booted up my classic computer setup, opened a browser, and googled any side effects of playing Merlin. That's when I came across the term "PTSD," and how it works and who it affects. I've had anxiey almost my whole life, I know how that feels, and Merlin helped calm me down as my brain became more accustom to being in stressful situations and allowing me to face my fears head on, but this was completely different. I felt I was in actual danger, that someone is going to make me do something awful and do awful things.... Panicking again. Stop. I told myself. It didn't work.

The weight of the world came down upon my shoulders as I reread the letter for the third time, the words "rejection," and "unfitness for painting" echoed throughout my head. This had been the second time I had received this letter and it was another cruel reminder of my father's last words to me. He would never appreciate the beauty and serenity of the arts like mother did, I only wanted to show the world what a beautiful thing it truly is, but now as I stared at the paper that destroyed every hope and dream I ever had I am reminded of that man. He never understood anything I did, especially after the death of my precious brother Edmund he remained as stoic as ever, I couldn't handle it how he just accepted his death as if his life was just garbage to swept away in the streets of life. It had gotten even worse when he had forced me to that reform school, he didn't care about what I wanted to do, nor did he even care for the thousands of times I had tried to convince him of the value of art, but he didn't listen he didn't care, he never loved me. Only mother cared, she was the only one who supported me, she was the only one who gave me hope when I applied for the first time, and she was the one who gave me the courage to try again when I first got rejected, but now mother is gone. And now my hopes and dreams are gone like mother buried in the sea of hatred and apathy that is this world. But I won't accept that. I won't accept a world that would destroy everything that I love and care about, I won't accept a world that subjugates the weak, I won't accept the silent cries of the innocent. I will change this world. Even if I couldn't make the world beautiful with my art, I will make it beautiful, I promise you I will. I threw the rejection letter to the ground and began walking towards my future.

This veteran of my sports bag has been with me for nearly half my life. Given to me at the first day of sport at school, we have been together ever since. Every race, every boxing match, every exam, he has been through them with me. Every mile I have travelled he was there. His scarred translucent body living testimony to some of my most vivid memories, the black chevrons almost worn away by being repeatedly thrown out of the boat to shore. A deep graze runs through the lower "MEL" where I came of my bicycle at nearly 40mph down a mountain and the grooves are filled with dust from around the world. It's dark black cap is slightly deformed where a girlfriend threw it at my head and missed, and the look on her face when it dented her wall makes me smile when I think about it even now. It is my water bottle, and it is irreplaceable.

The closing melody of the strings and brass played quietly over the black background of the rolling credits as the movie came to a close. How the hell did that movie end? I had no idea. I am to lost in the scent of Rose, the girl from 3B that I've been having dinner with for twice a week over the past three months. His hands moved slowly through her soft, red ringlets of her hair leaving the tangle every so often in order to caress her neck, pale as a winters moon. Everything about Rose drives me crazy. It was not just the looks; that was superficial when it came to her. She's a biochemistry student from Chapel Hill - my alma marta. In 5 weeks time, she would be passing in her dissertation and hopefully get a post at John Hopkins. She had dreams of going off to Cambridge University to teach. She was just fun to be around. Staying home on a Friday night to play video games? Robin was more than excited to do that with me. Go catch a midnight showing of Citizen Kane down at the small theatre? She'd run down as I put on my shoes on to grab tickets and save some seats - as long as I grabbed the coke and popcorn. She exhaled, slowly departing her lips from my neck and nestled into my chest. She sighed deeply. "I had so much fun tonight. You really can cook..... I need to keep you around." My heart flutters. "I'm not going anywhere." I say, kissing the crown of her head. "I have to get up early tomorrow. I have to be in the lab all day." "You can just stay here for the night, get up when you need to." "We both know that I will never get to sleep if I stay in that bed tonight, Mr. Snider." I can't help but laugh and blush. She always knows how to read my mind. "Okay..... okay. You win. We still on for Sunday?" "Absolutely." she whispers, as she goes in for one last kiss. I walk her to door; she bends down to throw her sandals on. "If I get back early enough from the lab, let's go to that new Library Bar place downtown." "Barrels n' Books? I've been wanting to check that place out for a while now." "Now you can! Goodnight!" She sneaks in one last kiss. That little devil. I close the door and turn around slowly smiling. That night was - The recorder! I run over to the TV set and push aside the books beside it. The little recording device was still blinking red. I press stop, rewind, play. Silence. The sounds of light kissing. My iPhone rings in my pocket and I turn to look at the clock. 9:30 PM. My mother is never late with her nightly reminders. At least she isn't here tonight - I told her I was having Robin over for dinner so she went to visit her sister in Jersey. I am 28 years old, mother. I can remember to take my damn pills. The kissing stops. "Pretty good movie, huh?" I hear myself say. I remember saying this to make her laugh after a 20 minute make out. Silence. My phone rings again. I take it out of my pocket and see the Called ID: Mom. I throw the phone to couch and rub my palm across my chin. My skin is feeling itchy. Why the fuck didn't it pick up Robin's laugh. I love her laugh. I rewind the tape recorder. I will prove to them that she loves me. "Pretty good movie, huh?" I hear myself say. I remember saying this to make her laugh after a 20 minute make out. Silence. The phone rings again. The vibrations amplifying on the couch cushion. It cuts out after 2 rings. Whatever. I will answer her after. My headache is coming back. Why won't this recorder rewind faster!? I walk into the kitchen to start picking up the dishes before my mom gets home. I put it on the counter and press play as I turn to get the dishes from the table. The kissing stops. "Pretty good movie, huh?" I hear myself say. I remember saying this to make her laugh after a 20 minute make out. White Noise. Silence. "Brandon! Are you in there?! Your mother called me saying you aren't picking up your phone!" White Noise. Silence. "How is the dissertation coming along? You never answered me at dinner?" White Noise. Silence. I look down at my hands with the plates from dinner. She ate her food. Why was her plate full? Did she get seconds? "You got to make sure to let me pick you up after you drop your dissertation. We are going to Louie's for an Irish Car Bomb!" White Noise. Silence. "Of course it is going to be good..... it's you we are talking about!" White Noise. Silence. The plates in my hand shatter to the ground as a migraine starts throbbing at the crown of my head. The phone rings, vibrating off the cushion of my couch. "Brandon! It's Will! Open up the door!" The phone rings. The door knocks are louder and the white noise of silence is the only answer the tape recorder receives. The noise makes my head hurt. My pill. I need to take my pill. My voice crackles out of the voice recorder: "Of course I think about all the time. You are always on my mind. I love you, Robin." The White Noise of Silence is the only response I hear as the room goes black.

I turned twenty-seven today. Not a major milestone like turning eighteen, or twenty-one, or even forty. I'm surprised I've managed to stay who I am this long. Especially with this power. I've had this power since I was six. Six years old. A man who's eighty shouldn't have this power! And I've had it since I was a toddler. The power to kill anyone with a single thought. Oh, you didn't use your blinker and cut me off? Boom. You're dead. Terrible waitress? You're dead. A terrorist who just blew up a school? Dead. Have you ever thought about how much a human thinks about killing other humans? In a single day? No one can count that high. And can you think how many times you've said "I wish you were dead!" When you were a kid? At least once a day by what I've seen. I haven't killed anyone. Anything. Doing so will end a life. And also mine. Not like I die if I kill someone, but I'd die. Everything I am. Everything I stand for. Will die if I use this power. So no, I don't plan on using it. I plan on staying locked in my house forever to lower the chances of me slipping up and ending a life. I turned twenty-seven today..... it's been an eternity for me. Sorry. Wrote this on mobile at work just now in notepad on my phone! Sorry if it isn't the prompt "exactly" but I got inspired. Any advice would be great!

They sit in a line, dozens of cars stretched from the edge of the woods well into the heart of the city. The line goes both ways, moving so slowly that it would seem to not move at all. Moss forms within the cracks of the asphalt as a deer casually walks through the line of automobiles. The timid creature shows no apprehension towards the human constructs as they are empty. Abandoned. Their drivers are no where in sight, nor do they still exist. Long since perished to some plight that history has forgotten. No meaningful records left in the wake of this monumental event. No one left to read them if they had been written. The scribblings of a dead man, his hand now returned to dust. Dust that, picked up by a breeze that slips through the broken window of his decrepit house, comes to rest upon the rotting pages. Termites and ants work quickly to stake their claim over the relinquished territories as their predators scrape and scratch the surface for their burgeoning meal. The wilds run rampant on the remains of our civilization, building upon the ruins in their own way to make the best of what we've left behind. A few unfortunate creatures meet their end in startling collapses of weather-beaten architecture as it gives to stress and disrepair. While the fauna take what they can quickly, the flora choose to creep by slowly. Still bearing scars, many that have forever altered their course, they seem reluctant to take back what was theirs. Deep in the green leaves and colorful blooms, a stir arises. A mournful, sweet melody played by the wood's kin, those that know its plight all too well. The song soon grows in volume, introducing new verses of hope as it swells toward future iterations. Meanwhile, the trees are whispering. " Free at last, " they seem to say. -235

We thought that we had the advantage, a full tank crew verses some grunts on foot. We didn't realize how many there were. First they disabled the tank treads, this prevented us from going anywhere, but at least they couldn't get in and we could still fire out of the main gun and take occasional shots out of the coupola. Johnny even figured out that he could use the viewports to occasionally mow down the attackers. There were just to many of them. We are now running low on ammunition. Frank came up with another idea, while we couldn't move we COULD spin the turret around which helped to knock some of them off of the tank. It was a great idea while it lasted, but that also required battery power and after the first couple of hours even that ran out. We have now sealed ourselves in the tank as best as we could, we so hope that perhaps someone else will get these things off of us from externally. I am not sure how long we can last like this. This was supposed to be short mission so we had very limited water and food, you do not want to know what we did to "relieve" ourselves. I can't believe one of them actually poured gasoline down our barrel, it is seeping down the barrel and into the turret seat. Johnnie got soaked in it before we noticed what was going on and we have been trying to come up with a way to relieve the irritation. When they lit the gas, the flames traveled down the barrel and Johnnie was completely toasted. The smell of the burning flesh, the heat of the fire, watching as first his clothing burnt and then his skin kind of slid off of him..... that's something that you will never forget. Luckily he died quickly. Frank wasn't so lucky, when Johnnie got lit up he thrashed a good bit and managed to get some of the fuel on Franks face. I watch as his face puckered, then started popping with heat blisters. Frank is still alive, but he keeps begging me to kill him. If I actually survive this, I don't think I will never ride in a tank again. As I take off the VR glasses and the mask, I am so happy to see that I am still sitting in my chair in the middle of the lab. I tell Johnnie and Frank, I think we have made this game a little too realistic and perhaps we should replace the scent systems to be something nice. Simulating the smell burning flesh isn't a good idea.

Call me crazy, but when someone jumps off the Golden Gate Bridge, you expect them to die. At least most of the time, that is. If it's not the impact that does them in, they'll drown for sure. They are exceptions - I'm aware of these more than most - but I didn't expect to be one. Yet, as I drifted to the bottom of the San Francisco Bay, I realized that it would be my luck. All I wanted to do was go out on my own terms after seventy whole years of this bullshit. Apparently, fate had other plans. I try to flail my arms but they are useless. I never learned how to swim. I'm not doing much more than wasting more energy in a pointless attempt to surface. The water grows colder, causing me to shiver. Each inhalation freezes my insides, the feeling of needles pricking my lungs. Yet, I still don't die. It just hurts like hell. You know, if you asked me where I thought I'd be at the ripe age of seventy, I wouldn't say this. I expected to be surrounded by family and loved ones, watching my grandchildren grow up into their powers. Little did I know, I didn't even grow into my powers myself. I was branded a Dud, the same as everyone else who hadn't gained their power by thirty. Some Duds got lucky, though. A had a buddy in my support group who finally got his at around forty-four. Another lady in the news got hers at sixty-two. But at seventy, I got the hint. God, or whatever not-so-benevolent force out there, has been sending me a pretty clear message for decades now. I was a mistake and had to live out my miserable life constantly reminded of so. My family disowned me. My wife left me for a super speed freak. Even my own kid acted like I had jumped off a bridge years ago. So I said enough was enough. I decided to end my eight decades of living off with a bang. I always like the Golden Gate Bridge, anyway. It was one of the few places that cleared my mind. Now, I'm not so sure. My mind is buzzing as my body is being pressed with a fuckton of water. I'm at the bottom now, I think. It doesn't feel like I'm sinking anymore. I sigh, or at least try to with a body full of water. Why did I have to discover my immorality now of all times? Oh well, I guess I better start learning how to swim. This is going to take a while. Happy fucking birthday to me.

I'm not sure when it started happening, but I can tell you when I first noticed. I was in high school. A song came on the radio-my good friend and I were pretty excited to hear it, it was a new release. From the first chord, I was very confused. When the vocals came it, I sang along. Word for word, pitch for pitch. When it was over, I looked at my friend. He was stunned. I stammered something about a re-release, but after checking it out, there was no doubt. A song I had grown up with and known as a child was now being played as though it had only been recorded for the first time a few months ago. In college, it happened again. Twice. A new song from a different band I remembered but the version I knew was faster, and a little higher pitched. The other..... oddity was when I once managed to make the trip from college to home in a third of the normal time- without having broken any speed limits. The cops in those little towns don't mess around. If I had been more than a few miles over, they'd have pegged me in a heartbeat. But by the laws of natural physics, I would have had to have averaged over 120 miles per hour. Maybe I crossed over and crossed back, I don't know. I thought it happened in my sleep, but now I think it happens between one second and the next. I've been lucky. I haven't jumped too far off course. Everyone still knows me. Even if I cross in the middle of a conversation, the topic is the same, though the subtext can be wildly different. If I could pick a time when I noticed myself crossing, I could maybe learn to control it, or at least track my progress, see if I had two or three and crossed between them, or if I just cross farther and farther from home. For now its manageable. All my friends and loved ones in all the universes I've seen (which means we've all been jumping....) know about my..... trouble, and see it as a curiosity, nothing more. My fear, though, is that the changes will be greater and more pervasive as I progress. For its own sake, that might be fascinating, but how could I cope with crossing, with no way to cross back, or guarantee that I would, into a universe where you and I had never met?

I don't let the really ugly ones in. Some procurers do - they say it's no difference when you've got bouncers, cameras, and connections. The ugly johns are the ones who need your services the most, pay the best, and keep coming back. 'So what if they're a little mean to the girls?' my friends say.'What are they going to do, hit'em? Big deal. You could have five guys in there before he throws a second punch. If he runs, every crook in town will know about it.' It's true, and it's not like men at the other end of the spectrum frequent brothels. Every man who comes in here has at least something wrong with him, even if it's just the vague, greyish tinge typical to someone who uses people for sex. We screen out the worst, but it's not like we can afford to be picky. On the other hand, it's almost too easy to find a woman so down on her luck that she's willing to sell her body, and yet beautiful enough to actually turn a profit. Sometimes you find these girls and they turn out to be mentally deficient - gorgeous, but with the mind of a six-year-old - and with parents so ugly the sight of them makes you want to vomit. I try not to think about it too much. Or I get these girls who are otherwise normal, but when they look in the mirror they see all these scars and warts that just aren't there so they compulsively do good things for people - even people who fuck them over. You tell them they're pretty and they laugh nervously, like they're so sure you're wrong but don't want to tell you if you haven't noticed. The saddest ones are the ones who know full well what they look like but don't think it matters. The world has shit on them all their lives while they've given nothing but good back, and they think that's just how it goes. They tell you that you have to show mercy to ugly people, because they think that the one time they had pimples when they were young equates to the beer gut and disfiguring scar their ex had. It's sort of understood in this business that turning tricks for too long will gradually fade a woman's looks. No one else really thinks it's because of all the guys she has to deal with. Even the madams I know say that prostitution is its own small sin. I don't really care, though. These girls have never in their lives said no to a man just because he was ugly. So, I do it for them. I guess that's how I got to be the handsomest pimp in town. Though, that really isn't saying much.

..... as I saw that..... thing walk out from the stone arch. At first glance it was no different than the rest of the undead that I had cut down before, wearing the armor of the gallant knight it had consumed. That illusion quickly fell apart as I saw the faint hints that whatever now resided in that armor had ever been human were nowhere to be found. Where I expected to see the sunken eyes of a wretched corpse was now a dark void, the joints of the armor where I expected to see rotting flesh peeking our from behind the rusted steel was only a pulsating darkness, and the shambling of a soldier barely clinging to what only a select few would call "life" was instead a confident stride. My steel felt so cold to me now that I nearly dropped it, letting it clatter to the floor of the stone parapet, just barely catching myself before falling into that chasm of pure terror. I raised my sword to it, steeling my resolve to face this darkness, and seemingly in response to my own willingness to fight, raised it's own sword as well with several dark tendrils reaching out from it's wrists to wrap around the handle. I swung my heavy blade as hard as I could, only for my blow to be cast aside by the creature's own with a loud clang as more dark tendrils burst from it's arm alongside a bubbling sound that I could only guess was a growl. My second swing would find it's way behind the creatures blade, slashing at a gap in it's armor to cut at the darkness beneath. It's scream deafened me, forcing me to recoil in pain as the creature's own armor burst open as a torrent of tentacles poured out into a writhing mass with bits of metal sinking into the darkness. As I regained my senses I was met with the mass crashing towards me, having abandoned any wish to disguise itself as a person. The wave of darkness only slowing as I helplessly flailed my weapon at it before being consumed by it like the knight before me. Enveloped in the darkness I could only feel the intense pressure as it squeezed me as tightly as it could, snapping my bones one by one before finally falling into unconsciousness. I slowly wake, the tiny flame's warmth comforting me once more before rising to my feet. I look up to see the parapet in the distance before setting out once more, feeling the emptiness in me grow ever larger.

The last thing I ever saw was her sitting on the bed next to me. She was reading a book. I loved watching her face when she read, she always looked so interested and content and I wanted her to feel that way. When I woke up my eyes hurt so I didn't want to open them. I could hear Sarah screaming in my ear to get up. I felt her holding my arm and helping me up. She said there was an earthquake and the roof had collapsed. We moved from the bed and she guided me to the door around the rubble which I could only feel. She left me on the landing holding in to the rail while she went to Jennys room to get her. A minute later I heard their footsteps coming towards me. Jenny was with her. Jenny was confused and scared. I could hear that she was trying not to cry. Sarah guided me down the steps and to the door. I think Jenny was clinging onto her on the other side. We reached the door. I could already hear people shouting outside. We got outside and Sarah sat me and Jenny on the pavement outside the house. She went to speak to some of the people outside. When she came back she told us a helicopter was coming. Sarah always handled situations like this well. When a tree collapsed in the neighbours house she was in there instantly helping them out and telling people to call an ambulance. The helicopter didn't take long to come. Apparently I was one of the first to be put on there. I ended up passing out on the trip to the hospital. I woke up a day later. I could hear machines beeping. Then I heard Jenny. She was excited about something and kept saying my name. Then another woman started talking saying she was a nurse and that I was in hospital. She then told me I had lost sight in both eyes due to head trauma. I was shocked. I snarled at her screaming about it being temporary. Shouting I have to see. It took months to get used to life without vision, but it took years to finally accepted its final. My only joy is that the last thing I ever saw was my wife and that it is really a great last thing to see.

In the middle of the city, a thunderous roar. As long lasting as an alarm and as earth shattering as an explosion. People all around started to flee from their lives, some leaving behind their piled up cars on the freeway after realizing they could have a better chance running on their very two feet. Despair and chaos. A typical scene straight out of a classic monster movie: Godzilla, the king of Monsters had arrived to claim his throne. "You'd think that with a name as mine I would be able to doodle around in the air and pull out something, right?" Da Mangaka said as she walked to the edge of the rooftop, using third person for the story. It sounds better anyways, proper for these kind of situations. "I may not be able to tap onto Heaven's Door, but there's always Exogenesis." "I'm surprised you haven't seen the series." Said my Editor who calmly saw the scene beside me. "There's a thin line between referencing and copying a Mangaka you know? Regardless of they are from this or other worlds. I got my own style and I think I can make it work." Da Mangaka's hand moved towards a golden key that hung from a necklace and gently pulled it out from it's position. After a quick glance, she threw it up towards the air, allowing it to grow up to 6ft before catching it with her right hand. "Well, time to get Mr. Kaiju back to where he belongs. Ready to do your job?" She said, grinning at him with excitement. "As long as you don't procrastinate too much on it." Perhaps you may wonder though why a Golden Key as a weapon of choice instead of a pen. That might take 10 more years to explain if she doesn't skip schedule - Editor

Plep watched the figure stumble his way down the dusty path. He or she looked as if they were dodging attacks while dancing to an erractic two-step. Plep fought the urge to laugh, this must be one of the Rusty Mare's patrons wobbling home in the morning. As the figure twirled madly, Plep guessed from the thick white beard it was a man. He wore dark leather hides over his calves and thighs, and forearms, quite similar to Plep's, though of a better quality. It was the chestplate that had caught his interest. It was black as pitch all over yet with a strange gleam that looked like it swallowed sunlight. The man had quit dancing in favour of a lie down on his back. Plep approached cautiously. Birds were still chirping to each other, which was always a good sign, and his old mule Lysa just looked bored. Once he was within a few steps range, he asked the stranger if he was alright. When there was no response, he shouted it. He hoped no one was watching, he felt very silly shouting at a possible dead body. With still no response Plep nudged him with his foot. He heard a moan and nudged him again in a manner that could be described as a kick. "Take this..... off me," the old man croaked. Plep removed the clips at his side, but when he tried to removed the shoulderclip the armour refused to move. "Do you..... accept," the old man muttered, eyes spinning wildly. "You muss..... slay..... the demon lo..."? Plep said he accepted and the armour unclipped itself while he manouvered the man into a position that he could remove it. He took it off and lay the man down again. Wait, what was that about demons? "Leave him, he will be fine," commanded a voice from his hands, "put me on, there is much to be done." Plep had to admit that the man on the ground did look a lot healthier, a little younger and probably just needed a good nap. True, talking armour was a little odd, but one of the best conversations of his life had been with a drunk throne. He picked the armour up and put it on. Plep was surprised how well it fit, thinking it would of been too large. Plep felt good, strong, his vision had improved and he was sure he was a master swordsman despite never weilding one in his life. He marched up to old Lysa and had some very strong words with her, telling her she was a young stallion who could gallop miles at a time without tiring. Lysa did feel like a young stallion, unfortunately she was a young stallion who had some very strong views on horse emancipation from human domestication. She turned round and rear-kicked him sqaure in the chest. The armour took the blow, but his feelings weren't as strong. Lysa was circling round, trying to bite his exposed arms. "You must break her in, and she will be your steed," said the armour. Plep wanted to reply that he had no experience wrangling horses, or mules that thought they were horses, but he didn't need to as his feet had already jumped when he wasn't looking. He landed on Lysa's back, on his feet, found his balance and nudged her into the right direction. The journey wasn't that bad, he arrived at a town in spectacular fashion at least. As he was about to ferret out some food, a little girl ran up to him and shouted that her family needed help. Plep was sixty-seven per cent sure he had replied that that wasn't his job, she would be better off asking the guards, or watch, or whatever it was called here, and did she know where he could get good food. But even before he had shut his mouth he was running full pelt behind the girl and somehow unable to catch up with her, even though she was half his size. They twisted round corners, around the backs of houses, even over a roof at one point. They startled kissing couples and sleeping beggars. Eventually, Plep came to an alley that narrowed the farther it went. He watched the girl disappear through a door, at the bottom of the alley, while panting heavily from the run. "You need a sword," said the armour, "and possibly some fire." "Real helpful, thanks talking armour!" Plep said, catching his breath, "like swords just appear out of nowhere!" Plep felt immediately silly after looking to his left and spotting what could only be a sword handle. He knew for a certain it was a handle because when he looked farther down he seen the sword part. Grabbing it up, and muttering something mean about things that shouldn't talk, he squeezed down the alley and launched himself through the door head first. Landing on both feet after a neat flip, he swung the sword upwards with force and heard it slice through something meaty followed by a deafening screech in his ear. The sword danced of its own accord, Plep an instrument and extension of it. He was still deaf from the creatures screech, and tears were flying from his eyes so he kept them shut while the sword killed whatever was flying at him. This continued for several minutes, with dozens of bodies thudding into the ground. "You can open your eyes, Plep," the armour said gently, "it's over." Plep was still crying and sobbing. The sword had sheathed itself in a sheth at his side that he didn't remember acquiring. A soft white glow was illuminating a fraction of the darkness around him, he wished the armour would stop it because he could see the wrecked and mangled forms of bodies. "There just vampires, Plep, silly vampires! They weren't people," the armour said, "there's treasure up ahead, do you want to go check it out? Might be something worth taking, maybe a nice helmet? Would you like that, Plep?" Plep hated to admit it but some treasure would be nice. He wiped his eyes and nose, gave another little indignant sniff then let the armour guide him through the mountains of midnight surrounding them.

"I reap. It's what I do." I shift my scythe between skeletal claws, the blood-stained metal catching the fires light. "Or, it's at least what I used to do. Until your kind went too far." Eyeing both my interviewers, I wait for a response. There is a pause in which they both consider what I've said. "So you take no blame in any of this?" The man in the large oddly shaped coat swallows before continuing. "Even though this is your doing, you feel you're not at fault?" I can't stand his arrogance. I can't stand their arrogance. They think they're above me? Death? Where would they be without my guidance? My cold embrace inspired their greatest inventions and art. The very essence of their culture is fueled by my actions. Without me they're not themselves. For I am them. "It disgusts me that you can't see the lesson I try to paint you." The other man, tries to speak, his swollen tongue causing him to stop briefly. In that moment I raise my scythe and point it towards him, turning the blade under his fat, hairy neck. "Don't you dare insinuate that there is no lesson here, that I'm being unjust. You're just an insolent pig like the rest of your kind." I lower my scythe, he heaves a sigh of relief. "I gladly accepted that you were able to prolong your lives so many times. I celebrated reaping the first man to live two centuries. Hell, I didn't complain when you claimed to have found immortality and immunity. I waited millennia to reap you. You were able to enjoy the world more than you ever were supposed to. You got to do and see things no animal ever should. But was that enough? No. Of course not." I pause, watching the two interviewers shift uncomfortably. I know they know I'm right, they're just too proud to admit it. I stand and face the fire, the flames lighting empty sockets. "You just had to go continue looking for more. You know you were the prized children of your god? He gave you the potential to live longer, do more, and be happier than most creators do." I laugh. I needn't wait for a reply, though I've sworn off reaping they fear me. I command the room, and them, while I speak. Turning, I continue. "You know, I wish you kept trying to live eternal within the confines of machinery. It was so easy to reap while you hid within it. A simple'computer virus' or'malfunction' and you were mine. Of course though, you soon realized how idiotic living within a machine was." I see the misshapen man watching his reflection in my scythe, it's cold blade showing his scars through the stains. "Once you learned the secrets of your creation and started your farms to grow and harvests yourselves, I knew you had crossed a line. That was still acceptable, though. I knew your need for life had perverted you and I accepted it." I sit again, my blade resting on my shoulder. I can't smile, but if I could I'd be giving them one hell of a smile now. "Once you started harvesting your souls. That was it. You went too far. You broke the natural order. I mean, what kind of creature pulls it's essence out of a filthy, desolated flesh heap and gets into a specially grown meat suit?" My disgust evident, I wait till the tension in the air builds past even my comfort. I stand and walk behind them, resting my scythe on both their shoulders. The unevenness amuses me, with a chuckle I lean between their heads. "So, as you're obviously here to plead with me like your kind does every few decades, the answer is no. I will not bring back death. I will not continue reaping. You and all your kind will continue to suffer the endless pains of having your body never die. You will burn, break, boil, swell, bleed, and hurt. But your body will never die and you can never leave it for a new meat suit." I turn to leave, as they sit there stuttering. "B-b-but..... please! You can't leave us like this again! The agony..... the torment..... we're living in Hell..... please Death..." I pause, amused at hearing such a request. "Maybe one day, after you're all laying there wounded, unable to heal. Maybe once you're all begging to have me back in your lives. Maybe then I'll considering reaping you pathetic wastes." I walk into the abysm, to reap other realms where less arrogant creations tread. Before I fade away, I call back. "In the meantime, enjoy your cancer fleshbag!"

Numbers. Fucking numbers. I can't say it's been my whole life but it's been a while. Probably since I was like seven or eight. Everyone has a number, everyone. I didn't know what they meant for a few years and hell I was terrified I wasn't about to ask my mom what they meant because even as a kid I knew it wasn't normal. My brothers six years older than me. Trish and I had just about reached the peak of our bi-weekly argument about her parents It's not my fault they hate you, Ryan! You're the one who said Snookums looked like a bilge rat with a heroin dependency! when I decided I'd had enough, threw up my hands, and went out onto the balcony for a smoke. Snookums. That godforsaken little weasel of a dog had been on my case as long as I'd known Trish. The first time I visited her parents, Snookums went for my ankles with the ferocity and implacability of a Patriot missile system, and I damn near broke his little neck with a reflexive kick that sent him careening across the room and into a Japanese vase. That had set the tone perfectly for the remainder of my relationship with the in-laws. As I leaned on the railing, I became aware of a commotion in the courtyard six stories below. A group of suited men were attempting to subdue a lone nutjob clothed in flowing black robes and sunglasses. Fists and feet were flying, and it was hard to tell exactly what was going on, but the gist of it seemed to be that the nutjob had the jujitsu arsenal to hold his own even against six guys. "Hey!" I shouted, as the kung fu guy ripped a tetherball pole out of the ground. "Hey! You can't just break shit, man!" There went another tetherball court. The next time Brad wanted a game, we'd have to go down the street to the public playground, which was always embarrassing, what with the kiddies flinging mulch and running into the line of fire. That's a fun conversation to have with another adult your age: explaining why their six-year-old took a tetherball at decidedly serious velocity to the back of the head, while the kid lies face-down in the dirt, shrieking such that you'd think somebody'd ripped his kidneys out. More of the suited guys were pouring into the courtyard, which suited me just fine. I saw a bench crumble to dust as four people were flung into it at once (I had to admit, the tetherball pole was doing work). Management wouldn't lift a finger to fix any of this shit, that was for sure. It had been enough of a struggle to get them to fix my sink when wastewater was belching out of the drain all hours of the day and night. It looked like the suited men were gaining the upper hand. There was an army of them, it seemed like. I couldn't see the black-clad nutjob any longer. He was buried beneath a pile of bodies like a football after a fumble. More guys kept running into the courtyard and jumping on, which I kind of figured was overkill, until all of a sudden the tetherball ninja BURST OUT THROUGH ALL OF THEM AND FLEW INTO THE SKY, at which point I took a real hard look at the cigarette I'd been smoking, just to make sure I hadn't accidentally been taking hits from something a whole lot more powerful, and then decided that maybe it was time to go back inside, and take a long hard think about what I'd just seen, and maybe see if Trish had cooled off a bit and wanted to order Indian, the way we always did after a fight, or when a human being flew straight up and vanished into the sky, Team Rocket style, that maybe it was my turn to apologize, then, to Trish, because it did seem to me in retrospect, based on the flying guy maybe being a vision from God, that perhaps I had been a bit harsh on her parents, and might just want to lighten up a smidge, just this once.

Michael strapped the angular backpack to his shoulders, "You think they could make these W.I.N.G. devices a little less extravagant, it's like R and D wants everything to be flashy and colorful." His partner, Albus, chuckled. "You think it's easy to decrease gravity? To simply defy inertia? You should be surprised they can even fit inside a rucksack like they do." The pressure suits they wore were sleek and glistening white. "Fine, back when I joined the Legion we didn't have to make ourselves so visible. We just went in with advanced camouflage and appeared when we needed to." Albus locked his helmet into place, the visor darkened. "So, what's the situation down earthside?" Michel pressure checked their suits and motioned towards the hangar, "We taking a Seraph?" Albus nodded, "848 is prepped and ready for takeoff, pilot Is waiting on us." They moved through the access corridor, the room beyond was large but teeming with Seraphim class dropships. The vehicles consisted of an outer layer of multiple interlocking flywheels serving gyroscopic functions, to keep the ship stable in flight. Michael ducked his head underneath the ship's moving parts and opened the access door, revealing the interior. Albus climbed in first, taking his seat right next to the door. Michael walked into the flight station and nodded approvingly as the copilot completed his checks. "Landing zone?" He asked the Captain. The man in a black uniform started up the auxiliary power unit, "near the fertile crescent, right by the euphrates river. A large portion of humans have congregated there at the metropolitan area, they laid the ground work for their project about 10 cycles ago, but recently larger shipments have come in so forward Recon decided it was time to give us a heads up." Michael nodded as the engines came to life, "Get us down on the ground Captain, we'll take it from there." The angel sat down beside his partner, "Might as well get comfy, it'll be a long enough flight we can get a bit of sleep on the way." The Seraphim's engines whined softly as the electrical shutdown procedure finished up. The cypress trees made a small forest where they had hidden the ship, the pilots activated the camouflage and watched as the screen went dark, starved of light. Michael opened the door and dropped into the tall grass, Albus followed him out into the open. "Engage W.I.N.G. apparatus," he ordered, a heads up display augmenting his vision. The two humanoid forms slowly levitated off the ground as the counter-gravity field took hold of them, the thrusters fired and brought them into the deep blue sky. The target came into view, a building unlike that humanity had ever attempted to accomplish. "They're not ready," Albus exclaimed. "I know, and so does Kyrios, which is why we're here. We have to stop it's construction, if humanity reaches space..... I can't even think of the consequences." Albus shook his head, "War, that'll definitely be one consequence. They'll finally make use of atomics as a weapon if they have means to get it into orbit." Humanity was special in one curious way when it came to invention. They were the singular recorded species in all of occupied space to have first created a means to get out of the atmosphere that didn't require rocketry of any kind. Every other race had invented flight first, it was likely that humans would too, once their technology was rendered useless by the machine these men were about to unleash. They landed quietly on a multi story building and engaged their camouflage, looking for the right moment to infiltrate the facility. A convoy approached the front gate, they snuck in behind it. "The center of this facility is the exact location of the middle of their city, if we activate the linguistic reprogrammer we will be able to target every person on this continent." "What about the smaller groups of civilization on the smaller continent to the west?" Albus questioned, as they reached the basement. "They've not yet Invented such technology, we won't have to worry about them for now." Albus removed the reprogrammer from his superior's back, "What of the currently completed section of the space elevator? What will we do with it?" "That, I can not say." Michael punched in the code and timed it for 5 minutes, "It will change 80 of the population to four different core languages, enough that no remaining group of scientists and engineers will be able to decipher the plans for the elevator. We're hopeful that most of the population will move out based on this change, perhaps even the unchanged group will vacate. Afterwards we can bring in a planetary salvage group and take the raw materials with us." Now finished, they exited the building and returned to the sky. "Their future could be so bright," Albus' face turned to sorrow behind the mask. "With this, they'll have yet another chance to do some good with their lives. I'm just glad Kyrios is in control, I'd have given up on these poor humans so long ago. He keeps giving them more and more opportunities, perhaps they'll accomplish something this time around." Their craft streaked across the sky, it's spherical shape painted matte white so as not to reflect light. Below them a swarm of nanites emerged from the box, each carrying a program that would erase the language of a person's youth, so effective was this device that it even changed what words you thought in, and what syntax. Within ten minutes the robots had integrated themselves into every person's mind and started the transformation. The human race would not know the significance of this event, but it charted the course towards their salvation from destruction.

The typing filled the dry office air. A'ding!' went unheard as the elevator doors opened and she stepped out and started walking down the hallway. It started with a man idly glancing up from his paperwork. His jaw dropped and his eyes slowly followed her as she kept going, completely unaware of his existence. Whispering slowly replaced typing. Someone dropped their coffee mug. Someone else even hazarded a wolf whistle and was immediately slapped in the head. "Damn." A man said as she disappeared behind a closed door. "I'd never seen any so..... you know." Another one said. "Ugh, you are pigs." A woman said, rolling her eyes. "Just get over it." "Aw, don't be jealous honey." One of the men said. "I still think yours are gorgeous. I mean, you're no palindrome, but..." He trailed off, winking at her. "Don't hold your breath,'honey'." She replied mockingly. "I know for a fact what they say about multiples of seven is true." "Ohhhh, burn!" The other man said, punching his friend in the shoulder. "Shut up, dude!" He hissed, glaring at the woman. "And just so you know, there's scientific evidence that there's no correlation between "Yeah yeah, I've heard it all before." She said with a roll of her eyes. "And my eyes are down here." She added, pointing at them. The door opened again, and the same change in behaviour happened as the woman walked her way to the elevator, pressed the button and waited for it to come. I came back to my office, locked the door and opened the secret compartment of my desk. I grabbed the folder hidden in there, and let myself fall on the floor. I closed my eyes, and tried to breathe. Slowly, I opened the folder, and looked at the documents. A reproduction of a sketch by Renoir from 1876, studies on the first Statue of David, by Donatello in 1408, a picture of an undated wood pendant found in Russia, a picture of my assistant that I found on Facebook and printed a few weeks ago... And about half a dozen other documents, all with the same face. Giorgio Alessandro Messia, 1357. Gustav Adamov, 1578. Francois Lemercier, 1875. Richard Smith, 1905. Nathan Boswell, 2016. This was no coincidence. I had known it for a while, but I still needed some evidence. Something that would prove that I was not crazy. I just did not think of the cost. " Doctor Hatcher? " The noise gets me out of my torpor. Nathan is knocking on my door. " Not now, Nathan. ," I reply with an unsteady voice. " Miss Hatcher, you are going to be late for the conference! ," he continues. The conference. The conference... " What conference? ," I ask. I am not the most organised person in the world, but I can not recall having any conference today. I get up and go to my desk. My laptop is on, and I have a reminder: " Conference. 10 minutes. " I am sure I did not have any conference planned today. " Nathan? Are you still here? ," I ask. No answer. Something is wrong. I take my handbag and open it. Earlier today, I had a meeting with a fellow historian, Professor Hughes, now retired. He was known for a research on the Count of Saint Germain, who was thought to be immortal. I had heard of Hughes for his eccentricity - most of my colleagues always thought he was crazy - but sanity is not really a prerequisite in our profession. It turns out that Professor Hughes had always been in his right mind. " I have never found evidence showing that the Count of Saint Germain and all these people were actually the same person but I have found a few statements describing some sort of miracles... let me have a look... " He had prepared some documents for me, and was flicking through them. " We had testimonies about a man who escaped after he got hanged in 1589, another who walked out of the Great Fire without a scar... " I took my phone, flicked through some pictures, and showed Professor Hughes a picture from Facebook. His face became suddenly red and he was gasping for air. I called an ambulance straight away. He was having a heart attack. I had to give my statement to the police, sign papers... I was not able to concentrate on anything. The only reason why Professor Hughes would have a heart attack when he saw Nathan would be... Because Nathan is the Count of Saint Germain. A loud noise brings me back to the present. " Doctor Hatcher! " Nathan appears in my office, a fire extinguisher in his hand. I look at the door. He destroyed it. He destroyed my office door! " Nathan, what the hell are you doing? ," I say. He walks towards me. I don't try to hide the pictures scattered on the floor. The pictures of him. " And what are you doing? ," he asks. He drops the fire extinguisher, and comes to sit next to me, on the floor. I look at him, intently. He is about 25, dark hair, dark eyes. And dark secrets, obviously. " Who the hell are you, Nathan? ," I say. " You are going to be late for the conference! Miss Hatcher! " I wake up in a start. I look at my office door. It's still there. " Doctor Hatcher! ," my assistant is screaming with her high-pitched voice. I can not stand her voice. It is lucky she is leaving next month. I look at the papers on my desk. Applications to become my new assistant. " Nathan Boswell, MA in History, currently studying for a PhD. ," says the CV. I look at my laptop. A Facebook page is showing, with pictures of Nathan Boswell, 25 y.o, dark hair, dark eyes. " Doctor Hatcher! ," says the voice behind the door. " I'm coming, Liz. I'm coming. " " Professor Hughes is waiting! You know how much he hates waiting! ," Liz says. Dear God. I wish I could go back to the world where I had a young handsome immortal man with a normal voice as an assistant. And a world where Hughes has retired. I take a breath, walk to the door and open it. " Would you mind calling this Nathan Boswell for an interview, please? ," I tell Liz while handing in Nathan Boswell's CV. This is my first go ever at such an exercise, I hope you enjoy reading it as much as I enjoyed writing it! Edit: grammar mistake

Are they like us in any way? Does their technology surpass our own? Is it possible that we are related? Perhaps an asteroid cracked a larger planet into two separate pieces. That would make the aliens our lost brothers and sisters. I do not regret volunteering to pilot the shuttle. My mind has been racing over the last few cycles and this will at least help put a stop to my worries. But until I get there the thoughts continue to swirl around my mind like leaves inside a cage. Wild and unruly - then calm for just a moment - and then swoosh! . Could they have achieved even half the things our race has? Did they fight similar bloody wars that brought them to the very edge of extinction? Part of me hopes that they are similar to us, whilst another part desperately hopes they are nothing like us. I am halfway through my mission when I pass the shuttle from the alien planet. A craft not unlike my own. As agreed, we will reach each others planets at a similar moment. I feel sorry for what their ambassador will see when it reaches my planet. My mind is bombarded with'what if's' for the next half a cycle, but eventually I see it looming ahead. It is slightly larger than my home planet, and slightly greener. I am only moments away and my hearts are racing. I think twice about my mission. It is not too late to turn back. That is when I see the bright light behind me. It engulfs my ship and causes the alien planet to glow. I now realise just how similar they are to us. How scared of us they must have been. I prime the bombs and close my eyes. - Plenty more scfi WP on my sub! rnickofnight

We considered it a culture. Those of us born without cones had to stick together. They called it the I Love Lucy syndrome after the supposedly black and white TV show. I say supposedly because I had never seen different. From the moment we're born we immediately start making sense of the world around us, even if memory doesn't serve as testament. For most people, regardless of memory, their first experiences of life occurred in color. For us, it has always been black and white. People have told me my whole life that I've been missing out on the beauty of a sunset. They've told me I'll never appreciate a flower until I have seen it as it truly should be. This to me has always sounded ridiculous. How else could something possibly be than how I am currently experiencing it? Isn't the true state of the world a subjective experience? It always seemed silly to me that people told me that I was missing out on the true splendor and beauty of the world simply because I could not see these supposed colors. Like I said though, we stuck together, we fought the norm. The truly colorblind of the world found meaning in each other. We found meaning in other types of beauty. In music, in the kindness of others, in the power of words. An objective definition of beauty is reliant on a subjective definition. So what then truly makes something beautiful? But now here we are. Stem cell research has allowed for even the most colorblind of the colorblind capable of full-fledged sight in color. I was one of the first to get the surgery. You know what I did? The first thing I did was take a hike and watch the sunset. I picked some flowers and smelled the familiar scent. Hell, I even took a trip to the Louvre. There has been some resentment from the fully colorblind community towards those getting the surgery. I try to ignore it, but I also tend to ignore those demanding I admit I am better off. Is the world more beautiful than it was before? Are people more vibrant and caring than they used to be? These are questions I can't answer. When your entire life is defined on a certain basis, it's hard to suddenly shift. Do I like watching sunsets more now? Sure. Do they make me happier? Not necessarily. People tend to disregard the capability for finding true meaning in a place that seems distant from them.

It first started 35 years ago. Back then, I was a little innocent boy of maybe 10 years old. I can't really remember. What I remember however, was myself raising my hand and asking the teacher to repeat a concept we had learnt the day before. Perhaps if I had not done so, my "defect" might not have been noticed till a later date. But no, I had. I remember the doctor's sadistic face, my classmates' laughter. So, I got enrolled into "special education." Even at there, I was shunned. I was the only one who had "memory loss." The others there might have weird behavior, but still, they has photographic memory. Sooner or later, I was shunned. By teachers and students alike. Sooner or later, my parents refused to acknowledge me. They only cared about my older sister, who was a scholar in her school. Sooner or later, I got bullied. Why? Why did I have to be born differently. That was what I asked myself. But after my schooling, I realised that perhaps it wasn't such a bad thing. As I look the others who had been bullied before, they couldn't forget. Permanently scarred where they. I, on the other hand, had forgotten the worst parts and could carry on with life. That was when I started smiling again. Then, my parents died in an automobile accident. For days, I grieved. Though they didn't treat me very well, they were still my parents. So like my sister, I grieved. But unlike her, I soon forgot. Not completely but still, enough to make me functional again. The pain was still there. But it was lesser. So, I carried on with life, unlike my sister. I soon settled with my soulmate. She was a historian, studying the days before the modification that made photographic memory a reality. She was intrigued by how I could forget stuff, and carry on with life. And we became soulmates and settled down. We had a beautiful boy. One day, a teacher called me. She said that my boy had a "learning disability" and could not remember things. I just replied that I knew how to handle it and put down the phone, smiling. My son will be free.

It's a cloudy, dim-lighted room. My vision is still foggy. I would have rubbed my eyes off of crusts if I didn't have restraints in the first place.
