" , Ed apologizes, "must be my excitement. It's usually just enough for me to read before sleeping." "It's okay. No harm done," I was closing and opening my eyes to get focus back. Never knew Ed was a big, book-lover. Nerd. My sight got restored without any problems. Ed continued putting more probes when we both heard a beep from his belt. "They need an assist. " , he said. "Must be important. " , I followed. Ed nodded, his eyes trying to give me a calming assurance. "Stay calm, buddy. We'll get you done after this emergency, okay? " , he quickly got out of the door and the springy door closed me to my isolation. This isn't so bad. Quiet. Well, not quite. Monitor buzzing. Cold probes weren't cold as before. They need to paint this room better. What a dull color! Wait. Did I hear screaming right now? Hmmm, some drama queen got too excited, I guess. Oh, another scream. I don't feel special on my birthday now, sharing birthdays with these..... Ugh..... It's my birthday! You're wrecking my birthdaaaaay! I wish I could just tell her to shut up. Huh, another one. Wait, that's not the same as the one before. Damn, are all people born on the same day as me all whiny? Another one. Oh, I hear sirens. Firetrucks. Lots. and police cars. Smoke. What's going on? "So please tell me, how did you die?" Tge death manager asked me in an unbelieving tone. I had trouble getting my last death approved by the government, so god only knows how this one will go over "I ate a live hamster" The heavyset black woman recording my death burst into laughter while I tried to make myself smaller in my seat. I tried to swallow my embarassment, but the words had already been said. I mean, atleast it didnt hurt my record very badly. it wasnt like I'd overdosed on anything or got shot in a gang, but it would still hurt my pride. The death recorder wrote up my death in an endless torrent of laughter. The last thing I heard from her office as I walked out was her laughing and telling her peers, who joined the symphony of embarassment. If you were in thee same situation that I was, you totally would of swallowed the rodent. I was at a party, everyone was lookimg at me, a ring of anticipating eyes waiting for the furry little bastard to go down my throat. Had I not had a few drinks, I probably would of chickened out. But I swallowed that furrball whole. The moment I swallowed I could feel its little claws trying to dig and scratch and scrape their way up in the abyss. All of the hamster's efforts didnt help it very much, but it did manage to damage my internal organs, causing me to die of internal bleeding. At work the next day everyone knew. At work, everyone laughed. I had a few new nicknames like "the guniae pig gulper" or "hamsters down the hatch harry" the laughs of the day came from questions such as: "could you eat my daughter's hamster? I never intended to create anything. In the beginning, a little before the beginning to be accurate, it was just my father and me. All there had ever been was us and nothing. A very uncomplicated existence for very uncomplicated beings. Father and I spent eons with nothing, but then one day I made a mistake. I found myself bored. I wanted something new, something different. My desires bubbled through me and rippled through the nothing, disturbing it. Out of the nothing, something appeared. Balls of gas exploded with new light, matter rushed into voids, and the energy began pulsing away what was left of the nothing. My desires became a universe. Father disappeared with the nothing. The only thing I had ever known, taken away because I was bored and made a mistake. Loss pounded through me as I surveyed this new universe. First I hated it for the pain it had caused me. However, time passed as it had never done before and my heart changed. For a mistake it certainly was beautiful. And I felt pride when I realized several of the planets nestled around their stars were developing consciousness. One planet did distress me. A tiny little blue thing that developed later than the others. A late bloomer. I was shocked at the creatures that appeared eventually. They raises their voices and cried "Father!" into the void. Father. I could be a father like the one I lost. These little things needed me. My universe needed me to be a father. With a blink of my eye, centuries passed. Still they shouted out "Father! " , still they needed me. It was nice. They pretended I talked to them, they wrote down things I allegedly said, several even claimed to be my son. And still they called for me. Finally I turned my attention from that planet. My universe was huge and a good father must divide his attention. It's a beautiful little mistake, this universe. But I would snuff out all these lights if it meant I could have my father back.

The trouble with becoming a writer he began, is that there is never enough time to write out the entire story. His nose crinkled at the sentence he had just written in sharpie, cursive with a swill and swagger to the s's. This was trying way too hard. Inquisitor Arensus, large in stature, pure of heart, broad chest and a mind of magic, - He scrapped the paper and threw it behind him. It fell the floor with a unsatisfying clack that wasn't crispy enough. The Mortimer twins, and Doctor Martyn- "Who would spell their name, something so common as Martin with a y? What is this, second grade?!" He scrapped another piece of paper. It was hard enough to start the story, it was harder to appreciate the crap you were trying to get down on paper. For weeks, years probably, he had built up a world of intrigue, politics and magic, something that resembled Django Wexler's musket magic series, something that would match the length of Steven Erikson, something that would inspire awe over the ages like Frank Herbert! He wanted to write it all down, in an exciting tale of friendship, loss, betrayal, everything! But the closest thing he could come up with that was anything near decent was: Magic man beats out even Mordecai with the help of twins that are magically connected and seem to get it on with their maid. His nose crinkled again, as he scrapped the paper.

"But I want one!" she shouted, clumsy fingers tearing at her now crinkled dress. The young girl stomped through her room, grunting and puffing in agitation to show her father just how angry she was. "My dear daughter, those creatures are incredibly dangerous," the king pleaded. "It would take many knights to roam the land in search of a matriarch." "I don't care!" screeched the princess, causing her father to wince. "I will be the queen someday! I have to emanate power and grace! And am I not already graceful, father?!" He patted his forehead with a small cloth and nodded eagerly. "Of course, love, of course." The princess sighed, clearly annoyed by how difficult her father was behaving. "And still you won't send someone to steal an egg from beneath a sleeping dragon? You can't love me that much, then!" She frowned in desperation, walking over to her bed, throwing herself onto the silky sheets in the most dramatic way. "Leave me be, father! Let me suffer in solitude," she muffled into the pillow. The king sighed. "You can't always get what you want, my dear child. I love you, but I won't sacrifice my men just for a rare pet." With that, he left her room, shutting the door behind him. The princess groaned, slowly sitting up and looking around. She just wanted a dragon and no one, not even her father, would stop her from getting one! She rummaged through her closet, searching for her favorite cloak. If her father wouldn't send knights to find a dragon, she would go herself! And she knew just the right stable boy to accompany her. Someone had to carry her belongings, after all...

I always check all of the tanks myself. It's just a habit I developed over a lifetime of diving, and like any professional, I took responsibility for all of my own equipment. Gale is a great grad student, don't get me wrong. But, well, frankly she just doesn't care that much about the diving. I understand her reticence at my solitary passion. She and any other person on the planet could simply type in our current coordinates, and see a RealMap 3D scan of the ocean floor below. The newer versions of RealMap even let you interact directly with the topographical scans through your Oculus, FaceMate, or even the other virtual reality hardware. But I'm old. I'm stuck in my ways, and I maintain that actual diving just can't be beat. I have always loved the physicality of sinking down into the depths, interacting directly with fauna, reefs and even wrecks. Nothing else even comes close. " How long do you think we'll be out here? " Gale asked, not even bothering to look up from her book. I almost grimaced at the insinuation that I was wasting her time, but I've grown used to her youthful impatience. If nothing else, maybe dragging her out into the ocean with me would help her learn some patience. " About 2 hours, all told " I responded. That was more or less true, but it's not like she could leave without me; my grant money paid her rent. Gale dispassionately rolled her eyes, mocking more than complaining. Two hours of isolation would give her time to study, especially since she was falling behind on the newest data sets coming out of California. She needed to get up to speed quickly, and she knew that. " Just remember, " I said, " if I'm not back in 2 hours, then something has gone wrong. Just engage the winch, and it will pull me back... " I was interrupted by her recitation of the speech I had hammered at her over and over so many times before. " It will pull you back at a rate of 10 feet per second, then I have to use the pole to bring you alongside the boat, and haul your fish-smelling carcass back on board. Watch the monitor for other boats, listen to the radio for your signal, or if you need me to winch you back. " We stared blankly at each other for several long seconds. " I got it " she said, turning back to her book. I hoisted the tanks onto my back, and made sure the regulator was delivering air. I pulled down my mask, and slid towards the edge of the boat. " Wish me luck " I nasally called to my indifferent companion. She waved noncommittally, indicating her utter lack of interest. I heaved my bulk gently backwards, allowing the weight of my gear to drag me down into the dark water below. The cold mass hit me hard, then caressed me down into the grey depths. I exhaled hard, checked my orientation, then righted myself, and began to slowly descend. Somewhere below me was an abyss of nothing. But for today, this was as far out as I could convince Gale to follow, and honestly we still had a lot to do back at the office today. Drifting further down into the water, I allowed all of those responsibilities do fade away, cast aside back at the surface. Down here, I was just a small part of the infinite flow of water, carried about on the currents, drifting down into the darkness. After a short time, the bottom came into view. I stopped myself just short of the actual sea floor, and hovered gracefully above the stones and muck. There was nothing of note as I journeyed along the bottom, but even just the variations of the ocean's detritus were able to hold my interest. No matter how many scans one looked at, there was still nothing like this in the world. The freedom of floating, heavenly in its embrace, and the adrenaline rush of the crushing depths surrounding me. This was my true love. Then, from somewhere out of the darkness, something was with me. I couldn't see anything beyond the murky water in front of me, and the silt below. But there was unquestionably something else there in the water. I could feel it moving along, shadowing my advance through the depths. From the corner of my eyes, I would see a shadow, or a flitting shape. But wherever I turned to observe my visitor, there was only the obscure depth of the ocean. But the presence around me grew stronger, and I could feel my pulse in my ears. My breathing was speeding up, and I knew I was risking injury if I allowed myself to panic. I forced myself to breathe in a slowing pattern, all-the-while aware of the unseen, yet undoubtedly moving manifestation there with me. I pressed the small button on my arm, sending an electric signal back to gale up on the surface. Any second now, the winch should begin retrieving me from this watery labyrinth, and its hidden occupant. But nothing happened. I pressed the button again, but still I remained there, drifting with the lazy current, steadily pursued by nothing, but fully aware that I was absolutely not alone. Suddenly, I felt myself thrust upwards by rushing water, hitting me in the chest hard. I could see no moving agent, nothing propelling the water and my frail humanity through the water. I found myself pushed out of sight of the bottom, and still far below the dim light of the surface. Instinctively, I exhaled hard, but my bubbles merely gathered about my face, refusing to reveal the direction of the surface. Beginning to panic, I exhaled hard once again, but still I simply found myself surrounded by my own exhalation. I went to press the button again, but found I was already hammering it in rapid succession. Without warning, I saw the darkness move beneath me. Some great unfathomable shadow lurched and lunged below me, towards me; menacing and demanding. I felt the air seize in my lungs, and my heart raced, nearly blinding me in its exertion. The shadows below climbed and shifted, alternately fleeing then surpassing me in my suspension. I saw the darkness itself seemingly reach towards me, threatening to consume my very existence. Suddenly I burst forth through the surface, and was blinded by the sky. The darkness below me receded, but I flailed in desperation towards the small figure of the boat. In the despairing moments it took for me to reach to boat, I could still feel the presence below, pacing my every move, seeming to be biding its time, relishing in my terror. I hauled myself onto the boat, and tore the mask from my face, I gasped at the fresh air, and scrambled backwards into the very center of the boat, waiting for my watery villain to spring forth at any second and destroy our little fibreglass island. I hollered at Gale, my voice almost a shriek. " Go! Go! Get us out of here! " " Wait, " Gale countered, " you're letting me drive the boat? Seriously? " My mind couldn't comprehend her words, but merely begged to be distanced from the murky horror beneath us. " Just go! " I shouted. " Go go go! " " Cool " Gale exclaimed, a gleeful grin alighting upon her face. She slid over to the driver's seat, and turned the ignition. The motor roared to life, and within seconds we were moving fast through the water. I peered over the side, but though I couldn't see the menacing shadow anymore, I felt that it was still there, ushering us from its home. I collapsed back onto the side, heavy with exhaustion, unable to move in my fear. " Anything interesting? " Gale asked as she captained us back towards the shore. I couldn't form the words to answer. All I could think was that the ocean had grown accustomed to our new absence, and was ready to ensure that we never again threatened its serenity. I for one would not be disturbing it again.

Samuel always thought his house was haunted. He somtimes would hear footsteps in the day, when he was trying to sleep. And when he would get back from his night shift, he would always find his stuff moved around. Also, he would find new stuff in his room. Once he found a brand new laptop. But he didn't mind. He would burn some inscense and go by with his day, or night to be precise. He was not going to move out because he thought his house was haunted. He had been living there for 10 years, since he was 22. Now being 32. This house was special to him. He was also a very lonely person. His lifestyle was a pullback in his social life, and his social skills. Samuel has always been a nocturnal person. He didn't hate the day, he just didn't found the appeal. Nights on the other hand, they were enchanting. He always liked the darkness that it provided, it's silence, it's calmness. So he took the night shift at his new job so he could live his dreamt lifestyle. Samuel was a heavy sleeper, he always slept very well. The only times he had heard the footsteps around the house was because he had woken up to pee. But nothing was never out of the ordinary. One day he woke up to his boss ringing him and telling him not to come in because there had been some technical difficulties. Of course Samuel was exastic. It wasn't the first time he had gotten a free night in his job, but he usually used them to walk around and appreciate the city. He woke up at 9:00 pm to have breakfast, usually he would wake up at 7:00 pm, but this time he could spare some more hours of sleep. He then went to make some breakfast, or dinner. And then sat to watch some late night shows. Everything was alright until a man entered through his front door. First they both were pretty shocked, just staring at each other. A million questions popped inside Samuels head; who is he? Why is he in my house? And how did he git the key? But it wasn't Samuel who spoke. "Who are you? And why are you in my property?" The stranger didn't seem hostile, just confused. Samuel was as confused as him. "I live here. How did you got a key into my house?" The man just appeard more confused. "No. I live here. Have been living here for 10 years." Samuel looked at him, he was serious. "No, I have been living here for 10 years." "What?" They both said it at the same time. "This doesn't make sense." The man said. "How did you went in and out of my house without me noticing?" "I could ask you the same thing." Then something clicked inside Samuels head. "Where's your room?" Samuel ask him. Although it was obvious he was going to point to the only bedroom in the house. "Back there, why?" "So, the laptop is yours." "What?" "And all the clothes I found that weren't mine in the drawers were yours too." "You were using my laptop and my clothes?" "I thought I had forgot I had bought them myself." At this point in the conversation the man was sitting in the couch with him. He was taller than him, blond and seemed the same age as him. "How come I haven't seen you sleeping in my bed? It still doesn't make sense how I didn't saw you all this years?" The man said. "I work night shift, making me nocturnal. I sleep at day, wake at night." "Huh." "You know, I thought the house was haunted." "Me too." The man sat back and try to process all of what had happen. "So, how are we going to do this?" "Do what?" "Well obviously I won't kick you out. And I don't have the money to move out so..." "You mean, still live like this?" "It didn't affect us for 10 years, why would it affect us now?" The man sat back again to think for a moment. And then he nodded, putting a hand over his head. "How did this even happen?" Samuel sat back for a bit and let it all set in. The fact that a man had been living in his house with him for 10 years, was bizarre. But it was even bizarre that he didn't knew either. But Samuel figured that everything that happens, happens for a reason. "What's your name?" Samuel asked suddenly. "Huh?" "Your name. I just figured that if we are going to be living in this house together, then atleast I need to know your name" The man sat up and smiled a little. "Malcolm." "Samuel." And just like that Samuel got his first friend in 10 years. (Just uploaded part two, its down below) (Also if you want to follow my facebook page its)

A black hole opened up in the center of the Earth, a meteor struck every major city, earthquakes started to rock ever inch of the planet, zombies rose from the ground, hurricanes and tsunamis struck every coastline, massive fires burst from the ground and lava poured out, electrical storms began to strike all metal objects with lightning. The Earth stopped rotating, all the water evaporated - thankfully canceling out the tsunamis - and a worldwide dystopian government began to deploy all of its nuclear weapons in order to flush out the resistance force which had been undermining it for the last Planck time or two. Aliens broadcast a message in some encrypted code before arming and firing their lasers and stuff right at the Earth. Everyone had about a nanosecond to think "Holy shit my fucking luck" - unless they were zombies, in which case it was probably more like "Fuck I can't get the brains if I die again" - before they were all obliterated. The entire planet collapsed in on itself as the black hole steadily sucked in the core, the mantle and the fine layer of crust, followed by the zombies, the storms and the meteors, the poor dystopian government, and the aliens. So yeah, it was a pretty bad day for everyone.

I've always lived my life alone in a world I thought was empty, desolate, and held no purpose or meaning. Sure, I've had "friends" and family but I've never really felt anything for them. All I ever felt was a sense of suffocation from their expectations of me. Will I ever amount to anything when I get older. I grew up living my life like that, forcing and pushing myself to learn new things, to become what other people want me to become. The fear of not being able to meet expectations made time drag on like a snail crawling on the sea floor. It got to a point where I wanted everything to stop. Between the studying and sleeping, the want to stop feeling the weight of expectation upon my shoulders, the want to stop asking myself if I can do it kept growing and growing. Every day was grueling, every hour, every minute, every second felt like an eternity. As time went on, the expectations grew. The more I learned, the more eyes laid upon me and measured my worth. I kept learning and learning wondering when will this end? It wasn't until I was 45 did I realize something was wrong with me. Those eyes that tried to see worth in me started to see fear, a monster. It wasn't until those eyes did I realize that I hadn't aged a bit for 20 years. My life changed that day. What I lived for wasn't to climb to the top of the mountain to see a sky empty of expectations anymore. I wandered for 222 years experiencing nothing but fear and loss. Fear of being seen as a monster, and the loss of the expectations from others. I learned that even I can not help from expecting things from myself, but what I expected not even I knew. I wandered the world trying to find a way to restore this feeling of expectation until one day, I found myself in a cemetery. That's where I met her. I was standing in front of a tombstone of my parents years before and wondered what they were up to and how I could ever rid myself of this ever living body. I stood there asking myself these questions, hoping I would find an answer. That's when she saw me and came to me and asked one simple question- "What brings you here?." It was at that moment everything clicked. I felt something akin to ice, slowly melting and turning a wheel inside me. I realized that my time froze so many years ago because I've never thought for myself before. I've never asked myself these self empowering questions before. I've never done anything for myself. That was the day time returned to me and I got to see what life is really all about. Leave feedback, I don't write very much (second prompt) but am working to improve. Thanks, I appreciate it.

"What the hell is this?" I shouted, waving the (not loaded) Glock around angrily. "Uh, it's your pistol, Chris. You know..... for your pistol duel? The one you've been scheduling for an entire year?" my lawyer said hesitantly. "NO! NO! This is unacceptable!" I ranted. "How the hell is this an appropriate pistol for a pistol duel? Have you ever seen a pistol duel? Nobody uses a freaking modern pistol! You use a flintlock pistol, or a six shooter, or some old timey gun! Not this new age piece of crap!" My lawyer ran his hand through his hair nervously. "Well, you see..... the insurance companies were only willing to sign off on modern guns. They didn't like the idea of older guns." That was the last straw. "Are you kidding me? You've been working on the paperwork for an entire year, and you couldn't get me any other pistol other than this?" I am death. Sounds like a cliche to open like that, huh? Well, frankly I don't care. I'm literally death. I take the lives of people whose time has come, and I do it swiftly, fast with no remorse. I always see the long and prosperous lives of the unworthy, and the short and disease filled ones of the poor. I experience every single moment of their life beforehand, but it never changes my view, the job has got to be done. The world is quite unfair, but my job is a moral greyzone because it's necessary. Without death there's no real life; what would you strive to be without a deadline? What would you want to do without an expiration date? How much time would you spend and cherish with your loved ones if there was no end? That's where I come in as said, I make life worth living. Steve Jobs, Leonardo Da Vinci, Muhammad Ali, all of them has been taken away by my hand. The thing that separates men and women like that is their understanding and acceptance of the natural order; their will and strength to fight, but their knowledge of when to stop. They accept the forthcoming and embraces the void. Okay, forget everything I just told you know, every single thing. There was one time where I actually felt remorse, where I questioned myself and the natural order of things. Here's a page I wrote from my memoir about that night: The whole night felt different..... There was something in the air, something undescribable. It was an ordinary night, but with a special fling to it. Darkness filled every corner, and lit up the sidewalk did several lampposts. I stepped upon the bricks and mortar of the low stairs towards the wooden door. It had fine insignias and metal brackets covering it. I flew right through it. A well lit house welcomed me, the Reaper, and I gladly accepted it. I navigated myself through the house until I found my client; or my victim as most would call it. "Finally," the silhouette spoke, "I've been waiting for you." "I assume you know who I am," I responded. "Oh, I'm sorry, hello mister Reaper," the old man let out. "And hello to you, fine gentleman." "You took your time, I awaited your arrival sixty years ago, I craved your arrival sixty years ago," the man said, coughing between words. I wondered. Why did the man tell me this? And more importantly, why did I get intrigued? "Well, your time has come, and I got interrupted. "Yeah, yeah, but everyone knows you have to sit and watch my entire life before you take me, it's common knowledge." Is deaths deepest, darkest secret common knowledge nowadays? Well, time flies. "That's correct," I answered after a few moments. I looked into his eyes, his oceanic blue eyes. I saw anger, despair, sorrow and pain. I didn't see a single flake of happiness; it was like the man was born in darkness, raised by the devil and adopted by a murderer. I saw his entire life, from the moment where he was born, to the one exactly now. I saw his first day in school and I saw the first time he got bullied and cried himself to sleep. I saw his first kiss and I saw the slaps from his mother. I saw his first love and his cheating girlfriend and the broken heart that came with it. His parents divorce, his cutting and low self-esteem. The death of his both siblings and the murder of his dad. The suicide of his mother and the following three attempts on himself. The alcohol, the drugs and the long nights. But in the abyss I was watching into, I saw a glimt of hope. I saw a beatiful girl; her name was Barina. They met in a church, and he fell for her instantly. They moved in together, got a child and lived like a perfect couple. They made each other whole, they made each other complete. It was a fairytale, and the man knew it. But I also saw the blade of a knife; dripping blood and gunshot wounds. I saw his dead wife and child, and I saw the face of the murderer. A hooded figure escaped the scene before the man came home from work. I witnessed the moment where he saw me capturing and taking his wife and child with me to the Realm, and I saw the same broken heart I've seen so many times before. Me, Death, shook with pain and sorrow for the man; I'd never been so reluctant to bring someone with me as I was now. I continued staring into his soul and I saw nothing but failed suicide attempts and tears; I saw nothing but misery. I looked at a broken man, one so fundamentally broken that you wouldn't actually believe his story. Although he'd been destroyed, he was one of the most generous and warm-hearted men on this planet. He had given his inherited wealth to the ones who needed it more than him, he had always told the truth and always been good to everyone. He was truly larger than life itself. "Go on, I'm waiting," the man broke the silence corrupting the dark room. "I admire you," was the only thing I managed to squeeze out. "You say that to everyone, don't you?" "No. No, I don't, you're special my friend. You're good." A few moments of silence ensued. "I just want to die, I just want to be ridden of this plague called life," he said. I saw a tear rolling down his wrinkled cheek. "This'plague' of yours, has saved countless souls from your faith; you have spread happiness, joy and liberating freedom to everyone you've crossed paths with." "Yeah, but it's all pointle This time I interrupted him. "You know, I've actually taken a few of those people. I remember a young lady with the name of Barina." "You know her..... I don't want to get reminded," he said. "She told me about you, she told me about all the good things you did. She told me how you lightened her every moment and loved her every single step," I responded. I saw the man trying to open his mouth but I continued talking. "I also remember a trubbled young fella. He died of gunshots to the chest, more specifically, police gunshots," I said. After a few thougtful moments he said: "No, it can't be..." "Yes it can, the man who killed your family." "I, I..." He got stuck on the first word," I..... Forgive him," he cried, tears flying around the room, drenching his leather coat. "That's the only thing he wanted," I said, "he only wanted your forgiving. He wa raised by an abusive father and mother, and took to crime early. He had no money and it was only supposed to be a robbery; he didn't count on the fact that your significant other and child was home." The man cried, he cried long a mournful. After an extended amount of time, the old and sick man opened his lips for the last time. He smiled and a tear of relief and joy bubbled down his torn face. "Jag ar redo nu," was his last words.

- I can't believe it! - said Jenny excitedly, watching tanks refill. - And all of this is possible thanks to your power, Jesse! Humanity will be able to reach outside of our own solar system, and we both will get to see it. I tried to answer, but was silenced with a fierce and passionate kiss. Jenny always made me smile, even back in the hero school. She is one of the few A-rank heroes who did not go for the typical "heroic" type of work. Jenny was always first and foremost an explorer. When there was some hidden pocket of reality, she was always there to unfold its secrets. When expedition went missing somewhere deep in the ocean cavities, she was first in line to try to find and rescue it. Always with her magic crystals and laser whip on hand, she explored all of the Earth and, eventually, solar system. But after a while, she fell in a bit of slump. What is the point, she said to me during our 5-year school reunion, if there was nothing else to explore? At that moment I understood what I have to do. I always liked Jenny, maybe even loved her. We were good friends, even though some said that one of the top students should not hang with C-rank, and especially not with Jesse "Free Refill." But after the graduation, she left to do heroic stuff, while I was just making money on my power, and doing my part in ending world hunger. Her confession, her miserable look that day shifted something in me. I had a plan, a purpose. It took me much less time than I imagined, but, after contacting some tinkerers I knew and blowing most of my savings on hiring couple more, we got to work. And, after it was done, I invited Jenny to come over. We slowly walked through the huge hangar in the middle of nowhere. I explained the meaning of different tubes, humongous empty tanks and other equipment. Then I showed her the fuel - most efficient liquid power source tinkers could create. After that, we went to the main control room - my lair. Jenny silently closed the door behind me, took the seat I offered to her. We sat in silence for a minute. Then she spoke: - This is all great, Jesse, but I'm not sure I follow. You said that all these tanks now belong to me, but what is the point if they are almost empty? To travel to closest planet, we would need to fill half of them at least! And there is nobody on Earth who could make this much! I just smiled. This was my point of triumph. - But what if you could always get a free refill?

He laughed confidently. Too confidently. He tossed his head back, letting his eyes rove the ceiling briefly before they scanned the bar to either side, looking for admiring glances. "So tell me, Christie, what's it like tossing guys around like that?" he said. "Stuff like that usually work?" I took a swig of beer. He'd bought. "You asked. I answered." "Okay, we'll play the game, then. Immortality. What's it like? Did aliens really build the pyramids?" His unctuous smile irritated me. I wanted to punch it off his face. But the other seventeen patrons probably wouldn't appreciate that. Neither would the bartenders. "I wasn't around for that, so I can't tell you." "Woah, woah, woah. What happened to immortality?" "Immortality isn't the same thing as eternality, bud." He held his bottle and free hand in the air. "My mistake. So, when were you, uh, born?" "1880." "So that makes you..... 134?" I clucked, my face alight with sarcastic approval. "You are quite the brainiac, aren't you? But the birthday's in November, so 133." Jake, as he'd introduced himself, flagged down a passing bartender. "Another two rounds, please. Same tab." Then he winked at her. I raised my eyebrows as her blue eyes met mine. "As long as it's got a big ass, bouncy boobs, and a sweet smile, it's game, huh?" Jake smiled at me. "Only you can deliver all that, babe. You seen Stone to Stone?" I shook my head and accepted the proffered bottle. "Can't say I have." "It's fantastic, really. Great documentary about Giza. Did you know they now think the spiral ramp theory is probably not correct?" "You know, I truly didn't know that." I looked across the bar, watching the lone man bathe in grey tendrils swirling from the tip of his cigar. I ignored Jake's eyes as they settled on my chest. "For an immortal, I expected a little better than that," he said. He paused before continuing. "So, what do you say, you up for learning something?" "That is the way to get me to spread my legs. Talk to me sardonically, insinuate stupidity, then turn yourself into a savior offering salvation from ignorance." He looked bewildered. "What?" I handed him my empty beer bottle. "Here you go, big shot. Take this home with you. Maybe you can fuck yourself with it. Might as well, since you won't be getting any help from me." I hopped off my stool and walked toward the door, but not before I winked at the smiling bartender. I'd known she would hear. I also knew Jake would be following me. He finally said something when we were alone in the alleyway. "Hey, bitch!" I turned around, knowing my surprise seemed genuine. "What do you want?" My former confidence appeared to have evaporated. "You think you can play me like that? Feed me that immortality bullshit, then belittle me in front of everyone?" "Oh, it wasn't bullshit. November 11th, 1880. And you belittled yourself." When you have more than a century's worth of experience, it's quite easy to recognize a fight before it occurs. I knew what was coming. His wild punches seemed slow, weak. The three men in 1980s Kabul had almost overcome me. But there were three of them. And they'd had knives. I ducked one blow, parried another, and evaded the third by yanking on the hem of his leather jacket. "You can still turn around, Jake," I said seriously. "I'm not going to fuck you, and I don't have to fuck you up either. You really don't understand what you're dealing with right here." A Guardian. Jake swayed drunkenly, reaching into his pocket. Oh, hell no. I leaped, twisting my hips and whipping my leg up. The spinning hook kick caught him in the jaw, and he crumpled. "Leggings do have their benefits." I vaulted onto him, straddling his chest and pinning his arms to the pavement with my knees. I winked. "I guess I was wrong. I will spread my legs for you." He groaned, blood leaking from the corner of his mouth. "Let..... me go." I leaned forward, dragging myself over his battered face. "I think I'll fly to Argentina tomorrow. It's the only country I haven't visited yet. But, unfortunately, I have to leave now. That innocent old man, the one smoking at the bar? He hunts people like me. And unlike you, he's someone I actually have to worry about."

"Tell me boy, what do you see in our new students?" the headmaster asked me, staring intently at the door through which they had just left. The headmaster knew - he had known for a long time - about my peculiar gift. I could see the danger in people. I could tell with a glance that manifested as a number in my head, on a simple one to ten scale. Dr. Butler, the headmaster, said the perfect wholeness and symmetry of the numbers was a sure sign that this was a gift from God, and as such I was to use it to warn all good Christians of His enemies. "Most of the boys are a three or four," I told him. I glanced at the headmaster's ledger. At the top of each page was written, Shrewsbury School for Boys and at the bottom Anno Dmoini 1818. Each new boy's name was written on the left, and as he read aloud each one, I gave the number. "Davies?" "Three." "Smith?" "Two." "Roberts?" "Four." "Hughes?" "Seven." "Seven? " "Yes, sir." I stirred uncomfortably in my chair as the headmaster wrote an extended not in his ledger, shaking his head at the horribly dangerous boy Hughes. Normally a seven was reserved for a full grown man who had served at least one tour in the military, or for certain criminal types. "Dr. Butler," I interrupted him. "Yes boy, what is it?" "The seven..... that's not the highest number I saw today." "You saw an eight? Good grief, which one was that?" "No sir, not an eight. A ten." The colour drained from the headmaster's face as he sat suddenly frozen in his chair. "You're sure?" he asked, "Absolutely sure?" I nodded, the fear showing in my face as well. "Well out with it then, which one was it?!" The headmaster was half standing over the ledger, reaching for more paper and his seals. Presumably all the teachers and staff would be warned about this boy. I leaned over the desk and looked down the ledger, trying to find the name. "This one," I said, pointing, "down at the bottom of the first page." The headmaster seemed surprised. "Are you absolutely sure?" he asked, "Why, his brother has been with us for four years already, and he is no more than a three." "He is a ten," I said, confirming. Dr. Butler began moving about his desk again, mumbling to himself about how he must warn everybody, and that any bad behavior from this boy would be entirely unacceptable. I just sat and stared at that name, which would now haunt me as the only ten I would ever see: Darwin.

I woke up with a start. It was one of those falling dreams I think, the kind that you wake up from bouncing on your bed. I'd never been able to remember the details of those dreams before and this one was no different; all I was left with was the remnants of a feeling of terrified awe. I swung my legs off the edge of the bed left my blankets behind for the frigid morning air. I don't think anyone gets used to the shock of cold that slides over you from all directions when you leave a warm bed. As I walked to the shower I tried to remember what I had dreamt during the night. I knew it was futile, but it always drove me crazy nonetheless. I quickly turned on the hot water and stepped into the scalding stream. I felt like standing in a waterfall of lava compared to the temperature of the air, but my body adapted soon enough. I relaxed and washed my hair as the bathroom filled with steam. I began to wonder why we forget dreams in the first place. Is it something our minds don't want us to know? Is it another life we lead that we aren't allowed to know about? Does everyone have a separate sleeping personality that just had reeeeeally bad short term memory? I chuckled to my self as I stepped back out of the shower. The steam filling the room and fogging the mirror had made the room comfortably warm. I enjoyed the rough feeling of the towel against my skin as I dried myself off. I wiped down the mirror and put some toothpaste of my toothbrush. Humming a little tune, I started to brush my teeth. Ah, how I love the taste of- The toothbrush fell from my mouth as I saw myself in the mirror, the white flecks of foam flying up to land on me along with my likeness that stared back at me with a shocked expression on its face. A scar as wide as my thumb and as long as my torso extended down from my right shoulder to my left hip. Slightly raised from the surrounding skin, my first thought in my state of shock was how similar it was to the line of toothpaste and saliva that had been slung across the counter when my toothbrush dropped. Then reality came back and I stood there in disbelief, trying to comprehend what I was seeing. I didn't have a scar like that. I've never even been seriously injured. It certainly wasn't there last night, and seeing how my sheets weren't covered in blood I didn't sustain any injuries in my sleep. I wasn't an expert on scars, but it also looked old. The skin around and on top of it was completely healed, with none of the pink that is the trade mark of new skin to be seen. I traced its path with my thumb, taking note of how clean the cut must have been to create such a smooth scar. I remembered my grandpa showing me a similar scar he had, on his side. Grandma said he got it when he fell off the roof cleaning the gutters, but he told a different tale. "It was inflicted by an enemy warrior on the field of battle." Grandpa would say. "You can't tell anyone, especially your grandma, but when I was younger I used to go on adventures all the time. Every once in a while I still do. Someday I'll show you how to go adventuring, but till then it will be our little secret alright?" I would always swear myself to secrecy, but it was a point of pride between my friends and I that my grandpa was an adventurer. One day, though, grandpa just disappeared. The cars and grandma were still there, his shoes were still in the front closet, but grandpa himself was just..... Gone. My finger came off the lower end of the scar, just below my left hipbone. I looked agin into the mirror and was surprised to see my reflection staring back at me, but not the way I was staring at it. The me in the mirror had a slight smile on his face as he crossed his arms. My arms remained motionless at my sides as he spoke. "So, ever wonder where Grandpa went?"

The bullet only hurt for a second and then it was over. It had torn, really quite easily, though the skin wrapped like a serafin wrap around my shoulder, shredding through the hot, pulsing muscle and straight at the paper thin fabric of my green wind breaker. Blood had squirted out like red paint, not really like it does in the movies, though. It was more like one big, throbbing stream, a thousand pricks of pain and then darkness. Never really expected it to end like that, I'll be honest. And then my eyes opened. I was in a room, dull, grey, administrative. A single, metallic table dominated, if you could describe it that way, the room. A few pictures, basic, bland scenery of mountains and valleys hung from disturbingly clean nails jutting out of the ball. I was in a reasonably comfortable chair, padding on the bottom with some kind of weird blue fabric. Maybe sixty degrees, I don't know. I stood up, heart racing and hands grasping for the edge of the table as the blood rushed to my head. My hands felt for the bullet wound, but didn't find. "Hello?" I screamed, voice echoing. I rushed to the door and tried it, but it didn't give. I tried again. More time. Then, I threw myself against it and heard something crack. I did it again, but the crack didn't appear again. "Whatcha up to?" The voice was commanding, maybe a little Scottish. I whirled and they're he stood. A tall man, older, regal grey hair in a dapper dark navy overcoat. Black slacks and what looked like mid twentieth century combat boots. "Who the hell are you?" I whispered. "Why," He laughs, "I'm the Doctor. Who are you?" "Quinn. Quinn Mallory. Where am I? Did you put me here?." "Oh, no, of course not. That'd be incredibly rude. And, besides, I don't even really know where here is. How did you end up in this," He looks around, a light frown on his," charming little room?" I ran my hands through my hair and sighed. "I got shot." "Oh my," "What?" "This might be purgatory?" My eyes widened and the Doctor laughed. "No, I'm just kidding. This is probably just a pocket universe. These things tend to work themselves A definitive pop and and a loud thump and there was another. The first thing I noticed were his eyes; They were wild, crazy eyes, shot through with violent red vessels. He was in a long, baggy hoodie, more yellow than red and a dull, black beanie with some kind of red skull logo on the side. His jeans were low, but I get the sense that that was a style issue. "Wait? What the hell,? His voice was hoarse and his sentences bounced with his yellowed teeth. "Hi, I'm the Doctor!," Voice unnaturally chipper. "Where am I? Who is this BITCH?" He took a step forward, his voice a scream. "Woah, calm down buddy!" I reached out my hand and he smacked it out of the way. The Doctor's eye brows bounced and his mouth widened into a smile. "Don't touch me, BITCH. Don't you touch me. Where am I? Did one of you put me here?" He looked around, grabbed one of the pictures off the wall and spiked it to the ground. "Manners, sir." The Doctor extended his hand, "I'd suggest you shake this," Baggie-Hoodie looked at him and then extended his hand, slowly. He grabbed it and the Doctor smiled. Tension defused. "I'm Quinn," "Jesse. Where the hell are we? "That's just what we were discussing," The Doctor walked around the room, testing the walls with little light shoves. He tried to the door to find it still locked. "This doesn't make any sense," Jesse pushed against the walls, banging with his fists," Let me out of here!" "You'd be surprised what does and doesn't make sense," I sighed. I heard the door unlock and spun around. The Doctor by the door, now slightly ajar with a whirring and glowing metal rod in his right hand. "It's a screwdriver,"

"Why do we do this to one another?..... Why do we hurt the one's we love?" She whispered lovingly in my ear as the steak knife plunged deeper into my gut. It had been an odd year leading up to our latest anniversary, Claire wasn't her usual talkative self, she was distant with an almost harrowed look on her face, like she was in mourning. I was worried obviously, had been for some time, ever since my retirement she seemed to lack something, that spark, that energy, which I loved her for. I thought it was our son moving out to go to college, maybe she felt like she lacked a sense of purpose in her life, not uncommon for housewives of a certain age living deep in suburbia. "I don't know" I grunted attempting to remain conscious. "Not surprising, you never knew anything, Paul. You were too stupid! Do you think I wanted you to find out like this? I wanted you to find me for yourself, to know me, I wanted it to be so special." She twisted the knife. Twenty five years on the police force, twenty years a detective and seventeen married to the love of my life, the only blotch on my perfect record, my perfect life was the Hobbs End Butcher. Always three steps ahead of the department, the FBI, me. The profilers said his knowledge of police procedure, likely meant he was ex law enforcement, or current, but they never liked to err such suspicions in front of us. His brutal killing of men, much taller and imposing than he was, likely linked back to something primal, oedipal. the killing of an abusive father figure perhaps? Maybe that's why he singled me out, maybe I reminded him of whoever it was he was really trying to hurt. "I thought I knew you" "No you don't, Iv'e always had to try to show you myself, but you never saw me" When I found the first note meticulously wrapped in a red ribbon next to a bloodied unrecognisable corpse of a local gangbanger, I knew it couldn't be good. I'd seen combat, I'd killed men, it's what made me so good at my job, when you see someone breathe their last breath because of you, it's not something you can just forget about. I was good at spotting that desensitization in others, that latent guilt, the same kind I felt. But when killers start toying with you, there is no guilt, there's only pride in a good days work and I could never understand that, never will. That's why I couldn't catch him. "Why, why do this? Why now?" "You retired, like a coward retreating to a comfortable life, I couldn't live like this anymore. You needed to see the real me, like you used too. Before you gave up." The notes had been getting progressively personal, somehow he knew how to get under my skin, I feared for my family, their safety. Months even years would pass between killings sometimes but the tell tale note would always be there mocking me for my complacency and lack of clairvoyance. I grew tired eventually, I'd see the note with its spine chilling message and shrug it off, the good looking men in sunglasses and black suits had taken over the case almost fully due to my incompetence in catching that ghost. All I cared about was going home to Claire, making up for lost time, I thought she'd be happy when I retired. "But I never gave up." "What?" Her grip on the knife loosening. "I couldn't, I tried but couldn't, I hid it from you, at first to protect you, but then because I wasn't sure if I really knew you." I wanted to understand why she was upset with me, but the latest murders drove me to look into the case again instead, the same all too familiar brick wall forming around every corner. I hid it from her as best I could I didn't want her to think I was falling back into bad habits, besides she seemed to be having enough problems herself without me adding to them. But there was something about the latest murder, the note, there was something familiar about it, something less mocking but more loving. "We've grown old together, shared so much with one another, it's time we stop playing these games." My suspicions arose when I caught a glimpse of her writing my anniversary card, almost the same words, surely a coincidence? But pieces began to fall in place like they never had done before and the closer we got to our anniversary the happier she seemed as if a great weight was about to be lifted from her shoulders. I hoped for divorce papers, perhaps a surprise second honeymoon to reignite the spark, anything else. "You knew?" "Of course I knew, I love you, you couldn't hide from me forever." I brushed her face tenderly, tears of joy welling up in her eyes. Sharing a last moment before the grim reality of the situation dawned. "Actually I think I do know why we hurt the one's we love" I reach down calmly attempting to identify the all too familiar feel of cold steel. "Why?" "Because they hurt us first" She hears the metal clink too late. I got home late from the precinct, attempting to find something, anything in the case files to dispel my fears, nothing. I walked into the candlelit living room, the table laid out in meticulous detail for our anniversary dinner. My nerves calmed as I saw her laying out the steak dinner a smile greeting me as I approached the table, taking my seat. "You're late" "I'm sure my gift will make it up to you" "Not before I give you mine" The card was wrapped meticulously in red ribbon, dread filled my heart before the steak knife pierced my abdomen, I took a moment to collect my thoughts as my body fell to the floor prostrate in shock and remembered the sidearm attached to my ankle. I loved my wife but lately I hadn't trusted her.

Aerius looked ahead, and saw he had another 150 meters before what appeared to be a sudden drop. He perched his foot on a rock to stabilize himself as he reached in his pocket to pull out a piece of paper rolled up into a dirty rubber band. Warm smoke from his cigarette drifted up into the air, filling the cavern with the scent of Marlboro ultra light red Tobacco 2. His boots were wet, soaked through, though Aerius no longer felt the chill gripping his feet. Now, he only felt excited, confusion...and a small but growing tinge of fear. Im definitely past the 1700 meter mark...where the fuck am I? According to the map, this particular cavern was only about 1700 meters long, and about 50 meters under the ground. I've gone twice that distance! And about four times as deep! Aerius thought. Aerius realized that in all likelihood, he was the first to have ever gone so far in this cave. In fact, he was likely the first person ever to be in the cave at all. Afterall, it had only been discovered last week. The U.S National office of geospace intelligence had teamed up with geologists to create the first all-inclusive global infrared mapping off the earth's cavernous systems. Using infrared sateliette imagery, every cave and spacious underground region in the world could now be mapped and measured. The project was originally a means to discover underground military bases and terrorist cells, but U.S special forces was also making use of it for training purpose, and for a bit of off-day excitement. CIA SAD operative Aerius Black was now one such beneficiary of modern day technology. Project GIST- for Global imaging of Subterrain Topology- was still in it's infancy, and so mistakes were be expected. Projects were usually refined and updated after the first few months of it's initiation as mistakes and glitches were uncovered. Of course it has to glitch out in the cave I go through, Aeruis thought. Aeruis continued to hike through the rough floor of the cavern. The ground was very uneven, and he constantly had to shift his gear and he climbed and jumped and bear-crawled his way through. I should have refilled my bottle at that stream earlier. I never thought I'd.. Suddenly Aeruis stopped. Up ahead, coming from appeared to be below the ledge of the drop...was a shining light. And not just a dim ebb from a flashlight, but a bright, golden glow, almost as if a ...city was there, right below the ledge. What the fuck....is THAT?!?!? It's not possible, Aeruis thought... I'm the first human in the world to have ever been in this cave! Then he started to hear it. The sound. A low, high pitched but unmistakable blinking sound, like something from a starwars ship. The sound started to get louder, and louder, and louder.... And suddenly aeruis heard a huge roar, and MASSIVE light started to come from below the ledge. Aeruis watched, stunned, as a huge metal orb rose from under the ledge into his field of vision. The orb was huge, maybe 50 feet ion diameter, and covered in red flashing lights. Before Aeruis could think, he was suddenly hit in the chest by what appeared to be a thick cloth, and then suddenly started drifted towards the giant orb. He was being carried to the Orb, and as he passed by, he looked down and saw something he couldn't believe...it was a city. A huge, bright spiraling city, over 1000 feet below him. He was sudden in a massive chamber, thousands of feet wide and thousands of feet deep. He could see the round spherical walls of the chamber miles away from where he was, and before he could process any of this, a hatch opened and Aeruis was carried into the ship. He found himself in a room unlike any room he had ever seen. The room was bright, but with an odd dark red glow. It was filled with machines that Aeruis has never seen before, like something out of a scifi movie. Aeruis noticed that the roof was a solid black color, and appeared to waving and bobbing, as if made out of some kind of Jelly. " Hello, Aeruis. " Aeruis snapped his head down to see a tall figure standing before him. The figure was about 6'3, dressed in strange looking clothes he had never seen before. On his wrist was a metal band with little buttons and lights, and on his feet were strange boots, also with blinking lights. He was about 22 years old, and in excellent shape. " I see you've found our hidden kingdom. " " I...what? " The figure gave a half smile. " Our home. It appears that you've found it. " Cia agents were trained to think quickly, and never get fazed, no matter what they came across. Aeruis still wasn't sure if he was going insane, or if he had banged his head and was in a coma somewhere, but his training kicked in and brought himself together. " What is this place? Who are you? And how do you know my name? " " This is the hidden kingdom of Valaco. I am Mortago of the high council, sent out to meet you. We've been watching your trek over the last few hours. We would had sent to get you sooner but we weren't sure you'd come this far. " " Tracking me? Tracking me how? And what IS this kingdom? Where did it come from? Aeruis realized they must have been descending and how now reached the bottom. " Please ," Mortago said with a beckoning wave of his hand, " come this way " Aeruis stepped out of the orb, and marveled at what he saw A massive city, bigger than anything he had ever seen. It was like downtown toyko or manhattan, but bigger, brighter, with more lights. The buildings had a very futuristic appearance, like something you'd see in a science fiction movie. Flying objects were traveling around, and waves of light filled the air. Aeruis then noticed clapping and gasping and cheering, and realized that there was a large crowd around the ship. " Wave! You are the first non valaconen they've ever seen! " Aeruis, still stunned, managed a wave. Suddenly, a much smaller orb appeared in front of them, and a hacth opened up. " Come inside! " Aeruis sat down next to Mortago, and the craft took off and starting flying over the city. Aeruis watched out of the window, still amazed and unsure what to say. " I imagine you have many questions, Aeruis. I'll answer them all, but before you do, I'll give you a brief summary of the history of valaco. Thousands of years of ago, human civilizations were visited by extraterrestrial beings- aliens, you might say- and they bestowed upon us great gifts and knowledge. Humans suddenly knew of the sciences and arts, and were able to build things they had never been built before. These beings were worshipped as gods, until one day, ANOTHER species arrived from the stars to attack both humans, and our own alien-gods. These invaders were not interest in us, but of our visitors, and destroyed all traces of them and their technology. They were at war, you see, and our visitors were hoping to establish earth as a base. Our people were able to escape into this cave, were we built this city with the sacred knowledge of the stars. For thousands of years, we've stayed hidden in fear that the invaders will return. But now, through a story that's quite long and perhaps appropriate for a better time, we've learned that the invaders have been destroyed, and we no longer have to fear.....im sorry if that's a little rushed, im just trying to get you the basics. " Aeruis's head was spinning. He looked at mortago: " I...this is incredible. We've always had evidence and signs of something the ancients has we couldn't explain...recovered artifacts we didn't know where they came from " Aeruis mind jumped to a secret installation 500 meters underground in Alaska, where the government had it's possession certain...machines, with properties that scientists couldn't explain. " Yes, Aeruis, Olosis bass on the brooks range does indeed contain alien craft and tools. " Aeruis was, again, stunned... " how do you know of olosis base?? it's the most tightly kept secret the us govern... " " Please ," mortago waved off with a laugh, " there is nothing we do not know. Our technology far exceeds yours. " Aeruis slumped into his seat, looking out of the window.... He could see people walking around, some hovering by the metal boots they had on, and other orbs whizzing by. He looked at mortago " everybody looks so young...I don't see anyone old. Or even my age! " Mortago laughed. " most of us are much older than you! I myself am 895. No, we've mastered biorenegation technologies. Everybody has the body and mind of one in their early 20s, and we do not age. We will answer any and all questions you have...but after that, there is much we have to discuss. You may find that you have a special purpose here...and a very special role. " " What do you mean? " The orb started to descend down towards what looked like a massive temple, well over a mile long. " Now that it is safe for us to come out in the open, we want to reveal ourselves to the world. There is a man sleeping across the room from me, his skin's a dark grey and his ears are pointed at the tips. I was confused, but I felt this sudden urge to go back to sleep. I dreamt of barren lands, a storm of ash sweeping around me as my lungs filled with the putrid soot that enveloped me. A woman was speaking in a tongue i never heard of before. I tried to scream but nothing came out until I woke up. I was being shaken awake by the man who was sleeping in the same room. " Wake up" , Wake up! Why are you crying? Wake up... You were dreaming. What's your name? I looked at his familiar face as my mind was racing. I can't believe it, I must be dreaming, i have to be dreaming. I look outside the room as one of the ship's guards was coming towards us. I turned back towards the familiar looking man and told him my name. " Well, not even last night's storm could wake you. The Guard approached, the lines on his face showed that he took his job seriously. " This is where you get off, come with me" . As I left the boat I was greeted by the morning sun and the crisp fresh air of the Bitter Coast Region. In front of me was the town of Seyda Neen and one of the local guards. My shackles were removed as the exchange was made and the two brothers said goodbye to each other. Not much thought went into filling out my census paper and that made me nervous, no character creation, no filling out a set of abilities.... than it hit me, I was myself. I was given a duty to deliver a small package to a man by the name of Caius Cosades in the town of Balmora. In the next room awaited the guard that brought me into the office. Carl Thompson awoke to open the paper. On the cover Larry his legacy. Years of planning and preparation, all printed up into a single news article. THE ATLANTIC ALCHEMIST SAVES ANOTHER LIFE. It was the fourth one in his career. They didn't know he was intending to kill his victims but apparently poisons weaken in potency over the years and Carl suffered a few years of nerves before he actually tried killing his first. Poison in their coffee every morning for a month. Unfortunately slow dose murder makes one feel ill. The kind if ill you seek a doctor for. And during their tests they discovered early stages of stomach cancer that would have proven fatal of not caught earlier. The second and third was a couple he tried to kill via a house fire. Their doors and windows were locked by call to ensure no escape but a nearby cat caught in a tree saw to make the fire departments response time a record breaking minute and thirty two seconds. The couple were told of the jammed exits and they sued the landlord for endangering them. The settlement moved them to a better neighborhood and away from Carl. Now this. A victim he was determined to see through to the end! He even left a calling card of sorts. The beautiful Emily Fallbrooke was his intended target. He got new poison, a knife, a gun. He want sure how he would kill her but he wanted her dead. He followed her towards her home and pulled her inro an alley to do the deed. A metal cup clatters against the stone floor, snapping me awake. Buttercup, my cat, must have knocked it over. He is usually roaming around at night. I roll my eyes, and glance at the window. The horizon is a shallow shade of blue that suggests dawn is approaching. I pause, hair standing on end, did I hear a gasp? Buttercup brushes against my leg and sleepily mews. I'm probably just tense. Today is my inauguration and my stylist will be here " At the crack of dawn. " Many prophecies have been made about the day I take the throne. I am to be one of the best prophets the kingdom has seen in decades, and as the king, my foresight will accomplish much good. It has been stated that I will expand the kingdom, amend many laws holding us back, and finally rid ourselves of the thief's guild that has plagued our land for so long. I step out of my room to get ready for the day. Everything freezes. My stomach clenches and starts stinging, then burning with pain. I open my mouth and inhale. A hand covers my mouth, stopping my scream. I fall to my knees, the pain spreading to the rest of my body. I look down and see the razor blade in my gut, I start to fall on my face, and snap awake, panting. It was only a dream. I'm up early, because of my nightmare, and I'm covered in sweat, for the same reason. I cautiously check around my door and see no one. Rolling my eyes I remind myself, it was just a dream. I get a bucket and start filling my bath with water. I always do simple tasks like this myself, thinking that paying a servant to do it will make me spoiled. I do not want to forget that as king, I will be a servant to my people, not the other way around. Targiston, a famous prophet that lived a few hundred years ago, wrote me a few tips on kingship, and I read his notes daily. One of his first was to find a job that would be done routinely by a servant, and do it myself to remind me to serve my people. I start reviewing my speech and edit it where I feel to do so. My inauguration is tomorrow and my speech must be perfect. Receiving prophecy is more and art of asking the right questions, and sensing if the answer is yes or no. The game 20 Questions was actually invented as a way to practice this. Only three prophets have ever been recorded as having had a vision, and all for incredibly important things. Looking out the window I see it is dusk. I must have spent a long time editing my speech. My dream re-enters my mind. David, one of the knights, is outside, so I ask if we can spar for a bit to get my mind off of " things ." We clash swords until dusk. I thank him for going easy on me and he replies " You're better than you give yourself credit for! " and We part ways. Exhausted from the swordplay, I walk into my room, drop my sword on the ground, and fall asleep as my head hits the pillow. A metal cup clatters against the stone floor. Every muscle in my body tenses. I think of buttercup, the cat I got to help with my stress. I carefully turn over to find him on the floor, next to my sword. Chills run up my spine. I slowly get up to grab my sword and hear it, a slight gasp. He knows I'm awake. He must be a member of the thief's guild here to save his clan. As silently as I can, I pick up my sword. Remembering the dream I jump out of my room swinging my sword to where he was. My blade hits the wall the man's torso by a hair's breadth. I lunge. He jumps out of the way and slashes. My training kicking in, I jump back, into stance. The guards are climbing the stairs. The man, a panicked look on his face jumps forward, grabs my sword, cutting his hand, and stabs me with his knife. I cry out. He runs to the window, and by the way the pain is spreading I can tell the blade was poisoned. Vision fading, I fall to my back, and wake up. I hear the cup, clattering on the floor, It chills my soul. I can tell this time is not a dream. I immediately roll out of bed using the noise of the cup to cover my bed's squeak. Buttercup meows in protest to me landing on his tail. I pick up my sword silently. And prepare to fight. I pause at my door, and call out " Guards! " In a panicked voice. The man bolds into the room, and stabs at me. Instinctively, I raise my sword, and his razor glances off of it, deflecting the blow. I slash at him and he jumps back. The guards are almost here. I circle the man to get closer to the door. He searches for a way around my sword. I look back for a second as the guards enter the room. David, the knight I sparred with yesterday is the first one in. I look back to the man, and he has already thrown his razor at me. I jump out of the way, and David stabs the man. Relieved, I thank him, and catch my breath. We laugh, and then I ask him to accompany me as I get ready for my speech. When we get outside, I see a shadow in a nearby tree. Then the crossbow bolt goes through my lung. I fall, and wake up, to a metal cup, clattering on the floor.

Dear Katie, It feels strange to be sitting here writing this to you. Especially in the form of a letter, emails seem to be a way of life, but I have to say that watching my pen move over this page has a certain draw. I never thought I would need to write a letter to you. In my mind you should be right here with me. If I close my eyes I can imagine that you're right beside me, our shoulders touching while we hold hands and enjoy each other's company. Even in my imagination my hands are a bit sweaty, but you've always made me nervous Katie. I remember you used to worry about that, you would say "just be your self. I'll love you anyway." I'm not sure I ever convinced you that I was being myself, the nervousness couldn't be helped. I couldn't stand the idea of hurting or disappointing you. Lot of good that does me now. It took weeks to write this. Seeing your smiling face in my mind and sometimes barely remembering your voice hurt too much. When the pain was all I knew you were my life raft in the ocean. Now I just have to drown until the waters subside. Know that I don't blame you, special. Remember when I called you that all the time? Anyway, I really don't. Everything was always intense between us. Amazing highs and amazing lows. I'm so glad you found someone that makes you happy. I used to tell you that as long as you were happy I would be as well. That's at least somewhat true. I'll never date again, people tell me never is a long time but it's not the same. Who knew I would be a one woman man? But I am and I found and lost the only woman I'll ever want. Ever. This could ramble on for a long time so I'll wrap things up. Know that I still love you, I never stopped. I don't blame you for moving on. It sounds ridiculous but sometimes I hold out hope that our story isn't over. That somewhere down the line you'll love me again. Hah, pathetic. Be safe special. P.S. I recently lost and then found the bracelet you made me senior year. It doesn't fit anymore so it stays around the gear shift in my car. Love you always, Alex.

"Good night, Jefferson." "Good night, Patchie." "Good night, Edna." "Good night, Sniffles." And good night, me! It had been a long day in the house. Cooking, cleaning, feeding the little rascals, watching the lottery results on TV (still no luck!), calling Margaret to catch up (she was in the hospital, poor dear; I planned to visit her the next day). But finally, it was time for bed, after some light reading. Just as I was good and cozy under the covers, a furry little ball pounced on my arm. "Sniffles, no! No snuggles on the bed, you'll get hair everywhere." I had to get up to let him out of the bedroom. He always found a way in! In bed once again, I shut my eyes, waiting for the sandman. I felt sorry for poor Sniffles: he always needed cuddles, poor thing! I had gotten him at the animal shelter, and if his left ear was anything to go by, his previous owners had been awful to him. Still, he got along very well with the others as soon as I got him home; Edna in particular. Those two! Always together, wrestling and napping, always restless and planning a raid on the cupboards. Patchie was very different. She was a wise old cat, and she knew that stealing was pointless; I was a good owner, and meals were always on time. A few years previously, she had given birth to half a dozen adorable children; amongst them was Jefferson, the laziest cat I have ever known. Once, he had tried chasing a mouse, and given up after three steps. My lovely family. My silly, fuzzy family. I fell asleep. Moments later, I was awake. There were whispers. A stranger in the house? Two? I slowly got up from the bed, and reached inside the dresser for my gun (an older woman has to protect herself, in this day and age). Clutching it tightly against my chest, I opened the door, and peered outside. I couldn't be sure of where the voices were coming from, but I realised just how high-pitched they were. Like children's. What would children be doing here, in my home? I took a few steps forwards. Were these kids in the living room? Edging closer to the door, I finally started to hear them clearly. "Shut up." "But..... We can't..." "I said shut up. We can, and we have to. This is the plan." "I don't like it." "You don't have to like it! You just have to do it." "Yes mother." "Good! Do we all agree, then?" "I..." "We know you have reservations." "She's nice!" "So you keep saying. That's not the point. They're all nice, in their own way." "Not..... Not all of them." "Don't worry, little victim. We don't need you. We don't really need you." "What if I..." "What if you tell her? You keep trying. And she doesn't listen, does she?" "I..... It's..." "Be quiet. We're going over the plan one more time." "Wait! No! I'm..... I'm warning her! I'm going to tell her right now!" "You won't." And suddenly, there was a flurry of hissing and screaming on the other side of the door. I could hear the pain and the violence, the bloodshed. Without thinking, my hands sweating around the gun, I opened the door. And I shrieked. The mangled body of Sniffles, bloodied and torn apart, was surrounded by Edna, Patchie and Jefferson. All three of them had gory faces and paws. By reflex, I did exactly what I had been taught at the shooting range. I pointed the gun and squeezed the trigger. I shot and shot until all I could hear was ringing in my ears and until my finger was sore. I shot them until they stopped moving. My four cats were laying in front of me, in a mess of flesh and fur. I dropped the gun and ran outside, screaming.
