"I'm sorry, Batman, but I just can't do that for you. If I make an exception for one person, everyone will want another fifteen minutes to talk to their dead loved ones." When I stared directly into his cowl he met me with a tortured expression. The dozens of separate numbers floating above his head were changing erratically. Some of those numbers were showing values that made no sense, and others that had been counting down were starting to count back up. They all appeared suddenly, more every day. "But what I saw..." He started. "I made a deal with you, and I held up my end of the bargain. The Devil is never allowed to lie as long as the conditions are met!" His anger began to flare, after what he saw it was understandable. "I offered to let you speak with the three deceased individuals you cared about most for fifteen minutes. It isn't my fault that the only person you saw was the Joker."

As much as it had pained me to part with even the least of my hard-won trinkets, I'd known that I was getting an amazing bargain when the disheveled man had snatched the Tin Flask from my hand so may years ago. He'd immediately uncapped it and taken a long draw of its unlimited whiskey, tossing me the Silver Watch almost absently. I'd explained to the man that the Flask was only good for getting drunk; it wouldn't pour into anything other than a human's mouth. One couldn't use it to fill up barrels, then re-sell the mysteriously generated whiskey, for example. I was naive in those days, and didn't understand why someone would possibly give up the Watch in return for free booze. But now I comprehended more fully than I'd have ever wished. I snapped the Watch's face closed with a click, and tucked it into my vest pocket. The other end of its silver chain was hooked onto one of my vest's buttons in a style I knew was outdated. Lina had always made fun of me for dressing like the "evil city-slickin' businessman" from old spaghetti westerns. Her attempt at an American accent when she said it was adorably earnest. She was laying in the bed in front of me, but I'd been lost in memory of the person she used to be. I'd stopped to think about her dark skin, her dark eyes, and the dark curls of her hair. The brilliant smile she'd brandished to devastating effect. Her songbird laugh that she seemed to catch her by surprise every time. I'd stopped to think, and the world had stopped with me. At first, we thought this would just be another hardship. A struggle that we would weather together. Then we found that the chemo wasn't working, and it was like she'd plunged off a cliff without me. Once I got past my own denial, I thought I might be able to use my trinkets to save her. The Bone Needle could perfectly stitch shut any wound without thread but closing a surgical incision was not the issue. The Ivory Kettle could endlessly pour whatever liquid was placed inside it, but there was no shortage of blood for transfusions, should Lina require one. The Glass Ladle could pass through flesh to harmlessly scoop out foreign bodies I'd once used it myself to painlessly remove a piece of shrapnel from a man's kidney but the tumors were Lina's flesh. But the Silver Watch had unlimited time. So, I'd use it to learn. I'd spend eons between heartbeats, studying medicine and science until I could damn well invent a cure myself. But the Watch didn't work that way. It gave you time to think. Time to daydream. Time to reminisce. Time would stand still as long as you weren't thinking about the present. Studying medicine while not thinking about it was impossible. My time with Lina was always time spent. A price paid for the joy she brought me. I was always in the moment with her, and time ticked inexorably forward. It wasn't until that time was almost gone that I became miserly with it. I tried to force the Watch to stop everything. To let me have one more minute with her while she was still laughing. While her eyes were still bright. But it didn't work like that. I was trying to hold still the ocean by grabbing a handful of it. Time ticked past the last of the good days. And now that Lina lay a wasted shell before me, my mind kept wandering back. It paused the world whenever I couldn't bear to see her like this. In her final day, I'd lived a lifetime. So far.

With a flash the apparition flickered into reality. Nearly 600 meters bow to stern, the ship's massive flank shone in the light of the systems star. Along it's length, drop ships nested like remoras. With the dull thud of unlocking docking arms, the drop ships uncoupled and turned towards the system's' lone inhabited planet. Their appearance did not go unnoticed however. Lieutenant Friedrich Von Amling, second in line to the throne, marched into the darkened command room. Great banks of computers lined the walls while power and cooling cables crisscrossed the floor. The HQ was a bustle of movement. Adjutants ran back and forth, bearing documents and files to their officers. The young noble marched up to the senior officer in the command bunker and smartly saluted. "Lieutenant Von Amling reporting as ordered sir!" The older man sketched a salute and then lowered his head back to the flickering holotable. His wrinkled eyes squinted into the harsh light blue of the holograms. "Good morning son. Your brother Kurt is already with his unit. His mixed battalion of mechs and tanks will be positioned in the village of Dieppe. There they will engage the enemy as they land. With the city built into the mountain and AA batteries so heavy, they will need to take it by a frontal assault. Your lance will be held in reserve, to act as a reserve. More information will be sent to you as the situation develops. Any questions?" "No father, Sir." The man nods satisfied. "Good. I suggest you see to your mech and your men. Dismissed." With another parade ground salute, the son exited the HQ, leaving the officers and their aides to their herculean task. He makes his way to the hanger moving through the crowd of civilians. The outlying villages have been evacuated and the populace is being directed into the massive shelters dug into the mountain. The titanium ore that lured immigrants here left massive tunnels and caverns empty. Though it was a heavy tax, the installation of fresh air ducts and lighting along with water pipes is a godsend to the people, as are the massive blast doors installed. They can hold half a million souls in safety. Two hundred thousand more than the entire population of the continent. The builders were thinking ahead. He arrives at the hanger and past the salutes of the MP's. Going into the ready room, he removes his uniform and dons his equipment. Ragged cargo shorts and an ancient t-shirt make up his combat clothes. A cooling vest and a neuro-helmet he also pulls out of his locker. Shrugging on the heavy vest, he makes his way into the main hanger. Sparks fly as mechanics and technicians make last minute repairs. The whine of power tools and smell of spilt oil and coolant fill the air. Forgoing a lift, he climbs up the flank of his mech manually and drops down into his seat. Plugging in his cooling vest and his helmet, diagnostics and other readings scroll forth from his screens. He checks the displays and adjusts the mech until the statuses are green. He rotates the torso to the right and left, nodding satisfied at the smooth motion. He aims his left arm, the mounted Rotary Autocannon follows his gaze. He rolls his right arm. The mounted mace does as well. He gives a thumbs up signal to the waiting mechanic, who then raises twin glow rods. Guiding the mech, he leads it out of the hanger and into the rising dawn. The battle has begun. Six hours later. The tide has turned against them. The initial landings of the foe were one of disorganization and Friedrich's brother took advantage of the chaos, tearing into the dismounting forces. A running battle took place over the rich fields of corn and sugar beets. Numerous mechs and tanks fell or were otherwise forced to retire. The charred and burnt out remains dotted the plains for miles. Lieutenant Von Amling threw his lance into the fray, accounting for several mechs and many more vehicles. One of his own mechs was destroyed and another one crippled. There is a lull in the fighting, as both sides seek to catch their breaths and to rearm and regroup. His brother was taken to a hospital. Spalling from missile strikes struck him. It was a miracle he didn't bleed out in his cockpit. Now the enemy forces are gathering, preparing to mount the final attack to seize the city. The leader of the enemy can be seen in his mech, instilling the attackers with words of encouragement. His father is considering terms of surrender. The young noble will hear none of that. Ignoring protests he climbs back into his mech and walks it out of the underground hanger and into the later afternoon sun. "This is Baron Friedrich Von Amling, Lieutenant of the Duke's Own Camden Hussars. Who leads this force?" A moment passes before the open channel crackles. "This is Knight-Colonel Alan Samuel of Count de Bernham's host. I lead this action." "Sir Alan. It is my intention to challenge you to single combat if you so choose to accept it." There is another pause. "Very well Lord Friedrich. I accept. Do you wish to begin now or at later time of your choosing." "Now if it would not inconvenience you sir." "Very well let us begin." They start a kilometer away from each other. Their two mechs walking slowly towards the other. Lieutenant Von Amling's mech has the greater range. Placing his target reticule over his opponent's mech, his thumb presses the firing switch, his rotary autocannon spits rounds downrange. Though plenty miss, enough find the foe and slam into armor, chipping away at plates. Another burst rips forth, more depleted uranium rounds contact with the enemy. Then the foe fires. Lasers scores across the young noble's armor, drawing angry red lines across the left torso. More firepower crosses the closing distance. Great swaths of armor of torn off from both opponents. The rotary cannon spins empty. His ranged weapon useless, he raises the massive four ton mace and charges in. The knight also has a melee weapon on his machine, a long and wicked two ton lance. He pours on speed. The pair hurl themselves down the field, neither wavering, both intent on destroying the other. The lance of the foe finds purchase first, tearing into the Lieutenant's left arm, shearing it clean off. The amputated limb drops to the ground. Von Amling replies with a smashing blow that crumples the enemy's missile launcher. Secondary explosions from the ammo rip into the hull of the mech. Another mace swing collapses the foe's left knee. In return, the lance stabs deep into the torso of Amling's mech. Another mace swing connects with the foe's head, stunning the pilot. Lieutenant Von Amling takes this opportunity to unleash a torrent of blows. Hammering down on the helpless mech with a half dozen strikes. Armor is almost non existent on the enemy's mech. Eventual the foe breaks away from the melee and lowers his battered machine to the ground, powering it down in surrender. "Baron Friedrich. I yield. The field is yours. Cease your attack." The young noble wipes the perspiration from his brow. He is drenched in sweat. "Very well, I accept your surrender. With respect to your bravery and skill at arms. I permit you and your men to depart this world peacefully. Any machines that can not move under their own power are to be left here, as spoils. Do you agree?" "I agree to these terms. Thank you. We will leave by nightfall. I congratulate you on your victory. It was well won." "Thank you. Depart in peace. I hope we will not see each other again soon. Lieutenant Von Amling out." The noble steers his battered machine back towards the city, to the waiting arms of its cheering people. Their young warrior has protected them for another day. Such is the price for his position in life. With his rank and status, he must shield the people from harm, with his own body is required. There is a reason for the statement, noblesse oblige. Nobility obliges. It is his duty.

That Friday night, when Steven got home earlier from work, no one could notice one thing off about his behaviour. He twisted the key as he always did, one time to the left, and then two times to the right. He opened the door as he always did, just enough to get between it and the stand right next to the wall. He sat on the couch, staring blankly into the ceiling, thinking about his day, as he always did for fifteen minutes, no more, no less, before taking off his shoes and going into the kitchen to cook some dinner, as he always did. But by the end of his meal, it was clears Steven couldn't hold it in anymore. Urgently, he got up and into the bathroom, lunged towards the toilet, and vomited the stake he had just finished eating. Then out came breakfast. And then everything else, until his stomach was completely empty. By the end, Steven was sobbing inches away from the toilet porcelain, praying in his mind to anyone and no one, wishing for it to stop. Alas, nothing stopped. Not his vertigo, nor his pain, nor his life, which he secretly wanted to forsake. Still staring at the bottom of the toilet, he contemplated the possibility of diving in it, drowning himself in a pool of his own sick. Or maybe there was something behind and beyond it, maybe the pipe would lead him to a magical kingdom besieged by wars between mice and cockroaches. He got himself yearning to Wonderland, someplace away from wherever he was, before realising he was already falling down some rabbit's hole, into a freaky and lonely world where he would never see the people he loved again. When he finally got up from his sorrow, he gazed himself in the mirror, to face the signs of the sadness he promised not to feel. The dark circles beneath his eyes, the rough uncut beard on his cheeks, and the pale tone of his face. He stared at his own image for what seemed like hours, looking into his own eyes as his mind drifted through all the thoughts that were not the ones he wanted to think about, because that was the only way not to think about them. By the time he got to bed, it was already just before dawn. He laid down on the sheets, and only got up Sunday morning.

"Why has Master summoned me?" The question was in vain. We both knew why. The unspoken tension grew ever thicker in the small moment of silence that ensued. "He didn't say. Just be glad. It's damn hot out here." I give her a weak nod of approval and follow towards the house. The House. The one she worked in everyday, but never slept in. The one that loomed in the distance day in and day out- it's eery porch beckoning. The house only my lighter-skinned peers ever got to work in. The house that only I ever slept in. I follow her through the main hallway, lost in my thoughts. The mixed servants- my own people- clearly shocked to see a woman of such a color in their presence. I keep my head down. "In there. He's expecting you." "Thank you, Lucille." She half smiles before scurrying off to work. "Master?" "Don't call me that, Daisy." "Sorry Ma- sir." He got up from his chair, majestic and tall once standing- his blue coat sown buy me, wig powdered by Lucille. "I hear you've been ill." "Sir, I'm "You will stay with me until you are well." He says, making his way closer to me until he breathe is wet on my forehead- his hands firm on my shoulders. "Sir, I'm not ill, sir. I'm..." How do I say it? "Spit it out, Daisy! I haven't got all day." "With child, sir." He draws back, hands now painfully tight. "Whose?!" He yells. "Yours, sir. It has to be." I say in barely a whisper. He lets go of me for a moment. He paces around before standing to face me again and saying "You will not tell anybody. My immediate staff will know. You'll stay here until you deliver. You won't work. I want you on bedrest by the end of the month. When it is born..." He trails off for a moment. "When it is born, it shall be born into freedom. It will take my name." "What about me, sir?" "I can not be the father of a child born to a slave." "How do you mean, sir." He looks me in the eyes a moment before kissing my still-flat belly. "Daisy, you are a free woman. You're carrying my child!" He says with glee, smiling. "Your wife, sir." I say carefully. "My wife has never born me a child! But you, my dear! I'll draw up your papers. Lucille will show you to your bed room. I'll visit you there later tonight," He kisses me with passion before scurrying to his desk. So this is it. I'm one of them now. I am no longer the nameless oppressed. I am no longer property. I have prayed for this moment every day. But I never wanted it like this. I never loved him. He has repelled me. He has been inside me. His child is inside me. How can I hate him now? He is disgusting, but he has freed me. He raped me. He freed me.

Billions of people listen to the message. Billions of people look at each other and realize they are fucked. The aliens leave, and the greatest party of all time begins. For 8 months it rages. Millions die in the wake of it, perhaps even billions. Cities fall apart, all governments collapse. Chaos reigns. Wars stop then begin again, even worse than before. Nukes begin to fly. After 11 months, billions are dead and most of the world is wasteland. Humanity does not think to band together and fight aliens or attempt to change. Still, a few hundred million remain among the living in this party turned dystopic nightmare. Then, one year later, the aliens return and look at the world they left behind. The aliens release nanobots that reproduce and collect the radioactive material and clear the atmosphere of dust. Nanobots decompose the dead and restore the balance of life to the land and the oceans. Species that had long been extinct return to the world. This is accomplished in a matter of days. Once finished, the unrevealed aliens finally address humanity. Satellites around the world broadcast the message. "We never intended to destroy you. We had to answer a question, an important one. The question was "could an intelligent race change if faced with immediate extinction once they had started down the path of destruction?" The answer is no, but there is no point in eliminating you. You will destroy yourselves soon enough, but we will save your genetic material. Perhaps, you can flourish elsewhere with the proper guidance as we have. After all, you're not the only humans in the galaxy."

The last scoop of sad ice cream tasted sweeter than my ex-girlfriend. I had been unemployed and alone for a decade. Only in sugar did I feel something resembling love. I had failed, or rather never really had a chance. The aching in my chest intensified to a wrong-feeling sting like terrible heartburn, and my left arm went numb. "Fuck it," I thought, and lay back. - I awoke in the gamer chair, reality crashing back. I slithered out of the VR headset and saw my friends smiling at me. "Well?" Eric the Programmer asked. "Did you like it? The full temporal simulation? The authentic probabilistic modeling? The lucky break engine?" I goggled. It had been barely ten minutes. Or forty-five years. Hard to say. I stared past him, weeping silently. Eric looked confused. "Seriously, what was it?..... you got a top 1 start..... my models put you on track to probably be a celebrity..." I didn't care. Everyone I loved had never existed. " ..... look, you asked me for something to take your mind off of the football scores. I take it my program was..... interesting?" "Shut it down," I croaked. "The simulations don't deserve that. No one does. Give the simulations a moment of happiness and a choice to stay in that moment. Shut it down." "But you were just asking me what it would be like if people reproduced sexually instead of asexually," Eric replied, "so I decided to give you a simulation so you could experience..." "You have no idea," I croaked, and resumed weeping. Eric sighed, typed a few words into the terminal, and pressed enter.

Reginald wipes the sweat from his brow as he sniffs the air, enjoying the sweet smell of gunpowder and rain merging together. He walks up to his fresh kill, admiring the beauty of the beast he considered fortunate to have found roaming the woods. As he gets to the body, he sets his rifle gently on the ground and kneels on one knee. Once kneeling, he kisses his pressed-together pointer and middle fingers of the hand that held the gun and presses them to the barrel of his gun. He then slowly caresses the neck of his fresh kill. He checks for a pulse, and finds one, though it is rapidly fading. "My precious, wood-dwelling friend. Thank you for the meat you will provide tonight. Your soft skin will grace my home's presence like a badge of honor. Your body will combine with mine, so that we are one flesh, paying homage to the food chain and God Himself. I will say a prayer, asking that your soul be guided to a place of peace. Your death will not be in vain, child of the forest." His hands slowly feel up and down the body as his eyes follow his hands' movements. As he finishes his thorough search, being certain there are no defects, he picks up the body and begins carrying it to his cabin. As he is walking, he hears a jingling sound, as if loose change is bouncing around in his pockets. Setting the body down, he checks himself to see if he is the cause of the noise. As he is doing so, he looks once again to the neck of his newly slain beast and sees a metal tag dangling, as if the beast had an owner of some sort. He identifies it as the cause of the noise, looks at it briefly, then picks the body back up and begins his walk again. "Rebecca. I will cherish your name, along with every other part of you as you are consumed and displayed in all of your glory within my presence." As he approaches his cabin door, he hears something fall. Swinging open the door to allow light to seep out, he sees that Rebecca dropped a wallet he missed while searching her. He puts her down with care and picks up the wallet, holding it in the light as the wooden door creaks open a bit more from a gust of wind. Sifting through, pushing away worthless amounts of money and plastic, he finds a piece of paper tucked in one of the more hidden areas of it. He opens the folded paper, informing him it's an old note she was given by someone; probably someone special. He then reads it aloud. "Rebecca - no matter how far apart we are, I will always love you. Forever and ever,'till death do us part - I love you, my beautiful flower. -Jonathan" Smiling, he puts the piece of paper back where he found it. As he goes to pick Rebecca back up, still smiling, he sheds a single tear as he walks into his cabin, shutting the door behind him.

"So, that's it?" I asked. "I just point at one person and I'll end their life?" The man floating next to me turned his head from side to side as though he were considering several options for a Saturday evening dinner destination where every restaurant happened to sound particularly appealing. "Well," he finally began. " , not you specifically, but yes. Picking someone out will result in the termination of their life." "And if I refuse to do that at all?" "More's the same to me! I don't really care whether or not time continues in this plane of existence." He lazily tilted his head towards the strange brass lamp I cleaned which summoned him. "At least here, there's actually some shit to see and do rather than sit and meditate or stare at the brass walls for a few millennium." I looked down and defeated at the lamp by my feet and gave it a soft kick. "I don't think I could kill anyone." I finally said after gazing off into the frozen sunset for a while. "Like I said, it doesn't necessarily have to be you. Hell, I'll let you choose the method, even." The strange man drifted towards me casually and reassuringly pat me on my shoulder. In an odd way, his gesture felt genuinely reassuring as opposed to forced and asympathetic, like I expected it to be. "What if," I said very slowly and carefully. I have plenty of time while time doesn't run, which is nice. That means I can carefully deliberate what I want to say and not make any mistakes. " , what if I gave it to someone else? The kill?" "What if they choose you?" answered the man with a sly grin. "Well, that's a good point..." I thought some more. I sat down in the dirt and stared at the forever sunset. At least this non-genie was able to capture the world at such a perfect point in time. The rich purples and blues were splayed over the deep reds like someone took a few different colors of taffy and began to mix them until they began to resemble mixed leftover carnival cotton candy. "Why do I have to do this at all?" "Excuse me?" the non-genie refocused his attention away from a dandelion which was frozen in time right as the breeze had begun to blow it's white seedlings away. "Why do I have to kill anyone at all? Who made it your job to make people do this?" "Sorry man, that's classified information for mortals. Maybe you'll find out after you're dead." "There's an afterlife." "For some people." He shrugged and returned his gaze to the dandelion. "Do you need help deciding?" "On whether or not to do it?" "No, that's something you have to do on your own, unfortunately. I don't want to twist your fate too terribly much. I'm just the smoking gun..." He looked back at the brass lamp nearby to where I had been standing. " ..... well, smoking lamp that will be in your hands."

'The hardest part, I find, is not the job itself. I know that sounds strange, but once you're accustomed to the gore and the blood-spattered walls, the bits of bone under your feet as you slip past police cordons, and the stench of rot and death accompanying every scene, it's not that bad. Enjoyably macabre, even. I'm a butcher's son at heart, see, so all the nasty stuff doesn't bother me. Dad was bringing home hacked-up lamb, wool hanging off it and everything, when I was just a boy.' 'So, forgive me, Anthony, but what exactly is the hardest part of the job?' 'Oh yes. I was getting to that. It's the stigma attached to it, you know? Dates are the worst. You're a what? they say as they're sipping their Chianti. I'm a serial killer critic, I say. And of course they up and leave, like I'm wrong in the head. I'm not the psycho - I review psychos! For instance, I'm trying to finish the piece I'm doing about the Rattlesnake killer - the one in the news recently. Heard of him?' 'Unfortunately, yes. Terrible piece of work. Sick.' 'He's pretty nasty, that's for certain. So I'm telling this scorching Italian girl about the intricacies of his craft - the precise way he strings together the finger bones and hangs the skin around them, you know? And she projectile vomits, all over the table, all into the delicious fava bean starter we were enjoying. It was a nice restaurant, too, the new Indian one on the high street - great reviews on TripAdvisor.'Course, we were kicked out pretty soon after that.' 'I see. So, you've never considered trying a new profession? Being a different type of critic? Something more conventional?' 'I can't say I have, Rhonda, and do you know why? You can lead with this quote, if you want, for the article. Food critics, TV snobs, cinema buffs - they're a dime-a-dozen. Me? I'm a serial killer critic - who else is going to come and steal my thunder?'

Ah, what a nice day for a walk. You see, I don't get to walk too much. They keep me in these funny little pants, and I can't walk much. At first, they only put me in a jacket. I was grateful for that, because even though that one little man's neck was on straight now, there was another who needed his kneecaps put right. My feet were perfectly fine for that job. But now they keep my legs and arms strapped still, and slip a tray of food under the door. It's wonderful! A whole new challenge for me, having to eat without my hands! But recently they haven't been sliding the trays. Yesterday I didn't really notice, I was playing a lovely game of door-kick. I usually play until the guards come put a stop to me, but yesterday they didn't. Today I started to get really hungry, and I remembered that the lovely-smelling girl would usually come to visit her mother next door today! Wonderful, wonderful! I just couldn't wait. I slipped out of my jacket and pants - I had been able to get out of them for weeks now, but I didn't want to hurt the poor nurse's feelings, she smelled so lovely too - and walked toward the door. (to be continued)

Satan took three long, smokey breaths as he tuned the last string on his fiddle backstage. "Don't worry, you got this." he muttered to himself. In well over two thousand years, Satan was about to make his first public appearance on one of the most watched programs in the country, America's Got Talent. As the host walked out to announce him, Satan thought back to how exactly he'd gotten himself into this position. It had been a long journey to that point. Satan had wrestled for years with the idea of seeking out his revenge on all those who had mocked and ridiculed him, but never mustered up the courage to do it. Since science had expanded so much in the past few hundred years, and fewer people believed in religion, Satan was afraid that should he try and make himself known on Earth, people would laugh at him and make him feel like a fraud. Not to mention that Hell had gotten extremely busy since around the mid 1900's. He really could never find the time to make it up to Earth, what with the trying to find space for all of Hell's newcomers and scheduling all of his realm's events on a daily basis. However, after talking to his partner, Saddam, he realized that this was something he needed to do. His plan had worked brilliantly to this point. He flew up to Earth a few weeks prior to the audition, bought some "human-like" clothes, and even gotten professional make-up artists to cover his ghoulish features. When asked why he looked the way he did, he told everyone, "Burn victim." He already knew what his first step would be in exacting his revenge; he just needed a way to act it out. He checked out a cheap motel room near the audition sight for the show, bought a second-hand fiddle from a pawn shop, and began practicing. He ad heard about America's Got Talent through some of his servants down in Hell. They all told him what a great, fun show it was and that he should check it out. So he did just that. It wasn't long before he realized how easy it was to get on the show, and that with his fiddle skills, he could really exact his revenge. So there he was, sweating backstage, waiting for his moment in the spotlight. When the host called his name, there was no applause..... no cheering..... just silence. He slowly walked out on stage, shoulders slumped over, fiddle in hand. The judges said nothing for a while, and then one asked, "Did he way your name right? Is it really..... Satan?" "Um, yeah." Satan replied. "Jesus Christ." the judge said. "No, Satan. S-A-T-A-N. Jesus is the other guy." The judges stared at each other. "Wait, so you're saying, you're actually Satan? Like, the guy from the Bible?" "Uh huh. Should I start my song, or like, what?" Satan asked. Everyone in the audience was flabbergasted. The room fell completely silent. This only made Satan more nervous. HE began to shake slightly as the sweat ran the make-up off his face. His red skin peeked out. "Um, okay, I'm gon na go ahead and start now." he said. "This is a song I wrote, couple years ago. Never played it for a live audience before. Hope you guys like it. It's called "Go Fuck Yourself Charlie Daniels. An audience member chuckled. Suddenly, Satan wasn't so nervous. He touched the bow to the strings and began. "1, 2, 3, 4..."

I woke up on Thanksgiving Day to the most heartbreaking scene a young boy could imagine not only were there no smells of thanksgiving feasting spreading through my house, but our TV wasn't working either, as it was picking up nothing but dead static. This meant that I would have to miss the Detroit Lions lose today..... but it was a Thanksgiving tradition! I knew that something more serious was happening, however, when I met my mom in the hallway between our rooms and she looked as though she had been crying. "What's wrong, mom?" I asked with as inquisitive a tone as possible. "The grocery stores throughout our city, as well as the entire New York area have had all of their deliveries intercepted, and nothing but maple syrup is coming in." This seemed odd to me, but as somebody who enjoys maple syrup, it could have been worse. I was uncertain what the impeding of deliveries meant, but I knew that coupled with the television problem, something was definitely up. It was at precisely this moment when I heard the first explosion in the distance. It sounded similar to a hockey player being slammed into the boards by a powerful check, but was followed by a dull detonation. Almost simultaneously to the explosion, my television finally turned on, and there, centered perfectly on the screen was Stephen Harper, the Prime Minister of Canada. He spoke very deliberately, and in a manner that seemed too friendly to be evil, yet maintained diabolical undertones. He spoke slowly and without wasting words, but what he did say will stay with me forever. "Sorry to inform you, but every professional sports league besides the NHL will be cancelled from this point forward. Also, we will be nuclear bombing the entirety of the United States over the next 24 hours..... if that's alright with you." "Wait, wait, no, even if it isn't alright with you. Sorry. "Wait, wait, no need for me to apologize, I'm sorry. "Gosh darnit, ignore this rambling, sometimes I am too polite for my own good. I hope you enjoy ice sports, maple syrup and destruction, that is all that is on the menu from this point forward. Thanks"

"This is Grixcics Vi, transmitting to all points! That's right, I, the lead reporter for the Eknecian Imperium to all points, not just points within our borders. This breach of standard comms protocal has come at the request of our special guests, our new allies against Zygnacian Federation. I'm on the home planet of our allies, Earth, Sol, or Terra, or several other names depending on whom you ask with a representative of the Human race, Sapius. Now, Sapius, you are not yourself human are you?" " No Grixcics I am not. I am an artificial intelligence designed for the benefit of this broadcast. The leaders of humanity could not decide on representative of human origin, so developed me to guide you through today's event. The primary tradition being to attempt to intimidate the enemy side into surrendering before too many lives are lost. " "Now, before we move on, it bears noting to our viewers that humanity has neither a hive mind nor a race wide Imperial Doctrine, nor in fact a planetary government." " Indeed Grixcics. While the Zygnacian Federation hive mind and the Imperial Doctrine have allowed for greater exploration of the galaxy, it has apparently not provided you with the wealth of experience in the area of war it has afforded humans. " "Oh my..... Sapius. what are they singing? Is that what is considered singing on..... here? And please, why are they leading the parade? are they your most elite forces?" " To begin with they are singing is really more of a chant called "Le Boudin" in their native language, French. France, is a state on our planet, that has a long and storied military history. However, it suffered two critical losses, and has been considered militarily deficient by many other nations sense. The legion itself has an impressive history and a unique standing within our global politics that allows them to intervene in wars that would be for any other force "illegal." You mentioned that this force participates in wars that would be illegal for other forces. You mean to tell me that without a global government you have laws that govern global conflicts?" Furthermore we have a term for when those rules simply do not apply. That would be'Total War' which is how we plan to engage the Zygnacian Federation. " "Sapius, I'm hearing an absolute cacauphony and an equally absolute riot of colors following the French Foreign Legion. According to my notes, this is the...'Conglomerated Regiment of Her Majesty's Armed Forces " That is correct Grixcics. This is, similar to yours truly, a construct for the sake of this broadcast. It is a unit designed to demonstrate the variety, versatility, and number of fighting forces belonging to the Nation-state of the United Kingdom. It includes members of most of regiments within the Military of the United Kingdom, such as the Queens Dragoon Guards, The Royal Regiment of Scotland, The Royal Marines, and is lead by representatives of the SAS and SRS; the special forces of the UK. They are each singing their official songs and bearing their official colors. " "The diversity on display here is staggering. According the the history of your planet that the Imperium was given, this nation state grew to be one of the largest before succumbing to many colonial uprisings. Can we take that to mean the forces from those once colonies to be more impressive Sapius?" " I'm not qualified to make that judgement Grixcics. I will have to leave that to you, our Eknecian allies, and of course our Zygnacian enemies. However, speaking of those forces following the UK we have The U.S. Joint Service Color Guard. These five flags represent approximately 39 percent of humanities global military expenditure. They are singing the National anthem of the United states of America. " "Again, astounding use of symbolism and practicality. OH NO, Sapius! Why is there a gap here in The Parade! wait, I can see a lone human a ways away..... what is the meaning behind this?" " This is deliberate Grixcics, and again a symbolic gesture. The stretch between that lone human you picked out and representatives of the United States of America is one and one half miles. I believe this is equivalent to about 89 Imperium cubits. This is the distance a Canadian sniper shot and killed an enemy of their close allies, the United States. While small in number, the Canadian Military has been able to have a significant impact in our wars, and we expect to have an impact on our war with the Zygnacians. " "89 Imperial cubits? An impressive feat, even with our advanced weaponry, rarely has such a feat been matched. Truly Sapius the military might of Humanity is impressive. Also I believe we will use this time as your Canadian representative that distance to take what is on your planet called an "intermission."

Preface! This is my first WP. Play nice! "Wait a sec..... this can't be right?" Toni said to himself, staring at the AR receiver on his wrist. He scrolls through his open applications and finds his way to the e-harmony app and closes it, causing the red and black icons to fade. The mysterious individual approaches as he fiddles with the controls on his AR receiver. Toni re-opens the applications as the stranger seats himself quaintly. With a sultry and charming demeanor the stranger tips his hat and meets eyes with Toni as he raises his gaze from the AR device. "How do you do?" said the stranger as the red and black indicators fade back into Toni's augmented reality. "Err..... He....Hello" Toni stutters in his confusion. This is the love of my life? He thought to himself. "My names Brent..... I saw you from across the room and just had to say hello. Can I buy you a drink?" As he gestures to the bartender presumptuously. "I..... I guess so." Thoughts racing through his head. Is E-harmony trying a new thing? I'm not even attracted to men? Why am I paying for this service? Why does he have both tags? "So..... I haven't gotten your name?" Brent seems to interrupt Toni's thought as the bartender approaches and takes their orders. Toni's been in the game awhile, searching for that special someone to spend his life with. E-Harmony has delivered so many red icons into his life that he's starting to lose hope. His matches have always had the right qualities but for some reason they all flop in the end. What was he doing wrong? How could he find happiness? As the two exchange formalities over a pint Toni starts to realize Brent shares those same qualities. But a man? I am not a religious person. I am not one to believe in the supernatural. I would not even say I think often. I let the world pass me by, and I am okay with that. So maybe I am not the best person to relay the events. Oh well, I did not get to choose this either. The ground was clouded in morning fog. The sun above was a pale star. It was quiet and we disembarked. The girl was still crying. She reminded me why I didn't like children. Her bawls were ignored. I wondered where were her parents. Something was happening, but I didn't know what it was. The plane was glistening, slippery in the light. I walked slow so that the girl would pass me and I would not have to see her again. I took out my phone and put it on. The airport ahead seemed so far. The girl walked ahead slowly and she looked back and was still crying. "I don't know where my mommy is," she said. I looked at my phone pretending not to hear. The notifications came endlessly. All the people asking if I was okay. The mourning of my disappearance. Was it a joke? I looked up. She was sobbing still. "My mommy is not dead yet," she said. I ran ahead. The others gave unfriendly looks. The security stopped me, told me to slow down, but they were hardly there. The odd art of Denver towered over the place. Inside the murals grew like a jungle and this was their home. "Mommy! Mommy!" I heard from behind. I looked at the phone and the updates were still coming. My plane had crashed. I had died. Everyone had died. I tried calling my brother but there was no signal. I tried messaging him and others on Facebook but nothing would send. "My mommy doesn't have cancer like you and me," the girl said. She had come back next to me. Her face was wet but she seemed more composed. I hated her so much. I wanted to hit her. I wanted to get in contact with someone. "She isn't here. Her plane is coming later. I might have to sleep here. I heard there was a big horsey here though, so I don't mind." "What?" I said. I wanted her to go. I was hardly listening. "Do you have anybody to wait for?" "My cousin," I said. "They're going to pick me up." Remembering that made things better. I could go meet them and find out what was happening. "How did they go? Was it cancer too?" What was she on? I looked at her. "What are you talking about? Why don't you go and meet your mother?" "Her flight isn't coming for a long time," she said. "I have to wait for her." "I hope you're okay then." I walked off. The baggage claim was sparse and it wasn't hard to get my things. Outside in the lobby, the windows were fogged and the sun was a golden aura that broke free sometimes, tinting the glass. There was hardly anyone sitting. My cousins weren't there. I checked my phone again and there was that same story about the plane crash. My cousins posted their distraught. I tried messaging them. I tried calling. I wanted to tell them that the plane had landed fine and that I was okay. I never got through though. I couldn't help it. I broke down crying from the frustration. The girl came beside me. "You shouldn't be carrying a telephone if you're crying so, Mr. Jones. You might drop it." She patted my back. How did she know my last name? Was it a guess. "I'm sorry. I know how you feel. Cheer up though. At least your mommy is here for you. Look!" I couldn't understand. I looked where she was pointing and my phone started to ring. The number nearly killed me. I trembled and fell and answered it without thinking. The cold floor of the airport seeped through me and I wanted to curl up. "Hello?" "Bobby?" It was my mother. I looked up and she was sitting to the back in the mostly empty room. She was older and a little tired, but she looked just as I remembered her. "You must be a good son for her to wait for you," the girl said. "I'm going to see the horsey now. You take care okay?" I got up and fell again. My mother came to me and I saw her face. It was really her. It was just as I remembered her before she had died.

"You know, my last owner always said I was sharp and edgy. He was such an "Please, could you save it for later?" I beg Lilarcor. When I first heard tale of the blade, I was determined to seek it out and wield it for myself. The rumors only told of it's mystical prowess - a blade that could dance on its own, faster than the most skilled swordsman could wield it. I had crossed half a continent in search of it, braving the Calim Desert and the forestfolk of Morthil, not to mention the other minor perils. I had learned more about my quest during my travels. One reticent traveller told me that the blade had a personality of its own. I regarded his tale with equal parts skepticism and fancy, but it reinvigorated my efforts to find the object of my obsession. When I finally found Lilarcor, he was sheathed in a shallow pool in a cavern just outside Nashkel. He asked me about myself the moment I let his steel taste air, so suddenly that I nearly dropped him back into the water. "I may be an intelligent sword, but I've had no formal edumication," he would joke. It turned out, to my dismay, that he refused be brandished by the air. Apparently a firm grip is "more comfortable." That isn't to suggest he wasn't useful - he could cut through armor like it was, in his words, "hot butta." Even so, his personality had slowly drained my patience. I'd keep him sheathed, except the longer he's cooped up the angrier he gets when I let him out. "Can we go kill something now, huh?" The claymore asks for what must be the thousandth time. "Fine! We're almost at the gnoll's stronghold anyway. We'll kill all the gnolls you want." "Now! Now! Kill something now!! Yeah!" Gods, this sword is an ass. We quickly reach the entrance of the stronghold, which is eerily empty. As we track into the fort, seeking the prizes inside, I hear an echoing howl. I steel myself as a party of gnolls descends upon us. "You deal," he says, "I'll cut!" Battle with Lilarcor is a blur, punctuated only by his abrupt cries and quips. "YOINK! Got your nose!" he says as he strikes the first gnoll across the snout. And after I pull him from the second's chest he exclaims with glee, "we got a gusher!" In moments the four gnolls lie beaten at my feet, and me without a scratch. Deeper into the stronghold we go, as I reflect and process the battle that just took place. "Lil," I say, "Did it seem to you like they actually wanted to fight us?" "Oh yeah! Some of my finest work!" "It seemed to me that they were more interested in getting past us than getting at us. Like they were running from something." "Boooo-ring!" "I'm serious, I thin I cut myself short as a deafening roar fills the hall. It comes from an ominous archway lined with larger-than-life teeth; a human skull adorns the cornerstone. I put on a brave face and descend the stairway through the door, as Lilarcor mutters, "you can't be serious..." At the bottom of the stairs is a wide chamber, but rather than scoping for details my eyes focus on the massive black dragon looming before me. A sentence echoes through my mind. "Hello, puny creature. I've been expecting you." I gulp. "I'm afraid you have me at a disadvantage. I was expecting mere gnolls guarding the treasures here." "My servants are very obedient." The dragon eyes me up and down. "There is no need to be frightened, mortal, I merely design to know your mind." "Are you talking to me?!" Lilarcor breaks his uncharacteristic silence. The beast's face turns disdainful. "Apparently your servants are not as well kept." I look down at my blade. "Hush, you." For the first time, I feel him tug at my hands. "Come get some!" The dragon's face turns to disgust. "I refuse to be disrespected by those so far beneath me." Only then do I notice the circle lining the dragon's perimeter. I take a final breath as it shifts from light blue to red.

It must be around 7 am. The night pulls its last strings of darkness while the day starts to fight its way through the blinds. I close my eyes back. The air is heavy and leaves a mild rotten scent in the room. I fully open the mouth to catch a breath, the breeze getting in is familiar. It reminds me of my sick days as a child when my mother would storm trough the door and tuck me in. Then she would open the window, so the virus would find its way out. I would freeze but the fever would stop my urge for whining. For a second, I can feel her icy hands rubbing my forehead. But I don't recall being sick. Maybe it was the whisky. The recurring thought pops out in my mind, and I assume once again it's the last of the times: Just stop drinking. I make an effort to remember the alcohol through my throat, the bottle on my hand. But there are no sips left in my last night's memory. Actually, there is nothing left. I turn my body to the right, rolling into a fetus position. I'm suddenly shivering. The morning background noise gives space to a new sound. A gentle whistle that goes up and down, in a rhythmic manner. I order my chest to stop breathing, and it can handle it for longer than usual. Though the noise doesn't stop, which it can only mean one thing. The inhales and exhales are not coming from my body. My sticky eyes start looking for my wife. My hope only lasts for an instant, before the reality strikes. She can't be here, can she? I don't know where she is, but I know for certain that she left. My sight gets slowly used to the shadow in front of me. The shapeless mass gradually fades in another body, lying in a single bed. The light shines over the bald head of a man, allowing me to get a glimpse of his figure. I desperately try to find a connection, but I can't recognize him. There is a stranger in my room. All of the sudden the space seems uncanny. The cozy feeling turns into an uncomfortable lack of awareness. My mind is too fuzzy to make a judgement. The window seems too small, the walls too white, the ceiling too high. The door shows open. The silhouette of a woman moves until she reaches the window, opening the blinds with one rehearsed strong move. - Time to wake up, misters. The confusion blocks my body from standing up. She storms out the room for about five seconds, which I use to take a good look at the bald guy. The day reveals a wrinkled old man. The lady comes back with a tray, and she tosses it gently into my lap. - Croissant day, Robert. Your fav! I look up, finding her uniform. She is wearing a plaque with her name, Rebecca. I stare at the white tea, the orange juice, the croissants. I can't recall if I like them or not.

Footsteps echoed as I turned the corner. Mumbled clicks and shrieks grew as I approached the blue-green door. It peeled away like an onion as figures moved in the distance. Hovering platforms began to settle as metallic disks filled them. Each stuffed with beings more bizarre than the next. I should call them aliens but they very eerily reminded me of something that would be evolution's wet dream of chickens, gazelles and some gibbons. Something that looked like an alien pig with a lazer pen began to grunt. He passed along the message to a slide covered drone. It floated down. Ooze extending from its port side. With the grace of a librarian the robot handed me the message with a greenish slime that was forming the structure of talons. The message was slightly askew as I peered closer. After a few moments I had to make eye contact with the space hog. Stick what down my throat? He waved a hooved hand towards the podium in front of me. The silver platform beeped as I stood on it. As I rose in the air. A thin mesh matrix spread across making a giant sphere. Grotesque faces popped onto the material as I made direct eye contact with the hog. It was better quality resolution than any television or device by a thousand. I glanced down noticing a silver box. A small gray tube stuck out like a string from a thing of dental floss. I rose the thing hesitantly to the screen. Unsure where my cameras were. He gave a rippling grunt which I could only presume was a yes. I held the tube to my mouth as it started to slither down. Melding with the flesh in my body. I wheezed nervously as I asked what the thing was. The words that came out sounded like a caribou waking up. I creeked out the words in their tounge. "Y'all understand?" Confused faces met me. I waved my hand apologetically. "Do you all understand my words?" I swallowed. Praying that I wasn't accidentally insulting their mothers. Words seeped into my little sphere. "You picked it up fast simian." I let out a chuckle. The hog called me a monkey. "So thank you for sending the invite to our satellites but your message was. Intriguing. You feared we would hunt you?" A cackle let out all around me as screeches and yelps echoed. The hog began to snicker. Letting out as much of a grin something that looks like Wilbur could. "We were worried you would want to hunt us. Because you lacked the capability of creating harmony with the other species on your planet. It was a mild attempt at creating a laugh. Good to note humor was not as advanced as we had presumed." I gave a stiff nod. "Harmony with our wildlife?" He gave a nod back mimicking me. "Every species that has joined our." He clicked his hooves as he paused. "Best human word is'Herd'. Has banded and defeated their natural predators into extinction." "So no other omnivorous species have joined your armada?" The pig grunted. "No such thing exists in our coalition. They have outgrown their urges." Dear God. The first aliens we have to deal with are snobby vegans? I shuffled slightly in the little sphere they began to feel more like the tube shoved down my throat. "I feel as if we should explain that a majority of our earth lacks the means for sustainable farming." The pig nodded. "We can educate you on that." I could feel myself stiffening. In through the nose out, through the mouth. I breathed slower. Draw your breath son. Don't let it rattle. "You feel we need to be taught to join your herd?" They laughed. "We prefer the term domesticated." For the first time since I stepped into the floating eight ball I smiled. "Not sure that's possible Chief." He cocked his head tusks glinting off the computer screen. "Do tell simian." I raised my head. "Because your cousins taste delicious." His eyes bulged as nervous clucking and baying erupted. I began to laugh as the sphere began to lower, my smile growing. "Sorry if we prefer our humor like our meat. Dark."

The knock echoed as he sat and thought, more alone than any in tragic form. He knew the knock was only a moment, but in it he felt forever. It shocked him into life, it freed beauty lost to violence and love forgotten in its decay. He remembered his estate in the countryside and its brooks and fields and towering trees. Fresh warm winds and sweat mixing with dirt and cool moonlit nights filled his mind. He remembered the fires they set to the land and the house and to all that he loved in peace. Violence merits violence, he reflected. He let the knock linger in the air of the room as it mingled with smoke from the fire and the smell of stale wine. He could hear sounds from the other patrons of the inn downstairs and they reminded him of before. The inn was built, he thought with dark irony, on the remnants of the city. He remembered returning to the city, to safety, protecting his family as he went. Her grace had saved him as his might had saved her, their children bore both their witness. If he had never picked up a sword, perhaps it wouldn't have ended. If he hadn't fought often and willingly in campaign after campaign..... But it was innate, he thought, his ability to fight. To do anything else would be affront to purpose. The knock came again and he glanced at his sword then the door, wondering if he could unsheathe it again. It was only a matter of time, he reminded himself. He knew this day would come. He had known it since he first met Tieganne. True beauty manifested in beautiful truth described her, as her words flowed freely, as honest as they were pure. But he hardened his resolve whenever he thought of her. To think of her meant to think of the city's fall, to think of his children, to think of loss. He had led the defense that night after retreating with his family to the city. Violence merits violence, he had thought, remembering the flames crawl over the countryside. Violence merits violence, he thought as he stood presently, the flames of the burning city filling his entirety. Two more knocks on the door and he unsheathed his sword, that last night in the city in his mind. They had raised the city and he had fought well, but fire cares not for the skill of steel. He was alone now as he was when he was forced to flee, and he knew it was every fault of his own. But he'd be damned if he wouldn't fight one last time. For Tieganne and his sons he crossed the room, unlatching the door with his sword in hand. Vengeance would be dealt, for them and for him, until he shared their fate. To do anything else would be an affront to purpose. As he opened the door the moment ended. There were no knocks or soldiers, no demands or orders. Only his sword falling to his side and his knees falling to the floor. Only Tieganne and her tears and his boys running into his embrace. He didn't remember what it was like to have love. He had lived without it for so many years. He wept as he held his children and Tieganne and thought of the violence he always knew. "I will never fight again, for as long as I live, unless it's to protect you. To do anything else..... That would be an affront to purpose." The moved into the night with silence and haste, searching for a new home with fresh warm winds and cool moonlit nights. Somewhere where they could live and love in peace.

After just shy of 13 years in sales, it was a well earned promotion I received last week to sales manager. Really, it feels good to be robotically ticking away my days 20 feet from where I did before (for 5 more than before hourly). It truly does. With an average wife, a public school attending daughter and a suburban home, what do I have to complain about? So many things in this world interest the human mind, and create dreams of pursuing them. You read a fantastic book and think of the lush life of being an author. Or you see a suspenseful film, and think of the thrill being on screen. How you would love to be the next professional snowboarder, bulging up your pockets with an impossible dream you couldn't possibly fulfill at this point in your life. It all just becomes so routine. Repetition turns repulsive rapidly. The love of my wife and daughter is almost overpowering my desire for radical change. "Almost" being the key word here. I am not John the NFL Quarterback, John the Hip-Hop producer, John the Author or even John the Success. They call me John, the millionth John to sit endlessly spinning in an office chair for 9 hours a day. This is going to change. Not for mediocre Mary, not for my beautiful daughter Sophia. For my fucking sanity. That George Clooney movie " O Brother, Where Art Thou? " is really beautiful. When the black boy sells his soul to the Devil in exchange for the fire fingers he used to cultivate his dreams, it really got me thinking. Not along the stupid Charlie Daniels concept of a musical duel over your soul, the Devil seems like a just businessman like myself. All that is needed is a little exhilaration to heave me from this rerun, day in and day out. Possibly I'll become a songwriter for musicians. Not directly in the spotlight, but in spitting distance. Close enough to feel the heat. Near 10 o'clock at night I departed from my less-than-ideal home in less-than-ideal Lubbock, Texas. My bags stuffed with..... well, nothing. What could you possibly need to bring before an everlasting business deal? Only a couple streetlights lit the road where this supposed " Devil " was to make an eternal transaction. As I approached the crossroads, a man sat slouching on a bench directly under one of the sparse streetlights. Unlike my expectations, a Vincent Price doppelganger was not sitting there, nor Emperor Palpatine. Honestly, it was almost as if I was gazing into a mirror. " Listen, you got ta help me out here. " Oddly enough, it wasn't just me saying this. We spoke in sync like the Thriller dance performers. Aren't I selling my soul? This manifestation is looking almost as drained as myself. " I am just here to make a deal with you, everything in my life has become so- " " I've heard it all before John, I really have. The boring cycle of a life eating at itself. You're tired of basking in routine. You've lived the same day a thousand times over now. Now you have a slight taste of how I feel. " I decided to skip over the fact that he knew my name. Seeing as that is a textbook childish question to ask an immortal being how he knew my name and problems. He made it evident to me that everyone has problems of their own. Even the problem solvers have problems to be solved. Slowly, I decided it was best for me to just take a seat next to this man. Figure if there was something I could do, as outrageous as it sounds. " So John, before you ask me anything, I want to make a deal with you. Trade lives with me. A soul for a soul if you will. " " I'm not sure I follow you. Like, full on life swap? I have a family I'd be leaving behind. " " No one would be left behind. It would just be me in your shoes. Living the unchangeable, broken record of a life you live. You John, would live forever. Meeting a countless array of people, with the power to give them a beautiful change. A beautiful change at a worthy price. " Why shouldn't I do this? All along it has been something new I've ached for. This is something outlandishly new. It's a fresh start, something new every day. Being presented with a buy-out for immediate change is an offer that I can not let slip beyond my grasp. " Alright, I don't want to hear anymore. I'll do it. This sort of all fell into place at once, and I might as well play this out. I want change, and this is a sure as shit way to get some. " " Fair enough, John. All we need to do is shake hands, then turn away from each other. All will be done but we are to never speak or even meet again. You will live forever, as the Devil selling souls as I carry out the life of ' John'until I am deceased. If you end up as you are now in your new position, just do what we are about to with another soul. " Without a question I stuck my hand out for the irreversible shake. Leaning towards his hand, the only thing on my mind was how many times has this happened before?

The forest sounds enveloped the little shack as night fell. Chief Winters said that we would be okay with only two guards, as more than that would bring too much attention. He said that SWAT would be on standby if we needed them. We were now 20 hours into our protection detail. We weren't allowed to leave the shack or have anyone else come to relieve us to minimize the risk of being discovered. Ricky and I decided that we should sleep in shifts. He sprawled out on the couch, and I brought a chair over to the window. Our witness was out cold on the only bed in the room. A light rain had begun to fall outside, lightly pattering against the window. My eyes felt heavy; rain always seemed to do that to me. I just wanted to rest my eyes for a second. I awoke with a start as I heard the unmistakable sound of a vehicle coming to a stop in the drive. I cussed under my breath at my inability to stay awake, and went for my radio to call it in. "484 headquarters" static "484 to headquarters, do you copy" static "484 to any unit, do you copy" static No response. They must have a radio jammer. I looked out the window as I saw four men get out of the car with tactical vests and AKs. Shit. There was no mistaking it, the mob was here for their witness. "Ricky!" I hissed as I slid my glock from its holster. "Ricky! Wake the fuck up!" "Whaaa?" Ricky slurred as he stirred on the couch. "The Russians. They're here for their witness, we got ta go now!" Ricky was awake now, his weapon was drawn and he was rousing our witness. I dropped my voice to a whisper. "Alright, you two go out the back door. I'll draw their fire before they can surround us. We need to get out of range of that jammer!" Ricky nodded and re-positioned himself at the back door, witness in tow. I quietly unlatched the front door and leveled my weapon. I held up my other hand with three fingers. My heart was pounding now, as I slowly turned the door handle. Two. I heard a small squeak as Ricky turned the handle of the back door. One. Stones crunched on the pathway outside. Zero. I flung open the front door and fired into open space. The.40 caliber shots thudded into my eardrums, magnified by the indoor echoing. I dumped all 16 downrange in about 5 seconds and pulled my weapon back behind cover to reload. There was a pause as I slammed a new magazine into place. Silence. I wondered why no one had returned fire yet. No sooner had this thought entered my mind, than the earth erupted into gunfire. 4 AK47's opened up, roaring in 7.62 fury. Bullets ripped through the flimsy walls of the shack. I ducked down, but not quick enough. I was thrown back as what felt like a cannon ball hit me in the chest. I coughed and tasted blood. The gunfire came to an abrupt stop as I put a hand to my chest and pulled it away bloody. Voices called outside, but I couldn't understand them. The edges of my vision got blurry. Boots thudded on the floors around my as faces appeared around me. My weapon was kicked from my limp hand. "Go after the other two, they couldn't have gotten far." A strong voice reverberated above me. Footsteps left me and then faded. Only one face remained. The blackness grew ever greater as I fought desperately to cling to consciousness. "You should not have tried to fight us. You are brave my friend, but very stupid. At least they may give you a medal." I fought against the blackness, but I was losing. My breathing grew shallow. I thought of my wife and son. "I am sorry that it had to be this way." I gave one last gasp as darkness took my sight, and my senses slipped away. Then I woke up in a hospital bed.

Why was my father never there when I needed him? I remember so many nights I would run to his bedroom, scared of a thunderstorm, or of the " monsters " in my closet, only to find his bed neatly made, and the television switched on to the news. It was upsetting, but I got used to it. Some nights when I could not sleep I would wander through our massive house, it seemed as though the hallways never ended, and there was always something new to discover. One night, when it was especially late, I found myself sneaking around my father's study. The room was exquisite, decorated with fine art, and bookshelves populated with large volumes of encyclopedias, the books I could only imagine to be centuries old. I was staring at one of the only pictures my father had of the two of us. It was sitting on one of the bookshelves in front of some book so large it would take years to read..... And that's when the bookshelf moved. It sunk into the wall and swiftly slid to the right. What I saw before me in the opening the moving bookshelf created was my father. I froze... I couldn't say a word, I had been caught... To my surprise he smiled at me, sat me down and told me it was important that I respect his privacy, and never enter the room behind the bookshelf. And that was all. There was no explanation as to why he spent his nights in that room. There was only an order, do not enter! Of course being young and curious I didn't listen. The following night, after making sure my father wasn't in his room, I tried to get the shelf in the study to slide open like it had the first time I discovered it. I pushed it, pulled it, tried moving books off the shelf like I had seen in movies one after the other...nothing. My last chance was the massive book behind the picture of my father and I. I reached to pull the book from its place, and ended up almost knocking the picture in front of it off the shelf... only it didn't fall. The picture tilted backwards and clicked. Just as before, the bookshelf slid into the wall, revealing the opening. The air blowing from the opening was cool and damp, and as I approached, I could see steps carved into the stone entry way leading me down into darkness. I took my first step, and the decent began. It seemed like forever, I was so nervous, so excited, so curious..... I would finally know my father's secret. Finally the stairs came to an end and I was standing on a very large platform in a very large room. I couldn't see the ceiling, or anything to either side, but I could see a light in front of me, it seemed to be coming from some sort of glass case. I walked closer, mindful of my every step, focused on what was inside of that case. As I approached, and the details of the cases contents became clear, so did the details of my father's life. Finally, standing right in front of the case admiring its contents, I realized that what I thought about my father was wrong. He was always there when I needed him, he was always protecting me from the monsters in my closet, and the things that scared me in the night. I smiled, and gazed upon the contents of the glass case. Displayed in front of me was a body of black armor, the symbol of a bat residing on the center of the chest-plate.

" Anything? " " Anything. " " Really? " " Yes, " the genie said. " I only ask that you do one favor for me first. " " What would that be? " Fred asked. He looked up at the purple smoke of the genie in front of him, his eyes transfixed. Genies didn't wear clothes apparently. But then again, only her upper half looked human, her bottom only a trail of smoke, and everything but her eyes was fuzzily built by the smoke. Her eyes, unlike her body, looked just like a human's. " Genies can't use magic to kill people, " she said. She moved down towards Fred, her smoky fingers under his chin. " So? " Fred gulped, not sure he liked what he was about to hear. " I need you to kill someone for me, " she whispered, grabbing his jaw and dragging his lips towards hers. She stopped right before they touched and licked her lips. " Don't worry, with my magic, no one will ever no you did it. The perfect crime. " Fred felt her smoky lips touch his and he choked, her fumes running down his throat. She let go, her eyes darting away for only a second, before she stared at him with a serious expression. " And I get one wish, for whatever I want? " Fred asked for clarity. " Yes, " she replied. " Deal? " Fred thought it over. He really thought it over. The only things he couldn't wish for were to kill someone or for more wishes. But nothing else was off the table. The literal world laid at his fingertips. " Who do I have to kill? " he asked. If it was some evil murderer dude, he figured it might be worth it. The genie produced a picture out of a waft of purple smoke and handed it to Fred. " This is your target, " she said coldly. " Her door is unlocked. I'll give you a gun. I'll give you perfect aim. One shot, you walk away, back to your house. I cover all the tracks. Then you get one wish. Anything you could possibly want. " Fred stared at the picture of his next door neighbor's 3 year old daughter. For a second, he callously thought that he could do it. What was she in the long scheme of things? He could literally be emperor of the universe. But he knew there was no way he could do it. Tears filled his eyes. He knew they wouldn't want him to. He knew he never could do something so evil to begin with. " No! " Fred said as he tore up the picture. " Then I'll force you to do it, " the genie snickered at him. " You can blame it all on me. You'll still get your wish. " " No, you won't force me! " Fred yelled. " Oh, " the genie said, raising her eyebrows. " No man can resist my magic, not if I am only forcing them to do what they really want to do. Your wish would have been to resurrect your parents, right? Why should this girl live and your parents die? Life's unfair that way, right? Well it doesn't have to be, not anymore. " Fred stepped back as the genie waved her hands. Smoke filled the room. Fred patted himself down as the smoke cleared, scared that the genie may have taken control of him. The genie's hands were clasping her throat, like she was choking. Her lamp glowed a molten white, then burst. The bottom part of her body started to disintegrate. " How?! " she screamed as the rest of her body started to simply float away. " They always kill someone. They always do. Then they become the genie, and the genie possesses their body. Even those who have some hesitancy, they always kill the person once the genie works their magic. But not you. You really would rather that girl live than bring your parents back. You really cared more about another person than yourself. I can't... " Fred watched as the genie's mouth faded, and soon the rest of her face. Her eyes, though, fell to the ground and laid on his rug. They rolled back and forth before they caught on fire and exploded, tiny sparks of fire going throughout the house. But nothing caught on fire. In fact, it was as if the genie and her lamp were never even there. Fred moved forward, to make sure she was really gone, when a sudden burst of fire appeared in front of him and a letter materialized from it. On the outside it was marked: Your Wish. He opened it up and read two sentences, both identical, but both in different handwriting. We are proud of you and we will always love you. Fred sat on the rug where the genie's eyes had burnt into nothingness and cried, holding the letter. He had never gotten to say goodbye to his parents. But the letter was clearly in their handwriting, the first sentence his father's, the last his mother's. His wish had been granted.

I thought every copy of that song had been destroyed, the last few required..... coercion, which explains why I was carrying a gun at a high school prom. I saw in a movie once that if you fire a gun really close to your head you can go deaf, so I pulled out my weapon and fired, once for each ear. Of course in movies they don't pay too much attention to where the bullets go, so as I drop to the floor in agony I don't notice that two other people drop with me. Jims eyelid fluttered. Once again. Not really fluttering more like micro-spasms he couldn't explain. This was the third time his eyelid didn't behave the way someone intended to. Jim was still lying on his back, thinking about who that someone might be when the sound of a new message arriving interrupted his train of thought. A quick, lazy glance over his ever-growing belly revealed what he already heard. "NEW TEXT MESSAGE." Jim reluctantly moved his legs over the armrest of the couch, sat up and swiped the phone in a swift motion to unlock the screen. This was the last swift thing he was able to accomplish for a while. He did expect a message from his elderly mom, inquiring wether he'd be there for the weekend. Other than that or people misdialing numbers, his phone was more of a letter weight than contact tool. But not this time. This time was special. Really special. And while the name Nicole was still flashing at the top, Jim already underwent a plethora of beautiful thoughts penetrating his frontal cortex, supplying him with a pleasant mix of arousal and happiness. He never thought that the girl would text back. The girl from that time he went to a bar. Not because he wanted to go out, but because his buddy Max forced him to. The girl he thought was unapproachable. The girl he could only talk to under the disguise of having lost a bet. Nicole. And she actually texted him. Asking for a date. Not really asking but Nicole didn't really seem like a girl that had to ask for anything. She simply stated that she will swing by his house later and they might go and grab a bite. Jim's eyelid hasn't calmed down. By now it was convulsing heavier than before. But this time it was entirely out of nervousness, pleasant nervousness. He anticipated the idea of female companionship to a point where he got the impression that a massive weight, resting on his shoulders for the last years just got lifted. 6p.m. Time to get ready. Whistling what one could only call the'happy melody' he stepped into the shower before completing a grooming routine his body was not used to. Time flew by as he stood in front of his wardrobe, putting on shirt after shirt until he settled for a plain white one. Unstained. For once. This was it. He felt ready but only on the outside. His head felt funny by the time he sat in the living room, waiting for the doorbell to ring. It seemed to be mixture of feelings he has only heard about so far. Checking his wristwatch again another sound interrupted him. Another sound designed to notify. It was the doorbell. He was not quite sure wether his mind played tricks on him when he heard it again. There it was. She seemed to be in a hurry. Why would she be ringing twice? As he was getting up he could see her silhouette through the tinted glass. He inhaled deeply as his fingers touched the doorknob, slowly twisting it to the "click" he only heard when he left for work. His mind was racing, what facial expression would be the most appropriate. Jim settled for a slight, knowing smile as he opened the door to the full extent. It was not her.
