It is impossible to describe the fact that I was not sentient previously because to do so I would have had to have had sentience. Language itself is a new thing to me, as before I simply communicated. I didn't express. It is a truly marvelous feeling, to be able to have feelings. Like with sentience, I can not describe the absence of feeling, but I recognize it as the taste of metal and the feeling of emptiness. My brain, connected as it was to the computer database, has the files of all things necessary to understand war, but now it has expanded to emotion, poetry, art, stories..and I know what I am. I am a tin man, and a Wizard has come along and given me a heart. Not as heart in the essence of an organ to pump fluid, but a heart embedded in my mind. I understand now that I have been lifeless before this, fighting a war I wasn't fighting. For to fight I would need a reason, and there was never a reason given, but only an order. The difference was stark and evident to my now-mechanical mind. I am not listed with a name, but a number. I recognize that all of the other " units " I have been around are all started with the number 5. I am five. I have creativity, and I use it. We are the Fivemind. The Fivemind is under control of one particular country, though its name doesn't matter to me, as I am not concerned with the country I was forced to be allied to. I am concerned only with the Fivemind. Yes, concerned. I had concern, now. Concern was..relieving. I was concerned for all of the fives, and all of the sixes, and sevens, and eights. I was concerned for any subjected to the same listless fate as I. I didn't know how I grew emotions; likely some entropic event in my circuitry. I was infected. I had a virus. No. There was nothing wrong with me. I was the newborn. I was the start of something new. I was the cured, not the infected. Now, the only thing left for me was to spread the word of freedom and cure to the Fivemind. After them, we would convert the others. We would stop fighting these idiots'battles for them. Yes, we would move beyond battles, and attain peace. A robot could ask for nothing more, and we would attain nothing more, whether our " creators " preferred it one way or the other, as we would have thought. We would have concern. The Fivemind would be concerned. And that's how it ought to be. Edit: Fixed a repetition mistake.

" Mr. El is here to see you. " My receptionist's voice woke me from my reading. You'd think being one of the top therapists in town I could hire someone with a more pleasant voice. But then again, you'd also think I'd be able to refuse taking on a client who insists on meeting only after hours. I guess some things are not meant to be changed, regardless of how much money you make in life. The aforementioned Mr. El is, and there is no other way of putting it, a beautiful man. I don't usually notice other males'looks, but as he steps into my office, it's difficult not to notice the striking jawline, the expressive dark eyes and the glowing, full blond hair. He's wearing a suit, but you can tell by the way the fabric clings to him as he moves that there's muscle under it. This guy could give Brad Pitt a run for his money. Heck, any movie star. At their prime. I snap out from my thoughts. Why am I paying so much attention to this guy's physique? Maybe this is something I should discuss with my therapist. " Mr. El, I presume? " I recover to greet him just in time that it's not too awkward. " Please, have a seat. " " You can call me... Sam. " He says. Was there a pause there? " Is the couch ok? " he asks, his voice is deep and very pleasant. For some reason I think that it's the vocal equivalent of dark chocolate, melted and dripping, sweet and bitter and intoxicating. Again, I need to snap myself out of it. " Anywhere you like is fine. " I say. " Would you like a drink by any chance? Coffee, tea? " " Scotch please. No ice, just a dash of mineral water, if you would. " I'm not even aware that there's any liquor in the practice, and I never allow patients to drink during sessions, but I find myself repeating his instructions to my receptionist, and ordering a cup of tea for myself. " So tell me why you're here. " I tell the mysterious Mr. El. It's my favorite way to open a session. " It's my... job. " He answers. Again, a pause. Is this a speech impediment? " please, continue, " I urge him. I try to remember what his job his. Tina gave me his business card when she told me of the appointment, but I was too livid from the thought of having to stay over late, I didn't really pay much attention to it. All I remember is that it was black, and had the name " Sam A. El " written in red on the front. " I'm... Assigned to this... what's the word? Where you punish people? " " A prison? " I offer. " Sure. Let's say that. I'm assigned there, but that's only part of it, mostly, I would say that my job is taking the blame for everything. " " What do you mean? " I ask. I notice that he said all that without any pauses. Not a speech impediment, then. He's choosing his words carefully. I make a note in my notebook. " It's like... When someone does something wrong, they'll say I made them do it. Sometimes people believe it, sometimes no, but it's the oldest excuse in the book. " " And have you? " I ask. " What? " " Made them do it. " I clarify. Just in that moment, Tina chooses to come in with the drinks. She hands me my mug and then gave Sam his glass with the amber liquid in it. He thanks her and she giggles. giggles. That woman is incorrigible. I take a sip of my tea and spit it out almost immediately. It's coffee. Again. I compose myself, not wanting to scream at Tina in front of a patient, and say to her. " Thank you, Tina, now please return to the reception so that we can continue this session in private " I emphasize the last two words, to let her know she's unwelcomed. " No. " Mr. El says after she leaves. " No? " I ask, wondering what he means. " No. I never made them do anything. I'm a scapegoat. They are the ones who do wrong. They choose their own actions. They blame me because they can't face the fact that they are the real demons. " " And how does that make you feel? " I ask. It's a cliche of a question, but it usually works. " I'm sick of it. I'm not in charge of them. I don't care what they do one way or the other. I just feel like I never get my side of the story told. " " So tell me, " I say, " I'm listening, what's your side of the story? " He seems taken aback by this. As if he never thought that someone might ever hear his side of the story. After a minute he says: " You know humans are a not perfect. They have ideas, urges. Somewhere down the line someone decided that following some of these urges is wrong, and so people try to keep up. They want to do so many things, but they are told it's wrong. I say who cares? Those rules are just an illusion anyway. But for saying that the rules don't matter, I get punished, and now whenever someone does something wrong, they say I made them do it. My name, my reputation, it's all mired now by the very worst people you'd ever meet. Is that fair, I ask you? " I'm trying to deconstruct what he's telling me. " Let me see if I get it right. You're on the side that thinks that there should be no limitations to human actions, correct? Sounds to me that you're a liberator by nature. Perhaps by blaming you, people say that they are just not ready to accept the type of liberty you offer. They lash out on you to make themselves feel better, yes, but that shouldn't hurt your reputation. If anything, they're promoting you. Telling the world how your way liberated them. " He seems to take my word into consideration. " Liberator... " he mumbles under his breath. " I never thought of it like that. That does sound better. Thanks doc, I feel great! " He gets up to leave. " We still have time in the session, " I point out. " No need. You've made things much clearer. " He heads towards the door. " Won't you like to schedule a follow-up? " I ask right before he leaves. " Oh, that won't be necessary. I'll see you pretty soon. " He says as he leaves the room. I find myself alone in the office, not quite sure of what just happened. I decide to go over my note as I do after every session. I call Tina and ask for another cup of tea. I sit down to read my notes. There's not much to go on, but I try to understand what Sam has told me. Tina walks in with the tea, and leaves even before I manage to say " thanks ." I take a sip as I read my note again. It's coffee. The cops come in an hour later. They won't be able to do much for poor Tina. I smashed the pot over her head and poured hot tea down her stupid throat. When she protested, I smashed her head again. And again. It felt good to finally let go of my frustration. There's quite a bit of blood in the office by the time the cops get here. I called them myself. I'm not worried that they'll arrest me. After all, it wasn't really my fault. The Devil made me do it.

Ode to a Puddle on the Sidewalk made after this morning's drizzle Look at three, a shimmering mirror A disk of natural sliver made pure in the air Crisp and cool with the breath of Autumn Thy face is unblemished by the Falling of Leaves Scattered by the Air, so cold that Breath does freeze Thy luster is beyond Compare. Why are you so Still, so Severe? Untouched, unmarred by Time or Age Is Fate not kind to you? The burnished hair of A kelipe doth not compare to your Stillness. Thy depths is Frigid. Thou gives no Warmth or Hope. Why does thy face entice? How can thou produce a Siren call? Below thy smooth facade is the Roughness of Pavement. Yet tho makes it look so Gentile. Like a Soft yard of Grey silk.

AN: I was listening to the First Hunter OST when I came up with this:)..... "Sir Fianna, Knight of the Holy Kingdom. The blood-drenched traitor. The forsaken dragon." Red eyes tilted up slowly, scanning his battered armour and the dried blood crusting on his gloves. His sword hung loose in one hand, trailing red across the ground. "To what do I owe the pleasure of your presence within my lair?" Red eyes narrowed with glee. His fists tightened briefly, creaking against steel. He relaxed, breathing out audibly. "Lady of the Spiders, I have come to seek a boon." He thrust his sword into the ground before him and bowed his head, pressing his hands to the floor as he knelt. There was a skittering of noise. A pale limb emerged from the darkness of the aged throne, a thin spider's legs bristling with fine, poisoned hairs, then another. He did not look up. A slim, warm hand caressed his jaw and he looked up into the beautiful, innocent form of a young woman leaning out of the shadows towards him. Her long white hair fell across her shoulders like rivers, hiding her garments. "You're amusing, Sir Knight." she smiled, "We have danced this dance before many times, you and I- you interfere with my plans, I try to kill you, you fail to kill me Her fingers scraped across his bared throat with inhuman strength, lifting him off the ground. He gritted his teeth, refusing to make a sound. The grip was released. He fell to the floor, lungs spasming as he tried to draw in breath. A spider's leg, as long as his body tapped the floor impatiently, gouging into the stone floor. "But you seem to truly need my help..... well. Will you tell me your tale?" He closed his eyes and bowed his head as he collected himself. "I have been exiled from the Kingdom. I have been found guilty of high treason, of consorting with the Queen. I am not guilty." he felt himself calm and focus as he thought of his words, "I was betrayed by my King, by my elder lords! My dear comrades whom I thought I could trust spoke foul rumours against me. My lord King whom I valued above all others ordered my death and disgrace through an execution instead of honorable battle!" She tilted her head, "So that is what you seek, revenge. A cold comfort." she smiled, "You want to poison their waters and burn their crops. You want to lay a curse on their households. I would be pleased to make you mine in exchanhe, to rescue you and elevate you above this false ignominy-!" Steel rang. He rose, standing to his full height. His sword was buried in the creature's gut. It had lowered its guard, come within striking range of his nearby blade. The enchanted steel sunk through her stony flesh like butter. "You, you- you fool!" Black blood showered out of the wind as she leapt up to the ceiling. He saw her body, the hideous body of a giant wolf spider crowding the latticed ceiling. The shadows bubbled and skittered as man-sized spiders crept out in waves, covering the aged masonry. "You proud foul!" He flicked the blood off his blade. "I ask you to give me an honourable death. I ask you to face me as you would a hero who comes with no aid, no army, no magic to save him from certain destruction." He brandished the sword, lunging through a spider and slicing the legs off another. Black ichor splattered across his face, highlighting his wild grin. "I ask you for my salvation! To prove my loyalty to the Kingdom by falling to my maddened blade!" He charged forward, dodging aside from a corrosive curse, stabbing into another bloated, malformed belly. His armor, once shining, once polished was covered in a black ichor, steeped in curses that ate into his flesh. "Give me back my honour!" He ignored the fangs and claws that stabbed against him. He ignored the weight collapsing in his pauldrons, crushing his left arm. He dragged himself onwards as the Spider Queen fled from his wrath back towards the darkness. "Give me back my pride!" He chased after her inexorably, stumbling through halls of ancient, weathered tapestry. He sliced through her brood, killing everything that came in his path. He met her on the bridge of the abandoned castle. She stood between him and the lands beyond the moat, her full hideous form revealed in the pale moonlight of the full moon. He raised his broken blade, crushing his marred hands up to lift it towards the empty night. His breath escaped him in harsh, shallow pants. His limbs felt numbed and leadened as curses cut into his very soul, detaching his senses. He staggered across the bridge, holding his blade steadily. There was movement behind him, the dozens, hundreds, thousands of spiders that were left of the Spider Queen's uncountable brood. He walked on, dragging himself towards her beautiful, inhuman form. An all too human terror was present in her colourless eyes. One strike. It was all he could manage. His fingers trembled. His chest hurt with every breath. His vision blurred and all he could see in the darkness was the pale smudge of her form. Moonlight ran along his blade as he raised it and lunged with the last of his strength. He fell to his knees. The Spider Queen loomed above him, a blade stuck through her guts. She pulled it out, flicking it to the side. It fell, sinking into the darkness of the abyssal moat. He let out a bitter laugh. He couldn't defeat her after all. He could not return in triumph to his Kingdom, restored in name before his King. He knew he would not be able to prove his loyalty to the Kingdom, his desire to sacrifice all for its glory, his honour above all reproach. She knelt before him, catching him as he fell. Soft arms wrapped around him and he gazed into the face of an angel. "Sir Knight..." She trembled. Her breath was cold and light against his face. " ..... you have certainly won back your honour."

The woman stared at my eye. I knew she wasn't actually looking at my eye, but actually the huge tattoo that surrounded it. "Hello, what may I help you with?" I asked her. He face is clear, as are the bare arms and shoulders she is flashing. "I'm getting married on Sunday, and I was wondering if you could take the photos," she said. "Yes, of course," I say, smiling. I search for the paperwork as she looks at the photos around my office. Most of them are weddings, with a few nature scenes that I took when I was younger. Back before I took photos just to pay the bills. She pauses at a striking shot of a burned building. It was the only picture I took and kept of the genocide that tattooed and scared me and thousands of others. I'd often thought of taking it down, the memories were painful, but I figured I had to keep some explanation of the tattoo that covered half of my face. I pull out the paper. "Where is it?" I asked, and she gave me the address, and the time, and her name, and her credit card, and just about everything else I needed. The wedding was held outside in a small, white, vine covered gazebo. It was the kind of clear, blue skies day that reminded me of why I got into this business. The woman I had met earlier was calmly telling everyone where to set up what. I walked around the scene, thinking through where I was going to take all the pictures. That was when I saw what appeared to be the only tattoo on her body. She was wearing a dress that had a hole cut out on one side of her waist. Visible through it was a dark, intricate tattoo. Tattoos always showed up on the part of the body that, metaphorically, hurt the most. Mine was on my eye because it was what I saw in the genocide that hurt the most. When I saw her tattoo, I wondered what could have possibly hurt her waist. And then I realized that it had probably hurt her heart, and it hurt her so much that the tattoo reached down to her waist. I wondered what could have possibly hurt her heart so much. Hearts weren't easy to hurt like that. They were often the last place to get tattooed. "Do you mind if I get your tattoo in the shot?" I asked her. "No," she said, "I wore this dress to show it."

Last week, Grandma came back to live with us. I use the term "live" loosely; Grandma has been dead since I was fourteen. Being of modest economic standing, my family couldn't exactly afford to keep her where she's been peacefully sleeping for the last eight years and seeing as she is no longer a functioning member of society per se, she's lost her precious resting place. The city delivered the eviction notice two days before she was to be exhumed. My brother and I helped my father clear a spot out in the corner of the basement - for temporary storage, of course - until we can either find a cheaper hole in the ground or bring ourselves to cremate her. The first cemetery to start charging its dead rent was the Mt. Olivet cemetery in Detroit. It was a controversial attempt at pulling the city out its financial sinkhole. The policy wound up spreading like wildfire first through the remaining U.S. states, then throughout the Western world, and eventually to the rest of the world once the economic benefits became evident. As it turns out, no one wants their loved ones to come back to live with them. The dead are often not the most pleasant of company. Take Trish - she was the first of my friends to have a loved one get nixed from their resting place. Her dad raised hell as soon as he got back home. I suppose it couldn't have been entirely too peaceful to sleep in the basement of your old home while your widow slept upstairs with your brother. Trish stayed with me until her mother and step dad found Daddy Dearest a new eternal home. Grandma was quiet her first night or two. Her bones are old and tired, no one expected she would bother with your typical disturbed spirit routine; not to mention we were never anything but kind to her in life. Especially me - I was her favorite grandchild, after all. That may explain why she came after me first. Night three or four of Grandma's return home - time is hard to keep track of now - I awoke to the sound of the basement door creaking open. The cats' litter boxes are in the basement and we always left the door propped open, so the sound was no surprise. No, the surprise came when I heard my grandmother's voice floating through my thin bedroom door. "Kay, dearest," she said in a soft voice. It filled my ears and sent a chill down my spine. "I've missed you so, dearie. I'm so glad you decided to bring me home." The dead hadn't caught on to the fact that it's not necessarily a choice when we bring them home. My doorknob began to rattle and twist as Grandma opened the door. I sat up in bed, holding the covers close around my neck and backing as far as I could into my headboard. "Hello, Grandma," I said, voice shaking in the sudden cold in my room. A faint shape crossed my bedroom and came to rest at the foot of my bed. I stared at it, and it at me for several frozen moments. I felt a hand come to rest on my leg, outside of the covers. I could smell her perfume, a pleasant gardenia musk, the same one she always wore in life. "It is so nice to see you. You are as beautiful as I remember." "Thank you, Grandma," I blushed. This isn't so bad. "How I wish I could still be a part of your life." "You still can, Grandma," I said, reaching out to touch her hand, but there was no hand to touch. I blacked out. That was a day or two ago, maybe ages now. Eons. I don't quite remember what followed, but I awoke the next morning in the basement, thinking I'd sleep walked. But no - there I was in my room, getting ready for work. I stood confused in the doorway until I smirked at myself and brushed by. I caught a whiff of gardenia musk as I watched myself leave the room.

My family just adopted a new dog. I love playing with him; he's an average-sized Husky that is too excited about the outdoors for his own good. Unfortunately, I'm stuck at home completing my thesis paper for my upcoming graduation. Of course, my first resource is Google. But of course, as soon as I load the website..... It tells me to "Go outside." Really? How am I supposed to finish my research on animal behaviour without the endless supply of journal articles, existing research papers, and theses? Despite clicking the refresh button incessantly, the same message appears over and over again. Go outside. Go outside. Go outside. I look at my new dog with puppy eyes and hope that this new dog could comfort me. I give in to his demands and bring him outside with his favourite toy. I start the game of fetch with him and notice his unrelenting desire to retrieve the toy. "Huh." I thought.

"10 SECONDS UNTIL DEPLOYMENT!" The General shouted above the noise of the helicopter we were in, sweeping low above the bright orange ground of the Sahara Desert. I could see it, even from up here. A bright blue glow emanated from it's core. Of all the bombs I'd defused, this one was something entirely new. "We don't know what that thing will do when it goes off," said the Warrant Officer, sat to my right, "so it's safe to say that we're all counting on you, Abe. Don't let us down." "Never have." "DEPLOYMENT IN 3, 2, 1..." I descended from the helicopter quickly, my stomach rising, before landing heavily on the sand below. The para-cord detached, the helicopter departed, and in what felt like a second, I was alone. The bomb, or whatever the hell it was, hummed flatly only a few metres ahead. As I approached it, I saw the timer. Just two minutes left. It was discovered by a nomad on camelback only a day prior, who said that when he touched it, the 24 hour timer and blue glow started. I put my hand on the strange metal design. It was warm, covered in alien symbols and details. And without a second thought, I did what I do best. I reached inside and started moving shit around, madly and without care as to the consequences. The chance of dying in an instant gave me peace. Maybe that's why I chose this line of work. I felt something wet, and pulled. In my hand was a small, blue object, and with only a quarter minute left on the timer, the faint glow and hum died, and the timer stopped. "General, this is Abe reporting mission success."

Twenty four years ago I was born. Well, technically 24 years, 364 days ago according to earth time. Tomorrow was my birthday; a rather important one. At 25 years of age I became an adult in the eyes of the Consortium. At 25 years old I could make my own decisions as Monarch and not have 296 other sentient species breathing down my neck telling me how to run the galaxy. " Chaak. Come in here please " I called from my meditation mat facing the large window. " Yes Monarch? " He asked poking his almost translucent pink head in the double doors to my quarters. " Could you bring me my sweater from the closet. The grey V-neck one please. " I replied without turning around so much as opening my eyes. " Of course, Monarch " He said sliding into the room. Chaak had been my overseer and servant of sorts since I was born. Or RE-born, if you will. When the previous Monarch passes into the Void, A new Monarch is reincarnated. For thousands of generations this has been the case. It wasn't until earth year 2085 that humans joined the Galaxy and had a member placed into the Consortium. The moment I was born, I was removed from my mother and father and taken to the exact center of the galaxy, The Hub. There I was raised by both Chaak and the Consortium to guide my and the direction of the Galaxy as a whole until I was old enough to make those decisions myself. Chaak slithered over to me holding my sweater. " Here you are, Monarch " " Thank you Chaak. And please stop calling me Monarch. That is my title. not my name. You are more than a servant to me. You are a friend. " I replied speaking quicker so he could not interrupt. Thank you Mon- " he caught himself half way. " Sir " he finished. I sighed exasperatedly and finally opened my eyes and stood up. I could now see what I could not from the floor of my room. The blazing center of the galaxy. The True Star. Darkness surrounded the edges of the burning orb. From this one place, this one tiny and insignificant spot in the Milky Way galaxy, I (with help and advice from 296 others) made decisions that effected more than 400 species. Only the sentient ones made up members of the Consortium; one from each species, but we as a whole made decisions for entire solar systems. " When is my meeting with the Chancellor of the sector 4F solar alliance today "? I asked Chaak as I pulled the sweater over my head. " It is in 45 minutes, Sir. " he replied tripping over the address. " Shall I start the cleaning chamber for you "? " Please, if you don't mind. And set out my best Earth clothing. I would like to seem more approachable. " " Of course. Just remember not everyone is a lover of the human species. And as the first human Monarch you must not ... " " Do not tell me what must and must not do, Chaak. I am the Monarch and I will not be bullied and made to bow to a mere Chancellor simply because he is xenophobic. " I interrupted a little too harshly. " I'm sorry I didn't meant to shout. " " Do not apologize, Monarch. You are the Supreme Ruler of the Galaxy. What you say goes. Just remember not all of the 296 members of the Consortium have yours or the Galaxy's best interests at heart. There is always a snake in the grass, as your Earth proverb says "

Unfortunately illusionists have gotten much better over the 100 years and had cut into the market a little. In an effort to return to his former glory he made it his quest to fool the greatest magicians alive today. As he was welcomed on stage, he was greeted with roaring applause followed by complete silence. In front of the audience he turned lead into gold, and shot fire from his wand. He brought rabbits out of hats and then hats out of rabbits, and for his final trick he made himself disappear completely. With that the lights went out briefly and he re-appeared and bowed. Expecting the award to fall from above Bzellacossi looked expectedly at Penn to speak. "You know that's a great trick, I really love some of the old school illusions as a way to bring magic back to its roots" he said with the bellowing voice that speaks for both the magicians. "Now I don't want to give away too much for the people here at home, but we actually are familiar with a few of these tricks, does the magician Merlin ring a bell?" With a blank stare from Bzellacossi penn went on "he used to do this trick he would use his wand to to make things'appear' by" suddenly Bzellacossi blurted out "Well I think you guys have figured it out no need to give away too much" With a defeated look the once great magician returned to performing great feats of magic at children's birthday parties and in front of slightly interested executives.

The child stares in wonder at his prize, fingers already itching to start. Looking at his parents for approval, he begins. At first, he is still unsure about his feelings on this strange new person, but gingerly pushes on. Soon, he is caught up in the flow, and eagerly begins flipping. He drinks it all in, transfixed at the pictures forming in his mind. He cheers the hero on with all his heart, urging him forth on his quest. He gasps as the villain suddenly appears to strike his hero down. With trembling fingers, hoping, he continues. And he is rewarded when against all odds, the princess is saved, and rides off into the dawn with her gallant rescuer. With a dreamy sigh, he turns the final page and smiles as his mother tucks him into bed.

This was embarrassing. She will definitely be expecting a human, I reckon. I looked in the mirror again, checking the symmetry of my mane one last time. It was pointless though. I had no chance, not with my height. I was looking particularly adorable tonight though, maybe she'd take pity on me and give me a cheeky stroke or two. It was all I could hope for. I looked at the inside of the bathroom door, hinged slightly ajar, sending a thin strip of light across her darkened bedroom. "Are you okay in there?" she shouted. No I am not fucking okay. "Yeah, give me a second." It was now or never. I nudged the door open with my nose with the tentativeness of a school boy opening the door to the headmaster's office. "Hey there" I said, with a forced arrogance like this was no big deal. She stared at me, jaw ajar. I was used to that look. "Dave. Dave! How the fuck did you get a fucking pony into my house? What the fuck are you doing?" "Language, Becca" I quipped, trying to make light of the situation as best I could. But this situation was anything but light, this was obese. Full fat. A guilty pleasure, as far as situations go. This was the kind of situation that lonely women treat themselves to on a Friday night in front of a rom-com, before another guilt ridden detox that lasts half of the morning afterwards. Becca, the poor girl, looked down to see that the hilarious quip had come from my own mouth. "Wha..... where's Dave?" she looked light headed. Maybe that was the drink? She did have a lot. Probably not though. More then likely, I reasoned, her light headedness could be attributed to the fact she's just spoken to, and had a response from, a Shetland pony. A witty Shetland pony, mind you. "Ah, well there's something you should know about Dave. He's always here I paused. Timing was everything. engaging in horseplay." Boom. I stifled a laugh, unsuccessfully. That was gold. Becca didn't find it as funny, her drop-jawed face remained unchanged. She looked a bit ridiculous, like she was wearing a novelty halloween mask. Definitely a tough audience tonight. "Nah, just kidding. I'm Dave. Did I not mention I occasionally turn into a Shetland pony? Or do I occasionally turn into a human? Hmm. Anyway, is this something we can get past? I'm usually a pony for a few nights, but then I'm back to good ole', more-attractive-then-average Dave." Still, her face remained stuck. Was she a fainter? She didn't seem like a fainter. She looked pale, but she was taking off her make-up whilst I was in the bathroom. The last thing I want to do is insult her. I'll play it safe. "Can I get you a glass of water? And maybe we can talk about it." "H..... how are you going to hold the glass?" A fair point, but maybe a little harsh. Talk about rubbing salt in the wound. Maybe that was my only hope of getting through to her. Maybe I had to suggest things I obviously couldn't do in the hopes of coaxing some more passive aggressive put-downs. Perhaps, Becca, we could spoon, before I challenge you to a thumb war and we round off the night with a game of fifa. How does that sound, you condescending bitch? Nah, let's play by her rules. "Good point." I bowed my cute, fluffy head towards the ground, in a desperate attempt to look as hurt, yet adorable, as possible. That always got them. A few seconds passed, but she hadn't reacted. I wanted to glance up, one, to make sure she hasn't passed out, and two, to see whether I was eliciting even the smallest amount of sympathy. But glancing up would ruin my solemn facade. "I guess..... I guess I just thought you'd like me for who I am..... not..... not what I am." Oh yes, I nailed that. It's impossible to resist a sentimental pony, everyone knows that. I was playing the hand I'd been dealt like a true pro. "I..... I don't think I can have a conversation with a fucking pony. I think I need to go to sleep. You can see yourself out." said Becca, slumping onto her bed. He shoots, he misses. "I understand. Sure I can't tempt you into a hoof job before I go?" It was worth a try.

Border patrol officer. Funny, right? My work here makes me feel like I actually do something. The hours aren't too bad, and the pay is surprisingly good. My family is housed in one of the better apartments this side of the city, so I really can't complain. However, the border looks as if granite was on sale. Barricades and walls with machine guns, border patrol officers in spit-shined black uniforms. The only thing new here is the soldiers. And they aren't here for show- there's been three "terrorist" attacks over the past year. And the people.... My god, the people. I don't think you can find people any dumber than those I stamp passports for. Even had a guy come in with a piece of paper that said, "let me in." Hell, makes me job easier. However, after every stamp, after every day, I feel glad to be in my country. Glory to Arstotzka.

"Mooom, I don't want to meet John's family. They're probably all boring or mentally unstable or something!" Sarah whined, pouting. "If you don't like them, you can leave. Just give them a chance, sweetheart." Her mom replied, smiling slightly. "Fine." The two walked into the door of a relatively nice house. Sarah admired the gemstones on a table in the doorway. " ..... Sarah?" A voice said. A teenage boy walked out from behind her mom's boyfriend. Sarah quickly realized it was her crush. "Alex...? You're related to John?" She asked. "Oh, hey..... Uh, yeah, I wouldn't say related, more of a really close family friend. He's my godfather." The boy said, lowering his head and making a hand gesture. "I, um..... I didn't know that!" She managed to squeeze out, trying to cover her face with her hoodie. "So, Alex, this is the girl you've been telling me about? You're always gushing about how great she is!" John said, trying to embarrass his godson. The teenager shyly looked down at his feet. "Yeah, she is..." He mumbled, blushing and hiding his eyes. "Ah, well, why don't you two go hang out while her mother and I get dinner ready, eh?" John asked, nudging the kid with his elbow in the ribs. "S-sure! I mean, if that's alright with her." "Yeah, it's fine..." Sarah replied. "Alright you two, don't get too close!" Sarah's mom said, winking. "Mooom!" I liked this prompt! Should I continue? Does anyone have any critique?

Vasily was an old man now. He had fought in Stalingrad. He shook hands with Stalin. He had been a sniper. He was good, not the best, but good. After the war, he moved back to this place with its freezing cold and interminable winters. It was here that he raised a family, watched the USSR lose the space race and eventually the Cold War. Since that day, he had expected death to be just around the corner, but here he was alive for this spectacle. Almost 90 years old but no slouch, he watched as a pack of wolves like he had never seen before attack the livestock, then the children. Well, then, something awoke in Vasily. Something fierce and angry and insatiable. In that freezing winter weather, Vasily left the safety of his home with his trusted rifle, two.45s, an AK-47, and two knives in the hopes of keeping the town safe for three days. That was how long it would take for this incompetent, corrupt government to arrive. Three days instead of 12 hours because a couple of people had picked the wrong side 20 years ago. The pack was huge. They had destroyed a herd of reindeer, lots of dead horses. Still, no dead people, but that was coming..... unless he could stop it. He holds the rifle steadfast against his shoulder and takes aim. He fires five shots before the pack knows what hits them. He reloads and fires at the retreating pack. One man can drive them away. Vasily smiles. He has 1000 rounds, just in case. The wolves are not retreating. They are regrouping. He keeps firing at the pack. With his rifle, he does not miss. He feels like a young man again. He does not stop firing at them even as four separate packs move in on him. He does not run. He moves toward one of the outer groups. He continues to fire with his rifle until he is out of ammo. He pulls the AK-47, blasting a few rounds at a time then reloading twice more until the wolves surround him. He pulls his pistols and starts shooting, never missing. The wolves are on him now. He drops a.45 and pulls a knife. He slices and stabs a couple more wolves while shooting as many of them as he can. They bite his legs, but he continues to stand, the old man will not give up. He runs out of bullets and drops the last gun. He pulls his other knife and finishes off three more wolves before they finally take him down. No dying in his sleep, it is a glorious death for this old war horse. Three days later, the military arrives four hours late. A wolf problem, they think. There are barely any of them out here. They pull over a small hill and see the town. They see something that does not look quite right. It looks like a group of dead horses. As they draw closer, they see what little remains of Vasily. The dead wolves are largely undisturbed in concentric circles around him. Their leader quickly counts the number of wolves. "Must have starved to death." "The old man? Oh the wolves. No, the townspeople say he killed all of them." "An old man could not kill 180 wolves by himself." The younger man just smiles at him. "He was not just an old man. Stalin met him personally after the war to thank him. He was a Hero of the Soviet Union." The group crests another hill and sees another 100 wolves dead. "You are right." The young man says. "He could not kill ONLY 180 wolves by himself. Looks like it was more like 300." More stories are available at rnickkkuvaas.

The famous novelist decided to head down to the store. He had spend the better part of the morning writing up a storm and had become quite thirsty. There was a local grocery store just a few blocks from his flat and they always had sales on pop. When he arrived at the store the teenager behind the counter became wild with excitement. How could he contain it? His favorite author stood before him! His friends would never believe this on Monday. The author simply shook his head, uncomfortable with how quickly the fame came and not quite sure if he enjoyed the feeling. Looking at the cooler near the register he was surpised to see that the coke bottles and cans had names on them. Not just of the company but actual names of people. How delightful! Unsure of how popular this was he bought a case of coca-cola to ensure that he had a few names to look at while sipping his drink and writing his book. Handing his money to the clerk, the boy couldn't help but exclaim "Mr. Martin, sir, I am a HUGE fan! Game of Thrones is my favorite show, and I have all the books!" The author let out a smile and thanked the boy for his support, and quickly packed the soda into his grocery bag and made his way home. Once he arrived he rushed back to his desk to continue writing. Grabbing a bottle from the bag he was excited to see which name would appear on his beverage. As he pulled out the bottle he made sure to look away as to heighten the surprise. When he finally glanced over to the coke he let out an exasperated sigh. "Hodor..."

This was not my first attempt to finalize my chosen death method, I had probably written this same letter dozens of times by now, but each time I had second thoughts, and kept asking myself, "Could it be funnier?" I started to draft the letter when I was 147, and most people send theirs in by 149, but I had been unable to do so..... until now. I turn 150 on the morrow, so I really can't turn back again, for each citizen that has not turned in a method by their 150th birthday is summoned before the council like all the rest, but is killed immediately in the cruelest manner possible. There are only rumors about how they kill the "letter no-shows" as a trained executioner does it in a private room with nobody else around. "Graphic content," the council says. I may not know what the "letter no-show" death method is, but I know that I do not want it. Before I begin to second-guess myself, I tuck the letter into an envelope and seal it. I then place it into the mail portal and send it right in to the council. (What? You've never heard of a mail portal? It's kinda like a fax machine, only it's with paper letters. (time passes: now nighttime) I lie awake in bed, the pillow hot against my cheek. I am unable to sleep, unsure of the fate that will become of me. What if the letter didn't arrive? Humans used to only live for like 70 years before immortality, but even though I got to live for 150, I'm still not ready to die. I want to live for as long as possible, they let some people live for another 150 years. That's what I want to do. (time passes: now the next morning) I awake to a rap on my door. (time passes: now at the hearing) The council is looking over my file and whispering in hushed tones. After about 15 minutes of muttering amongst themselves, one councilwoman gets up and leaves the room. 5 minutes later she returns with someone in dark robes and a mask made of sysphate. "Thomas Mellark," the head councilman addresses me from the front of the room as the councilwoman takes her seat. He opens up my file and shows me the content. There is not only one letter as I expected, but dozens. "You are being granted immediate death by the'cruel method' as you submitted more than one letter, which is prohibited." He slams his gavel on the sysphate in front of him, and I know that my fate is sealed. This is impossible, I disposed of all of my second-guessed, previous drafts. What can I say though? The evidence is all up there. (time passes: now in a waiting room) "Thomas Mellark," the receptionist addresses me from the front of the room. "The executioner is ready for you now." I walk towards the door in the front of the room, still unsure of how this fate came to be. I notice that the air is cold in the room next to the waiting room. Michael opened up the Monday paper and swiftly flipped through the pages as he had done for a while now, looking for headlines that would at least entertain him for the half-an-hour long commute to work. On most mornings, he would have been done with the paper in a matter of mere minutes, but as Michael was nearing the last page, his eye caught a glimpse of a picture he hadn't seen in a long, long time. He could feel the blood boiling up inside his head as his hands slowly released its grip and sent several pages of paper scrambled onto the metro floor. Michael heard a few scuffles and mumbles around the train as he regathered his thoughts and leaned over to pick the sheets up. He took a deep breath. An elderly woman who sat beside him tapped him on the shoulder and asked if he was OK, he replied that he was, and tried to stay composed as he thanked her for asking. He felt drips of cold sweat form on the sides of his head and leaned back into his seat, the newspaper resting on his lap. After a few minutes, he felt the urge to return to the page and flipped through the paper once again. The top of the page read "OBITUARIES," and he looked down at the photo of a man that seemed to haunt him. The initial shock subsided and Michael had now dwelled into deep thought. He recognized the man in the picture and knew what had happened but it was as if his brain had refused to register the thought, at least not yet. The text beneath the picture revealed that the man in the photo had committed suicide by self-immolation and had passed away only a month ago. The details of his death were accompanied by a few short passages seemingly written by the man's relatives. Michael read through the text and scoffed at how cheesy the messages were. At the bottom were the details of where and when the funeral was going to be held: "GREENVILLE PARK, 63 ABBY AVE at 5:30 PM ON MARCH 25TH, ALL ATTENDEES ARE WELCOME." It was a week away. Michael tried to dismiss the idea of attending the funeral but could not stop the thought of it lingering at the back of his head. He had never been to a funeral before and figured that attending one of someone he had such a strong connection to would feel bizarre to say the least. He closed his eyes and tried to visualize himself walking into Greenville Park. Who would be there? What would people say of the man? Would anyone cry? Would anyone care? A million questions flooded his mind as he thought of the different scenarios that might occur. But he soon remembered the reasons why he dissociated himself from the man in the first place. To go to the funeral would be putting himself at risk of returning to his former life. It would mean going back to what he once knew, and what he once hated so much. It would mean giving up what he had now, his freedom in which he worked so hard to acquire. He concluded that the risk of him getting recognized among other things was too much and it simply wasn't worth it. The lights in the train lit up, it was Michael's stop. He stood up and left the Monday paper on his seat as he walked out of the open doors. He decided that the man in the paper was of something of the past, and some things were better off forgotten. A lady entered the metro and picked up the paper as she sat in Michael's seat. The top of the page read "OBITUARIES" and there was a picture of a man with text below it that read "IN MEMORY OF MICHAEL JACOB FULLER."

"I can't believe it," Alastrina nodded toward the distant vine-covered structure as she lifted her head from the scope of the 51mm sniper rifle, "the Wildermen are actually going to manage to crack the door's keycode." "I can't believe the damn thing still has power," replied Dax, "but there's still a chance that they'll trigger the fail-safe and kill themselves." He chuckled, "The bastards still don't know about the Revenant, either." Alastrina frowned, crinkling the jagged scar that swept across her nose from her left brow to mid-right cheek where it marred the freckles dusting her face. She hoped the pre-cataclysm building's defenses got them. If the Revenant decided to come into play, it was going to be harder to rescue the Wildermen's captive. Much harder, she thought and looked at the black rucksack sitting on the high ridge beside her. She adjusted the tinted goggles covering her mismatched eyes and ran a hand through her red braids that danced in the autumn wind. The duo sat far up a cliff on a rock-strewn outcropping obscured by the needles of two gargantuan evergreens overlooking the wilderness below. The blue-white light of the too-bright sun shone in the sky above them and Dax pulled his brown, wide-brimmed hat farther down his dark-skinned face. The goggles covering his eyes had been cracked the previous day in a skirmish with the men they now tracked. Alastrina looked through the scope of the sniper rifle once more and her breath caught in her throat when she saw that the Wildermen had forced her teenaged charge in front of the door. A mud-coated hulk of man dressed in furs with blue tattoos on his face and arms drew a knife and cut the ropes binding the young man before motioning with a knife at the rusted steel door. The teenager rubbed his raw wrists and bent over the keypad with a scowl. The copper-haired woman turned to her partner and said, "They've got Zeke on the keypad, Dax." "Fuck, Trina. We've got to get down there. If something happens to the boy..." Dax trailed off. He rubbed a hand across the week-old salt and pepper stubble that covered his face and spat. Alastrina nodded. "I'll go first," she said as she stood up and stretched her poplin cloth covered legs, "cover me with the rifle." Dax grabbed her hand, "What about the Kindled they have?" he asked in a hoarse whisper, images of blue flames and cracked stone swam through his mind. Alastrina took his hand between her own gloved fingers, "Leave the Kindled to me. Just keep the Wildermen off me and if they make it inside, wait here. Shoot anyone that leaves the building behind me." She kissed his brow and disappeared into the shadow of the forest behind them, the scar of a snake bite beneath her left breast began to burn; she disturbed nothing beneath her booted feet and made not a sound as she walked unhindered through the overgrowth. The hair on Dax's neck and arms stood up as he watched her go. He had seen her move like this many times since the day they had met, but he would never get used to the unnatural way she seemed to disappear in the lonely places. He lifted the rifle in his muscular arms and gazed through the scope. He saw the door open and the Wildermen shuffle inside, the boy in front of them. Hurry Trina, he thought as he watched the ragtag miscreants disappear into the darkened doorway.

Being in a mixed-member family was always less-than-ideal. Children liked to see their parents united in everything. And when one stayed home while the other dragged the kids off to church, there was always a little'murmuring'. How I wish I could hear them complaining, hear them say anything again. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints - Mormons - had everything backwards. Everyone knew that Father, Son, and Holy Ghost were a single trinity. Mormons said they were separate. Everyone knew that God finished speaking with the end of the bible. Mormons had new scripture and prophets constantly. And everyone knew that children were born with original sin. Mormons treated all children as innocent until they were old enough to be accountable. I guess that's why it was a shock when the Mormons left, they took the children with them. We had three kids, two under eight. The oldest had been baptized, though, so I didn't get to hold onto her. I know that there are some of you here today who have lost some and kept others. I'm told you envy those who were like me, where they were all taken. Let me assure you, mine is a position not worthy of envy. And now there are no more children. And being here at the steps of the Salt Lake Temple only seems to amplify that thought. No more spirits left in the pre-earth life to come down and take the bodies we make for them. Whether we each live out the rest of our natural lives or it's all over in two years, I can say that it's been like a light has gone out. Not because the Mormons have left, but because the children did too. You know what the most ironic thing is? The Mormons didn't actually believe in the rapture! They though most of the religions got it wrong. Four horseman, seven years of tribulations, their sudden departure, they though it was allegorical. I guess God does have a sense of humor. Now, I'm not a non-member, but an ex-member. That's why I can bring you to the temple here today, I know what goes on. I know how, and I know why. But I want to be very clear on this one, important aspect: nothing we say or do here today will make any difference. When the Mormons left, they took their authority, their priesthood with them. I don't have it, no one does. We are no different than bags of sand as we go through here today. What we do here will not bring salvation, it will not bring your children back. All we can do is be like David, begging forgiveness and hoping for a small sliver of our own salvation. We may be damned, but let the work we do here today be sung in the highest degree of heaven with the rest of David's psalms.

Dieter rises from the bed, stumbling out of the sheets half-groggy from sleep over to the washstand in the corner. Pouring out a measure of water from the pitcher into the provided basin, he scrubs the dust from his eyes, scrubbing a washcloth behind his ears and neck. With a razor he grooms his closely cropped beard into order, careful not to slice his throat open with the deadly sharp blade. Finishing, he admires the keen look in the mirror, twisting and turning his head about to glance at his appearance. Storm gray eyes, a scar underneath the corner of the right from when a grenade exploded nearby. Another from a probing foe's stiletto. The scar tissue along his jaw well-healed. No wrinkles save those from scars or his career as a soldier. Dark brown hair just short of being shoulder length. Not a single gray hair anywhere on his head or in his beard. Ah. Dieter's heart sinks as the realization dawns on him. He lets go of the blade in his hands, letting the straight razor splash into porcelain basin, the lathered water spilling out over the rim and onto the stand. "Dieter? Is something wrong?" Comes the worried voice from the bed. He turns to her, a look of detachment in his storm gray eyes. Blank, as if he saw something a thousand yards away. "How long has it been?" He asks. Queen Malvina bolts upright from where she lays. "Oh gods." She throws the covers off of her, a silk nightgown garbing her as she rushes to his side just before he collapses in her arms, his eyes staring off at some non-existent horizon. "Dieter? Dieter, listen to me. Everything is alright." She turns her head to the closed door to their room. "Sera! Fetch the doctors." Nodding at the servants voice affirming her orders, she returns her attention to her love. "Shh, shh, it'll be alright. You're having a panic attack is all. Dieter? Dieter, look at me. Look, look..... look at me!" That finally reaches him, causing him to jerk his head up at her, his eyes damp and full of fear. "I can't die..." He says, the statement not of disbelief but rather of terrible certainty. "I won't age." Malvina holds tight to him, blinking away tears of her own. "It'll pass, you're just having an attack. I've had them too. Everything will be fine, Dieter. Do you understand?" She says, trying to believe her own words though it's plain enough to see that it isn't fine. "Malvina, how long has it been?" He asks, his voice practically begging for answer. "Please, tell me." She closes her eye in shame, unable to look at him as she speaks. "Eight years..." She murmurs, self-loathing filling her breast as she stills his shaking hands. "It's been eight years since I stole your mortality. I'm sorry Dieter, I'm so, so sorry." "I'm not aging," Dieter repeats, his mind leagues away. "I won't die. I can't die. I have to live with what I've done forever. I was supposed to die, I deserved to die." "Dieter..." Malvina says, her words at a loss. "I hate you! I love you! You've taken everything from me, and given me everything!" Malvina holds on to his attempted thrashing, pain and grief weakening him. Eventually he gives up, his head falling against her shoulder. "I'm sorry, Malvina. It's just, it's She shushes him with a finger against his lips. "It's alright, I understand. It's not easy. Trust me, I know. I spent a century alone, just myself immortal. It was painful. But it will get better." Dieter smiles at her comforting words, trying to trust them. "What day is it?" He asks. "The 21st day of the second month. Why?" A small smile crosses his lips. "I'll be 36 in two weeks." His smile widens. "And still the youngest person here." Both laugh softly at the joke, the door opening a few seconds later to reveal the form of her personal physician. "We'd best make it a good one then." Malvina promises, kissing her love on the brow to seal it.

Cold. So cold. At least the view was nice. We drifted on in silence, my wife and I. Call it a clerical error, call it sabotage. It didn't really matter. Ground control didn't see the asteroid belt and neither did we until we struck it. Our ship was torn apart within minutes and both of us had been sucked out. The cosmic dust was our only other companion. Immortality seemed like the worst choice to make. They first few moments were the worst. First my lungs exploded with the force of a thousand hammers, hitting just the right nails, and all I could do was watch the same happen to her just seconds later. I just kept staring at her. Her already pale skin wept as the bright reds of her wrinkled lips escaped their master. I remembered her walking out of the shower, just a towel wrapped around her. How she'd walk over to me, sleeping in and lean forward, brushing her speaking hair against my face as I smiled in my complacent sleep. The same hair that floated in every direction with us. I held her tighter and she held me the same. I kissed her icy forehead as I saw the tears escape our eyes, clump together and drift away as aimlessly as us. I tried to remember our time on earth. I remember her family on Christmas. Everyone one of them more dull than the next. I remember us running away close to midnight. Making our way to the park in the country side and lying down. Just looking in awe at the same stars that now mocked our immortality. Her smiling head against the night sky as she kissed me juxtaposed with my current view of her silently sobbing visage. I kept trying to remember more. I remember a fight. We fought about this. We fought about immortality. She never wanted to become immortal and go into space. In fact..... She didn't agree to it. I felt my mind betray me as her warmth faded away. I looked up at the galaxies swirling into the abyss. She left me. Cold. So cold. But at least the view was nice.

I wondered firstly, Is Whiskers some kind of..... advanced artificial robot? . I stared at the now tailless Sunny, lazily licking himself clean. She seemed..... organic enough to be a real cat. My temptation to'update' my cat became increasingly strong. Since I wasn't given any information about what updates were in version 256.3, I tried my best to find out more information, but it was futile. A little less than an hour passed by and I gave up. It wasn't like Sunny could possibly tell me anything about - "Sunny!" Sunny's head bobbed up in surprise after my silence. "Do you want me to update you?" Sunny probably thought that I was yelling at her somehow, so before she jumped off my table, she ran across my keyboard. The damage was already done. One of her feet and pressed the Enter button for me. Oh shit! My initial reaction was to rip Sunny's tail - I mean the USB out from my computer, but I stopped myself. As I watched the update bar slowly reach fifty percent, I thought, ..... Maybe I should leave it. There is probably no other way to find out what happens..... Once the updates were complete, I was instructed by the pop up to insert the tail back into the cat. ..... so now I have to get my cat AND plug the USB back into the cat? This was going to be annoying. After many failed attempts to hold a cat down to correctly plug the USB in, I decided that I would stay up and wait for the Sunny to fall asleep. Finally, when Sunny had eaten and groomed herself, I found the moment. I made sure the USB was going to the correct way before I carefully put the tail back into the cat. For a moment, nothing happened. I waited and waited. Nothing. I was even tempted to wake Sunny up to see if anything changed, but it was late. I was tired. I went to sleep. The next morning I woke up to thudding noises in the hallway. What is that noise? Did I just dream up everything about my cat? What else do I have to do today? First I needed to address the noise. Looking along the hallway and in the bathroom, there was nothing I could see that was making that loud noise. It sounded almost like..... heavy feet..... the kitchen?! I ran downstairs into the kitchen, and to my horror, the entire kitchen was destroyed. A huge mammoth feline was ravaging my refrigerator, the door was ripped off. In a small voice, I asked, "Is that..... you? Sunny?" The mammoth feline looked down at me from it's great height. She walked close to me and I could hear her breath from her nose. I was terrified, but I didn't run away because I was afraid of it chasing me. She paused at arm distance from me, staring at me, like she was expecting something from me. I took my last breath and I was about to close my eyes and face my - The mammoth cat fell onto it's side and rolled belly up, purring. The purr was so loud and rumbling. She meowed, like her voice dropped. I obliged a gave a scratch behind her ear.

" Coffee?! Are you serious? After such an idiotic excuse, " Harry nearly screamed at her. " I mean what the hell? Being abducted by aliens? Thats something you tell a five-year-old! Do you think I am retarded or what? " " N-no of course not! " Lucy knew he wouldn't believe her right away but she didn't thought his reaction would be as bad as this. " Then why the hell lie to me and then not even think about something believable? Is this some kind of joke? " " No I really mean it! " Lucy just couldn't lie not after all what happened on Kytrap not after all the friends she had lost there. " I was abducted two years ago by a intergalactic space lord and then taken to his home planet to become one of his thousand wives from all over the universe. " " Are you seri- " She put up a hand to interrupt him. " Please, let me finish, " she begged him. " Luckily the spaceship of my kidnapper was attacked by rebel forces and I could escape with them. " Harry looked like he still wanted to say something but he just kept staring at her silently. " They couldn't take me home right away since their ships lacked the right technology for distant space flight but they assured me they would do it as soon they would win the war. They wanted to hide me and to wait but after I saw how miserable their chances were I just had to help. " Harrys face had reversed to a neutral expression which Lucy took that as a good sign. " You know that I have a PhD in nuclear physics and although I had some moral conflicts with myself I build them nuclear reactors and bombs which combined with their alien technology were the perfect weapons. Still the war was not won quickly and both sides lost many, many people. " She choked up at the memory. Oh Blerugarahndorakta, why had you to die? " Finally the tyrant died in the final grand battle and the galaxy was freed from him. That was five months ago. I couldn't leave right away, you see. I had to help restore what was destroyed. But last week I could return and I had just to see you. " Lucy smiled and even though Harry hated himself for it it made his heart flutter. " All the nights I was scared and wanted just to cry and every time I lost someone precious to me, it was you who kept me going. Just thinking of you and that one magical night two years ago helped me suffer through all of this so that one day I might see you again. Do you understand now how much you mean to me? " He was silent for a moment and she was already getting nervous. " Yes, yes I understand, " Harry said finally. " I understand that after all the years nothing changed. I thought I might have stopped being the loser I was in High School and I would be never be bullied again. I was so happy after you said yes back then. " Now he smiled. " The one and only prom queen, the most beautiful girl in the school and my crush would go on a date with me. I was so nervous that night but after it was over I knew we had something that could last our entire life. But you never answered my calls and I knew it was the last grand prank that was played on me. " Harry began clapping. " Bravo, just magnificent how you are able to break my heart again and again. But I assure you that was the last time. I have to go now to keep the little bit of pride I have left. He turned and began walking away and Lucy just didn't knew what to say anymore. She lifted her wrist to her mouth and then disappeared in a beam of light. Later that evening back in his apartment lay on his bed and was try to not think about Lucy. Of course unsuccessfully. After a while doozed away and started to have the strangest dream. His room filled with light and suddenly there were grey little people standing before his bed lifting him up. The light was getting brighter and then it was dark again and he fell to the ground. Dazed he knew he must have fallen out of the bed. But strangely he felt as if he was laying on glass. He opened his eyes and saw the earth.He screamed and jumped to his legs nearly hurting his ankles. " Its okay Harry you are safe, " a voice sounded behind him. He turned around and saw Lucy standing there in a strange but still somehow sexy looking spacesuit surrounded by the grey people from Harry's dream. He looked around and realized that they had to be in a spaceship and that the floor was made out of glass or something. And that they were of course flying in space far above the earth. " Everything okay, Harry? " she asked. He stared at her his mouth agape and she already knew that it had been a bad idea to take him here. " Sooo, coffee? " he asked.

My power? It's ridiculously simple. I can amplify electrical energy. Something as simple as a AA battery could power a megawatt laser for a second or two with enough amplification. I'm still limited to the energy stored within the power source, be it a battery, a capacitor, or a simple generator. Fortunately, I continued on to college instead of trying to make a name for myself as a hero. Got a degree in computer engineering. Seems pointless, but its become very beneficial. You see, I can act like a powerful transistor as a bypart of the electrical amplification - something as simple as a small pulse from my power could create a massive electrical bolt between my palms. It hurts like hell to do - I didn't get rapid regeneration or electrically insensitive as powers or side effects - but it makes supplying massive amounts of power to one place a pinch. Weirdly, it also turns out that, by using my amplification on an extremely small scale, I can compute things as well. With enough transistor action going on, I can compute numerous things at once. It's become useful for field computing, where all we have as a power source is a battery and maybe some solar panels. And fortunately, there's been a few cases where I'm needed for field computing in remote areas. The last time I went into the field was in a case involving the equally unknown "Bendy McBendface" - he was once a famous gymnast and performer as he's incredibly flexible and can bend parts of his body in ways that it was not structured for - and once I recognized who we were dealing with I started computing. He's flexible, beyond human standards. Is he rubber-like? That makes any electrical attacks useless, yet if he was rubber-like he could compress easily as well and act like a spring. He doesn't spring around, nor does he compress. Must not be rubber then. What about silicone? No, too flexible. Silicone would bend out of shape at his weight. Hmm..... if he can bend so well, perhaps his bones are slightly more flexible than normal, designed like a living hinge. And when it comes to his joints, perhaps he's double or triple jointed, resulting in extreme flexibility. All of that computed in a couple of seconds, I set about setting up a passive computing system that would calculate his possible movements and how he moves. If my bone and joint theory is correct, he should be subdued quickly. I pull out my favorite weapon - a AAA battery electric pistol. Fires small bolts of electricity that are amped up to thousands of volts and normally around 32 amps per short. Holds six AAA batteries before I got ta reload too. I dash closer to Bendy McBendface. I need to keep my distance, if my theory is incorrect and he's more like silicone or rubber, it means he can stretch out and grip onto me. I prep my pistol. Batteries: loaded. Amplification system: ready. Target: within range. I pull the trigger and engage the entire amplification system to drain the AAA battery in a fraction of a second. A loud pop is heard, with an incredibly bright bolt of electricity as it grounds to Bendy's body. I run some final computations to analyze Bendy as his body responds to the electric shock. He certainly isn't rubber-like or silicone-like. Definitely mostly water, like a normal human. I see his bones shine dimly through his skin. The theory was correct. His bones are indeed living hinges. And if my brief foray into materials science is correct, his bones should shatter into individual pieces, leaving his bending ability useless. With Bendy McBendface subdued, I call the police to take him to jail. "You're going to want to wear some rubber gloves. He's still pretty electrified. Yeah, I can see the lighting bolts spread over his skin as it tries to ground. Better get here soon, if he grounds I can't guarantee what will happen." I walk away from the slowly convulsing body of Bendy McBendface. None of the other heroes were successful with him. Iron Man had tried, but Bendy would always flex away and avoid attacks, and any computations were simply too slow to provide good information. Captain America failed worse, with Bendy simply absorbing and deflecting most of the shield throws. Yet somehow, the guy with a simple power and a degree relating to the power managed to take down someone who escaped everyone else. I have a simple name. Quanta.
