I stand at the door, hollering to get my alien's attention. I Just woke up from my first afternoon nap, grabbed a nice snack from the kitchen, and would now like to stretch my legs. However, I do not like the level of urgency in which my alien is making their way to the door, so I scream louder until they hurry. Once the door is opened I look outside, but it is a little too sunny and warm for my liking, so I linger in the doorway and try to decide if I want to go outside, or inside....or outside.....or inside.

When I enlisted, I was fully prepared to fight Vega's Centauri's heptapods, because I knew I would have a fully equipped Thor VI suit, with my energy rifle and my second blaster, just in case I would lose my rifle. I was really proud of being one the commanders of the Solar Space Commandos, and the soldiers under my commanding were really good human beings. After weeks of fights, we conquered the planet; we even had some heptapods to interrogate when the ground began to shake. Dr Liz came to see me with a terrified look in her eyes and said " The heptapods managed to make the core of the planet unstable. The planet is doomed and so are we ." I don't recall exactly what happened afterwards, but geyser of lava were coming out of the ground, flooding everything and I'm sure I died. But here I was, back to the livings, at least I thought, on another planet, which seemed like the Earth. A giant man walked toward me with obviously a purpose, he had an eye patch, a Viking helmet, an impressive beard and a spear in his hands. " Hello Hero! I'm Odin the King of the Gods, and I gathered you on this day to the greatest battle of all time, here we are for the Ragnarok! On your previous life, you fought well on the battleground, and you protected the human population, thus, you deserve the honor to fight with us on this battlefield. -Wow thank you, great Odin, but what are we supposed to fight? -See by yourself " I looked the battlefield and what I saw impressed me. On our side were a lot of soldiers, of all times and all sides, I recognized King Leonidas of Sparta, Vercingetorix of Gaul, King Arthur, Knight Bayard, Cortez the conquistador and many others from more recent times. The integrated computer of my suit estimated we were about half a million warriors which was a good point because defeating half a million heroes wouldn't be a piece of cake. Facing us was an army of monsters, giant wolves, ice giants, ugly elves, they were a lot too and this was going to be a great battle. Odin and Thor gathered us to make the battle plan: the least armored with distance weapons would be at the back of the army to shoot without being in danger. In the middle of the army would come the more armored guys and at the front would come the best prepared with the best weapons, led by the gods. I was assigned a squad of futuristic soldiers, some more advanced than me and some less, but all were great soldiers. We compared our experienced, grade and time of leading a squad to see which one of us would be the commander. I was declared commander by the majority of the squad and we started discussing about our strategy, when Odin shouted to prepare us for the upcoming battle. Battle horns sounded through the field when the monsters began to runs in front of us. Archers began to shoot arrows, snipers were shooting bullets and lasers and heavy soldiers were launching rockets. Some monsters collapsed and died but the rest was still running, the clash would be ferocious. My team and I were on the first row, since we had the best combat armor; ready to kill everything that would threatens our lives. The wolves were the first to come to us, being the fastest, but were easily killed by our weapons, except one who dodged everything. But one soldier of the far future jumped on his back, unsheathed his light sword and stuck in the monster's head. We were impressed but the giants were following the wolves and then the battle became more confused. It was the first time I witnessed magic and even if we had technology with us, the battle wasn't easy. When one of my soldiers died pierced by the spear of an ice giant, as if his armor wasn't really there I realized we underestimated enemy's weapons. Odin and Thor were fighting alongside with us, which was a great thing, but I noticed we were losing so many heroes, so fast, when something caught my leg. I looked down and saw a snake starting to roll up around me, I raised my rifle to shoot the snake in the head, when a giant dug his sword into my chest. The frost of the weapon was a good thing to counter the burning sensation of the wound...

"Why can't they just fucking share some?" "Dude, I don't know - they have always been douche-bags. How long have you known about them now?" "Just a couple days now. I just thought that the first intelligent race we interact with would at least give us some pointers or advice on the universe. I mean, we did send them 500 trillion tons of coffee beans last week like they asked, right?." "What do you think they did with those coffee beans? They got high and laughed at us. That's what they did." "Ugh - you would think that they would care just a little bit. I mean, we do share the same solar system and our planet is millions of times as populated as theirs. It's only a matter of time before...." "Enough of that talk! We are a civil people and even though they are fucking assholes we have to maintain the status quo. Remember that they can destroy us in an instant if they wanted to....you were briefed on this." "Ugh, I know. But it's just so much bullshit man. There's only 3 of them hogging all those coffee beans - and I bet they don't even share with their underlings who literally just comb the Mars desert all day looking for stray beans. I like coffee too - and since they are so addicted we've had to trick the human race into thinking they are drinking coffee, when in fact, they are drinking something totally different." "Heh, it's kinda funny when you think about it. If they really knew what they were drinking...." "Hahaha, I know right? Anyway, what's the plan here - do we just give in to their demands?" "That's the plan. I know you are new at this so just try not too look too frazzled. They may make fun of you. Have you ever seen one of them?" "No, but Debbie told me they just looked like purple Jabba the Huts with funky hats on..." "Yeah, kinda - but did she tell you how big they were?" "No - but how big could they be?" "They didn't evolve on the planet, Mr. Obama - they fucking took it. Those losers come from a planet 100x the size of Jupiter and with 150x the gravity of earth. They are fucking huge - and strong....really really strong." "Bullshit." "Dude, you have no idea. They are nearly 4 kilometers in diameter - each." "No way." "Yep - and they have really big guns, man." "Why do we even call them a "colony" anyway?" "Well, they technically "colonized" the planet centuries ago - but that was just because they were planning on the coffee bean thing once the human race started cultivating them. They are too big to do it themselves. You were briefed on this." "So....they came all the way here, and live in giant holes on Mars just to get high all the time off our coffee beans? And demand we give them over, or else?" "Yep - that's pretty much it. It's why we have SpaceX. It would be nice if we were going to explore and colonize Mars - but in reality we just need a more efficient way of getting those douches more coffee beans." "Those motherfuckers. Harry, dial them up. I'm ready." Dude, I think you need to chill out before you go on another one of your fits. Remember what happened when you tried to do the whole healthcare thing a couple weeks ago?" "Shut the hell up, man. That shit worked." "Dude, it was a complete disaster. I know you have only recently been brought up to speed here, but this is a delicate matter." "Just spin up the fucking line, Harry."

I walked through the streets of my great city toward the Senate. Caesar wasn't one who was kind to people who were late to meetings. Lately, I'd been wearing his patience thin with the questions during the night. Other senators were meeting for some reason, but I had always had work to do, the city needed attention, and I had a way to give them hope. I arrived in the Senate just as Caesar was. I didn't have a lot of time to get to my position, and I couldn't allow the man to see me. I motioned to Tullius to distract the man for me. He and I had been good friends for our time in the Senate; I figured he would cover. The men of the Senate rose as Tullius asked Ceasar to approach Climber. The two of them were moving for a greeting; there was somewhat of a power play going on right at that moment. Climber was reaching to get a better hold on Ceasar than he had on him. Ceasar wasn't the kind to stand for that; he would punish Climber. I slipped between the rows and glanced down at the waist of the man beside me. He was Cassius, a man who had long wanted Ceasar's position and rank. He had removed a dagger from his Toga. I nudged him, "You aren't supposed to bring those into the Down the stairs, Servilius pulled out a dagger of his own and stuck the leader of the Senate in the shoulder. He cried out in pain as other men moved to rush him. I stood still, awestruck at the rebellion that I was watching. The men were brutally killing him. I didn't move to stop them, they had their reasons for wanting him dead, I had mine. Ceasar drew his last breath a dozen minutes later, bleeding across the Senate. Minutes later everyone reconvened to discuss the matters of the day. Cassius, who had retaken his place beside me, approached me at the end of the day. "Sorry for the shock," he began, "we wanted to invite you to the meetings, but you were always busy." "It's all right," I replied, "just know that if anyone asks I am telling them that I put a dagger right in his neck." "His neck?" "I want to seem important to history you know."

The Great King slumped on his throne, defeated. He had battled long and hard, but he knew it was for naught, as he trembled and shook upon the throne that had now become his last bastion of hope, he KNEW..... he had lost the day. A tremendous bellow gurgled and shreaked close to the throne room door. The king could hear his enemy as it drew ever closer to where he was cowering. Tears cascaded down from the poor kings eyes as he recounted the time he was sure his fate was sealed, a day he was sure to be his happiest, such folly. If only he had listened to the wise words of his father, maybe he could have avoided such an end. Scratching at the door now! The frightened king holds his breath, frozen in terror. He has been found, his time has come. The creature draws breath and presses its slobbering mouth to the bathroom door and screams, "DADDY!! Are you in there?!"

Fortuna took up a third of the sky. It was terrifying, of course. The scale of it. The implication. The inevitability of gravity. But there was also beauty in the swirling red-orange dance of hydrogen, helium, and methane. When astronomers discovered the rogue planet drifting through the solar system, it was already inside the orbit of Mars. That was seven weeks ago. No more clinging to drunk hope or questioning whether calculations might have been wrong. The small red dot in the sky had become a great sobering wheel, crushing and tremendous, bowing all before it. Amelia poured some water from a plastic jug into a metal pot and set it on some sticks above a small fire. Fortuna was an impressive at night even in the crowded sky of the city. But in the middle of the Adirondack Mountains, the sight was incredible. The colors were so vivid, it was like the planet itself was straining to be a sun. She had left the city three days ago. The riots were so ugly. There was no need anymore for policies or governments, power or control. Who could enforce a rule? All the armies had disbanded. Everyone knew what this was. The whole world was on the top floor of a building, watching it burn to the ground. Eliot stayed behind. He wanted to be with his family. She couldn't argue. They had spent two years together, but it always felt like a prologue to a story they had yet to write. He was a kind man and she wouldn't begrudge him his choice of where to die. It was the only choice anyone had. The dam at the foot of Mt. Marcy was more crowded than Amelia remembered it being in her youth. Her father used to take her up the mountains when she was a child. He brought her up Algonquin on his shoulders. They explored the wreckage of an old plane crash on Wright. Amelia remembered picking through the fifty-year-old debris, filled with sadness and curiosity. Her father was in Colorado now, too far to travel, and all the phones were dead. It was fine. He was with her stepmother. Amelia opened a packet of chili-flavored ramen noodles and emptied the contents into the boiling water. A flashlight cut through the forest and a young woman hiked down the trail. She was carrying a small backpack and was followed by a chocolate lab. She was looking for something, apparently frustrated by not finding it. " Hey, I'm sorry, do you mind if I set this down here? I don't - I don't want anything, I've just been walking a lot today and I was not expecting this many people. " " Sure, " Amelia offered. " Do what you need. " " Oh man, thank you. " The hiker set down her pack with a relieved grunt. " My car ran out gas back in Keene. I walked the rest of the way here. Guess we're staying on the mountain. Me and Frodo, I mean. Frodo's my dog. Oh, my feet my feet my feet. " She looked up at the planet, opened her mouth as if to speak, then closed it. " What's your name? " Amelia stirred the pot. " I'm Sam. Sam and Frodo. " Sam let out a practiced chuckle. " I'm Amelia. " Sam smiled. " Nice to meet you, Amelia. I wish it was under... better... " " I know, me too. You by yourself? " " I mean I've got this pupper. I drove up from Albany today. It was too much. Scary. I mean this is scary, " Sam gestured up, " but people can be awful. And now, there's no... there's no filter. So, you know, I had to go. " As Sam spoke, she began holding back tears. " I'm glad I'm here though. I am. It's so beautiful, I had to see it here. I wanted to really see it. " Her emotion was obvious now. " I'm sorry, " She wiped her face. " I'm sorry, you don't want - I'm just... " " No, " said Amelia, " really. It's fine. You're fine. " They sat for a time under Fortuna's carnelian glow. Sam Spoke. " I wasn't coming here. I was going to see my parents. They live about a hundred miles north of here. I thought I'd be able to make it, but... all the gas is gone. And with the time we have left, a hundred miles could just as soon be a million. So I'm here. It's the end of everything and I'm here. " " And you have Frodo. " Sam smiled. " I do. Yeah. " " If you need some space, it's crowded by the dam but you're welcome here. I've got some extra room. I'm by myself too. I didn't want to be, but here I am. So, if you need something, if you need someone to share this with... I'm trying to say I like your dog. " Sam laughed. " He's my special gentleman. " Amelia took the pot off the fire. " You want some ramen? It's chili which is my least favorite, but it's food. " " I don't have a bowl. " " Share mine. "

There was a knock on the door. I wasn't sure what I was expecting, but it definitely wasn't this. Acid- My nemesis. He used his trademark hydrofluoric acid guns to break into bank vault, break people out of prison and blind anyone who got in his way. I leapt back, and took a defensive stance. "Get back! Get away! Help some-one cal He strode into the room, slammed the door shut and pressed his hand over my mouth. "Drop it, Starman. I know it's you. No need to involve bystanders, is there." He met my eyes, and let go. "I have no idea what you're "Save it. I've known your alter ego for two years now. Never saw the point in busting you for it." I keep me eye on his, warily. "What do you want?" He stepped back, and took a deep breath. He pulled off his mask. "I need your help." This was the first time I'd seen his face- he was a master of escaping. His skin was sallow, and his hair was falling out. He looked like death. "What happened to you?" "Lung cancer. Turns out acid ain't great for your lungs. Doc says I have two months, tops." "Well.... there's nothing I can do.... you must know that." I was confused as all hell. I didn't want to help him- he was a murderer, a thief..... dangerous. But even if I did want to, what could I do for that? He reached into his pocket, I flinched reflectively. He pulled out his wallet, and offered it to me. I took it, hesitantly. Inside..... were dozens of pictures of a little girl, maybe five years old. "My daughter..... Anna. She doesn't know about this. About any of it. Her mama..... she's gone too. She's all alone in this world when I'm gone, and I sure as fuck don't want her anywhere near the foster system. I've been there..... I know what it can do to people. I mean, look at me?" "Acid..... a "My names Kyle. Kyle Davidson" "Kyle..... why me? Surely you must-?" "I spray acid in people's faces for a living. I have money, enought o give her the life she deserves. All yours, if you'll take her." "The money you stole." I said, bluntly. "Some of it." "I can't take it, What you did was wrong..... I can't be a part of that." "Please. I'll do anything. I just need to know she's with someone I can trust to do right by her, look after her. Name your price. Anything." I looked back to the pictures..... I had him on a platter. I could get him to confess to his crimes, serve as much of his time as he had left. Her smiling face held me. She only had two more months with her dad. I handed him back the wallet. "I don't want your money. Give it back, or give it to a good cause. My price is this- no more trouble from you until..... Spend time with your little girl, give her something to remember you by. When the time comes..... she'll be safe with me. I promise." He looked..... relieved. Like he hadn't expected this to work. "Thank you. You have my word...... I was afraid you'd send me to prison. I would have, you know. For Anna." "Go on. Go find her, and show her how much you care. I'll be there when you need me, Kyle."

It was cold and dark in the bedroom when the alarm clock went off. As I blearily swiped away the annoying alarm on my watch I noticed I appeared to be naked. As I don't normally sleep in the nude this was a strange feeling. I heard a noise from the kitchen. I quickly grab some pajamas from the dresser and head that way. Thinking it was someone I thought too drunk to probably leave the previous evening I walk in the kitchen to find a gorgeous blonde woman sitting at the kitchen table eating cereal in my robe. She sees me enter and winks at me as she continues to eat her cereal and points at a note on the bar. Trying to remember the night before I walk to the note and begin to read it. It's in my handwriting and plainly states the following. "Don't question the lost memories, enjoy your day, the rest of your life is ahead of you, you won't miss them anyways." Them? The memories? Why did I have to be such a shitty writer at a time like this? Couldn't I have written something more clear and concise? As the blonde finishes her cereal she rinses the bowl and places it in the dishwasher and says "The maid will be by later today, don't forget we have an appointment with the lawyers in an hour, you might want to freshen up with me. I've already packed our bags." Bags? Where we going somehwere. Something else to ask about later I guess. After a lovely shower and getting dressed by my companion who's name turned out to be Janetta she moved us along to a limosine downstairs where we waited in silence in traffic. Janetta could tell I was curious and seemed to be waiting on me to start the questions. I stared out the window and began the twenty questions game. "How much memory did I have erased?" to which she answered "A year, 11 months and 15 days to be exact." I looked at her curiously. "Do you know why I did it?" she looked directly at my eyes and responded with a look of pain in her eyes "Yes, and you directed me not to tell you, and to remind you about the note you wrote yourself, God I don't know why you wrote yourself a note if you won't even listen to yourself." Two questions will have to be enough I guess. She silently lets a tear fall and grasps my hand. I can't get over this feeling like I love this woman. I don't believe in love at first sight. But is this truly first sight? We pull up to a legal office. I ignore the name across the front of the building, it's obvious they make enough money already. Let's just hope I'm not being sued. After several thousand signatures on some very confusing documents that I'm not wholely allowed to read by Janetta I'm informed that 2 billion dollars after taxes and legal fees have been wired into my bank account as agreed. My lawyers congratulate me on this result and usher me out the door so they can get back to counting their portion I assume. Janetta next instructs the driver to carry us down to a sea-side cottage about an hour away where we will be spending the next month. It's a strange affair to be so intensely rich and not know why. I can remember my life up to a year ago. I was single, doing ok on a manager's salary at a local tech firm. I wonder if the place got bought up and this was my payment. I was there from early on but that's still a lot of money. I didn't think the whole place would be worth that much. Maybe Johnson finally cracked that marketing code and one of our game apps hit it big. That had to be it. After we got to the cottage I decide to look up the tech firm online. I had to know what happened. Just as the computer boots up and I login I'm greeted by another note from myself. "Don't dig too deeply, you erased it for a reason, just let it go." I pause at this. If I knew I was a stubborn fool then why did I erase it anyways? Janetta came over and collected me from the computer sensing my confused state and took me outside with two plates covered with sandwiches and chips. We sat and ate in silence for a little while. After she finished her chips she had a look on her face that showed she was deep in thought. Then she seemed to make a decision to herself and nodded as though it was done. She looked deep into my eyes at this point and began "Are you going to keep digging until you find out what you erased anyways?." I chewed on the last bite of my sandwich considering the question. Not knowing the answer until the words fell out of my mouth I gave her the most honest words I could coalesce. "I don't know, I feel like I want to know what it was, but I'm afraid to find out." A tear rolls down her face and she wipes it away and says "You've put yourself in this state knowing damn well you would dig up the truth anyways, it's the way you've been as long as anyone has ever known you, your mom even told me so. So let's cut thru the pretend private eye game and save us all the time and hassle." I felt like the whole world stood still for a moment. What in the hell could have happened? She seemed to collect herself and started up again after she figured out how to phrase it. "Let's start with your questions. I'll be honest about anything you ask but you have to understand I had no choice in any of this matter nor do I take any responsibility for the current state of that thing you call a skull." I take a moment and consider my first question. "Why did I do it?" She rolls her eyes. "Because you love me, you made a huge mistake and when everything was over and done with you just wanted to forget it ever happened, I agreed but told you that you would never let yourself have a memory gap that big and not dig into it, you said so be it and did it anyways." She seemed to pause then. As though waiting on the next question. I almost couldn't hold her gaze. Her beautiful face that I'd seen smile at breakfast and in tears far too often already today. I chose my second question in what I hoped was a safer direction. "Where did the money come from?" She paused as though that was not the question she expected. Maybe this wasn't the safer direction. "The money is from the sale of your company, that tech firm you joined two years ago finally made it big. After all the bigwigs ended up in jail you ended up in a pile of cash. You took one hundreth for yourself and divided the rest among the other managers and dev teams. You thought that was fair and decided on early retirement." Well that's a nice little package deal I guess. All those 80 hour weeks paid off. Big wigs in jail though. That's a mystery. "Why did the bosses go to jail?" She hesitated before taking my hand across the table. "I think this is the part you really wanted to forget. Are you sure you want me to answer this?" I nodded silently. For fear that I couldn't speak the words. She sat back releasing my hand although I left it within her reach having enjoyed the touch of her fingers on my own. "After the company went big the investors and board got together for one hell of a party, they invited everyone from the company over to that big hotel downtown. Everyone brought their wives along and it was crazy how much drinking was going on. After our wedding six months ago I haven't really been much of a drinker and so I had a few glasses of wine and retired early to a hotel room we reserved in advance. You were apparently very drunk and kissed me good night but decided to party a bit more before calling it a night. At one point everyone noticed the executives had disappeared to another room but noone really wanted to find out why. You were the curious cat that night and walked in on some sort of crazy orgy and were distraught because one of the escorts resembled me a great deal. You went back to the bar where you began drinking in earnest and were quite upset but wouldn't talk to anyone except the bartender to order more drinks. After you passed out at a table you woke up to the sight of cops walking the big-wigs out the door in hand-cuffs. You were questioned and told the police investigators everything you remembered. After it was over we found out that two escorts had died from drug overdoses and when all the executives failed drug tests they were all brought up on murder charges. The amount of evidence piled against all of them lead to guilty charges on every one of them. Apparently the legal contracts for your company had a clause about misconduct and they were all fired before the sale of the company was completed. When the dust settled you were the highest man on the totem pole. But you were distraught over the escort that resembled me and we almost got a divorce over it. After it was all said and done you felt so guilty for having mentally accused me of doing something like that, and then you couldn't get that poor girl's face out of your memory. She was one of the two that died. You seemed to take her death personally and we both went to counceling for a while. After you couldn't seem to let it go you decided to get your mind erased. The technology is pretty new still but they guaranteed they could reliably erase the last year. That would mean our entire relationship would have to start over but I love you and was willing to do that if it would help you move on."

Clunk When Sabir opened his eyes, there was only blackness. Deep, impenetrable blackness, as cloying as a heavy blanket pressed over his face. For a moment, he felt unable to breath, as if he had somehow awoken to find himself hundreds of feet below the ocean's surface. Then, with an incandescent brilliance, the fluorescent lights over his bed flickered to life and brought him fully into the world of the waking. Good morning, Sabir. You are certainly up early today. Will you be initiating an extra sleep cycle, or shall I prepare you a meal? "Mornin' Computer. Nah, that's fine, go ahead and make breakfast." Sabir rolled onto his side, eyes still blurry from sleep. His little cabin was a brilliant white, from his sheets to the walls to the floor. It would have been dazzling, if it were not for the layers and layers of fading posters, pictures, and other curio that coated the wall behind his bed like wallpaper. It was the only place on the entire ship that he had been authorized to make his own, and he had filled it with every scrap of his life that he could possibly make fit. It wasn't as if there was someone else on board who could enforce the rule, but Sabir had always followed protocol to the letter. It was his adherence to the rules that had first made Sabir stand out as a candidate for his current mission. He wasn't sure what it was that the cargo ship was carrying, but whatever it was they were taking no chances with it's disposal. He had strict instructions not to tamper with, interact with, or even LOOK at the thick steel boxes kept in the deep cryostasis compartments at the back of the ship's hold. He was to simply fly into the black hole's gravity well, jettison the entire rear of the ship, and make his way home again. It was a simple task that would allow him to live a life of luxury for the rest of his days, which was all the more impressive considering that it accounted for the medical immortality that had also been part of the deal. It was unusual, but Sabir was used to taking unusual orders from the higher ups. The hard part of the task came from one of the other conditions he had been made to agree to: He was absolutely, under no circumstances, allowed to activate the onboard FTL drive until his cargo had been delivered. What was more, he was only permitted to go into cryosleep for one week at a time, making his journey almost unbearably tedious. As Sabir rolled out of bed, panels on one of the walls began to recede, revealing a mirror, sink, and compact shower. At the top right of the mirror, a glowing blue display read: "5:45 am, August 19, 8299. It has been 789,000 days since the last workplace accident." He shook his head at the time, wondering why he was so wide awake. With a start, he remembered the noise that had roused him, cursing his sleep-addled brain for not remembering sooner. "Computer! Run a full diagnostic on all ship systems. I think I heard something strange, possibly from the engines." Yes, Sabir. Diagnostic underway. Sabir dressed quickly, wanting to patrol the the ship's habitable zones manually. It wasn't that he didn't trust the ship's computer - it practically ran the ship all by itself - but even a small anomaly like the noise could be fatal this far from home. Just as he was pulling on his shirt, he heard it again - this time much closer. Clunk. "Computer! Did you get a read on that?" Confirmed. Noise originated from quadrant V, right above the mess hall. Sending scout drones to investigate Clunk With a curse, Sabir stood, staring at his doorway. The noise had originated just outside. Black tendrils, like corporeal shadows, slid through the gaps around the door. Sabir stared, rooted to the spot, as they poured into his tiny room until it seemed as if it would burst. Then, all at once, they stopped. For a moment, it seemed as if the mass was staring at him, and then it suddenly contracted. Tendrils twisted around tendrils, tightening, shifting in color, until a woman stood in front of him. She was completely nude, with long red hair and pale skin that was nearly as white as the walls of his room. After a moment of realization, Sabir recognized her as belonging in one of his posters, the one beside his head. She was an exact copy, human in every way except for her eyes, which shone coal-black. " Greetings, Sabir. " The woman spoke, her voice echoing in Sabir's head in a way that made his blood feel like ice. We have been watching you for quite some time. If you don't mind, we have a few requests we would like to ask of you. As Sabir watched, the counter on his mirror started to decrease rapidly. "6:04 am, August 19, 8299. Gage sat up suddenly. Scary movies, haunted houses, frightening novels, - he found enticing. He chose them. Forcing himself to be afraid, to face his fears, was something he enjoyed. Nightmares were a different thing completely. With a nightmare, he had no choice. He found the lack of control, as a horror unfolded within the synapses of his mind, left him feeling weak and powerless. He pursued fear because he wanted to have power over it. He did not want it to have power over him. In his nightmares, his choices gone, it did. "Stop being a baby!" He said to himself. It wasn't that this nightmare had been particularly scary. In the dream, there was only a brown a paper bag siting alone in he middle of the floor. His dream self, had reached into the bag only to have his hand grabbed by another. A hand that was green and lizard like - almost alien in structure and form. It was stupid really. He laughed at himself, as he sat in his bed, his white t-shirt sticky and see through with sweat. Still laughing, he got up to pee. Opening the bedroom door he moved towards the hall - what he saw on the hall floor made his stop. "Eeeeeeeeh." He screamed, as he sucked in air, almost squealing. He was surprised that such a feminine sound came from his mouth. He stared at the brown paper bag, partly crumpled with the top folded slightly. It was the size of a grocery bag, but had no label. It looked eerily like the bag from his dream. He continued to stare at the bag. "You're being a baby." He said to himself. "Just open the bag." He didn't move. "Come on man. This ain't a dream. You are in control....and you got ta pee. Now just look in the bag." He still didn't move. "Okay it is time to man up. Now come on. You'd make fun of somebody acting like this. It's just a bag." He looked inside his doorway and found a metal hanger on the floor. Grabbing it tightly he turned back toward the bag. Bending over just a bit, he poked the bag with the metal hanger. And then...... ....... Nothing happened. He started laughing to himself and poked the bag again. Still nothing. He put the hanger down. Gage bent further over and grasped the bag. He carefully unfolded and pulled it open as it's brown fibers made a crunching sound. He spread the mouth of the bag wide. Inside he found the source of his fear, two dusty wingtip shoes, courtesy of his messy roommate. He laughed harder, bent over in the hall, looking at the shoes. In one motion, a strong green hand grasped his ankle as another covered his mouth and pulled him backwards, still hunched over, and launched him into his room. He never had time to scream. He was never in control.

I sat in the center of the classroom on my first day of Junior year in high school. The first bell hadn't rung yet, and my friends were gathered round, joking and laughing, swapping stories of their summer vacations. I smiled along with them, but was silent. There was a new kid named Jon; he had moved into town over the summer, and we were rapidly working to bring him into the fold and make him feel at home. A particularly raucous bout of laughter went up from the group. I threw back my head, mouth open in a silent laugh. "Hey," said Jon, turning to me, "I still don't know your name yet. You've been quiet this entire time." "That's Resonance," replied Vince in my stead, "He's sort of the silent type. A true man of few words." "Why's that?" asked Jon. The rest of the group fell silent, awaiting my answer. I spoke up for the first time that day, as loudly and clearly as I could. "Do you really want to know?" Jon visibly shuddered, and the rest of the classroom drew back. "My voice strikes fear into the hearts of men," I explained. After a brief pause, everyone, save Jon, broke out laughing. Jon looked at me, then Vince, then back at me, and asked, "What the Hell was that?" "You heard Resonance speak," began Vince, "but what you didn't hear was more important. His voice carries an second frequency, just flirting with the boundaries of human hearing. It lies on the edge of your range of detection, that you can barely hear and feel, but aren't consciously aware of. Most people suffer some sort of malaise from being exposed to it, though just how much and the variety of it can vary from person to person. Also, he can tone it down or amp it up to a certain degree. It is impossible for him to truly eliminate it, so I speak for him a lot." I let out a low, murmuring laugh, and Jon recoiled. That seemed like it might have taken things to far, so I tapped Vince on the arm and made a couple of quick hand gestures in his direction. "Res says he's sorry, and hopes that you won't hold it against him," said Vince, interpreting my sign language. The two of us had been friends for a long time, and had taken up the language so that he could better act as my second voice. "It's okay," said Jon, "that's actually a really cool power. You just caught me off guard, is all." "Keep telling yourself that," I said, causing Jon to cringe yet again. "Don't worry, it's a natural response to his voice. You're not a coward or anything, you just need to get used to him," reassured Vince. At about that time, our teacher walked in, so we had to settle down. The bell rang, and the year began. Homeroom and first period passed quickly. Second period was English. The teacher, knowing my special ability, called upon me to read an excerpt from our first reading for the year: Macbeth. I read the entire "Is this a dagger I see before me?" soliloquy in the most menacing tone I could muster, and the class was clearly shaken, even the teacher. Clearly he had underestimated my power, because he thanked me, then jokingly asked that I not say anything again. Eventually, lunch rolled around. Vince and a couple of other friends had talked me into an excellent beginning of the year prank. We sat in the center of the cafeteria, and waited until the building was packed wall to wall. Fortune smiled upon us; we were in the middle of an autumn rainstorm, and everyone had taken shelter indoors. I gave the two of them a brief signal, and they covered their ears. I began to laugh, starting from a soft chuckle, and slowly raising in volume to a mad cackle. By the time my evil laughter had reached it's apex, the entire room had fallen into silence. That was all we had planned to do, but I saw an opportunity for some improvisation, and leaped onto the table. "Students of Clearlake High," I boomed, "I am Resonance, hear me speak! You shall come to know me by my voice! You shall learn to fear my words! Tremble before me!" I punctuated my impromptu speech with another round of insane, maniacal, evil laughter. Everyone was clearly intimidated, except for one girl, sitting alone in a corner despite the crowd. She just kept on eating, seemingly oblivious to me. "Thank you, that is all," I concluded as I stepped down from the table to chants of "All Hail Dark Lord Resonance" from my loyal companions. Numerous fist bumps and high fives were exchanged between us. What a way to start the year. As we left the cafeteria, I felt someone tug at the back of my jacket. I turned to see the girl from before, who had been completely unfazed by my speech. "What business do you have with me?" I asked her. She cocked her head to one side, and raised her hands, quickly and adeptly making the motions of sign language. It was at that point that I realized she was deaf. "I'm sorry, I saw you were making a speech, and it seemed terribly important, but I couldn't hear you because I am deaf and I wanted to ask what you had said." Anyone who had attempted to say all of that would have been breathless after that sentence, but she didn't miss a beat. This was awkward. I considered my response. There was no easy way to explain my voice to her. I made up my mind, and signed, "Oh, it was just a prank. Don't worry about it, I had nothing important to say." "By the way, how did you know I knew sign language?" I asked, changing the subject. "I saw you signing to a friend in the hallway. Is he deaf too?" "No," I replied, "We use it as a sort of code between us. Most other people don't understand it, so we can have silent conversations unnoticed by those around us." That wasn't entirely false. We had been known to sign to each other in class when the teacher wasn't looking, or to use exchange messages that nobody else would understand. I had intentionally left out the part where I had him speak for me when I didn't want to make within earshot uncomfortable. "Can I spend some time with you and your friend them?" asked the girl. The question caught me off guard, and when I didn't respond right away, she continued, "Not many people know sign language, so I don't have many people to talk to." My hands remained idle. "I'm not asking you to act as interpreters for me," she added quickly, "I wouldn't want to be a burden. I just would like to have someone to share conversation with." I turned to Vince, who nodded. I looked back at her and followed suit before signing, "We would be glad to hang out with you, and interpret if you need us to. That's Vince, and I'm Aidan, but my friends call me Resonance. Since it looks like we're friends now, you can call me that as well." "Thank you," signed the girl, looking up at us with a smile. "I'm Anita." The school year continued as normal. Vince and I spent our lunches with Anita for the first couple of weeks, before introducing her to our friends. She really was a nice girl. Vince did most of the talking for the three of us when we were in larger groups. One week in October, Vince was out sick for a couple of days, so it was just Anita and I. Since she didn't speak, and I couldn't without putting those around me off, it ended up being just the two of us for a short time. The second day of Vince's absence, Anita said to me, "I notice that you don't speak a lot, and when you do people around you seem uncomfortable. Why is that?" I sighed. Explaining this would be inevitable sooner or later. "There is something different about my voice," I signed. "It is hard to explain. When a person speaks, they are vibrating the air at a certain frequency. The exact frequency at which we do so determines the pitch. When I speak, the air vibrates at two frequencies. One of them people can hear. The other isn't so simple. It stays between 16 and 18 hertz, and it makes people feel uneasy or afraid. I get a kick out of watching people around me squirm, but it would be inconvenient to do it all of the time. So, I let Vince do most of the talking. That's why I know sign." "Well, I guess for once I am lucky I can not hear then," signed Anita with a smile. "Yeah, I think that is why we get along with each other so well," I signed back. "I speak and others fear, others speak and you don't hear. We're certainly an odd pair." In hindsight, I'm not sure if rhymes carry the same weight without the phonetics, so my brief display of poetic wit may have been lost on her, but it didn't matter. "You know, I'm like you in a way," I continued, "There aren't that many people I can converse with. Not in the way I can with you and Vince. If I talk too much, it just becomes too uncomfortable." She put her hand on mine, then awkwardly pulled it away to sign, "I enjoy our time together."

ding "It has been 789,000 days since the last workplace accident," declared the robotic tannoy, as Axel and Craig hauled a metal crate onto the conveyor belt. Axel pulled a lever, and the belt rumbled loudly as it carried the box down-line. Craig followed it. ding "Please ensure you are wearing your safety gear at all times while handling the machinery." Axel pulled on a set of thick gloves, while Craig double checked his helmet. The heat inside the heavy clothing was almost unbearable, but without it the forge would sear their skin, burn it black. It could also, they'd heard, survive almost any impact that could occur. Neither wanted to test the theory. ding "Grey Corp appreciates your work, and thanks you for not removing any Grey Corp hardware from Grey Corp worksites." The box halted by a pair of metal clamps attached to hydraulic pistons; the boys stuck them on opposite faces of the cube. The crates were designed not to be opened without factory-grade equipment, their cargo too valuable to be stolen. ding "When operating heavy machinery, please stand away from moving parts." They rolled their eyes and stepped away, each pressing a button on either side of the conveyor that would activate the pistons, tear the box open. Inside lay a weapons-grade helmet, with infrared and all those similar trappings built in. The thing was worth more than either of them. Possibly both. Axel lifted it from the box and moved it across to the assembly line, setting it down on the shoulders of a power armour suit. He held it steady while Craig connected the wires and bolted it together. ding "Now testing; IPA Suit MKV in room 6. Please vacate the room." They'd drilled for this, a long time ago. The world around them seemed to slow as the suit came to life. A metal gauntlet grabbed Craig by the coat, but he managed to slip out of the top layer and hit the floor running. Axel, on the other side, was already halfway towards the bunker room. crash The intelligent suit tore straight through the conveyor belt as Craig had to sprint around it. If it beat him to the door, he'd be trapped. He was faster, but the suit had no care for obstacles. Axel had reached the bunker door, but the insulated gloves were too thick to operate the door controls. He fought to get them off. Craig vaulted the next conveyor belt, but came down hard, twisting his ankle. The mechanical whirring closed behind him as he limped onward. The control panel accepted Axel's commands, and he ducked inside the bunker. Axel looked out at Craig and the IPA. He made a snap decision, and pulled the door closed. There was a hiss as it sealed, and then all sound from the factory room cut out. Axel dropped to the floor, where he wouldn't have to watch through the window. Blood spattered the glass. Even through the sound-proofing, he thought he heard the screams. ding "Grey Corp would like to thank you for your work. We would like to remind you that without our expendable human workforce, the Grey Corp Automatonic Union would not exist. It has been 789,000 days since the last workplace accident." A yellowish haze began to seep into the bunker room. Axel took off his mask. The sooner it was over, the better.

Is this inspired by John Wick? I love that movie! I wish I was a better writer but here goes nothing. I'm inside my room, chilling out. I called the guy down front for some room service. The window, the door, the air ducts. I also listen closely to the noises outside the door. Its quiet, too quiet. I hear the ding of the elevator down the hall, as I look through the peep hole I see its the bell hop. I sigh in relief. The bell hop knocks on the door and I let him in. To give him one last chance I came into work early. My shirt was slightly over sized so as not to "show an indecent tightness around my breasts" and my slacks were neatly pressed. I greeted all of my coworkers with a smile and even helped an old woman get a pair of security locked headphones BEFORE I clocked in. I gave my manager and happy grin as I opened my locker in the break room to store my purse. "Happy Tuesday," I told him in a chirpy voice. His eyes were looking blankly into mine when I turned to him after I closed my locker. Go ahead, I dare you. I thought. My manager's name tag was crooked, he was leaning on the locker instead of cleaning, and he was sipping tea out of a travel mug instead of bottled water as per company policy. Yet his mouth opened. "You shouldn't have walked through the store to get here. I thought I reminded everyone yesterday that we are using the backdoor for entry from now on. Please try to remember that, okay? I don't want to be everyone's babysitter here, nor do I feel I have to continually repeat myself." Continually repeat seemed a bit redundant. "Sure, sorry," I said. I smiled and tilted my head. Game on, motherfucker I turned around to leave. "And another thing," he told me. His eyes flicked up from my ass to my face. "Please try a bit harder to follow the dress policy here. If your khaki pants are shrunken and," his eyes traveled downward again, "tight that way..... we're going to have to have a discussion about dress policy violations." He looked at me with a perverted intensity. Perfect. "A discussion?" I asked, blinking at him. "You mean like in your office?" He smiled at me. "Yeah." I smiled too, and slowly undid the buttons of my blue polo shirt to show the beginning of my cleavage. "You mean dress code violations like this?" I ran my finger along my skin. His slimy smile did not fade. "In my office, missy," he said. It has been so long since I last opened the world around me. I felt into his mind and found his deepest fears. I drank them into myself as if I was dying of thirst. I followed him into his office. A bare and depressing little room. Cement blocks painted white, a calendar and "team goal progress" poster hanging up, a desk and a few chairs were the only things within. This was the only room that didn't have a security camera. I closed the door behind me and locked the door. He grinned and reached for his belt. "I am 17 years old. " I told him. My voice was slightly distorted. "What?" he asked, pausing. "When I inhabited this body, I expected to find a man like you." My bones cracked and groaned as I allowed them to grow. I became taller, my neck bending against the ceiling. "CHRIST!" he yelled, watching me in terror. Vertebrae were adding to my spine in a way that would make any human die from pain. My head was now positioned above him and I grinned at him with many sharpened teeth. His eyes were unable to look away. "FUCK!" he screamed, scrambling backwards on the desk. "Aren't we going to? " I felt feathery legs and fragile exoskeletons of insects crawling out of my mouth as I spoke. Beetles and cockroaches and spiders fell from under my eyes. They traveled down my face and fell around my manager with audible crunches. "Jesus," he said under his breath and he pushed himself all the way back, jumping off of the desk to crouch on the other side. "Jesus!" "No, " I stooped over him and reached out with a long, bony arm. "I am the eternities, " My words were garbled from the insects leaving my body. I could feel them climbing up my throat and I smiled. "Get away!" my manager cried, and he scrambled to hide underneath the desk. I picked up the desk to reveal him cowering. I laughed and my breath hissed between my teeth. "I am life and I am death! " My manager lay on the ground, grabbing for his phone. I turned it to a rat. The rat multiplied, each new rodent being tied to the others by its tail. Soon a quivering, furry mass began to fill the room. I opened my manager's perception of time. What I did next would feel as though it lasted for years. The rats filled the room and covered his body. He screamed loudly, a scream that tore out of his body and rang through the air. "Death, death, death! " A coworker was turning the office's door knob quickly. "You okay, Keith?" he called to my manager. The rats disappeared. My manager stared at me in horror, his hair was now white. Not a sound escaped his mouth. I let my two human eyes fall out, showing two black empty sockets where they once were. My lips and tongue rotted away, showing my teeth in a grimace. All of my carnal body fell away; I became a large deformed mass decaying on the floor. My manager yelled again. He shouted curses at the human on the other side of the door, pleading for help. Pleading for an escape. At once, I plucked his spirit from his body so he could see me. His body stood frozen. His screams were choked out. His spirit now faced me. I was more horrifying than he could ever imagine. He was unable to focus on my thousands of eyes, and beastly limps and faces that constantly morphed into terrifying contortions. I was a thousand burning columns of fire guarding a black abyss where souls screamed from within. I moved toward him. His spirit shrank into a small boy who began to cry out, "Oh god, oh god!" I laughed in my many voices and reached down to pick up the spirit boy. "Happy Tuesday. " With that, I gave myself a great gaping mouth and swallowed him. His cries were silenced forever. His mortal body lay on the ground in the office. The door to the office unlocked.

People were shocked, but eventually, they learned, Bing soared a bit in popularity, but then made room for competitors like Yandex and DuckDuckGo. The OpenStreetmap Project was used instead of Google Maps, eventually, when it was clear just how much data was corrupted, Sailfish replaced Android. The advertisements were not missed by anyone at all. GMail users had to resort to using an email service which doesn't suck. The Google employees and the management were the only ones who actually suffered: the former lost their jobs, the latter their freedom after it came out that the company cooperated with foreign secret services as well as the domiestic ones. And somewhere, a black hat hacker was in his lair (it is not the parents' basement, it is a secret lair!) and crossed one name off his kill list.

I won't let him die; I won't let him die. Five years old, that means I have to play out the next thirteen years exactly the same as the first time. Two years in I forget my goal. I survive middle school and in high school I fall in love with the same girl as last time; Delanie. I made the same mistakes; I got her pregnant in my senior year. Nine months later we had our son, I was holding him in my arms, just like before. Then he had an asthma attack at four in the morning, just like before. Then there were no nurses around, just like before. Then he died in my arms, just like before. I fell to my knees and sobbed over my sons body. "You didn't make her get the shot," I was standing over myself, talking to me. I tsked at myself, "You should have done better, we only have one more shot." I looked up to my future self, tears filling my eyes. "Can't you send me back closer? Not to when I'm litterally five, when I can do nothing?" "Maybe you should have remembered to leave yourself notes, or remind yourself some other way." "I won't fail us again," I say setting my son down and rising as my tears fall from my face. "Send me back, I'll save our son."

After exhausting all the standard approaches, we'd traveled to Arizona to meet Dr. Christo Milonas, a Memory Loss specialist who had some unorthodox techniques. My mom hadn't reacted well to the doctor's suggestion. "Reading?" Dr. Milonas smiled, probably having had this conversation hundreds of times before. "Yes. Josh needs to learn to read and write." "But he's only nine years old! You want a child to learn to read? That would be absurd even for a child without ML." "Mrs. Smith, you've traveled thousands of miles to come see me. At least listen for a few minutes." My mom said nothing, which Dr. Milonas took as his cue to continue. "I've found that children as young as six can learn to read and write with the same proficiency as a college reading or writing major. In fact, they learn even faster than college students due to the plasticity of their young minds." My mom still wasn't convincend. "Okay, let's pretend for a moment that Josh can learn to read. How could it possibly help? It's not like there are jobs for readers or writers." "Whenever Josh learns something important, he can write it down. And when he wants to remember that thing, he can read what he's written. By doing so he'll be able to remember just as well as anyone else. There are even a number of techniques to do mathematics using a pen and paper." "Pen?" "Oh sorry. It's a type of writing equipment." Now my mom was a bit worried. "I'm not sure we can afford specialized equipment. Will our insurance cover it?"

I have been walking at least eight hours a day for three days. Sore doesn't even begin to describe it. My blisters have blisters. I don't want to get graphic, but let's just say I'm pretty sure it's not just sweat soaking my socks. I love my dog, I remind myself as she sniffs the bush..... again. I take the opportunity to shift back and forth, foot to foot. If she had understood what she was doing, I tell myself through gritted teeth as we set off again, she would never have done it. Is that true? She charges off after a squirrel. I, of course, charge too. Lunging, Lulu nearly teleports across the lawn. I am jerked off my feet as she sinks her teeth into the squirrel's furry body. She'd never caught a squirrel before..... until three days ago. Now she catches every squirrel, and yet she never seems to tire of them. Chewing absently, she drags me towards the park. We're almost at the soccer field. I know what comes next. The squirrel morphs and changes into a tennis ball. Her favorite. Of course. Hey, at least I get to stand still. I throw the ball as far as I can, then collapse on the ground as she gleefully chases it. If the pattern holds, we'll get to go home in about three hours. Then it's belly rub time for about an hour, followed by a hamburger and buttered toast. We have a freezer full of nothing but hamburger, a pantry full of toast. Not bread. Hot, buttered toast. The house smells amazing. Lulu returns and drops the ball in my lap, expectantly. I throw the ball and she yelps with joy as she runs to retrieve it. I guess it isn't all bad. Unlimited food even if it's a bit repetitive and I'm getting into the best shape of my life. I don't seem to have a job anymore. That's OK. I guess I wasn't exactly dying to get back into the office. Still, as I throw the ball for my overjoyed dog yet again, I can't help but wonder what life might have looked like if I had been the one to find the magic lamp in the cave...

Dear Sister, Our last conversation left a lot of thing unsaid. I see your points: me not reaching out to you, checking to see how you are. You call me and others selfish because, in your mind, the conversation never turns to you or what's happening in your world. The truth is, it's hard for me to relate to you now. I used to see you as strong, that you could overcome anything. Now all I see is you being conquered by the eating disorder. You say you are lonely, and I know that the disease makes you this way. You've called our parents narcissists, not wanting to have anything do to with them (especially since you don't want them to know about your disease) and yet have no problem asking for handouts when you've needed money (which they've gladly done). You can't accept gifts from then denounce the same people who have helped you. I hate that you've missed family events, putting money ahead of it but preach about the importance of family. I know that this but be a daily battle between your heart and mind. I don't understand what you're going through, I love you, and I want to help you heal. I've seen you do extraordinary things in pursuit of your dreams. You say you don't want to be this way anymore, but I don't see you pursuing something that deeply affects you. I guess the reason why I don't reach out is because maybe, if I pull away, it will hurt less when this disease finally conquers your body as it's done your spirit. If that's selfish of me, then it is what it is and I will have to live with that. Right now, it feels better than watching one of the great loves of my life slowly die. I don't know where to go from here. I just know that I love you. Truly yours, Sister

I woke up to the smell of hot butter and scrambled eggs. My head still on its side I opened one eye to a wash of marigold light. The fan was still quietly stirring and the curtains which I remembered to be blue the nighy before were now beige. I jerked up, squinting towards my open bedroom door. My head was spinning and I shuffled around in my bed of bears in space suits and toothy stars. "Come here, baby, switch of your fan" what the fuck I jumped out of bed towards the door to only see the back of mother entering the kitchen. I stared at her hair, neatly curled on its ends. "Look at how it curls, Aiden. Mama's hair looks like the petals of the sunflower" she twirled her fingers into her hair whilst admiring them in her reflections on the car window as we made our way to a family friend's birthday party, I remembered. My body felt tighter. More tout. My limbs short and pudgy. My hair was curly and it fringed my eyes. WHAT THE FUCK I ran along the corridor to the kitchen where I found my mother, in her sundress, pouring apple juice into my feline-patterned cup I cried over when it was broken because of my clumsiness. "Come here, eat with Mama" She gestured me to the high chair as she placed my full cup around the steaming plate of hearty breakfast. Her face was glowing. Her cheeks still rosy from her morning shower. I remembered her mole on her left cheek. My nose picked up the vivid scent of pink pepper and lemon which I only recognized to be her's. Mama I paced across the kitchen, my eyes fixed to my mother's hazels. Her smile soft and safe. I am in a dream Her scent was becoming so vivid. Mama don't leave me She held up her hands to reach mine Mama please stay here I grabbed her hands, smooth and warm, just as I remembered Mama I miss you so much she wrapped her arms around me to lift me up to the chair. I didn't care that I was back in 2006. The absence of my father hadn't bothered me a bit. I knew I was with her again. My mouth, slightly agaped, drooling, quivering. I had no words. My five-year old self hadn't known many words. My five-year old self hadn't learned how to react. My five-year old self hadn't known how to prevent my mother's passing of a heart attack that was about to happen that night "Good morning, my darling Aiden. Mama wants you to know that she loves you very much." She scooped a forkful of the golden platter and lifted to her lips to cool it before feeding me "I love you, Aiden, remember that"

Josh was dozing in on his bed, his house quiet after a noisy session of Rock Band that took place a few hours prior. He was jostled out of his sleep after hearing the shrill robotic sound pour from his TV speakers THE FOLLOWING MESSAGE IS BEING TRANSMITTED AT THE REQUEST OF THE FEDERAL GOVERMENT. ALTHOUGH EXACT NUMBERS ARE NOT YET KNOWN, IT IS ESTIMATED THAT OVER 1 MILLION MAGES HAVE DESCENDED UPON ALL CITIES AND TERITORIES IN THE UNION. ALL CIVILIANS AND LOWER GOVERMENT PERSONELLE ARE ADVISED TO SHELTER IN PLACE, WHILE MILITARY AND UPPER GOVERMENT PERSONELLE ARE REQUIRED TO MAN THEIR RESPECTIVE DUTIES. Josh already has his uniform on, with a pin his Father had worn in the 2nd war. It was a good luck charm to him. "Fatah?" chirps Claybill. He rises slowly from his learning creche, pale, blond brow curled in reproach. "There's a year missing." I smile, sliding off my black and chrome symbiote-handler's gauntlets. "Whatever do you mean, child?" Claybill pulls the dashwires out of his chest and slips out of the creche. "Year 34, Pre Zero Event. 2016, under the old demarcation. There is no catalogue of any event during that orbital year." He is a curious, strong-willed boy, so I know he will not be easily placated. "And what is 34 PZE to you, my son?" "There was an Olympics that year," says Claybill, gliding across the static plating of the Hub Room. "The precursor to the Oh-126 games. I was working to tally national victories over the centuries." "For what purpose?" I muse. "To know," says Claybill flatly. That is always the answer. I know it is the answer, but I revel in hearing him say it. "Hold," I say, pulling up a fresh relay and dipping my port-finger. I loop through centuries of black, crusted data, dank with decay and lacking adequate architecture. I loop around and around, swooping through aged piles of unsorted waste and find nothing. There is 33 PZE, there is 35 PZE..... "You are correct," I say, wiggling loose my port-finger and clapping down the relay node. "How strange." "What does it mean?" asks Claybill. I long ago promised the boy that I do not know would never be seen as an adequate response, so I have set my own trap. "We will find out," I say, reaching for my wave-coat. The boy dresses and follows me out the door. We take the light tube to Washington, where the Historical Collective huddles in dark, stale buildings, worshiping the wrinkled pages of smudged, senseless ledgers. I sign in at the door and we take jump-plates down to the fifth sublevel. In stall -525 we find a man named Carbunkle pinned to a linejunkie's saddle, head and arms submerged in a tactile data display, dangling legs prodded with electric needles to keep the muscles active and engaged. "PZE 34," I say, pressing my thumb to the payment metric. "The former 2016. What happened to all records associated with this year?" Carbunkle swivels in his saddle, the white flesh of his arms swinging downward, hanging like wobbly stalactites. I can just see the backside of his data display, all white and blue and blurry. "No records," croaks Carbunkle. "We know," says Claybill, scowling at the dangling man. "Why?" The saddle whips around, rotating, corkscrewing throughout the little stall. Suddenly the whole contraption sighs, settling back to the floor. Carbunkle pulls his head free from the tactile display. "Nothing," he says, almost sadly, if these history wonks are capable of such feelings. "I don't see it." "Before and after," presses Claybill, unwilling to accept nothing as a payment for his curiosity. "33 and 35. What changes?" "Much," says Carbunkle, sliding his head back into the display. "Oh. Oooh. Oh. " The saddle rocks gently, like an infant's cradle. "What?" says Claybill, impatient. A conversation we will need to have. Not everyone is of the same speed. "That is the line," says Carbunkle. "The before and after." "Yes?" urges Claybill. "Full organic," says Carbunkle. "35 PZE. All flesh. No metal. Before we were wired. By 33 we had begun..... but still, that does not answer the question, does it?" Claybill strokes his forehead. There is still a faint indentation from where his head was recently resting against the lip of his learning creche. "In the old year 2015 we were full organic. By 2017 we were not. And somewhere, at some time, we struck all records of 2016." "The year we changed?" I suggest. "The reason why we changed," counters Claybill. I smile. I never expected to be bettered so quickly. It is difficult sometimes to hide my pride. "It was a great leap," says Carbunkle, as if to prove his own value. "The world of 35 PZE is strikingly quaint compared to 33 PZE." Claybill nods, the answer formulating cleanly in his mind. "The year we realized we could no longer trust ourselves." "We looked to computers to save ourselves," I add, like Carbunkle, trying to show some merit of my own. "And removed all traces to hide our shame," says Claybill, smiling himself. "What horrors must we have unleashed? To take such drastic measures?" "I do not suppose it matters," I say, leading the boy back towards the jump-plates. "We survived. If it took forgetting to do so, so be it." "What other events have we forgotten?" wonders Claybill as the plates lift soundlessly towards the ground floor. "And how long have we buried our shame in this manner?" I shake my head. "I do not know," I sigh. "And that, one supposes, is entirely the point."

David tossed and turned, unable to quite fall asleep. The pressures of leading one of the worlds foremost teams responsible for developing the newest nanotech theory and application was something that he could not seem to come to terms with. Not with assholes like Williams to deal with every day. Arlan Williams was a powerful man. He controlled the purse strings. He owned the facilities. He held all the cards. Without him, research would come to a halt. With him present, it was unbearable. He was constantly interrupting, wanted to know the latest progress. Demanding the data be turned over to him immediately for his review. It was maddening to David and his team. On top of these pressures, there were other scientists across the world doing the same kind of work. Some of them always seemed to be just a step ahead. He was feeling less than effective these days. He slowly became aware of a ringing inside his head. Call coming in. The ringing became louder until it pushed all other thoughts aside. Interface. In his mind's eye he sensed blackness, then a very rudimentary green glow. It quickly coalesced into a small green dot in the upper right corner of his inner vision. It began to blink. A small icon in the form of an archaic telephone handset flashed in the lower left. He was always slightly amused that a piece of hardware made obsolete generations ago would still be the universal signal for an incoming call. No caller ID. Very odd. Either the caller ID was blocked, or the signal encrypted. "Hello," he answered groggily. "David?" the caller asked. "Yes..... this is David. Who is this?" "There is no time to explain. I have created a user account for you. You will find a hyperlink and passkey in the attached packet." "What the hell are you talking about?" David asked. "I have to go, just get here," the voice said. A short beep, then silence. The call had ended. David was fully awake now, and extremely intrigued. The voice sounded familiar. Very familiar. He focused on the attachment. It contained a web link in the form of an IP address and a passkey to access it. " Get here? Get where? " David mused aloud. He copied the IP address to his browser and almost instantly the page was before him. It was blank except for a dark blue background and a text input field waiting for the passkey. No clue to it's purpose was evident. David sighed. This could be anything. It could all be dismissed as a prank call, except the voice sounded so familiar! He paused and considered. That voice..... Something danced on the very edge of comprehension..... then was gone again. Damn it. He focused on the input field and entered the passkey.

Yesterday was my graduation, the day where all of my life finally comes together and everything starts to make sense. All of my friends and acquaintances went there own way. Everything moved so fast. six months came and passed. Pathetic. I mean I knew that I didn't have a plan. I usually didn't need one. I can see all of my friends moving on, and they're just as lost as me It seems like everyday since graduation, I've let more and more of my self fade with their memories. Initiative finally set itself ablaze in my heart, knowing who I was again I could once again give myself to art. As I wrote my final goodbye, I looked in the mirror and saw my corpse leaving me behind.

Every morning, he gets up, makes a pot of coffee, and reads the paper. It's been his routine for nearly 40 years, and at 79 years old, he's not planning to change it now. He starts with the sports section, sadly noting that the Cardinals have lost once again. When he gets to the obituaries, he sighs. There are many disadvantages to aging, but the worst is watching his friends slowly fade from this life. A war veteran, Stanley Millhouse is no stranger to death, but it never gets any easier to find out that someone you care for has died. He fortifies himself with another sip of coffee before he begins to scan the names on the page. It's been sixty years since he last saw Amelia Riley, and he almost misses her name completely. But there's a picture. In black and white newsprint, not much bigger than his thumb, is a photograph of the woman he loved before he went off to war. He nearly forgets to breathe when the tiny letters inform him that the funeral service is tomorrow. His grandchildren are coming to visit him, like they do every Sunday. It's part of their routine. Disrupting it for a funeral would be..... illogical. But he hasn't seen Amy in sixty years. He has to see her one last time. He knows it will be heartbreaking, to see his highschool sweetheart lying in a coffin. He'd written to her while he was in Vietnam. She never wrote back. After six months, he stopped mailing the letters. He spares a brief thought for the box up in his attic. What is he going to do with those letters now? He can't go to the funeral, he tells himself. He wants to remember Amy the way she was, 19 years old, her red hair flying in all directions as they cruised to the beach in his convertible. The paper, that horrid newspaper, he wishes he'd never picked it up this morning. Wishes the delivery man had skipped his house. But it's all there, her life's story. Three children, it says. Two grandchildren. How can he intrude on their lives? On their grief? As he folds up the paper, he tells himself he'll stay home. Have lunch with his grandkids. He puts his coffee cup in the sink, rinses out the coffee pot. Kyle was working on a big science project for school, and wanted his grandpa's help. He shakes his head and reaches for the crossword. It's just another funeral, he tells himself. It's been six decades. He's moved on. But his fingers shake in a way that has nothing to do with his age as he picks up the phone. He finds his granddaughter's number, presses call. He won't be home tomorrow, he tells her. He has a funeral to go to.
