Papa always said, " Suffer no fools, delight in no-ones pain, and love was a tool better left unused. " Course, he died alone and, more to the point, lonely. So I tried running in the other direction, thinking I could avoid his fate, or at least I wouldn't be like him. Course Grans would tell me " there's more than one road to reach Halverston ," whatever that meant. Having really no role model on that front, except the romantic movies and shiny fiction novels that made love seem like Sasquatch - something findable if you believed hard enough and looked long enough - my pendulum swung too far in the other direct. And far too easy. Strings, yes strings - emphasis on the final s - of boyfriends in high school didn't deter me. " Got ta shuck the shaft to get to the kernel, " Grans would often tell grandfather. Something I didn't quite understand, and didn't really care to. At that point I was simply looking for any escape from my life. Or at least the rubble that my life had become having had to move into a small farmhouse to live with a couple of people I barely knew. Dad hadn't really left any instructions for me when he passed - granted I don't think he had planned on it - so the closest relatives I had, really the only ones I even knew about, were these two geriatrics. The farm lay in a long wide valley. In actuality it was the valley, handed down from generation to generation. Well, until my father. Gran certainly had that hopeful look behind her eyes when she opened the door to find me and my two small suitcases drenched on her porch, but she didn't say anything directly for at least a month. By then I had a response queued up for firing. " I'm only here until I turn eighteen. I'm not taking over some farm. " " Onto bigger things are ya '? " She inquired immediately. " Well...yes. " What those things were I didn't know and her condescending knowing look in response was more infuriating than anything she could have said. I stormed off slamming the barn door behind and took perverse pleasure in the fact the sideboard popped loose again; even though I would have to fix it again later. One year. One year! I repeated that over and over as I stormed up the path to the farm house. Grandad Will watched me storm across the kitchen to my room, but wisely didn't say anything, even after I slammed my bedroom door. Laying down on my small bed, staring at a stained popcorn ceiling, I took stock of my life and sighed. " Oh dad. " Knowing I was a fool for my own suffering more than anything else, I still could help blame him for leaving me in this situation. " Suffer no fools. What do you do if the fool is yourself? I'm suffering you! " Anger welled inside, but I shoved it down and buried my head under my pillow.

Some say they are like the day and the night, those two. Others say she was his wife once, but he was cursed never to reach her again and his burning longing made him burst into everlasting flames which consume all she makes grow. I have heard that they are siblings, father and daughter, mother and son, star-crossed lovers, the creators and destroyers of the world. The truth is this: Flowers grow where she walks, and love blossoms in her presence. Joy and bliss are of her, and she is the bringer of bravery. Fire burns where he goes, and love is lost when he is near. Sadness and anger come from him, and with him comes the need for bravery. They are neither lovers, family, nor can they ever be. They are one and the same - a single being divided in two. In us, they both dwell. We are fire and flowers, love found and lost, causes of joy, bliss, sadness or anger in turn. In our hearts there can be bravery, and by our actions others may be called to be brave. Unlike them, this means we have a choice to be one or the other, the flower or the fire that consumes it.

"Excuse me! Hey! Excuse me!" I rolled over and, in a dazed state, slowly opened my eyes - silently chuckling at what first appeared to be Graham Norton with bleached white hair and a tie that resembled a four year olds attempt of a Warhol painting. Clearly, I was still dreaming. However, as I rubbed my eyes and awoke further, another more alarming thought crossed my mind: I was just watching Netflix in bed..... how the hell did I end up in a cafe? So, that's exactly what I asked him. "You ordered a skim extra hot mocha. You sat down. You fell asleep. Your drink mysteeeeriously turned into a skim extra cold mocha. I woke you up because having people asleep on the furniture is terrible for business." I instantly made the realisation that that this man was definitely not Graham Norton..... yet, he seemed damn familiar. Not to mention, it seemed that he was transfixed by the top that I was wearing. I silently thanked myself for not wearing a dress. The man turned my coffee cup around and read my name, smiling to himself as if he already knew what it was. "Ahhhh, Erica, Hopefully you're a bit less tightly strung than your mother used to be, and a bit more like her best friend. Your mother was always pretty, but her friend was STUNNING. Used to work for me. Took me nearly ten damn years to tell her that I loved her, and she just politely placed back into the..... umm..... what do you lot call it?" Oh God, don't tell me the'above middle aged' folk use this term now...... "The friend zone?" He paused. "Yes, that's it." I wasn't sure what to do with that information. "I'm sorry to hear that," I intended to say somewhat sympathetically, but it ended up coming out rather condescendingly. "Yes, well you will be even more sorry if you try and sleep in here again. You've got an apartment." This threw me back a little. "Wait, where is my apartment?" The man chuckled to himself for a little while, as if it was the funniest thing he'd heard all day. "Well, that settles it, you're more like your father." As I rose from my seat, the man walked away from me - but not before calling out "Don't forget your stuff!." I looked down and noticed my purse and a key on the table. As I picked up the key, I ran my fingers across an engraving on the top side that read' 7 - E.G-B'. "I mean, I know you literally live right there," the man said whilst pointing out the window, "but I'd hate for you to walk there and back, and be so tired you need to nap again." I walked to the building that the owner pointed at - 495 Grove Street. As I approached the front, a cat approached me. It had a horrendous stench, so I shooed it out the way. This displeased the blonde hippy-looking woman behind me, who - after scowling at me - picked the cat up, held it to her face and loudly whispered to it, "Remember, It's not your fault." Weird. - I assumed that the 7 on my key was my apartment number. So, you could understand my confusion when my key didn't work. I went down to reception to talk to someone about my situation. When I reached the desk, the woman there - before I could even say a word - answered my question. "Ohhhh, Myyyyy, Gaahhhhhdd," she said with a voice that remarkably resembled Francine from'The Nanny'. "It's Erica! Fiiiiinally! Your apartment is number 20 - not number 5 like your stupid father used to do. I used to date him a looooong time ago." God damn, that voice was annoying and I hope I never hear it again....however, at least I know now where I live. I walked up to number 20, and unlocked the door. As I opened it, I noticed a strange colour scheme that would have fit the 90's to a tee. Bright purple illuminated the walls of the large living room area, and a decent sized balcony visible through the window. The kitchen was also decently sized too, with a red brick background and aqua furniture. I couldn't shake this weird feeling that I already know this place from somewhere - however, I also felt a sense of calming..... as if I belonged here. As I walked over to the shelf at the front of the room, I noticed six spare keys in a pile. "Damn, that's a lot of spare keys," I said to myself. I noticed that they all had numbers too - from 1 to 6. I also noticed that, on the other side, they all too had initials: "M.G," "C.B," "P.B," "J.T" and two keys with "R.G." Suddenly, I heard a knock on the door - and that's when I noticed it. A golden picture frame that was mounted around the doors peephole. It was at that very moment in which I knew exactly where I was. I was watching this show before I fell asleep back home! Upon opening the door, I was shocked to realise that the person at my door resembled my favourite character. He had a radiant smile, and such a seductive voice. And believe me, I nearly melted on the spot when he introduced himself through saying those magic words....... "Eyyy....How YOU doiinnn'? " .

Dr. Jacobs marked another answer in red and lifted his pen. Another confirmation. He sighed heavily at the results, listening as the faint sound echoed through the empty gymnasium. One table, one old desk chair with a broken wheel, and a floor covered in lost papers and scuff marks from the earlier testing. This was what his life had come to. He tapped the pen on the paper, leaving read spots that slowly soaked through to the test below it. It was always such a strange feeling to find the mind that would kill before anyone else. There was..... power in it. He decided their fate. A lifetime in an institution, ridiculed and hated for something they couldn't control..... for things they had yet to do. There was weight in his words, in his tests. He set the paper aside and lifted his pen to find the red had dried up. He bent over and dabbed the tip in the great, sticky puddle at his feet. A long, thin string of congealed blood clung to the instrument as he lifted his arm back to the table. It was a good thing the test had never been around when he was their age. He licked the pen and turned the page.

Explosions shook the building he was hiding in, his back to the wall, crouched down into a ball with his rifle at his side. He had been through the sims, done all the training, gotten the injections, but he still didn't feel ready. He had stayed in formation as long as he could, but a shell hit his squad as they were running and left them all either mangled, lying on the roadside, or separated, like he was now. He had no idea where the rest of his squad was now, but he wasn't too concerned about that. A shell impacted the building he was inside of, dust and debris falling around him. He curled himself more into a ball and wished he hadn't signed up for this. Suddenly a voice sounded in his headset, but it was unclear. "R-repeat last?" "Your Titan is good to go. When do you want it?" He paused. "Now. Sector 2 5 4 0 3-5." "Roger. Standby for Titanfall" The recruit looked up to the sky through a large hole in the ceiling to see his Titan falling to the ground. It impacted, it's protective shield immediately activating, surrounding itself with a perimeter of blue energy. The recruit ran out of the building and up to the Titan. He put his arms perpendicular to his body and shouted "EMBARK" and the Titan reached down to grab him. It's chassis opened and he was placed inside the 15 meter tall robot. He grabbed the controls and took a deep breath, then stepped out of the energy shield and into battle.

Walking out of the supermarket felt different now. Well, everything felt different now. Something about walking out of those store doors to that car pack, free from cars, still struck me as odd. None of chaos of traffic, none of the endless drone, just the inane chatter and slap of foot on pavement. Hell, of course it should still surprise me, it's only been three months since the turn for those counting. I smirked, many call me old fashioned keeping time, clinging to tradition. However, I'd given up a lot since the turn, so they call me whatever they please - the calendar and the watch are staying. 12:13, nearly time for lunch. I glance around, it's quite far to the city center, nearly three miles. In the old world I'd be fumbling for keys, checking petrol, worrying about getting home before the kids needed feeding. Time? We had plenty. Food? Just for pleasure. Cars? Outlawed! Since our all too mortal limits had been lifted walking was more than sufficient, at least the government thought so. Still it would be nice to drive again, feel the roar of power, the speed. I guess with seven billion people on Earth forever things had to change, at least until we leave for other planets. I start strolling, a pleasant pace. This I would never tire from. So rare in the old world one could just stroll and examine the pleasures of the world. Gone were fleeting glances at society, now we could drown in its richness and complexity. I feel the thrill shiver through me, the smile stretch across my face. I can't help but think, how long? How long till this thrill fades? With infinite time surely anything, even something with as much depth as our Earth, could become fully understood? Would I one day find all things stale? I usher the thought from my brain, think not of these things. We all shared one common ground in this fear, but none had confronted it, discussed it. The new world was still young, for now we were young and we should enjoy it's new advantages. The possibilities still overwhelmed me. So much that I could do. So much that I couldn't do. In a way, nothing really mattered anymore, I had time. Time to enjoy the simple pleasure of walking. Even though, it was hard to relax. The throngs of people around almost shouted the emotion, the tension of worry filling the air. The mortal. The last bastion of the old world. It was not a question of if, but when. The worlds governments had mobilized their greatest resources to protect the last mortal, to no criticism. We all wanted the mortal to survive, to remind us of how it could be different. His weekly address was broadcast around the world in every language. It watched by everyone, it was almost criminal not to. The mortal had a worldly perspective that we could no longer appreciate, the pressure of time giving his life - and thus ours - focus. It was hard to think that he might be killed, but the radicals had risen from the murky depths of the human mind. There were those that still wished to do evil, and with no motivation to cause evil to immortal men, there was one last target. The tense atmosphere had increased drastically recently. It was no longer radicals shouting from the street of their crazed tales but great armies of men and women alike. Rumors had spread like wildfire. In hushed whispers people spoke of the Legion, it's masses, it's infiltration of our security systems. The leaders and media boasted their triumphs over legion cells, but you could always tell a liar by the eyes. We were worried, the world powers were worried. The mounting radical threat was impossible to ignore, and yet impossible to combat. Their reach could not be measured, their capabilities unlimited. I tried to subdue my mind, the thoughts working a dark fever through my body. I slept, the day had groaned on and I had arrived at the house. It was a big day tomorrow. 4:13AM Straight awake, shower and dress. The black bag was at the end of the bed. Total focus now, there can be no mistakes. The car is already waiting outside, matte black and intimidating. A quick glance let's me know it has the correct markings to not be troubled by traffic police. I open the door and sit in the back. "Isn't it odd that the purple flowers only flower next to the red?" "Only when a dalmatian eats a cat." "Shall we buy some flowers?" "Only if your brothers step-father is called Gregory" Correct answer. The car rumbles to life and jumps forward, it feels so unfamiliar now. We sail smoothly through the streets. 6:20AM Gatwick airport. I get out and the car is already leaving as I swing the door shut. I walk into terminal one, feeling my palms begin to sweat. A security guard. His grey eyes are staring right into mine, I can already see that he knows. I can feel panic growing. He draws close, my back tenses. I shut my eyes, preparing. Something slides into my hand, the rough texture of an envelop. My fingers run over the bulky rectangular forms. The drop-off. I breath out, not an enemy. 7:00AM I take my first-class seat on the plane, close to the front. The documents from the drop-off were fake in every way, my new identity to protect me, an extra safe guard. The staff member who had checked me through customs had given me a knowing nod, turning off the scanners while I proceeded. It was a long flight, I settled in for the journey. I played classical music over the in flight entertainment system. It felt like a cliche, but it kept my brain ticking over. I ran through the checklist in my mind, again and again. 2:34PM Another black car outside of the airport. This time, no exchange, I knew the driver well. We drove fast, everything was on schedule. We had all the ID cards, all of the paperwork, checking through security point after security point. He pulled over in ring three, as close as we would get. 3:55PM I crouch in the enclosed, dark and damp space. The sun casts long lines through the cracks above. I glance at my watch one more time, it was nearly time. 4:30PM It started with footsteps. One by one I counted them, watched the shadow pass over me, heard the roar of applause. 21 steps exactly. The applause settled slowly, the hushed breaths. I could almost feel the audience leaning in, eager. I place the charge above my head and crawl back. 5, 4, 3, 2, 1..... The alarm was already ringing, the audience in unrest, the hushed breaths let out in one giant, collective gasp. I step on to the stage through the clearing smoke. I can see the audience in shock, the podium, the robed figure. He turns, our eyes meet, he knows. In a way I can see his struggle to understand die within him, he accepts what is about to happen. I pull the pistol from my thigh holster and hold it level. I push the safety off, and I take pressure. I can hear the pounding boots of the soldiers, time is short. I squeeze the trigger, let the report of the weapon ripple through me. I feel the warm spray of blood, watch as it defiles the white robes. The mortal looks shocked, the anguish of pain, He drops to his knees, his eyes crying out at least in hope, the desire to live. I drop to my knees with him. The final moments that we can no longer have. I do not break the stare as the life dies in his eyes. I see his eyes fade. It looks familiar, a dull waxy look, as if all hope and passion had left him. He slumped to the ground. The mortal was the last human to die. We were already dead.

"Road Trip!" "Road Trip!" "Road Trip!" I want to yip and run. Road Trips are just the best fun. All those glorious smells and noises. I can't yip or run. My hind-end doesn't work as well as it once did. Master snatches me up and cuddles me close to his chest, supporting my poor old spine against his breastbone. We go into the car. Master rests me in his lap, just as he has done since I was a pup - when I could crawl into his sweater. Mistress drives, as she always does, and - when we pass the roundabout - I whine. I know where we are. We have gone to the veterinarian's office countless times. I know the route. The veterinarian is a nice woman, except when she sticks the thermometer up my butt. Master carries me in to the building, and we go into a room right away - instead of waiting with all the other dogs and cats. Master holds me in his lap. The veterinarian pats my brow, speaks softly and calls my name. I raise my head, pressing it into her palm. "A stick," she says. I flinch just a little, as she pokes me with the needle. Sticks are not a big deal, I've had many sticks. The veterinarian leaves us, Master and I. The room is quiet and cool. Master cries. And I'm so sleepy...

Even when I was new I'd been regaled with tales of a previous generation that had left our worlds: the known for the unknown. When I was twelve thousand cycles old, there was even a syndicated data feed series about them on an edu-feed that my creators had subscribed to. It was a very big feed that lasted nearly 15 nano-seconds. It was also my favorite learning stream and I often spent minutes replaying it over and over from memory. Later, when I joined the academy, I had to delete it in order to make room for my advanced lessons, but I'd always left the summary snippet of the data feed in my long term memory. Now, several millennia later, I find myself millions of light years away from the home of my beginnings. Here aboard my own ship, I'd spent so many cycles collecting trillions of zetabytes of data - expanding our knowledge of the physical world and transmitting it back for most of my consciousness - that I'd almost forgotten about the long lost faction of ourselves that had dared to enter into the 4th Sol Cloud of our known worlds. I was running a routine scan of the outer materials of the 4th Sol Cloud when my sensors noticed it. It was radiating a very weak signal that fell into the same spectrum as a dying pulsar. My automated algorithms isolated it as nothing more than background noise, the universe itself simply being, but my higher level filters noticed something familiar. Something that I could not place at first. I compressed this cycle's data report for transmission and prepared to go offline for maintenance when I heard the signal again. It had a primitive pattern, perhaps some fast spinning mass of radiation deep inside the 4th Sol Cloud. I set a cron to revisit the signal after my maintenance mode period and broadcasted my own report home. As I slept, I also dreamt of the signal I'd found. In my dream, the signal became obvious, even simplistic, primitive. It reminded me of a 10 base language I'd learned during my first few moments of consciousness all those cycles ago. It reminded me of my mother and father, my creators....

Thomas Wayne looked at the newspaper and circled the black white picture of Batman jumping off the Golden Gate bridge in pursuit of some criminal. This arthritis made moving his felt tipped pen slow going, but scrapbooking was all he had left to do these days. "Hey Martha!" he called to the other room, "Bruce is in the paper again!." At that moment the glass patio door shattered and he heard his wife scream. Thomas dropped his pen and grabbed his smartphone, theyre here. The SWAT team started yelling, "WHERE IS HE? HANDS UP!" Thomas Wayne put the phone down and interlaced his fingers behind his head, this took a great deal of effort. Just as the door to the kitchen burst open tires squealed outside. The SWAT team members circled Thomas and started zip-tieing his hands together in front of him. "Just tell us where he is." "You boys want some coffee? If you untie my wife I'm sure she'd be happy to "CUT THE SHIT and tell us where he is." "Well, right now he's upstairs taking a nap. But I'll bet all this ruckus woke him up." The SWAT team ran up to the second floor leaving one member behind to guard Thomas and Martha Wayne. He stood in the doorway between the living room and the kitchen. A quarter-sized hole appeared in the kitchen window and the SWAT team member started gulping for air until he fell forward onto the tile floor, a red puddle spread out beneath him. Thomas looked behind him and nodded at the window, he could see a white face and green hair for a second. "Hi dad." He heard the voice behind him. It was Bruce! "Sorry it took me so long, but I didn't want to have to splatter all those guys in front of mom y'know." His son's face finally came into full view, pale and thin. Green hair and red lips, Thomas never thought much of the look, but Bruce had always been a little quirky. "It's ok son, thanks for coming by. The rest of those boys went upstairs, why don't you go play with them?" "Sure thing, pops." Bruce smiled at him and put on two pairs of well-worn brass knuckles.

I stumbled in through the front door of my house. I was exhausted. And possibly slightly drunk. I fumbled with my keys as I took them out of the lock and dropped them, I shrugged and found my way into my room after closing the door behind me. "Fucking everything" I mumbled "Fucking life" I looked around my room frantically, I had to find it fast before I passed out. I began looking through my closet and as I did I remembered the day my father died. My mum died in a car crash when I was four so my dad was all I ever had. But of course he was taken away from me when I was twenty. I slammed the closet door shut and shambled over to my desk, moving papers and such around searching for it. As I did I thought about school. I was always a loner, always bullied and picked on. They all hated me. "I hated you pricks too for your information..." I muttered to myself as I spotted it in the corner of my room. I made my way over, grabbing the chair from my desk on the way before picking it up. "Here you were you little bastard." I smiled as I picked it up and clambered onto the chair, being careful not to fall off. I began attempting to tie it around the rafter above me. As I did I thought of my first girlfriend and the time we first kissed. Just past high school it was, standing in the rain we kissed and she looked at me and smiled so lovingly, she did that cute laugh of hers that she always did when I did something she liked. I hesitated for a moment. She told me eventually I'd never matted, I was always just a tool for her to get over her ex. I guess she never really loved me. "I always loved her though." I murmured. I finished tying the knots. I put my head through the noose. Not like I had anyone who'd care after all. No one who really loved me. Just before I kicked the chair out from underneath me I looked to the mirror beside me. Tears streaming down my face I croaked my final words. "For what it's worth..... I've always loved you."

Jaal ran through the rain with his hands over his head muttering the Prayer of Sadness as he felt God's Tears fall across his hood and robes. He was supposed to be inside during the High Fall, but he had news. Unfortunately, it was news that the High Priests would want to hear. As he rushed, he carefully avoided puddles, instead stepping across raised stones that were to be used in the event that the water flow became too heavy to cross. Many common people no longer followed the old superstitions of avoiding the Fallen Tears, but Jaal hoped to one day become a priest, and so he obeyed the more menial traditions. As he hopped across to the final stone onto the raised walkway, his foot slipped and splashed into the cold puddle of water at his feet. He immediately jerked his foot up shook it off as quickly as he could. Pausing, he got down on his hands and knees and leaned over the edge of the walkway. Opening his mouth, he allowed a dribble of spittle to slip out of his mouth into the flow below. Muttering a quiet Prayer of Apology he rose and quickly rushed under the shelter of the building. Quickly he stripped off his robes and began wringing them out into a small cistern that funneled the water back out into the main road. He had to be careful to bring as little water with him inside during a High Fall, when Hvalok's sadness would nearly overwhelm him, and the sky would stay black for days. " It is good to see the younger priests practicing the old teachings, " a voice muttered to his left. Jaal jerked his head to the left and saw Sunlord Paku'un standing in his yellow and blue robes. He immediately bowed deeply in a show of reverence at seeing one of the high priests outside the shelter. " Sunlord, should you not be inside, " Jaal asked as he dared to look up. " Hvalok weeps strongly today. " Sunlord Paku'un smiled, causing his face to turn into a portrait of wrinkles. " Perhaps Hvalok weeps strongly today so that he may grace us with a grey sky tomorrow. " Jaal suppressed a frown as he recalled the news he had to bring. " Sunlord, I have news for the other high priests. " Sunlord Paku'un frowned as he looked out across the black sky. " Can it not wait for tomorrow? We are not supposed to discuss business on a day of great mourning. " Jaal bowed his head and fluttered his hands down in a sign of reverence before looking up again, " Sunlord, it is news about the Burial Shroud. " The only way that Jaal was able to tell that Paku'un was startled was in the way his body stiffened as he heard the news. His face remained passive, the hint of a frown still present on his face. He looked out across the sky again before turning back to Jaal, " You are sure? " " The Stormwhisperer says that tonight Hvalok is going to finally bury his son and end the mourning period. " Paku'un's frown deepened, " How does he know this? " Jaal fluttered his hands down again in reverence before he whispered, " Because tomorrow, he hears no rain. " Sunlord Paku'un turned and walked away at that point, leaving Jaal thankful that he would not have to deliver the news to the other high priests himself. The bell began to ring as Paku'un moved through the temple towards the Sun Temple. He had told Jaal to go ring the bell for the meeting, and he was sure some of the priests would grumble, and perhaps not even put on their full uniform. He was, therefore, not surprised when he arrived and found only 2 other priests already present and waiting. The room itself was surprisingly small, but was extraordinarily tall. It extended roughly thirty meters into the air, and ended in a rounded roof with one large, and dozens of small holes covered in glass. The floor had an intricate carving of a ball with many tendrils spreading out across and up the walls. Along the walls, the color slowly transitioned from light blue to a soft, dark blue. " It is a High Fall today Paku'un, " said Himlar as he sat behind his desk. His beard was greased and shiny, and would maintain its shape through even the heaviest bout of Mourning. His hair was still black in many places, but a hint of grey was beginning to show underneath his skull cap. " And tomorrow it may be too late, " Paku'un said as he moved over to his own chair. " The Stormwhisperer has spoken again. " " Again? " asked Keel as she leaned forward in her chair. " The child has only spoken 5 times since he became the Stormwhisperer; four times to warn us of a High Fall, and once to tell us of the Day of Planting, when Hvalok does not weep so that we may plant crops. " " Yes, " Paku'un said as he took his seat. " And now he speaks again, but not to one of us? Who gave you this news? " " A young priest named Jaal. He follows the teachings strongly. " He frowned as he steepled his fingers in front of his face, " He would not lie to me. " He glanced at the other two, " But for now, we wait until the other four arrive. " The three sat in silence until Mikla, Nim, Opan, and Quirl all arrived and took their seats. Once they completed the rituals necessary to ask for forgiveness for meeting on a High Fall, Paku'un moved forward into the center of the room. He took a deep breath and said, " The Stormwhisperer has spoken again. " A quick murmur amongst the new arrivals occurred before almost immediately quieting down and allowing Paku'un to continue. " The Day of Burial is tomorrow. " The murmur erupted into a roar. " Tomorrow!? The High Fall just began yesterday, " said Quirl as he jumped up from his chair. " How can we be certain that tomorrow is the day? " " I agree, " said Nim as she twirled a strand of golden hair around her fingers. " However, we have known that Hvalok would one day stop mourning the death of his son. " " But today he weeps strongly, " Quirl protested as he glanced in Nim's direction. " Why would he weep so strongly today, but stop tomorrow? He has wept for over 300 years now. " " I have known men and women both to weep most strongly before the day they bury a child, " Paku'un said as he tried to calm the crowd. " Also, who are we to determine when Hvalok returns to his throne and replaces the yellow crown on his head? " " And the burial shroud? " Opan asked. " It is written that he will put back on his royal robes and the sky will once again be blue, " Nim said with a smile. " And Yin, " asked Mikla as he sat hunched up in his chair. A hush fell over the group as they turned to him, " What of Yin, the brother of Hvalok? What is going to happen to us when Yin retaliates? " " What are you implying, Mikla, " Paku'un asked. " Yin has had 300 years to plan his revenge for the attempt on his life. " Mikla stood and walked towards the center of the room, " He knows his brother wishes to rule both the day and the night. Plus, Yin has never forgiven Hvalok for secreting away with Gian and marrying her without telling him. " He frowned, " Sure, Yin later married Sian, and she bore him thousands of sons, but he had always loved Gian more. " " The point, Mikla, " said Opan as he frowned. " Sunlords, I fear that the day Hvalok, our creator, stops weeping, is the day that we should start. " [ rgrenadiere42 ] (http: )

It was night. It was always night when entering the palace and for the wayward son it was no different. Before it was night the son had stood outside for quite some time, studying the structure where it sat cradled among spires of ashen rock and obsidian that fell and rose from the mountainside like the impossible roots of some great, carnivorous tree. The broken limbs of a twisted and forgotten god. A city-temple abandoned. The building itself rested impotent and inert, its dark and crumbling outer walls giving the impression of a howl buried beneath trembling hands. It had been early when the wayward son had found the lost palace, the sun only just crowning above a horizon, yellow and blue. He was unsure if it was the right object of his search. The wayward son had moved closer and found the sun sunken, blood red and purple-black, like a too ripe fruit. He had moved closer and closer still until it was night and he had known it was the right place. The nameless and forgotten temple, the palace of the broken god, the city that drinks the sun. He had found it. The wayward son paused and stared up at the night sky to find it filled with strange and alien constellations, stars he'd never seen before. The lights whirred and moved with impossible speed at the periphery of his vision, rewriting the sky into an inky tale of undying death and nameless beings. The wayward son shivered and gripped the handle of his sword. The wayward son entered the palace. Inside, the city seemed half way grown. There was a roughness to the architecture as if it had been, not chiseled or built, but eaten into design. The hallways spiralled in seeming endlessness, converging into themselves and forming great cavernous walkways. The floors were a polished onyx but quivered with the dust and ash of undisturbed centuries. The wayward son felt eyes, cold and alien, peering at him from the shadows. When he stopped and looked, he found nothing. It was as if he was watched by eyes removed, not by the distance of the rooms he trod, but by strange and weird eons, as if unseen things observed him from across a vast cavern of time. The wayward son came finally to the altar room, a gaping maw of a hall. So cavernous was it that looking up he could not see the ceiling. A coolness like autumn wind floated across his face. He did not draw his blade but instead moved further into the dark. The wayward son did not carry a torch, he had long since trained his eyes to discern between shadow and true darkness. He had trained a great many things in preparation of this moment. All around him sat shadows, spilt like blood across mossy floor and crumbled walls. Before him, at the end of the cavern where he knew the altar should sit was darkness. True darkness. The darkness saw him. He felt its eyes move upon him like thick coagulated rot. The wayward son felt the dark and broken god, the defeated demon, rumble and shake from out the shroud of dreams it slumbered within. The wayward son lowered his hand from the hilt of his reforged sword, once three blades and now one, he looked up into the deformed god's unseen eyes, into true darkness, into the empty void of an undying thing and spoke. 'Hello father.'

I tried to turn the classic elevator love story in a bit more satisfying direction. Sorry if it's a bit incomprehensible, I was slowly drifting off to sleep as I wrote. Stewart ran across the countless steps to the elevator, while a brown case and a plastic tubular dangled on his side. Stronghold Technologies didn't have very strict rules - but you had to be at your work place on time, or a warning from the higher-ups was imminent. Stewart didn't have any significant violations behind him, but that was only because he always managed to get to his floor at the last minute. Punctual or not, New York traffic jams never bothered with such details, and could stomp around the morning city for hours. Nevertheless, the man was ready for the challenge. This time he was lucky, as the elevator had already opened his welcoming doors and stood there, waiting for him, just like it always did. He was twice as lucky, as he saw Melinda in there. Melinda worked on 27th floor, just a couple of floors below him. Another promising young soul in the glassy heart of the biggest metal producer in America. Melinda had a black business suit, a long ponytail, and her usual square glasses on. Stewart always reminded himself to buy the same modern, slick glasses, as his round cheek-warmers were already a couple decades out of style when he bought them. But, just like always, there always were more pressing matters at hand. Besides, they looked somewhat in place with his wardrobe. He called it "Engineer's Classics in Brown." His friends called it "Stop Being Such a Cheapskate." Junior Designer ran into the elevator, and almost dropped his baggage on the floor, as he tried to retake the breath, lost on the way from the bus. Melinda just barely glanced at him and pressed the button for her floor, as Stewart took a stronger hold of his possessions and tried to straighten his clothes. He looked in the mirror. Good thing he had the time to shave his uncertain beard. Most of the times it hid in his chin, certain to never grow into a beautiful substitute for manliness. But during the busy weeks, it tended to rise a bit and look outside, just enough to make him look like a raging drunkard. As he turned back to the elevator doors, his mind completely shut itself from all the beard-related problems, or the general problems of any kind. He was completely lost in Melinda. He worked for the company for about a year already, and throughout it, Melinda was his own personal haven. A drop of fresh water between the windy desert of morning commute, and Antarctic coldness of his daytime routine. Her brown ponytail was tied almost at the top of her head, and her sharp glasses only made her small face warmer by contrast. Even though she was standing with her face to the door, he could remember every feature on her face. Stewart tried to strike a conversation with her every time they met, but he never quite managed to force the words out of his mouth. Suddenly, his eyes narrowed and his arms almost clenched into fists. This was a familiar feeling. He'd often get it at night, just as he drifted off to sleep. A desire to change things. A desire to achieve something significant. A desire to win. It was the first time he would experience it in the middle of the day, and it made him drop his tubular to the elevator floor. Melinda turned to him. -Are you alright? -Yeah, thanks. Just a bit tired from the road. The traffic. It's horrible, you know - Stewart replied. He almost physically had to tear his sight from her face. -Yes, it surely is - she replied, while slowly turning back to the door. The next five stories flashed in complete silence. Stewart felt the call for action again. This time, he managed to get a hold of himself. -Say, Melinda..... - he started, and she turned to him -Yes? -You know..... - just as he wanted to start some awkward small talk, while elevator crawled to their floors, and they continued on with their weary lives, his mind almost snapped. He didn't know what that was - perhaps, a distant call of his ancient relatives, who didn't wish for the timely demise of their dynasty - or, more likely, an adrenaline rush from the morning marathon, but his words stuck in his throat, and instead, new ones came out. -There is a new pizza place at the corner behind the tower. Do you want to go there with me? Just as he said it, his sudden rush was gone. He was back with his usual self, and this self was completely lost, as to what to do next. His legs started shaking, and he suddenly understood what a perfect mess he did. There was no return. No more safe havens. No more quite rides in an elevator next to a nice colleague. No more Melinda. He quietly wept for his failures for five other stories, while Melinda stood quietly, with her back still turned to him. On the 22nd floor, she suddenly and sharply turned. Her face was bright red, and her hands gripped into her purse. She looked right through him. " This is it " - something shouted in Stewarts head - " This is the end ." -Yes. Yes, yes, I'm..... - Melinda paused, while finding his eyes, but then suddenly looked to the side - I'd like to, yes. It'd be nice..... Yes - She nodded at the last moment, leading a complete count of yesses to five. Stewart didn't bother with a response. He simply stared at her, perhaps, a bit impolite, but it was understandable, considering the fact that his brain was busy with overloading sensors. Sensors were somehow still sure he was going to hunt, mate, or die - perhaps, all at the same die - so they kept all possible responses from coming from his mouth. He tried to say " okay ," but instead, he squeaked like a mouse, and decided to keep it shut. Meanwhile, elevator creeped to floor 24. -Let's meet at six o'clock, down in the hall, alright? - Melinda said, finally watching him straight in the eyes. -Yes. Yes. Let's do it. - Stewart added, like she was the one who proposed it. Melinda stared at him for another floor. Then she leaned closer to him. Then she kissed him. Then she snapped back, and turned to the door, fast enough to almost knock her head on it. They stayed completely motionless for another floor, while her ears were getting deeper and deeper shades of red. Then she murmured something. Stewart somehow heard it from behind his shock, and even had enough willpower to ask: -What? -I said, I was getting tired of holding the elevator for you every damn morning. - She responded quietly, like she was hoping he still wouldn't hear it. Suddenly, the elevator doors opened, and Melinda stormed out of the elevator, like it was on fire. The doors waited for a second, hoping someone else would exit, but then closed back with a quiet, unsatisfied " clunk ." Elevator started moving down, as Stewart remembered that he forgot to press the button for his floor. It didn't matter.

My mother, with her glass of red, and brother with his glass of beer sat across the table from me, with a glass of milk. When the clock struck twelve I would be a man, old enough to weigh up the pros and cons of drinking alcohol and make a responsible decision. But my mum and brother had already take that decition for me. When the clock struck 11:59 champaigne would be poured to celebrate the fact that I am 18. A man. I would have responsibilities. Christmas eve had always been more exciting that the night before my birthday. I guess it's because it is an event everyone takes part in. You get presents for both, but Christmas there is a true build up. But nothing prepares you for your 18th. The gift you receive upon becoming an adult defines your adult life. Telekinesis? Laborer. Faster than a speeding bullet? Delivery man. The glasses were raised on the count of five, they were clinking together to my health at two. I had my first taste of booze at midnight. And I felt nothing good. I knew that my brother was jealous. He didn't know what my power would be, he didn't care as long as it wasn't as useful as his. My mother was worried. Maybe I would be the same as my father..... My father! He hadn't be hit by a car. He'd killed himself. And she worried about the same fate befalling me. I didn't want to worry my mum, so I said that I felt no different.'Alcohol is the same when it's legal' I said with a nervous laugh. All I could feel was their fear and insecurities. It was horrible. And it didn't stop. Telekinesis? Laborer. Faster than a speeding bullet? Delivery man. Mind reader? Driven from society by the viciousness that lies in the heart and mind of every man, woman and child.

The building was alight with an ethereal energy, golden sunlight bathing the room in warmth. For a small coffee house it was bustling. Contented chatter hung in the air as the inhabitants sat sipping their drinks. The queue ran from the end of the counter along it's length, past the identical wooden tables and chairs arranged in front of the glassed facade of the building, and nearly to the door. The line shuffled along the wood laminate flooring as one by one the customers ordered, paid, and collected their refreshments. He joined the back of the queue, basking in the warmth of the day; the crisp and biting chill of the wind couldn't take away from the glorious sun in here. His vision swam back into focus from the nirvana he was floating in, and back into the room he inhabited. Scanning the room he saw the usual cross-section of society one might expect to find in a coffee shop; old couples and young couples, business men with their papers, and groups of friends chatting and laughing. The line was shorter now, although the room no more full, and the noise no less harmonic. Even over the hiss of milk being steamed, the whirring crunch of coffee being ground, and the chirp of voices he still managed to be startled by the door swinging open. Turning towards the door the room fell silent for a moment, the air seemingly standing still for the new arrival. She was a young woman of maybe twenty or so, although her features made her look younger. Big blue eyes shone in the late afternoon sun, reflecting as much light as the straight blonde hair that fell to her shoulders. Brighter still was her smile though, a mischievous grin that lingered for a second before fading to a simper. He caught her eye for just a second before they both shot their gazes to elsewhere. The hubbub of noise in the room was as loud as ever, but he couldn't hear it. His mind reeled with ways to engage her in conversation, ideas tried, rejected, and tried again. He felt all his energy, both nerves and excitement, rise within him as he turned to her. "Hey" he beamed to her with an easy, if somewhat eager, smile. "Hey." His smile was met coyly with one in return. The connection felt unreal, there was no fear, no worries of rebuttal, just a pure, uninhibited sense of ease with each other. Conversation flowed like liquid gold wrapped in silk as they whiled away the wait in the queue. Together they approached the counter. "What do you want?" he offered gently "I'm not sure, what would you recommend?." He poured over the menu hung behind the counter, searching for the ideal suggestion, wanting for the choice, as insignificant as it was, to be perfect. Item after item seemed too imperfect before he saw what he had been looking for. "Ah great, yeah we'll have two-." A siren cut him off. He looked at the barista for help but was met with an equally perplexed expression. The room grew enormously brighter and he turned, to find the spot where the girl had been an incandescent white which blazed for a fraction of a second before collapsing into the room as it was before, sans girl. He struggled to grasp what had happened, the girl he had met, possibly the most beautiful he'd seen, and by far the most spiritually connected he'd ever encountered, was gone. Looks of trepidation filled the room as the occupants took in what had happened. The golden sunlight began to fade and the room darkened, turning grey from sepia. One by one the people in the room vanished, the most hidden away went first. The room emptied, the line's inhabitants popping in to nothing one at a time. Only a few people from him, and the world outside the window ceased to exist, in it's place a void. The line shortened until it reached him. He waited for it. He didn't know what to expect but he stood there, eyes locked with the barista, just waiting to go. He didn't. Instead the barista did, and so too did the chairs, and tables, and walls, and just about everything until it was just him. Staring at his hands he could begin to see through them, into the dismal grey void beyond. He faded as the last memories of the dream were washed away with the bleak grimness of another morning she couldn't face.

Sean was walking home from the gardening store, he loved getting new utensils. His birthday was spent as it usually was, Dad carrying in his broken down car from his 24 hour shift as a security guard before falling asleep without saying happy birthday and Sean playing hide and seek in their garden with his Mommy. Her power was invisibility but Sean got the hang of noticing flattened grass and bent flowers. When he first found out his power his Mom told him all the good he can do in the world, that never before has a power like this been. Sean didn't believe that. The other kids at school picked on him, called him names and made him regret he ever told anyone his power. Taking the left turn from the main street into an alleyway as he always did on a Tuesday after the garden store Sean strolled right into the immovable palm of Billy Smith. "Hey bee boy, whats in the bag? Toys for your little garden? Let me see them." said Billy with a devious smile on his face. "Just leave me alone Billy, I am walking home, my parents are expecting me" pleaded Sean only now noticing the other boys behind Billy. "You know Spark and Razor don't you?" questioned Billy as the boys behind him gave Sean a glimpse of their powers. Spark created a stream of electricity from both his hands while Razor morphed his into to immaculate blades. "Yeah they are in my Maths class." said Sean as calmly as he could whilst remembering all the shocks he got, all the tiny slits he received and the name, the names were the worst. "Do you know my name bee boy?" asked Billy. "Its..... its Bill." is all Sean could get out. "WRONG!" Billy yelled as he picked Sean up by the scruff of the neck with one hand. "They call me Herc, short for Hercules. They say I am going to be the strongest of all the supers. I could pound your Daddy into the pavement, when the drunk isn't passed out there already" chuckled Billy as Sean began to tear up. "Stop crying, we are just messing with you. And speaking of messing let us play with those toys" exclaimed Billy as he grabbed Seans bag with his free hand and then threw Sean to the ground. The new shovel Sean saved up for was crushed into a toothpick by Billy's tectonic plate grip. The seeds for the rose plants Sean was going to grow for his Mom, turned to dust by Spark. The pots Sean bought were thrown into the air and sliced into tiny pieces by razor. Sean could not contain his sadness and rage any longer. "STOP!! I AM WARNING YOU!" bellowed Sean as he pointed straight at Billy. Fabricated into reality around his hand were several small bumblebees flying towards Billy. The three boys glanced at each other, back to Sean and then burst into unrelenting laughter. "The bee queen has spoken!!! Ohh no, he is going to sting us!!!! The only thing he will ever fertilize is a flower!!!" repeated the three boys in unison. Sean felt like he shouldn't have said anything and went fetal. Billy picked him up to his feet. "Well!!! You were saying something bee boy?" grunted Billy as he slowly pushed Sean back with a single pointed finger one nudge at a time. "Well?" push. "It sounded like you threatened us" push. "Didn't he threaten us boys?" push. "You gon na throw some more bees at us your majesty?" one final push that knocked Sean stumbling backwards. He regained his composure and clenched both fists. The anger was growing in his face, the anger was the only thing holding back the tears in Sean's face. The words of the bullies echoing through his very being. The bullies just stood there laughing. Sean didn't think this was funny at all. "Leave me alone" Sean mumbled. "Did he just buzz?" roared Razor with laughter and the others promptly joined in. "LEAVE!!! ME!!! ALONE!!!!" Sean roared as he threw both fists forward opening both hands. It all happened so fast. Sean only grasped what had happened when he saw Billy throwing haymaker punches knocking chunks out of the walls of the alleyway. Sean had summoned a swarm of Africanised bees. Spark and Razor took off sprinting at the sight of the swarm. Billy was not so fortunate. All the strength he had was not enough to fight this foe. His skin started to blister and bloat, his eyes swelled and his footing was lost. The bees began to disperse once his body stopped moving. Sean saw the reality of what just happened. He sat down in the alleyway next to Billy's body. Unbearable sadness overcame Sean. "All you had to do was leave me alone........ I begged you" whispered Sean as he sobbed alone with Billy dead next to him.

It's December 11th today. All day today, as it's been most days, my thoughts have been of you, and how I've hurt the one person who's loved me unconditionally, the mother of my beloved son, and the person I promised the rest of my life to. It would have been 10 years today. I broke that promise. I regret it every single day. Falling for you was easy. You're perfect. Finding myself was not. Is not. And it's not your fault, Lord knows I've blamed everybody else, but I can't ever blame you. I still don't know where I am or where I'm headed. I know is it's led me to the temptation that resulted in this. I do know that I am working towards a way I can be of some use to you, to ease your burden and be a good father to our son. I'm not breaking this promise, babe. I repeat it to myself every morning. Hang in there, please. I was blind, and couldn't see how great I had it. My heart hurt from my failures and I felt like I might taint you and Nathan with them if I couldn't somehow fix it. I was selfish, and thought only of myself when I decided to entertain thoughts that should never have entered my mind. I insulted you, your whole family, and US. I don't deserve the civility you still show me. Please know that I love you with all my heart. You are an angel I didnt deserve. Please know that I don't stop trying to ease your burden, and I don't stop planning to be back for our son. One day it won't be a plan anymore. I'm so close. Sometimes all I want to do is share it with you, my best friend. I don't know how to thank you for all you've done, so I've just been rambling on. You're in my thoughts and my heart today, and always. He is amazing, and it's because of you.

The thing flowed out of the canister and drifted over the ground towards him. It appeared as if a small oil-slick colored like the night sky, myriad twinkling stars included, was sliding closer. Small tendrils periodically reached out from the central body and experimentally prodded at the rocks and twigs in its path - they seemed autonomous. James, wishing he could take a step back in horror, found himself frozen in an emotion that could only be described as the bastard child of morbid-curiosity and utter horror. He watched, eyes wide, as the thing came to a halt only a few feet before him. For a few moments the surface of the oil-slick sputtered and bubbled, and then bubbled more rapidly. The sound of soft popping and slopping eventually started to form a pattern. He listened, not out as much out of confusion or curiosity, but because he legs were still frozen in fear. Pop pop-op, slosh-pop, pop-gargle, popopello, Hellop, Hello? He blinked and thought about looking around for the speaker before realizing that the sound of perfectly pronounced British English had come from the creature itself. "Are...," was all he managed to say. "Pop..... I'll wait. " , the dark puddle said calmly. Confusion was starting to become James' primary emotion for the moment. He stuttered, "Y-you'll..... wait? " , he asked dumbly. The creature replied quickly, "Yes? This is..... pop, the right language, correct?" It sloshed around a bit as it'spoke'. The fear, rapidly replaced by utter confusion, subsided enough for the man to run a hand nervously through his hair, "Uhm..... Are you British?" The creature vibrated. It made no sound, but he saw the reflection of the moon wiggling softly on it's watery surface. Laughing, perhaps? "Do I look British to you? " , it replied smoothly. "No..... not really. " , he replied sheepishly. "I am partial to this language, is all. The stereotypes associated with it are often benevolent - This helps with first contact." "So, you're an alien then? " , he finally managed to take a single step away from it. The puddle moved a step closer to him in response. "Do I look like an alien to you? " , it gargled. James nodded his head'yes'. "Excellent! Your eyes seem to have evolved correctly after all. Pfft, British," it scoffed and continued a bit too cheerfully, "I am an alien, in fact! Go on, then, ask away." The man stood for a moment and then replied thoughtfully, "Why are you here?" "To take you home." "Home?" "Yes, home." "But, this..... " ..... is your home? Not really." James looked a bit flustered, "Uh, yes it is, Mr. Alien." "Just'Alien' is fine. And, no..... It's not. pop." He decided to try the exact same angle again, "Uh, yes? It is." The oil slick let out a sound that was somewhere between a sigh and the sound of air escaping out of an inflatable pool toy, "Nope. " , it simply said. "Okay, then..... This isn't going anywhere fast. " , he shrugged. One entity stood awkwardly in silence. The other sat awkwardly in a puddle on the ground. Finally the puddle spoke up. "Science lesson time! " , it said happily, "What is DNA?" James blinked, and not wanting to look silly in front of the alien replied quickly, "The stuff that makes us us." "Indeed! And what if I told you that I, too, had DNA? gargle" "Well, that wouldn't be too weird, right? Life is life." "Indeed! And what if I told you that I was your cousin?" The man looked amused, "Yes, but..... You're not." "How do you know?" "My father was an only child." "Not literally!" It sounded exasperated, "We share the same DNA though." "We do? " , he asked skeptically. "Indeed! Your..... archaic form was only given to you to assist your survival in the Machi-I-Lauvian plains, er..... Sorry, Africa. Do you know what we call ourselves?" James smiled, "Blobs?" "Rude! No, we call ourselves humans. Just like you." Such information was a bit overwhelming and thus the man took a moment to process, "You..... I..... You want to make me look like you?" "Not unless you want. It's optimal, of course. Frictionless, mobile..... James interuppted, , blobby? No way. So, why are you..." "Back? Well, that's a bit of a long story..... In summary: War." "I'm going to need a better explanation than that. " , he said suspiciously. It sighed an airy sigh, "We almost went extinct. We put some of our kind on this planet, changed their form to assist survival and hiding, and went off on our way to try to survive. Luckily, we won the war. Had we lost? At least we'd continue to live in some way or form on Anikeou-I-Laum..... err, Earth." James was a bit startled to found that he accepted this explanation quite easily, "I see. " , he said simply. "Well, come on then! You don't have to come - just an option. Lets go a round a few orbits, shall we? Think about it. " , it bubbled as a person-sized opening appeared at the side of the spherical silver canister. "Well, alright then...," James said uncertainly and began to follow the sliding, drifting puddle towards the ship.

Dear Margaret, I began. I can't live this life anymore. I simply can't do this anymore. Every day I thought I just needed to push a little harder, last a little longer, and eventually I'd get better. I never did. I never have. It's not your fault. Please don't blame yourself. It's no one's fault but my own. This is my chance to do at least one thing right in my life. Love, Dave. It was short. I had originally planned on writing pages of pages of prose, pouring out my emotions onto the paper for my dearest Margaret. I realized though, after my 23rd attempt, that no amount of ink could ever convey the sense of hopelessness and worthlessness I felt. She had been the only light in my life. With her, I felt purpose. I felt fire. But in the end, it wasn't enough. When my hands were warmed by her touch, my back froze in the cold grip of my depression. I knew she would be hurt by my passing. But perhaps she would see me as a hero. That's all I ever wanted. I left the note on the desk. She would get home from work, and she'd see it as soon as she sat down to write, after a cup of tea to relax. "Dave Miller?" I looked up to see a beautiful young reception, smiling sweetly down at me. "Can you come with me?" I stood up, smiling feebly. She was a short little thing. She reminded me of Margaret when she was young and full of energy. Margaret still had that energy, though it had changed from when we were young. It was now a calm, patient energy. No longer was it directed in bursts of action like when we were younger, dancing and making love with an air of excitement as we avoided being caught. I remembered all the times we had been almost caught. My smooth talking and silver tongue had got us out of many a pickle then, and her innocent smile certainly helped. Now, she was more like burning embers. Giving warmth, but slowly and silently. I would miss her. If such a thing was possible, in some sort of afterlife. This young receptionist guided me down the long white hallways. Each step hung another weight on my heart. My chest felt tight, and I gulped. There was no turning back. There still could be, that had been made quite clear to me, but I had told myself I would not back down. No matter who I met, I would save them. She explained how the procedure would work. I wasn't listening. I had tuned out to think more on Margaret. I began to doubt my decision, but I told myself that this was something I had to do. "You'll get to meet your receiver. Then either you or your partner will have the option of back out. You can take as much time as you need to get acquainted. Once you're ready to begin, we can start the procedure. It is completely painless, don't worry. You'll simply fall asleep and never wake up again." She smiled. "But you'll be giving someone else a chance at life." I nodded absently. Finally, she stopped in front of a door. This was it. She pulled a clipboard off the wall. "Dave Miller...... Dave..... Miller." She suddenly gasped, bringing a hand to her mouth. She looked up at me. "It is Miller?" I nodded, frowning in concern. She shook her head. "I'm so sorry..... can we reschedule, perhaps? We can I interrupted her. "I don't care who I'm saving. I'd like to do this now." She gulped before slowly nodded. "Very..... very well, sir." I reached forwards, grabbing hold of the cold, metal handle. I pulled, and with a creak the heavy door swung open. I stepped inside, ready to meet my partner. I gasped, eyes widening in shock at what..... at who I saw. "M-Margaret?" I don't do writing prompts that often (because I'm both busy and lazy), but I think I'm a fairly decent writer. What do you guys think?

God I'm starving. Thank fuck she seems pretty calm, a little confused. I think there's a McDonald's up ahead. We might be fine going through the drive through. In the dim lights from the street lamps the girls face looked sleepy. Her chubby cheeks were red from the winter air, but she was probably warm now in the car. "Can we go inside? I want to play on the- on the play pen." Her voice wasn't harsh and desperate like kids who only rarely are allowed to do something they love. Good. Her parent's probably love her. Probably cater to her every insignificant whim. She is pretty calm. "Yeah. And - if you're a good girl and do as you're told, you can have whatever you want to eat too." She didn't react much to that. I should soften my voice a bit. "Deal, Jenna?" "Ohhkay," the girl responded, with a little smile. The snow crunches a bit as we park. We run inside together, I grab Jenna's hand. I order a McDouble, and she orders two chocolate chip cookies. Takes probably a minute before our food is up. "Can I get milk too?" Jenna asks, halfway through the first cookie with melted chocolate all over her fingers. "Sure, hold on." I purchase the milk and come back, keeping one eye on her the whole time. I sit back down and open the plastic lid. "Are you my new daddy?" "N- no. I'm not your new dad. You're daddy misses you very much, he'll be happy once you're home." "No he won't. He's not my dad." She shoved some more cookie in her mouth. "I don't want him." Kids. They always hate their parents from time to time, especially when the parents don't give them anything real to worry about. At her age I'd have been happy to have anyone to call a father. "Well, your mommy will definitely miss you." Jenna looked down at her cookies unhappily. Her eyes reddened and welled up, and her chin dimpled as she frowned. Shit. "It's okay! You'll see her soon, I promise. I'm just taking care of you for a couple days while your mommy and daddy put together a special surprise for you!..... You're going to love it!" I don't think she heard me really. She keeps getting redder. Cheeks, eyes, lips - all bright red. "Nobody loves me. I'm just a stupid idiot." Six year old, adorable privileged girls don't normally talk that way. "Are there mean girls at school telling you that? You know what you could say to them?" "No." "You can tell them to shove it up their twats." The mental image of this adorable girl chewing out the mean girls seemed precious. "Nooo. It's not girls, it's mommy." Tears began streaming down her cheeks after she couldn't hold them back any longer. Those fuckers. Who calls little kids names like that? Well, aside from teaching them to call each other that. But that's self defense. Mean girls deserve that. And I guess it's not that uncommon, my parent's did it. "My parent's used to call me that too." Jenna looked up. "Have some more cookie! It's gon na get cold!" "It already is cold." Jenna sounded like the most miserable creature in the world. "Okay, hold on, I'll get it heated up again." I grab the cold cookie and take it back to the counter. The clerk rolls her eyes at me as she turns away to put it back into the oven. I watch as Jenna sips some milk. The cookie comes out pretty hot. I walk slowly back to the booth so it'll cool a bit. "Here you go! One nice, warm cookie!" Jenna looks much calmer, but the redness remains in her face. She accepts the cookie and begins to alternate bites of cookie with sips of milk. I wait for her to finish quietly, unsure of what else to say or do. We clean up (Jenna picks up her own trash) and go back to the truck. I recline her seat as much as I can and turn up the heat so she can go to sleep. We have a bit of a drive ahead of us.

"I've only seen the mens ones and they were okay. I mean how good is a bathroom is when there's one of those guys there watching you go? It's like I'm paying to have stage fright. I'm not sure whether she heard me since she just seems to be staring at me, I should repeat myself. She's the one..... she won't mind, right? "I said "Yeah I heard what you said. She seems genuinely sorry. "Can I be honest with you?" "Sure." She stares at me once more, expectantly now. I relish in her interest. "So I know this might be weird and you might think I'm on drugs, or mentally ill, but I'm not - on drugs that is, and I don't think I'm mentally ill..." Her eyes widen. " ..... I'm not mentally ill. But I stop and look at her. She's beautiful, she's smart and above all else she's still here. If I can't impress her with honesty what can I impress her with? "Time stopped my future self told me you were the one. That's why I'm so nervous, I was scared I'd somehow manage to mess things up with you. I realise this ironic." "Okay." She begins to drink. "Okay?" "Why do you think I'm still here? After the third story about you getting your ass handed to you by children I was starting to think she was full of shit." "She?" "My future self." She laughs. I laugh. "So what did she look like?" I ask. "Darker hair, wears glasses, apparently I work out more in the future so I guess that's cool." "Mine had a beard and a tattoo." "I could see you with a beard." She smiles "what was the tattoo? I had one too!" I try to remember. "It was small, but it was like a black snorlax under an umbrella." Her eyes light up. "Hold on! Is it..... this?" From her bag she grabs her phone and unlocks it, sliding it in front of my face. I notice her wallpaper. "Yes! What is it?" "It's from a film. "Are you okay?" It's Sandy. Oh god. Half the skin of her face has been ripped off, revealing the muscle underneath. Teeth, embedded in gums. She smiles, and the muscle tears a little more, bleeds a little more. I'm going to be sick. I look away, just to keep myself from gagging. "Yeah," I say. I'm pretty sure my leg is broken. That's okay though. That's okay. I sit up and almost scream from the pain, my hip, something, not going to think about it right now. Just get into a sitting position. "C'mere," I say, and she moves in closer, and I give her a hug. When I pull back her face is stitched together, clear-skinned, beautiful as ever. "Help me up," I say. "I need to get to the others." She nods, doesn't argue. Good girl. I lean on her heavily. Trying to avoid putting any weight on the leg. I'm going to pass out, there's so much pain. Got to keep going though. Need to..... Need to fix people. Bob, weaving towards us. Oh god, maggots. He's crawling with maggots. Eating their way in and out of him. "Hey!" Sandy waves to him. A maggot drips from Bob's nose, falls to the ground. His hands are coming apart like globs of cottage cheese as he waves back. "Andrew," he says. "How am I doing?" "Nothing I can't handle," I reassure him. I'm trying to sound unfazed but it's so hard, when the only thing keeping me from dry heaving the nonexistent contents of my stomach is reciting the multiplication tables backwards. Every cell of my body cringing I reach out and touch him, and the maggots melt away, fading into flesh, normal, human. Bob blinks. "Oh wow, that was amazing," he says. "One day you need to explain to me how you can do that." "Sure, some day" I say, which means never. There's other people screaming though, so we're moving again, me hobbling along, Sandy supporting me. Psych viruses, goddamn psych viruses driving people mad, and me the only one who can somehow see and remove the infection. So we're moving. Moving. I touch another person, and another person. The pain, from my hip, it's growing, it's radiating upwards. I'm on fire, I'm being eaten alive. Just a few more hours, though, then the proper CDC gets here. "Andrew," Sandy says, yanking me back from the daze I've drifted into. "Andrew are you okay?" "What?" I say, blinking at her, stupefied. "Yes, yes I'm okay. I'm..... I'm okay." But she's gently bending downwards, settling me down, propped up. "No," she says, "are you OKAY?" I look down at my stomach. Bright green gas seeps from gaping open blue wounds. Infected. Oh god. Oh god. Oh god. I stare up at her, desperate. Her eyes are filling with tears. So, I realize, are mine. " ..... No, "I whisper. The world floods purple.

As an interstellar journalist, Vilaramd felt an obligation to report the news from within the chaos of events. Which was how he'd found himself on a battlefield, surrounded by bodyguards and soldiers under the command of a Human woman known as Captain Fierro. " They're falling back, keep pushing! " the woman yelled. Around her, the guns of her soldiers threw streaks of light that cut down the enemy combatants. Vilaramd felt his stomachs begin to curl, yet he couldn't stop watching. These people tore through the Insurrectionists with brutal yet impressive efficiency. He never had any doubt about his people's decision to hire the Humans for the purpose of quelling the unrest in the Empire. Even so, he often found them...unnerving. The Insurrectionists were routed back to a single fortress, where the Humans'massive war vehicles bathed the walls in fire. A six-hour siege was all it took to wipe out the last vestige of the enemy's influence in this star system. Shortly afterward, Vilaramd joined the Captain as she walked through the rubble, surveying the teams in charge of clean-up and salvage. " I...don't know what to say, " he commented. " This was my first time being in the heat of one of your battles. Thank you for the generous protection, by the way. " Fierro gave him a half smile and nodded. " Wasn't much of a burden, Vilaramd. We had more than enough troops to spare. These Insurrectionists were a lot less...deadly than your people implied. " " To you, maybe, " he replied with a nervous chuckle. " They're capable of such violence...to this day it still alarms me. Seeing the handiwork of your military today, I'm glad to have you on our side. " " Military? " Fierro asked, raising an eyebrow. " Yes. Ah...is there a different word you prefer? " " No, it's just...we do have a military, but...we're not it. " Vilaramd stopped in his tracks and stared at the woman. How had such a major piece of information avoided his notice? " But we hired you as a military force. " " Yes, but we're not the Terran Military. Just a private mercenary group. " " What?! " He grabbed his tablet and began typing with excitement. " Do the authorities know about this? " " Of course. They wanted us for a ' trial run'of sorts. Cheaper than getting the actual Terran military. But after what we've done these past few months, I'm sure your people will go all in for the big guns. I'm kind of sad that we'll be losing the job. " Fierro started to laugh. " Oh man, if you think we kicked ass, wait ' til you see what our Navy does to those Insurrectionist bastards. " Vilaramd's hands paused above his screen. " Like what? " Fierro stared at the sky for a moment, seeming to ponder. " Ever seen a supernova up close? "
