"We've been over this already. We can't be off gallivanting past the Dracon Mountains, it's more than a months ride away! Anyone who needs or help will surely have gotten it or moved on," Broxi was struggling to be heard over the cacophony inside The Toothless Orc. The tavern had a cosy feel to it, which is to say that it was a miracle they could find a seat in the "quiet section" as the barkeep had called it. "And besides, we don't want to help too many people. Did you hear what happened to Sonwar, that fishing town? They started doing alright and then BOOM! Battle priests everywhere!" Broxi received disapproving looks from her companions. They hadn't been together long, but it was long enough for learning each others sore spots. "So you're..... you're suggesting we don't do the adventuring and the..." Jopal looked for the next word at the bottom of his flagon, "Killing!" he decided. "That's my favourite part!" Lopaj slammed his fist down on the already battered table. It dawned on Broxi that their lack of creativity was clearly genetic. Who names their twins Jopal and Lopaj? "And we got ta get the priests back! They ruined my home town!" "And mine!" Jopal was not the brains of the two. Broxi stood up, she wasn't riddled with muscles like the twins but she stood a head taller because of her heritage. Her tusks drew imposing shadows across her face in the light of the tavern. "Don't assume you're the only one who's hurt by the High King." She thanked the gods that her tusks hid her watering eyes. Broxi had just come of age when her small horde had been assimilated into the Kingdom of Tirith. Her people had been butchered, forced into slavery, used as cannon fodder. With the kings expansion settling down, she wasn't the only one with dreams of revenge but High King Keless ruled with an iron fist. "Look, if you're'unna stay here, I'm leaving. And I'll be taking my brother with me." Lopaj stood to leave and looked a Jopal. "Y-yeah! Me too!" Jopal chugged the rest of his ale and nearly fell as he stood. Together the twins marched through the crowd towards the door, leaving Broxi alone with her thoughts and the pile of help wanted notices on the table. Broxi watched as her only guards walked out of The Toothless Orc and out of her life. She slumped back onto her stool and took small sips of her remaining drink while scanning the room for some travelling companions. She didn't want to stay here, it was too close to the seat of the empire and she was worried what she'd do. At least she didn't have to argue with Tweedle Dee and Tweedle Dickhead anymore. "Excuse me, is this seat taken?" Without waiting for an answer, the hooded stranger sat. "What're you doing with all those hmm?" The stranger quickly brushed his hands over the requests to kill basement rats and collect bear pelts. "I uh..... I'm uh..." Broxi wasn't going to tell her life story to a stranger, but she didn't quite know what to say. There wasn't really a plan, and she was normally much more proactive in choosing how to start a conversation. The stranger lifted his hood to reveal a plain face, "I'm "You're the bastard who got Sonwar razed," the realisation rushed over her. It was Hayr, the High King's old messenger. "I should "I know. I made a terrible mistake. But I need help setting it right, and you look like you've got just as much to lose as I do," he slid another drink to her across the table. "I've left my wife, I was rewarded depressingly well for my..... advice OK?" Hayr continued. Broxi took a slow sip, not taking her eyes of the man responsible for the eradication of not only an entire town but half the food of the surrounding province. "She'll survive without me and my daughter won't have to know what I've become but I need help setting things right. The empire is fucked, and so is everyone if there isn't a king whose sane on the throne." The tavern started to slow down, people were whispering and pointing to the man talking quickly in the back to the orc lady. "I can explain on the way but I have a quest and I think you can help me." The poor guy was helpless, even the alcohol couldn't hide that from Broxi. Given the options before her did she have any choice? It's not like she had anything going on at the moment. So they left together. Hayr had provided Broxi with a horse. The didn't need a pack horse either, Hayr packed exceedingly light and Broxi had minimal supplies after the twins took off with almost everything. She laughed at the absurdity of everything that had just happened, a deep laugh, one she hadn't used in years. Toppling an empire should be an easy quest, compared to escorting some fisherman. - Constructive criticism welcome, more like this at rdacriawrites.

I have determined that you have no heart, no soul. Maybe I shouldn't have waited so long to write this to you, but I shouldn't have had to. You've seen me, watched the way I act around you. You can't even begin to pretend that you didn't know that I have loved you for years. Has that mattered to you? No. Not one bit. No, instead you have taken advantage of my kindness and affection for you, and you have abused my emotions and my desires to the point of no return. I was there for you when you needed help so many times, fixed your car, gave you the money you needed when things got down, even consoled you when your myriad boyfriends turned out to be the douches I always told you they were. And yet, here I still am, pining my time away on someone who could care less. God, it's infuriating. I wish that when you first realized that I was in love with you, you had pushed me away then. That would have been easier than this daily torment you submit me to, keeping me close yet always out of arms'reach. All of the shit you've put me through, and here I still am, melodramatically penning my sappy, uncontrollable emotions to a woman I already know I'll never have, because she's the bitch that will never return my love. Sorry I called you a bitch. You know I don't mean it..... I just..... I don't know what to do. Tell me what to do. Is it possible that you will ever care about me the way I care about you? Is it possible that I will ever grow the balls to actually give you this letter, call you out for treating me like this? Will I ever be able to get over you? If you do get this letter..... please don't judge me too harshly. I don't know that I could take it if you really did cut me out of your life. I hate being near you while you don't love me like I love you, but if you were to reject me, and we were to lose the closeness we have..... I don't know what I'd do. But you'll probably never get this letter anyway. Sorry for being such a coward. I'll always love you.

The sky was dark, with ash filling the air. Bullets and spells whirled past the heads of soldiers and civilians alike. Thousands of men, women, and children alike perished on a minutely basis. The worlds of Althmir and Earth have never been the same since the Rift occurred. It started years ago, in the year 3,072 U. Althmir was a planet that had perfected its civilization; it created a blissful utopia for all of its inhabitants. There was not a day with strife, not a soul was starving, and death was just a mere legend. Children were eager to learn and play, whilst still retaining kindness for one another. Bigotry had faded among adults, with people of every sort lacking judgement for each other. All the issues their ancestors thousands of years in the past had faced were gone. But what is the source for this flawless society, you may ask? Magic. Unlike our world, Althmir lacked significant progress in scientific, mathematical, and philosophical study. Rather, it was a world dedicated to magic. Studies occurred, yes, but they were focused to getting in tune with one's soul, learning to harness their inner power. Day and night intellectuals of the past worked to fine tune their spells and tomes, to try to find the solution to all of their problems. For generations they struggled with these answers, until one day, a magical prodigy was born. This prodigy, who has been given the name Alek Braxton, was born into a family that was peculiar in society. The Braxtons, rather than having tried to learn traditional magic, took a liking to dark magic, a far more powerful and more secretive sort of magic. They were regarded as kind people, but everyone knew their secret, however due to the obscurity of dark magic, no harsh judgement was received beyond the raise of an eyebrow. This study of dark magic heavily attributed to Alek's ability. From the moment he was born, individuals were aware of Alek's abilities. Upon being conceived, the child had turned the one who delivered him into a toad, equipped with a smile upon his face. He continued to showcase his unique abilities throughout his life, being happy and eager to practice spells, his parents growing more and more excited to teach him their ways of dark magic. Once he reached the age of which he was capable of actually being taught how to use and control such abilities, he was immediately schooled in dark magic, with traditional magic sprinkled in to allow him to better fit into society. His parents also had taught him to care deeply about others, something we will see become crucial soon. Day after day he excitedly learned, becoming more and more gifted in magic, better learning to control his powers. Eventually, at the mere age of 10, Alek surpassed his parents in his powers. He also began to take more of an interest in traditional magic, and after reading various scholarly tomes, learned to harness both dark and traditional magic on an equivalent level. However, due to this, he began to become more distant. Alek became extremely introverted, and utterly refused to talk to other people, including his family. In the extremely rare exchanges he did have, he only made slight noises and grunts, in a way to ask for food and drink when he was deep in study or meditation. But, in spite of his being against socialization, he became extremely powerful, and by adulthood he was one of, if not the most talented sorcerer on Althmir. Upon reaching this age, he decided he would abandon his family and become a hermit, further dedicating his life to magical study. This left his family grieving, as they missed their young, once happy and eager boy. But, amazingly, despite him despising social interactions and not caring for his parents' grief for him, he cared deeply about Althmirian society as a whole, thanks to his parents' teachings. This, in combination with his magical study, led to him eventually discovering and creating powerful spells and enchantments that would completely remove any problems Althmirian society had, which were much similar to those in our world. But this was not without cost. Shortly after accomplishing this, Alek had decided to go for a long walk through the woodlands. It was then that he discovered a strange appearance in the midst of the densely packed flora. It was a tear, not of any describable color, that floated in mid air. As Alek approached it, it shot energy at him of the same color. He took cautious steps back, deciding he would magically analyze this. He began to ponder of what spell he should use, when it hit him. This..... tear, was composed of raw magical energy. It was a representation of the world's magic, somehow compacted in a form he could see. Alek realized that it likely appeared due to his usage of a large dosage of magic, something that no being has ever had before. In terms we can understand, he had created his world's equivalent to a tear in the fabric of spacetime. Alek then realized that more and more of these would appear. Unless the source of this raw magical power was eliminated, they likely would end up destroying his world. Thus, he only knew of one solution: His sacrifice. Alek proceeded to jump into the rift, his being dissolving into magical energy. He had become one with the Althmirian universe, as well as one with magic. While his body faded, his consciousness did not, and from the magic he became, he received an abundance of information, including things about the future, past, other worlds, and things no mortal could comprehend. From this, he also realized that his existence is based purely within a Reddit post in another, more scientific and philosophical universe. He also realized that I, the narrator, was telling all of you this, which angered Alek. While he cared deeply for his world, as we know, he did not like to deal with other individuals, and to have one such individual breach his privacy and the secrecy of his accomplishments only to reveal it to a relatively large gathering of people on a subreddit provided no shortage of agitation for him. This agitation caused him to get incomprehensibly angry, with each word I type only adding to his rage. His near-omnipotent and near-omniscient magical ability, while failing to give him complete access over our world, did grant him almost full leverage over his. So much so that, in what was mere seconds to him but years to the Althmirians, caused him to appear to mortals in the year 3,072 U, the U of which stands for'Utopia.' The mortal beings saw Alek as a God, and proceeded to bow in His name. Alek took advantage of this and, in a fit of rage, commanded the beings to attack another world that he grant them access to via a Rift. This world was Earth. Thus began a war that was waged between the two worlds. On our planet, every nation united in an attempt to protect their world from the Althmirian invaders. They used all sorts of weaponry, even nuclear weaponry, which decimated parts of both planets. Millions, no, billions have died due to this, and it is all my fault. Outside, I can hear it. I hear Alek yelling my name. The Althmirians are closer to my location, their magic proving stronger than the weaponry of the Earthlings. He's commanding me to cease this, to delete this Reddit post. He claims it will all be over once this is done. But, I do not believe him. I know he is reading this, and I know it is too late now. I am the narrator over both of our worlds, but unfortunately I am confined to one of them. This world is far too damaged to save, with the last remnants of humanity fading. I must keep typing, no matter what may occur. I must ensure this post survives, as it is all that will remain of us. While Alek could easily guide his soldiers on how to access my account and delete this, it won't do much. It may remove this post from my universe, but I have a bit of knowledge that transcends his near-omniscience, knowledge that will allow people to read this and know of my mistakes, and to allow them to only view it as fiction, to perceive it as a bit of fun a writer had one evening. This knowledge is of what will happen to this post. You see, after this post is sent, it will not just be sent to my universe, but to an alternate Earth. One that is beyond Alek's knowledge. It is capable of transcending his near-omniscience, for in that Earth, we are but a smaller universe, a pocket one, so to speak, that is but a bubble in what is a bubble that is so incomprehensibly large to us as well as to the residents of that Earth. And, that Earth is within another bubble that is in another bubble, and so on so forth. I would go more into detail about this, however my time is drawing short. I can hear the spells disintegrating my house, and now I must allow this tale to come to an end. I can only hope that my world's history is never forgotten, for that is a fate worse than humanity's extinction. Farewell, dear reader, and never forget u- - So this was my first time writing a story for rWritingPrompts. How did I do?

He stood up before the class. "Uh..... Hi. I'm Jeff." he stuttered, clearly uncomfortable in front of the group. The teacher, Mr Taff put his hand of Jeff's shoulder. "That's ok, Jeff. Go take the empty seat at the back. Next to Sam there." I was Sam. I look up from my notebook full of doodles to catch a glimpse of this new guy, wondering what number he'd get. A 3 maybe, if he had any issues. Most people measured around 2-4, one guy I saw had a 6 but he had killed himself that same day. The gym teacher had a 5, but he was ex-military, he had killed people, in war of course. But Jeff..... No, Jeff was a 10. This awkward little boy with bad skin and baggy clothes. This guy was dangerous beyond anything I'd ever witnessed before. He sank down into his chair next to me. The teacher said something I didn't quite catch and everyone started grabbing for their books. I raised my hand. "I-I'm not feeling good. Excuse me!" I got up and started walking out of the room before Mr. Taff could respond, but he grabbed my arm at the door. What I then saw must have been reflected on my face, because Mr. Taff let go of me right away. He was a Zero. My eyes widened and I took off running down the hall. - I ended up in the principal's office. the gym teacher caught me running for the door, he dragged me the whole way. He was still a 5. "Stop acting so strange Miss Stevens." The principal had gone from a 2 to a 3. They were clearly upset about something. "Why were you running from the school in the middle of class, without any of your belongings?" I didn't have a good answer. "I will see you in detention, Sam." Said the gym teacher, "You can help the janitorial staff wash the plaques in the gym halls." "Yes sir." I said, having calmed down. But I had no intention of showing up, I was going to get my stuff and leave. Run away if I had to. I never wanted to see Jeff again. - Having retrieved all my stuff I headed for the exit at a brisk pace. The school had mostly emptied, only a few groups of after school classes remained. I took a side door out into an alley behind the school. It was quicker than running around the whole school. I was looking down and moving fast, so when I ran head first into an unexpected alley occupant I fell flat on my ass. "What the hell? What do we have here?" A hand grabbed my wrist and pulled me up. "Looks like we get two payday's today guys!" This guy had a 5 hovering over him. Robbers, was all I could think, armed robbers. He grabs my collar and slams me against the wall. A knife appears in his open hand. I quickly look around to get a grasp of the situation. "I've got no money, take my phone take whatever you want!" I manage to sputter through the fear. I find myself wishing I had gone to detention. "Come on kid! Show me what you got!" I hear from just a little way down the alley. My blood runs cold as I see Jeff, held off the ground against the wall with a knife in his face. The 10 still hovering around his head. Three guys are standing around him, two are by me. "Jeff!" I yell out. I know he can take these guys. They're only a 5 and...... and 4 zeros..... What's going on here? He looks at me, no fear in his eyes. "Is that little guy your friend?" The guy standing next to me asks. "Maybe he's your ugly little boyfriend! Hey guys, we caught a couple of pervs trying to sneak some action behind the school!" The muggers laugh. They shouldn't be laughing, they should be running. "Fuck man, she's got nothing." the guy holding me turns to his friends, "Even her phone is shit! We couldn't get ten bucks for it!" The zero next to me, he was taller than the 5, maybe the ringleader. "I know what thing she does have." He leaned in close. Terror struck me when I realized what he meant. "No!" I shouted and started kicking and screaming. "No! Get away from me!" He put a hand over my mouth and turned to the other guys behind him. "Take care of that punk. I'll take care of this sweet thing." Tears filled my eyes and my vision blurred. This couldn't be happening! A soft crunch sounded and I fell to the floor, free of the grip that had been holding me. Something warm and wet sprayed my face. Blood. I looked up. The mugger who had been holding me was holding a bloodied knife, and his throat was slashed open. Jeff stood in the alley, staring down the remaining thug. The three who had held him all lay on the ground, blood pooling around them. "What the fuck is going on!" The remaining 5 shouted. Jeff just stared at him. "Leave." Jeff said. His voice was nothing like before. The mugger charged at Jeff, slamming him to the ground. His five vanished the second he touched Jeff. He was now a zero. The mugger reached for a knife, as if to stab Jeff, but instead thrust the knife into his own neck. A scarlet fountain erupted, spraying the alley with even more blood. Jeff stood up, and rubbed his head. Here I was, alone with Jeff. "What are you?" I asked, fear and shock made the words stick to my throat. "I don't know." He said, and walked away.

"Kill the child. It's the right thing to do." "Pops please your not making this any easier" said Mark "It's not supposed to be easy to experience the death of a loved one, much less a daughter." Clint leaned in and held his son for a short second. They both just stood there in silence and looked at her. It had been a year and a half since she had smiled or laughed or done just about anything. Now her face was thin and skin held too tight in some places and too loose in others. It hurt to see her like this but it would have hurt more to know he'd never see her at all. Clint let go of his son and moved to the other side of the bed. "It's your call Mark, it all ways was and it always will be. But you know as well as I that she wouldn't want this. For herself or you." "I just." Mark exhaled heavily and looked away from his daughter for the first time since they had arrived his gaze met his father's. Clint leaned against the wall and released a breath he hadn't realized he'd been holding. "Could you do it pops, kill one of us I mean." The old man took a hard breath "If I could have done anything to help ya, you know I would I'd kill you to stop the pain. I wouldn't be happy about it but I know it needs to be done." "she's not in pain pops she's on straight morphine." "You know what I meant, and even still she's becoming less responsive to it, you can't tell me you don't see the dosages of the drugs just keep getting higher and the concentration of the are going up too, I don't want her to be dead but she will never walk again, never dance or sing laugh or play. She's paralyzed and with the damage to the brain that she's received we would be lucky if she could blink." Clint looked away from his son and faced the window the sun just starting to raise. "I'm sorry Mark I really am. It may be that this old man has lost faith. I just can't stand to think of what's happening in that head of hers. Is she in pain does every forced breath burn and sting, can she hear or is it silent, can she see the light and shadows or is it all just dark, does she dream or is it nightmare after wakeless nightmare breaking in her mind. "Clint was now in tears they creasted his nose and were lost in his short cut beard. Mark couldn't think of another time he'd ever seen his dad cry like this. Even when his mom had passed he was the stoic bolder of flannel and strength for the family to cry on, not with. The year or so after moms death Mark moved Clint in with him and his wife and daughter, he knew Clint got along famously with the girl that's why he was here today. To say goodbye on last time, Mark had decided a little while back that was time he just didn't want to rush it for Clint. "Would you mind calling the nurse pops when your ready of course "Clint nodes his head and regained a little composure. Then went to find the nurse. Mark bent at the knee so he was at eye level with the young girl. He held her hand in his own. The rest all seemed to go by in a blur Clint and the nurse came in. The nurse had asked him something but Mark was to busy starting at her closed eyes he let out a yes maybe and the nurse get to work plugging in extra I.V.'s and moving to different machines now a small team of doctors and nurses rush form machine to machine calling out things it all just sounded like radio static to Mark then the next thing he remembered was the oxygen pump stopped inflating. The he blinked and it was quite no doctor, no nurses, no Clint, no steady beeb of equipment, nothing just him and her. Hand and hand. Mark took note that he could see the moon already high in the sky. He blinked again and he was in the car Clint was driving somewhere it was a road Mark couldn't easily identify. The he saw it the morgue, the cemetery all around it. "Thought maybe you'd want to tell her mother" Clint's voice was raspy. All Mark could muster was a pitiful" Yah." In another blink he was standing in front of the family grave his moms name carved in a brass plate with the years and her role within the family, his wife's right underneath it in the same fashion. Clint extended his hand to Mark passing off a brass plate that says Emma Roberts April 2005- July 2016 beloved, daughter and a friend to all. I slowly opened my eyes. I'd just had a crazy dream where I was examining a tabby and it started talking to me. Shaking my head, I sat up in my bed wait, this isn't my bed..... "You're finally awake." purred the tabby peering down on me from the exam table. "What the my vision started going gray. "For goodness sake, don't pass out again!" yelled the tabby. I shook my head. A talking cat! I must still be dreaming. "What's going on?" I asked the cat. "I'm talking to you, obviously." "But why?" "Well, I was getting to that part before you decided to pass out on me. Humans are such feeble-minded creatures." I shook my head again to clear the dizziness. This was turning out to be a very vivid dream. "I was hoping I could convince you to not shave my fur off." said the tabby. "What?" I asked. "Well you see," said the tabby, "I have a very important meeting tomorrow afternoon and I must look my best." "I'm sorry, but I have to shave you. You have an operation tomorrow." I replied "About that, I was also hoping to postpone the operation. This is a very important meeting." "I can't do that either." I replied, "Your owner has his own schedule that he needs to keep." "My WHAT!?" screamed the cat. "How dare you even suggest that I am owned by that idiot of a servant!" "Excuse me?" "What has the world come to? Humans don't seem to know their place anymore! The idea that I am the property of a human? Preposterous! From a medical'professional' even!" The cat bellowed. "I don't think I understand," I said, confused. The cat grumbled something about having to, "explain the world to them every time." "Humans are our servants," began the cat, "not just the servants of cats as you seem to believe, but of all animals." The cat began pacing across the exam table while glaring at me. "You think that we love you, but we don't not even the dogs. "There has been a system in place for a few hundred years now governing the interactions of the various higher species cats, humans, rodents, dogs, and some reptiles. Humans are on the bottom rung of this system, your job is to ensure the comfort, health, and safety of the other species. "Right above you are the reptiles and dogs, they are the informants and enforcers. Their job is to find and eliminate any rebellion in the servant class before it becomes dangerous. "At the top of the hierarchy are cats and rodents. Cats are the governing species, overseeing the operations of the entire animal kingdom, and rodents are their messengers." "Ahem." Squeaked an albino rat from a nearby cage. "My class is the rightful ruling class. We ruled for hundreds of years before the cats started exterminating the royal family." "Silence, before I have you executed!" Screeched the cat. "Cats have been the rulers since Animalia was established! You are mere pretenders!" "A bit touchy about our legitimacy are we now?" Yelled a guinea pig. "I will have you know that my family has been..." The sounds of the bickering animals faded as I began to pass out again. Maybe I'd wake up this time.

It was noon on the 6th day of the year, the solstice. They had been sailing West from Spain for 3 days now, and morale was running low after so long at sea. The relentless heat from the sun as noon was approaching had prevented anyone from sleeping for over 48 hours now. The crew were getting weary, and although swimming in the sea granted some respite from the heat, shark fins had been spotted which meant no-one was brave enough to risk it. A garbled cry went up from the crow's nest, who was pointing to the West. As Captain John Silver's eyes searched the horizon looking for masts, he gasped as a semi-circular light appeared from across the horizon. What did it mean? It must be the heat, he told himself, the solstice often caused men to see things which weren't really there. It would pass in another few hundred hours. If only he could get some sleep....

The worlds capital city was a huge, walled masterpiece named'Virtue' to echo its extreme moral standards. The city was walled off into 200 sectors, each increasingly smaller than the last, until you reach the high rises in the city centre for the 200's or'true citizens' as they were affectionately referred to by the media. In stark contrast, the outer sector was effectively a giant slum for the 1's. Here in Virtue your number determines the standard of living, many call this virtue incarnate. Others call it bullshit. I am inclined to agree with the others, and the situation is becoming toxic with the installation of a giant golden statue of Arete, the Greek goddess of virtue and valour in sector 200. The true citizens were playing a dangerous game, as it turns out that most people do not score well. Over 70 of the cities population resides between sectors 1-50. "BROTHERS AND SISTERS! HEED MY WORDS!!" begun a local fanatic. People were putting a temporary halt to beating the shit out of one another and petty acts of vandalism and theft to see what the commotion was all about. "Why do we follow a law that condemns us to a life of squalid containment!?" his eyes were bloodshot as he spat each word. High as a kite I mused as I watched whilst smoking from the safety of a street corner within ear shot. "We have 15 of virtues people in this sector alone, no other sector has more. I pose the question to you, my fellow brethren. How are the 1 truer citizens than the rest? Who has the right to decide were less good than others.." he reasoned as murmurs of debate broke out in the ever-increasing mob. "We should rise up! And free our fellow brothers over the walls and take what should be everyon BANG the fanatics body lurched forward as a hole was torn through the robed man, spurting blood into the faces of those closest. The cigarette dropped from my mouth as I strained to see the source, way up high almost in the clouds. A man donned in brilliantly white, steel armour with a sniper stood atop the towering walls of what I would assume was the wall between sectors 197 and 198. Uprisings were not tolerated. The mob erupted in cries of pure hatred, people grabbed sticks, guns and makeshift weapons as they hopped in trucks, cars and everything they could and charged the wall between 1 and 2. The wall stood merely 10 foot high and was in a state of disrepair. The skeleton crew of guards were took by surprise as I and thousands behind me plowed through the wall in mammoth truck rigs and into sector 2, where the industrial sector begun. We broke out in cheers as the guards were bludgeoned viciously behind us in the mob. -2 months later and we have reached sector 90 and the uprising will not stop until the pretentiousness of the true citizens is brought down. -

The city of the future, that's what they had called it. A sprawling city center of metal and glass stretching as high as the eye can see. Fully automated and catered to its citizens. A place of opportunity for a simple man like me to make it. Little did I know what a different world the megacities of today were from the secluded town where I had lived my life. "What is the purpose of your visit Mr. Winters?" The harsh metallic voice came from a dark window located in the bustling terminal of the skyport, spitting the words at me. I tried to peek in, to see who I was talking to, but only saw my own reflection staring back at me, bemused and lost. "I- I'm new here and I have come for a job offer." "Business," the voice corrected, sounding entirely detached from the conversation. "Oh, yes that's correct" "Passport," It was a command not a question. A slit at the bottom of the window opened up and I tentatively put my papers through. The passport was sucked through with a gush of wind. After a few seconds of whirling and grinding, the passport was launched back out. "You have been cleared," the cold voice alerted me. "You are authorized for 3 weeks of temporary access to the city. All developments of your business inquiries are to be reported to the proper channels." As if it were a after-thought, the voice added "The City is currently in a state of warfare. Any interference with these activities are prohibited. Enjoy your stay." "Wait what? What does that mean?" I waited for an answer but the window remained silent. "Hello?" When it became obvious that whoever (or whatever) was behind the window was not going to respond, I picked up my backpack, containing everything I own in this world, and walked for the exit. Outside was a sight I would not forget. Skyscrapers rose to the sky, touching the very heavens with their steel tops. The buildings were so intricately designed, it was unclear where one ended and where another began. On the ground level, expressways winded between the metal giants, the hum of electric vehicles zipping to their destinations. Among all this mayhem I found a tiny cafe; its green awning tucked between a skyscraper and an expressway, patrons sitting at tables sipping their drinks. I was about to figure out where to go when I spotted it. There was a human-like figure moving towards the cafe, yet on second glance I could tell it was not human but some sort of machine. Instead of wheels it had treads. And instead of hands it had two guns. I watched in a sort of a daze as the machine moved closer to the cafe. The metallic soldier raise its deadly arms in the direction of the cafe. With a sense of dread, I remembered the words at the window: "warfare." "Noo!" I shouted, desperately trying to warn the people but it was too late. The machine fired and the bullets sprayed towards the unaware patrons..... and over their heads. The bullets found a mark on a similar type of machine that I had not even noticed, positioned on the roof of the cafe. It exploded in a display of fire and smoke. I rushed towards the people seated just below all the chaos. In the back of my mind I found it curious that not a single one had moved from their spot. In fact they acted like nothing was happening at all. A woman took another sip from her cup. A man yawned and patted his substantial stomach in satisfaction. Didn't they realize what was happening merely yards away? But I barely noticed this. My mind was focused on trying to rescue them, to warn them. I reached the awning of the cafe and shouted, "Run! Watch out! It's too dangerous to be here!!" As if to prove my point, the machine began to fire again. Bullets whizzed just above my head and I began to move, expecting that the cafe patrons would follow me to safety. But they just stared at me, one old man shaking his head in disgust and returning his eyes on his food. "What's wrong with you people!" I yelled over the sound of gunfire. "You need to move!" But they did not listen. They did not move. The firing stopped, but when I looked up I saw why. Three small airborne machines were flying this direction. The machine had stopped firing for the moment to aim into the sky. The flying machines in the sky were preparing to fire back. This was the eye of the storm. In any second, the area was going to be plunged into chaos. I made a decision. If these people were not going to save themselves, it was up to me to stop this. I started running towards the gun-wielding machine. I didn't have a plan but if I could just somehow disable that machine then maybe the flying ones would leave. But I knew above all I needed save the people. Bullets erupted again. All around me as I ran; rain drops of death that I somehow eluded. In this moment, I was brought back to my childhood, playing cops and robbers with my friends in the backyard of our country home. Of course I was always the cop, dodging the bullets of the robbers and saving the people. Then I was on top of the machine, ripping and tearing, trying to destroy the weapons it called hands. The machine's emotionless head was inches from my own as we struggled, flesh versus iron. I was looking into the very face of evil and it gave me strength. I reached up for the head pulled with everything I had until it snapped. The machine fell back, nothing but a twisted heap of scraps. The machines overhead withdrew and I fell back in relief, everything going black, the last thought I had was a blissful one: I had saved the people..... I woke up. I was laying down on a couch in some sort of office. There was a desk which was curiously empty. A potted plant was positioned in the corner of the room. I looked over and saw a window, overlooking the cityscape, high above every other building. Just above us was the clouds, just a heartbeat away from the heavens. The door opened and a man walked in. He had a aged faced but one that had aged well. His eyes were of a man who seemed to know exactly how you felt. He had a slight smile that seemed to convey that he knew the exact words I was forming. "Where am I?" I asked "What happened? Who are you?" The man put out a hand to halt the words spilling out of my mouth. "You were very brave out there," he said simply. "But..." I had so many questions. What were those machines? Why didn't the people run or even react? The man casually walked over to the desk and sat, taking me in with a measured look. Then he spoke. "My name is Mr. Montemercy. I am the CEO of InterGlobal Corporations" I recognized the name instantly. "You were the one who offered me the job" "Yes. We picked you because of your unique qualities. You were born outside of the megacities that have dominated this planet. In fact, the small town you grew up in was one of the last remaining pockets of undeveloped land left in the world, "Let me explain what we do here. We manufacture Autonomous Warfare Units, or AWUs." My eyebrows shot up in surprise. "Yes, you are already familiar with one of our products. Our corporation is at war with other companies. In our world, land is the most precious commodity we know. Whoever has the land has the power. To answer your earlier question, these robots are specifically designed not to harm any civilians, per regulations. That I why the people at the cafe did not react. They have become used to this state of constant warfare. Wherever they go, there is fighting. But it does not affect them," "But why do you need me?" I asked. "I am the last person you want. I lived on a farm for goodness sakes. There was not a single machine in my house?" "Exactly!" the man exclaimed with delight. "There is not a single machine in your house. The problem with people today is that they have become lazy. Everything is done for them. There are robots that make food for them, that drive them, that tell them what is planned for their day, that think for them. You are untouched by this. You are one of the last pure, uncorrupted humans left on this Earth and we need what is in your mind," I was speechless and I just waited for the man to continue. This was all too much to take. "Let me tell you the problem with our AWUs. Yes they are autonomous but they don't fight for anything. In fact they are much like the humans of today. Programming tells them what to do. They are un-motivated. But if they think like you do, imagine how much better they would fight than other robots. Think about it. You were motivated to save the people in the cafe, right? This was all you thought about. And you managed to defeat one of our machines. Albeit, they are programmed not to fire at you but with your motivation and their firepower, they would be unbeatable. We want to study you, find out what makes you tick, then program those ideas into our machines." As he spoke, I was slowly becoming more horrified, more disgusted. "No," I answered "I will not take part in this. I can't. I will not be a test subject to further your agenda and spread more destruction. I decline your offer." Montemercy nodded, all the while with the look that he knew this was all coming. He slowly left his chair and began walking towards me, smiling sadly. "The fact is you have already accepted. You are already working for us. In fact, you have been for some time." As he spoke his voice began to morph, from the soft human tone to a harsh metallic voice, the same as the window, and my heart grew colder with every word. "This is a simulation. Day 3,743 of your time with us. We are slowly integrating your very essence into our fighting machines. We will begin the simulation again. You will arrive in the city. You will save the people. And you will bring us one step closer to our goals," He was standing above me now. It was very cold. The feeling in my arms and legs slowly faded away to nothing. As my vision blurred, the voice said, now void of all human emotion and as cold as ice, "What is the purpose of your visit Mr. Winters?"

I'm still not sure how it went where it did but I had fun with it, hope you do too. " As we move forward, toward peace and prosperity, we must confront our collective past... " The voice of the new Chairman of The Democratic United States of China and the Americas droned on. Ten long years had passed since the invasion had begun, and we had been completely overwhelmed. America had been on the decline since the nineties, with the collapse of the Soviet Union serving as a historic turning point. We became complacent in our hegemony, and we suffered the consequences. It was 2042 now, and we were subjugated into the Chinese sphere of influence. " ...some yearn for the past, others yet for collective security and the end of the Nuclear winter... " We were gathered in Washington to hear the Chairman speak. It was cold, a bitter January day, even without the new climate that we now deal with. Christ, it's cold. I can feel my arms starting to get frostbite. The Chairman was finally wrapping up his speech. It was mandatory listening, made for a good show for the outside world. Suddenly, the Chairman stopped. I perked up. Faintly, but distinctly, you could hear it. " Oh saint can you see... by the dawn's early light... " Almost as a whisper, it began to rise. By the time it had reached the mid-song, it was in a full crescendo. Looking around, men in black suits were shouting into their mics. It was inaudible, all you could hear was the glorious former national anthem, now a banned song. Slowly, we began to sing along. " land of the free... and the home of the brave! " With the last few notes, we began cheering. The Chairman looked horrified, and turned to escape the now violently rioting millions he had assembled. However, blocking his escape was a figure in the doorway. He leaned closer. " Who are you? " A growling Austrian voice replies. " I'm the party pooper. " Arnold Schwarzenegger stepped out onto the balcony and pumps a shotgun blast through the heart of the Chairman. He quickly delivered fatal shots to the various secret service agents and moved to the microphone to address us. " Fight with me if you want to live. " The crowd roared cheers of approval, and we all pulled out the semi-automatics we've been conceal carrying for the last decade. Within the day, we had taken back the capital, within a week, the surrounding states, and within a year, the whole country. " And that, son, is how Arnold Schwarzenegger became the 49th President of the United States with the highest approval rating of all time. " " But dad, if everyone loved him, why isn't he the President anymore? " Tears welled up in my eyes. " Because, son. There is a two term limit. " He got up and gave me a big hug, and started crying. I hug back, and through shallow breath, I whisper into his ear: " Don't worry, son - He'll be back. " Edit two months later: improper verb tenses!

My father opened the door to my bedroom and I peered across the hallway, "Daddy, why is there a door there now?" My father looked down, shocked to see me, then he looked at the door and his face went white. He stuttered and stammered for a moment before regaining some composure and speaking clearly. "I put that door there years ago when I added on an extra room." He answered. "Daddy, what is the extra room for?" I asked. My father was visibly shaking. He was scared, but he regained his composure and tried to answer. "I..... needed a new room to put your sister in. I didn't want her to sleep in yours" He answered. "Daddy, why have I never met my sister?" I asked. My father broken down. He looked into my eyes and spoke from the bottom of his heart. "Julie, I love you. I love you so much." He reached out to hug me and his arms passed right through me. The world started to fade into white light around me. It took fourteen years for him to open my door again. Fourteen years trapped waiting to hear what I needed to so I could finally move on.

I awoke to find a hooded old man extending his hand toward me. He looked at me with a tired, aggravated expression, expecting something. I tried to take his hand, but apparently he wasn't trying to help me up, since his hand disappeared entirely as I went to grab it. I stood and looked around to see myself on a simple wooden raft, in the midst of a frothing purple river. The old man sighed, rolled his thin eyes, and extended his hand once more. I was scared, of c ourse, because I knew where I was, but despite everything I felt clarity, and some level of calm. I reached into my pockets and pulled out a ziploc bag holding the two golden drachma I picked up earlier today. That is, if it even is still today. How could I know how much time has passed since my death? The old man took the coins, the plastic evaporating at his touch. He motioned once at the river, and we flew through hades, presumably at great speed, but I couldn't tell. We moved as though a current in the ocean, and I was only glimpses of where we moved. A man pushing a boulder twice his size, a dog sleeping, chewing a bone, and licking his ass all at once. I guess dogs are dogs regardless of how many heads they have. A field of flowers in colors and shapes I couldn't name. They were gorgeous. The raft eventually stopped as fluid and calm as it started, and I stepped off it onto a slab of rock, just like where we fell. I surveyed the drop, there was no rocky bottom this time. I turned behind me to find that Robert Downey Jr. was standing behind me. "Pleased to meet you, I'm Hades." I looked back at him, rather stupended. He saw my confusion, I could tell by the way his breath sped up, as though he was about to tell a really bad joke. "It's only a costume. Got ta pick some form you can understand. Didn't you like The Avengers? Thor didn't, the crabby old nord." He smiled. I burst out laughing. "I knew it all along! They all called me crazy, every one, but here I am! If only they could see me now!" The smile wiped away from his face in the same fluid motion that brought me to the cliff. "I thought you might appreciate a good shapeshifting joke before you go on the whole egomaniac rant. Really, Jonathan, I had hoped you'd be more amiable." I looked at him, how could I take this guy seriously? The Lord of the underworld standing in front of me dressed like Iron Man? I felt no fear. "Don't act like you're gon na up and torture me, I was faithful, no one else was! No one in the world believes like I do!" He looked down at me, disappointed, not angry. The poser. "Yes, you remembered us, Jonathan. And you forgot your hubris. You cut the rope, Jon. You killed them. Because they didn't "Give me what I deserved! All those years of study and they never recognized it, all the time I spent, all the papers I wrote and no one recognized my work, and the bastards had the nerve to make fun of me at the peak of my work. I killed everyone of the poser heathens on the excavation and I'm proud of it!" The cliff fell out behind me, I suppose that symbolized the poser of the moment. A good journalist recognizes these things, you know. And the best in the world is speaking to you now. "The gods don't care for arrogance, Jon. We get enough of that from ourselves. I'll be seeing you, professor." The raft flooded back in and the iron man stepped back on it. I reached out to follow him and then found myself stopped in my tracks by a pale figure, whom I recognized. Dr. Carlton stood with broken limb and similar sounds all over. To my left was Stacy, the intern, and Francis Cabot, the translator for Abdul, my guide through the ruins. He stood to my right. I found I couldn't move while they enclosed on me. "Wait, where are you going?! You can't leave me, you don't have malice like some demon! You don't live to punish, you can't do this!" "This is your punishment, Jonathan. I don't make the punishments, I just watch the realm. The punishments make themselves. Be seeing you." He disappeared in that same fluid motion, leaving me with the specter of my dead comrades. At least I could gloat. "I told you all, look where we are!" Carlton looked at me, blood dropping down his skull. "What are you on about now, loony? I swear you're right fucked in the head." Stacy's head swiveled around to see me. Mr. Edwards, did you miss your meds this morning? We're just on this old cliff!" The color trained from my face. "Are you in sun-stroke, my friend?" "He's a lunatic, is what he is!" "Don't be an ass, doctor, you know he has issues!" "Bah! He's a murderer and a hack, nothing more!" "Poser!" "Looney!" "Psycho!"

"Look, I know this is hard for you, but you're needed. Get up." The high-pitched voice hurts my ears. Why do they have to be so loud? Wait. Where am I? I sit up and look around the brightly lit room. It's filled with large drawers and the floor is covered with what look like metal coffins, bolted into the floor. It's cold, and my hands have a tinge of blue to them. Thinking out loud, I say: "But where am I?" The squeak answers. "You've just woken up from cryosleep. You were frozen in the year 2016. It is now 2712. But your cryochamber was the only one that worked. Everyone else is dead, except for you and me. I am the only living descendant of the rebels. To answer your question, you are currently in a large space station that is orbiting 173km above Earth. I am sorry to inform you that the planet you once called home is dead. It was killed by the Root." I slowly reach for the sides of my cryochamber and pull myself out. The voice continues. "You may have heard of the Root. In your time, it was known as "Blight," but after the great prophet Daniel Hardcastle released his prophecies, we started calling it the Root. In the year 2307, around 100 years after the invention of time-travel, it made a deal with an unidentified man and started invading the world. You are a descendant of Daniel Hardcastle. You are the only one who can save the Earth, Alex Hardcastle. Good luck and best wishes." The voice shuts off, and somehow I know it's never coming back. All I know is that I need to find the person who was talking, and fast. We're the only ones left, we must be special. I set off, out of the door and into unknown territory.

The well dressed red-head shuffled her papers into a neat stack. "Well Mr. Henderson, your granddaughter is choosing to legally kill you. We are required by law to notify you of her intentions. Can I just get you to sign here?" Henderson took thepen. It was cool and heavier than he expected. He signed and licked his chapped lips. "When?" "Sometime next week." She took the paper and pen from him and slipped it into a folder labeled with Amy's name. "Amy has chosen to administer the lethal injection herself, so once she's cleared by the Department, she'll stop by, accompanied by an agent, of course." Henderson nodded. "She can't..." he waited for the machine to pump another breath into his lungs, " ..... come sooner?" "I'm sorry. I can't rush the process. Have a good day, Mr. Henderson." She stood and walked out, leaving the ICU and its beeping behind. Henderson looked at the ceiling, the only view he'd known for the last 8 months. One week. One week.

(This is my first submission, hope you enjoy!) There were only 3 people in front of you now. You'd been waiting in line ever since the announcement was made; Reincarnation proven, in who's footsteps do you follow? It was a discovery that shook the world. Sit in a chair, let a machine scan you, and discover who you were in your past life. You had no idea how the science worked, but renowned scientists around the world had confirmed the machine's authenticity. And so, the masses swarmed the Reincarnation Centers, of which there was only 1 stationed within a 17 hour car ride of your hometown. There were 2 people left in front of you. The machine had already ruined several aspects of the modern man's life. Last you'd heard, a woman in Canada had Jesus Christ as one of her past lives. There was another fellow in Iceland that laid claim Albert Einstein's genius, though he knew nothing of physics. Hell, in the trial runs of the machine, an infant had been found to be the reincarnation of, despite the test sample being only 300, Adolf Hitler, who had then been abandoned at the testing center, his parents fearing what he might become. There was 1 person left in front of you. When studies were done, it was discovered that who you were in your past life had almost effect on the kind of person you were. Only the most fervent passions were carried into the next life. The reincarnation of Mozart didn't play an instrument, but he had perfect pitch, an enthusiasm toward classical music, and, surprisingly, absolutely loved heavy metal. That is to say, the collective group of people you were in your past life made up the finer details of who you were, for better or worse. After waiting 8 hours, it's finally your turn. You step into a room full of wires and men in lab coats, and you finally begin to understand how complex this machine must be. As you stand in marvel a woman in a suit approaches you, asking your preferred method of payment. You wave her off with the check you had prepared before you left home, wishing to get the memory of the twenty grand you're spending on this test out of your mind. As a man in a lab coat waves you forward you begin to imagine the people you might have been in your past lives. Maybe you'll be able to brag to your friends that you were the reincarnation of a historical celebrity, or a great scientist! There are too many possibilities to consider as you are strapped into the chair that may change your life forever. The man who took care of all the preparations for the test finally backs away, looking satisfied. After giving you one last look over he looks at a camera mounted on but one of the walls of the massive machine and gives a thumbs up, and the machine hums to life. The test is by no means quick, as evaluating the human soul is no small endeavor, and is estimated to take at least 30 minutes. In order to ensure that the person being tested doesn't grow uncomfortable during this time the patient is given the choice to be sedated until the test is over. I decided to be sedated, as I figured my excitement would turn 30 minutes into 30 hours. And so as soon as the machine began to whir, I nodded off, ready to embrace the achievements and glories of my past lives. Queue black. When I came to, the first thing I noticed is that I wasn't in the chair of the machine, like I should've been, you're supposed to be handed a sheet of paper with your 100 most recent past lives and then escorted out of the facility. However, I found myself in what appeared to be an office building. After I had been conscious for about 3 minutes a man in a lab coat entered the room. When I asked him about why I had been moved he replied that the sedative was designed to last 30 minutes, and the machine had only needed a fraction of that time. Before I could ask any more questions the man shoved a folded sheet of paper at me, saying it was my results, and again I was overwhelmed with excitement. I came to this place to find out what I might do with my life. I came here to find out who I was. But it was not to be. I opened the paper, and started at the top of the paper and worked my way down. I froze. Slowly, I glanced at the man in the lab coat, who was still watching me, and meekly pointed to the paper in confusion. He nodded. The paper was blank. I was a nobody.
