"So, your people and my people are at war then? Just like that?" I asked, staring into the screen. Outside, masses of rock moved silently through the asteroid field. My former comrade from the other side was only a few meters away from me, in a spherical ship that, just like mine, was devoid of external lights and signals. We'd used these ships to goof off and enjoy a few minutes of peace between shifts, but this meeting was something other. "We didn't know that word until we met you," he said, voice eerily clear over the communicator. "We didn't understand you until recently. I personally do not think you are like some of..... them. I would have liked us to still be friends." "I still don't understand," I replied quietly. "The books," his voice replied. "You're the only race we have contacted, out of dozens, who has written fiction about going to war with other races in outer space. In fact, the word itself was mistranslated until recently - we believed it to mean a grudge or some kind of existential conflict. Your concept, it is a form of mass-murder. Yours is the only race that practices it, at least that we know of." I sat staring at his ship through the window, and I was angry. "War? War isn't always wrong. Factions have gone to war to prevent genocides or injustice..." " ..... that were also created by people of your own race," he pointed out. "Genocide. We have prejudices. Every race does. But yours is the only one that has pushed it to that extreme. Wait." I watched the inside of his cockpit light up. The light of a single viewscreen illuminated his rigid, still face. "Nuclear weapons. You are the only race. Genital mutilation. Only race. Not the only race to commit slavery, but had the longest duration of slavery of any race. Disease warfare. Only race. Serial killers. Only race. You have no idea how many years it took us to actually decipher what some of this meant. You were a brother to me, human. Your kind sickens me." "This is in the past," I protested. "You're reading our history files." "Three months ago, a nuclear strike destroyed one of your far colonies," he said. His race's version of an accusatory tone was high pitched and grating. "That was a galactic backwater," I said. "Those aren't civilized people." "Still your race," he said. "A religious organization committed some kind of ritual suicide last year. One of your race's preachers convinced over a thousand of your people to kill themselves. Why?" "They're..... crazy," I finished lamely. These weren't groups of people I was affiliated with. "The eradication of Yavesh-5," his voice said, in a cold monotone. "Starting a terraforming process by destroying an entire planet's ecosystem, including budding sentient life." I sat silently. That was the Prade Corporation, which was one of our former company's competitors. Those were people a lot like me. "We can be greedy," I said quietly. "But we're not all like that. Our own government punished them." "They were fined. It was 12.7 of one yearly net profit for them. They murdered a planet and paid your government to do it. This is not a meaningful punishment." "Fine, we're scum," I sighed, throwing my hands up. If they had already judged us, there was nothing we could really do. "I just hope we can end this stupid war. What caused it in the first place?" "We did," he answered. I stared at him across the vacuum. "You what?" "We declared war," he said simply. "Once we learned what it was, and figured out what your race was capable of, we realized that war would be inevitable between us. The only way we can exist peacefully is to make sure that your people are kept under control." "You're going to condemn us as warmongers and then declare war on us?" I demanded, standing up in the cockpit. "You fucking hypocrite!" "Not hypocrite. Survivor," he replied. "Your people are too aggressive and cruel. We do not want neighbors with nuclear arms, or random splinter factions suffering from insanity attacking us. We do not want to be attacked because one member of your race wanted to steal from us to further his own ambitions. Your race is ridiculous. I do not understand how any of you cooperated enough to leave your planet in the first place." "Well, we don't want a neighbor who is going to suddenly declare war on us because of our history," I shouted. "You call us ridiculous? You won't be saying that in a few years. There's something you forgot about us, old friend." "I find this doubtful," he hissed. "We're a contentious race. We fight like wolves over things you find stupid, using methods you'd never dream of. But what happens when we face a common enemy? If humanity has a choice between aiding their worst enemy or being ruled by an alien race, which do you think we will choose? Oh, and all of those things you mentioned? If we came up with all of that, what are we going to come up with in this war?" "You will not succeed," he said. His voice quavered slightly. "Even if you win, billions of your kind will die," I stated, staring into his cockpit. "If we begin to lose, we will use nuclear and chemical weapons. We will make plagues against you. We will sterilize your planets and even sacrifice our own lives to take more of yours. You have no idea how fucked you are right now. Why in the fuck did you think those writers wrote those fucking books? We were ready for this the entire time. The entirety of human history was leading up into our war with you. You're right, I guess. It was inevitable." My cockpit lit up with bright lights. Several of the erstwhile asteroids outside were lit up, displaying installations of metal and spotlights on their surfaces. "We have finished recording," a foreign, alien voice sounded over the communicator. "Thank you, human." "What? What is this?" I protested, shielding my eyes from the light. "From your race, we have also learned the meaning of propaganda," my former friend said. He made a high-pitched keening noise, the sound of his race expressing mirth. The asteroids closed in. I had a sinking feeling that I would never see a human world again.

Lenny checked his gyrojet pistol again and again. Light came in through the broken blinds in the cut-rate hotel room. He carefully pulled out a handful of teflon coated bullets and loaded them into the pistol. He paused for a moment to feel their unusual heft. His wristphone rang and he put it up to his ear. "Yes.." "Hello, this is the Getty Corporation fulfilling contract 44595. 21 is approaching the car now on State and Wacker. This ends our contractual obligations." The mechanical voice hung up. Lenny sighed, peeled off his cheap wristphone and smashed it with his heel. He flushed it down the toilet as he put the gun in his waistband. He put on a long coat, examined himself in the mirror and put on a lead lined helmet. It sat heavily on his head. Lenny winced in pain as his neck negotiated the weight. The number above his head slowly faded way. Outside a woman with long blonde locks and wearing a bulletproof vest walked towards her car. Lenny watched from a bench pretending to read his tablet. He spied the 21 floating above her head. He stood up, pulled out his pistol, walked up to her, and asked, "Pardon me miss, do you know how to get to...." She turned around, gasped, and he shot her. Her body exploded like a plastic doll plastic bits and hydraulic fluid went flying everywhere. Lenny's eyes went wide. "An android," he said outloud as he felt a tap on his shoulder. "So long fucker," said the real 21 as she fired her revolver into Lenny's chest. 21 sighed, kicked over the body, and got into her car. She pulled off her long blonde lead-lined wig, revealing a short brunette hairdo. She tapped her expensive looking gold wristphone as it blinked. "Hello, this is the Getty Corporation fulfilling contract 445623, revealed location of assassin. This ends our contractual obligations." "Sure does, hon. Sure does, now lets talk pricing on finding me number 20," she replied with a grin.

The blood was spilled across the dugout hole of the latrine. Cut at the gut with intestines like a tar-smeared rope splattered near the door. His one good eye was still open, gently I closed it. He was a good man, a father and a husband. This is a land of law, whether people like it or not, and I intend to find the killer. Stepping out of the outhouse I placed the ripped note in my pocket; evidence, not many in my town can write. I put on my black stetnson hat, tug at my leather trousers, and thumb-lick my badge. My horse, my Bessie, neighed nearby, tied to post. I grimaced at the harsh sun and the plain orange land that surrounds me. A scattering of wood cobbled together to look like buildings blots the view, but most are empty now. This town is dying, gold left many years ago, but still some poor souls linger on. Untied my horse, and galloped back into town. Approached the local saloon, the Bar Sink. Its second story windows were bordered-up, not many come to stay. I swung open the doors and the dust of the place blew into my face. I snarled and stepped out of the light and into the shadow misery of the sullen that laid before me, drinking their lives away. No man dared to lay their eyes on me as I walked up to the bar. Marvin, quivering, turns to me with his beady-eyes and gray unkempt hair. Sputters, " What kan I do'for ya Sheriff? " " We have another dead man. I need to talk to Mary. Where is she? " I said. Too many seconds passed by and I slam my fist onto his cracked bar. " She-she-she's up-upstairs! " I tip my hat out of well-worn respect, and I climb. It didn't take a genius to figure out which room was still occupied. I pounded on the door and yelled, " Sheriff! Open up. Don't make me break this door! " A male voice, " Wait! Coming, goshdarn it. " With sounds of tossed blankets and pushed over cases, the door opened revealing a man half dress, but with a sophisticated demeanor and an eastern-style beard. " What-do-you-want? " He said. I pulled out the note from the outhouse, " Is this you? " " Of course- " and I sock him as hard as I could. He barreled backwards into his room, and I continued to kick him. Mary, naked in bed, trying desperately to cover herself in sheets, screamed. I didn't give him a chance, he tried to twirl away from my kicks, but I began stomping on his head until he laid still. I shook the blood off my spur. " Why!? " Shriek Mary, " Why? " And she broke down into sobs. I showed her the note, " No one writes this well in town. Had to be an out'a'towner. No other man here would follow your words, no other man here would've had the guts. " Her blue eyes widen, " But Sheriff. I, I was raped. I swear. I was drunk, it was dark... " I began to unbutton my shirt. " You fool of a girl. " And I shut the door.

The arithmetic was wrong. The teacher had written an example problem, and she had solved it wrong. The class rejoiced. The confused teacher looked over her math. There were no mistakes. She did the problem step by step as the class looked on in confusion and found the base of the issue: nothing was as expected. Every number, every mathematical process had resulted in a completely different answer from the one that had made sense five minutes ago. The weirdest thing was that this new answer made sense all of a sudden, too. The whole class, and everyone else in the world, suddenly felt stupid for ever thinking that 2 and 2 equaled 4. 2 and 2 really equaled..... well, that was difficult. Governments brought in the greatest mathematicians to rebuild modern mathematics from the ground up. But they could do little. As they looked on, basic currency broke down. Economies were crushed by the altered values. Even machines got confused. Computers went dark, their basic programming not built to function in this new reality. Nothing mechanical was reliable. Car, train, and even airplane accidents brought transportation to a halt. At the same time, the Earth itself became confused. Its escape velocity lessened to a fraction of what it once was, causing birds and bugs to be sucked out into space along with much of the atmosphere. The space station was flung by its inertia out of orbit, spiraling at an impossible velocity. The Earth followed suit, finally leaving the sun and going off on its own journey. This, of course, is when the people died. Stars began to burst, following no clear pattern, the galaxy bubbling with light until the black hole at the center reverted back into a star itself. As all of existence exploded distance became meaningless. Atoms were ripped apart and energy settled into an eternity of meaningless chaos. The universe broke down as energy leaked away into nothingness..... But this didn't happen, of course, because the math teacher is never wrong. Never wrong, kids, even if it looks like it. Don't question it.

Kruel twittered his mandibles. He couldn't stop. He had been studying millennia of human development and culture thanks to the photoretroamplifier. The humans, or homo sapiens sapiens as they called themselves, for his whole academic career. He had to make a case to the high council Consortium for galactic peace now. They had entered a new era of growth and technological advancement and reached the five billion mark. They had already launched satellites into orbit over their planet, sent a ship to their small moon and had the start of what could grow to be a global governing entity called the UN. Kruel had been thrilled to study this planet. It spawned many truly ferocious empires, but what fascinated Kruel was that they were not simply barbaric nations winning by numbers. The Greeks defined culture of the western part of their continent and founded one of the first democracies on the planet, even if it was somewhat exclusive in it's citizenship. The Roman republic welcomed it's conquered foes into being equals, at first. Kruel was bed ridden with grief as he learned about it's fall into a tyrannical empire. The ottomans likewise grew to great size and prominence while making great strides in medicine and mathematics. China was another beautiful civilization to him. It had survived long centuries while existing as a vast dominion. His studies were enthralling. Of all his peers, he felt he was the most blessed by the forebears with the privilege and challenge of collecting and gathering history. Even their biology was fascinating. Their planet was mostly oceans and yet they were bipedal land creatures. They were the only class one sentient species on their planet and yet they had no other feature that seemed to aid them in their rise to power. They didn't have the fore arm scythes his people had, or the sheer size of the Gret'haim or any other trait that seemed would provide any help, other than their ability to communicate and use tools And they had made it on the merit of that alone. They didn't even have fur to protect them from the cold of the regions that were surprisingly some of the most well populated areas on the planet. Clothing was not just a matter of fashion or tradition it was a necessity, also an oddly universal matter of modesty. But after two world wars, multiple genocide events and a current era of strife between the planet's two superpowers, Many in the high council thought that they might pose a galactic level threat. This upset Kruel to no end. He had been delighted that it seemed the planet was slowing down and scaling back to wars, ironically in part due to the mutual fear of the use of atomic weapons. He thought that this species, young and " warlike " as it was, definitely merited further study to say the least. In a century or two perhaps even inclusion! But the Gret'haim's member of the council thought otherwise. Being perhaps the most belligerent species to be granted membership, Kruel thought the idea of them opposing on that basis alone was hypocritical at the very least. But they took it a step further. They advocated the complete desolation of the species! Now he had only this one brief statement he could make to the council about the matter He gathered his data, drew himself up to full height and entered the amphitheater. The announcing drone spoke in galactic common " The council will now observe high scholar Kruel of the Maistons on the issue of the status of the Humans of planet 44356 titled Earth " The room was massive and intimidating. Kruel stood at the center of a stadium of the brightest minds the galaxy had to offer. Liaisons of every member planet were represented in the audience. The council itself had only three members who would weigh in on this hearing. Thul, an cephalopod telepath of the planet Kraoen, suspended in a vat of water Grik a member of Kruel's species, he looked neither impressed or particularly concerned about And most pressingly Whol, one of the Gret'haim, standing massively beside the podium, already tall enough on his own to be of the correct height. " Greeting's valued members of the council, I am here to make the case that the Human's of Earth are not in fact parasites nor unworthy of future considering for membership, " the last part drew gasps from the collective, well the part capable of gasping. Thul's tank bubbled a little more for a moment. " First, Earth has yes been greatly depleted of what we would term fossil fuels. The effects of the humans actions on their own environment are well established and document, " he pressed on his datapad and showed figures of the earth's current projected usage of resources over the past century and estimates of present sources went up to massive veiwscreens. " But the humans are aware of this, in fact much work is being done to correct it. They are researching alternatives like nuclear power and Critical superpowers like their " United states " are passing legislation in an attempt to limit pollution. They are looking to sustain themselves. " Thul's eerie telepathic voice echoed across the amphitheater " And what of their proclivity towards Imperialism? Doesn't that in conjunction with their resource usage lend itself to future parasitism? " Kruel gulped. " Ah-em well...ah yes. But the issue against that point is that as an increasing portion of the nations become democratic, the instances of such actions have decreased drastically. Wars of conquest are becoming rarer events. Most nations do not seek to expand their boundaries, merely to secure their interests internationally. " Whol bellowed across the amphitheater. " This after two cataclysmic wars in the past century alone? And the worst Genocidal event on record? " " I maintain my stance, they are growing out of that, slowly but surely. Secondly by percentage it was no worse than your own planet's latest civil war, " Kroel regretted saying the last part. Whol " Such outburst are unbecoming of a high scholar. Do you have any non-inflammatory closing remarks? " Grik chided. " Many apologies, Yes one final point in their favor is the development of a computer facilitated communications network similar to our own. " " Ah yes then the our choice of actions is clear, " Grik spoke solemnly " There is no other course available to us, " the telepath empathized. Whol bared his ugly maw " Once their network reaches the masses, the 4chan test will begin. Should they dissolve into chaos, we will eliminate them " Kroel bowed and exited. Happy that he had at least forestalled the demise of his precious studies. If only for a while.

(....) I yelped when I saw it. This I will admit nowhere but here. When I saw it for the first time, I yelped like a startled child. I dug my nails in the cave wall and held on for dear life, as if that could save me from what my eyes were seeing and my mind refused to accept. It was... in all the years, I am yet to find the words. It pierces your eyes but it's not light; there is nothing there but it is not darkness. It's gone when you try and see and there when you look away. You try and look and all you see are after-images of everything that is not it, and the pain, the dull ache as your mind tries to make any, even the smallest bit of sense. So I shut my eyes, and kept them shut until my guide spoke. " Isn't it beautiful? " he said, and I looked at him like he was a madman. " What is this? " I demanded. Tried to demand, really, because I think it was a weak croak. " This, my dear- " he said, and I wanted to hit him again " -is our way across! " He sounded positively giddy. I really wanted to hit him, and hard, somehow knock the crazy spirit out of him. It wasn't until later, much later that he would explain it to me, tell me about the Lich and the Spell, the Collapse and the Divide. Later, he'd explain (or at least try to) how it worked, how these crossings worked, but back then, I had more important things on my head. " Are you insane?! " I shouted, glaring at him. Somehow, looking at his worn coat and stupid grin was preferable to the nothingness behind him. And I swear the damned, damned, thrice damned warmblood actually hesitated. But he never answered. He blinked as if remembering something and reached into a pocket to pull out that round golden locket he carried with him. I remember calling out in frustration and actually reaching out in his direction, because I didn't recognize it yet and clearly this was the time to look at a painting of his parents, mate, offspring or whatever it is warmbloods put in those. Then he looked at me and called out " Come on, we don't have much time! " " Have you lost your mind?! " I demanded again, missing the wall that I left behind. " I'm not coming near that- that-! " I gestured feebly at whatever lay past the ledge. And... this I remember, he rolled his eyes and rubbed them with his fingers, and then he gave me this look, the calmest, sanest one I've seen from him yet. Later I realized, that maybe that carefree attitude was how he coped with a world that wouldn't make sense, but this, this was how he was when it was life and death. " Fine. " He said, calmly, evenly. " But we won't get another chance, and you'll have to go back, empty-handed. " I thought of coming back, a failure, and I shuddered. I nodded. What could I do? I nodded. That damned smile of his returned, and he turned and started walking towards the edge. " Come along then. " He called, almost playful. " Wait up! " I said and started after him, for a moment forgetting about the abyss in front of us. Even small as he was, I had to work to catch up. " How do we get across? " I called out. And he laughed. He laughed, and shouted " Like this! ." And he leapt. He just leapt. What was I to do? I jumped after, and I shouted, " I HATE YOU! " I remember... falling. A sudden impact that pushed the air from my lungs, yet didn't stop or even slow me. Noise. The rush of air. And then, hard stone underfoot and above my head, and a curving smooth wall before me. And noise again, a terrible, abyssal clattering right behind me, lights flashing like mad. I felt dizzy. I felt... a sense of wrongness. Like I did not belong. Like everything else was too small. And then there was that stench, an oppressive wall of old warmblood sweat. I'd come to hate that smell yet. And then the noise disappeared, and the flashing lights went dim, and I saw him standing next to me, with that damned grin of his. " Welcome to London! " He said, spreading his arms as if inviting an expected guest. " Hope you like it here. Now let's find you something to wear. " He added. And he was lucky I was dizzy and missed the punch, because you don't say that to a warrior. And so it, once more, began. - -065 [ more ] (rvonBoomslang)

"Larry?!" That voice. He knew that voice. He turned around from his view of the city sky line, its towers and spires lit up like a Macy's in December. Now in front of him was a 42 year old accountant (who would be a virgin if not for the Boy Scouts), unfortunately wearing what looked to be a bright red spandex suit with matching cape and mask that clung to every awful curve of his jiggling body. "Randy." He facepalmed harder than Picard after losing another Red-shirt. If only he could lose the one standing in front of him. "What the hell are you doing here?" the sad, mouth-breathing sop asked as he waved his arms in the air. "I am justice, you fucking plebian," he muttered under his breath, his hand struggling to massage away the headache growing at the front of his head. "Wow that's awesome, I'm Constipation Man!" jiggled the complete oaf of a human being. "Constipation Man?" Larry sighed. "You're goddamn right!" "You've got to be shitting me." Oh wait, he can't. "I wish I could!" shouted Randy from what was too small a distance to even stand next to a person, let alone throw his spittle and verbiage all over their face every time he talked. Larry turned away. This shit of an excuse for an intelligent life form would not hinder his vengeance tonight. No. No one could stop the sour wrath of the Elemonator. "So why yellow? Isn't that kind of a lame color for a super hero outfit? I mean who wears yellow?" yelled Randy. "Wolverine." replied Larry, quickly and without an ounce of emotion. He can not feel emotions they will only hinder him on his path to justice. "Ohhhh, good point." Larry was dressed from head to toe in yellow spandex, sans cape they were just too dangerous. He needed to survive long enough to ensure the flames of his wrath had reached all who had a hand in the injustices that he had suffered. "Besides, I'm not yellow because I think it is cool. I'm yellow..... for what it stands for," he growled. "Cowardice?" "No "Joy?" "Nev "Jaundice?" "No, you don't "Ohh, lead paint." "NO YOU WORTHLESS SON OF A "Wait! I get it. Snow." Randy was now nodding confidently, the crinkles in his neck only highlighted by the obnoxious hue of his costume. "I give up." muttered Larry, feeling rage. Yes, good, rage, he needed that. He was angry..... no..... furious. YES! Furious! They had taken away everything he loved. He went to that same shop, FroYO Momma on the corner of Winkle St and Harrison Avenue, for every week on Friday for 22 years, and ordered the same damn thing everytime. The ONLY thing that could satisfy his incredible urge for the succulence..... the sournosity his taste buds so painfully craved: their Lemon flavored frozen yogurt, Lemonberry Sunshine. It gave him life, happiness. He could always rely on a cup of the stuff to change his day for the better. Now? Now it was gone. Now, FroYO Momma was no longer where it stood. Now it was the Super Shop, a one stop all-you-can-think-of emporium for run of the mill, everyday losers like he and Randy to go and drown their sorrows in delusions of grandeur. People walked in as idiots, and left as idiots with less money and a shitty costume..... and they LIKED IT. Ass loads of people suited up and became "masked avengers" over night, and now, now he will never get his delicious frozen happiness. So he decided to become a villain, the Elemonator, a masked vigilante willing to execute his justice on anyone that was responsible for the buying out of FroYo Momma and the astounding overnight success of the Super Shop..... including himself. But he'd leave that for another day. Tonight..... tonight he'd start with Randy. His hand moved instinctively to his hip, resting on the handle of his water gun, no, he'd need another name for that. Lemonsqueeze? Hmm, whatever, he could think of another name later. Either way, he'd use it deliver his sticky, sour justice across the city until he was satisfied, shooting lemon juice into the eyes of those that poured concrete into his soul. "Let's begin."

To my 18 year old self, You've got nothing to regret. I know you don't believe me, and it is me, but if you don't make mistakes how to do you know what is correct? You won't know what I am talking about until you get there and then to here. You are going to be terrified of the world you find yourself in and you aren't going to want to live sometimes. You are going to hate everything and hate yourself for it. And you are going to cry. I don't mean to scare you. I don't want hurt you. But you are going to be hurt, by yourself, by others, but mostly by yourself. And he's not pleasant. He is vindictive and some of the things he is going to do will shock, surprise and sicken you. You will learn that he doesn't want you to be him and that there seems like nothing he could do to stop himself. Just keep going. He is you and he is me. He is more scared of himself than anything else. Even the fear of failure and depression that is going to plague him. He doesn't know what he is doing to himself, and eventually to you. I want to tell you this because I wish someone did. I wish someone had given me a heads up that life can get much worse. Worse than you ever thought and the worst part is that, outside of your head, life is okay and actually has the capacity to be good. It takes some time of being him to learn what I am telling you. I'm not telling you this so that you can prevent it. You can't. You can only learn to see it coming and do your best to minimize the frustration. You will learn that you need to have a release valve for him. You are going to live with your depression for the rest of your life, but as I sit here crying because I wish you didn't have to go through this, I know somethings can be okay sometimes. And it's enough to get to keep moving. Hopefully, Forward. I don't actually have advice because you won't listen to it just like I didn't and I still have a problem with doing now. I just want to say I love you, and you at least deserve to love yourself even though he is frustrating. Only do your best to remember that and when you can't love yourself, take him for a run. He seems to feel much better after that. I love you, Your Future Self

My foot crashes through the door of the tavern, sending wooden splinters flying. The group of men harassing the bartender shoot to their feet. Though surprised, they draw their swords and get into a fighting stance. The man on the far left is trying his best not to show that his knees are shaking. Amateurs. They rush me. I draw my sword as the first one makes his move. His guts spill out onto the ground before he can even understand what has happened. The next one puts up a bit more of a fight, raising his sword to block mine, but he's still not prepared when I shove a fireball into his abdomen, causing him to scream in pain. His scream is cut short as his head topples from his shoulders. The third one is tougher, clearly more experienced. He dodges my strikes with ease, weaving between the swings of my sword and avoiding the fireballs I hurl in his direction. For a moment it looks as if he may have the upper hand as he knocks the sword from my hand, causing it to slide across the room. He backs me into a wall, and his sword raises into the air above my head. It's the opening I need. I drive a dagger into the bottom of his skull, sealing his jaw to his head. He's dead before he can even process the pain. I stroll to the other end of the room and pick up my sword. As I do, the last man drops his blade and falls to his knees. Tears begin to stream down his face, and from the large dark spot appearing on his trousers I can see he has wet himself. "Please. Have mercy," he stammers. "I'll leave. I promise. Just let me go and you'll never hear from me again." I walk over to the man and kneel in front of him, bringing myself to eye level. "Do you know who I am?" He tries to steady his voice as he looks back into my eyes. "Y-you're Harvey Black." "Now, see, if you knew that, then why did you still come to my town?" The man tries to speak, but I cut him short. "Deliver a message to the king. Tell him that this is my town, and if he sends his scum here again, I'll do what I did to..... Are you even listening?" "I-I'm sorry. It's just a lot to The man stops his stammering as I drive my blade through his mouth and out the back of his head. He chokes on his own blood as I remove my sword and he falls to the ground, lifeless. As I stand I turn to the bartender and smile. "Don't you worry. You're safe now." "I didn't ask for your protection!" the bartender bellows. "Why won't you just leave us be?" "Leave you be?" I step toward the man, and he backs against the wall. I don't like scaring people, but at the moment I don't care; he's upset me now. "I'm protecting you. I saved your life from the royal guards. You should be thanking me." "Thanking you? You killed those men in cold blood! They didn't do anything to me. They were looking for you! " I ignore his insane ramblings and turn to look around the bar. Most of the patrons have left, and the few that remain are huddled against the walls in fear of the royal guards. "It's alright!" I say. "You're all safe now. No need to thank me." Silence. I can feel my face contort in rage, and suddenly against my better judgement I cleave my blade through one of the bar tables, eliciting screams of surprise from the civilians. "I said,'No need to thank me. " A quiet round of "thank yous" come from around the room, and pride swells in my heart. I sheathe my sword and go to exit the building. "Remember everyone! If any royal guards come around town, just send them my way and I'll be sure to protect you!" I'm just about to leave the bar when a single voice speaks up from the corner of the room. "You're a monster." I turn to look and see a young woman crouching in the corner of the room. She's trembling in awe of my magnificence, but her face is stern, doing her best to hide the excitement she's feeling at seeing me. I wonder, not for the first time, if I'm really doing the right thing here, or if I may be doing more harm than good. Perhaps I'm misreading the situation, I think. But the cheerful voice in the back of my head reminds me that I'm doing this for the good of the kingdom, and all of those fears melt away. As I leave the tavern, the screams of the civilians continue to fill my ears. They sob in fear as they hold the charred body of the woman, unaware that they are mourning the death of a loyalist to a corrupt king. I give one last call back to them as I walk off into the night, the reward of a job well done still warming my heart: "I'm not a monster," I say. "I'm a hero."

"I am old now, old to my bones, and weary of travel." Olm looked down on his granddaughter Elm, whose eyes were widened with youth and green as spring. He smiled. "I've walked many roads with these bones of mine, and each path taken has left its mark, its wear." He showed her the wrist, where the infamous crescent scar marred his tanned flesh, a grin from the past itself. "This particular nasty wound was given to me by a dragon." Elm narrowed her eyes, looking startlingly mature. "Dragons don't exist, grandpa. I'm not stupid." Olm sighed, feeling tired, and his bones might as well have groaned with him. Youth, they didn't know how to appreciate a good story anymore. "A dragon can take many shapes," he grumbled, frowning the bushes of his eyebrows. "Many forms." For a moment he collected his thoughts, until Elm interrupted: "Grandpa!" "Yes, yes," Olm mumbled. "Ahem. This particular dragon was in the business of kidnapping princesses. Now it just so happened that he had abducted the most beautiful princess of all, a girl whose eyes were as radiant as the sun, and whose spirit was fiercer than the molten core within." "The sun's not molten, grandpa, it's fusing gas." Olm shook his head. Kids these days were too smart for their own good. Sometimes too much knowledge got in the way of solid wisdom. "The point," he said, "Is that this princess had a spirit that burned so bright, that the dragon became jealous and wanted to take her for his own. Even though the princess was already promised, to a handsome prince." Olm paused and stroked his beard, trying to look noble, and Elm couldn't help giggling. "The princess could do better!" "Probably," Olm conceded, "Yet she meant the world to the prince, as you now mean the world to me, Ellie." Elm beamed, and Olm paused for a moment, recollection misting over his eyes. "If only I had been able to show her that..." Olm shook his head. A man takes many paths in life, and only when he looks back, does he see the distance travelled, the paths he could have taken. The mists of time had come, and went again. "But we were talking of the dragon." Elm had gone quiet, with that children's intuition of sensing deep emotion. "Life is funny, Ellie. I could have chosen to reason with the dragon..... or to have faith that the princess would figure a way out of his claws alone. Instead I chose to fight." "Did you use a sword?" Elm's emerald eyes were full of excitement. Olm nodded slowly. "Swords were the customary way of dueling at the time. And I was spry, when these bones still had spring in them." Olm made a riposte with his hands, and Elm grinned. Olm was quiet for a moment. "I intended to merely scare the dragon off, but a fight is like a wildfire, especially against dragons: it moves in unexpected ways, and each flame sparks a bigger one." Elm nodded, grasping the metaphor this time. "So the dragon bit you?" Olm peered at the scar, saying: "Yes. The thing about wildfires is, they grow and grow, until they consume you. In the end, I slayed that dragon." He shook his head. "I went too far. Life is sacred, even that of lecherous dragons. What I didn't realise was that the princess, whose spirit burned so brightly, had come to love the dragon's flames." A deep sadness had come over Olm, as he looked at the scar. "When I snuffed the flame of the dragon's life, I also killed the love in the princess's heart. She foresook our kingdom in search of something to revive her light, and never returned." Elm looked up, her eyes bright and understanding. "The princess was grandma, wasn't she, grandpa? Do you wish she had stayed?" Olm smiled sadly at her. she had always been too clever, his granddaughter. "I've walked many paths with these bones of mine, Ellie, and sometimes, I admit, I did dwell on roads I could have taken, or sought paths back to her. But it does no good to speak of roads not taken." He looked at Elm, her green bright eyes, those eyes that burned with an indescribable fire of their own, and smiled. "Because this is the only path that lead to you, Ellie." Elm reddened and rolled her eyes. "Grandpaa..." she complained, the child again. "That's so cheesy." Olm chuckled, watching her get up and run out into the blossoming garden, where her parents were sitting, talking. And for a moment, his bones felt young again.

The doctor strode into his office, a calm, complete stride that he had adopted working in the mental facility. No physical uncertainty translated to no mental uncertainty - and he needed that kind of protection working with the patients. After thumbing through his strictly organized file cabinet and removing a crisp manila folder, the wizened doctor lowered himself into his office chair and swung to face the man seated in front of him. The best way he could be described is paradoxical - While his body was stringy and lean, his eyes conveyed deep strength and determination. Determination, it was evident, to get out. "Jesus" the doctor drawled, his impatience lining his face. "You must understand. I can not legally release you until you've proven to Ms. Sarah" he motioned to a portly woman standing by the door. that you are well and will not continue any of your previously threatening actions." Jesus Christ smiled, the small wrinkles on his face turning into a smile and enveloping the entire room with warmth. "I'm not here to ask for release." The doctor looked intrigued. "I'm here to ask that you trust your whole life in me." Jesus removed a large scroll of paper from his baggy uniform. "Here are my terms and conditions." The doctor slid the paper over, peering into his eyeglasses. "Wha- The Ten Commandments?!" The doctor angrily discarded his 12th copy of the law code. "Find out where he gets those in a high security prison!" The doctor shouted as the pair exited. He turned back to his desk, removed a bottle of Advil, placed one in his mouth and snatched up his water bottle. A few minutes later, the doctor's secretary was seen discarding the contents of his water bottle reluctantly, it had been a long day and she needed some wine. Edit: Breaking up of text

It has been one year since that night. The stars had seemed to skip across the sky as we went about our merry lives, drinking and feasting on earthly delights, with young eyes flirtaciously dancing across both a pub table and drunken shouts alike. You had been beautiful. Our friends had slowly drifted off, leaving just the two of us to sip our drinks furtively and claw at conversation. I held your hand as I walked you home, and the taste of the cheap sugary alcohol on your lips blasted through me as I leaned in for a goodbye kiss. I remember you then, full of vigour and the beauty of your youth. Passionate and wonderful the kiss lead to coffee, which lead to the night I remember in my dreams. I left early the next day for work, your face was a watercolour of sunlight as I scratched my mobile number into the paper, and left it beside you. You stirred with a smile as I planted one last kiss upon your forehead. I waited for weeks, but the phone never rang, and the message never got delivered. I walked back to your flat but only saw darkened curtains and an empty hallway. Perhaps it was just a chance encounter of two minds alike in the same place and time, I hadn't wanted to be too eager, and over time my memory dimmed. Imagine my surprise one year on to get a text from a strange number, only to discover it's you. Despite how long it's been my heart fluttered in anticipation, as we agreed to meet. You hold yourself differently now. There is a weathered strength in you I couldn't see before, and as you talked of planets and aliens, of rebellions and distant rulers my heart lurches out of orbit, plummeting into regret. I want to help you, but I know I can't. Despite myself though I listen, and hope to see through the madness you speak. You tell of the first few days you returned, the emotional reawakening of your family ties, and wanting to continue with your old life, including a phone number from a night in times past. You show me artifacts and letters, strange devices and armour from wars fought in the darkness of space. The dawning realisation that I believed you was both petrifying and exhilerating. We talked again, two minds alike in the same place and time, and the end result was as beautiful as it was before. I awoke first, and the curiosity burned inside. I planted a kiss on your forehead as I walk across to your collection, to gaze at your other life. It was a small thing, but I shouldn't have touched it. A device, cylindrical, no more than a centimetre in diameter, attached to the armour glistening with artfacts out of imagination. I prodded it like a caveman with a fire, and it leapt up and burnt my hand. It speaks to me now, it controls me. It is from him. He whose intergalatic empire was brought crushing down by one lonely woman. I see you now, as I sit outside my own mind. The pillow resting firmly over your mouth as I watch the starlight glisten in your tears, as I watch the light dim from inside you. I want to help you, but I know I can't.

I sat at the coffee shop with my fiance Brooke. We had been engaged for about 6 months and were aggressively planning our wedding. Sure, it was stressful, but worth every second. The smooth jazz constantly empowering my internal presence assured me that every small argument we had over this matter was completely harmless. All seemed well until Brooke's ex walked into the coffee shop (He had a brown vest on for some reason. Looked kind-of retro) As the music remained the same, I assumed he was not going to come talk with us, or even see us with that matter. The ambience knows everything after all. Just then... out of nowhere.... the smooth jazz turned to the.... the Imperial March (I had never seen Star Wars. But I knew it from that Volkswagen commercial. Funny stuff) Something was coming. It had to be Jerry. Stupid Jerry. He was going to come try to fight me and get Brooke back. I had to be ready. As the music slowly built up, Jerry noticed us. He was coming our way. Even thought I was proud of myself for finally having my powers adjust to music used in the media, I had to act. I saw something shiny in his pocket too. This was all happening so fast. As he got closer, he reached into this pocket for the shiny object. " Hey Brooke and- " Before he could say any more, I decked him in the face. He wasn't completely knocked out, but he was close. It was a good punch. I was proud of myself. It had to be done. A gasp came from the fellow coffee shop goers and the Imperial March stopped, and the smooth jazz came back on. " Dave, what the hell? " The shiny object then came out of his pocket.... and it was one of those mints you get at coffee shop counters. " Brooke... the music... it was.... " The manager then walked up to me. " I can't believe you started on a fight on Mos Eisley Cantina Night! You're out of here! " That is when I noticed the band. Shit.

You slowly open your eyes to find that your hands are covered in blood, and a pile of bodies lay around you. It was a simple adventure, the reward was big. In YOUR eyes, you see countless enemies with swords and spears pointed at you. They were the targets. In YOUR mind, you heard them grumble and say words like "steal, murder, revolution." They were evil. You hacked and slashed away, you have done this many times, over many conquests, over many lands. In YOUR eyes, you saw a better land, greener pastures and a better tomorrow for those you leave behind. They were the ones in the way of that future. Yet..... Why does this quest feel so different now? Why now? Why ONLY now? From the corner of your eye, the once greener grass turned gray, as the last of your opponents turned a dark red. From the depths of your ears, you hear them plead for mercy as the ones who struggled with their limbs cut off..... "No more..... the madman is stronger than us!..." You slowly open your eyes to find that your hands are covered in blood. The Jewel that lies on your chest..... was not the reward from a princess from a previous quest. No..... it was her heart. "Monster....ughhh..." You turned your back and tried to comfort the dying man. "Who did this to you? Is he still around?!?" The man slowly points his finger at you..... "You..... you didn't even know..." slowly..... then suddenly drops his finger as he lays there motionless. "Who knew medieval men were this easy to trick?" Said a voice from a metal flying bird. "This is the limits of their imagination friend, They think it is magic when we brandished his weapon fire when we just added a oil and a lighting mechanism on his sword." said another voice from the same metal bird. "Who are you people!?!" "What did you make me do?!?" You screamed out loud as you begin to remember all the things that happened. You were granted a magical sword that breathes fire, imbued by magic by a magical cult. You were blessed with a magical helmet that you must not take off as it is a blessing to see the evils of this world. You were chosen when you turned 18...................as you were picked off the street by that cult. A cult of men and women in white robes that held pieces of board and paper. "Looks like he's trying to remember" said the voice. You slowly gripped your sword and tried to slash away at the metal bird. "Tsk..... I thought our experiment could go longer" "Abandoning FanAdv.03." "Quest completed, target however is able to recognize his actions and previous life, experiment failure, Lessons learned: Must increase Psycho neuron dosage to maintain questing form. FanAdv.04 will be done on parallel world KNG459. Moving out" The metal bird suddenly disappears into thin air. The weight of your sword suddenly got lighter..... It didn't breathe anymore fire and some type of oil was leaking from the tip. The new Kingdom army has a warrant on you: "Mass murderer and killer of the throne, Must be killed" it was one of the many papers scattered on the grass alongside the men's dead bodies. This was their blessing..... "I must move on, I must!" As you hear horses coming your way, you hide in the forest. As you vow to take revenge on this "cult." "They will pay."
