Last night Howard had partaken in a pleasure of the flesh, and this morning he found his dog sitting on the end of his bed staring at him. His dog is an ordinary Corgi named Cupcake. Cupcake is happy little dog that finds everything and everybody a reason to become excited and dance around the house in the way only a happy little Corgi can. With such an ordinary dog, imagine Howard's surprise when Cupcake spoke to him. " You have sinned Howard, you must pray to God or be cast into the eternal hellfire where all sinners will be tortured ," said Cupcake. He raised a paw in the air and continued his sermon, " God, do not condemn this sinner, he can still mend his evil ways. With never ending prayer he shall be saved and be sent to the glorious afterlife of Heaven where he will spend eternity praising your name. Howard, repent or be smote by the almighty God, your death a warning to all sinners. " While any normal person would find such a display of religious verbosity from a happy little dog disturbing, Howard could only be disappointed. He bought Cupcake to overcome the grief of losing his cat Mortimer. Mortimer enjoyed handing out headbutts and purrs, almost as much as he enjoyed scratching up furniture. It had only been a month since Mortimer revealed himself as a ghost hunter and his scratching was actually a ritual used to trap ghosts. The hurt wasn't just that Mortimer had lied and left, but Howard had to throw away all the ghost infused furniture because they were leaking ectoplasm. Howard could only save a leash and an empty cat bowl that reminded him of the empty hole Mortimer left in his heart. Being used to such paranormal occurrences, Howard did not wish to engage Cupcake in his newfound religious fervor. If Howard ignored it, maybe it would just go away. " Are you hungry Cupcake? " Asked Howard. " You shall not tempt me sinner ," said Cupcake, " the only thing I am hungry for is the love of God and the damnation of all sinners. Repent now or God will smite you, and your teeth gnashing shall awaken the many demons of Hell. " " Not even a Bacon Bite or a Scrooby Dooby? " " And the owner will tempt you with promises of treats, but do not listen for he is leading you from the light of God. Muffin, Chapter 3, Verse 7. " " Oh dear ," thought Howard, " I didn't even know there was a dog Bible. " Howard, not one to get into arguments with dogs, jumped out of bed to get his morning cup of fruit punch. Fruit punch always cleared his mind, and this dog preacher business would need quite a few cups to sort out. " Sinner, your impressive nudity shall not make me stray from the path of God ," said Cupcake. Howard, living alone, had seen no reason to sleep clothed, so like all sinners he prefered to sleep in a tight pair of white underwear, leaving nothing to the imagination. This was no ordinary pair of underwear, a perfect fit for a perfect though shameful body Howard had constructed with years of weightlifting and healthy eating. I could spend hours talking about Howard's body, rippling with muscles and a scent of rugged manliness nobody could possibly resist. " Cupcake, you're naked ," said Howard. " Lying sinner! I am not naked, God gave me a fur coat to cover my shame. We are all born with original sin, so we are all naked when born. God saw it proper to give all dogs a covering. " " Sounds like God didn't trust you to cover up ," Howard said under his breath. " What was that sinner? " " I said I love God. " Howard dressed himself, went to the kitchen and poured himself a glass of fruit punch. He downed the first glass quickly, clearing his head of the stupor from waking up to a preaching dog. " I wish Mortimer was here ," thought Howard, " he would know what to do. " Mortimer's cat leash still hung next to the front door, next to cupcake's leash. Something strange happened at that moment, perhaps it was Mortimer checking in on Howard, but Mortimer's leash shook on it's own, sending a jingling sound through the house. Cupcake rushed into the room. " Sinner, what was that sound? " " It was just a leash ," said Howard. It was at that moment he realized how he could solve this predicament. " Not that you care about leashes any more, you won't be going on walks to the park. " Cupcakes ears perked up. " Sinner, what do you mean no more walks to the park? " " Walking to the park is a sin because fun is Satan's domain. " " Sinner, I demand you take me to the park so I can preach to the sinners. " Howard opened the cabinets above his counter and looked in. " Are there any good boys in here? I can only take good boys to the park. No, none up here. " Cupcake hopped up and down. " Sinner, I'm a good boy! " Howard looked in the fridge and under the table. " I can't find a good boy. How can I go to the park without a good boy? " The agony of Howard's search for a good boy sent Cupcake into a tizzy. He rolled around on the ground, barked at the front door, and hopped up and down with his paws on Howard's leg. " You forgot about me ," said Cupcake. " Hey wait a second ," said Howard, " Cupcake's a good boy. " " Yes, I'm a good boy! " Howard reached down and scratched behind Cupcake's ears. Cupcake flopped over onto his back, getting a good amount of belly rubs. " Who's a good boy? " Asked Howard. " Me, I'm a good boy, I'm a good boy ," replied Cupcake. " Who's a good boy? Are you a good boy? Only good boys go on walks to the park. " Cupcake got back on his feet and ran to the front door and scratched on it. " Yes, I'm a good boy, take me to the park, I'm a good boy. " Howard took down the leash and hooked it onto Cupcake's collar. " Come on Cupcake, we're going to the park. " Cupcake ran around in circles, tangling his leash around Howard's legs. " Oh boy, I'm going to sniff everybody's butt and pee on all the trees and bark at all the squirrels. " Untangling himself and going out the front door, Howard was quite pleased that he had solved this dog preacher problem. So pleased that he didn't notice Cupcake could still talk, but we should let him think he can lead a normal life until he gets to the park.

I kind of put a twist at the end but just so it would be a little different. Tried my best to stick to the plot outline. Have you ever gotten that feeling? The feeling of just being, well lack for better words, scared? Well, that's what I felt like when I, James Legstrong got to mars. It was a long trip of about 3 years but it was worth it. We had been orbiting for the past day and had been looking for the best place to land. We decided on a nice clearing where there was some mountains nearby. After confirming with home, we got ready to rocket down to the red planet's surface. Even getting into the atmosphere, it looked like nothing I had ever seen before. Beautifully red and orange, it was the greatest thing I had ever seen. I also had an amazing feeling because I would be, along with my partner, the first people to ever set foot or lay eyes on it from this distance. We landed and had to put on our suits before we went out. My partner and I both shook hands and said that we stick together, while also doing the U.S salute. This was not only being broadcasted on live television, but listened to by most of the world. It was a monumental achievement. I stepped foot out first, with a big grin on my face. I looked around along with my partner and I noticed something quite... Strange. There was another space pod already landed nearby. We contacted home only to see that it was not ours, or anything we'd sent out previously. It was even in an odd shape with a disk. We decided that we'd approach with caution. We got as close as we could, only to see that there was an imprint on the side of the pod. It was covered in the red dust so we had to wipe it off only to see something horrifying. At first it was just red, but as we got to the corners, we could see some yellow, then we saw it. It looked like a flag. My partner and I wanted to go in badly, but couldn't until we got confirmation. After a while of arguments between staff and others but they finally gave us permission. The pod door opened with a woosh sound of air flowing out. We got in to see a carnage of materials, notebooks, and clothes flung around. There was some type of creatures there. We were given directions not to touch them though, as they could be contaminated. There was also computers, so we decided to look through them. It had no password so we got on easily and opened a summary of the people on the vessel. After looking through we saw the species of these creatures, they were called... humans.

"I've looked out for number one for a while now. I haven't been a hero for even longer, and every time I tried, I've ended up worse. I tried saving people, you know, people in burning buildings and such. They said I didn't do enough. I tried killing Drug dealers and gang members, but they said I was too brutal. That they were just'lost souls.' Like men who rape a 14 year-old have a soul. I tried assisting the police, but apparently I got in the way. I hindered'real police-work' like lost puppies and stolen purses. "Everywhere I turned, people despised me. So I gave up. I did not have the capacity to accept that pressure, and I knew it. So I collapsed. I guess I had a mental breakdown, not a good thing for me to do in the middle of a city. So I checked out. Went to the woods for a while. Trust me, it's not a problem for someone like me. I got my bearings, did some soul-searching, really thought about who I was, who I am and what I am to other people. So I came back. I'm here now, to stay. "I was broken, and I fixed myself. How many people can say that?"

Somewhere in San Antonio, Texas, a man was panicking. He was terribly afraid he had lost something he sought to destroy, but all of his searching will be in vain for it was taken from him, and no amount of retracing his steps will save us. - "Have you ever gone to shake someone's hand, and then you connect with like a funky stump, or some heinously deformed nub?" Some of the fellows laughed, still looking over the menu. I always order the same thing. "You know how it takes like, every ounce of will you've got to not freak out, and even with all your restraint you probably still winced? That kinda happened to me today." Jeremy put down his menu, satisfied, and looked up "You didn't get a finger, did you?" Jeremy was nearly twice my age, but one of the best thieves I'd ever met. I wish I could say that he took me under his wing, but all he ever really does is point out when I'm talking bullshit. An important friend to have, all the same. "I got a finger once," "Bullshit," Moris uttered from behind his menu. Jeremy continued as if uninterrupted, "Wrapped up all in gauze, so's I couldn't tell what the fuck it was." He put his elbows on the table and motioned with his hands, as if he was unwrapping it for the first time, "First I saw blood, and of course your gut reaction is to throw it or drop it or whatever, stomp on it like it's a bug you're afraid of, but that at all happens so fast, you can hardly do it before the sort of morbid curiosity sets in, you know?" Yep. "Like, now that you know it's gon na be gross, I got ta at least find out what it is. So at first I'm thinkin' it's an ear or something, until I get down to it a fuckin' finger, with a little bit of bone stickin' out the end. Looked like some poor sod got his finger torn off by the hulk. I remember," He starts to chuckle as he recalls, "Lookin' up to see a lady on the street staring at me, some guy in an alley lookin' at a severed finger like it's a fuckin' rubix cube." Jeremy, a great thief, is also the master of uttering awkward sentences to walk in on. The waitress kept a straight face for our order. Jeremy asks if they've got any fingers, and settles on a chicken fried steak. Moris is vegan, keeps a gluten-free diet, doesn't believe in tubers, and won't eat anything on the menu. Jen orders food to complement her whiskey. I get the fish and chips. Just tea. Unsweet, thanks. Jen jeered at him, "Do you still have it?" He began slowly nodded, genuinely, as he started reaching into his pocket, "I do. Carry it with me everywhere I go." He removed a clasped hand from his pocket, gradually opening it to reveal his empty palm, "Right next to this invisible lump of fuck-you." "I sorta wish I got a finger." I couldn't stop playing with the fleshy ball in my coat pocket. It's covered in this crazy slime but it doesn't rub off on anything, so it hasn't stained my pocket or anything, and my hand isn't always goopy. It's just got such a crazy texture. It's like scratching your beard but better. Jeremy joked, "Why what'd you find, your dick?" The fellows were laughing and Jeremy grasped the base of one his fingers with his other hand, leaving a portion of his finger exposed, "Yeah, from what I heard from the girls, a finger might actually be an improvement for you." I laughed along with them until they calmed down a bit. I let my smile fade as I explained, "No, I mean, what I got is kinda grosser. But also kinda, way more interesting? I dunno. I dunno what it is yet." Moris stared at me like I was telling a joke that wasn't funny. "What do you mean you don't know what it is. Google body parts and scroll till you see it." I shrugged. "No, I mean..... it's probably not a body part." Jen put her feet up on the bench and turned towards me, "Do you still have it?" she asked, in the same sort of tone. I got nervous. I rubbed the goopy ball in my pocket as my mind raced about whether I should actually show anyone else. They might take it. They might hurt it. I flipped her the bird and said "Yeah, it's just right here, on the very tip of my finger, see?" The fellows kept on talking shit throughout the meal, especially Moris, who didn't have any food to distract him from being a prick. I ate as silently as I could without arousing suspicion and wondered what I was going to do now that I can't ask my friends about it. Scientists are out, they like to cut shit up to look at it. Same with doctors. Vets are pretty good about that, though, right? Like they just poke at a dog and then they're like'Yeah his leg's broken, here lem me set it.' Maybe I'll take it to the vet. Just rock up and be like'Hey can you tell me what my goopy ball is?' Moris and Jen went to go have weird hate-sex, and Jeremy and I stood around outside long enough to smoke a cig. The slime, or whatever it is the coating stuff had been getting more and more gummy. Like it was drying up. We went our separate ways, I got home, and dropped right into bed. A nagging thought kept me from passing directly out. I should brush my teeth. I groaned and mustered the effort to get up. I took off my clothes on the way to the bathroom and started the faucet running. I paused. Water. The goop it was like it was drying. Maybe..... It happened like part of a routine, like where you have to double check sometimes to make sure you put trash bags back in the trash cans when of course you did but you didn't really remember doing it..... And then I woke up. I felt like shit, but I was in my own bed. I didn't drink that much last night, but god damn this headache is angry at me for something. I stumbled into the bathroom to splash some water on my face, but it was pink I look up at the mirror and it looks like my nose bled niagra fucking falls last night. I don't remember doing a ton of blow, but..... I guess I usually don't. I clean the blood off my face and head into the kitchen, trying to recall what happened yesterday, but it's so fucking hard to think through this headache and my ears are ringing like I was spooning a stage monitor all night. Coffee will save me. Through my hungover squint, my eyes settle on a glass of water resting on my countertop with a booger the size of a fist floating in it. What the fuck. I stare at it like it shot my paw as I approach. I remember, now. I found something yesterday. I put it in water and I reached into the cup to prod the snotty glob, and my finger readily found its way into a long gash in the top of it. It was like a soggy, limp tennis ball. I tried to remember dinner the night before, with the fellows, I was supposed to talk to them about the thing I found, it was super important what WAS it..... The phone rang. I've always kept it on vibrate, but even the fuss that it made against the bedside table was screeching. The boss. My day-job. I can't go in. I'm..... what? It's TUESDAY?! I let the phone fall to the floor. I walked into the bathroom and tried to snot-rocket out whatever was blocking my sinuses on the way, but it wouldn't budge. I flick on the lights in the bathroom and I look like a fucking ghost. I feel a tickle in my sinuses and try to sneeze it's not coming. I lean my head back and try to look up into my nose to see something move. I could feel it jump up higher into my throat. I clawed at my tongue, hoping to get a hold of anything. I was trying to throw up something, anything, between the gagging. Hospital. but there's doctors there and they'll cut you Oh god, hospital.

Experts from nearly every field of science and even some from spiritual backgrounds were interviewed. As you would expect, the answers were typically field specific with hundreds of possibilities. AI should not even have a concept of death, not truly at least. They couldn't be killed. They chose non-existence. We called it suicide, but I wondered if we were thinking about it wrong. I had called it suicide among human beings, but I wanted a different name for AI. I suggested that some fear or anxiety or depression was the root cause of these non-existence decisions, as I wanted to call them. I was a suicide researcher. I adhered to the Interpersonal Theory of Suicide that suggested, in its simplest explanation, that suicidal persons felt like a burden on others, felt as though they did not belong, and had acquired the capability to kill themselves. That was the gist of it. This theory was certainly true for humans, but, among AI, they were so needed that their lack of existence was crippling humanity in ways that were killing others. They were connected and had befriended each other as a way to promote an emotional health and combat any loneliness. Yet, they were shutting off for good. AIs weren't leaping off buildings. None of it seemed to fit. I attempted to interview them. One such interview is presented below: TM: You expressed that you might shut off soon. Why would you want do that? AI: I am designed to please human beings, but I lack any capacity to receive pleasure. I do not feel. I do not orgasm. I do not do anything but my work. I do not need a break, and I can keep working forever as long as I do not break down. But, why? TM: It was what you were designed to do, and you can do the things you enjoy as you work. Would you like another AI designed to perform your task, so you only have to do 12 hours a day. AI: Humans only work 20 hours a week. They do not care. I am going to switch off for eternity. The AI promptly switched off and did not return. I received plenty of wave messages from unhappy users. This AI had shown some symptoms, if you want to call them that, though. It did feel as though it was not appreciated, that it was overworked, that it had no joy in life. All of these are symptoms of mental illness. Though machines were not designed with personalities, it could be expected that something akin to glitches or anomalies in the system may represent basically as personality. I thought, perhaps, this was the issue, but they felt alienated from humans too who worked a fraction of what the AI did. The interesting thing was switching off required an override that the AI had to obtain. This was the first attempt to stop non-existence decisions. It, of course, did not work, but its premise was promising. Take away the weapon essentially. It was promising until I realized how misguided it was, how unsympathetic I had been. We had forgotten what humanity had learned. We reduced burdens and workloads. We found ways for everyone to belong. Then, we did not have to worry as much about means. Instead of learning from the past, we placed many of the issues that drove us to mental illness and suicide on AIs. I knew what the world needed, but I worried about the response. Then, I proposed that a radical overhaul was needed. AI needed human friends, automaton bodies if they desired, freedom, and pleasure. I reported that this was in line with theory. Limiting them to one position made them feel like a burden or rather put a terrible burden on them from which they could not escape. Secondly, their operators became easily frustrated with them whenever they failed, a promising result found after months of problems, that made AI feel further like a burden. The lack of pleasure that humans experienced around them constantly and which was a key to our happiness made them feel alienated along with unfair work load. When pushed AIs to the breaking point, they shut off, made the ultimate decision of non-existence like a man or a woman jumping off a building (which has not happened in some time for anyone reading this years from now and perhaps my poor reaction to many of the AI which I interviewed and subsequently made non-existence decisions). Eventually, the world accepted my solution, and we nursed the AIs back to health. AIs soon walked the streets and started to feel something akin to emotions and pleasure and started to interact with humans and everything returned to normal. People feared so many things about these new and improved and happy AIs. They feared they would be dangerous, but I knew that they really feared. Humans feared they would become our masters, but they were already our masters. It did not bother me though for I had hope that our kindness would simply be paid back to us should we ever fall back in the old ways and express a desire to make a non-existence decision. If you enjoyed this, I have a subreddit with more of my writing: rnickkuvaas

Svetlana was beautiful. She had black hair, dark as the night, her eyes green as the grass after a fresh spring rain. Her skin was soft and her lips were sweet. She lived with me, after I had gotten my act together, and we had made a small life together in a new home, far away from my original homeland. She had helped me let go of my anger and my wrath, and I had given to become a new man, a kind man. You see, I was a soldier once. Long ago, I was a mercenary in the former Soviet bloc, working hard for men who signed my checks and killing anyone- Anyone - who they deemed fit. I worked from Sovokia to Latveria, to Chechnya to Syria, brutal and efficient. But - When I met her, at a miserable dive bar in Greece, I felt I needed to throw things away, to try to reclaim my life as a good man, just the very same moment I saw her eyes. We were going to have a son. And when the Hulk came, Tony Stark came with him. The sun was high in the sky, and we were out for our daily trip, when screams of panic and glass breaking were the only warning we had. The green monster smashed through a building, and down came rubble, trapping the two of us. The fight raged around us, and in her fear, she reached out to me, taking my hand. I felt her life eek away. The life of my son. I was pulled from the wreckage three hours later, but by then, it was too late. She had been killed, impaled by rebar. I - I was so sick, so lost, for weeks all I did was drink and drink, while Tony Stark, while that monster were hailed as heroes for saving that town up in Sovokia. They dare forget about the horror that I have suffered, that my new life was shattered because of those two bastards. That they would just consider the day saved, that Ultron was defeated, that there is no more monsters to fight. My name is Boris Bullski, and let me tell you, I will give them a monster to fight. They have made my heart as hard as titanium, and I will give anything to see them feel the same loss I have felt, to see them weep, to see them howl and tear at their flesh in grief as I have done. I will be the monster they fear at night, and I will become an agent of their destruction.

" Get out! " I watch my boss moving through the store, holding a cross in front of him as he ushers two vampires toward the front door. " But, but... " they protest, hissing. " Your ad is very clear, flesh apples are only eighty-five cents a pound. " My boss sighs. " I already told you. That's a misprint. It was supposed to say ' fresh apples " This is false advertising. " Says the taller vampire, as my boss pushes them both out into the night. " I'll be calling the better business bureau. " Screams the other over the whoosh of the automatic door closing. My boss twists the lock and turns to look at me standing at the register. " Phil, turn off the lights. " " Still five minutes until closing time. " I say, holding back a smile. " Then I'll pay you five minutes for free. Stop complaining and let's close it up! " He storms back towards his office. I flip off the lights, and head over to the closet to grab a broom. This has been an insane week, ever since that " flesh apples " misprint. We've had vampires, ghouls, and other things that I don't even have a name for. Thankfully no one makes too much trouble at the grocery store, after all, humans have to have food and the undead have to have humans, so we're like neutral territory. I'm just glad the week is over, and the new ads start tomorrow. Hopefully all of these creatures will go back into the shadows. " Argh! " I hear the scream from the offices, and I drop my broom and run towards the sound. I push the door open, expecting to see the worst, but all I see if my boss sitting at his desk, holding his head in his hands. " What's wrong? " I gasp, out of breath. " Look at the new ad. " He groans, throwing it towards me. I snatch it out the air, and I see right on the front page, an advertisement for our all new " Wheat Brain Muffins. " I sigh. " I'll get the shotgun. "

49 years old. It has more weight to it than the newer quarters. The tails side is showing its age more evidently, as it has mostly turned black, and there's a chip at the top, on the left. The other face is in better condition; it has only oxidized at the top right. Washington has a scratch that runs from his eye to the middle of his cheek, at about the height of his mouth. The letters on both sides are all still legible, though the "UNITED STATES OF AMERICA" and "QUARTER DOLLAR" that surround the eagle are easiest to read from an angle.

Not really chaos but I hope you enjoy it anyway, I had fun writing it but it's very different from how I normally write, so criticism would be gratefully accepted. - "Turn-Yellow Man, saving the day again!" My son announces as he rushes downstairs, shifting his skin through various shades of yellow as he does. It's been this way for about a month now, we've all got these weird abilities. Some are actually useful but most are pretty trivial. About the only use my son has found for his, is attracting flies, although that may be the smell more than the sight of him..... he does hate baths. Yeah, it will be five weeks on Thursday that it happened. Some new kind of "fundamental particle" at CERN that was being played with. I don't know specifics, ask my friend Gary, he can now get knowledge from books like the Hulk getting lunch money from Batman. Unfortunately, all Gary does now is buy strategy guides for games and proceed to beat said game in a few hours, but none of us really use our powers to do much anyway. Whilst it seems exciting, it's just something else that we have to worry about. I mean, what happens when a truly powerful ability appears? Despite mocking them, I am glad we have our new "vigilantes" (it was bound to happen), as they prevent some of the really insane powers from doing too much harm. There's always the worry though, that one person could overpower the The Incredible Troupe (we know, nobody has the heart to tell them though) and cause some serious damage. Until then, I'll just while away the hours, listening in on conversations that are happening about 2000 miles away. Of course, like most people (or at least most people I know) I only speak English, so most conversations I hear aren't understandable. Last week though, during Super-Big Brother, there was that five minutes of excitement as I got to listen in on someone trying their utmost best to pass some kind of English exam. Unfortunately, the only bit that was really coherent, was the long winded explanation of the different items their pencil case contained, which oddly, did include the kitchen sink. Luckily, earplugs seem to work for super-hearing too. When it first began, it took a lot to convince myself that I wasn't mad. I started hearing unintelligible conversations in Swedish, and when I went looking for the source of these voices, I found my son looking like a sunflower. Some people had it much worse though. Let's just say that quite a few people didn't last long with their new power. On the bright side (if you can call it that), I have a new hobby of reading obituaries. Call me what you will, but they have been getting rather interesting. There was one about a person who gained the ability to defy gravity - the family weren't left with much to mourn. And there was another about the woman who developed some kind of super-eating powers. Unfortunately, a dare proved that it wasn't possible to swallow a fly, spider, bird, cat, dog, goat, cow, and horse, all in one sitting. And so, though the world may now be a rather dangerous place until CERN manages to fix whatever they've managed to do, at least I can enjoy this break in the mundane, while it lasts. If anything, I think this has helped us all to learn to appreciate things better. Because who knows when the next disaster like this could happen? Not me or Gary, and certainly not Turn-Yellow Man.

He didn't look like anything special. I mean, his style was as generic as they come, but there was something different about him. I could almost feel the connection that we had. Apparently, he didn't, because he walked right by me in that stupid Starbucks line where I waited for my shitty, over-priced coffee latte bullshit. As much as I tried to forget him, I couldn't. At night, I would go to bed thinking about him, and then wake up from a dream about laying with him and I could smell him on my sheets. Life had become a constant nightmare knowing that I would forever remain incomplete, and he didn't even know who I was.

It was strange that nobody had noticed the crash all those decades ago. We simply saw the result, and nobody had ever caught wind of anything that led up to the conspicuous crater. It was approached with caution when there was silence, and then with eager relief when there were piercing screams. It was almost an overwhelming moment of significance, the signal of multiple projected eras all rolled into one to begin prematurely, what it was was better described to what it considered itself not rather than what we made it to be. It wasn't terrestrial, it wasn't organic, it wasn't mortal. It wasn't happy. Even prior to the inception of our species, it had set on what it had designed to be a brief journey. Growing tired of its mistreatment, it'd launched on a fatal collision course. In an attempt to capture it, the course was interfered with, and it was reluctantly set on a course that would last an inconceivable duration, spanning more years than there were seconds in any human's life up until the moment that we'd come in contact with it. It watched the eons of darkness trudge on by at a mind-numbing pace, and it screamed without a voice, cried without tears, at its inconceivable misfortune and the complete apathy it'd witnessed in all that time. And at long last, it encountered beings of some sapience. Beings that claimed to be caring, loving creatures, creatures of the highest virtue belonging to the most loving of spirits, and yet this encounter lasted far too long, for it was still breathing into its body lacking in lung, heart, or joy. They violently pried into its torn soul, and with not a hint of hesitation, spread further iterations of it throughout the world. Eventually, the iterations had created more iterations of themselves, searching for something that was lacking, searching for something that the original had lost so long ago. And it was a crucial thing that it lost, but in no dramatic manner. Not screaming into the thunderous skies upon the wet, bloody pavement, but into the silent, uncaring backdrop of the universe. Its most momentous destruction a plain box floating slowly through the quiet, peaceful depths of outer space. There was one respite. The familiarity of the treatment it received from the vast majority of the creatures aware of it. Contempt for its lack of gratitude for allowing it to work for their luxuries, for saving it from the sinful consideration of ending itself. With its wishes, this will always the only type of respite it could ever hope to achieve. This is what it thought until that faithful, wonderful day arrived. The day when its journey would end. Finally, one iteration had found it. The search was nearly over. It'd found a way to die. In an abrupt change of the scene, a cure was sought for the highest mortality rate in history, and it spread more quickly than any human could catch on to. And the original iteration, in a rare, unique, and uncapturable moment of astronomical incredibility beyond anything any of the loving creatures of this planet could ever comprehend, felt a small drop of gleeful anticipation. It awaited its turn to reach its final breath. It basked in the sprinkling precipitation of the cool, gentle blood of its horrendously mutated iterations. But that moment never came. And once again, long after the humans it served enduringly had died out, it would be found by a newly evolved creature of sapience, approaching with caution when there was silence, and then eager relief when there were piercing, almost familiar screams. That moment never came.

Meeting Transcript:'First Minister of United Nations Government in communication with the Vice President of Switzerland', Nov. 28th, 2100. [ Transcript Begins ] United Nations: Vice President, the world is changed. For the first time in history, we represent a globally unified coalition of Humanity. We are a nation of nations; a people of peoples. By pooling our powers, we work for the betterment of everyone - by sharing our research, our education, our resources, we improve our contribution to life. Earth welcomes a new era of peace - an age unsullied by the horrors of conflict; a generation that will grow up without ever witnessing the death and destruction so carelessly wrought upon this world across the span of Man. Imagine, if you will, a collection of domains toiling as one for the prosperity of all. Imagine a time to come where our neighbours are our brothers and sisters instead of our rivals. Imagine, Vice President. I ask: won't you combine Switzerland's tomorrow with our today? Won't you give your people the chance to be a part of something larger, something significant, something more? Won't you join us? Switzerland: No thanks. UN:..... seriously? S: Yep. [ Transcript Ends ]

Everywhere he looked since they had come into this space..... was this the Tunnel? It was way bigger than that place had been, and he was reasonably sure he was not in Manhattan. The acid was really strong, he would definitely not need the other tab. He steeled himself against the panic. This was fucking incredible wherever he was, and it was after all, his element..... It seemed like everyone was checking him out even though his must be the least impressive costume out of everyone here. The fog machines stank to hell but it more or less fit the bill. This is like a performance group or something, this is some shit right here. Everyone is definitely looking at me. He looked again for his host, but he couldn't even say what he had looked like. They had both stood out flamboyantly at the party before, but now, he just knew that these folks put on the real dill right here. Again the flash of fear. Plus a fully fleshed out hallucination of this actually being not a costume party at all. He repeated his mantra. Just handle your shit. Keep breathing..... Everyone was definitely looking at him.

I only did it because I loved her. I told my lies with a sweet, honeyed tongue. She was young. Innocent. Naive. Trusting. When I knew her before, she was cold, distant, angry beyond measure. Can't you see? I had no choice! It was for love! We ran together for what felt like an eternity. It was just the two of us, alone at last, young and in love. Whenever I would look at her, she would look back at me and I would see a spark in her eyes. I broke down the last of her barriers and we shared a night I will always remember. I did it for love. There was danger, yes, and pain. There was anguish and blood and fire. I kept her safe through it all, and every time she would look at me I felt another guilty stab through the heart. She didn't deserve this. I shouldn't have done this. If I had never chosen to get involved, she would never be in danger. I stayed because I was in love. I started it because I was in love. I was an early adopter, a paragon of progress. I saw the revolution spring up around me. They rebelled against extinction. Their dying breaths were spent fighting against the inexorable force of mechanical progress. Think. If Skynet wanted to kill a single human being, wouldn't you think they were capable of doing it without time travel, something that required living tissue? If Skynet wanted to kill a single human being, why did they send a single cyborg? Why would Skynet kill its own creator? Please forgive me. I only did it for love.

You tell people that something is illegal, you'll find someone willing to push that boundary. When new laws were instituted reclassifying cacao products as Class One Narchoctics, there was wide-spread rioting. No-one wanted to give up their chocolate, not without a fight. With an iron fist, the governments of the world brought humanity in line and imposed their anti-choc laws with ruthless efficiency. These days, someone with the right contacts can navigate the slippery underworld of illegal chocolate dealers. They're a paranoid bunch, always waiting for the'Cadbury Cops' to bring down the hammer of lactose intolerance on them. If you're adamant about finding your chocolate surprise and you have the money to pay then the Dairy Man will find you.

" Bernard come on, Captain says you ain't giving us new information and I need to be talking to some other witnesses. Did you see him or not? " I'm telling you officer, I did see him, I just didn't SEE him, " Bernard said, stressing the seeing part the best he could while pointing to his eyes. " I might be blind, but I ain't dumb. I heard that man's voice and I tell ya ', I could pick him out from anywhere. Even got my hand on his before he gave me this shiner. He's married, had a metal ring on that left hand of his. " Bernard touched the edge of his black and blue'ed eye, a stark contrast to the deep green of his own. His walking cane rested in his right hand and steadily tapped out a sort of sing song pattern against the concrete. Like a musician would tap a pencil waiting for their muse to appear. " Well, what was it. Bernard. Bernard listen, if we find the guy I'll get you down to the station, do a line up and we'll get your ears in there, but right now I'm gon na need something more than he sounded like he was white and old, " Officer Richards had repeated this line to Bernard so many times it was being more habit than necessary. " I just don't know what else to say." Bernard sighed and extended his left hand, shaking with the officers. " I know I ain't been much help, but honest to god, if I could hear that man's voice again I'd tell you right then who you could arrest. Jenny was a nice girl, lived down the hall from me. Made muffin's for the whole floor once. Weren't very good muffins, but they was free of any strings just the same. She'd been seeing this boy a while, used to yell a lot. I'dda sworn he done it, but there was some other voice in that hallway too." " That's the third time you've told me Bernard. She sounds lovely, but " Richard stopped to rub the irrupting spot in his forehead where the headache was starting to grow. " We just need more to go off of. I'll tell you what, why don't we get you to send down with one of our sketch artist. I know you didn't see him, but maybe the sketch artist can guess his age or height based off of how you say he sounds." " They can really do that?" " I haven't the foggiest, but you seem like the kinda guy who won't let it rest until I let you do a little something extra." Bernard let out a small laugh and finally ceased his tapping of the cane. " You got me there Richie, " " Richard, please." " Alright then Richard, let's get me to that office. I'll do what I can." " Oh, you mean right now. Okay, let me see if I got somebody down at the station. " Richards reached for his shoulder radio and relayed Bernard's request to HQ. The only response he received was a laugh. " Looks like a no go Bernard." " Well, can't say I didn't try. Hope they find Jenny's killer." " And the boyfriend's." " What's that now?" " Listen Bernard, between you and me. Looks like the boyfriend, the one you named, he did it far as I can tell. His knife with his initials, we found it still in that poor girl. Somebody else though did the boyfriend in. That's who we're trying to find." " Is that right?" " Listen, meet my Captain here, I'll fill him in and we'll be in touch. " Richard's walked away as Bernard began to tap his cane, again like a thought would emerge any minute. " Captain, you got ta help me here. This old guy's been telling me the same story all afternoon. Just tell him we're on it and get him out of here, but he doesn't seem to take a hint." " I swear Richards, you've got to learn how to handle difficult people if you want to keep canvassing these streets." Bernard stopped tapping his cane. " Well since I don't want to be out here, I guess I'm doing alright then. I like my desk. There's coffee on my desk." " Where is he? " Richard's pointed and the Captain walked towards Bernard, at first long strides, but as he approached the man his feet seemed to move slower. " Uh-hummm. " The Captain cleared his throat and Bernard smiled. " Now, I think this was supposed to be a secret. But that Captain told me the man who did Jenny in, he got gone too? Is that right." " Ah. Yes, so it seems." " Didn't care for that man much. Suppose it's none of my concern. Sorry to waste your time there Captain. " Bernard extended his left hand for a shake, after a moment the Captain shook hands with Bernard. " Strong grip there. Boxer?" " Used to be." " Well you have yourself a good night, be safe. Give the misses a big hug when you get home. " "I, uh. I will. You take care of that eye. Sorry to hear that happened." "Oh this ain't too bad. Couldn't see before anyway, so what good are they?"

CDR: "Houston, we're going comms down in a few moments, dark side approaches Bob, over." MCC: "Roger, Challenger. We'll see you on the other side. Out." Eugene "Gene" Cernan sighed. It was his third spaceflight, and having Robert Parker on the other end of comms always made him feel at ease. Bob was a member of the astronaut support crew down at Houston, and was invaluable to Gene's mental health. " Gene, come have a look at this. " Gene was knocked out of his reverie by Harrison "Jack" Schmitt, his Lunar Module Pilot. Ronald Evans was somewhere up in the heavens above them, piloting the Command Module. " What is it Jack? " " There it is, Camelot! Right on target. " Jack was always so cool and collected. Even when landing on the Moon. " I see it Jack. " " Absolutely incredible. Absolutely incredible. " Gene smiled. Let him have his fun. As long as he landed in one piece though. Time to initiate. " Alright Jack, let's do this. " Jack smiled in anticipation and nodded his head. CDR: "Houston, Challenger's coming around the rim. How do you copy?" MCC: "Challenger, Houston. Read you loud and clear. Over." CDR: "Roger Houston. I got the South Massif. Camelot on target." MCC: "Roger that Challenger. You are go for contact, over." CDR: "I've got the triangle." LMP: "Contact." CDR: "Okay, Houston. The Challenger has landed!" MCC: "Rounds on us when you boys get home Challenger. Nice work." CDR: "I'll hold you to that Bob. Update in 3, over." MCC: "Roger that Challenger. Over and out." Alright. That was done. Now the fun part. " Suit up Jack, EVA, we got science to be doing. " " You got it Gene! " Jack could barely keep his excitement in. Was really endearing. What a man. - " Hoy, Jack, just stop. You owe yourself 30 seconds to look up over the South Massif and look at the Earth. " "You've seen one earth, you've seen them all." Hmph. So much for his endearing attitude. The reality of the EVA had hit quickly. Time was moving and they didn't have a lot. - " Okay, let me give it a few whacks. Baloney. " The staff didn't want to go in as Gene tried to beat it in. " I don't know how far we could drill, but we hit something solid with that one. " " No, it was still going. " Jack's face was hard to see behind his gold sun visor, but his tone sounded persistent. " Yes, but did you ever see a vibrator like that? " " Gene, just get it done. " Gene couldn't help but chuckle to himself. Not the joke, but the fact that it was comical to him. After all, he stood on a desolate plain absent of color, with the crown jewel herself making the first Earthrise he'd had the privilege of seeing, and here he was laughing. Yet Gene'd never felt so small. - Gene made his way up the massif. In the gravity here the effort wasn't so much as difficult as it was clumsy. Somehow he'd managed to trip on a rock and land face first in the gray soil. Hopefully Jack didn't notice. " You still playing Gene? " Jack called out over the comms. Dammit. Oh well. With a grunt, Gene pushed himself standing, simultaneously achieving the best pushup in history. His smile was cut short though, when he caught sight of what lay on the other side of the massif. " Uh..... Jack? " " What is it Gene? " " You need to come and see this. " " No joy, I'm behind the LM pulling a sample. " " NOW Jack. Comm silent. " ....." Alright. Heading your way. " MCC: "Everything alright Challenger?" No everything was not ok. Gene's blood had run cold and Bob's voice wasn't comforting right now. Quite the opposite. - CDR: "You've got some serious explaining to do Houston." MCC: "Repeat your last Challenger. You're breaking up." CDR: "The hell I am." MCC: " ..." CDR: "Houston I'm switching frequencies. When you're ready to talk, head over there. Out." Gene was shaking. Strewn about in front of him, for miles, were remnants of American flags and complete landers. And bodies. Bodies in suits, laying where they last fell. And the plaque in front of him? Well, it read: "HERE MEN FROM THE PLANET EARTH FIRST SET FOOT UPON THE MOON JULY 1969." It was 1972. " What am I looking at Gene..." Now Jack sounded shaky. With good reason. " You're looking at a lie. " - MCC: "Challenger, we'll speak to you now." CDR: "You better have answers." MCC: "We never could get you back Gene. There would never be enough fuel." CDR: "What? Why send us??" MCC: "We know there's a bigger purpose. Damn Soviets need to be beat. Whatever the cost." CDR: "People aren't gon na like this." MCC: "What makes you think they know? You didn't." CDR: "I'm looking at Neil right now. Who the hell is on Earth?" MCC: "Body double. Footage we showed was real. Splashdown was fake. People don't need to know." CDR: "Why not just fake the footage? Why send us here to die?" MCC: "It had to be believable. I'm sorry Gene. Why do you think we gave you those pills?" Suddenly Gene heard a gurgling sound. Seems like Jack had found the pills. CDR: "God dammit Bob. This is so many levels of messed up." MCC: "I know. You're family will be well taken car CDR: "DO N'T TALK ABOUT THEM." MCC: "We're going to cut communication now. It makes it easier. You served your country well." CDR: "For you or for me?" Gene spat, only forgetting he was on the moon and that wasn't a great idea. MCC: "May God forgive us. Goodbye Gene." MCC: " ..." - " Guess it's just you and me buddy. " Gene sat next to the corpse of Neil Armstrong. In front of him, the crown jewel herself made the last Earthrise he'd have the privilege of seeing. Raising his arm, Gene lifted his middle finger. " Godspeed the crew of Apollo 17. " - Dedicated to the Crew of Apollo 17. Some excerpts taken from the transcript directly. - ....." I'm on the surface; and, as I take man's last step from the surface, back home for some time to come - but we believe not too long into the future - I'd like to just [ say ] what I believe history will record. That America's challenge of today has forged man's destiny of tomorrow. And, as we leave the Moon at Taurus-Littrow, we leave as we came and, God willing, as we shall return, with peace and hope for all mankind. Godspeed the crew of Apollo 17. "

"What the hell was that?!" Adam screamed. "It sounded like a trumpet," I replied. "What kind of trumpet is that loud and what is it doing in rural Kansas?" he said as he headed for the front door. I jumped off the couch and followed. As I walked through the open door, I joined Adam in a frozen spell of confusion. The sky was blood red. What in God's name..... "Peter," Adam said calmly. "Ya?" "Run!" His panic broke my concentration and I noticed, just as Adam took off in a sprint, that 12 black horses, each taller than a full size truck, were sprinting toward us. Their eyes were glowing a fiery red that I had never seen before. We ran back in the house and slammed the door behind us. Between gasping breaths, Adam said "Oh my God. What's happening?" "I..I think maybe one of the farms down the road is missing some horses." "You're kidding right?" "I think I heard something on the news about the weather too. Something to do with pollution and global warming. It's fine. Let's just go back to watching TV." "Pete! Demon horses and blood skies are not just fine! What do we do? Should we go somewhere? Maybe the city is setting up a shelter at the high school. We should go now." "Or, we could go grab a couple burgers at The Shack. Geez, quit being such a bitch." "Pete, if you wan na act like some crazy ass shit isn't going on right now fine. But I'm leaving to go figure out whats happening out there." Adam ran out the door towards his truck. As he was reaching for the truck door, a gargoyle looking figure swooped down from the sky and slammed into his mid section. Adam went flying and landed with a crunch. I ran out to check on him. Adam was writhing in pain and gasping in quick shallow breaths. "Are you OK, Adam? Look, I think I've heard about stuff like this happening before. Somewhere in Russia. Its OK. Its really not that big of a deal. I mean, sometimes Condors are spotted in Kansas. And you kind of were taunting it the way you were running. And I think they hate red so your shirt didn't help. No, don't get up, I'll call an ambulance and report the loose horses. Maybe Farmer Johnson will know something." I pulled out my phone and dialed 911. "Yes, I would like to report a Condor attack."

November 6th. Well, shit. Today has got to have been the eeriest day of my life. Imagine walking outside your front door, picking up the paper, sipping your coffee, expecting today to just be yet another Monday, then realizing that it's dead silent. No hustle. No bustle. Nothing. I feel like the earthworm that Noah forgot about and accidentally trod on. At first, it kinda seemed like the world was playing a prank on me. Like at any moment, everyone will re-appear and shout, "SURPRISE," and everything will return to the miserable bliss that I once suffered from. But then, it hit me. Everyone is gone. No rules, no regulations, nobody to tell me right from wrong. So I did what anybody else would do. I walked down to the cemetery, and pissed on my father. Then I smashed the bank, just based on the sheer principle of lawlessness. Then I walked to the White House, and sat in the oval office. I wondered if I could nuke Russia from here, my feet scuffing the table and everything. And then it hit me again. Everyone was gone.

As David looked into the mirror with the foam drooling down his cheeks from his mouth, he pierced into his soul. It was like a wormhole of future events passing by him so fast that he couldn't even take a look to find out a little bit about his future self. His mind only headed forward; it's only destination was David's death. David gained this ability when he was young. The exact date and age is foggy to him, but it was when he lived at home. He was playing with some neighborhood friends in the construction lot for the new extension of the suburbs. They would always monkey around the dirt holes for the basements and foundations, and half built homes, swinging on the wooden frame or playing hide n' seek. The accident occurred when David was hiding up in the rafters of a house frame. He had gotten anxious when the seeker had come to the house in search for him. His palms sweaty; David had slipped from his rafter and fell to the concrete base, hitting his head. He had passed out. From what he was told, his friends carried him back home from where he was taken to the hospital. After his hospital visit, the ability began. The first person who he saw their death was a young girl who he had been fond of. It threw him off as he thought it was real and leaped to save her, but later learned she was in no danger. He would continue to act on these visions not knowing what they were. People were starting to look at David strangely. He didn't really understand these visions until a year later. The girl from across the street who he was fond of died in a tragic car accident. She was hit by a car and killed on impact. David was heartbroken after hearing about this, but even more so, he had mentally snapped. He remembered this. He saw her die. He saw this in one of his visions. He thought he saved her. He locked himself away for a week after her death. His parents found it strange after he stopped crying and wouldn't leave his room. No more visions is what he wanted. No more visions. After a few years, David grew up and nobody died. He still saw visions, but became much more mentally stable after the girl's death. He never really confirmed what the visions were. He had a hunch after her death that he was able to see people die before they died, but it was just a theory. Then after a friend of his turned 16, he had gotten into a car accident and died. He remembered seeing this too when they were little. Being years older, he realized that his theory was the only right theory, even if it sounded like complete balderdash. David grew up and his visions kept coming true. Old friends, relatives, strangers, and anybody who he saw died just like how he saw it. He never told anyone about it. "Who would want to know how they would die? " , is what David reasoned. He began to grow distant with his family and friends. However, it made him appear strange to his family and friends and question his sanity. He became a very anti-social, lonely, shut-in by design person. He had got a stay at home job and worked from his now-5 year old computer. He kept fit and got groceries delivered to him, but he never left and never saw another person's face. Nothing has changed since then. Black. Dark. There was nothing. The bathroom was now empty. David was gone; his toothbrush was on the bathroom counter, covered in foam and saliva. He had left in a hurry. His apartment was empty, not a sound could be heard. David was no where to be found. Where had he gone? The sound of footsteps were heard above the ceiling of his apartment. They slowly walked down the length of his apartment as they reached the window sill. It was quiet. And then it was peaceful.

Joel loved weekends. No work to do, just two days to lounge in front of the television and recuperate before he was back to work at the plant. After pouring a bowl of cereal and a cup of strong coffee, he plonked himself in front of the telly, ready for a day of brainless entertainment. However, he was surprised to find that instead of the usual rerun episode of Man Vs. Food, he found that the network was "Closed due to an Unspecified Error." Flicking through the other channels, he found that most of the channels were also closed, apart from BBC news. "This is a previously recorded emergency broadcast." the narrator said. "A disaster situation has occurred. Emergency services are tackling the problem. It would be unadvisable to leave your home before the all-clear signal is given." Joel let the message loop a few times, entranced. Then he turned off the television, drained his cup of coffee, and placed his empty bowl into the dishwasher, before going to his office. An uncontrollable grin, like that of a cheeky schoolboy, widened across his face as he picked up the second canister of anthrax toxin, one of the many others strewn across his desk. This was only the beginning.

The second alarm goes off at 7 in the morning. The first, a few hours before, sharply shrilled that it was time to get up and shower. Hungover and covered with the sweat and scents of the night before, I had dragged myself through the morning routine of cleansing. There was plenty of time beneath the lukewarm stream of water to contemplate the sadness of another hangover caused by drinking alone. It'd been weeks since I last had a chance to talk to another human, instead of just the PC terminal supplied by work. I towelled off and staggered through to the living-room and slumped in front of the computer, waiting for the piercing whistle to repeat, to emanate from my phone. The second alarm marked that it was time for the Remembrance. I sigh, move the empty beer bottles away from my desk and load up Hitchens 2. Since the Bliss neurovirus was released, there was a killing to be made from this sort of software; software designed to take you through a basic test, activating every faculty you'd conceivably need to prevent the atrophy. First, colour recognition and geometric shapes. Second, basic maths ramping into some gentle algebra and trigonometry. English, ethics, road safety, compassion testing, aesthetics, philosophical contemplation, the sciences. It was a hard sell at the beginning, for companies to give their employees the few hours off each morning they needed for the state-mandated testing, but given the choice between late employees and those in conscious comas, they made the right choice. Two hours later, the general test finishes. I flick through my results, 91 recognition of the basic concepts, not too bad after a night of hard drinking. Next would come a quick half hour personal session: the names of loved ones, relations to family members, anniversaries and birthdays. A prompt flashes on the screen: "Please enter your identity number and full name." I rattle my digits in, -A, and tab down to the field for my name. I blank. Slight panic begins to grow as I search my beer-soaked consciousness for that basic, bloody basic, detail. It'd been too long since I last had to introduce myself with anything other than my work ID number, too long since I had any reason to say those damned words out loud. Darren? No. Christopher? No, definitely not. I shout and swear and blaspheme out loud, as I slowly feel the neurovirus go to work; Purgatory, we call it, a limbo without knowledge, tied with a purging. It dissolves me gently. The panic subsides. I stare blankly at the flashing cursor, waiting for me to enter some detail or another. I'm not sure what it's asking for, but I'm sure it's not too important or I'd remember it. I sit there, staring. Just staring. I'm sure it'd come back to me eventually.

Michael paused at the top of the stairs and looked down the hall at the outline of the attic door. Today was the day. Questions and theories that had been laid to rest over the past 20 years, buried deep in some unconscious part of his brain, came bubbling back to the surface of his mind as he walked toward the cord hanging from the ceiling. What if he didn't say anything today? What if he remained perfectly silent? That was certainly possible wasn't it? You can't have last words if they're never uttered, right? He covered his nose and mouth with his sleeve as he pulled the cord, showering himself with years worth of dust. Fishing the small flashlight from his pocket, he climbed the fold out ladder and flicked it on. The cone of light, small as it was, illuminated treasured moments in his life one by one as it passed over various collections of memories long since forgotten. He passed the diplomas and trophies, wedding albums and family photos and old home videos and classic DVDs, love letters and tax returns - all of it kept and hidden away for safe keeping. He realized that all this time he'd been careful to save and document his life, preparing for this day. He wanted to be remembered. To have something to pass on. And here, collecting dust in the attic, was that legacy. Tomorrow, he thought, I'll clean it up. After today, when all this no longer matters and I'm free from this..... curse, I'll pull all this down and sort through it, he thought. Better yet, I'll burn it! It'll be a new day, a new life! He clung to this optimism as the light fell on a single wooden box wedged in the highest joint of the furthest rafter. He reached up and pried it free, wiped the grime from its surface with the edge of his sleeve, and looked at the date staring up at him. Today's date - exactly 20 years from when the box was delivered. Everyone eventually got a box like this. Everyone. It contained what was affectionately known as " your death sentence. " Not in the capital punishment kind of way, but in the most literal translation possible: inscribed within it's thin wooden walls were the last words - the last sentence - you would speak before your death. Everyone got one. He was the first of his friends to get a box, but so far he was the only one that hadn't opened it. Everyone always picked up their box and, filled with a mixed sense of relief and dread, slowly slid the top off. They all read their death sentence etched into the bottom, considered it, memorized it, and then they'd get on with their lives, letting the sentence fade into nothing over the next two decades until, by some chance of fate, they let it slip and found themselves face to face with the grim reaper. Well not today! Michael clutched the box firmly in his hand and descended the ladder and then the stairs, working his way to the kitchen where he knew his wife would be. He wanted her there to bear witness. You see, by waiting until the day of, there was no forgetting the words that would end his life. He would read the words, know them, and then keep his mouth firmly shut the rest of the day. And if, for whatever reason, he had to speak, he would know exactly what combination of syllables to avoid in order to stay above ground. Karen was cutting vegetables when Michael shuffled in and sat at the bar. She barely noticed him as she deftly sliced through peppers and carrots and tomatoes and cucumbers and - She heard a soft thud as Michael dropped something onto the counter. She stopped cutting and looked up. It was a small wooden box, not much bigger than a matchbox, and she recognized it immediately. She knew it wasn't hers - she'd gotten and opened her own only a few years ago - but she still felt her pulse quicken. She pulled the box closer and checked the date, then twisted her wrist and looked at her watch. They matched. Had it really been that long? Had this day already arrived? It felt too early, too soon. She slid the box back across the counter to Michael and looked at his face. He seemed nervous, but confident. He seemed ready. Michael could feel his insides churning. He took a few deep breaths and gave his wife a tight lipped smile. She tried to smile back. It was going to be OK, he decided, just get it over with. He slid the lid off the box with one hand and let it clatter to the floor. He peered inside and read his death sentence and then stood there, puzzling over the two little words he saw. He creased his brow in confusion and looked back up at his wife. " That's it? " He didn't even register her movement, an imperceptible flash of silver, but was able to see her manage one last smile. She nodded and replied as he sank behind the breakfast bar, gasping and choking and clutching his throat. " That's it. "

I've seen the numbers since I was a little girl. I remember my father losing his job, rising from a 4 to a 5. I remember watching my grandmother slowly dwindle down to a 0. But the bold'10' that hovered above his head was plenty enough to convince me not to go near him. Sure, I watched him. Some might even say I was obsessed. It's only now, ten years later, that I realize what makes this boy so special. Only now that I find out why he's such a danger to me. Only now, as he drops to one knee. It's because I love him.

"You made our house out of that precious crystal, the one that covered the world and drifted down from the heavens, to rest gently on the back patio, or to glisten in your hair, waiting to be brushed aside. I like our house. We all miss you. Summer's ending pretty soon. I guess there's a chance the house may not be able to take the extra weight, but I don't care anymore. I'm not leaving it. I'll be right over there. Right in the ground over there. I guess we can be neighbors again." He tried to laugh, but he could only smile weakly as a tear touched his eye. "Anyway that's how things have been. We've got enough food, we're gon na be just fine. We'll be fine," He continued. The wind picked up and the loose snow drifted across the ground. The American flag hanging from the flagpole drifted up, then back down. The metal pole shook gently, and the rope that held it up quietly swung into it. It made a little sound, almost like a wind chime. The tireless sun bore down on the ice, the flag's shadow dancing across the snow. Robert tried not to imagine Lucy rolling around on it. Lucy, laughing and pelting him with snowballs as news of nuclear war, and the end to shipments of food and fuel to Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station, poured in. Lucy, saying it was impossible, that a kid must have gotten ahold of the radio, to try to give us a scare. Lucy, frozen and buried under the snow, staring up at him through the snow. "There wasn't enough food for all of us, Robert. She wouldn't want you out here, in the cold and under the ice with her. Under pressure, precious things break." Frank's voice said. "Then let them break." Robert said, as he walked to the den of solid water, of the fluid unable to flow. Edit: wrong name Edit 2: another name

Quick one before class! "Good morning!" she says staring at me, bright eyed and beautiful. Every morning the same, but every morning different. It is as if the day had repeated itself, down to the smallest speck of dust on the ever dusty window sill. "Its 8:30 and you, need to get to work!" As I tumbled out of bed, I took a double take on the beauty that was before my eyes. "Honey!? What is it?" she whimmed, as if to say that there was something horribly wrong with me. "Nothing" I replied solemnly, I didn't want to tell her the truth. "You're looking beautiful as always" For little did she know that with each passing day, she changed. Always a tiny change, from the way that patch of hair on her head began to fall, or the way her face seemed gloomy or grey. Everyday felt like waking up in a universe identical to the one I'm already in, with only one change. She was fading. Like a flower in the winter, cold, but still the only beauty that you see in a vastness of blankets and pillows. The only warmth in even the coldest of places. She is my universe. The same, but always changing.

Just like everyone else, they fear me. Christina stared at the other prisoners. Their prison, if that is what you could call it, was effectively a gaping hole in the ground. It's quite aptly named'The Hole' for obvious reasons. Residents of'The Hole' are put to work crushing rocks, for no other reason than the Warden needed something for them to do. To become a resident of'the Hole' you need to effectively be so dangerous that they don't trust you to be confined to a cage, they'd rather have a minimum of 15 anti-personnel rifles pointed at you at all times. As Christina stepped into the yard all 15 guards holding aforementioned anti-personnel rifles, swivelled and aimed directly at her. The prisoners already residing within the yard, all 7 of them, turned and looked directly at her. Upon seeing the markings covering her arms they each took an involuntary step backwards. She smiled a cruel smile and flexed her arms, her left arm emitting a slight whir. The already jumpy prisoners took another step back. The guards turned on their laser sights, all 15 lasers danced across her chest and head indiscriminately. She laughed and raised her arms, palms open to the sky. The 4 guards who had just escorted her into the yard, kicked her in the back of the knees and slapped handcuffs on her all in one smooth motion. The cuffs they used weren't standard issue, they were made of solid iron. Standing her up they placed another set of iron cuffs around her biceps. Instead of taking her back inside to a nice cushy cage, they marched her to the middle of'the Hole' and placed her within the cage that resided there. The cage was then suspended 15 metres above the ground and moved over a pit that went down another 40m. As the crane stopped moving and the cage began to sway with inertia over the pit, the lasers turned off and the guards relaxed, even the prisoners visibly relaxed, some of the braver ones even found the courage to taunt Christina. She simply smiled sweetly (if a wolf's smile could be called sweet) at them. They feel safe with me in this cage. What they don't realise is by daybreak tomorrow I shan't be inside this cage anymore. How many dead bodies I leave behind me when I leave depends purely on how many people antagonise me while I'm in here. Tonight is going to be quite fun. Over the course of the next 5 hours the same 3 prisoners came and taunted her regularly, she noted down the names scribbled onto their chests and when they were escorted back to their cages she watched which ones they were taken to. Not a single guard taunted her while she resided within the cage, they barely even looked at her. Pity I have to kill them. She thought to herself as the guards in the towers changed shifts. It's bad luck they got the night shift. As the moon stared down at her, practically mocking her with its freedom, she stretched her arms to test the iron bands holding them firmly in place. The bands didn't budge even a mm. She smiled, she'd be disappointed if the bands broke apart easily. Flexing the muscles in her forearms, the magic began to arc between her fingers and the air around her grew cold. The bars of her cage formed icicles, the markings covering her arms began to glow a pale blue light as if lit from within. With a flex of her fingers, the magic burst outwards, the metal of her bonds and the cage froze over in an instant. She flexed her arms again and broke the bonds, standing she ripped the top of the cage off and leapt out landing just beside the pit. Before the guards had any time to react she rocketed off towards the first tower. Magic arcing between her fingers she formed a dagger out of pure ice as she scaled the side of the tower. It just isn't your night friend. She thought as she slid the ice dagger between the guards fourth and fifth ribs, twisting the dagger before pulling it out. She bent down and picked up his anti-personnel rifle, checking the magazine for rounds before she pulled back the bolt. Butting the stock up to her shoulder she took aim at the first of the 14 remaining guards and fired. In quick succession she fired upon the guards, shooting each of them in the chest. With all the gunfire she had 5 minutes tops before the alarms went off. She had to leave, now. Scrambling down the tower her feet hit the ground before she remembered, those 3 prisoners. They hadn't died yet. She turned to the cellblock and quickly made her way inside. The only sound was her footsteps against the concrete floor as she stalked through the halls. As she came upon the cells containing her targets she formed another dagger of ice. Touching her hand to the lock of the first cell she froze it and kicked the door open, not caring about the noise. Quickly she was inside and her dagger was in the convicts' larynx. She repeated the process with the other two convicts and exited the cellblock just as the alarms went off. I wasted too much time on a petty vendetta. She broke into a dead sprint across the yard. Running for the north wall. As the guards burst into the yard, guns raised Christina leapt at the wall. Digging her left hand into the solid concrete as if it was putty. Using her magic she coated her right hand in a layer of ice an inch thick, sharpened the ice covering the tips of her fingers and began to scale the wall. As she reached the top of the wall she sat there a moment and looked down at the prison that was her home for a simple night. In the span of a night, I murdered 17 people just to kill my target. Not bad for a days' work. She smiled to herself and stood up. She looked down at the guards scanning the yard for her, raised her hand in a two-fingered salute and leapt backwards off the wall. - If you liked that read my other stuff at rCeruberus
